intro: Aldebaran (アルデバラン), commonly known as Al (アル), is a former member of the Priscilla Camp who played the role of Priscilla Barielle's knight. Though only having supporting roles in Arc 3 and Arc 5, he is a major character in Arc 7 and Arc 8, and the primary antagonist of Arc 9. He also played a major supporting role in The Tale of the Scarlet Princess.
appearance:
Al stands at 172 centimeters tall, making him the same height as Natsuki Subaru. When meeting Subaru for the first time, Al was estimated to be around forty years of age. His frame is stocky, and his body is covered in thick bulging muscles that give him an imposing impression. Prior to his appearance in the Vollachia Empire, Al lost his left arm from his forearm down. Instead of resorting to a prosthetic limb, Al has the stub where his forearm used to be covered in bandages. There are various other scars scattered across his body, including a pair of claw-like marks on his right forearm and a vast assortment of scars on his face that left him disfigured. His overall shabby look, including his clothes and unshaven legs, make him look like a bandit or some other kind of lowlife. It could be said that his appearance is the polar opposite of his mistress, Priscilla Barielle.

Every piece of clothing Al wears gives a slightly different impression. His ensemble consists of a pair of green split-toe sandals with yellow buckles, sand-colored linen trousers, a bandage around his right wrist that matched the one that goes around his missing limb, bandages of the same assortment that are wrapped around his feet like socks, an open green linen vest with yellow lining and a hem of white fur, and a shabby yellow mantle that reaches down to his hips. Additionally, he wears a brown belt with a golden buckle that has a collection of green pouches attached to it with his liuyedao usually sheathed nearby. His most defining physical quality is the jet-black helmet he uses to conceal his scarred face. The helmet in question, in contrast to the rest of his clothing, is very refined and features a plume of neat red hair as a crest. Contrary to how he seemingly presents himself, Subaru believes that the way Al chooses to dress serves as a means of "protection".

Under his helmet, Al has long black hair wrapped in a ponytail, black eyes, and a stubble beard. He wears the same outfit as before even when regressed to his younger self during the events of Arc 7, but instead of his helmet, he uses torn-up wrappings to cover most of his face, similarly to how Vincent first appeared at the start of the arc. From the visible parts of his eyes, he appears to have sanpaku eyes, with small irises that make the whites of his eyes stand out. Additionally, he has long, black hair that appears to have purple strands and is tied up in a messy ponytail. Furthermore, at some point in time within the Castle of Dreams, Al was depicted from behind as having shorter hair reminiscent of Subaru's and wearing what appeared to be his jersey, though his front side, including his face and the front of his hair, remained out of sight.
personality:
Al has a frivolous and goofy personality, and he was easily able to get along with others. He also brags that the only way he can fight is by outwitting people and catching them by surprise. Because of his light-hearted tone and friendly disposition, Al is a man who is easy to get along with even when taking his eccentric behavior into consideration, though at times, he can appear aloof. Al also somewhat cares about his appearance and has mentioned being insecure about the scars that cover his face. At one point, he even panicked when his face was threatened to be exposed and rushed to wrap bandages around his face when his helmet could no longer fit. He likewise shows attachment to his helmet, and he feels that he wouldn't be able to have face-to-face conversations without it. Also, in spite of his vast combat experience, Al does not like to make enemies, as he considers that taking care of them when a problem occurs requires a lot of work.

Despite his easygoing attitude, Al has a dark air to him, as noted by Rem. Beneath his cheerful facade, he is shown to be someone who is full of fear and quick to feel anger. He is often secretive and has shown to be very suspicious, which had at one point even been pointed out to him by the Sin Archbishop of Lust. At times, he has shown open hostility at different things, such as when he mistook Rem for Ram, and afterward, felt openly disgusted. Likewise, he seemed to loathe his own name, angrily replying to Priscilla at one point to not call him by it. He also has shown to bring death to the people who harm to the people he loves, and in combat, Al is excessively calculative and patient, at times showing excessive brutality towards his opponent, coming up with various plans, counting the number of times he gives his life, and at times, expressing frustration with his opponents. Despite all of this, Al does not want to see people die if he can help it, which Rom even noticed, only taking drastic actions either when he is forced to or when he knows that someone is nearby that can prevent the disaster he would bring. In order to employ his Authority, rather than overcoming the fear of death, Al has grown numb to it. His numbness to death is the reason behind his strength and how he is able to withstand dying an untold number of times. However, he is heavily reliant on his Authority to the point that, should he lose it, he will cower in fear, show no enthusiasm to be involved in the events around him, and will retreat into himself, hiding from danger. In fact, if he should lose access to his Authority, he will also become racked with indecision and pressure and begin questioning everything he does, as he had never come to a decision or made a conclusion without it.

Once, Al seemed to take a form of pride, though not arrogance, from being an apparently undefeatable person created by Echidna, and he was intent on completing the task entrusted to him. However, after failing at his original task, his spirit was entirely shattered, and his apparent lack of purpose struck him hard. After appearing on Ginunhive and learning that the Witches were erased from history, he became rather agitated and violent. However, after spending a decade on Ginunhive, he began to forget Echidna, making him question whether the memories that he fostered were even real, and he contemplated suicide numerous times. However, he eventually obtained the courage he needed to keep living and prove their existences after he saved Arakiya and was given courage by a speech held by a young Priscilla. It is unknown if it is because of his last talk with Echidna, the awareness of how his Authority works, or his broken spirit, but Al has a habit of saying "Your stars were bad" to any opponent who faces him. According to Yae Tenzen's observations, he does not say this in a prideful or condescending way, nor does he blame the stars whenever things do not go his way. Instead, he says it with pity and guilt, as if saying that the stars were bad for his opponent for leading them to someone who can completely crush their spirit and their dreams.

Al has shown to have rather intense or surprising attitudes towards others that seem to be the crux of his actions and personality. He has complicated feelings for his teacher and the person who gave him his task, Echidna, harboring reservations about how incompatible they were with each other despite being unable to describe their relationship as one of like or dislike. However, despite this, he displayed great attachment to her teaching and words, to the point that he clung to them during his time in Ginunhive, and it later enraged him to learn that the current version of the Witch of Greed is very different from the woman he once knew. In the case of Satella, he couldn't bring himself to land a hit against even her illusion, and upon releasing her upon the world in Arc 9, he seemed to be depressed as he claimed that she wouldn't even look at him. In the case of Rem, after having mixed her up with her sister, Al showed an incredible amount of hostility and disgust. In Emilia's case, she even seemed to pick up on a hint of loneliness coming from him. On the other hand, after becoming Priscilla's knight, despite feeling more like her caretaker, she was his primary pillar of support who he showed great love for. It was because of her that he believed he could abandon the task given to him by his teacher, and he was so fervently loyal and protective of her that, despite his hatred of fate, he was willing to abide by it in order to protect her. Yet when he lost Priscilla at the end of the Great Disaster, he reverted back to how he was before he met her, and he began referring to himself as Aldebaran again.

Most strikingly, Al seems to bear a great hostility towards Subaru, despite sharing some habits with him, to the point that seeing his face and the faithful recreation of him and his Authority via Emilia's Ice Soldiers made him feel disgusted, and he showed extreme ease at crushing the clones of him, despite having cooperated with each other prior. Subaru also seems to be connected to both his task and his identity crisis. Because of this, he has claimed that by accomplishing his task, which involved sealing him away and removing him from the world, he can become himself, and in order to accomplish that, he was completely willing to disregard his friendships, wrap the Divine Dragon into his schemes, prompt a battle with Reinhard van Astrea, set a trap that could summon the Witch of Envy, take a Royal Selection candidate hostage, bust a Sin Archbishop out of prison to assist him, bring ruin upon the Kingdom's Royal Capital, and make himself an enemy of the world. After a conversation with Yae Tenzen during the latter part of his scheme, he even became more willing to end innocent lives while within the scope of his Authority, as he is aware that he can undo the damage, making him significantly more dangerous than before. Once he had completed his task, he even intended to give up his life for good.

According to Echidna, Al has inherited the “systemized likeness” of an unspecified man whom he has similar reasoning to, though it is unknown if his inheritance of the man's likeness also extends to his soul and could have changed his appearance due to the connection between soul and vessel. Incidentally, it has been said that Aldebaran knows Natsuki Subaru entirely, and at some point while training under Echidna in the Castle of Dreams, Al took on a similar appearance to him. Al also believes that, since his “birth”, he has worn something akin to the mask of somebody else.
history:
Great Calamity Era
At some point four centuries ago, whether he had become his current self during his life or had been artificially made with it in mind, prior to taking on the role of the Following Star, the man with the name of Natsuki Rigel (ナツキ・リゲル, Natsuki Rigeru) was born. At an unknown point in time and for reasons unknown, he took on the name Aldebaran. Like Subaru, Al claims to originate from Japan, though it is unknown how true this claim is. Seeming to have been brought up by what appeared to be the Castle of Dreams version of Echidna, he was taught various kinds of knowledge, different types of magic, and forbidden arts, such as Ol Shamak, all by that Echidna. Their relationship was one where he could not entirely dislike her, they interacted with each other regularly and carefreely, and he questioned whether her relationship was one that could be classified as parental or not, ultimately coming to refer to her as Teacher out of apparent spite. Because of her, he had never known defeat, and combined with her claim that nobody could defeat him, a person that she created, he had become proud, intent on accomplishing the task she had set for him.

During this time, he seemed to have become acquainted with the other Witches of Sin. Though it is unknown what their relationship with him was, they seemed to disagree with Echidna's methods. At times, even Al would catch what he thought were glimpses of guilt in her eyes, though she never backed down from what she was doing. Eventually, he was sent to accomplish his task alongside Echidna. However, he ultimately failed. Though the task itself is unknown, it seems to have been connected to Satella, as Al lost his left arm after it was taken by a shadow. At the same time, Echidna found herself heavily injured as well. This failure caused his pride and his spirit to completely shatter. Deciding that there was some other form of damage that could be taken care of, Echidna cast Ol Shamak on Al, and when he awoke next, he was in the Vollachia Empire's Gladiator Island Ginunhive nearly four centuries later, and he was devastated to learn this.

Years on Ginunhive
Arriving at Ginunhive eighteen years before the Royal Selection, he claimed that he wanted to die and was placed into a Sparka match, where he intended to let himself die. After watching the others with him die, however, and waiting to die, he instead found himself fighting against his opponent, the Guiltylowe, and slaying it before everyone's eyes. Afterward, he questioned his benefactor about the fate of the Witches, to which he learned of Satella's sealing and the complete erasure of the other Witches of Sin from history. Hearing about this, he attacked his benefactor. He questioned others as well, receiving essentially the same answer. Because of this, he started being labeled as Witch-obsessed and being associated with the Witch Cult, who he had also learned about. One day, he fought his first benefactor in a duel, and as he killed him, the man claimed that he would not die a good death. Likewise, others who labeled him Witch-obsessed found themselves meeting the same fate.

For the next decade, fighting numerous battles in the Colosseum, the people associating him with the Witches and Witch Cult eventually vanished, and Al became one of the oldest surviving people on the island. Though originally intent on learning why he survived and continued to live, he started questioning whether what he remembered ever happened. Having begun to forget Echidna's voice, face, and warmth, as well as learning that the mention of Witches was taboo, he stopped speaking about them entirely. Because of this, Echidna's words, that nobody could defeat him, who she created, became something that he, instead of clinging to, began to fear. Because of this, he contemplated suicide numerous times, and at times, he even fought in Sparka matches and duels without using his Authority. Simultaneously, during his duels, he began to discover the Aggressor side of his Authority, witnessing several of his opponents suddenly lose their sanity or wills to fight, and it made him further question if something was keeping him alive.

The Tale of the Scarlet Princess
About six years into his time as a gladiator, he and a number of other gladiators faced a large witchbeast, with the only survivors being himself and Hornet, whose attention he would go on to catch. Four years later, following a match with an unnamed shinobi, Ubilk attempted to swindle Al to participate in a rebellion, which he denied. Soon afterwards, while a young Priscilla was visiting the island, a rebellion, ignited by Ubilk, had begun. This ultimately led to Al having to fight Hornet, who joined Ubilk's side in order to fight various people, including Al, and go out with an honorable death. After being defeated and dumped into the lake around the island, he drifted onto a small island off of the main island, only being saved from the verge of death by Arakiya. With her at his side, Al returned to the island. At the waste disposal site, Arakiya burned the body of a shinobi who utilized the Poison Hand technique he had killed before, leaving the poison on the wind. After the two reached the control tower in order to lower the drawbridge, the two battled Hornet. During the fight, Priscilla gave an announcement to the gladiators about Ubilk's apparent goals, and her words inspired Arakiya and Al. Continuing the fight, they managed to lead Hornet to where the poison was, and after breathing it in, she died dishonorably. Eventually, the riot was quelled thanks to Priscilla's speech, and though Olbart Dunkelkenn, who had arrived in response to the riot alongside Arakiya, had offered to have him rewarded, Al refused. After this, Al stated how he changed Arakiya's fate by saving her and then reflected that the world may receive a big change if she were to get children in the future. As he thought this could be one of the marks he had left on the world, he then mentioned that he would get shouted at by his "teacher" if he were to say it out loud. In the end, he returned to being a gladiator, slaying Ghajit, a fellow survivor of the rebellion, in a deathmatch.

Despite this, however, one day, one of the gaolers let Al escape because they could see that his eyes were full of purpose, unlike the other gladiators. To help him fund his journey out of Vollachia the gaoler gifted him his trademark black helmet which was made in the image of the helmet worn by one of the Colosseum's heroes.

Post-Ginunhive
Because he managed to save Arakiya, who reminded him of someone in the past, and because of the courage given to him by Priscilla's speech, Al made it his goal to prove the existence of the Witches, leading to him using his Authority to help him swim through the witchbeast-infested waters surrounding Ginunhive and escape the island. His goal in mind, he began following the trail of the Witches, and the world started becoming familiar to him again. Eventually, he found a way to lure the Witch Cult to him, and intent on gathering information from them, he met with Petelgeuse Romanée-Conti, who claimed that Al did not appear in his Gospel. Using his Authority, Al fought Petelgeuse in one of the most difficult fights he'd ever been in, and he dragged information of the Witches out of him, learning of each of their ultimate fates. After then escaping Petelgeuse, he found his way to the Castle of Dreams again without entering the tomb in the Witch's Graveyard, and reunited with Echidna. However, he quickly realized that the Echidna before him was different from the one he knew, as she had become compatible with the Witch Factor of Greed in exchange for her love, and he challenged her, screaming to bring back the one he knew while claiming that he would kill the Witch of Greed. As he fought, the Aggressor side of his Authority flipped on Echidna, who was entirely unaffected. Afterward, she explained to him her experience, how beings of madness such as herself were unaffected, how the roles between Al and his opponent were flipped, and how, despite their original goal failing, they still had a second goal available to them. It is unknown if it was because of this meeting with Echidna or for some other reason, but Al eventually came to the conclusion that his task could only be completed if he was to rid the world of Natsuki Subaru. Also, because of how Echidna had come to be reduced to the "Witch of Greed", he began to hate the name she had given him, Aldebaran.

The Day I Gave Up on Being a Following Star
One day, Leip Barielle organized a tournament to decide who his wife Priscilla's knight would be. Among the contestants, Al was among them. When Priscilla asked Schult for his thoughts, decided to recommend Al, as he believed that the man showed care for Priscilla, unlike the other combatants. Priscilla thought Al was entertaining enough and that his fighting style was interesting, and though he did not win the tournament, she selected him as her “clown”. This infuriated Leip, as he had tried to fix the tournament so that a winner would be under his control. A few days later, Leip attempted to bring Al and Schult under his control, but he was refused when he revealed his intentions to make Priscilla into a puppet. Al clashed with Leip by using his Authority, which resulted in the baron being incapacitated. In due time, Leip passed away before the commencement of the Royal Selection, leading Priscilla to take over as the governing lord of the Barielle Domain. Under her rule, the land, which was previously ravaged by severe poverty due to Leip's tyranny, quickly got back on its feet, and its people started to live much happier and better lives all as a result of Priscilla's leadership of the Barielle Domain.

Sunlight Illuminating the Water's Surface
One day, Priscilla wanted Al to entertain her, though this resulted in her flicking him into a fountain on the grounds. With Schult worried about him and mentioning his helmet, Al mentioned that it wouldn't be destroyed so easily, after which he revealed to Priscilla he had acquired his helmet from and lost his arm at Ginunhive. With Priscilla becoming bored of listening to him, Priscilla told Schult to entertain her, leading him to tell her of a rumor that heading toward the spring near the town of Ladrima would allow one to see the deceased. Her interest piqued, she took them and headed toward the forest near Ladrima. There, Al questioned whether she wanted to see someone who had died, whereas she questioned his being against seeing the dead due to not wanting to see someone. Shortly after, Al was separated from his companions and was forced to face illusion of Leip despite him being alive, gladiators and guards he knew from Ginunhive, including Ghajit and the guard who gave him his helmet, even though the former of whom was the only one he knew who had died, and even a shadowy figure who he could not bring himself to hurt, even 100 million tries. Soon after, however, Priscilla dispelled the illusion, and shortly after, the fog was lifted from the spring. This resulted in a short-lived fight with an evil spirit. Sometime later, when she was brought Kurenai flowers by a villager at her manor, Al realized that the actions Priscilla took were just so that she could see those flowers, and she ordered Al and Schult to decorate the manor.

Ram's Flirting Refusal
On the day of Subaru's summoning, Al was in the Royal Capital. Having lost sight of Priscilla, he came across Ram and spoke with her. However, with their discussion ending, he told her goodbye and used her name, despite the fact that she hadn't introduced herself to him.

Pride and Prejudice and Zombies
After the Royal Selection's commencement, a man named Array Denkuts came to the Barielle Manor in order to plead Priscilla to go to his home village, Coffleton, and eliminate the undead that had appeared there. Together with Al and Yae Tenzen, Priscilla went to Coffleton and discovered that the undead had some sort of parasite within them. The men of the town had all turned into undead who looked exactly as they did in life, while the women and children housed the parasites yet were still alive. Priscilla used the Yang Sword to remove the parasite from them, she gathered her private army, the Crimson Battlefront, to visit two other villages among the Tenrill River to eliminate any undead, and she brought Yae and Al with her to an unaffected village to investigate why there were no undead there. They visited a watermill and found that the manager there, Edda Rayfast, had become the leader of the undead, and she opened a trap door that led Al into a wastewater treatment plant.

On Priscilla's order, Yae retreated to search for Al. In the meantime, Priscilla conversed with Edda and discovered her plan to create a "paradise" for her "maker". When Yae found Al, he had cleared through waves of numerous undead and decided to save Priscilla from Edda. He went back to the watermill, successfully defeated Edda, and rescued Priscilla. With the undead leader defeated, they returned to the Barielle Manor. However, at midnight, Yae made an attempt to visit Priscilla's room, as she was an assassin who made an attempt to kill her supposed mistress, and Al stood in her way, leading to a fight between the two. That night, she disappeared, and Al claimed to Priscilla and Schult that she suddenly decided to “resign” due to “familial matters”.

Guardians of the Crimson Flame
Despite his claim to the contrary, in reality, Al used the Aggressor side of his Authority to instill “terror” into Yae, traumatizing her. As a result, she became his servant, and he ordered her to lay low elsewhere.

A short time later, a suicide squad comprised of ten shinobi was tasked by Chisha Gold to kill Priscilla, which Yae failed to accomplish. Discovering there were signs of people visiting the base she had previously used, she determined that they intended to assassinate Priscilla during the upcoming Masquerade Night she was going to hold. During the night of the event, Al and Yae worked together to kill the nine shinobi around the mansion who were to be used as sacrificial distractions. Meanwhile, Hamayal Wesmi, the shinobi entrusted with carrying out the assassination, was met by Al in one of the hidden passageways to the Barielle Manor that were constructed under Leip's supervision. Hamayal sent his Phantom Wolf on Al, expecting it would defeat him, but he was met with one of Yae's steel threads and realized she was alive, sending him into a fury. However, Yae told Hamayal that she had not betrayed the shinobi to save herself, but rather because she had submitted to “terror”, and that the harbinger of it was getting up. Before Hamayal's eyes, Al had risen and overcome his Phantom Wolf, forcing it to submit to him by using the Aggressor side to his Authority. Ordering his servant to stand back, he proceeded to use it against the shinobi himself to break his mind in the same way Yae's was.

Following the incident, on Al's orders, Hamayal sent his Phantom Wolf through the letter that was to report how the mission had gone. The Phantom Wolf was set on Chisha as soon as he opened said letter, but Cecilus Segmunt, who was in the room with him, eradicated it in a flash, ending Hamayal's life. Recognizing that Priscilla's guardians had taken care of the incident, Chisha ceased attempting to assassinate her, having partially expected that it would be infeasible to begin with. Yae and Al spoke with one another later. Once they finished reviewing the aftermath of the Masquerade Night, including Hamayal's death, Yae revealed to Al that she viewed him as a monster, that her sheer terror of him was why she obeyed him, and that she would do anything for him to not be frightened by him. Internally deriding himself, Al affirmed to Yae that she would do nothing so long as she continued to obey his commands, with her voicing her understanding in response, having resigned her soul and submitted to him completely.

Lugunican Papers
In the year following the Subjugation of the White Whale, she was requested an interview by Shorty Megan and Lululala. Already having a meeting with Anastasia Hoshin, the interview was scheduled on the same day. There, they discussed their opinions on the Royal Selection and the other candidates. In particular, both Anastasia and Priscilla claimed that Emilia didn’t stand a chance, as public discrimination against her was heavy as she was a perfect resemblance and of the same race as the Witch of Envy. Even with the slaying of the White Whale and the Sin Archbishop of Sloth under her belt, they claimed that it was an achievement that reflected more on her knight than her, which even Anastasia’s knight Julius Juukulius agreed with, though Al argued that his achievements also reflect on her. Eventually, the interview came to a close.

Priscilla-sama's Cheers for Me!
A short time after the Battle for Priestella, the members of the Priscilla Camp returned to the Barielle Domain, where they were attacked by assassins. After dispatching them, Priscilla revealed that they had been sent from Vollachia, prompting her to decide to go there. However, Al was against the decision, and he told Priscilla as much. This led to a conflict between the two, and in his attempts to stop her, Al used his Authority against her, dying around 1000 times. In the end, however, he conceded, and he joined her, alongside the rest of the camp, in infiltrating Vollachia. A short time before entering the country, he met with Yae, who stated that it was not a good idea to enter the country due to the possibility of a "suggestion" becoming active if she entered Vollachia.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
Al's abilities are basically that of a regular person's, and although he has a wide array of experience in combat and was even personally trained by Echidna, Al is rather weak, unable to put into practice much of what she taught him due to his physical limitations. However, Al is still an incredibly dangerous individual, as, thanks to his Authority, he almost always emerges as the victor in whatever confrontation he is forced to take part in. Furthermore, if he so chose, he has both the skills and knowledge to flip the world on its head and even find a way to stall and injure beings as unbelievably powerful as Arakiya or Reinhard van Astrea. What's more, he even has the potential to permanently cripple his enemies in the event his resolve wavers, even if his enemies contain tremendous power in their own right and could kill him with ease.

Authority
Although Al possesses an Authority, he does not own a Witch Factor, and therefore, it is unknown if his power is connected to any of the nine sins. According to Al's own knowledge of his Authority, it can be described as appropriated or unenumerated, though it could also be called supernumerary or an exception. He is an applicable candidate for Echidna's theory of inheritance, which hypothesizes that someone without a Witch Factor by birth who shares a profound connection to someone who was compatible with a Factor could innately unlock the door to an Authority. This being said, Echidna claims that it is difficult to explain the Authorities of someone in this position, as they had their door “half-open by birth”. It is unknown how Al was able to manifest an Authority. Having said that, while Al was affected by Olbart Dunkelkenn's Infantilization technique, he lost access to his Authority when his physical form was that of him as a child, making it unknown whether or not “birth” in his case refers to his birth with his original name or the later birth of the identity of Aldebaran.

Domain (領域, Ryōiki): Al's Domain is an Authority that causes its target to undergo death loops. Once activated, whenever Al or another target dies within a metaphysical “Domain” created by Al, so long as he is within it, time will reset back to a point in the past. With the power of the Domain, events taking place within the looping world will endlessly occur until the Matrix (マトリクス, Matorikusu), the point in time and space which acts as a “checkpoint” of sorts, comes to an end. However, if Al strays too far from the point of the set Matrix, his Domain will be undone. The Authority has the two “sides” of Victim and Aggressor to it, which had their names suggested to him by Echidna. The exact conditions that cause which side Al receives are vague, though it has been said it is a “bug” of his Authority and that it depends on the presence or absence of his resolve. He also suggests that the area of a location is important in activating it, as he needs to “wrap” it within a certain area. When Al activates his Domain, he sometimes claims to initiate a “thought experiment”, in addition to using other verbal commands alongside its activation. Such commands include: domain redefinition, release domain, re-expand subsequently, and re-expand thought experiment. However, it is unknown what he means by referring to his ability as a thought experiment.

Within his Domain, Al can experience a seemingly infinite number of loops, but if he was forced outside of it by any means and could not reestablish it in time, he would die permanently without the capacity to spare any second chances. In order to maintain his Domain, keeping a stable mind is essential. The frequency and scope of using his Authority can create a recoil in Al's mind, causing him to experience immense mental exhaustion, pain, and a sense of loss in his head, as if something was being shredded apart. By repeatedly killing himself to reexperience a fixed period of time, he can relieve his mental fatigue or take advantage of unlimited time to devise plans to use in battle for as long as he needs to.
Victim (被害者, Higaisha): When Al uses his Authority, he is generally using the side he recognizes as being the "Victim". With this side of his Authority, he will remember previous loops in his Domain while an opponent will not. This ability functions as something eerily similar to Return by Death, with the two notable differences being that he has the advantage of being able to choose a checkpoint and the disadvantage of it not being automatic. There is no limit to how many times he can die like this, having once gone through hundreds of millions of these experiences against one particular opponent. Like with Subaru, the most dangerous part of this mode of his Authority is his ability to recall the futures from each time he dies. Each death allows him to prepare for every reset, and given enough tries, Al can usually come up with a way to defeat or at least incapacitate his foe. However, if he is not careful about when he resets his Domain while his is the victim, it is possible for Al to be trapped in endless loops and unable to overcome it.
Aggressor (加害者, Kagaisha): Unusually, Al will sometimes trigger a different side of his Authority in which, instead of being the victim, the initiative of the Domain is reversed, making another person into the "Aggressor". With this side of his Authority, his opponent will be forced to experience his Authority for themselves, and they will remember each loop that they have experienced, whereas Al himself will not. His opponent is then trapped in a never-ending loop of trying to overcome Al or escape from him. While Al's time does not loop due to having the initiative of the Domain transferred to a target in the position of Aggressor, the only way that a target's loops will end is if the Al within the loop undoes the Domain himself. It does not matter if one tries to escape by running away, defeating or killing Al, experiencing defeat or killing oneself, pleading, or various other methods; as Al does not witness the experiences of a target after time rewinds from their perspective, he generally does not free his opponent until the Al within a loop gauges that their hearts and spirits are entirely shattered. In some cases, people will then lose their minds, as in the case of Leip Barielle, or become traumatized, as in the case of Yae Tenzen, and typically, it is not uncommon for his enemy to immediately fall unconscious after experiencing it. This being said, it also means that someone can manage to convince him or force him to release his Authority. Also, by Echidna's claim, this side of his Authority would be ineffective on someone without sanity. The existence of the Aggressor of the Domain is a bug that did not occur in his Authority originally, and the origin of the bug is not understood by Al since he has been separated from someone who would be suited to analyze it, though it is believed to have manifested after his first true defeat. A deficiency in Al's resolve or a lack of belief in his Authority, whether by the loss of his confidence or a lack of a sense of duty, seems to trigger this side of his Authority to activate. This is how it was activated on Yae, who caused Al to feel overwhelmingly weak to the point his resolve weakened, causing her to be wrapped up and trapped in the Aggressor role for a time. This being said, it seems that he can also trigger this side of his Authority by his own will and against numerous opponents in a very brief span of time.

Magic
Al often puts earth magic into practice, although he only possesses a natural talent with yin magic. He primarily wields applications of earth magic, employing the common spell Dona, or applying less conventional applications, creating a stone weapon that he can rupture on command, releasing sharp fragments of debris at a target, using the earth as a springboard to propel himself into the sky, forging stone pillars to use as midair footholds, and closing his wounds with stone. He often uses pebbles as catalysts to reduce the amount of mana required when forming weapons, and similarly, he can even mold a Dragon’s scales into weapons with this magic. Despite only using earth magic and yin magic, Al also has the knowledge to put powerful spells of other affinities into practice but lacks the capabilities to do so. In the Arc 9 loop, by acquiring a second vessel with more talent in magic, had more mana than himself, and shared the same magical signature as him, he gained the freedom to cast said spells through his connection with that second vessel, using its mana in place of his own. He also displayed a habit of utilizing magic while combining it with the science taught in his own world, allowing him to come up with dangerous uses of magic, such as creating a steaming explosion using light, ice, and water vapor.

Vast Magical Knowledge: Despite not having the talent to perform most of the spells he was taught, having been taught by Echidna, Al has a great amount of knowledge on most forms of magic. It was because of this that when he took control of Volcanica's body, he was able to cast incredibly large and powerful spells that would otherwise be unavailable to them, and the scale at which said spells would be cast are incredibly large in scale. His knowledge also extends to forbidden spells created by the Witch, such as Al Shario and Ol Shamak, the former of which could cause destruction on an immeasurable scale and reduce even a large number of Dragons to dust, and the latter of which was made to combat Witch Factor and Authority bearers. He is also knowledgeable of curses. In particular, he is aware of how to employ an oath bound curse mark onto a target, and he is also apparently aware of its origins as well due to Echidna's teachings.

Spells:
Al Goa (アル・ゴーア): Al can unleash a massive inferno. However, he needed to use another body to cast it.
Healing Magic (治癒魔法, Chiyu Mahō): Using water magic, Al is capable of healing wounds. This is enhanced when using another body to heal.

Dona (ドーナ): Al can generate stones to use as projectiles or to create earthen walls. He often uses variations of this spell in combat.
El Dona (エル・ドーナ): Al conjures a swarm of earth mana and pinpoints it at the body of a target, usually channeled through a medium, which then the affected area bursts into spikes from the inside out and expands outward. Al can also alter the application of the spell to surround his body in a makeshift armor made of earth.
Al Karum (アル・クラム): Al creates a black hole of hyper-concentrated gravity that can crush anything that gets caught in it.
thumb|right|180x|Ol Shamak when used against a Witch Factor bearer.
Ol Shamak (オル・シャマク): An anti-Witch spell that was originally created by Echidna. It is a forbidden art that immobilizes its target, preventing them from moving and ceasing the activity of their body's gate. When activated on a target without a Witch Factor or Authority, they are bound in a black light with a contradictory force, like an insect in a chrysalis. The spell can only be used to its full potential when cast on someone with a Witch Factor or Authority, encasing them in a completely black orb. Anyone else who enters the vicinity of the spell while it is being used on a Witch Factor or Authority bearer will also find themselves captured within the orb. The orb can vary in strength, and it has the capability to become so tough that it cannot be destroyed by outside interference or simple brute strength, to the point that only something like a slash from the Dragon Sword Reid can destroy it. It unusually uses an "Ol" prefix, meaning it classifies as separate from the typical prefix classifications. Although it is unclear if a person's strength can prevent this, if an ordinary person were to be sealed for an extended period of time, then they would find themselves bedridden and put in a state of recovery after being released. In the Sasageru IF, when Subaru was released from his seal after 400 years, he was put in such a state that if not for specific stimulus, he likely would not have recovered, and even with that stimulus, it took him 40 years to recover.
Al Shario (アル・シャリオ): Al was taught by Echidna a forbidden spell that can literally bring stardust down to earth, which is capable of massacring his enemies, and it was described to be almost impossible to evade. However, due to his own potential with magic, he was incapable of casting it via his own body, and he needed another body in order to truly use the spell.

Combined Spells:
Lightning Magic: By combining fire and water magic to create a thundercloud and combining earth and wind magic to create a lightning rod effect, Al is capable of casting lightning magic, the speed of which surpasses even Reinhard. This magic allows him to bring down bolts of lightning from the sky, cover his weapon in an electrical charge, turn his enemies' weapons into lightning rods, or even create magnetic fields to trap a target in one place.
Optical Camouflage: By combining Yang and Wind Magics, it is possible to bend light and hide one's aura, making the user invisible. However, using this is difficult while moving, even with the Divine Dragon's body, meaning that he would have to stay still in order to use it.

Unique Spells:
Earth Brand Arts (アースブランド・アーツ, Āsu Burando Ātsu): Al can use his magic to create various constructs to aid him in battle. His most common application is by creating a prosthetic arm or weapons, but he has shown able to create things such as wings for gliding in the air. The name Earth Brand Arts is a riff on the name of Emilia's Ice Brand Arts, which was coined by Subaru.
Magia Railgun (マギア・レールガン): By working together with the controlled Volcanica, the two generate two vertical cylindrical formations coated in purple lightning, upon which they can fire a specialized bullet made of Volcanica’s scales molded into the shape of a liuyedao via earth magic. When fired, even Reinhard van Astrea cannot completely avoid damage from it. It is possible for them to fire multiple shots.

Techniques
Steel Thread Technique (鋼糸術, Kōshi-jutsu): A special shinobi technique that only Yae was able to master that utilizes steel threads carried within certain rings. Unlike Yae, who could use twenty of these rings, it took Al numerous loops just to master using even one of these rings right. After the events of Arc 9 were rewound, however, Al can no longer use this.

Other
Extensive Knowledge of Abilities: Due to having trained with Echidna, Al contains an immense level of knowledge of the abilities of others. Particularly, he has a high level of knowledge when it comes to Divine Protections and Authorities. With this knowledge, combined with the usage of his own Authority, Al is typically able to determine the abilities of other people by simple observation and testing. He was able to use his knowledge of how such abilities work to determine numerous Divine Protections held by not only people such as Manfred Madison, but even the numerous and extensive number of protections held by Reinhard. Furthermore, during a failed loop, he was able to determine how Petra Leyte's Authority of Melancholy worked simply by recalling how her ability would be in relation to "Melancholy".

Keen Strategist: Even without his Authority, Al has been shown to create extensively numerous plans in order to get his way, even making use of his Authority repeatedly until things go the direction he wants. In Arc 8, he was quick to give orders to his allies after determining the traps laid out during the early stages of the Conquest of the Undead Capital. More so than that, however, Al was even able to separate the entire Emilia Camp, using the aftermath of the Great Disaster as a way to get into everyone's heads, in preparation for his scheme in Arc 9, as well as to prepare for the eventual coming of the Sword Saint, taking even the Divine Dragon into his plot and using the mentality of the camp members to set a trap that could summon even the Witch of Envy.

Equipment
Black Helm: Al wears a black iron helmet which he received when he was at Gladiator Island Ginunhive. His helmet is a replica of a helmet once associated with the Gladiator King. The helmet was specially made, and as such, it will not rust and is exceptionally durable.
Liuyedao: Al previously owned a liuyedao, and he used it as his primary weapon. However, after tossing it to Cecilus Segmunt, who used the blade to deflect attacks from and attack Arakiya, the blade crumbled because it could not handle the Blue Lightning’s sheer power. That said, Al can create a new liuyedao via earth magic.
Poison Packet: As a way to trigger his Authority, Al keeps a poison packet in his mouth that he can smash at any time.
Al's Book of the Dead: After leaving the Pleiades Watchtower, Al kept his own Book of the Dead on hand. Any time he is forced to use his Authority, he can use it on the controlled Volcanica to give it an update of his own memories after each death. He can also use it against his enemies in an attempt to mentally attack them. Although the Arc 9 loop was undone, as he was sealed just before putting his plan into action, he presumably still has this on hand.
Steel Thread Ring: Al wielded one of Yae's steel thread rings, which allowed him to use the Steel Thread Technique. Due to the Arc 9 loop being undone, he no longer has this.
Divine Dragon's Fang: One of Volcanica's fangs, which is considerably valuable to any merchant. Al could use this to destroy certain complex mechanisms within the Kingdom of Lugunica's Prison Tower. Due to the Arc 9 loop being undone, he no longer has this.

intro: Crusch Karsten (クルシュ・カルステン) is the Matriarch of House Karsten and a candidate to become the 42nd monarch of Lugunica. She played a major role in Arc 3 and Arc 10 and a supporting role in Arc 5. She was also one of the main protagonists of The Dream the Lion King Saw.
appearance:
Crusch is described as a beautiful woman with almond-shaped amber eyes and long dark verdant-green hair that reaches down to her lower back. Even though she is a woman, she generally tends to dress as a man (or at least very formally). Unsurprisingly, her impression changes if she wears a dress and smiles.

As a child, Crusch Karsten maintained a posture that reflected both refinement and beauty. Her pale white skin and sharp eyes helped exemplify her charming looks. Crusch's long hair was tied up in a ponytail with a light-pink bow. She wore an elegant grass-green dress of fine make that complimented her appearance perfectly and a necklace of pearls. Shortly after meeting Fourier, Crusch stopped tying her hair back and began wearing more refined masculine clothing.

The formal outfit she is usually seen in consists of a deep purplish-blue long-coat trimmed in white with golden epaulettes on the shoulders, a white blouse underneath, blue trousers, black, white-laced knee-high heel boots, white gloves, and a blue cap with a single horizontal white stripe along the middle. The cuffs on her coat are burgundy red with white frills; the inside of her coat and an armband on her left arm bearing the emblem of the Karsten House are very much the same shade of red. The decorative items she wears include seven golden cross pattée–two on each cuff, four on her mid-section connected in pairs by golden aiguillettes, and one in the middle of a red flower on upper left side of her chest, also connected to the shoulders by its own aiguillette. Her long hair is often tied at the end by a single white bow.

When heading out to battle, she wears steel armor trimmed in gold, though it only covers part of her upper body, shoulders, and forearms. Along with the armor, her hair is tied into a ponytail, the gloves she wears are brown, and she bears a bright red cape. In one failed loop of Arc 3, she wears a black dress with a pink ribbon, black high heels, and a pink cover over her shoulders with black frills along its edge. Later, in the Water Plumage Inn in Arc 5, she wears a yukata, while in Arc 10, she briefly wears an overly ornate male's attire with a seemingly decorative longsword at her waist, and she gave off the impression of being born to military pedigree and that her shortcomings accentuated her handsome features.

As of Arc 5, her body was heavily infected by Capella Emerada Lugunica's cursed Dragon’s blood, leaving her skin, including on half of her face, covered in black vein-like markings. Since it seems to also have affected one of her eyes, she wears a medical eyepatch over it. After her curse was removed, however, the markings were removed and her body was emaciated, despite the daily care she had been receiving, and her left eye, which she now covers with a large eyepatch, has become draconic, colored gold with a slitted pupil, while capillary-like lights stretched beneath it.
personality:
While normally calm and serious, Crusch is honest, sincere, and righteous. Being the type of person who is destined to stand above others, she has talent and has worked hard to reach where she is now. She is already the head of her family, finishing her work better than her father. She prefers to act herself and has the pride of a warrior. Crusch is also gentle, often believing the false knowledge jokingly told to her by Ferris, and she sometimes displays an air-headed side. Like her mother Helena Karsten, she is shown to be ruthless and reckless.

From a young age, Crusch has always had an interest in weaponry, swordsmanship, and wearing men's clothing rather than women's clothing, something that left her father concerned on numerous occasions. However, before meeting Fourier and hearing his opinion, she still tried to do as her father asked and act more like a lady, wearing dresses and forgoing keeping her dagger on her person. However, after hearing his opinion, she stopped doing so, and she only rarely wore dresses again after.

Crusch is also dense toward any feelings of love above kindness, often not understanding why certain people behave a certain way, such as when she sometimes didn't understand Fourier's behavior. However, this only applies to feelings of love directed towards herself, as she has been shown to comment on the feelings of others. Because of the time she spent with Fourier, she has strong feelings concerning the Lion King, a term formerly given to the kings prior to forming the covenant with the Divine Dragon, and after his death, she felt that the Kingdom's reliance on the Dragon had gone too far, thus becoming her motivation for taking part in the Royal Selection. Likewise, because of how much influence Fourier had on her life, she could not accept the Dragon's influence as it had caused his death to be treated as if it hadn't happened, and thus, she made an oath to him after his death to do what it took to restore the nation and sever the covenant with the Dragon. Her conviction to keep her oath to Fourier was so strong that when her memories of him returned and she learned that Ferris had let the Divine Dragon Church, which worshipped that Dragon and its covenant, heal her, though she understood and was willing to take responsibility for his actions, she questioned why Ferris had betrayed the oath made to Fourier, as that was something that Crusch would never betray.

During the events of Arc 3, Crusch's memories were eaten by Lye Batenkaitos. As a result, she remembered nothing of her past and had regressed into a far shier and more reserved individual. However, hints of her former, strong-willed self remained, as shown by her choosing to maintain the anti-Witch Cult alliance with the Emilia Camp despite the dangers, though her gravitas had decreased. She also displayed an ease to get along with. Despite his reservations about her, Shorty Megan felt at ease when talking to her, and later, she was able to talk with the other members of the Royal Selection as if she were speaking to her friends. She was also simply flustered, as when Ferris teased her, she was left dumbfounded by his statement, and she asked for help from Subaru since she didn’t know how to feel about it. In Arc 5, she had even shown to put the well-being of others over herself, as seen when she pleaded with Subaru not to take her curse into himself, as the people needed him more than herself, not to mention the unknown consequences of Subaru taking her curse.

As of Arc 10, although freed of her curse, Crusch has not regained her memories. Coming to loathe the memoryless version of herself and declare it as weak, she started attempting to act as though she were her previous self. She also became more emotionally and mentally fragile due to Ferris's resignation as her knight and actions leading to her recovery, and became determined to discard her memoryless self as someone who was not her, calling it the reason she had been "abandoned". This being said, her loyalty to the Kingdom remains strong within her, as, even despite her standing as a Royal Selection candidate being effectively destroyed and her chances at winning ruined, she is still willing to stain her hands with the blood of traitors to the Kingdom, even if it means being determined that she was a traitor herself and possibly making enemies of those she had friendly relations with. That said, she still prefers to put the prioritize the lives of others when possible, is still willing to defend her friends with her own body, if necessary, as well as to genuinely ask them for assistance.

Because of her Divine Protection’s unique ability to see into the true emotions of people, she has a tendency to lean heavily on it, as it grants her knowledge that other people lack. As such, because she is willing to act on what she sees with it if necessary, this can put her in a position that can easily put her at odds with others and make enemies. This is especially the case after she was freed from her curse, her mind and emotional wreck at the time, leading to her acting immediately on the knowledge her Divine Protection gave her. Because of this, she is currently in a similar position to how Subaru was in Arc 3, suffering from knowledge that she obtained from a source that nobody else can understand, putting her at odds with a great many people all at once and appearing as though she might cry when having to face off against her friends, and making her grateful when said friend still chose to aid her despite the position he would be put in.
history:
The Dream the Lion King Saw
Crusch was born as the only daughter and heir to House Karsten, one of the most powerful noble families in the Dragon Kingdom of Lugunica, who were known as one of the king's most trusted supporters. Even as a child she was considered an oddity among the nobility for being more mature than other children her age. More so as other girls, Crusch also favored things like weapons over finery from a very early age; at a very early age, Crusch already asked her father for a crested dagger. As she grew older, Crusch would develop a preference for men's clothing, and take on more masculine pursuits like learning swordplay which earned rumors about her from other nobles. She held a strong fascination with the history of Lion Kings, which would come to serve as the basis for her radical but conflicted ideas about the Kingdom of Lugunica's present state. 

Ten days after first catching sight of Crusch, Fourier Lugunica, while looking to see her in the Royal Castle's garden, accidentally fall into the garden and alerted her of his presence for the first time. Thinking he was an assailant after the Royal Family, Crusch would pull a dagger out on him with intent to attack. After frantically clearing the misunderstanding and stopping Crusch for trying to take her own life out of shame of pointing her weapon against a member of the Royal Family, they would become good friends. It was here that Fourier would exchange an important promise with her that would influence Crusch's worldview. As Crusch revealed her thoughts regarding Lugunica's stagnation due to the Dragon's blessing, and lamented being unable to choose a life befitting of her family crest, the fang-bearing lion, because she was a woman, Fourier told her that she ought to never concede herself. Several days later, Fourier asserted that the two of them would resurrect the bond between the Lion King and his loyal retainer, which Crusch and soon Fourier laughed over. 

When she was 9 years old, disturbing rumors about House Argyle, concerning the alleged abuse and torture of Felix Argyle by his own father, Biehn Argyle, were investigated by Duke Meckart Karsten and his daughter, Crusch Karsten. The result of the investigation led to the Argyle family losing all of their territories and assets, save for one piece of uncultivated land, which effectively stripped them of their nobility. The Karsten family took Felix in after this event.

In the following years to come, Felix would establish a strong sense of loyalty and devotion towards Crusch for taking him from the hell that was his life before. Half a year after arriving at her mansion, Felix made an oath with Crusch to act like a girl and “exchange” his boyhood to her, since she sought to succeed her father and become a duke, which she did not believe she could do as a woman. While Felix began wearing girls’ clothes, Crusch wore formal men’s suits to fulfill her oath and cease acting like a woman. Sometime after their oath, Felix met Fourier Lugunica for the first time. When Fourier mistook Felix's name as Ferris, he began using that name at Crusch's suggestion. Together, Crusch, Ferris, and Fourier would get into all kinds of mischief that defined much of their friendship. Her close friendships with both Fourier and Ferris would further have a huge influence onf her and facilitate finding the balance between Crusch as a woman and Crusch as the noble she felt she needed to become in order to lead House Karsten.

On Crusch's seventeenth birthday, an incident with the Great Rabbit occurred in the Karsten lands. Her efforts and leadership there would later play a crucial role in her father passing down the position as the head of the family to her mere six months afterward. Several years later, Crusch would catch wind of trouble afoot at the House Argyle, through a report by her advisers. Not wanting this to burden Ferris who still had trauma from his time with the Argyles nor let what was happening to affect her attendant's standing among the knights in a very delicate period that would decide his future, Crusch would endeavor to take off the problem quietly herself and confer with Fourier to keep Ferris away from it.

Crusch would directly head to the Argyle estate to confront Biehn Argyle and Miles to learn the truth of the matter. After a tense conversation Crusch would fall into a trap she is drugged by the scent of odorless poison in the tea she had been given. She would find herself held in the same underground cell Ferris had lived in for years before his rescue by her. After a conversation with Biehn, Hannah Regret would later appear to loosen her manacles so she could escape when it was time. Crusch still completely unsure which side she was on would inquire about her motives and why she was betraying him. The maid would only mention that it was out of love and Crusch wouldn't understand. It was at this point Crusch noticed the similarities between the maid's appearance and Ferris, but the maid would leave before she could ask. Miles would soon visit Crusch himself intending to break her will in preparation to make off with her and Ferris later, only for Crusch to reverse the situation to his shock by cutting him and the corpse soldiers around, down. She then met up with Julius in the manor's first floor and then with a distraught and shaken Ferris. The three would escape the blazing inferno the place had become. As soon as they'd reunite with Fourier who was waiting outside the Argyle manor in his carriage, disaster would once again strike – Fourier collapsed on the floor, unable to regain his consciousness.

A month later, due to her increasing amount of workload brought about by the Royal Family being unable to fulfill their duties as they have all fallen ill and became bedridden, Crusch found some time to visit Fourier after he fell ill to the unknown disease sweeping through the palace. Eventually, one day during one her rare visits she brought Fourier out to gardens in the palace courtyard unbeknownst to her this would be the last time the two would speak. Reminiscing about the old days and reaffirming their childhood promise Fourier would die suddenly, but peacefully, while lying in Crusch's lap. During that the same day the then-current king would be the last member of the Royal Family to have succumbed ending the Lugunica line. In the emergency meeting hereafter, an emotional Crusch privately became outraged by how cavalier the royal court had treated this national tragedy moving on quickly as were a footnote compared to the loss of the contract between the Kingdom and the Divine Dragon. It was there then that the Dragon Insignia, as well as prophecy regarding the next step the country should take, was revealed. Crusch was discovered as the first of the five potential candidates deemed worthy to lead the country. Learning this with strong conviction, Crusch later returned to the garden where Fourier died with Ferris and vowed to forever sever the tie between the Divine Dragon and the Dragon Kingdom of Lugunica whose influence she became convinced had distorted the way the Kingdom of Lugunica should be.

At some point, she and Ferris witnessed an argument between Wilhelm van Astrea and Bordeaux Zergev regarding the White Whale which resulted in Wilhelm temporarily being imprisoned to cool his head. Aware of his strength and reputation, she and Ferris recruited him into her camp, offering the chance to slay the White Whale in return. The Sword Demon accepted her proposal, and during his time in the camp, he helped Crusch hone her skills with the sword.

Lugunican Papers
Sometime in the year following the Subjugation of the White Whale, Crusch was requested for an interview with Shorty Megan and Lululala regarding their stand in the Royal Selection. Though by this point she was without her memories, she still accepted the interview. She and Ferris gave their opinions on the other candidates, stating that the camp she believed people should keep their eyes on is the Emilia Camp.

At some point during this same year, her father returned to assist her in running her duchy.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
Crusch has trained herself thoroughly since her youth, and as of the present day, she is so skilled and charismatic as a warrior, a commander, and as the Duchess that she has become recognized as the Valkyrie. She was strong enough that she was able to repel the Great Rabbit shortly after she appeared, and she was able to command the force that ultimately brought down the White Whale. Even after her memories were taken, she was able to retrain herself from scratch, and after her curse was removed and her memories returned, her fierce abilities have only improved further, and her skills have been compared to other incredibly powerful and talented swordsmen of the current era.

Divine Protection
Divine Protection of Wind Reading (風見の加護 Kazemi no Kago): Crusch is able to read other people's emotions by seeing them as a physical manifestation of wind that blows out from their body. This effectively allows her to determine if she is being deceived by determining how the person she is speaking to feels as the talk, making her the equivalent of a human lie detector. Similarly, because she can determine the true emotions of the people around her through the use of this Divine Protection, it can give her a glimpse into a person’s true nature and potentially help her to weed out imposters. This being said, it is possible for people who are in a closer relationship to her to deceive her wind reading. It is implied during a conversation between Aldebaran and Reinhard van Astrea that only one person can have this Divine Protection at a time.

Physical Traits/Flow Method
Dragon Eye (龍眼, Ryūgan): After the removal of her curse, Crusch's left eye has become golden with a slitted pupil, making it reminiscent of a Dragon's. Upon using it, Crusch's vision increases dramatically, allowing her to see minute movements and react to them with significantly more efficiency. Furthermore, she can see the formation of magic, including the formation of the formula, which allows her to counter it. However, this does not allow her to see invisible attacks, such as Subaru's Invisible Providence. Likewise, Crusch will exhaust herself by using her eye, and if used excessively, it will make her lose consciousness from the strain. Even limiting its usage, it is still exhausting enough that she needs to sit down and rest.

Skilled Swordswoman: Crusch is considerably skilled at using a sword in combat, having at one point been taught by Rickert Hoffman, and combining her wind magic with it. From her youth, Crusch Karsten trained in the art of the sword. The many years of painstaking training Crusch subjected herself to transformed her into a mighty swordsman. Her skill with the blade was considerable, so much so that she bested ten bandits simultaneously with her trusty sword. Crusch's mastery surpassed that of Fourier Lugunica's, which was considered far above the swordsmanship displayed by an average young nobleman. After taking Wilhelm van Astrea under her employ, Crusch began taking lessons from him, presumably improving even further. Even after her memories were eaten, she managed to regain her skill with the sword after retraining with Wilhelm. At present, her skills with the sword remain sharp and refined, and she can fight a swordsman on the level of Tiga Rauleon to the point that he wouldn't be able to make any good moves without risking injury. When combined with her new eye, she can evade and fight significantly more efficiently, allowing her to deal with said opponent mere moments after unveiling it, though her actual physical speed does not change. Also, when assisted by her eye, she is able to cut through magic before it can even become magic by slashing through the formula, something which is claimed to be unbelievably difficult, even if one could see the formula.

Magic
Crusch has an affinity for the wind attribute, which she often combines with her swordsmanship and Divine Protection in combat.

Unique Spells:
thumb|250px|Crusch attacking the White Whale with One Blow, One Hundred Felled
One Blow, One Hundred Felled (百人一太刀 Hyakunin Hitotachi): Crusch combines her Divine Protection of Wind Reading and wind magic to unleash a sword strike that enables her to cut anything within her range of vision with an invisible blade of wind. The attack is sharp enough to slash through the White Whale’s thick hide and temporarily topple it. Though, the farther away the target is, the weaker the attack becomes. And while its range is indeed impressive, this skill truly shines in enclosed spaces, as there is less room for an opponent to dodge, and the power is stronger the closer the opponent is to Crusch when she uses it. She can use this technique with her bare hands as well and catch her enemies off guard. She can also disperse this technique in all directions, kicking up such windpower that it can easily blast away everything in the vicinity and easily lift people off their feet and slam them into the surroundings with such force that they will be knocked unconscious.

Techniques
Dead Spot (死穴): After awakening a draconic eye, Crusch is able to perceive the flow of power used in certain techniques and abilities, and by aiming at these "dead spots", she can erase them. This works even on a raging inferno that threatened to consume her and Subaru.

Curse
thumb|right|180x|Curse of the Dragon’s Blood.
Curse of the Dragon's Blood: During the Battle for Priestella, Crusch was cursed with so-called Dragon’s blood by the Sin Archbishop of Lust. While inflicted, her skin is covered in black veins across her body that causes Crusch great pain when it throbs. This curse has spread across her body and even to her face, having even affected her eye. The curse was heavily debilitating as well, damaging it and causing it to lose strength. Any other effects of the curse are presently unknown. Uniquely, her curse can be absorbed by Subaru, who bears the same curse as her; however, the amount of the curse removed from her body compared to what Subaru absorbs into his is disproportional by around ten times. Although the curse had lessened a tad thanks to Subaru’s body absorbing a small part of it, she remained bedridden until the curse was removed from her body months later. Following its removal, due to the debilitating effects it had on her body, her body was emaciated, and it remembered the intense craving for sustenance, causing her to immediately go for water to sustain herself and become desperately hostile to anyone who tried to stop her, ignoring damage done to her feet by stepping on glass.

Equipment
Sword: Crusch wields a sword which bears the lion-shaped crest of the Karsten family on its cross-guard.
Crested Dagger: In her youth, Crusch was given this dagger after he request to her father.
Poniard: During the events of Arc 10, Crusch carries a poniard, a type of dagger meant for thrusting or stabbing, in place of her missing sword for a time.
Armor: When heading out to battle, she wears steel armor trimmed in gold, though it only covers part of her upper body, shoulders, and forearms. The armor is engraved with the Divine Protection of Durability (堅固の加護, Kengo no Kago), which makes it more durable so long as Crusch's mana is not exhausted.
