intro: Anastasia Hoshin (アナスタシア・ホーシン) is the president of the Hoshin Company based in the Kararagi City-States and a candidate to become the 42nd monarch of Lugunica. She plays a major role in Arc 5, a supporting role in Arc 3, and a lesser supporting role in Arc 6 and Arc 8.
appearance:
Anastasia is a petite woman with blue green eyes and long, wavy purple hair that extends to her hips. She wears a long white dress with a fur hat (similar to the Russian Ushanka) and scarf along with a large purse shaped like a wallet. She also wears a yellow star-shaped hairpin on her hair and a small teal pendant around her neck. She is described to have cute looks and an aura similar to a small animal. Later, in the Water Plumage Inn, she wears a yukata.

During the events of Arc 8, she wore a white kimono with red internal lining, and at the ends of her sleeves and the hem of the kimono, there was a light pink design on it. She also wore sandals and carried a red parasol with tassels on the sides of it. She also had her hair tied in a side ponytail, held up by a flower hairpin, and she continued to wear her scarf.

When she first met Ricardo, Anastasia wore ragged clothes with her body covered in dirt. After Ricardo saved her from becoming a slave, he had cleaned her up and bought her a small pink and purple kimono with polka-dots and gave her a short haircut. When she was 13, she wore a white and blue kimono, but as she got older, she grew out her hair and wore a long kimono with flowers on her sleeves.
personality:
Anastasia has a crafty personality. She always puts benefitting herself first, though as a merchant, she prefers when both she and the one she negotiates with mutually benefit from transactions. Anastasia herself admits that she is greedy, and it stems from the fact that she was an orphan, and she is willing to proclaim this publicly to others, as she did during her speech at the start of the Royal Selection. She is highly realistic, always remembering her position as a candidate for the Royal Selection while speaking with other candidates, no matter how friendly or idealistic they are, and she is also bluntly honest when she needs to be, directly claiming that Emilia had no chance in the selection due to the widespread prejudice against half-elves and her appearance resembling Satella's, as well as when she told Subaru that a person's past actions will not disappear, both during the events of Arc 3 and when regarding how to deal with Spica. She is also not above manipulating people to gather information, as she did with Subaru during one failed loop when he was going through extreme anger and tunnel vision. In times of crisis, Anastasia has a tendency to act as the voice of reason and will often act as a leader, typically directing people appropriately. Likewise, she is not unwilling to work with others during such times. She also loves food like daisukiyaki and is mentioned to love liquor. Anastasia also seems to prefer being around demi-humans, fluffier ones in particular, and she speaks in a Kansai dialect.

She is ordinarily a rather wary person. Though she at first thought of Subaru as nothing more than a loud-mouthed individual due to his outburst at the Royal Selection Ceremony, after his success during the Subjugation of the White Whale and Subjugation of Sloth, she immediately looked into his history. Though she ultimately passed him off as just some lucky kid, his actions during the Battle for Priestella reignited her curiosity. Similarly, she is also rather cautious of people similar in shrewdness as herself, such as Priscilla Barielle. Though, in Priscilla's case, she also disliked her for her chaotic personality and actions and is willing to exclude her from certain gatherings precisely because of this.

Despite her faults, she is actually sympathetic and has a strong sense of duty. Although she typically does not like to show weakness and often covers up her intentions with an objectively realistic attitude that she crafted as a merchant, she is willing to act when her friends are in trouble, whether that is acting out in anger at a merchant who ripped off her knight or even crossing countries when another friend was kidnapped. In the case of the latter, she was even willing to buy the services of the strongest man in Kararagi, Halibel, to search for the friend. Likewise, although they were forced back to being rivals with her since their more recent troubles had been taken care of, when she spoke with Emilia following the Great Disaster, she was not against remaining friends with her, regardless of the outcome of the Royal Selection, and she was even willing to accept another outing with the Royal Selection candidates like what her original intentions were for meeting them in Priestella. She is also a lot more easily frustrated around certain acquaintances; when Halibel speaks to her, treating her like he used to when she was a child, she often finds herself pouting and annoyed by it. This being said, she is also afraid of losing her connections with the people around her. In particular, before Julius had his name eaten by Roy Alphard, she locked herself away in her Od and let the artificial spirit Echidna keep control of her body so that she wouldn't lose her memories of Julius. Later, though she didn't show it on her face, after Priscilla's death, she was sad about it as well.
history:
Anastasia's Rising in Life Memorial Day and Anastasia's Kararagi Merchant Path
Anastasia was an orphaned child in Kararagi who lived in the slums of Banan. Roughly 15 years before the main story, she attempted to save two fox humans from being taken into slaves. However, she nearly got taken as a slave herself, until she was saved by Ricardo. The two got to know each other, and Anastasia eventually stated that she would be the one to remove his slave collar. Ricardo later introduced her to work in a bar. Several months later, Anastasia's business talent was recognized by Chuden Agri, leading her to be taken into his company. Once Ricardo heard about this, he joined the Chuden Company and became a mercenary. He was also offered a new collar with no control crystal to signify his identity as the Hound.

Kararagi Girl Meets Cats
Several months later, Anastasia was kidnapped by a thief and was sold to the Razcrew Company. The head of the company, Didorii, planned to sell her to the slave market north of Kararagi. In the cell, Anastasia met with Mimi Pearlbaton and Hetaro Pearlbaton. She utilized their Divine Protection of Trisection to send a message to Ricardo. The message enabled him to kill Didorii and save the captives. From then on, Anastasia took an interest in the Pearlbaton siblings and frequently visited Roshi Pearlbaton, who adopted the trio, to ask for them.

Kararagi Girl & Cat's Eye
Nine years before the main story, Ricardo was visited by an old friend of his from his time as a slave by the name of Reisel, who asked for help in stealing a meteor inside a cart. They ambushed the fleet but were stopped by Shiroro Tonerico. While Ricardo was fighting with Shiroro, Reisel stole the target carriage and abandoned his old friend. However, his plan was inadvertently thwarted by Anastasia, who exchanged the carriages. In the carriage, Anastasia met an artificial spirit named Echidna, and the two formed a bond. Reisel came back to take the true cart, but he was defeated by Anastasia, Echidna, the Pearlbaton siblings, and Ricardo, who formed a ceasefire with Shiroro.

At some point after this, when Halibel was sent to slay Ricardo for breaking his oath to his fellow wolf human tribesmen, Anastasia stood between them and settled the matter, and she’s kept her connection with the Admirer ever since. Roshi also would go on to make a kamikaze attack while on a mission, blowing up with an enemy in the process. A funeral was held for him, and though Mimi appeared strong at first, cried afterwards, which only Anastasia was aware of.

Pre-Royal Selection
Eventually, she took control of the Chuden Company, purchased its parent company, the Ryuushika Commerce Company, and renamed it into the Hoshin Company, making Chuden the vice president. Anastasia sought to expand into Lugunica's market, so she decided to have talks with the Juukulius family, having met Alviero Juukulius several years prior. As the meeting began to progress towards a fruitless result for both sides, Mimi happened to find a Dragon Insignia. Anastasia told her to give it back, and she claimed it from Mimi, apologizing for the hassle after Julius told her it was a valuable artifact. However, as she held it, the insignia shone brightly. This designated her as a candidate for the Royal Selection, and after learning of its meaning, she soon set her mind on participating.

Camp Formation Stories
Anastasia and Julius went to a meeting at the Royal Castle with the knights, the noble civil servants, and the Council of Wise Men, with Crusch Karsten also in attendance. She declared her intent to participate in the Royal Selection, and Julius explained how she was discovered as a candidate. Bordeaux Zergev lashed out at Julius for bringing a foreigner into the mix, but Miklotov McMahon reprimanded him, causing him to back down. Anastasia agreed to sign a non-disclosure contract and proved her candidacy to the audience by making the Dragon Jewel shine. Following the meeting, Crusch spoke with Anastasia and recognized her as a rival for the throne. Afterwards, Julius and Reinhard van Astrea went to Conwood Melahau's tavern, the Silver Shield, where he requested the Sword Saint to become Anastasia's knight. That night, Julius returned to his mansion and spoke with Anastasia again, and upon learning of his request to Reinhard from him, she immediately became upset and said she would return to her home country, quickly leaving the mansion.

Julius was troubled and did not realize the mistake he had made, but after receiving encouragement from Joshua, who said the Kingdom's number one knight was the Finest of Knights and that Anastasia needed the best knight, even if it meant that House Juukulius would face opposition for supporting a foreigner, he resolved himself to meet her. At an inn, Anastasia told Ricardo and the triplets to not allow anyone through to her. Julius encountered them and fought with Ricardo without a sword, easily beating him, although he had not been in top condition because he had been drinking. Julius then spoke to Anastasia through her door, retracting his request to Reinhard and offering his services instead, after which she opened the door and they performed the ritual of knighting, and in the end, the Finest of Knights became the merchant's knight. Anastasia and Echidna spoke once he left, with the former telling the latter that she would show her the end destination of her greed.

Lugunican Papers
In the year following the Subjugation of the White Whale, she was requested an interview by Shorty Megan and Lululala. Already having a meeting with her rival and fellow candidate Priscilla Barielle, she decided to schedule the interview on the same day. There, they discussed their opinions on the Royal Selection and the other candidates. In particular, both Anastasia and Priscilla claimed that Emilia didn’t stand a chance, as public discrimination against her was heavy as she was a perfect resemblance and of the same race as the Witch of Envy. Even with the slaying of the White Whale and the Sin Archbishop of Sloth under her belt, they claimed that it was an achievement the reflected more on her knight than her, which even Julius agreed with, though Priscilla’s knight Al argued that his achievements also reflect on her. Eventually, the interview came to a close.

Riot in Flanders
Toward the end of the incident in Flanders, the Anastasia Camp came across Mozolite and helped to put end to the incident. There, she met Felt, and the two became friendly with each other.

Joshua Juukulius's Careful Encyclopedia
Deciding to directly ask Anastasia her intentions of sending him to act as the Emilia Camp's messenger to invite them to Priestella, Joshua Juukulius shared the thoughts about them that had been worrying him with her and asked her outright. Though she said that Emilia and Subaru wouldn't be scary, she had called for Julius and told him that Joshua was worried about coming off as rude toward the members of the Emilia Camp, which Julius agreed with since he said that they were nothing like the rumors claimed them to be. However, he also said to watch out for Subaru, who was more than what he seemed, was very loyal and determined, and had earned his position as her knight as a spiritual arts user himself. After a moment of silence, Joshua thanked Julius for sharing that with him, knew to be wary if Subaru, and left the room, leaving Julius and Anastasia to speak with each other.

Anastasia's Companion Searching Chronicle
Following the events of the Pleiades Watchtower Expedition, Anastasia, alongside Julius and Echidna, after leaving the sealed Roy Alphard with the Lugunican government to be imprisoned within the Prison Tower, intending to search for Subaru and Rem, who had been taken by a shadow, decided to enter the Sacred Vollachia Empire via Kararagi through official channels. Upon returning to the City-States, after meeting with the League of Cities and reuniting with Halibel, they learned of a startling incident in Nanou in which the living had been replaced by the undead. Believing the situation might be involved in their goal, Anastasia hired Halibel to accompany her to Vollachia, where, along the way, he explained to Julius the reason for his acquaintance with Anastasia and Ricardo.

Kararagi Reaper Incident
Shortly after the events of the Great Disaster, Anastasia, accompanied by Julius, Halibel, and Echidna, returned to Kararagi, where they decided to report their discoveries to the mayor of the Third City Ivada, Orgo Hayata. Unfortunately, there was yet another problem: the windstorm created by the Slasher, Zarestia, that was thrust upon Banan. After learning of this, she, Echidna, Julius, and Halibel made their way to Banan to meet up with Ricardo. Sometime after Ricardo quelled Zarestia's rage, Anastasia's group arrived and were led to the holding cells in Riften Magoji's mansion, where Zarestia was being held. During their conversation, Anastasia learned that Riften went missing, Julius noticed that Zarestia was a Great Spirit and introduced himself, and Halibel unintentionally riled her up by noticing her strange constitution, that something was missing. However, when Anastasia mentioned Zarestia being responsible for other such town-destroying wind cataclysms, Zarestia declared otherwise, saying that she only rampaged in Banan. Shortly afterward, this is confirmed when a massive tornado appeared outside of Banan, not made by Zarestia. After giving her orders and securing Zarestia's assistance, the group made their way to stop the tornado.

After leaving Riften’s mansion, Anastasia’s group and Zarestia managed to quell the winds. However, in the process, Anastasia and Echidna were kidnapped. When Anastasia later woke up, she found herself in Zarestia’s Bed, and Echidna had left her side to ensure her safety, as she was the main target behind their enemy’s actions. Anastasia spoke with said enemy, a woman identical to Zarestia who she referred to as Black Tia, and after a one-sided conversation, Anastasia promised to help Black Tia, as otherwise, everyone who would come to find Anastasia, Black Tia, and Anastasia herself would find themselves likely killing each other. Not long after, Echidna appeared after realizing Anastasia would be safe, and despite her concerns, Anastasia convinced her that everything would be fine.

A full day after being taken, she and Echidna were brought back to Banan by Black Tia, and shortly after, likely due to her exhaustion catching up with her, Anastasia passed out with a fever. Though Julius tended to her and attempted to help heal her with his spirits, he was unable and settled for practicing with Halibel to become stronger. At some point, Anastasia woke up from the sound of clashing steel to find Zarestia waiting for her. Zarestia, who wanted to talk with Anastasia about Black Tia, told her that Black Tia was currently in a cell and that her attitude and speech were due to the Light Sphere's influence on her. Afterward, Anastasia asked Zarestia to gather the others.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
Anastasia has at one point been claimed to be among the five weakest characters in the series. She has effectively no skills for combat, and because of a defect with her gate, she cannot use magic either. However, she more than makes up for her lack of combat prowess with her business-oriented mind and leadership skills. It is because of this that she has been entrusted with leading important businesses and why she has yet to face any true setback in the Royal Selection since its start, unlike each of the other camps.

Intelligence
Keen Intellect: Anastasia is a commercial genius who serves as chairwoman of the Hoshin Company, the most influential company in Kararagi. For many years, this position in her nation was occupied by the Ryuushika Commerce Company, but thanks to Anastasia’s personal commercial genius, it was reconstituted under a new name, the Hoshin Company. She has also shown to be quite the tactician. During the Battle for Priestella, she, alongside Subaru, acted as generals in the fight against the Witch Cult, and they were actively coming up with methods to counter them together.

Skilled Businesswoman: Anastasia is extremely skilled at business, having worked her way up from nothing to being the president of a prominent company. Her skill is mentioned to be natural, and it is because of her business acumen that she is capable of cornering other people in negotiations, whether they are other business leaders, merchants, or otherwise.

Magic
Anastasia has an affinity for the yang attribute, but she unfortunately has no aptitude for it. This being said, though not actually contracted with the artificial spirit Echidna, she and Anastasia share good compatibility with each other. Because of their connection, Echidna can take possession of Anastasia's body at times and use her Od to cast spells.

Defective Gate: According to the artificial spirit Echidna, Anastasia's gate is unable to absorb mana from the atmosphere properly, causing her to be chronically mana deficient. When Echidna takes over her body and uses her Od to cast magic with, this ultimately causes extreme strain on her body due to the backlash, and she is likely to lose consciousness.

Other
Iron Fang (鉄の牙 Tetsu no Kiba): Anastasia owns the mercenary group Iron Fang, and she often uses them for numerous tasks of labor.

Equipment
Knife: During the Pleiades Watchtower Expedition, Anastasia is shown to have a thick knife as a means to defend herself. However, as it is mentioned that the knife was part of their emergency bag and that her artificial spirit was possessing her, it is unknown if she normally uses any weapon at all.
Conversation Mirrors: Following the successful Subjugation of Sloth, the Iron Fang brought with them a set of Conversation Mirrors. During the Battle for Priestella, she brought them out to share with her allies during the crisis to keep in contact with them.

alias: Sin Archbishop of Lust (色欲の大罪司教, Shikiyoku no Daizai Shikyō) ; Lust (色欲, Shikiyoku) ; Mother (母, Haha)

occupation: Sin Archbishop of Lust ; Mother of the Beloved Children
intro: Capella Emerada Lugunica (カペラ・エメラダ・ルグニカ) is a Sin Archbishop of the Witch Cult, representing Lust. She is also known as Mama, the individual responsible for assembling and leading the Beloved Children. Due to Capella's control over her collective "children", including Elsa and Meili, she can be noted as a minor overarching antagonist in Arc 1, Arc 2, and Arc 4, while she is one of the main antagonists of Arc 5.
appearance:
Because of her Authority, Capella's actual form is unknown, though she has transformed into a giant black dragon with golden horns, a small girl, a well-endowed woman, an honest looking village girl, a multitude of field mice, and an innocent looking young girl with a lewd smile.

In her most common form, Capella has short golden hair with a string of hair down her right and a rose attached at the end of it. She wears revealing clothes, hot pants, leggings, a bikini and nothing more. She also has a yaeba that becomes prominent when she laughs. This form also has a great resemblance to other members of the Royal Family of the Dragon Kingdom of Lugunica. Lastly, just above her waist, two larger circular appendages can be seen sprouting out of her body. According to the series' main illustrator Shin'ichirō Ōtsuka's notes featured in Volume 17's additional illustrations page, those appendages help Capella adjust her mass when she's transforming, as well as to make it look as though her entire body were made of liquid metal.
personality:
Capella is considered to have the worst personality among the Sin Archbishops. She speaks in a way that sounds like she spits and tramples on courtesy while having a cruel personality to boot. She will actively mock everyone and laugh at them, even going so far to use a city's broadcasting equipment to ensure that her voice reaches everyone in said city. She claims that all the love and respect in the world exists to be monopolized by her. Even among the Sin Archbishops famed for their vulgar personalities and irredeemable actions, Capella is considered a special brand of evil. She views people other than herself as mere bags of meat meant to operate as she deems fit. As she sees those around her as little more than animals, she cares not for the opinions and feelings of others nor whether or not her actions cause pain and suffering. She also revels in the pain of others, often cackling whilst bringing torment to other people, lacking any regard to their lives. She plays with the dignity and values of other people by changing their appearances, spitting her brand of ridicule upon those who don't share all of her ideals, and has no qualms toying with corpses to create demi-beasts. Her ridicule extends to her fellow Sin Archbishops, often referring to them with extremely degrading and vulgar titles rather than their actual names.

Capella presents excessive pride in regard to herself, often citing herself as a kind woman whose beauty is compared to none, and befitting her title as the bearer of the Witch Factor of Lust, Capella is obsessed with the concept of love and feels a great urge for every single person in the world to love her. Although, like everything about the Archbishop, Capella's idea of love is severely warped. She is considered "completely loose", takes the stance that all of humanity loves her and looks down on everyone from above, and is uninterested in the concept of couples and lovers. Her point of view regarding love is that it is derived from one's physical appearance, and she is willing to completely disregard a person's outward appearance, including her own, and transform others to degrading or downright disgusting forms, while she will transform herself to take on the person's most desired type to make them hers, claiming that all she has to do is transform into a person's favorite form, and then they'd always love her. She would even go as far as restoring a blind person's sight and forcing them to love her, or even transform herself into something as unsightly as a fly to do so, as she is a person who would "go through any lengths". Furthermore, she heavily believes that the personality has nothing to do with falling in love, and she would toy with people who love each other by transforming into each other and interacting with them while claiming that they weren't "seeing what's inside". In the event that she meets someone who will not love her, she will become hostile and transform said person into bugs or something similar.

Despite her point of view on love and her overwhelming desire for everyone in the world to love her, Capella is afflicted with trauma, and according to the author, claiming to like Capella "just the ways she is" is considered a landmine that could result in the person saying it being killed, implying that she has an extreme aversion to her actual self. This being said, it is unclear what this aversion is specifically.

Under the moniker of Mama, Capella spends her days gathering brilliant and extraordinarily eccentric individuals who she refers to as her children, using them as underlings for her own benefits and goals. She actively uses her Authority to instill fear into her "children", forces them to call her their mother after thoroughly frightening and traumatizing them, and making them act as "siblings" or the like, effectively mocking the entire concept of family in the process. According to both Elsa and Meili, Mama is extremely cruel and unforgiving, as even the slightest mistake might result in harsh punishments, such as being temporarily morphed into countless frogs, being slaughtered, or simply getting turned into a shapeless pile of meat for all eternity. According to Capella, her children are individuals who will devote their bodies and souls to make her wishes come true and give her gifts beyond her wildest dreams, no matter the cost. By doing so, they will express their unbounded love for Capella, something she cherishes more than anything else in the world.
history:
Currently, little is actually known about Capella's past, as her background is surrounded in mystery including how and when she became the Sin Archbishop of Lust. That being said, the author did once hint that Capella is hiding away deep trauma. However, it is known that she has been active for at least thirty years, having been collecting talented people to be a part of her Beloved Children, and over the course of those three decades, she has been silently at war with the Six Tongues as she slowly but certainly replaced certain important members of the government with her own people.

At an unknown point in time, Capella destroyed the Kararagian village that was being resided by Reize and her mother, leaving Reize as the only survivor. It is unclear what her goal in doing so was.

Nine years before Natsuki Subaru's summoning, Capella tasked a former slave named Reisel with retrieving an object relating to the legacy of the Witches. The object in question was a foxlike artificial spirit created by the Witch of Greed roughly four centuries prior. In order to help him complete his mission, Capella loaned him a magical artifact that would allow him to manipulate shadows in certain ways. However, Reisel's mission was ultimately thwarted, and he was forced to destroy the artifact that Capella had given to him. Mama, in her usual ruthless fashion, decided to punish her failure of a subordinate, pruning him and turning him into a pile of meat without any shape or form.

At some point in time, she tasked another one of her children, Sithonia, to retrieve a perfected curse doll for her. To this end, Sithonia infiltrated the Featherrun Sisters under Holosseo Featherrun and became a curse doll. Following Holosseo's death, she attempted to kill Elsa, intending to use the power of a perfected curse doll to betray Capella, but ultimately lost her life to her “sister”. When Elsa departed from the Featherrun mansion, Capella intercepted her, revealing what she truly desired was love from someone who could devote themselves to her. Threatening Elsa with the lives of Ornea Featherrun and Oliver Zeppes, Capella successfully managed to acquire her as a new “child”. Some years later, Elsa brought Meili Portroute to Capella, and she paired the two of them together. It is also implied that Roy Alphard, one of the Sin Archbishops of Gluttony, also became one of her children, as he refers to her by the name Mama.

Later, after Elsa was hired during the events of Arc 1, Capella gave them another task, which Meili took on by herself, leading to the events of Arc 2. Yet again, when Elsa was hired in Arc 4, Meili accompanied her despite not being hired by Roswaal, indicating that someone else had been involved with the attack on the mansion. Two months later, after Subaru led the successful subjugations that resulted in the deaths of the White Whale and Petelgeuse Romanée-Conti, Capella began to panic, allowing two of her Beloved Children to defect and join the Six Tongues, which allowed them to prevent more of her plans from coming to fruition. Because of this, Capella orchestrated the Battle for Priestella, where she intended to reveal her face, name, and Authority for the first time in order to combat the Six Tongues and speed up her plans.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
Although the full extent of her power is unclear, Capella is an incredibly dangerous individual, capable of easily defeating the likes of someone like Crusch Karsten and keeping her bedridden for months. However, what makes her the most dangerous is her tactical prowess and mind, exhibiting a kind of intelligence unseen by other Witch Cultists. Most notably, she is the only Sin Archbishop still currently active, and she was the only one who managed to escape the backlash of the Battle for Priestella with little true harm done to her.

Authority

Transmutation and Transfiguration (変異・変貌, Hen'i Henbō): Capella is the current wielder of the Witch Factor of Lust. She is shown to able to use its respective Authority to transmute her body and the bodies of others down to the very cores, allowing her to turn any living thing into whatever form she desires.
Self-Shapeshifting: The most commonly seen use of her Authority, Capella is capable of turning her entire body, or even part of her body, into the forms of others. In combat, she has a tendency to turn her limbs into the body parts of beasts, such as a lion's head, or she can turn herself into a strong black dragon that is roughly the size of Priestella's City Hall. She can also use this ability to turn her body into numerous smaller creatures, such as rats, allowing her to escape most methods of confining her. Beyond that, she can transform her physical appearance to look like other people, as well her voice and even her gate; it is unknown if she can affect the Od. This gives her the ability to torment others by changing her physical appearance to someone they love or adore or give her the potential to be a master of escape, infiltration, and subterfuge.
Regeneration: thumb|right|250px|Capella restoring her whole body from just her head. This ability can also be used as a way of healing herself by transforming damaged parts into uninjured parts, with Al mentioning that Capella was able to heal after he "cut her head off and crushed her heart", and any spare parts generated through healing dissolve on their own.
Black Flames: In her dragon transformation, Capella is capable of producing powerful jet-black flames that consume everything and cannot be put out by water.
Dragon's Blood (龍の血, Ryū no Chi): thumb|right|250px|Capella infecting Crusch Karsten with her Dragon's Blood. Capella possesses unique blood, which is, according to her, mixed with Dragon's Blood, which contains a great curse. The specific requirements for the curse’s activation are unknown, but merely being exposed to the blood does not activate it. It is unknown whether the Dragon's Blood that runs through her veins is the same blood that's stored away in the Royal Castle. She is able to curse people with it, covering her targets with black veins and making them sick, as shown when she infected Crusch. However, different people react differently after being exposed to the blood. Some fall ill, like Crusch, while others appear to have a symbiotic relationship with the blood's curse, like Subaru.
Storage: Capella is capable of carrying objects within her body, and by transforming her flesh, she can retrieve such objects. Any limits to this ability are unknown as she has only shown to carry her Gospel in this way.
Battle Form: According to the author, Capella has a yet-unseen “battle form” she uses for combat.
thumb|right|250px|Capella transforming Meili into a Zodda Bug.
Shapeshifting of Others: Capella can also apply her power to any living thing within her reach. She has repeatedly shown to have transformed others into various animals such as flies, frogs, birds, beasts, or even into unrecognizable lumps of flesh without any of the five senses or self-awareness by simply touching them with her hand. It is worth noting that when she transforms a single person into a group of animals, their consciousness splits and every animal shares the same mind.
Demi-Beasts (亜獣, Ajū): Capella’s Authority itself is not limited to just transmuting and transfiguring living organisms, but also corpses. Using dead bodies, Capella is able to create any number of strange organisms that are a cross between flesh and inorganic objects, with weapons like axes or spears protruding from their bodies. She has primarily used them as shock trooper fodder for one of her operations.

Intelligence
Keen Intellect: Unlike the other Sin Archbishops and despite her vulgar speech, Capella is a rather intelligent person. She managed to successfully trick several powerful and intelligent fighters in each appearance she’s made, utilizing her transformed victims and turning herself into what appears to be a helpless child in order to catch her enemies off guard. She even predicts how her enemy will move and will target them where they are at their weakest, as she displayed multiple times in the Battle for Priestella. Her strategies are so effective that she has successfully evaded the clutches of the Six Tongues for thirty years, and she has even led them around by the nose several times.

Keen Observation: Capella’s observational skills are rather exceptional. By combining her behavior with the transformation ability of her Authority, she can draw out different reactions, minute and large, and use them to determine a person’s likes or dislikes in regard to other people. By doing so, she can slowly and surely transform herself into the preferences of the other person, using said appearance and voice to agitate or anger her opponents. She has done this to transform into both Emilia and Priscilla Barielle to agitate both Subaru and Aldebaran, despite having never met either of the former two.

Other
Beloved Children (愛し子, Itoshigo): Capella has taken in numerous people from various parts of the world to serve her, and she refers to them as her children, while they recognize her only as “Mother” or “Mama”. Their duties span from retrieving certain items, such as a legacy of a Witch, to assassination jobs, to infiltration, among other tasks she may have for them.

Equipment
thumb|right|250px|Capella's Gospel.
Gospel (福音): As a member of the Witch Cult, Capella is the owner of a copy of a Gospel. Each Gospel was a replica of the Book of Wisdom, a book that had been in the possession of the Witch of Greed Echidna. The Book of Wisdom would provide exact details of future events concerning the Witch of Greed, essentially bestowing Echidna with a form of precognition. Unlike the original Book of Wisdom, the Gospels of the Witch Cult were imperfect replicas, meaning that, although they detailed the future of its owner, the events conveyed were subject to change and the information provided was often up for interpretation. The Gospels took the form of small black books that could only be read by their owners.
Conversation Mirror: A meteor that allows the user to get in contact with people who hold other such mirrors.

intro: Carmilla (カーミラ) was the Witch of Lust. She formally debuted in Arc 4 as a supporting character.
appearance:
Carmilla had round red downcast eyes and long pale-pink hair that was parted down the middle and tied into loose asymmetrical bunches falling down the front of her shoulders that went all the way to her hips. As a reflection of her personality, the Witch of Lust's physical demeanor more commonly than not conveyed meekness. Her face looked very refined, and, as opposed to being a standout beauty, Carmilla's charm was derived more so from how abnormally adorable people found her. Although her physique was well-hidden by her clothing, Carmilla was known to have a shapely figure with surprisingly large breasts.

Carmilla, who was averse to exposing her skin, would often resort to wearing baggy clothes that hid her generous physique. Her ensemble consisted of a dark-red dress that reached down to her ankles and had diamond patterns on the bottom, a pair of light-brown boots, a long snow-white coat with a pink collar that covered her dress and reached slightly lower down than it, and an exceedingly long light-green muffler that trailed along the ground behind Carmilla. Overall, the only parts of the Witch of Lust's body that were exposed were her head and her hands.
personality:
Carmilla had extremely low self-confidence, often having downcast eyes and overall acted very timid. She tended to stutter and question her own words, more often than not irritating other people by doing so. She spoke in a very polite manner, trying not to cause any disagreements or disapproval. At times, she acts submissively when dealing with her fellow Witches of Sin, as seen when she had no problem in taking part of Echidna's scheme to lure Natsuki Subaru into the Castle of Dreams, despite knowing it would end badly for her. Due to her timid personality and low self-confidence, she was frequently seen shying away from stern gazes, often pleading people not to hit her or exercise any form of violence towards her.

Despite being the Witch of Lust, Carmilla felt no desire to love others or be loved by others due to a traumatic experience she suffered during her life. Ironically, while Carmilla felt love was an important concept in the world and could transform into whomever their target desired to see most with her Authority of Lust, her feelings of love extended to no person other than herself. As her personality trait of meekness was separate from her trait of combativeness, she bore deep grudges and hatred for anyone who took actions to oppose her or whom she perceived as being against her, accordingly viewing them as unforgivable by her own admission, having the willingness to show no mercy to anyone who dared make an enemy of her. Her declarations of enmity to those who elicited her ill will or her assertions of her views were uncompromising.
history:
A long time ago, Carmilla was a normal girl who lived in a village of a small country 400 years ago. She was loved by the people in her village and even had a fiancé. However, one day a man of power came to the village and desired her. Angered by the man's actions, the villagers rose up in defiance and fought against him, eventually burning him with his mansion. The cities and villages around theirs began to regard them as dangerous, causing the fighting to spread, and soon their force was toppling countries, all the while claiming that it was for her sake. Carmilla began to be regarded as a heavenly maiden, nevertheless, she didn't desire such a thing and saw that they were being misled by their own fantasies and manipulated by their ideals. After they had toppled a large country, her fiancé proposed to her at the top of the castle, though she ignored him and left everything behind, despairing that what she had originally wanted no longer existed.

According to Echidna, Carmilla granted emotions to non-human beings in an attempt to fill the world with love. At some point in time, she burned to death. Like with the other Witches of Sin, Echidna located her soul and collected it, allowing Carmilla to manifest in the Castle of Dreams, alongside her deceased friends.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
Although she is one of the weaker Witches of Sin, Carmilla is still quite powerful, supposedly being capable of just barely defeating the next wielder of her Witch Factor, Capella Emerada Lugunica. Likewise, she is incredibly dangerous just by simply existing, having unintentionally caused wars and ending countries due to the effects of her Authority.

Authority
As the Witch of Lust, Carmilla was a user of the Authority of Lust (色欲の権能, Shikiyoku no Ken'nō) and was a compatible holder of its corresponding Witch Factor.

Faceless Bride (無貌の花嫁, Mukao no Hanayome): Carmilla's Authority grants her abilities that relate to captivating others, altering her appearance, and create empathic understanding between people.
Lethal Captivation: Her Authority gives her abilities that can captivate the people around her, making them so absorbed in watching her that they forget how to breathe, lose all sense of awareness to the point they wouldn't notice if someone stabbed them or if they were burning and in the vast majority of cases, and eventually, their hearts would stop beating, effectively killing them without them being aware of it.
Illusions: She can cause people to see and hear her as what they want to see and hear, such as when Subaru saw and heard her as Rem. 
Empathic Understanding: She seems to be capable of making people "understand feelings" like love, as seen in the Witch's Tea Party when she used her Authority of Lust to help Subaru understand Satella's love for him.

intro: Bordeaux Zergev (ボルドー・ツェルゲフ) is a member of the Council of Wise Men and the former Commander of the Zergev Squadron. He played a supporting role in the Sword Demon Trilogy and The Travelogue of the Finest. He also plays a role in Arc 10.
appearance: Bordeaux is an old bald man with wrinkles and big blue eyebrows. He wears a purple outfit used by the Council of Wise Men with a long coat. Four decades before the start of the main story, Bordeaux was a tall, muscular, and somewhat frightening man, usually donned in heavy iron armor. He had short, spiky light blue hair, and equally thick, blue eyebrows. His eyes radiated a strong fighting spirit.
personality: He is an honest, frank, and direct sage who does not hesitate to speak his mind. According to Marcos Gildark, he is well known for his demi-human prejudice in the Royal Capital. In his younger days during the war when he was the captain of the Zergev Squadron, he was a far more jovial person and did not have such a negative view of demi-humans. However, this changed when a close friend of his, Pivot Arnancy, was killed during the Demi-Human War. This changed his life, eroding away much of the once free-spirited man and replacing him with a much warier and sterner figure. Now heavily part of the country's politics, he is much more stubborn and is staunchly prejudiced against demi-humans.
history:
Sword Demon Love Song
Following the Battle of Castour Field, Bordeaux and Pivot decided to meet Wilhelm, and afterward, Bordeaux and Wilhelm had a few matches. After a few matches with Bordeaux, in which most of the wins went to Wilhelm, the two informed him that he and Grimm Fauzen were both chosen as part of the Zergev Squadron, to which Wilhelm warned that the previous units he was with were both completely annihilated, though neither man seemed to mind. With the great defeat at Castour Field, the Kingdom decided to call in the magic specialist Roswaal J. Mathers to analyze the magic circles used. Eventually, they arrived at Castour Field, where they officially met Roswaal and her bodyguard Carol Remendis. After once again getting into an argument with him, Wilhelm, Grimm, and a few other members of the squadron moved on as a group to the magic circle. Along the way, they ended up fighting a bunch of the undead that were risen by Sphinx. Afterward, meeting up with the Wilhelm's group, Roswaal relayed Sphinx's identity and the threat she bore. Later, he, Grimm, Roswaal, Wilhelm, and Pivot all reported to the Kingdom's officials, including Miklotov McMahon, about the threat.

For 3 years, he and the other members of the Zergev Squadron, and often Roswaal and Carol, were sent to some of the most dangerous and brutal battles of the war, both losing some of the original members of the Squadron and obtaining new members, pushing their numbers upwards of 100. Before long, their sights were set on Aihiya Swamp, where both Valga, Libre Fermi, and possibly Sphinx were supposed to be. Soon, everyone met their new commander, Leip Barielle, who struck Wilhelm for being disrespectful. With Roswaal pacifying him, they and Carol walked away. Despite the others' worry, Wilhelm turned their concerns away, and soon conversation turned to Grimm, who he teased, and his gift from Carol, where he showed the locket had contained a flower that Carol's master had given her.

During the Battle of Aihiya Swamp, Bordeaux fought alongside the rest of the Zergev Squadron as the fighting progressed, soon deciding to move toward the center of the fighting to remove the root of the war itself. There, they came across Libre, who challenged Wilhelm to a duel. Although putting up a good fight, Libre was able to corner Wilhelm and push him back, and in response, Grimm, Bordeaux, and Pivot surrounded Libre to cut him off. However, they were all put under the effects of a wide spanning magic circle, left at the mercy of the demi-humans. With Libre pointing his blade at Bordeaux, Wilhelm attempted to fight him off, only for Libre to nearly kill him. Pivot, instead, jumped in the way of his blade, and as he lay on the ground, he yelled at everyone not to let Wilhelm die, rousing them to take arms against Libre. However, they were all nearly slaughtered, and Grimm, who was able to defend himself for longer than the others, sustained a wound to his throat. Before he could be finished off, Wilhelm pounced Libre and fell into away from the others. Meanwhile, Pivot died in Bordeaux's arms, only to be revived as an undead and attempt to strangle Bordeaux. The barely conscious Grimm managed to push him off and gave Bordeaux a chance to put him to rest. Afterward, while laughing, crying, and cursing the Witch, Bordeaux fought and killed his undead subordinates. Following the battle, he was one of the people who wanted to see the demi-humans slaughtered.

As the military was being reorganized, Bordeaux found himself increasingly busy. Although at one point he got the chance to visit Grimm in the Royal Treatment Center, it was a short visit. He also made sure to warn Wilhelm about going out and about to be prepared in case the demi-humans decided to attack. Before long, uprisings began, and the rebuilt Zergev Squadron began to move. With Wilhelm realizing that the target was the castle, everyone left for it, and with Roswaal's and Carol's assistance, the managed to enter. Inside, Bordeaux left for the audience room while the others made for the chapel. In the audience room, he encountered the undead Libre and battled him, ultimately defeating him. Falling through the floor that had been damaged by a battle beneath him, they came across Bordeaux's allies, and Libre cut off Sphinx's other arm, forcing her to retreat after Libre disintegrated. Leaving Roswaal to chase after her, the others went to assist Wilhelm, who eventually defeated Valga.

Over the following year, Wilhelm became much friendlier with the rest of the squad, leaving Bordeaux proud of him. However, when Wilhelm went to defend his lands during the Battle of the Trias Domain, Bordeaux, Theresia van Astrea, and the rest of the Zergev Squadron went to go save him. After this, Wilhelm was not seen with the army until after the Demi-Human War was over. During the ceremony to award the Sword Saint, Bordeaux attended and bore witness to the battle between Wilhelm and Theresia, and after witnessing his victory and his kissing Theresia, he and the other members of the Zergev Squadron reunited with him.

Sword Demon Love Story
After Wilhelm was released from the Prison Tower and met with Theresia's group, Wilhelm spoke with Bordeaux about rejoining the military, which Bordeaux claimed would be difficult due to having gone AWOL for two years and interrupting an important ceremony afterward. Later, Bordeaux took part in a battle against Wilhelm alongside the rest of the Zergev Squadron in order for him to allow Theresia to retire from the military. Though he was the last man standing, Bordeaux ultimately lost, and he listened as Wilhelm and Theresia became engaged. In the following three months, he was promoted, leaving Wilhelm to become his replacement as commander of the Zergev Squadron. He was also recommended by Wilhelm to free Orphe and use his skills, an action that would later give rise to the Six Tongues organization. One day, he was asked by Theresia to look into the person abusing their authority to move the Zergev Squadron around despite the date of the wedding being so close, and he later informed her that in was her father's doing. A few days later, he informed her of the squad's return, and he was one of the many attendees who watched the two marry.

Sword Demon Battle Ballad
Years later, he participated in the events against Stride Vollachia. After their triumph, Bordeaux retired from the army and stepped into the political world. He also became a teacher of some kind and had several students, including Marcos Gildark and Heinkel Astrea.

Stories of the Great Crusch-sama Opening, Blue's Studies
During Ferris's magic training days in the Royal Capital, Bordeaux did not like Ferris' presence in the training grounds initially, even suggesting to Fourier Lugunica to cut ties with the demi-human from the Argyles. Fourier took this opportunity to impose himself to Bordeaux, saying that he would choose those he would have ties with by himself and that Bordeaux should let go of his demi-human prejudice.
abilities_text:
Military Prowess: In his younger days, Bordeaux was one of the strongest knights of the Dragon Kingdom of Lugunica, leading an elite squad named Zergev Squadron, acting as its commander until he gave the command to Wilhelm van Astrea in the months following the end of the Demi-Human War. Throughout the final two years of the war, Bordeaux led the squadron into numerous battles, even acting as the Sword Saint's support. His achievements with the squad eventually led them to becoming the most elite unit within the Kingdom's military.

Equipment: Bordeaux's weapon of choice in his youth was a halberd.

intro: Archi Elior (アーチ・エリオール) was an elf who inhabited the Elf Village and was slated to be the next guardian of Elior Forest. Though a minor character overall, he had some prominence in Emilia's backstory.
appearance: Archi has long blonde hair which he ties in two tails and has light green eyes, and, as an Elf, he has pointy ears. He wears white and purple clothes with purple lines similar to Fortuna and Emilia's own.
personality: Archi was absolutely loyal towards his superior, Fortuna. In addition to that, he was friendly towards Emilia as he claimed it wasn't her fault for the attack when she blamed herself.
history:
Archi was an elf living within the Great Elior Forest who, along with his fellow forest dwellers, protected a mysterious seal and a half-elf child named Emilia who could unlock it. Despite his youth, Archi was a strong warrior proficient in magic who was slated to become the Guardian of Elior Forest once the elven woman Fortuna retired. A kind young man, Archi cared deeply for Emilia and her adoptive mother, Fortuna.

Unfortunately, the radical faction of Witch Cult led by the Sin Archbishop of Greed, Regulus Corneas, and the Witch of Vainglory, Pandora, attacked the elven settlement in an attempt to seize Emilia and unlock the mysterious seal. Emilia was entrusted to Archi by Fortuna who named him the new Guardian and instructed him to flee the forest with the child. Although apprehensive, Archi agreed and made for the exit.

Archi's life was cut short when the plague-bringing witchbeast, the Black Serpent, intercepted the pair as they tried to escape. stayed behind and valiantly sacrificed himself so that Emilia could escape the forest and live happily. His kindness and strength of will earned him a permanent place in Emilia's heart as she remembered him later in her life.
abilities_text:
Magic (魔法, Mahō): Archi was capable of using magic. He has shown to be able to use Wind Magic and either Fire or Water Magic.
Fura (フーラ): One wind magic spell Archi was capable of using was Fura, which allowed its user to project a swift blade of concentrated wind that was deadly enough to slice through flesh and bone. He demonstrated his use of Fura when he sliced off his own leg in an attempt to prevent the spread of the Black Serpent's venom through his body.
Huma (ヒューマ): Using fire or water magic, Archi had the capability to rapidly cool the air around him to the point that he could conjure ice out of thin air. The simplest variant of this technique, which Archi could use, was called Huma. The future Guardian exhibited use of Huma when he cauterized his own leg with a block of ice after he sliced it off with wind magic to stop the Black Serpent's venom.

intro: Biehn Argyle (ビーン・アーガイル) was the former head of House Argyle and Ferris's father. He played an antagonistic role in The Dream the Lion King Saw. Originally the head of the noble House Argyle, following his mistreatment of his son and the raid by House Karsten, he lost his nobility and land. Later on, having lost his mind after having killed his wife, he spent his time wasting away in an attempt to revive her, leading to the eventual raid on his home, as well as his death by his undead wife's hands.
appearance: Biehn had a beard, long hair, big eyebrows, and wore a suit. He was once described as having the appearance of a decent man, but apparently age was not kind to him, and his hair started to become tinged with white.
personality: Biehn was a cold, delusional, and heartless man. This was especially the case with his son, who bore demi-human traits due to atavism, and he was quick to lock him in a basement for a decade since he was a reminder of possible infidelity. He was capable of summoning a homicidal rage, which he felt and gave into by repeatedly stabbing his wife multiple times, killing her. However, because a part of him truly did love his wife despite his belief that she had been unfaithful, he was driven to the verge of madness, his eyes becoming unfocused as he wasted away in his days trying to revive her. Being forced to remember what he did to her seems to make him feel a form of guilt and make him become defensive, while sounding crazed the whole time and desperate. He also gained self-harming habits, tearing into his face with his fingers and using his healing magic to heal his face. Despite his knowledge and skill with water magic, he seemed to either hold hope or denial throughout his endless failures, and after remembering his son's far superior skill with water magic, he gained a twisted care for him, even going so far as to chide Miles for referring to him as a demi-human, as well as attempting to speak to him as if he was a father, despite his cruelty towards him, as if he'd forgotten everything. Despite his madness, he was still scheming, even if he knew that he was bound to lose, being willing to take a Duchess in order to bargain with his son.
history:
The Dream the Lion King Saw
Several years earlier before Ferris came to live with the Karstens, the Argyle family lost everything when it was discovered that Biehn and his wife had locked up their son, Felix. This was due to his demi-human characteristics, which were a recessive trait from an forebear of him and Biehn. After the Karsten family punished the members of House Argyle, Biehn and his wife had supposedly laid down quietly and live with what meager possessions they still had in their home, while they also let go of all of their servants, save for his maid, Hannah Regret, who chose to remain.

Some years later, Biehn's wife would die. Distraught and being nearly driven to madness, Biehn desperately sought means to revive her. After using his magic to preserve what he could of her body, Biehn would then turn to Sacrament of the Immortal King, a spell capable of resurrecting the dead and experiment with it for that purpose. However, the curse was incomplete due to the other half of the inscription being lost over the ages and Biehn's magical prowess wasn't enough to complete it, leading to the creation of mindless undead. These factors would bar much of his progress for years.

One day, he would meet a man named Miles, a merchant who dealt in the sale of corpses. Miles would assist him in experiments by providing corpses as material for some time, a fact that would soon catch the attention of Crusch Karsten. Crusch and a company of around 50 of her soldiers would go to investigate the matter unaware that this was in fact a trap to lure her and ultimately Ferris back to the estate. With Crusch captured, the snare would work as intended, as Biehn would force Ferris to come to the house and meet with him alone. There, he would reveal his full plot that brings about a darker truth; that there weren't any slaves being brought here but actual corpses that Biehn was currently using as an army to fight the Karsten militia outside the compound. Using Crusch's life as a bargaining chip, Biehn would demand that Ferris use Sacrament of the Immortal King to revive his wife, believing that his superior talent could make it work. With no choice, Ferris does as requested, and Biehn's wife was seemingly returned to the world of the living. Although still looking like a malnourished husk nevertheless, Biehn was overjoyed. However, Hannah would suddenly strangle him to death with a serene smile on her deathly face, and he was subsequently killed. In the end, his maid, Hannah Regret, locked herself in the same room as Biehn's corpse and his wife's ashes, and she set the manor ablaze, completely destroying his corpse.
abilities_text:
Magic (魔法, Mahō): Biehn was a highly talented user of Water Magic.
Healing Magic (治癒魔法, Chiyu Mahō): While not quite on Ferris' level, Biehn is shown to be highly skilled in healing magic to the point he could recover wounds instantly and unconsciously without effort.

Sacrament of the Immortal King (不死王の秘蹟, Fushiō no Hiseki): Sacrament of the Immortal King is an ancient spell created by an unknown Witch long ago. The spell, when cast correctly, will allow the user to reanimate corpses of the dead and make them do their bidding. Sadly, the technique to properly cast the spell has been long lost to time, and only an incomplete incantation exists which was transcribed in an old and withered book regarded as the most important heirloom of House Argyle. Originally, the spell was thought to be capable of fully reviving a dead person, and there are legends of the aforementioned Witch being supposedly capable of bringing back people exactly as they were before their demise. Effectively, the written chunks of the spell's full passage is incapable of producing anything more than walking corpses with no soul of their own, creating "corpse soldiers" whose flesh slowly withers away and decomposes through time. To further limit the usefulness of this mostly-lost spell, a caster with an extremely rare natural affinity for it must be found in order to recreate even the most basic effects of this forbidden spell. Even after persistent refinement, Biehn could only create zombies. There didn't appear to be a limit to the amount of zombies he could create and command, as he had no issue reviving over two-hundred people simultaneously.

intro: Clind (クリンド) is a house steward serving Annerose Miload. Despite joining the main cast after Arc 4, he does not play a supporting role until Arc 9.
appearance:
Clind appears to be a handsome young man around the age of twenty with a slender face and a tall, lean body. Along with that, he has eyebrow-length dark blue hair and gold eyes. Clind wears a well-starched black butler uniform with a frilly blue tie and sports a monocle on his left eye.

Despite being a dragonkin, Clind has shed his past and conceals his draconic characteristics in order to blend in with humanity. When manifesting his true power, he has removed his monocle, which has no special qualities whatsoever, as a gesture to signify his shift in mentality, prompting his natural deep black horns to protrude from his head. He may also possess other characteristics associated with dragonkin, such as wings or a tail, though they have not been observed with him.
personality:
Clind is well-mannered, highly considerate of others, is extremely skilled as a servant, and tends to add idioms to the end of his sentences. Despite his good traits, he sometimes jokes around a little while behaving in a polite manner. According to Frederica Baumann, he apparently has low self-esteem, which leads him to believe that his work as a butler is unworthy of praise, and likewise, despite having been responsible for teaching the other servants of House Mathers or House Miload, he is convinced that he has merely had the chance to convey what he knew many times due to his position rather than because he wanted to be a teacher, claiming it to be a noble role. However, by Petra Leyte's observation, he is fully aware of what he is capable of yet believes it is not something to be proud of, something which makes him come off as though he was modest, reserved, and had low self-esteem.

Clind is loyal to Roswaal, willing to follow him despite his faults. This being said, though he will not go against his orders, he does not necessarily approve of his actions, even going out of his way to ask for an explanation for why he would be willing to put his own servants in such a dangerous situation, even if it did result in someone getting their just punishment. He is shown to worry for the man as well, even going out of his way to attempt to convince him to marry and wash away the face paint.

As the dragonkin of Volcanica, Clind has inherited many of its memories, experiences, and emotions. One of the traits that Clind inherited is Volcanica's envy and high opinion of those with unrealized potential. In particular, this makes Clind to be drawn towards the souls of those within children, which is filled to the point of bursting with potential due to their youths. By his own claim, he is drawn to people who have pure and genuine souls, and that those who have such souls are also typically young in age. However, he is also able to determine that Emilia was mentally young for her age and that Ryuzu's soul was much more mature than her appearance suggested. This inherited nature often leads to others, such as Frederica, misunderstanding him. However, as there are secrets related to dragonkin that he prefers to be concealed from Frederica, he deliberately does not correct the misunderstandings of her and the people around her, leading to his discontentment to be kept at a distance from certain individuals and thus not fully witnessing their potential.
history:
Early Life
Clind was born as the dragonkin to the Divine Dragon, Volcanica. Having lived before the Great Calamity, Clind was acquainted with the Witches and Warlocks of that era, as well as the Valiant and the Saintess. At some point in time, he let go of everything, feeling empty as a result. However, he gained and accumulated things in the path he began to walk afterwards. He went on to make a contract with Roswaal A. Mathers, which entailed Clind to protect Roswaal's property by any and all means, though he was prevented from interacting with Beatrice by Roswaal for yet unknown reasons. According to Roswaal, he had compensated the contract with Clind by forming a united front and defeating Roswaal's nemesis. Clind has faithfully abided to his contract ever since, due to his ability to perceive souls and sensing Roswaal A. Mathers's soul in the bodies of his descendants.

At some point in time, Clind became the custodian of the Witch Factor of Melancholy, having succeeded its previous user, Hector, following his and Roswaal's joint battle with the Warlock of Melancholy. However, he notes that while he does bear said Witch Factor, this does not make him a Warlock. According to Clind himself, he has also made a covenant with a person he cannot name that restricts him from revealing his origins to others, and he claims that revealing said origins would greatly trouble the Emilia Camp.

Sword Demon Battle Ballad
Following the end of the Demi-Human War, Clind accompanied Roswaal J. Mathers (Julia Mathers) to a pub where she met with the Sword Demon, Wilhelm van Astrea, where they discussed the threat of Stride Vollachia. During their talk, however, the trio were assaulted by a group of shinobi, who were swiftly dispatched by Roswaal, Wilhelm, and Clind. Wilhelm noted that Clind's technique was neither sword skill nor magic, but something completely different. 

To ward off any risks to King Gionis Lugunica during the Subjugation of the Blight Dragon, Roswaal made the suggestion to let Clind protect him. After receiving Miklotov McMahon's approval and having Orphe make the preparations for it, Clind attacked and subdued Raizo, who was attempting to assassinate Gionis. Using his crushing power, he defeated Raizo, who thought he had accounted for every powerful individual in the Kingdom. As a send-off, Clind revealed to Raizo that he was a part of history and had been around since the era of Witches, before dealing a final blow to him. Following Roswaal's death at the hands of Stride Vollachia and Shasuke, he started to take care of her son, Roswaal K. Mathers, who at the time went by the name Karl, who inherited the soul of the original Roswaal A. Mathers. During the funeral of Karl’s mother, during the short exchange with Wilhelm, Wilhelm swore he would do everything in his power to help Karl if in need in order to honor Julia who greatly helped him during and after the Demi-Human War. A few minutes later, Karl and Clind left the cemetery.

Post-Sword Demon Trilogy
Sometime in the following decades, Clind was entrusted with protecting and training Frederica Baumann, teaching her how to work as a servant and to control her beast form.

The Oni Sisters of the Hidden Village
After Rem and Ram were hired as staff for the Roswaal Manor, Clind was responsible for the creation of their maid uniforms, something that made Frederica suspicious and started an argument. During the following months, he and Frederica taught the sisters how to be servants. One day, two months after they were hired, Roswaal order him to give Rem the key to the basement so that she would find the imprisoned Fogg. On the day that everyone left the manor, Clind had also left. However, after Rem fought and killed Fogg, Clind found her bloody body and brought her to her room. After she and Roswaal spoke, Clind confronted him for why he gave that order, though he did not get an answer. Afterward, he urged Roswaal to get married and wash away the face paint, to which Roswaal said that he would consider marriage prospects but not removing his face pain. Another month later, after the deaths of Dudley and Grace Miload and the birth of Annerose, because most of the servants had either died or resigned because of the attack by the Witch Cult, Clind and Frederica were tasked with serving her, and they would also continue his hobby of training demi-human servants there, leaving Rem and Ram as the only servants of Roswaal Manor.

Emily-san's Maid Path
Shortly after leaving Elior Forest, Emilia encounters and helps Annerose and Clind. Due to this intervention and a letter from Roswaal, Emilia is taken to the Miload mansion, where Annerose decides to take her in as a maid. During her introduction, her name is misheard as “Emily,” a nickname by which she becomes known in that environment. At the mansion, Frederica explains that it is a place that shelters discriminated demi-humans, allowing Emilia to remain there. However, Emilia misunderstands the situation as a test imposed by Roswaal to evaluate her effort and character, leading her to take her role as a maid very seriously. Despite her determination, her complete lack of experience with human life and household tasks causes her to fail repeatedly in her duties, and she is regarded as incompetent for the role. Even so, Emilia continues to persevere, convinced that overcoming these difficulties is part of her path toward a greater future.

The Emilia Camp's Great Evaluation Meeting
Following the Sanctuary Incident, Annerose and Clind, who had been tasked with making preparations by Roswaal, arrived at the Sanctuary to board all the villagers on their carriages, intent on leading them out of the snow-covered and heavily damaged forest. Annerose was quick to scold Roswaal for his behavior and approved of his being struck, claiming to Garfiel that she would be his ally should he hassle him again. abilities_text:
Overall Power
As the dragonkin of Volcanica, Clind is incredibly powerful. He is shown to be able to work alongside other strong combatant like Roswaal in order to fight and win against opponents on the level of the Warlock of Melancholy Hector, whose strength is considered among the top combatants introduced thus far, and Volcanica while under the control of Aldebaran.

Authority
Clind is a user of the Witch Factor of Melancholy and its corresponding Authority of Melancholy (憂鬱の権能, Yū'utsu no Ken'nō). As the Witch Factor's custodian, he is in possession of a black box containing the Factor from which he has employed the Authority. Although he is incompatible with Melancholy, Clind has maintained his sanity unlike Petelgeuse, and is limited in making use of its full power unless it is in exchange for a price.

Compression (圧縮, Asshuku): Using this Authority, Clind possesses the power to compress space and time. He primarily wields Compression as a form of teleportation by compressing the distance that would be required to travel from one point to another, or as an offensive force that dissipates and crushes targets of his choosing. As any individual besides Hector is incompatible with Melancholy due to its nature, Clind is required to bypass Od Lagna to wield Compression. In order to do this, he must take from people something with the possibility to influence the world as compensation to offer to Od Lagna in order to use the Authority, whether that is the existence of a spell that could open up many futures or something else with a similar influence. Clind has been provided compensation by Roswaal L. Mathers, who gave up "four magics" to allow him to use his power, and in one failed loop, Petra, who forfeit the possibility of becoming Subaru's bride. Once the price is paid, an incompatible user of the Witch Factor can unrestrainedly exercise Compression until the provided compensation is used up. However, Clind's mentality is such that he refuses to accept how the Witch Factor of Melancholy stifles potential as compensation, and thus, he has not been shown to forfeit any compensation of his own.
Instant Teleportation: With this utilization of Compression, Clind can seemingly instantaneously transport himself and other people alongside him if necessary in the blink of an eye from a place he started at to another place of his choosing by compressing the time and distance that would be required to travel from one point to another. In Clind's case, it can be employed so long as it is within the Kingdom of Lugunica, whereas another user, Petra, was not forced to abide by the same limitation. It is also difficult for Clind to reach a place such as the Pleiades Watchtower. However, using this form of Compression becomes significantly more difficult on wary and resistant opponents, and it is considered a herculean task to perform it on foes such as a Sin Archbishop or the Divine Dragon. To use this manner of Compression effectively, either the target must give their consent, or the opponent must be caught off guard.
Dissipation and Crushing: This offensive utilization of the Authority of Melancholy allows Clind to dissipate or crush things. By dissipating the space an object or person occupies, he can effectively make them vanish. Though the full extent to how he can use it is not known, in one instance, he was shown to use this technique of assault against Leonardo Baroness through the action of spreading his hand and clenching it. As a result, Leonardo's body was filled with holes and the space his body occupied was “devoured”, leaving no drop of blood or a trace of his existence behind. However, according to Clind, he is not required to use his hand to utilize his abilities. Furthermore, he can also squeeze an object or a person from a short distance, completely crushing a target. Unlike his power of teleportation, it is not known if these utilizations of the Authority of Melancholy require compensation.

Physical Traits/Flow Method
Increased Lifespan: As a dragonkin, Clind is not bound by age, and he is capable of living for centuries at a time without so much a hint of having grown older.

Enhanced Strength: As a dragonkin, Clind's base physical strength is superior to a typical human's. He has enough might that, despite not being able to pierce through its scales, he was able to knock down a being as tough as Volcanica with a single kick to its face.

Skilled Swordsman: Clind is talented enough with the sword that he could fight with it in emergencies, though he is never seen holding a sword or engaging in a sword fight.

Whipmanship: Clind is skilled at using a whip and taught Subaru the basics on how to use one.

Parkour Talent: Clind is skilled enough at parkour to teach it to Subaru. Subaru mentions that he is able to finish the Athletic Zone that Garfiel made without rumpling his clothes and without breaking a sweat, calling him inhuman.

Other
Sealing Shackles: Through an unknown method, Clind is able to seal his own power away. By doing so, he can disguise his dragonkin traits and appear fully human, which he has used to deceive people into thinking he was human for decades, as well as restrain his own power. These seals seem to have multiple layers to them. It is unknown if this is an ability related to his race or due to an outside influence.
Second Stage: By further unlocking his self-imposed shackles, Clind can access more of his own power. Upon releasing this shackle, his lightning can intensify to the point that it can produce Dragon-like defenses.
Third Stage: By unlocking yet another shackle, more of his strength is unleashed, and it allows him to pierce through Volcanica's reverse scale.

Lightning Manipulation: Clind is able to generate lightning from his body, primarily the soles of his feet and from his horns. By doing so, he can dramatically enhance the effectiveness of his strikes, including being able to sever one of the various uncharged breaths of the Divine Dragon, as well as increasing his speed by a dramatic amount. By utilizing the shockwaves created by lightning, he can achieve pseudo-flight by kicking against the air. He can also create a defense on par with Volcanica's by wrapping lightning around his body like a barrier. In fact, by Ezzo Cadner's observations, while the lightning can be used offensively, its utilization seems to be focused towards defense more than offense. It is unclear if he is able to do this naturally or if he is required to generate the lightning through magic.

Soul Perception: Clind has the power to perceive qualities from the souls of other people. For example, he used this ability to perceive the soul of the original Roswaal within his descendants. Presumably, he is also able to use this ability in order to perceive the "purity" of a person's soul. It is unknown whether this ability falls under his Authority or his traits as a dragonkin.

Possession: As the dragonkin of the Divine Dragon, Clind is able to inhabit Volcanica's husk, allowing him to control its body freely. He has done this in order to act on the covenant made during the time of the Great Calamity. The last known time he has performed this is during the Subjugation of the Blight Dragon. However, if something has taken over Volcanica's husk, he cannot possess it.

Survival Skills: He is mentioned by Subaru as being skilled at survival, enough to be able to teach him the basics (finding water, how to start a fire, etc.).

Excellent Teacher: Due to his vast experience, Clind is a talented teacher. He was able to teach Subaru how to utilize a whip, survival skills, and parkour in just a year.

personality:
