intro: Carol Fauzen (キャロル・ファウゼン), née Remendis (レメンディス) is a servant of House Astrea, was the personal attendant of the late Theresia van Astrea, and was the former bodyguard of Roswaal J. Mathers. She played supporting roles during the Sword Demon Trilogy.
appearance: Carol was a beautiful young woman with medium length blonde hair and green eyes. When she was young, she wore a blue and white outfit along with black stockings and armor.
personality:
On the surface, she comes across as a stoic woman with a strait-laced personality who rarely minces her words when she has something to say. However, Carol has a more nuanced and softer side that is typically reserved for those who have earned her trust. Her fierce loyalty and personal affection for Theresia can also sometimes overpower her usually rational sound judgements and reveal more competitive and childish characteristics, particularly when in the presence of Wilhelm, who stole her master's heart. She has shown to be especially soft around Grimm. Otherwise, she is a very dutiful person.

In her later years, Carol is a kind old lady, though she will get mad at people who don't show proper manners, such as licking a plate clean after eating. Though she still shows respect to people, she also is not afraid to lash out at people who are deliberately rude.
history:
Sword Demon Love Song
Carol was born as the heir to House Remendis, a warrior class noble family that has produced excellent swordsmen that would serve House Astrea for generations. Two years before the Demi-Human War began in earnest, when Theresia had awoken to the Divine Protection of Sword Saint at age 13, a 14-year-old Carol, who had been displaying skills among the best of her generation in her House, was assigned to be Theresia's personal attendant. Although their relationship had started off somewhat rough, after attempting to challenge her and being swiftly defeated, she learned of her Divine Protections and saw her genuinely crying for hurting her. Gaining immense respect for her, she decided to loyally follow her.

However, Theresia soon lost the ability to smile after her failure in the beginning of the Demi-Human War which resulted in one of her brothers' death. With Theresia unable to wield her blade, Carol took her place by Roswaal's side to protect her. Following the Battle of Castour Field, the Kingdom decided to call in the magic specialist Roswaal J. Mathers to analyze the magic circles used. When the Zergev Squadron arrived at Castour Field, they officially met Roswaal and Carol. However, it took no time for Carol and Wilhelm to start arguing, Grimm having to step between them. With everyone split into group, Grimm kept Carol company to keep her mind off of Wilhelm. After arriving and allowing Roswaal to check the circle, after she claimed it would be a threat to the Kingdom, Grimm had a bad feeling that he thought Wilhelm might share. That feeling turned out to be correct when the undead Tholter fired arrows at them and corpse soldiers began rising. Leaving Grimm to cover Roswaal alongside Carol, Wilhelm went to fight the undead, where he met Sphinx. With Roswaal intending to join the fight, furious, Sphinx decided to retreat, leaving everyone to clean up the undead. With some help from Roswaal, Wilhelm realized that Tholter was the main corpse soldier to defeat, and after giving him the push he needed to overcome his trauma and fight, Grimm ran forward and put his old friend to rest. Shortly after this, Carol spoke to Grimm, who was still fearful after having killed Tholter, and after calming him down, he fell in love with her. Afterward, meeting up with the Bordeaux and Pivot, Roswaal relayed Sphinx's identity and the threat she bore.

For 3 years, he and the other members of the Zergev Squadron, and often Roswaal and Carol, were sent to some of the most dangerous and brutal battles of the war. Once, while speaking with Grimm, he alleviated her fears over both Wilhelm and her own master, saying that people could change. Before leaving, she offered to teach Grimm to use the shield, leading to their regular meetups to train. Likewise, more and more of Theresia's family began to die in the war, breaking her heart further. With people trying to convince her to join the army, Carol, who was upset that she couldn't help Theresia, convinced her to go outside and away from everyone, which resulted in the girl making a flower field in the slums. One day, however, when she went to retrieve her, she found her smiling, with the girl saying that she met a rude boy that day. In time, she learned that boy was Wilhelm, and at times, she would even spy on her conversations. Though frustrated that it was Wilhelm's influence that was healing her, as she still didn't get along very well with him, she was grateful and started harboring more respect and envy for him for letting Theresia smile again. One day, she met Grimm and gave him a locket with a flower as a good luck charm. However, that day, everyone met their new commander, Leip Barielle, who struck Wilhelm for his disrespect. Though Roswaal pacified him and led him away, Carol followed, still worried about Wilhelm.

During the Battle of Aihiya Swamp, Carol joined Roswaal and ten other knights to investigate the location of a magic circle, which activated and brought everyone to their knees. Not wanting to allow it to be destroyed, Sphinx appeared and got in her way, killing several of the knights in an attempt to convince Roswaal to join her. However, Roswaal managed to easily corner her, causing Sphinx to fly away. After Roswaal destroyed the circle, Carol was worried for Grimm's safety on the field. In the month following the battle, Carol visited Grimm after he lost his voice due to a throat injury, apologizing to and crying for him. This led to him kissing her and their becoming lovers. During a later meeting with Grimm, she gave him a House Remendis shield as a present for surviving. Later, she visited Wilhelm when Grimm wanted him to visit, and she chastised him for the way he treated Grimm.

A little while after this, uprisings started all over the country, forcing the regional lords to take care of them on their own. With the Zergev Squadron rebuilt and left behind, they prepared to move as well when Wilhelm realized that the enemies' movement was a distraction so that the leaders could attack the castle and the king. With the rest of the unit, Grimm, who returned to duty, and Bordeaux Zergev trusting his judgment, they made for the castle, and with Roswaal and Carol's appearances, they were allowed inside. With the squad split up to cover the castle, Wilhelm took his group to the chapel while Bordeaux split off from them. Confronting Valga and Sphinx, the former of which had enhanced is size via a magic circle and his ancestors' bones, he had his companions chase after Sphinx while he battled Valga. With Carol's aerial combat, Roswaal's techniques, and Grimm's defenses, they cornered Sphinx and forced her to retreat, with Roswaal chasing after her and leaving the rest to assist Wilhelm, who eventually managed to defeat Valga.

Within the following year of the Invasion of the Royal Castle, having been knighted and being made the vice commander of the Zergev Squadron, Wilhelm started to become friendlier to his comrades, to the point that he would even share drinks with and tease Grimm about his relationship with Carol, much to Carol's frustration. However, one day, when Roswaal informed him that his territory was in danger, he disappeared without telling anyone. Learning about it, Carol decided to inform Theresia, who chose to pick up a sword to protect Wilhelm. Later, they arrived in the Trias Domain with the Zergev Squadron, where Theresia started killing their enemies, much to her sadness and Carol's worry. After Battle of the Trias Domain, once Theresia spoke with Wilhelm, Wilhelm disappeared for years. It wasn't until after the war was over that anyone saw him again, when he challenged and defeated Theresia in the middle of her award ceremony, and Carol, who was worried for him for both her and Theresia's sakes, was happy to see him again and grateful that he managed to take away the reason for Theresia to wield the sword anymore.

Sword Demon Love Story
After Theresia dragged Wilhelm to her mansion and forced him to take a bath, he spoke with Carol and Grimm, the former of which lashed out at him, and he learned of her position as Theresia's attendant. After this, they informed him that he was unemployed, leading him to finding a way to rejoin. Later, upon Carol and Grimm's return to the mansion, Carol chided Wilhelm for upsetting Theresia and went to speak with her while Wilhelm and Grimm finished all of the food that Theresia prepared. The next day over breakfast, Carol warned him not to do anything that would upset Theresia. The day after that, Wilhelm found himself face to face with the best warriors the country had to offer, including Bordeaux, Carol, and Grimm. With Gionis and Miklotov overseeing the battle, Wilhelm fought and defeated all forty soldiers. However, after Theresia arrived and chided the king for allowing this, it was revealed that she would have been let go of her position if she married Wilhelm, much to everyone's but the king and Miklotov's shock. Wilhelm accepted this, and they embraced, Theresia calling him Wilhelm van Astrea, much to Carol's relief.

Three months later, she and Theresia went to confront Theresia's father, Veltol. When they met, Theresia was quick to chide her father for his actions, and she even threatened to leave House Astrea because of him. Even Carol and her mother, Tishua, joined in to chide him. However, she believed in Wilhelm, and she knew that he would arrive on time for their wedding, despite her father's meddling. The next day, wearing her wedding dress, she waited patiently for the return for the Zergev Squadron with Carol and her parents. Eventually, Bordeaux arrived and informed her of the squad's return, and soon after, her wedding took place. Carol was one of the many attendees who watched the two get married. Towards the end of the reception, Theresia threw the bouquet to her, leading to Grimm taking it, pulling her close, and holding the bouquet in the air, essentially declaring that they would be next. In the month that followed, Veltol made numerous appearances, much to Theresia's frustration, and eventually, he even suggested going along on the honeymoon as well, leading to another argument. However, with help from Tishua, they were able to get him to leave. Given two months for their honeymoon, they prepared to leave, taking Carol as Theresia's attendant, and they decided to visit the cities to the south of the Royal Capital.

Sword Demon Love Story: Earth Dragon Capital, Flanders
After their marriage, Wilhelm and Theresia went on their honeymoon with Carol accompanying them, and they first visited Flanders, the Earth Dragon Capital, where Theresia was going to ride an earth dragon for the first time. After experiencing one for a moment, Carol interrupted them after Wilhelm got a little intimate with Theresia, to which Theresia scolded Carol. Though Carol was heavily reluctant, partially due to her own misgivings and Veltol's request to not let him take things too far with her, she entrusted Theresia to Wilhelm's care. As they rode atop one earth dragon, Theresia told Wilhelm about how the different species of earth dragons were named after flowers, which Wilhelm was curious about. As they rode, Wilhelm was reminded of his family, and after Theresia grabbed his attention, she described them to her. After a few hours time, Theresia improved her riding to the point that she surpassed Carol, and she and Carol ran around on their respective earth dragons. Wilhelm, watching them from a distance as a rancher watched approached him and said the earth dragon she was riding became attached to her. After he offered it to Wilhelm, he was told its name was Diana, which Wilhelm laughed at.

Sword Demon Love Story: Silver Flower Dance of Picoutatte
After leaving Flanders, because Theresia insisted they not visit her home in Hakuchuri, they made for Picoutatte, where her father was waiting, leading to another argument. However, with his reason for visiting to collect the present for his wife, they accompanied him to the Suwen Company. With Veltol asking Wilhelm and Carol to allow him and Theresia to shop together, they left to observe the town. However, when a commotion at the shop ensued, they returned to find a ton of blood and Theresia, and they were soon rushed to the hospital, where Veltol lay cursed and injured, as informed to them by Garitch Fabless, who attempted to heal him. Accordingly, the only way to remove the curse was to cut it off at the source. Soon after, Yaktol Suwen, who ran the shop, informed the group of the message given by the perpetrator of the incident, Stride Vollachia, that they would be waiting at a great bridge in Picoutatte's west district with the source of the curse. Impatient, Carol ran off with Yaktol in search of the man while Theresia resolved herself to go to the bridge with Wilhelm.

The next morning, Carol returned, unable to find Stride. After Yaktol then provided Wilhelm with his new sword that Veltol picked out for him, he and Theresia left for the bride where Stride and his champion Kurgan were waiting. Meanwhile, Carol remained behind at the hospital to watch over Veltol. Eventually, the curse was lifted, and when Theresia and Wilhelm returned, she informed them as much. Later, she and Theresia bought an accessory for Veltol to gift Tishua. However, when Theresia got into another argument with his dad, she and Carol left to greet Tishua, who was informed of the situation and decided to come to Picoutatte.

Sword Demon Love Story: The Other Side of the Honeymoon
Following the Silver Flower Dance of Picoutatte, Theresia and Carol wandered the streets of Picoutatte while Wilhelm and Veltol were recovering from their injuries. As they walked, they came across Garitch and spoke with him. Theresia apologized to him for having destroyed the bridge and creating more work for him, but he waved it off. Still worried about it, Carol tried to pin the blame on the one responsible for the challenge while Garitch said that Veltol could pay for the damages and treatment and nobody would be upset. However, he also asked her if she could get Veltol to reconsider his recommendation of Garitch to the Royal Capital, as he did not want to go to the capital since the mother of his son was there. Though he believed that it would probably be for the best that he didn't go, Theresia claimed that happiness was up to the individual to choose, which ultimately cemented that Garitch did not want to go, saying it wasn't the right time yet, and the girls left his going to the capital to Veltol. Afterward, they asked about the mother, which he described, leading to Garitch telling her that someone so immoral should not be recommended and telling her that Wilhelm was fastidious, so she didn't have to worry, triggering an emotional response from Carol. After he recommended the sherbet, he left, and the two had a bowl for themselves.

Felt-chan Saw!
In the ten days that followed the Loot House Incident, Felt tried several times to escape, having managed to escape Reinhard's side only once successfully before being caught. Likewise, the other servants stopped her. Being served confectionaries by Carol, Felt enjoyed it and asked if Carol wouldn't go with her when she escaped, to which she appreciated the offer but claimed that she had to refuse for Grimm's sake.

Felt-chan Rises to the Center Stage
On the way to the Royal Castle, Felt, who had lost a bet to Reinhard, started to kick at him in annoyance while Carol drove the carriage with her husband. She ultimately failed to hit him even once, and she asked once more where they were headed. Though Reinhard wanted to keep it a secret, they reached the castle, much to her frustration. Inside the castle, Reinhard left her side and Felt was brought to be dressed by maids while Carol watched on. However, Heinkel, having come in response to Reinhard's arrival, entered the room, much to Carol's anger and Felt's annoyance. Afterward, Carol informed Heinkel of Felt's reason being in the castle was for the Royal Selection, which he laughed at. Though Felt was ready to attack him, Heinkel stepped in front of her quickly and claimed that they were both in the same position before leaving. Felt asked Carol about her Heinkel, and she replied that she, Grimm, and Reinhard all had connections to him, and she was dismayed that Reinhard had apparently guessed correctly. Deciding to get things back on track, Felt positioned herself to continue getting dressed while a couple of the maids cleaned up a mess Heinkel had made, and while that was happening, Felt noticed Heinkel's hair tone being like Reinhard and claimed she knows people with red hair suck.

Felt-chan Forms a Hooligan Squad
Felt sat with the trio of thugs to discuss with them, and after some talk and a bit of resistance from them, she eventually convinced them to help destroy the country, as she thought they had similar views to her. Later on at night, Reinhard had a secret meeting with Grimm and Carol, commenting how the events that transpired confirmed that his choice to follow Felt was the correct one and that he felt a little guilty that he would use her to make the Astrea family name rise to glory again. Changing the main subject, the old lady asks if they really should allow their master to get near Reinhard's mother, as they feared what could come of the encounter. Reinhard stated that he cannot deny him this, as it was his right, and he mentioned that he would soon leave with Felt to take care of other matters, thanking the both of them for everything they had done.

intro: Chisha Gold (チシャ・ゴールド) is the Fourth ranking Divine General of the Sacred Vollachia Empire and Emperor Vincent Vollachia's military advisor and decoy. He played important roles in The Travelogue of the Finest, The Tale of the Scarlet Princess, and Sword Identity, where he aided the emperor with the best of his abilities. As the instigator and ringleader of the civil war that struck the Vollachia Empire before Arc 7, he was the apparent main antagonist of the aforementioned arc.
appearance:
Chisha Gold was a tall, lean man with relatively long snow-white hair with the tips of his bangs being purple in color. His extremely pale complexion made him give off an impression as if all the color drained from him. He was also noted to emit an aura of not entirely being present in the room. His golden eyes had a decorative purple teardrop at the outer side of each of his eyes which give off an air of mystery which befitted the Divine General rather well. He dressed in a long white coat that covers his body in its entirety. The coat had a rather high white collar and what appear to be 6 purple-colored gems at his chest area; three for each side of the chest. The inside of the coat seemed to be a mixture of different colors arranged in stripes; darker white, grey and grey with circular purple designs respectively.

Before the coronation of the seventy-seventh emperor of the Vollachia Empire, Chisha wore the exact same dress but solely black. His hair was also of the same color, as well as his weapon. Following his injury that almost cost him his life, Chisha's hair turned white, and thus, the Divine General decided to entirely switch his color scheme.
personality:
Chisha was a calm and collective individual, preferring to rely on his keen intellect rather than on his limited fighting strength. He walked around with an air of mystery and uncanniness, spoke in a polite manner, in contrast with some other Divine Generals such as Cecilus and Yorna, and generally gave off a more pacifistic vibe. Despite being a Divine General in the Vollachia Empire, Chisha was shown to not have much of the nationalistic tendencies others have, and admits his poor fighting capabilities, claiming that he only became a Divine General out of necessity. In fact, he even believed that he was being overvalued. Since his youth, he has also had an impatient and slightly impulsive nature, something which had once resulted in him getting into trouble and even drove him to answer a query by a young Vincent with his true thoughts. He had a proclivity towards theory over practice, and he was aware that he was socially clumsy as well.

Despite his outward appearance, however, Chisha was cold and calculative, planning his every step and manipulating all of his opponents with borderline ease. With his keen intellect, he was easily able to impersonate Vincent's mannerisms and ways of thinking to perfection, while his decoy ability seemingly allowed him to morph into the emperor, keeping the throne occupied and preventing a nation-wide rebellion from occurring. This being said, by the speculation of Natsuki Subaru, his actions, despite not being born of loyalty to Vincent, despite his own claim that he would not give his life for Vincent, were in an attempt to challenge and overcome the fate that seemed to ridicule Vincent. Chisha himself even believed that his actions were for that day, to challenge and mock the disaster that was beset to claim Vincent's life.
history:
Chisha was born in a commoner family under the name Chesha Trim (チェシャ・トリム, Chesha Torimu), and because he had been born with black hair, his social clumsiness, and was inept at performing tilling or harvesting of fields, he had been a subject of mockery. Due to his impatient nature, Chesha had gotten into trouble with someone important and was banished from his hometown. Chesha first met Vincent Abellux when he was fourteen, when Vincent's dragon carriage got stuck in a ditch. Using his calculative skills, Chesha helped the prince get his dragon carriage unstuck, and immediately afterward, he was brought aboard that very carriage, both as a way to thank him and to bring him to his mansion. Afterward, Vincent asked him Chesha if he would die for him, which Chesha declined on impulse. Despite expecting to be executed for his insolence, his answer impressed Vincent, and telling him to keep that outlook, decided to hire him. His confusion led him to question Vincent's decision, as he was aware of the events of the Miracle of Abellux, to which Vincent merely replied that his actions were to prevent any future rebellions through fear. As Vincent asked what Chesha thought he expected of him, Vincent claimed that the road he walked was one filled with ditches, and he believed he would need Chesha's abilities to get out of such problems.

After being hired, Chesha started to go by the name Chisha Gold, adopting the surname of a certain house that Vincent had exterminated, because he did not want to cause his family any troubles. Thanks to the adoption of the Gold name, rumors began to spread that Vincent left one descendant from the family alive to serve him in order to condemn the family to endure the humiliation to escape his control, further reinforcing his own reputation. From then forward, Chisha helped Vincent get out of various "ditches", and once he was well learned about the flood control systems, he decided to finally be rid of the administrator and have him executed for embezzlement. As more time passed, Vincent eventually told Chisha about Stride Vollachia and his journal. However, he did not tell him what he read within it. At an unknown point after this, Vincent picked up Cecilus, and about six months after a conversation between Chisha and Cecilus regarding their roles came the Imperial Selection Ceremony.

The Tale of the Scarlet Princess
During the time of the Imperial Selection Ceremony, Chisha worked as Vincent Abellux's chief of strategy. His plans were instrumental to Vincent's success, though one of them, concocted in preparation for the Siege on the Abellux Castle, led to his near-fatal injury caused by Arakiya. This led to him completely losing his color, as well as his sudden manifestation of his Noh ability. After Palladio Manesque's death at the hands of Prisca Benedict, Chisha made his presence known in the Manesque Castle and offered wine to her, which she ordered Arakiya to destroy, expecting it was poison. However, Arakiya, who had been convinced by Vincent to join his side in order to ensure Prisca's survival, began to lick the poisoned wine, quickly falling in an unstable condition. Chisha watched as Prisca took part of the poison from Arakiya in an attempt to save her life, and before she lost consciousness, proclaimed that he would have been willing serving her if he had not been working under Vincent. Much to Chisha's pleasure, Vincent's plan to defy the rules of the Imperial Selection Ceremony and spare his sister was successful, with the girl managing to take on a new identity while Arakiya joined their faction. Meanwhile, thanks to his near-death experience, Chisha changed his color scheme in order to match his new ability, Noh, an ability he decided to keep the particulars of a secret from everyone. Following the selection's conclusion and Vincent's ascendance to the throne, Chisha was appointed to the ranks of the Divine Generals.

The Travelogue of the Finest
After the rebellion four to five months before Arc 1, Chisha took place in a meeting about the incident alongside Vincent, Goz Ralfon, Groovy Gumlet, and Moguro Hagane. About a month later, he visited Lugunica in order to retrieve or dispose of Gramdart Holstoy, the culprit who conspired with Balleroy Temeglyph in the recent rebellion against Vincent and had faked his death to escape to Lugunica, in addition to finding and stop Cecilus, who entered the country without warning on his own accord to catch the traitor himself. Before returning to Vollachia, he witnessed the bout between Cecilus and the Sword Saint, Reinhard van Astrea.

In The Years That Followed
During one of Ubilk's visits to the castle, he spoke with Chisha and Vincent, saying that the Great Disaster had been foretold by the stars, something that he brought up with the intention of informing Chisha about. When Chisha began questioning him, having not heard of this Great Disaster, Ubilk claimed that it would bring ruin, also mentioning Yang Sword's glow, implying he knew about what went down with Prisca and resulting in Chisha nearly killing him for it. Afterward, he claimed that it would be the death of Vincent Vollachia that would trigger the Great Disaster. After Ubilk left the room, Vincent and Chisha discussed why he kept it secret from Chisha, which Vincent claimed was futile and something that Chisha could not prevent anyway, something that Chisha disagreed with and claimed his intentions to go against, which Vincent refuted. When asked for how long he had known about the Great Disaster and its trigger, Vincent brought out the journal, and he stated that everything he had done was to minimize the damage, including preparing Chisha for the future.

A few days later, having come to realize that he had no way to directly reject Vincent's thoughts, Chisha cornered Ubilk, intent on getting answers out of him. Despite the threats of Ubilk's inevitable death because of Vincent's possible death, Ubilk was undeterred and merely claimed that his role was to prevent the destruction that was to follow the Great Disaster, and if the Great Disaster didn't occur, since he would need to fulfill his commandment, he would become one of the causes to trigger the Great Disaster. Though Chisha was tempted to kill him to prevent that, Ubilk merely claimed another Stargazer would appear in his place. Afterward, he mentioned that four disasters would occur to destroy the world and that the time to stop one of them has come. As he thought about what to do, he asked how the commandment was conveyed to Ubilk, and when Ubilk said he would have dreams, Chisha claimed to wonder which Vincent it was he saw in his dream, using his Noh to paint over himself and become "Vincent Vollachia".

Guardians of the Crimson Flame
In an attempt to remove Vincent's little sister from the board and bring the Yang Sword to its full power, Chisha made attempts to snuff her life via the shinobi. At the recommendation of Olbart Dunkelkenn, he requested to meet with Yae Tenzen in hopes that she could carry out the task of infiltrating Leip Barielle's staff to observe Priscilla. He received her evaluation of her own skills and tasked her to stand by and closely observe Priscilla once hired and await the possibility of being given new instructions depending on the situation. Eventually, the time came for her to assassinate Priscilla, but she failed in her attempt, having been stopped by her knight, Al, who forced her into becoming his servant. Some time later, in response to Yae's failure, Chisha assigned a suicide squad comprised of ten shinobi, to kill Priscilla. The shinobi squad, led by Hamayal Wesmi, who was to personally carry out the assassination, took advantage of an event held by Priscilla in their effort to kill her. However, the majority of them were killed by Aldebaran and Yae, and Hamayal's mind was broken by Al, who made him into a pawn. Following the second failed assassination attempt, on Al's orders, Hamayal sent his Phantom Wolf through the letter that was to report how the mission had gone. The Phantom Wolf was set on Chisha as soon as he opened said letter, but Cecilus, who was in the room with him, eradicated it in a flash, ending Hamayal's life. Recognizing that Priscilla's guardians had taken care of the incident, Chisha gave up his attempts to assassinate her, having partially expected that it would be infeasible to begin with.

Imperial Coup
When the time came to set the board to achieve his aim, after directing most of the Divine Generals to various locations, infantilizing Cecilus after convincing him to go along with his plans and sending him to Ginunhive, placing the Stone in Garkla, and dispatching more shinobi assassins to lure Priscilla Barielle back to Vollachia, he teamed up with Berstetz Fondalfon and instigated a coup to oust the emperor. Defeating and imprisoning Goz, who was defending the emperor, they successfully managed to make Vincent retreat to Buddheim Jungle. In order to make sure that Vincent was taking the threat seriously, Chisha sent imperial soldiers after him while he prepared himself. With Ubilk, Olbart, and Kafma Irulux as his escorts, he soon set out to visit Yorna in Chaosflame.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
Chisha's power and proficiency can be described as being that of an average person. He had trained himself in martial-arts for self-defense after being taken in by Vincent, and though he has the skill to defeat most average people, his combat capabilities lag far behind that of the other Nine Divine Generals. However, Chisha makes up for this with his intellect, and his rank as the Fourth among the Nine Divine Generals reflects this. Although not as physically dangerous, the majority of his plans have led to victory.

Techniques
Noh (能, Nō): Chisha utilized a "power" that he dubbed "Noh". By stealing the "colors" of a target he wished to become and wearing the "mask" of them that he received as a result, he could take on the exact form of another person, allowing him to reproduce eighty percent of their abilities. When putting on a mask, his body underwent a grotesque transformation to match that of the individual whose mask he wore. However, he could not wear and remove someone's mask repeatedly, and after he had torn off a mask a single time, it was used up and reduced to dust, and he was required to steal their colors again before being able to reacquire their mask. Furthermore, his thorough replication of the original person was not determined by simply wearing their mask alone, as in situations where he was forced to wear the mask of Vincent to act as his body double, Chisha had to devote his utmost efforts to avoid being perceived by someone such as Groovy, whose sense of smell could expose him, unless he successfully obscured his heart from being smelled. Having acquired this ability during the Imperial Selection Ceremony after being brought to the verge of death by Arakiya and losing his color, Chisha was required to maintain constant awareness to dye himself in another's colors. However, in one case, when he was in front of a mirror while taking on someone else's form, his true appearance could be briefly reflected in the mirror, before quickly returning to match the appearance of the person whose mask he was wearing. Prior to instigating the civil war, he used this ability to take Olbart's colors, and donned the mask of him to reproduce the Infantilization technique to shrink Cecilus, before going on to don Vincent's mask until the end of his life. He kept the true nature of his ability a secret to everyone, including Vincent, as a contingency. To this end, he had also stolen the colors of other people he had met in his life such as Ferris and Priscilla, preserving their masks in case there ever came a time where he needed them.
Infantilization (幼児化, Yōji-ka): By taking Olbart's "colors", Chisha was able to reproduce his Infantilization technique. By forcing a contract onto the target and altering their Od, he can rejuvenate the target’s body and physically make them younger, even altering their mind to revert to their youthful personality to match their body. This was originally a technique made to render the target powerless against the user. Likewise, unlike Olbart's usage of the technique, he was able to seal the memories of his targets.

Intelligence
Keen Intellect: Chisha possessed considerable intellect and was capable of rapid critical thinking and planning. He had ascended to the rank of Fourth purely due to his calculative skills and outstandingly brilliant tactics. With him at his side, Vincent easily won conflicts and swiftly dispatched any and all dangers facing him. Furthermore, Chisha's keen intellect allowed him to impersonate Vincent to perfection and predicting his next moves, all the while fooling everyone in Vollachia with his "ability". According to the author, Chisha was the smartest character in the series.

Equipment
White Fan: Chisha wielded a fan in combat and was somewhat skilled with it.

intro: Balleroy Temeglyph (バルロイ・テメグリフ) was the former Ninth ranking Divine General of the Sacred Vollachia Empire. He played an antagonistic role in The Travelogue of the Finest, Arc 7, and Arc 8, as well as a small supporting role toward the end of the latter arc.
appearance:
Balleroy was a tall man with ashen brown hair and blue eyes. He had a pale complexion and droopy eyes. He wore a green shirt under copper-plated armor, and brown gloves on his hands. He also wore black pants with four small bags around his hips and brown boots.

As a zombie, he possessed a vessel of earth, pale skin bereft of color, various cracks that ran across his body, pitch-black sclera, and radiant golden irises.
personality: Balleroy was a calm, talkative and cheerful man, who took pride in his title as the Ninth Divine General. Despite his apparent nature, however, Balleroy was cold and ruthless in battle. In his own words, whether they were men, women, children, or the elderly, if he was tasked with killing them, he would have no problem with doing so, though before he died, he expressed a sense of gratitude at never having actually killed any women or children. Following the death of Miles, Balleroy swore to take revenge on Reinhard van Astrea no matter what it would take. Sadly for him, however, he never had the chance to face off against the Sword Saint, as he was defeated and killed in a duel between him and Julius Juukulius, roughly four to five months before the start of the main story.
history:
Balleroy was adopted by Miles as a child and grew up at House Dracroy. He had a deep attachment to Miles and thought of him as a sworn brother. When he was around 12 or 13 years old, he got his hands on a dragon egg and decided to incubate it. During this process, he came across two kids like him, Flop O'Connell and Medium O'Connell, and became friends with them. Together, Balleroy, Miles, and Flop thought up a name for the flying dragon, Carillon, when it hatched. When Carillon's fangs were replaced by new ones, Balleroy gave one fang each to Flop and Medium as souvenirs.

The Tale of the Scarlet Princess
Around seven years before the main story, Serena sent the Miles and Balleroy, now Imperial Soldiers of the Imperial Army, to the Pendleton Estate in order to invite Jorah Pendleton and his wife Priscilla Barielle to the Gladiator Island Ginunhive. While they were there, the gladiators attempted to spark a revolution that would render the island independent from the mainland, which later ended up failing thanks to Priscilla's actions and the intervention of the Imperial Army. Serena Dracroy, Priscilla, Jorah, Balleroy, and Miles then went back to the Pendleton mansion after this incident. Later, after Jorah was killed and Priscilla escaped execution, Balleroy and Miles were sent to find Priscilla, and after they found her, the three helped smuggle Priscilla into the Kingdom of Lugunica. At an unknown point in time after this, Balleroy became the Ninth of the Nine Divine Generals.

Meeting Madelyn
At some point, Balleroy decided to fly to the peak of Mount Palzoa with Carillon, where he met a young girl and the Cloud Dragon Mezoreia. Though initially shocked to see her, he decided to continue visiting her, gifting her with clothes, teaching her how to speak, and giving her the name Madelyn after an acquaintance of his. In time, the two became close, and Balleroy sought to bring Madelyn outside of the cave. This resulted in a fight with Mezoreia, though they made peace in the end, and Balleroy stopped trying to take her away from the mountain, and his visits became less frequent.

The Travelogue of the Finest
Roughly 4 to 5 months before the start of the main story, Reinhard van Astrea, Julius Juukulius, and Ferris escorted two members of the Council of Wise Men on a diplomatic mission to the Empire in order to sign a non-aggression pact between the Kingdom and the Empire. After an unfortunate turn of events, Reinhard found himself standing in front of Balleroy's corpse and was subsequently labeled as guilty for the man's murder, leaving him no other choice but to escape, taking the emperor as a "hostage". After battling with three of the other Nine Divine Generals, Vincent, Julius, Ferris, and Reinhard came to the conclusion that Balleroy was not actually dead but rather faked his own death in order to divert the attention of the three Royal Guards. He attempted to use the situation to seize revenge on Reinhard for killing his sworn brother, Miles, who had died a few months earlier during a mission in Lugunica. Before long, Balleroy entered a deadly duel with Julius after the death of his beloved dragon, Carillon, which concluded with his death when he was pierced on the left side of his chest.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
Despite having held the lowest rank among the Nine Divine Generals, Balleroy was one who even members of the Kingdom's government felt the need to be particularly wary of. His strength was such that he could kill his enemies long before they noticed him, and regardless of obstacles, his attacks effectively could not be prevented without extreme preparation. 

Techniques
Flying Dragon Rider: Balleroy was an expert flying dragon rider and the best in Vollachia. He used his talent for dragon riding in conjunction with his magic for mobility. His dragon was named Carillon. Balleroy learned how to tame and fly flying dragons from Miles.

Magic
Although it is unclear what attribute Balleroy had an affinity for, he could use wind and yang magic, and he was one of only a bare few within the Empire capable of even using magic. Even one of the Kingdom's strongest combatants, Roswaal L. Mathers, after having confronted him in combat, felt as though he would very likely lose if they had fought one on one. What's more, due to his abilities as a Flying Dragon Rider, he has command over the skies, meaning that nobody can hide from him.

Spells:
Magic Bullets (魔弾, madan): Balleroy is capable of firing relatively large and colorless bursts of yang magic, using his spear to aim them. Each bullet could move extremely fast since they lack weight, and they have enough destructive power to easily destroy trees, walls, and other structures. Likewise, since the bullets are magical in nature, they leave no physical trace behind, they can easily burn straight through an enemy and kill them in one shot, and there is no recoil. He is not necessarily limited in firing single shots either; by his own claim, if he so chose, he could easily wipe out a forest in front of him by firing repetitive shots of magic bullets, allowing him to strike hiding enemies. The bullets themselves also cost very little mana, which further improves the number of times he can fire his shots. Despite the simple nature of his magic, his proficiency with and perfection of the magic bullets left even a master of magic, Roswaal, impressed.
Wind Shrouding: Balleroy was able to shroud himself and his partner in wind, allowing him to increase their speed and reduce impacts levied onto them.
Scope: By focusing yang magic directly in front of his eye, Balleroy is able to see far off enemies and snipe them from far away.

Combined Spells:
Camouflage Magic: By using magic to bend light around him and using the wind to diffuse his aura, Balleroy is capable of becoming invisible. While invisible, however, he is unable to hear his surroundings. According to the Aldebaran taking over Volcanica's husk, performing this magic while moving is difficult. However, Balleroy seems to be able to circumvent this issue by riding on Carillon, allowing it to move while he focused on his magic.

Physical Traits/Flow Method
Incredible Marksmanship: Balleroy is an accomplished sniper whose precision has been considered so dangerous that he was considered one of the Empire's greatest threats. He was capable of shooting his magic bullets with extreme precision and immense speed, dispatching enemies with ease and deadly proficiency, even from a super long distance away, and given a clear line of sight, he could snipe someone from kilometers away. He even learned how to ricochet shots off of falling debris, as seen during the Great Disaster. Combined with his reputation as one of the best flying dragon riders, which he often utilized to give him the freedom of movement to pursue his enemy while sniping at them and their potential hiding spots simultaneously, Balleroy became feared through the lands under the alias of Magic Bullet Sharpshooter. According to Roswaal, in ordinary circumstances, he is not sure he would come out victorious against him, and in one failed loop, Balleroy was even capable of predicting the movements of an infantilized Cecilus Segmunt and sniping off his legs.

Spearmanship: Although understated compared to his marksmanship, Balleroy is an accomplished spearman, able to swiftly handle experienced gladiators with a mere few attacks of his spear and fists combined. He later fought evenly against Julius Juukulius with his spear.

Intelligence
Keen Strategist: Despite his carefree attitude, Balleroy is strategical in regard to how he typically fights. According to Flop, if he were to serve in the vanguard, he would move in before anyone else to take out key strategical points, and part of the reason he does this is to prevent reckless casualties from his own soldiers' side. Even when not on the vanguard and defending a strategical location, he is smart enough to keep himself hidden and watch over a relatively wide area to prevent dangerous people from advancing while simultaneously keeping his own location hidden. Likewise, he is also capable of quickly striking at the leader of the enemy, and because of this, the Kingdom considered that, alongside Olbart Dunkelkenn, Balleroy was one of the most feared war assets the Empire had.

Equipment
Spear: Balleroy wielded a long spear from the tip of which he used to fire his magic bullets.

intro: Cecilus Segmunt (セシルス・セグムント) is the First ranking Divine General of the Sacred Vollachia Empire. He acts as Vincent Vollachia's sword and is hailed as the indisputably strongest individual from the Empire as well as one of the strongest individuals in the modern world alongside the Kingdom's Reinhard van Astrea, the City-States' Halibel, and the Holy Kingdom's Vague Adgard. He played pivotal roles in Arc 7 and Arc 8, and he played supporting roles in The Travelogue of the Finest and The Tale of the Scarlet Princess.
appearance:
Cecilus is a youthful man of the same age as Reinhard, who usually stands out as an oddity to those who see him. His blue eyes, which give off a rather playful and relaxed aura, coupled with his long dark-blue hair which he has tied messily into a ponytail, make Cecilus give off a rather mysterious aura. To further exemplify his messy personality, various strands of long hair can be seen covering the right side of his face, although not to the extent that his right eye is obscured in any way. Completely opposite to his true nature, Cecilus' facial features are soft enough that, when coupled with his slender frame, he could be mistakenly identified as a woman if one were to quickly glance at him. On the left side of his face, just below his mouth, Cecilus has a noticeable mole. Despite the many hundreds of lives he has taken throughout the years, his face isn't burdened by a sense of guilt and his smile is usually described as surprisingly friendly, warm, and welcome.

Although he is the greatest warrior in Vollachia, the Blue Lightning wears clothing commonly found in the western Kararagi City-States. During one of his rare visits to Kararagi, Cecilus fell in love with the clothing and had some custom-made for him to wear on daily basis. His outfit consists of a subdued peach-pink kimono with a purple mist-like pattern along its bottom, a bright blue haori that rests over his kimono with a pair of white diamond-shaped patterns on its breasts, and a pair of hand-made wooden zori sandals on his feet that he takes off during more serious battles. A white sash can also be seen tied around his waist that keeps his blades attached to his side. He wore the same clothing as a teenager and while under the effects of the infantilization technique. As Cecilus has more than two blades, the katanas dangling from his waist often change. The coupling of his youthful appearance and odd dress-sense could at first glance portray an image of a boy playing dress-up, entirely disregarding his cruel and often-times brutal personality.
personality:
Although considered a rather charming and easy-going person, as the strongest member of the Nine Divine Generals, Cecilus is incredibly prideful of his position to the point he believes that he should be the center of the universe and therefore receive attention and praise, which in turn often results in him looking down on other people and treating them as inferior, though he is not unwilling to accept the strengths that other people have. He often speaks in an overly dramatic flair, acting as if he is in the center of the world's stage and that he is being watched by an audience, the Observers or other people, and he often uses theater terms when speaking about everyday life, such as foreshadowing, hero, heroine, climax, main character, performer, leading actor, development, or other such words. He often speaks quite nonsensically, sometimes going off on long tangents that have basically nothing to do with what someone has asked from him, a trait he seems to share with his father, and he is also prone to acting with a certain level of maliciousness when he wishes to ascertain things, such as when he kicked Aldebaran off of a roof for apparently no reason while claiming that he could have been an undead. He's shown to be extremely childish as well, overreacting to small and insignificant things which regularly irritates the people around him. Despite his eccentricity, he is actually quite friendly with the people around him, he believes that the world is filled with blessings, and he is absolutely loyal to the emperor, referring to himself as his sword, and is nigh impossible to bribe.

Although he rarely takes his opponents seriously, he is shown to be overly passionate about fighting, as he was elated seeing how skilled Julius Juukulius was when he attacked him. Following his initial loss against the Sword Saint Reinhard van Astrea, Cecilus went to great lengths in order to illegally trespass the closed borders with the Empire and fulfill his desire to fight the famed Sword Saint once more in order to finally defeat him and prove his superiority. Though, despite his arrogance and childishness, following his duel with Reinhard, he admitted that Reinhard was an incredibly tough opponent and rather than sulking in his failure, he decided to strive and do his best to surpass the Sword Saint. 

He is also implied to be somewhat of a flirt as he told the thugs that attacked him that he would be far happier to give them his signature if they were women. He has shown this side of himself while speaking to Emilia, and he has even claimed to want to show off in such a situation. Though, if he learns that such a person is the object of affection for someone else or that someone else sees them in such a way, though he will remain friendly with such a person, he will back down with his advances. He is also shown to be generous, shown when he gave the owner of a restaurant too many holy coins and he mentioned that she deserved it. He also claims to be the same kind of person as Natsuki Subaru in that he is a promise breaker, and despite the number of lives he has claimed, he does not want to see people who are not his enemies die in great numbers, as he claims that the world would get lonely.

His sole goal is to achieve the Heavenly Sword, a title that is made for the strongest swordsman existing. Contrary to common belief, if it means achieving the Heavenly Sword, he would easily go against the word of Vincent.
history:
Well over ten years ago, Vincent came into contact with young Cecilus and took him under his wing as he recognized his insane prowess with the blade. From there on out, Cecilus acted as Vincent's sworn sword.

The Tale of the Scarlet Princess
Roughly 7 years before the start of the main story, Vincent and the rest of Drizen Vollachia's children entered the Imperial Selection Ceremony, in which they slaughtered each other with the sole goal of surviving and claiming the title of the seventy-seventh Vollachian emperor. During those dangerous times, Vincent often employed Cecilus on different missions, most often on assassinations. One event in particular catapulted Cecilus' name amidst the ranks of the most feared and renowned swordsmen alive; Lamia Godwin and Prisca Benedict orchestrated the Siege on the Abellux Castle. Lamia commanded her army known as the Pruning Corpse to siege the manor's entrance. As a countermeasure, Vincent employed a single swordsman: Cecilus Segmunt. He single-handedly slaughtered the entire army which numbered in hundreds. The word of a one-sided slaughter soon spread throughout the Empire and soon reached the ears of the neighboring countries and kingdoms as well, forever engraving the Blue Lightning's name in history.

Years during Vincent's rule
A couple of years before the main story, Cecilus was tasked with escorting a convoy in Vollachia and act as a bodyguard of an important person; the very same person Elsa Granhiert was sent to assassinate. Cecilus and Elsa proceeded to fight; Cecilus easily came out victorious but slipped up and gave Elsa an opportunity to kill the VIP, which she did. At another point, he engaged in a battle with Arakiya that resulted in the destruction of a portion of the Imperial Capital, and that area was repurposed into a reservoir by Chisha. Likewise, he was also forced to confront and nearly kill his father, Rowan Segmunt, when he plotted to attack the emperor, and he dumped him somewhere where he had a chance to survive.

The Travelogue of the Finest
Shortly after the death of the Lugunican Royal Family (roughly 4–5 months before the start of the main story), Reinhard van Astrea, Julius Juukulius, and Ferris accompanied Miklotov McMahon and Bordeaux Zergev, two members of the Council of Wise Men, on a diplomatic mission to Vollachia in order to negotiate a pact of non-aggression between the Kingdom and the Empire. After an unprecedented turn of events which lead to the three Royal Guards and Vincent escaping to a nearby forest, Cecilus was dispatched and ordered to retrieve the emperor and kill the "murderers". After locating the trio of Julius, Ferris, and Vincent, Cecilus began his faceoff with the Spirit Knight. Seconds before finishing the fight by beheading the knight, Groovy Gumlet and Moguro Hagane arrived at the scene after retreating from the Sword Saint. Pursuing them, Reinhard came to the rescue and took the Blue Lightning's attention, swiftly defeating him with a single kick to his neck afterwards, rendering Cecilus unconscious. Upon waking up later, he resolved himself to eventually seize victory in a battle against Reinhard.

Roughly a month after the signing of the non-aggression pact, Cecilus was sent on a secret mission to assassinate or bring back the perpetrator who wanted to seize the Vollachian throne, Gramdart Holstoy. On his unannounced trip to the Kingdom, Cecilus encountered Julius and Ferris. After exchanging words over a nice cup of tea, Cecilus requested their help as he wanted an opportunity to fight the Sword Saint for real. After initially refusing to give him help, Julius and Ferris finally gave in as if they'd continue refusing, they'd lose their heads and risk further unnecessary bloodshed. They told the Blue Lightning about Reinhard's whereabouts and upon realizing there's no way to fight him, Cecilus decided to stay in the Royal Capital and eagerly await the red-haired knight's return. He spent the next couple of days in the Juukulius Household where he spent his time talking with Joshua Juukulius and sharpening his sword skills. Not long after, Cecilus ran away in search of the Vollachian traitor; it took him no more than a couple of hours to locate him, slaughter his guards and behead him–or so he would have done if Chisha Gold, the Divine General sent to help Cecilus retrieve Gramdart, wouldn't interrupt him. After their successful mission, they were preparing to return back to the Empire when news came of the Sword Saint's return and Cecilus was finally given an opportunity to face off against the most powerful opponent in the world. Reinhard van Astrea with his Dragon Sword Reid unsheathed and Cecilus Segmunt with his beloved blades fought; both survived the battle, which resulted in a draw, confirmed by Cecilus himself.

Sword Identity
About two months before the events of Arc 1, Cecilus and Arakiya were sent to quell the rebellion raised by Yorna Mishigure in response to the death of Zoey. Though Cecilus himself confronted Yorna, he was unable to kill her or deal any lasting damage to her due to her Soul Marriage Technique. In the end, the rebellion came to an end when the soldiers responsible for Zoey's death were caught and killed, and Cecilus's party retreated from Chaosflame.

Imperial Coup
A short time before the events of Arc 7, Cecilus and Chisha talk in the latter’s office. During their conversation, Chisha asked of what Cecilus would do if Vincent and Chisha were at odds, to which Cecilus states that he would take Vincent's side. Because of their friendship, however, he was willing to at least let Chisha try to convince him otherwise. With Chisha trusting him to take care of Vincent after his plans were complete, Cecilus allowed Chisha to infantilize him, and he was sent to the Gladiator Island Ginunhive with the memories of a child.

Undead Busters
Following the Great Disaster, Subaru and Vincent entrusted Spica’s protection to Cecilus and Arakiya while she was hunting down the remaining undead in Vollachia. Unfortunately, when they went to retrieve Arakiya, she immediately attacked Cecilus, leading to a battle between the two. Though he warned Spica to stay back, having every intention of respecting Subaru’s and Vincent’s wishes, Spica was the one who put an end to the fight, using Leaper to incapacitate Arakiya and impressing Cecilus. Afterward, they reported back to Vincent. After a turbulent conversation caused by Cecilus's rambling and Arakiya's aggression, the group finally set off on their mission, with Spica being in charge of keeping Arakiya in check.

After setting forth, they encountered several undead, including Harlein, who the three dispatched with ease. After sitting down for food, they soon encountered the undead Volcas, who clashed with and was defeated by Cecilus. However, because he did not want to let Spica eat his name just yet, this led to an argument between him and Arakiya, while Spica attended to Volcas. Afterward, they returned to Garkla with Volcas, intent on letting Volcas speak with Vincent. Shortly after their arrival, however, Yorna took Volcas away, and the two engaged in combat, everyone else standing to bear witness. Eventually, the battle stopped, and Volcas mentioned that he recognized Yorna as Iris.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
Cecilus is one of the most powerful people in the world and one of the only people considered claimed to have a similar level of martial prowess compared to Reinhard. Even among them, Cecilus’s strength is so immense that he fought against Reinhard to a draw both in the Second Silver Flower Dance before the story’s start and in the non-canon Oboreru IF. Furthermore, in the latter, he was also among the only people to have survived fighting against him. His strength is feared due to having once massacred Lamia Godwin’s Pruning Corps by himself, and it has even been stated that he could kill all of the Imperial Army if he so chose. Likewise, it has also been claimed that he has one of the highest kill counts in the series, further cementing how immensely dangerous he is.

Physical Traits/Flow Method
Extraordinary Swordsmanship: Cecilus is extremely skilled with the sword. Utilizing his inhuman speed and reflexes, Cecilus can move at breakneck speeds, circle his enemies and strike them down with extremely precise and powerful slashes. It is said that as the personification of the sword, Cecilus is capable of killing even invisible things by simply touching his blade. It is noted that most opponents do not manage to block more than one of his half-serious attacks and when Julius was able to block all seven slashes, Cecilus was left genuinely impressed and decided to take him a bit more seriously. When serious, he can move at such speeds that his opponents think they're fighting hundreds of Cecilus clones at the same time. Thanks to the combination of his insane sword talent, inhuman speed and razor-sharp katanas, Cecilus in his early teens, single handedly slaughtered an entire army that was sent to kill Vincent Vollachia, roughly seven years prior to the beginning of the main story. He even managed to cut through Al Shario, a spell that drops a star from the sky and is said to be unavoidable.
Maximum Power Sword Slash: Cecilus unleashes a devastating attack that destroys everything around him and tears through any technique before him. His blade gives off a brilliant white light and upon slashing down on the opponent, the area in front of him is blown apart, which he demonstrated during his battle with the Muspel-empowered Arakiya. A downside to this technique is that if the sword Cecilus uses is of insufficient quality, it will be destroyed immediately after the slash is unleashed. This ability is the same technique utilized by Reinhard during his clashes with Elsa Granhiert and Regulus Corneas.

Extraordinary Strength: Despite mostly being seen wielding swords, Cecilus has immense physical strength. With a single kick, Cecilus can kick Madelyn Eschart's Flying Winged Blade with such force that it can both turn aside the head of the Dragon Mezoreia and create a shockwave on impact, as well as ground said Dragon with ease. With a single chop of his hand, it is capable of creating a shockwave so intense that it was compared to thunder crashing, and the surrounding area caught in the shockwave will collapse. It is even claimed that a chop from his hand is capable of splitting an iron castle in two.

Extraordinary Speed: Cecilus is stated to be the fastest person in the world, surpassing even Reinhard van Astrea. He is able to move as fast as lightning, surpassing human senses, being able to run right through checkpoints without being noticed. When serious, he removes his zori before running and is even able to surpass the speed of a lightning bolt, even able to leave behind afterimages, and even with his zori on, he is capable of running freely even on magma despite them not being fireproof, which Al compared to being similar to a technique by which someone runs on water by taking a step forward before the opposite foot sank. He is also capable of kicking off of even the smallest grain of rubble in the air to propel himself forward. If such small rubble was kicked up during battle, he could use this to perform three-dimension maneuvers, making it appear as if he was kicking off of the air, and likewise, his speed would not be inhibited. In fact, even without rubble, Cecilus is capable of kicking off of the sky, using the ensuing explosion to propel himself like lightning. However, doing so can cause severe damage to whichever leg he uses to kick off of the sky, though it would not necessarily prevent him from being able to run.

Techniques
Cloud Cutting (雲切, Kumokiri): Cecilus can use a technique called Cloud Cutting, a powerful slash of the sword so lightning-fast that it leaves no sound behind and creates a force that can rise to the sky, literally allowing it to cleave clouds in two. For people who lack uncommon courage, the sheer strength of the technique is enough to make them feel as if their own flesh has been cleaved. The technique was created by Cecilus's father, Rowan, who spent his lifetime to devise it. However, Cecilus himself used to not see a use in the technique and only viewed it as something to use for show in order to surprise other people. After recognizing and defeating his father one last time during the Great Disaster, Cecilus used Cloud Cutting in his subsequent fight against Sphinx, using the force of the slash to cleave the latter's fire magic in two before it had a chance to make contact with him.

Other
Extraordinary Intuition: Cecilus has an amazing intuition. It allowed him to figure out Joshua's condition in a few minutes just by the way he walked, perceive the nature of Al's looping ability, recognize the effects of Subaru's Authority (albeit referring to it as "true sight"), predict and dodge all of the impossibly difficult shots of an invisible sniper, and recognize Sphinx following her vessel's transformation into that of the Witch of Greed's. Likewise, it was because of his intuition that he did not unilaterally slaughter all of the undead during the Great Disaster, as he felt as though doing so would not end well.

Hyper Concentration: During battles in which he is forced to give his all, Cecilus's concentration can continuously increase, allowing his thoughts to accelerate at a tremendous speed. Furthermore, by cutting off various senses, this concentration can improve further, allowing his thoughts to speed up even more, to the point that, in his mind, an instant can be slowed to the point that it has stopped.

Great Spatial Awareness: Cecilus is ordinarily capable of remaining aware of everything that is happening in his vicinity, whether or not he is in the middle of battle or whether or not he can actually he see the people around him. Thanks to this, he can act appropriately in accordance with the people or objects around him.

Vigorous Mana: When Cecilus's motivation increases, the mana circulating inside his body can rampage with such inexplicable vigor that it can restore his body heat and instantly evaporate ice holding down his body.

Equipment
thumb|300px|Cecilus wielding the Fiend Sword.
Fiend Sword Murasame (邪剣ムラサメ, Jaken Murasame): The Fiend Sword Murasame is an Enchanted Sword belonging to Cecilus with a cutting edge so mighty that crafting a sheath for it was riddled with complications. Murasame has the ability to sever the perceived “point” signifying something's essence that exists in everything, no matter the person, object, phenomenon, or concept. This allows it to cut through things without a physical form, including curses and contracts. The sword has a very long and storied history. Due to it being an Enchanted Sword, it requires sacrifice and blood in order to satisfy its hunger for violence. In other words, the owner of the Fiend Sword must use it as a killing tool rather often. It also needs suitable compensation in order to be wielded, something that would cost an average wielder their very life. According to Julius, even when sheathed, Murasame emits extreme cruelty and bloodlust. Cecilus obtained Murasame from the storage of the Crystal Palace. It was originally a sword with a different form that was reforged into a katana by Groovy Gumlet.
thumb|175px|Cecilus wielding the Dream Sword.
Dream Sword Masayume (夢剣マサユメ, Muken Masayume): The Dream Sword Masayume is an Enchanted Sword belonging to Cecilus with incredible power. Masayume has the ability to grant its wielder's dreams, or the motivation for a wish they have to come true, in exchange for devouring them. However, a wielder who harbors an extraordinary yearning for their dreams can avoid the Dream Sword devouring their motivation, allowing them to utilize the blade to its full potential, which is what happened in Cecilus's case. It can also sever things in a manner similar but not identical to the Fiend Sword Murasame. It uses dreams as its sheath and can be accessed from a dream of any kind that its owner experiences. Just like Murasame, Masayume has a long and storied past. Due to it being an Enchanted Sword, it requires sacrifice and blood in order to satisfy its hunger for violence. Were Masayume's owner in an altered shape, it would not be as unyielding in recognizing its owner as Murasame would be. As with Murasame, Julius notes that, Masayume, even when sheathed, emits extreme cruelty and bloodlust.
Other Swords: Other than his Enchanted Swords, Cecilus has shown to use other swords. However, the one he proclaimed to be his fifth best was broken by Julius.

intro: Chuden Agri (チュデン・アグリ) is the vice president of the Hoshin Company. He was the former president of the Chuden Company before it was inherited and renamed by his apprentice, Anastasia Hoshin.
appearance: Chuden is a fox eyed man around 30 years of age.
history:
Anastasia's Kararagi Merchant Path
Approximately ten years prior to the start of the story's beginning, having been impressed with Anastasia's business talent, Chuden decided to hire her as his apprentice in the Chuden Company. Ricardo, who had worried that the company could be a pretext for one that dealt with slaves, immediately headed to the Chuden Company, where he met Chuden at the reception, as well as Anastasia. Ricardo demanded to know what he wanted with Anastasia, suspecting foul play, but Chuden assuaged his fears and told him that he had hired her after being impressed by her talent. Ricardo eventually accepted Anastasia working for Chuden, and he offered his services as a mercenary to him. Chuden accepted and hired Ricardo to work at the company as his personal bodyguard. He was given a new collar that marked his status as the "hound" of the company, though the collar had its control gem removed.

At some point after this, he relinquished his company to Anastasia, who renamed it into the Hoshin Company, and he became its vice president following the company's relocation from Banan to Ivada.

name_jp: ベルステツ・フォンダルフォン
alias: His Excellency (閣下, Kakka)
intro: Berstetz Fondalfon (ベルステツ・フォンダルフォン) is the Prime Minister of the Sacred Vollachia Empire, and the second-in-command after the emperor in terms of political power. Though playing minor roles in both The Travelogue of the Finest and The Tale of the Scarlet Princess, he was one of the main antagonists of Arc 7 as one of the masterminds behind the Imperial Civil War, and he played a supporting role in Arc 8.
appearance: Berstetz is a very old man of short stature. He has relatively long grey hair that is tied back with an aged and wrinkled face. Underneath his slightly crooked nose, he sports a bushy mustache. Befitting of his position as the Prime Minister, Berstetz can be seen wearing a dark pink long-sleeved robe in addition to a purple and uniform with the Empire's symbol, the Sword Wolf, near its base.
personality:
Berstetz is a very wise and shrewd old man who is easily able to outsmart people. He is loyal to the Empire, and though he was never able to due to his meager strength, he always wanted to be one of the Empire's Sword Wolves. As such, when Lamia saw worth in him, he felt gratitude. When he was loyal to Lamia as her subordinate and strategist, he was willing to assist her in the murders of her siblings in order to put her on the throne. Despite having been heavily loyal to Lamia before her passing, he had no qualms about working for the emperor partially responsible for her death, as he was more than capable of leading the country to prosperity. However, that loyalty is so strong that if he believes that the emperor is not doing his duty as the country's ruler, he is willing to scheme to dethrone said ruler and replace them with someone more fitting who will do their duties as expected of them, even if he knows he might lose his head were he to fail.

Despite his advanced age and his rather meager power, he also believes in the way of the Empire, and he is willing to die fighting in order to rid the country of its enemies, even if said threat was his undead former master.

Berstetz seems to have more going for him than what meets the eye as Vincent himself seemed to be aware that something was off with the old man. According to Ubilk, the Empire's Stargazer, Berstetz hides “hell itself” within him.
history:
The Tale of the Scarlet Princess
During the Imperial Selection Ceremony, Berstetz, having been a Count of unknown rank, acted as a strategist under Lamia Godwin's command, helping her achieve her goal of slaughtering every single one of her half-brothers and half-sisters in order to be crowned as the seventy-seventh emperor of the Vollachia Empire. During the Siege on the Abellux Castle, Berstetz helped to command the army led by Lamia by controlling the artillery on her behalf. After Lamia realized the battle was lost, she ordered him to cover her retreat. Following Lamia's death and Vincent's coronation as the seventy-seventh emperor of the Vollachia Empire, Berstetz started working under him and was eventually appointed as the Prime Minister, granting him political strength second only to the emperor himself. 

The Travelogue of the Finest
Six months before the events of Arc 1, two members of the Council of Wise Men, Miklotov McMahon and Bordeaux Zergev, accompanied by Reinhard van Astrea, Julius Juukulius, and Ferris, chose to go on a diplomatic visit to the Empire in order to sign a non-aggression pact between the Dragon Kingdom of Lugunica and the Empire. While not immediately meeting with the five diplomats, Berstetz acted in the shadows, swiftly getting rid of the traitorous noble who planned the coup d'état during the aforementioned diplomats' visit in the Empire, effectively keeping the rebellion at bay.

Sword Identity
Two to three months after this, Madelyn Eschart was suggested by Berstetz to inherit Balleroy Temeglyph's position as the 9th ranking Divine General, despite not having any concrete accomplishments and being largely unknown to the other Divine Generals. After Yorna's rebellion, his suggestion was confirmed, and Madelyn was appointed as the 9th ranking Divine General to the reluctance of the emperor.

Imperial Civil War
Sometime before the events of Arc 7, his frustration with the emperor for not siring a child as his duty as the emperor requires was reaching its peak. Taking advantage of this, Chisha Gold, who was attempting to thwart the Great Disaster by replacing Vincent as the one who would die, offered Berstetz the proposal to remove Vincent from his throne, hiding his true motives. Accepting the proposal, he and Chisha led a coup that resulted in Goz Ralfon's defeat and Vincent retreating to the Buddheim Jungle. Afterward, he and Chisha sent imperial soldiers to the jungle to flush him out. Likewise, they sent Arakiya to Guaral as reinforcements.

Shortly after the Fall of Guaral, when Todd Fang returned to Lupugana with the injured Arakiya, Berstetz officially made Todd Arakiya's subordinate. Afterward, he gave them a directive to go to Ginunhive and give Gustav Morello an order from himself as the Prime Minister, rather than an order from the emperor, that the lives all of the prisoners on the island were to be reaped. Otherwise, he was to be killed. Similarly, he ordered Madelyn to attack Guaral with her flying dragons in response to Guaral's fall. With those failures, however, and the rise of a "black-haired crown prince", he and Chisha prepared for an all-out civil war with the Rebel Army.
abilities_text:
Keen Intellect: While Berstetz is not a powerful warrior, he is an intelligent man, and he was the one to act as both an advisor and strategist to Lamia during the Imperial Selection Ceremony. Even after the selection, Vincent found his intellect worthy of praise, and he took him on as the Prime Minister. His intellect and foresight are on a similar level to Chisha Gold, and the two were both capable of leading a civil war together without allowing anyone to found out.

Equipment: Berstetz wears a meteor ring on his finger that is imbued with the element of fire. It has enough power to blow out the side of one of a coupled dragon carriage’s walls.
