intro: Arakiya (アラキア) is the Second ranking Divine General of the Sacred Vollachia Empire. She played a major antagonistic role in Arc 7, and a major supporting role in Arc 8. She also played a supporting role in The Tale of the Scarlet Princess.
appearance:
Arakiya has red eyes, uneven dog ears, wears only the minimum clothing that allows her to keep her modesty so to help her attract micro-spirits, and has short silver hair with one of her bangs being red, and long, drooping silver ears that are black at their tips. She also wears an ornate eye patch on her left eye, which she cannot see out of, and a sash-like decoration on her right hip.

Following her defeat in Guaral’s city hall, Arakiya was cut down by Priscilla's Yang Sword, leaving a nastily deep and cauterized scar spanning across the entirety of her back.
personality:
As a spirit eater, Arakiya has a diluted sense of self and ego that is neither particularly strong or weak. She also takes certain measures to maintain her sense of self, as the side effects of her being a spirit eater directly affect her personality. One of those measures, of course, is wearing the clothes that she does, but more importantly, Arakiya needs a sort of emotional anchor: her "pillar", which in her case was Priscilla, an older sister figure, who she considered her "sun".

Most of Arakiya's personality is defined by her fierce loyalty to her pillar, Priscilla. As imprinting is something deeply instilled in spirit eaters, Arakiya's mind and power are occupied and wielded for Priscilla, and she became the reason for her existence. Her immense loyalty leads her to acting solely for her and obeying her as her right hand, even going as far to neglect herself. She is very protective of Priscilla as well, going as far as to attack Cecilus both on Priscilla's command and out of anger towards him. She was even willing to devour the likes of the Stone in order to fight and protect her, despite knowing that doing so could kill her; she did this on two occasions, the first time to fight for her and the second time in an effort to rescue her. Likewise, this loyalty and protectiveness makes her someone who is easy to use or deceive. Vincent once used this to have her fake Priscilla's death; Chisha Gold used the girl's wish to have Priscilla sitting on the Vollachian throne to have her assist in the Imperial Civil War on his side, even if it meant confronting Priscilla and injuring her to make her stay; Sphinx used her desperation to try and rescue Priscilla to make her devour the rest of the Stone to rescue her, despite it being part of Sphinx's schemes to have her die and end the country as a result.

Outside of that, Arakiya also has a sense of attachment toward those who feel like they lost someone close and even wish for vengeance, something that others have also taken advantage of; Todd Fang used this as a way for her to protect him until they made it back to the Imperial Capital. Likewise, once she trusts someone, she is willing to listen to them, which Todd also used to make her fight smarter and more efficiently, and she would even take such a person as her own subordinate. She is also rather kind and somewhat naive; when she first met Aldebaran on Ginunhive, after listening to his self-deprecation, she innocently refuted his words. She also has a temper, however. For various reasons, she carries a grudge against both Vincent and Cecilus. In the case of the former, she was willing to kill him when she had the chance for Priscilla to be put on the throne, though she was also willing to listen to him as the emperor before this since he also saved Priscilla from being killed during the Imperial Selection. On the other hand, she is constantly hostile towards Cecilus, leading her to attacking him on various occasions. This being said, it is thanks to Cecilus's behavior that her ego did not fully collapse after she was separated from Priscilla, as his presence stoked her inferiority and stimulated her individuality.

Following Priscilla's demise, Arakiya was heavily affected, hiding herself away in a depression. Her sadness and rage culminated into yet another battle with Cecilus, and she even rejected people who showed her kindness like Spica. However, despite this, she did not completely reject Spica's kindness, and it was later noted by Medium O'Connell that her mood overall improved after traveling with Spica and Cecilus.

Despite having taken in the entirety of the Stone, she does not seem to have been affected personality-wise.
history:
The Tale of the Scarlet Princess
When she was young, numerous sacrifices were made in order to make Arakiya into a spirit eater. However, the organization responsible for doing this were believed to have been taken out in part by Olbart Dunkelkenn, and even he believed that what they had done had gone too far. At an unknown point in time after this, she was presented to Drizen Vollachia, and he offered her to his daughter, Prisca, for unknown reasons. Thanks to this, Arakiya grew up with Prisca Benedict and was her sworn sword and foster sister before and during the Imperial Selection Ceremony.

During the Siege on the Abellux Castle, a fierce battle between Prisca Benedict, Lamia Godwin, and Vincent Abellux, Arakiya fought against Chisha Gold, swiftly defeating and almost killing him. As Lamia tried to exploit the fact Priscilla and Vincent would inevitably duel, she set up a bombardment of the forest Prisca was located in. Arakiya had no other choice but to eat a portion of the Stone, Muspel, to save everyone from certain death, though she almost died in the process.

In the months following the battle, Arakiya made a deal with Vincent, which gave her a chance to save Prisca from certain death by Vincent's hand. As Prisca received a bottle of sake mixed with poison, Arakiya drank half of it, which resulted in Prisca's life being saved, however, Arakiya herself lost vision in her left eye. Upon waking up in the Crystal Palace, she was greeted by Cecilus Segmunt and Chisha Gold, who explained her situation and notified her of Vincent's request for her to join his ranks.

One day, Vincent heard of a rebellion on the Gladiator Island Ginunhive, and he sent 2000 people to exterminate the perpetrator, two of them including Arakiya and Olbart. After arriving at the island, they discussed how to get the drawbridge down, to which Arakiya devoured a lesser water spirit in order to become water and bypass the witchbeasts infesting the water. On the way, she followed the scent of blood and discovered Al on an island-like pile of rocks in the lake. After giving him first aid, the two made their way to the island, where Al explained things about an enemy called Hornet and how somethings on the island worked. After having her burn the body of a poison-infested shinobi nearby, the two made their way to the control tower, where Hornet lay in wait. After Al mentioned that he could do nothing about Hornet, Arakiya, still invisible after devouring a lesser wind spirit, attempted to sneak by Hornet, but she was easily seen through and quickly cornered. Al, having seen this, stepped forward to defend her and fought Hornet in her place, surprising her with his "miracles" while fighting her. As she attempted to get up, she heard the voice Priscilla speaking to the gladiators, and Arakiya stood to fight against Hornet with Al. Eventually, the two led Hornet to the area with the poison, where Hornet ultimately died. Afterward, the two lowered the drawbridge, allowing the soldiers to reach the island. After a short conversation with Olbart and Al, she thanked Al and left the island with Olbart.

When Priscilla and her new husband Jorah Pendleton were accused of treason against the emperor, Goz Ralfon was sent to deal with them, and Arakiya joined them. Though Jorah was killed, Arakiya let Priscilla go, and she reported that she committed suicide, eventually becoming the Second of the Nine Divine Generals.

At some point, she and Cecilus fought in an area of the Imperial Capital. The aftermath of their battle left the entire area destroyed, leaving it to be later repurposed by Chisha to be a reservoir.

Sword Identity
After Madelyn's failure to quell the rebellion of Yorna Mishigure, Arakiya and Cecilus were sent to deal with the matter. During the fight, Arakiya razed a portion of Chaosflame to the ground, but she was unable to kill and of its residents or even Yorna herself. In the end, when Yorna's demands were met, Arakiya and Cecilus pulled back from Chaosflame, and the rebellion subsided.

Undead Busters
Following the events of the Great Disaster, Arakiya hid herself away in a shack-like building, depressed over losing the source of her light, Priscilla, while she survived. Having been tasked with guarding Spica and using her own power to sense the remaining zombies left in the country, Cecilus and Spica went to collect her, resulting in yet another fight between her and Cecilus. However, Spica ultimately put a stop to the fight by using Leaper on Arakiya, leaving her unable to keep fighting. Afterward, they reported back to Vincent. After a turbulent conversation caused by Cecilus's rambling and Arakiya's aggression, the group finally set off on their mission, with Spica being in charge of keeping Arakiya in check.

After setting forth, they encountered several undead, including Harlein, who the three dispatched with ease. After sitting down for food, they soon encountered the undead Volcas, who clashed with and was defeated by Cecilus. However, because he did not want to let Spica eat his name just yet, this led to an argument between him and Arakiya, while Spica attended to Volcas. Afterward, they returned to Garkla with Volcas, intent on letting Volcas speak with Vincent. Shortly after their arrival, however, Yorna took Volcas away, and the two engaged in combat, everyone else standing to bear witness. Eventually, the battle stopped, and Volcas mentioned that he recognized Yorna as Iris.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
Arakiya is one of the most powerful people in Vollachia, whose strength allows her to contend with the likes of Cecilus. Thanks to her connection to Muspel, she has the power of one of the Four Great Spirits, making her abilities with magic tremendous. In terms of sheer firepower, Arakiya is the one most capable of causing widespread devastation from among the Nine Divine Generals.

Techniques
Spirit Eating (精霊喰らい, Seirei Kurai): Arakiya has the power to eat spirits, assimilate her body with them, and use their powers as her own without needing to form a contract with them. Among all the spirit eaters, Arakiya has surpassed all of her predecessors in strength. Doing so comes with the risk of ceasing to be human and extreme self-harm. By eating a Water micro-spirit, for example, she's described as almost becoming one with water, allowing her to swim past witchbeasts residing in the waters, undetected. Her power is so strong that it even allowed her to take in one of the Four Great Spirits' power without losing her sanity. Arakiya is able to use other spirits' powers until she completely digests them, and it is unknown what happens to spirits, after she eats them. Furthermore, the firmer one's sense of self is, the better they are with their power. This ability does have a downside, however. If exposed to larger quantities of mana, Arakiya will become confused and eventually sick, as she starts experiencing symptoms of mana poisoning. This trick was used against her at the Fall of Guaral, when Vincent flooded the entire room with mana, confusing her and allowing Al to hold his own against her. Also, if she devours a spirit that is too powerful, such as one of the Four Great Spirits, she risks her body self-destructing, and likewise, even if her body can contain such power without destroying itself, if she cannot acclimate to said power, it will cause her to temporarily lose control of her body and go berserk. Furthermore, during the acclimation process, the immense power threatens to paint over her sense of self with much more fervor than other spirits. This ability was originally a secret technique wielded by unnamed tribes living on the frontier of the Empire but were wiped out due to the ability's potential. After devouring the entirety of Muspel and fully assimilating with it thanks to the Dream Sword and the Priscilla's Soul Marriage Technique, her power has increased severalfold, and now, her life is synonymous with the Stone, and in turn, at present, the Empire.

Shadow Diving: Although it is unspecified if she achieved this by devouring a yin spirit, Arakiya can mask her presence by diving into the shadows.

Magic/Spiritual Arts
Arakiya’s spirit-eating gives her a plethora of abilities surrounding the elements of mana governed by spirits, including:
Fire: Arakiya can launch intense flames which can destroy ranks of soldiers or half of a city with ease. She can envelop her limbs as well as her whole body in fire. When doing so, she is often seen flying in midair, and when her whole body is fire, she becomes unable to be grabbed until she reverts to her normal state or unless someone has a way to bypass those flames and directly strike her body, such as with the Yang Sword. The flames can also change color, becoming blue, and the flames are also intense enough that they can scorch the ground to naught and even paint the sky red. While under Muspel's influence, she was even capable of producing so much heat around herself that foreign objects will threaten to burst into flame and turn to ash, and both she and the space around her appears distorted. She has also displayed the ability to enlarge her fist of flame to ten meters, and her strike packs enough punch to make even the Giant Magic Crystal Soldier stumble.
Wind: Arakiya can summon powerful gusts of wind that can devastate and uproot the earth with ease and blow her enemies away with force equivalent to be stricken by a giant palm, and even someone of Priscilla's caliber can be threatened to be crushed by it if it her directly. She also has the ability to assimilate into wind, making herself invisible. She can also use the wind to lift and hurl hundreds of buildings towards her target if she wishes, as well as to fly.
Water: Arakiya can summon jets of water powerful enough to decapitate people or tear through the land with ease, or summon a massive flash flood. She can also fill people’s heads with water to make them burst from the inside. Additionally, she can turn her whole body into water to swim at high speeds.
Yang: She can turn her body into light to both phase through attacks and counterattack in all directions. She can also unleash belts of light with enough power to evaporate anything they hit.
Earth: Numerous magic crystals burst out of Arakiya’s body, some in scattered places across her body with other forming wings from her back. The crystals are sharp enough that they can be used like blades and slash through her enemies. However, this form was the effect of Muspel's great power attempting to devour through and spill out of her body, so it is unlikely she is able to use this form at will. Regardless, she can fire off countless of these crystals, which Cecilus has compared to diamonds, like missiles with intense speed and power, create and manipulate crystal pillar from all directions, and generate stone constructs to grab and crush her opponent, which even Cecilus Segmunt struggled to avoid or fight against. The projectile crystals that she fires can act independently of each other, and attempting to defend by normal means aagainst them can be self-destructive. Likewise, these crystals are capable of breaking down and reconstructing themselves, which allows them to multiply into numbers unenumerable, thus making them next to impossible to avoid.
Lightning: Though the process by which she generates it is unknown, Arakiya is capable of summoning lightning as part of her attacks.

Massive Mana Pool: After devouring a portion of one of the Four Great Spirits, her mana pool expanded greatly, allowing her to generate all forms of magic. This pool increased later when she devoured and assimilated with the rest of the Stone.
Mana Sensing: Thanks to her connection to the Stone, she is able to sense the flow of mana that is connected to the Great Spirit. Using this, she can sense the zombies that were revived by its power and locate them. However, this ability seems to be exclusive to anything that is using its power.

Flight: After having devoured the entirety of Muspel, Arakiya has displayed the ability to float in the air without the assistance of the elements. While she can achieve flight through turning her body into flame or using the wind, it seems that she doesn't necessarily require doing so, as she was seen floating while she was influenced by Muspel's power. This being said, it is unclear if she can do this freely without Muspel's influence.

Physical Traits/Flow Method
Enhanced Physicality: With years of experience and becoming one of the strongest people in the Empire after Cecilus alone, she is capable of fighting against Cecilus, and though she has yet to defeat him, their clashes are devastating enough that they tend to cause extreme collateral damage. After devouring the entirety of Muspel, Arakiya became significantly tougher to damage. She was even capable of withstanding a chop from the infantilized Cecilus, which is capable of splitting an iron castle in two, and she was able to counter him rather easily.

Intangibility: Having taken in the power of Muspel, Arakiya can switch back and forth between a physical and mana-based body, allowing her to temporarily become intangible. Though this can be exhausted should she exhaust her Od, with Muspel’s immeasurable amount of mana, the chances of this are practically moot, effectively making Arakiya unkillable.

Extended Lifespan: Due to absorbing Muspel, Arakiya's lifespan has been dramatically extended. In the Sasageru IF, she had lived for 400 years.

Equipment
Wand: Arakiya carries a tri-pronged wand with her to help channel her magic.

name: Colette
intro: Colette (コレット) is a girl who once lived as an outcast in a forest after being shunned from her village for being a “Beast”. She, alongside Palmyra, later joined Omega and formed the Omega Party.
appearance: Colette is a girl with light brown hair, brown eyes, youthful-looking features, and a short stature. She wears a green coat, a green trapper hat, and average-sized boots. She and Palmyra have matching hairpins.
personality: Colette was initially presented as a recluse with a warm yet wary temperament. Due to the prejudices she faced as a result of her circumstances, she was labelled a “Beast”, and attempted to conform to those expectations until she met Omega and they began to travel together. Her true disposition was quickly shown to be that of a kind and accepting girl who quickly befriends and makes an effort to understand the people she meets. In a similar vein, this makes it to where she is willing to accept other people in her party and not worry about potential problems that might come with accepting them. Because of her innocent nature and vulnerability, she is often excluded from discussions on grim matters with her companions, and her friend Palmyra is particularly protective of her.
history:
Early Life
As a young child, Colette's parents were on business outside of their home village and brought back home a bracelet they received during their travels as a memento for her. This bracelet was the Beast Protection bracelet, a meteor that transformed its user into a “Beast” whenever it sensed danger. Due to Colette being a young child, this effect could cause her to feel danger even in a nightmare. As such, she transformed into a “Beast” when the bracelet sensed danger, unwittingly killing her parents in the process. Although taken in by other families, she was eventually outcast from her village after being accused of being a Witch for surviving supposed witchbeast assaults that would kill everyone near her. As a result, she grew a warped belief that she herself was a Witch and tried to perform rituals to become one, turning into the “Beast” and killing animals to do so, with her friend Palmyra making graves for the slain animals.

The Requirements to be a Witch
One day, Colette happened to meet an elven girl being swept along the river she was at and saved her from its currents. She introduced herself as Omega, and the two got to know one another over the course of several days, exchanging stories from their pasts. Omega decided to take a walk on another day, Colette informed her to not travel to the eastern side of the forest to avoid a witchbeast that had been attacking people there, though she visited anyways, meeting Palmyra there. Upon returning, Omega relayed to Colette her intent to leave the forest but take care of the witchbeast first as a show of gratitude for her kindness, which the young girl hesitantly accepted. That night, she travelled to the eastern side of the forest and attempted to murder the beast herself until Palmyra came and revealed that it was Colette. Piecing together the circumstances behind the “Beast” and its attacks, Omega manifested her true form to Palmyra and the unconscious Colette, before deciding to set off for the village in hopes of setting things straight with the villagers. However, this only made things worse for Colette, as she was forced to leave the area as a consequence for being acquainted with an actual Witch. Seeing as how Colette had nowhere else to go and Palmyra had used up all of her courtesy for the village, the two of them were invited by Omega to join her, officially forming their party.

One Wild Night
The trio then proceeded to cross over into Gusteko. One day, they were caught in a severe blizzard and rescued by Noelle Tuérico, an Itinerant Preacher of the Gustekan Church, after Omega launched a fire spell into the distance. They waited for Omega to regain her energy in a makeshift snow house Noelle created and spoke with her in the meantime, learning about the term Silver Blessing, her position in the Gustekan Church, and the nearby church building they can use as a refuge. They visit the church once Omega is rejuvenated and acquaint themselves with Podoso, Admonsah, and Maqueena, each of whom had come to the church to meet the pastor who lives there, Coatl. The trio learned of Coatl's history of having saved a local town from the effects of an avalanche unintentionally caused by the Ice Thieves and how he took up a position of the town's watcher following his charity towards its people, becoming known by the moniker Saint of the Avalanche. Maqueena and Podoso split off from everyone else to visit another part of the church, and another visitor named Trellock arrives while they are out. Eventually, Maqueena discovers something and screams, prompting everyone else to follow after her to find what has caused her fear. They all stumble upon Coatl's corpse, prompting Omega to say that there was a cold-blooded killer among them.

Omega took charge of the situation, using detective work to determine the killer's identity. She heard from Podoso that there had been a string of serial murders, with Coatl being the eighth known victim. The other victims were peddlers and travelers. Querying him about the seventh victim, Omega then sets her sights on Admonsah, whom she was certain was associated with them. They learn Admonsah was a former slave who unexpectedly killed his owner. Colette scolded Omega for the presumption that Admonsah had acted out of malice and proposed that he was acting in self-defense, which led to him being unequivocally forgiven by a majority of the group. Omega tries to ascertain why Coatl would be murdered, searching for any hidden savings. Suddenly, everyone but Maqueena in the room fell asleep to the effects of the Muskrim flower, and she made her getaway with Coatl's collection of magic stones, not wanting to stay and fall victim to his murderer, and Noelle chased after her. While Omega, who had woken up, went to deal with them, the culprit responsible for the serial murderers, Trellock, attempted to murder Colette, but her Beast Protection Bracelet activated, severely injuring him. In the end, they pretended that Noelle had apprehended Trellock and left, Podoso decided to take in Admonsah, and Maqueena was forced to stop conning people. With her revenge foiled, Noelle was left aimless. Colette proposed for her to join their group to which she accepted upon Omega's approval.

One Wild Night Extra
Later, the party decided to head to the town Podoso had told them about. Eventually, they set up camp, and while Colette and Noelle set up the camp, Palmyra decided to talk with Omega about including Noelle in their travels, worried about getting her involved in their troubles, which included Omega being a half-elf Witch and Colette's bracelet. Omega believed that there was nothing to worry about, and shortly after, Noelle, who had heard part of their conversation appeared and said that she already knew about Omega's secret and chose to follow them regardless. Though Palmyra asked if she had a thing for odd people and Noelle's joking reply that she did, just like Palmyra, she claimed to be just as odd, as she was an itinerant preacher from the Gustekan Church who had decided to leave. Though Palmyra thought it wasn't as bad as Omega's secret, Omega told her that she was underestimating the Church and what they bestowed Noelle, and the two claimed that they would not be amicable toward her effectively breaking a contract, something which might end up leading to them falling into her mess. Though Palmyra told Omega to be prepared to fight, when Noelle told her to feel free to kick her from the party if she ever became a burden, to which she replied by saying not to underestimate her and spoke of her own circumstances, basically unintentionally cornering Noelle into staying in the party after saying not to use Colette as an excuse. Colette arrived shortly after, and the group decided not to talk to her about their conversation. Instead, they ate, and Noelle explained repairs that she had made to their equipment and offered her knowledge of how to use their equipment and how to survive in Gusteko, including knowledge on the Gustekan Church, to which Palmyra and Omega realized that they wouldn't be able to survive in Gusteko without Noelle.

Omega in Wonderland
The party continued to trudge to the snows of Gusteko, with Palmyra and Omega becoming exhausted. Attempting to give Palmyra some more energy, Colette attempted to let her use her bracelet, but when Palmyra tried, it left her weak and vomiting. Omega explained the reason for this, claiming she allowed it to happen because she wanted to see the look on her face. Afterward, she had Noelle carry Palmyra while Colette carried her. As the got closer to the town of Sylphoa, Omega dispelled a barrier, and eventually they reached the town, where she and Colette fell subject to the Dream Arts spell that had been cast over the town.

Impressed with the size of the space and likening it to her Castle of Dreams, even claiming it as superior to herself, Omega cast Al Shario in order to lure out the caster. The caster, Lilac, appeared shortly after, erasing the star Omega summoned and questioning who they were. After a small dispute, she left convincing her to take down the spell to Colette. Despite her standoffish attitude, Omega claimed that Colette's words were getting through to her. However, upon hearing Omega's use of a loan word, Lilac wanted to know where she heard it, leading to negotiations. Despite becoming frustrated with her and even slapping her, she decided to give Omega a chance to take care of the Temple Knight who had come after her, breaking the seal that she'd placed. The fight that followed was short lived as the Witches of Sin quickly dispatched her, much to Lilac's shock. Shortly after, Palmyra entered the dream space with a message from Lilac's partner, Shion.

Following this, after Omega spoke to the other Temple Knight who had come to retrieve Mikli and had him leave with her and report the death of the heretic, Lilac released the people of Sylphoa from her dream world, and Omega offered Shion and Lilac to join her party. Since she couldn't quite trust the two, having just met them, she would give them a chance to look into her memories with their Dream Arts, giving them a chance to find the person from which the loan words they speak come from. The two accepted her offer and joined the party.

Witch Trials
One day, having moved on from Sylphoa, the Omega Party was walking in a snow field, where they encountered a Snow Blight. However, Omega swiftly dispatched it with Minya. Soon after, they arrived at Limbus, where signs claiming it was forbidden to go out at night and to comply with the "vows of the faith". Though slightly concerned about the town's eeriness, as the group was low on supplies, they decided to enter Limbus, where after a few minutes, they found themselves surrounded by the townsfolk who were armed with farming tools. Though they attempted to calm the townsfolk and offer them a gift in the form of the Snow Blight's crystallized head, they instead accuse her of being a Witch after seeing it, leading Omega to warn Colette against using her bracelet's transformation and Lilac from turning back into Shion, else they be declared Witches. Thanks to the appearance of Nananna Pezza and speaking with Noelle, she was able to vouch for them and clear them of being Witches.

Omega's group finds an inn to reside in where they discussed the issue at present, warning everyone about how easily they could be made into scapegoats whether for their abilities, race, or even the look in their eyes, and Noelle explained about Witch Hunts and Witch Trials being rare occurrences in Gusteko that Itinerant Preachers were sometimes sent to deal with. Although wanting to leave the town quickly, the group decides to stay in the town to help Noelle repay her debt to Nananna, and soon after, they meet with Nananna when she arrived to ask for the group's assistance. That night, the Witch Hunt is for a person named Piditz who had been tipped off as a Witch, and Nananna wanted him taken into custody only. When they later spotted Piditz and chased after him, Omega split off to corner him, only to find Mireille Hetia using her spiritual arts to kill Piditz. Thanks to being near the body, Omega was quickly turned into a scapegoat and declared a Witch so that Mireille could cover up her kill and at least prevent her from getting in the way of her and Nananna's revenge, and Omega was taken into custody.

Later, Colette visits Omega, and they point out that killings began before the party arrived, which should clear Omega's name, but instead, Mireille decides to have her executed anyway, and Palmyra objects to Edmon Quayle. As part of Omega's plan, Noelle persuades Nananna to speak up, and Nananna insists on the town holding a Witch Trial for Omega, and Palmyra declares that if she is a Witch that she would burn with her. At the inn, the party discusses how if the scale of this event expands, they will be unable to prevent the spread of the news this time, which could result in the party's persecution, even abroad, and their possible extradition back to the church. To clear their names, Colette states that they should find the real culprit for the murders. Lilac and Colette go to gather information around the town, and they meet with Mireille, who explained to them how the hunts started.

The next day, the Witch Trial is being held for Omega, overseen by Nananna and the Town Hall, while Palmyra acts as Omega's attorney. Despite her arguments, Edmon counter with his supposed knowledge of the Witches and Omega's chatter does not help. Colette speaks up and claims that she believes that things will not go as the council claims, as people will begin to notice that the entire event seems off, which resounds with the townsfolk. Because of this, Palmyra claims that there is a conspiracy, which Edmon fights against and asks for Nananna's assistance. Because she sides with the town, Lilac and Shion believe her to be part of the conspiracy, and they decide to use their dream arts to influence the people's mental states. Palmyra then claims that the council is using the Witch rumors to get rid of inconvenient people, which Edmon also fights against, though is quickly silenced when she states she heard it herself from a council member and declares that there is no Witch. Unfortunately, Omega claims otherwise.

Despite angering Palmyra, Omega decides to clear things up by declaring that there were two conspiracies taking place in town. Despite Nananna trying to prevent her from talking, Omega ignores her and explains that many of the victims were relatives of council members, and she claims that Nananna is the second conspirator, calling her the bastard child of Edmon whose mother was banished from the town, and as a result, she despised the town. Noelle later appears and confirms that her actions were in response to the death of an elderly healer, and she claims that Nananna tried to remove her from the trial by knocking her out since her only ire was with Limbus. Afterward, Noelle declares that the secretary, Mireille, was helping Nananna, as she was a bastard child of Edmon as well, and she stated how the corpses of Piditz and other people connected to the council and other outside officials were already dumped in a hole. Omega also declares that she witnessed Mireille killing Piditz. Enraged, Mireille uses her spiritual arts to char Edmon's arm with blue fire, and with the intent of killing the entire council, surrounds the council with blue fire, and she and Nananna stand against them. Although Omega is fine with leaving things as they are and taking their leave, Colette states she doesn't want things to end like this, and Omega decides to end the fighting in response to her plea, burning through her restraints and declaring herself a Witch.

Later, as Omega's party begins to leave the town, Noelle says her goodbyes to Nananna, and it is declared that the evil spirit accompanying Mireille will be disposed of. Likewise, it is claimed that Edmon's position is under threat with both his severe injuries and the loss of the citizens' trust, and Mireille claims she was mistaken about real Witches. Despite Colette believing that things were settled peacefully, however, Omega thinks to herself that Limbus would soon face its destruction, as since Omega, Nananna, and Mireille were not executed, there would be continuous Witch Hunts and deaths for scapegoats for the whole incident. Although considering telling Colette about this, she decides against it.

Miasma Resistance: Colette seems to have a higher resistance to miasma compared to the average person, as noted by Minerva. Despite having been exposed to the miasma of Omega, which had previously caused numerous fully grown men to go mad and kill themselves, Colette showed no signs of being negatively affected by it.

Equipment: Colette owns the Beast Protection Bracelet (獣護輪, Juugorin), a meteor that allows the user to transform into a beast to protect themselves against danger when the bracelet senses it. first_game: Re:Zero Lost in Memories
intro: Alcor (アルコル) is an exclusive character from the video game Re:Zero Lost in Memories. He is one of the main antagonists of the game.
appearance: Alcor wears a black coat with black fur around the collar and a purple tracksuit inside with a large black scar on the torso. He wears a white mask with a large purple scar across his right eye and black feathers behind the mask. It was later revealed that Alcor was an illusion of Subaru created by Lilac. When unmasked, he has black hair and dark circles under his eyes.
personality: Alcor's personality was the opposite of Subaru's. Alcor has a cold and heartless personality as if any emotions from him was gone. He also claims himself to be the "real" Natsuki Subaru.
history: Unlike the loops that Subaru fought, Alcor was from the failed loop where he had tried to defeat Petelgeuse. He had died so many times up to the point that he had discarded his original name and adopted the name Alcor and took on a different appearance.
abilities_text:
Return by Death (死に戻り Shinimodori): Return by Death is an Authority that allows Alcor to return back to an unspecified, unpredictable and uncontrollable "save point" after his death. It happens instantly after his life is taken and there's no lag between the point of death and the point of resurrection. To Alcor, it looks exactly as if someone switched camera angles inside his head and the sudden influx of new information and sensations often makes him feel dizzy and confused. This ability was given to him by Satella as a means to help him save the ones he loves, should he need it.
Penalties: Alcor is unable to reveal his ability to others. There are three primary penalties for attempting to do so:
Alcor will be forcibly and painfully silenced by the Witch's hand, and, in some cases, die.
Anyone who is told about Return by Death might potentially die.
It will increase the density of the Witch's Scent at least for a short time, which will draw any witchbeasts in the immediate area to him like moths to a flame.
Memory Retainment: For some unknown reason, anyone who has some intense bond or connection with Alcor will slightly remember past iterations of the timeline before it is reset, similar to Deja Vu. Though knowledge is limited, it can help them predict future events which is extremely useful to any allies of Alcor as they can predict what will happen next, unless the timeline was changed in a far different manner from its previous incarnation. It can also be used in a fight to throw of his opponent by using an attack they didn't predict or fighting in a way he hadn't done before.
Postmortem Timeline Alteration: Alcor has an ability which allows him to recreate or force changes in the timeline after his death if it does not end how he wants it to end. He can alter events or prevent possible situations which can completely change the timeline to his liking. This even works on realms where time is non-existent. The changes during a reset are strong enough to bring back the world after its destruction and revive or recover anyone no matter their condition.
Penalties: The butterfly effect of Alcor's reset is completely out of his control. This means that any changes Alcor's Authority produces can be manipulated, and what happens beyond said time is completely unknown. Future events could happen entirely differently after he changes the timeline and could be nothing like his prediction. He would have to use the ability again if he wished to change the timeline to his preference.

name: Beli Hainelga

intro: Beli Hainelga (ベリ・ハイネルガ) is one of the most fearsome serial killers from the Holy Kingdom of Gusteko. His gruesome reputation is second only to the Bowel Hunter. Until the climax of Arc 6, his name and memories have been eaten by Lye Batenkaitos. Currently, his status remains unknown.
appearance: Beli was a large obese man with a long beard and ponytail.
personality: Due to his reputation as one of the most feared serial killers from the Holy Kingdom, it can be deducted that Beli was a rather sadistic and disgusting person. As his only actual presence was through Lye and Rui using Solar Eclipse and Lunar Eclipse, there are no concrete examples of Beli's personality.
history:
Having been born with an extraordinary growth spurt, Beli Hainelga was blessed with physical predispositions which are impossible to be achieved by any normal human beings. Due to his inhuman strength and resistance to damage, he soon discovered joy in harming men to his liking, and before long, he committed several heinous crimes. His reputation would soon label him to become one of the most fearsome serial killers from the Holy Kingdom of Gusteko. At one point, when Beli was attacked by a garrison, his skin was so sturdy that, from the thousand swords pierced into him, not a single one had been effective, and the garrison failed to seize him. 

Sometime before the events of Arc 6, his name and memories were eaten by the Sin Archbishop of Gluttony, Lye Batenkaitos. Following the Sin Archbishop's death, it's unknown if he awoke from his vegetative state or not.
abilities_text: Carnivorous Beast (肉食獣): Due to Beli's extraordinary growth spurt, he was blessed with inhuman physical attributes. This ability allowed Beli to strengthen his body which gave him two advantages: he could withstand powerful attacks and strengthen his limbs to deliver devastating blows. This move was shown in Arc 6 when used by Lye Batenkaitos. With this ability, he was able take a hit from Emilia's ice spear and come out unscathed, and deliver a retaliating punch that, from Subaru's perspective, would be as devastating as getting hit by a car.

intro: Alec Hoshin (アレク・ホーシン), better known to history as Hoshin of the Wilderness (荒れ地のホーシン), was a man who lived in the era of the Great Calamity and traveled with the Witch Era Party. He is most well-known for uniting a multitude of small countries, founding one of the Four Great Nations known as the Kararagi City-States, implementing within it a culture that strongly resembled that of Japan, and being the first chief of Kararagi. He is considered a world-wide symbol of success for merchants and, as such, is a figure who is looked up to by any individual remotely associated with business.
appearance: Alec appeared to be a middle-aged man with long, dark red hair tied into a ponytail, amber eyes, a small mustache, and a beard. He wore a long, black cloak with red on the inside and grey woven robes. He was also adorned with a bronze pin that featured a hanging red robe and a cane given to him by Farsale Lugunica.
personality:
According to Echidna, Alec was personable and the kind of person who could hit it off with anyone. Despite this, he was incredibly shrewd, a schemer, and a colossal liar whose ability to sway hearts could achieve results on par with Authorities. Furthermore, he was compared to a beast tamer for being the only person able to handle Reid Astrea and preventing his rampages. He was also claimed to be a gentleman to Echidna and Satella, and despite his quirks, he was fundamentally good at heart.

Alec considered himself pessimistic. His nature was to long for the company of others. He hated the sky because he thought it looked down at him and tormented him. It is mentioned that he was both brave and sympathetic. Some theorized that Hoshin was a lolicon, as Ricardo described him as one, though the word was coined as a common term in Kararagi that meant "love at first sight".

Remembered as Hoshin of the Wilderness, he is said to have been a rather brutal and, at times, savage person who did everything to achieve his goals both as a merchant and as the founder of the Kararagi City-States. It is precisely due to this trait that he was able to unite all the countries and cities into one of the Four Great Nations. If one refused to join them, he did not hesitate to topple the entire city and build a new one from its ashes.
history:
At some point in the distant past, Alec, along with Flugel, Reid Astrea, Farsale Lugunica, Echidna, and Satella travelled together. Alec went through many brutal experiences, including being chased by a Dragon, being swallowed by a great flood, and the bloodless capture of a barbarian fort.

According to Echidna, at the time of their travels, they needed to keep their identities secret. However, at one point during their travels, they ended up in the country of Magrizza. Despite attempting to hide their identities, Farsale declared his own name, resulting in a noble discovering them and inviting them to a banquet of nobles. However, the nation's crown prince, who was also in attendance at the banquet, became enamored by Echidna and went behind the scenes to arrange a marriage between the two of them, with Echidna's party going along with them after they were split from their capable fighters. However, at some point, for reasons yet to be explained, Reid and Volcanica went on a rampage, ultimately resulting in the marriage being cancelled and them being driven from the nation. It was a short time later that they learned that the Black Serpent destroyed Magrizza. According to Echidna, it was likely that they were being chased by the Black Serpent.

Though it is not known how much the claims of his past is accurate, according to history, Hoshin was responsible for uniting the cities and small countries scattered around the Western regions of the continent. Eventually, he was able to successfully bring them under his dominion, thus creating the nation that would soon become known as Kararagi. During that time, he was purported to have given the small nation of Banan the choice to surrender or face an all-out attack, thus creating the anecdote "Hoshin was Banan's sunset". Hoshin is also thought to have introduced cultures and previously unseen cultural aspects, such as clothing, like kimonos and yukatas, and foods, like okonomiyaki (later named daisukiyaki), and dorayaki, which became a popular phenomenon in the new world. He also introduced the new world to Kansai dialect, a version of Japanese that was used in the Kansai region of Japan. It was adopted in the world, and it became the native way of speaking in the Kararagi City-States.
abilities_text:
Divine Protection
Divine Protection of Evaluation (目利きの加護, Mekiki no Kago): This Divine Protection enabled Alec to determine if an item was of good or bad quality and, if the item was in front of him, he could evaluate its condition and quality with perfect accuracy. However, if he happened to be evaluating an item he'd never seen before, he would only know if it was of good or bad quality and therefore gained no knowledge of how it was used or how much it was worth. According to Echidna, this Divine Protection was unwieldy.

Intelligence

name: Black Serpent
alias: Vilest of Witchbeasts (最悪の魔獣, Saiaku no Majū)
relatives: Daphne (creator)
intro: The Black Serpent (黒蛇), alternatively known as the Vilest of Witchbeasts, is one of the Three Great Witchbeasts created by the Witch of Gluttony, Daphne, and it is currently the only one of the three that is still roaming the world of Re:Zero. It played a secondary antagonistic role in Arc 9.
appearance: The Black Serpent's true form, rather than being a snake covered in flesh or scales, is instead a massive coalescence of all manner of disease and pestilence forming together to create the shadowy contour of a serpent. Ulcerations akin to a serpent's scales swell and burst across its body, and anything the pus-like droplets touch rots away. The serpent seems to bear multiple heads, each one commanding different types of blights and plagues, while within those very heads writhe tentacle-like or tongue-like protuberances akin to a gathering of parasites, with its only known head as of now being the one representing Elder's Blight. Its mere presence also exudes a dense miasma so thick that it could be seen with the naked eye and immediately recognized as miasma.
history: At an unknown point after its birth, the Black Serpent was claimed to be chasing after Flugel's party for unknown reasons, and in this time, it destroyed the country of Magrizza. It has been said that the Black Serpent was responsible for destroying what was once a great nation around this time, reducing the world's Five Great Nations to four; it is unclear if this great nation was Magrizza or a separate nation entirely. Around three hundred years after Daphne's death, the Black Serpent was manipulated into attacking the elven village in Elior Forest by the Witch of Vainglory. Pandora's Authority of Vainglory allowed her to manipulate phenomena, meaning she could direct it into a rough direction she wanted it to go. In the aftermath of its attack, a large quantity of the Black Serpent's venom was left frozen in the Forest which eventually emerged about a century later and caused havoc before being stopped by the half-elf Emilia. At some point nearly one century after its attack on Elior Forest, it infected the birthplace of the members of the White Dragon's Scales, creating a disease in the soil that would turn any person infected by it into stone. Because of this, Dynas Trussardi formed the White Dragon's Scales.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
The Black Serpent is considered the worst of all witchbeasts and is responsible for far more deaths than any other witchbeasts, including the other greats. Having been made specifically to quell the number of people living in the world, it was made in such a manner that it was basically almost impossible to touch or get close to it, let alone kill it. It is thanks to this trait that it remains a threat in the present day.

Physical Traits

Plague Inducement: The Black Serpent is known to be able to inflict any living being it touches with a hundred diseases, and regardless of whether the target was human, animal, or witchbeast, they would succumb to its plague. When Witch Cult members came into contact with its tongue, one was scarred with reddish black burns, another had their skin from the neck up covered in reddish black spots that gushed black blood, and another had their body dried up to the point that touching them might break their body apart. Even if one removes the part of their body contaminated by the Black Serpent's diseases, it will not stop it, and said diseases will continue to encroach from the wound. The Black Serpent can also take advantage of its rather malleable body in order to splash multiple targets at once. It can spread its pus-like "scales" like rain or expand its body like a pillar and fall onto its prey, allowing it to cover a wide area in its plague. As of yet, the only living being known to have survived being contaminated by the Black Serpent's filth, touch, or cursed land is Heinkel Astrea, who was turned into an "immortal knight" via Dragon's blood.
Elder's Blight (老苦, Rō Ku): The head that represents Elder's Blight is able to dole out plagues that would not kill those inflicted. Instead, the targets would be robbed of their mobility and thinking, essentially placing them in a state of eternal stasis. Anyone inflicted by Elder's Blight were claimed to suffer in endless darkness and anguish and would never be able to recover.

Corruption: Any ground that it slithers over is cursed, making anything, including other witchbeasts, unable to live on it. Upon the ground touched by its filth, trees wither, plants rot, water becomes blighted, and any and all life that touches the cursed ground will quickly come to its end. Mere moments after a Guiltylowe touched corrupted land, it died. It is possible to weaponize this corrupted land as well by scattering debris from corrupted land to scatter among living beings, inflicting them with diseases.

Other

Semi-Sentient Poison: The Black Serpent is capable of secreting a potent poison which takes the form of a black liquid-like substance. The poison is capable of semi sentience, as it moves on its own and attempts to devour any and all living creatures it comes across even when its creator isn't present. The liquid is incredibly durable, as blunt force attacks had no effect on it. The poison was also potent enough to completely erode a Guiltylowe, one of the strongest living witchbeasts that is neither unique nor one of the three greats, in seconds.

Shadow Stealth: Through an unknown method, the Black Serpent is capable of hiding within the shadows. While hidden away like this, the land is unaffected by its presence.

name_jp: バルトロイ・フィッツ
relatives: Drizen Vollachia (father) ; Vincent Vollachia (younger half-brother) ; Prisca Benedict (younger half-sister) ; Lamia Godwin (younger half-sister) ; Rommel (older half-brother) ; Palladio Manesque (half-brother) ; Stride Vollachia (relative) ; Eugard Vollachia (ancestor) ; Terriola Goldario (ancestor) ; Radkain Vollachia (ancestor)
intro: Barthroy Fitts (バルトロイ・フィッツ) was an Imperial Prince of the Sacred Vollachia Empire. He worked with Vincent Abellux to save the lives of his nine siblings who did not participate in the ceremony. Before Barthroy could see his plan come to fruition, he was killed by Lamia Godwin's poison. Despite this, his plan turned out successful in the end.
appearance: Barthroy's appearance was never described.
personality: Barthroy always acted sweet and friendly to his siblings, which were unusual traits for the Imperial Family, as most of them either hated or were distant with one another. He also had a minimal amount of personnel at his mansion, making him appear relatively incautious. However, Barthroy's outward sweetness and friendliness was an act that served as his means to achieve what he desired. Contrary to many of his other siblings, he hated how the Imperial Selection Ceremony required his family to kill each other, and in order to prevent unnecessary deaths during the ceremony, he worked with Vincent to save their lives while burying the truth of his machinations, which even had his own death factored into them.
history:
Unlike many of his other family members, Barthroy seemed unwary of his siblings for at least seven years preceding the Imperial Selection Cerermony. While he was attending a party celebrating his father's birthday at age 20, he met with Lamia and lamented how it was not possible for his siblings to get along. Barthroy looked deeply moved when Lamia pretended to share his sentiment.

Barthroy chose not to lay his hands on the Yang Sword during the Imperial Selection Ceremony, thus forfeiting his qualifications to participate in the ceremony. During it, he worked with his younger half-brother, Vincent Abellux, by persuading nine of his siblings to abandon their hopes of participating and giving Vincent their territories in exchange for their lives. In the midst of a meeting with Lamia, however, he passed away due as a result of his younger half-sister poisoning the wine he was drinking. Although he perished before he could see his plan achieved, it was successful after his nine siblings betrayed Lamia during the Siege on the Abellux Castle.

Ever since it was in an egg, Carillon was cared for by Balleroy. When it hatched, Balleroy thought up its name together with Miles and Flop O'Connell. However, it was knocked out of the sky by Julius Juukulius's Al Clauseria, which gave it a fatal injury. Before Carillon's death, Balleroy comforted it in its last moments by patting its nose, and he asked it to tell Miles to wait for him.

alias: Saint of the Avalanche (雪崩の聖者, Nadare no Seija)
nickname: Pastor Coatl (コアトル司祭, Koatoru Shisai) ; Old Man Coatl (コアトル爺さん, Koatoru-jīsan) (by Maqueena)
previous_affiliation: Gusteko ; Gustekan Church ; Ice Thieves ; Leanotte
intro: Coatl (コアトル) was a pastor and a former Itinerant Preacher of the Gustekan Church.
appearance: Coatl was described as a middle-aged man. In the past, he lost a part of one of his legs.
personality: In the past, Coatl was not above thievery until Leanotte’s avalanche. The avalanche led him to act selflessly by prioritizing saving the townspeople’s lives and watching over them out of a sense of regret and his desire to repent. However, he was prone to being blackmailed, and he refused to put his former comrades, who also contributed to causing the avalanche, in danger.
history:
Coatl was an Itinerant Preacher whose name was famous in the Gustekan Church while simultaneously acting as a member of the Ice Thieves. One day, when he and his cohorts attempted to retrieve the buried treasures they stole, they caused an avalanche and became unable to reach them. The town of Leanotte was caught in the avalanche, and out of regret and repentance for causing it, Coatl decided to participate in rescue operations, losing a leg in the process, and to offer up his savings to restore what was damaged in the town. Afterward, he decided to become a pastor, moving to a nearby church. Watching over the town for years to come, he lived a simple life of atonement, and became known as the Saint of the Avalanche.

Years later, a con artist named Maqueena perceived the connection between Coatl and the Ice Thieves. She masqueraded as a bard and blackmailed Coatl to extort money from him countless times. Twelve years after the avalanche, a survivor from Leanotte, Noelle Tuérico, was forwarded a letter from Coatl by the Church. In the letter, he confessed his sins and revealed that he had belonged to the Ice Thieves. When Noelle arrived at the church he resided in, he welcomed her, affirming the sins he had committed, and requesting that retribution be limited only to his life. Noelle, whose reason for joining the Gustekan Church had been to exact revenge against all of the Ice Thieves, refused to accept the result. She tortured Coatl in an attempt to force him to divulge the identities of his peers, but he refused, leading Noelle to murder him by dealing a blow to his head.

name: Admonsah
intro: Admonsah (アドモンサ) is a former travelling entertainer and slave.
appearance: Admonsah, as a member of the Multi-Arm Tribe, has dark blue skin, a tall figure, and four arms. He is a young man who wears a long robe to cover the scars that cover his body and the white burn marks left on his neck he received from a Collar of Subservience.
personality: Admonsah has a kind, honest, and gentle disposition. He is considerate and acts protective of children.
history:
One Wild Night
For years, Admonsah was a slave who suffered abuse at the hands of a cruel slave owner who whipped him and shocked him with a Collar of Subservience. He gained his skills in knife throwing under the slave owner. Eventually, he got in a confrontation with his owner, used his fists to crush and kill the man in self-defense near the town of Leanotte, managed to remove his slave collar, and took all of his former owner's belongings. The next day, he sought refuge at the nearby church that Pastor Coatl lived in, finding Maqueena and Podoso within it. Omega's group and Noelle Tuérico quickly followed, and the seven of them were forced to stay inside it as a shelter for an ongoing blizzard outside. While Podoso and Maqueena moved to a separate part of the church, Trellock arrived, and Admonsah was the one to hand him a towel.

A short time later, Podoso and Maqueena discovered Coatl's corpse in the church's hidden basement, and the whole group followed, seeing the scene for themselves. Admonsah quietly listened as Podoso disclosed a recent string of serial murders and Omega deduced the situation until she pieced together his involvement in the death of the man from the previous day and exposed his circumstances and past to everyone in the basement. However, everyone except Maqueena recognized his kindness and was sympathetic to him. Noelle, an Itinerant Preacher, forgave Admonsah for his actions, and he was comforted by Colette as he began to weep. 

When Maqueena was close to having her true profession exposed, she used Muskrim to escape the church, rendering everyone apart from Noelle unconscious. In the end, Maqueena was exposed for her crimes as a con artist, Trellock was revealed to be the one responsible for the serial murders, and Podoso, hypothesizing that Admonsah's crime may very well be attributed to the actual serial killer, offered the young man to become his assistant. The two parted ways with Omega's group on friendly terms, taking Maqueena with them to Leanotte.
abilities_text: Equipment: Admonsah is skilled at launching knives at fast speeds to hit targets as part of a performance. He views his knives as simple tools and does not use them as weapons.

intro: Cragrell Dawson (クラグレル・ドーソン) was the leader of the Demi-Human Alliance and the sole leader who succeeded the Alliance's previous three leaders. After the Demi-Human Alliance fell and the fighting ended, he was the representative who met with Gionis Lugunica and signed the treaty that officially concluded the war.
appearance: Cragrell belonged to a subspecies of lizard humans. He was an elderly man who had green scales, a yellow crest on his head, three-fingered hands, and a long tongue that often darted in and out of his thick lips. At a glance, he looked similar to a frog human or a lizard human, but his eyes were more similar to a fish's than a reptile's. He also had the capability to keep objects in his stomach.
personality: Cragrell was a self-deprecating man who described himself as feeble and stubborn. He cared deeply about his comrades and assisted others who shared his feelings.
history:
As one of the leaders of the Demi-Human Alliance, Cragrell was an intermediary between Valga Cromwell and Libre Fermi. He did not take part in combat and merely watched as Valga brought Sphinx into the Alliance and became its backbone, having Shamrock Valley cleared out for her plans. A couple of years later, following Libre's death at Aihiya Swamp, Valga and Sphinx's apparent deaths at the Royal Catle, and the rise of the Sword Saint, Theresia van Astrea, negotiations with the Kingdom finally ensued. In due course, Cragrell agreed to end the war peacefully.

Following the war's end, Cragrell was conferred a rank of nobility for his contributions to ending the war and granted a mansion in the Royal Capital. His mansion was kept strictly guarded to prevent the possibility of his assassination and having his death reignite the flames of war. When Stride Vollachia began his attacks in Lugunica, Theresia van Astrea, visited him to request his cooperation, and the two of them had a conversation about the Demi-Human War and the past. It ultimately ended with Cragrell agreeing to cooperate with Theresia and the Kingdom.

Because Cragrell was already at an advanced age four decades before the beginning of the main story, it is presumed that he is deceased in the present.

name: Belmont
nickname: Young Bel (ベル坊, Beru-bō)
affiliation: Kingdom of Lugunica ; Royal Capital ; Six Tongues
intro: Belmont (ベルモント) is a member of the Six Tongues, acting as a subordinate of Russell Fellow. In accordance with his orders, he infiltrated the membership of The Brotherhood and Reiner Wahrheit's organization in the past.
appearance: Belmont is a thin man with orange hair, cat-like orange eyes, and wears an oversized hat pulled low over his head. Fifteen years before the start of the main story, he was under the age of fourteen, had a short stature, and dressed in a light button-down shirt with cut sleeves and dark pants. Ten years later, he appeared to look a little bit over twenty years of age, and he donned a more casual shirt with a vest and gloves.
personality: When he was a boy, Belmont maintained the disposition of an ornery slum child, but in reality, the attitude was a pretense. He displays a deep allegiance to Russell.
history:
Once Upon a Time in Lugunica
On the day when a ceremony was held to appoint Roswaal L. Mathers as the new head of House Mathers, Belmont was tasked with stealing the nobleman's golden plume. Although initially successful in stealing the plume, and counterattacking Roswaal to make a getaway, Belmont was eventually cornered in an alleyway until the leader of The Brotherhood, Marcos Gildark, rescued him. Marcos made quick work of Roswaal and made him lose consciousness. With Russell in tow, Roswaal came to reclaim his plume, which bore similarities to fake golden plumes owned by the Golden Wing Faction.

Upon recovering his plume and learning of the circumstances between The Brotherhood and the Golden Wing Faction, Roswaal hosted a meeting between both groups which Bel attended. It resulted in both groups agreeing to move to Costuul so they could begin to create magicreation tools there. Later that night, Belmont met with Russell to receive orders on his next course of action and inform his superior of the origin of the power that affected Marcos earlier in the day. Finished with his duties in the Royal Capital, Belmont followed Russell's orders to accompany the Golden Wing Faction and The Brotherhood to Costuul and keep in touch with him.

First Mission
Ten years later, Belmont, now a young adult, had left Costuul at an indeterminate time and returned to the Royal Capital to infiltrate Reiner Wahrheit's organization, becoming an irreplaceable member of the underground group responsible for distributing the Hexcel drug. While acting as an insider, Belmont got to know Julius Juukulius, who managed to rescue him from capture by the knights. In an attempt to shake up the organization, Belmont spread a rumor that he was affiliated with the knights. The two were assigned to transport Hexcel to the Royal Capital. However, just as the city was about to reach their sight, the members of the organization ambushed them and captured Belmont, suspecting he was a mole for the knights due to his former membership in the Brotherhood that Marcos, the knight commander, used to lead.

Holding himself responsible for Belmont's capture, as he had been the mole for the knights who had infiltrated the organization to aid in taking them down, Julius and his two collaborators, Bikram Edditz and Helaine Gatness, the latter of whom was a covert Six Tongues member like Belmont, hatched a plan to save him before he could be executed by Reiner. Using Blau, a member of the organization whom Julius had injured, Helaine drugged him with Hexcel of potent quality, sending him on a rampage that ended with his life being cut short by Reiner's hand while Julius rescued Belmont. The plan succeeded, and Julius sent Belmont outside to a boat along a river where Bikram and Helaine retrieved him. In the end, Julius took down Reiner and another person who had infiltrated the group, a girl calling herself Adelheid, also captured his collaborator, Count Easley Oruon, ending the duo's operations once and for all. With their mission complete, Helaine and Belmont prepared themselves to move to their next tasks, briefly conversing with one another after the latter's reunion with Marcos.

Following the incident, Adelheid, who had actually been Reinhard van Astrea in disguise, bargained with the Six Tongues to promote his father, Heinkel Astrea, to the role of the knights' deputy commander, which they accepted. Following Heinkel's departure from a bar in the Commoner District in which he had been speaking to Reinhard about his promotion, he happened upon Belmont, who told him that his group's people were keeping an eye on his father. Thought Reinhard was surprised that the young man had been a member of the Six Tongues, Belmont surmised that, while acting as Adelehid, he realized that he had been hiding something. Reinhard informed him that he had gained permission to join the knights from Heinkel and subsequently swore he would never swing his sword for the sake of the Six Tongues, a sentiment which Belmont wholeheartedly accepted on behalf of his organization.

intro: Black Dog (黒狗) is a member of the Six Tongues and a defector of the Beloved Children. He plays a supporting role in Arc 10.
appearance: Black Dog is a tall young man with dark skin and golden brown hair. He is described as having a gallant appearance as well as a handsome and refined face, though his face, which is often twisted into a sneer, is claimed to not suit his personality. When obscuring his appearance, Black Dog dons a yellow uniform with a black overcoat that touches the ground, black gloves and boots, and switches between several masks with different expressions. At least one of his masks is known to have Xs in place of eyes, while another has a crying expression. He also briefly wears a waiter's uniform reminiscent of a bartender, though his expression and attitude almost make him appear as if he was wearing entirely different attire.
personality: Black Dog is an extremely talkative person who outwardly acts foolish. However, his words are typically malicious. He will laud praise towards who he is talking to while his tone actually hurling sarcastic insults, and he will even insult people who should be considered his benefactor. Even after a mere few seconds, one can tell that Black Dog is not a decent person. He shows no qualms towards attacking people he is meeting for the first time with the intent to kill, as well as attacking uninvolved parties in order to achieve the goals of himself and his associates, and if the person he is talking to does exceeds his expectations, he will pretend it did not happen and continue hurling abuse. He is also not above behaving childishly, stomping his feet when being scolded for his behavior, and he is fond of using hand gestures that Natsuki Subaru taught him, particularly the throat slashing gesture. According to Beatrice, rather than having a lack of tact, Black Dog instead lacks comprehension of people's hearts.
history: At an unknown point in time, Black Dog, alongside Melty Pristis, became subservient to Capella Emerada Lugunica, who forced them to refer to her as Mama and work as part of her Beloved Children. It is unknown how long they worked for her. However, following the Subjugation of Sloth led by Subaru, they were provided a chance to from the Beloved Children as Mama was panicked. Afterward, they joined the Six Tongues, taking on the names of "Black Dog" and "White Sheep", and for the next year, the managed to thwart several of the Beloved Children's plans.
abilities_text:
Magic
Although it is unknown what attribute Black Dog has an affinity for, he is shown to be capable of using magic. However, for unknown reasons, it seems he can only use specific magics a limited number of times, and once he uses one element, he does not seem to be capable of using it again. It is unknown if he can replenish his uses of magic. Thus far, he has exhibited the ability to produce fire, wind, and earth. Furthermore, the flames he produces are capable of changing colors, from orange, to green, to blue. It is unclear what significance there is to the changing colors, however.

Curse
Curse Mark (呪印, Juin): After joining the Six Tongues, Russell Fellow placed a curse mark on him that, according to Black Dog, is capable of killing him.

Other
Smokescreen: It is unclear if he is using a tool or magic to produce it, but Black Dog can produce a large amount of black smoke which can act as a smokescreen to obscure his and his allies' movements from their enemies.

Equipment
Conversation Mirror (対話鏡, Taiwa-kyō): Black Dog has a Conversation Mirror on his person which allows him to get in touch with his allies.
Cognitive Disruption Cloak: Black Dog has been lent a cloak with cognitive disruption built into it, allowing him to obscure his features from others.

name: Arbalest
intro: Arbalest (アルバレスト) is a member of the Beloved Children. He plays an antagonistic role in Arc 10.
appearance: Arbalest is an elderly man with dark skin, grey hair, green eyes, thick eyebrows, a thick beard, and a massive build that is tall and wide. He wears work clothes that have a style similar to what is seen in Kararagi.
personality: Arbalest acts like a generally friendly man, and he has a tendency to bring up hypotheticals, whether in response to others' actions or in a discussion. He believes that respect ought to be shown to objects or people that have existed for many years, which includes himself. Despite his general attitude, however, he has displayed a certain level of hostility, having said that, hypothetically, in a manner of respect for him as an elder, if he told someone to die, that they should hurry up and die. When participating in a meeting with the other members of the Beloved Children, he tends to stay on track with the topics being discussed. He also seems to have a certain level of pride in his craftsmanship, and he prepares himself for both praise and criticism.
abilities_text:
Physical Traits
Expert Woodcraftsmen: Arbalest is skilled at crafting things from wood, having been responsible for creating the table used by the Beloved Children.

name: Bellaris
alias: Ring Finger (薬指, Kusuriyubi)
intro: Bellaris (ベラリス) is a member of the Beloved Children. She plays an antagonistic role in Arc 10.
appearance: Bellaris is a woman with yellow eyes and purplish black hair that appears to be so long that it can reach the floor and is curled at the ends. She wears a black dress with one sleeve and leaves one of her shoulders exposed, is slitted from the right side of the waist down, reaches the floor and is fuchsia at the ends, has fuchsia flowers and black feathery protrusions along the top of the dress, a large fuchsia flower adornment at the right side of her waist. She also wears a large purple and black hat with fuchsia spider lilies on it, black high heels, a black collar that matches her dress, and a black glove that matches her dress. Despite giving off a mature look, the gleam in her eyes is said to be reminiscent to that of a daydreaming young girl.
personality: Bellaris has a fixation on the concept of love and speaks about it positively, excitedly, and excessively, bringing it up at seemingly every opportunity she gets. Due to this, she consistently creates justifications based on others' interactions with each other to assert that one person is in love with another person, regardless of their age or gender. She will even posit that others are in love with her based on their interactions with her. Bellaris also believes the greatest obstacle to love is death, as in her mind, there is nothing that separates two people more than death but also brings the love between two closer together. Having said that, her mentality comes off as insane to other people, including to other members of the Beloved Children. Furthermore, similarly to Clarissa, she has a deep-seated fear of doing anything that could create trouble for Mama.
abilities_text:
Techniques
Ring Finger (薬指, Kusuriyubi): Bellaris uses a technique that employs various chemicals in combat, using them for various purposes, both in support and in offense. However, because she uses airborne chemicals and agents, it is possible to use wind to blow them away and redirect them elsewhere, likewise with the effects that she might be able to trigger.
Multi-Colored Explosions: By using a sulfuric compound, Bellaris can generate explosions with flames of various colors. The explosions carry enough power to injure the likes of someone like Reborn or cause the limited collapse of structures around her. However, prior to the explosions, the smell of sulfur permeates the air, which can provide the targets a warning and give them a chance to disperse the compound beforehand or redirect the explosions elsewhere.
Emotion Amplification: By using a chemical that affects one's brain, she can remove the limiters on their emotions. Even the emotions that one becomes used to over times, such as minor annoyance at someone's actions or slight excitability, will intensify greatly, and in some cases, it will lead those with violent temperaments or even those who are usually calm to attack each other. She typically uses this to incite panic or discomposure in her targets.
Pain Numbing Agent: It is implied by Reborn that Bellaris can use a chemical of some kind to numb one's sensation to pain, allowing the target to continue fighting in spite of their injuries.

appearance: Dandon is a tall young man with black hair, golden eyes, dark skin, and a long black cloak with gold and white accents.
personality:
Dandon generally expresses a relatively friendly and jovial mood in the presence of his “siblings”, whom he claims to care for and consider precious. He also has a tendency to emphasize certain words that he uses to refer to people.

Dandon is the one who Mama tasked with being in charge of keeping the Beloved Children in order. As such, he takes charge of their meetings and orders his fellow siblings to act. He has also claimed to be governing a nation.
