intro: Gaston (ガストン), commonly known as Ton (トン), is one of the three thugs that attacked Subaru at the very start of story. He later joined the Felt Camp when Felt employed him after Royal Selection began. He plays an antagonistic role in Arc 1 and Arc 3 and a supporting role in Arc 5 and Arc 9.
appearance: Gaston has a large body with purple hair and eyes. He wears tan clothes, an orange sash around his waist, a green vest, and black shoes. After joining the Felt Camp, he starts wearing a suit.
personality: Gaston has a rough personality, though he is loyal to Felt after joining her camp. Even following his enactment to the camp and having a more noble life, Gaston still retained his thug-like mindset and often berates Reinhard just like how Felt, Rachins and Camberley do.
history:
The Travelogue of the Finest
Roughly 3 to 4 months before Subaru's arrival, Rachins, Gaston, and Camberley met an Imperial traitor, who paid the trio and fifteen other thugs a fair amount of gold coins in order to tail a Divine General who was after his head. The thugs disobeyed the orders and lured the swordsman into a dark alley, wanting to attack, beat and rob the man. However, as they were dealing with Cecilus Segmunt, the strongest person from the Sacred Vollachia Empire and one of the three men who are about as skilled as Reinhard in terms of martial arts, they were defeated within a second and left beaten half to death. Following their arrest by the Knight guards who rushed the scene soon after, the three thugs were then approached by Julius Juukulius, Ferris, and Chisha Gold, who wanted to know about Cecilus' location. Upon being promised freedom, they spilled the beans and were subsequently freed, with the money they would have gotten from Gramdart.

Behind the Scenes of Life in Another World from Zero
A short while after harassing Subaru and being scared off by Reinhard, he, Rachins, and Camberley, attempted to corner Emilia, who was looking for Felt. However, before they could do anything to her, she quickly cornered them. Afterward, she asked them about the Loot House, and they pointed her in the right direction.

Ram's Flirting Refusal
Later, they attempted to ambush Ram, who was searching for Emilia throughout the capital. However, she easily dispatched them.

Felt-chan Gathers Thugs
While Felt inspected the slums with her camp, she found Gaston, Rachins, and Camberley running away and badly injured. They decided to attempt to rob her to make enough money to get away from Lugunica, as they had attempted to trick Russell Fellow into a shady business that did not end well for them, and they were now marked for death by him. Reinhard easily defeated one of them as the others attempted to run, but they were intercepted by Felt while she was scolding Reinhard, as letting them run away would mean they would be dead by Russell's capable henchman the next day. She then recruited the trio for her camp in hopes of using their help for ruining the country. Since then, Reinhard van Astrea started to train all three of them so they would grow stronger with his help.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
Despite his large physique, Gaston is not particularly powerful. In fact, early on, not only was he easily defeated by Subaru at one point, but he was also defeated easily by several other relatively decent fighters. After joining the Felt Camp, his proficiency in combat has increased, and he can do considerably better compared to before, but overall, Gaston would still likely be defeated by most combatants.

Physical Traits/Flow Method
After being trained by Reinhard, Gaston learned how to use the Flow Method, and as of Arc 5, he was declared to be average with it. It is unknown if his proficiency with it has improved.

thumb|right|250px|Gaston using the Flow Method to break one of Lye Batenkaitos's blades.
Enhanced Strength/Durability: Gaston can temporarily boost strength and durability to act like a shield capable of snapping weapons, including one of the blades of Lye Batenkaitos.

Considerable Endurance: Though not as much as other fighters, Gaston is rather tough. Even after having been struck down by someone as strong as the Sin Archbishop of Gluttony, he retained his consciousness and even grabbed ahold of him while still on the ground.

Acrobatics: Despite his brutish size, Gaston is capable of performing feats of acrobatics that can even catch veterans off guard. The extent of said acrobatics is unknown, but it can be used to help him escape and counter his enemies simultaneously.

intro: Felix Argyle (フェリックス・アーガイル), commonly known as Ferris (フェリス), is Crusch Karsten's knight, a member of her camp, and a member of the Royal Guard. He plays a major role in Arc 3, a supporting role in Arc 5 and Arc 10, and a minor yet important role in Arc 9. He is also one of the main protagonists of The Dream the Lion King Saw and The Travelogue of the Finest.
appearance:
Ferris has flax colored hair and yellow eyes, as well as cat ears and a tail. His casual wear consists of a blue collar with a ribbon, primarily white dress with a light blue chest with thin white stripes as well as a light blue hem, light blue ribbons with thin white stripes attached to the waist of the dress, a large white ribbon tied to the back of the dress, black tights, blue leggings with thin white stripes, dark blue shoes, white arm covers that are detached from the dress and leave his shoulders exposed, a dark blue scarf tied around his right arm, and a dark blue ribbon tied around his left ankle. He also wears white-and-blue ribbon hair accessories on either side of his head, which he wears regardless of his outfit.

At times, however, he can be seen wearing the standard uniform of the Royal Army, primarily whenever he is acting with the army itself or is involved with major operations such as the Subjugation of the White Whale and Sloth. In Arc 5, he wore a yukata. In Arc 10, he can be seen wearing a slender, navy blue tailcoat alongside more masculine clothing. Later, he briefly wears a waiter's uniform reminiscent of a bartender's.
personality:
Ferris usually refers to himself in third person, calling himself Ferri-chan. Though in the past, he has shown himself to be accepting of Crusch's father, Meckart, formally calling him Felix, and used it once in a formal capacity when receiving orders from Fourier, in most contexts, whether informal or professional, he has admitted he generally hates being referred to by his birth name, preferring to instead be called Ferris and also finding Ferri-chan okay. Even during a ceremony of great magnitude for Lugunica's future, the Royal Selection Ceremony, he showed visible frustration after Marcos used his birth name. He also enjoys teasing other people, especially those that are surprised that he is male, using cutesy language and gestures in order to agitate them.

Ferris carries a very strong point of view over life and death, and although he hides it through his actions and words, as a healer, he holds those who no longer have any will to live in contempt from the bottom of his heart. Because of his own complex about being weak and helpless, he often hates and finds himself disgusted with weaklings, something that initially caused him to hate Subaru. He also often feels helpless when he is unable to prevent someone from dying or heal them, as seen when he showed endless frustration and disgust at seeing all of the victims of the Sin Archbishop of Lust. He attributes his father, Biehn, and the cruel abuse suffered at his hand, as being responsible for depriving him from the body he could have had, and accordingly, for being too physically weak to protect Crusch.

In his youth, he greatly hated his parents for locking him up and abusing him, and by the point that he was freed, upon seeing his mother, he attempted to attack her as soon as he saw her for the many years of injustice he faced, though he was stopped by Crusch. Despite this, following being saved, cleaned up, and given a new home and family, Felix become extremely loyal to Crusch, to the point that he tried to train himself in the way of the sword, despite having no talent for it, and learned how to use healing magic to be of assistance to her, and he is constantly thankful for Crusch and for her giving him a way of life when he had lacked one. When Crusch one day unloaded her worries about the way she is seen for her behavior and more masculine preferences and the way she gets scolded by her father, Felix made a promise with Crusch that he would act as Crusch's feminine side while Crusch could be the man that he never could, a promise that was kept for years, and after his name was misheard as Ferris, he started using that name in place of his own.

Because of his loyalty to her, Ferris can get extremely emotional when it comes to Crusch; there are times that he will suggest things that she herself does not want, such as when he proposed nulling the alliance between the Crusch Camp and Emilia Camp after she was attacked by the Witch Cult to prevent her from being involved with such danger again, or the time when she was infected by Capella's dragon blood, becoming visibly stressed by her poor condition and even going as far as to demand to see a captured Sirius so he could torture her to gain information on how to cure her, and at one point, he even had to use Subaru as a support when he didn't know what to do because of this and his inability to help her. Later on, despite knowing the consequences towards the camp, Ferris was even willing to accept the Divine Dragon Church's help, even though it meant that he would be going against the oath they made to Fourier. Likewise, for others that he is close to, such as the late Fourier, he was willing to attempt to perfect the Sacrament of the Immortal King so that he could bring him back to life perfectly, though Fourier ultimately convinced him not to do this.
history:
Stories of the Great Crusch-sama Opening
From the moment Felix Argyle was born, he had cat-like appendages due to a distant ancestor from his father's family, the Argyles, having them as a recessive trait. However, his parents mistreated him because they suspected an affair. He was locked in the basement of the Argyle Mansion for the first nine years of his life and was barely cared for. One day, as a result of rumors that were in the Karsten Duchy, a young Crusch Karsten visited the Argyles’ household and found Felix. After slowly learning about the truth behind his circumstances, he encountered his parents and attempted to stab his mother out of hatred. However, Crusch was ultimately the target of his fury, and as she approached death and told him to live in a way that brought no shame to his soul, a blue-white light emerged from Felix and spread to the girl's body. By using healing magic for the first time in his life, Felix saved Crusch's life and, remembering her words, requested that she allow him to use his life by her side. He was subsequently taken to the Karsten Manor to be cared for and made Crusch's attendant while his parents lost what little standing they had with the Karsten family, leading to their decline.

In the following years to come, Felix would establish a strong sense of loyalty and devotion towards Crusch for taking him from the hell that was his life before. Half a year after arriving at her mansion, Felix made an oath with Crusch to act like a girl and “exchange” his boyhood to her, since she sought to succeed her father and become a duke, which she did not believe she could do as a woman. While Felix began wearing girls’ clothes, Crusch wore formal men’s suits to fulfill her oath and cease acting like a woman. Sometime after their oath, Felix met Fourier Lugunica for the first time. When Fourier mistook Felix's name as Ferris, he began using that name at Crusch's suggestion. Together, Crusch, Ferris, and Fourier would get into all kinds of mischief that defined much of their friendship. Under Fourier's recommendation, he also took lessons from Garitch Fabless, the then-court healer.

The Dream the Lion King Saw
When Ferris was 13, talks of a political marriage for Fourier were in the works, and in an effort to help him out of it, when it was time to speak with the other party, a woman from the lineage of Gusteko's Archbishop, Tiriena, Ferris accompanied him during the meeting. In the end, after meeting with her and Misère, they were able to instead lead them towards their own marriage. A few years later, before Crusch's 17th birthday, Ferris spoke to a worried Meckart about his daughter, and soon after, they bore witness as Fourier challenged Crusch to take part in the party and even wear a dress at the event. On the night of her birthday, however, the Great Rabbit was spotted, and everyone was tasked with preventing Crusch about learning of it. However, when she did and decided to assist in holding it back, Fourier and Ferris were tasked with keeping the party attendants distracted while she was out fighting. Eventually, after warding it away, she and the rest of the Karsten militia returned, and she made her debut as the Valkyrie.

At age 18, Ferris would join the Royal Guard under recommendations from Fourier and the Royal Treatment Center. Although he wanted to be of better use to Crusch, Ferris at first was not very comfortable in being the elite group for several reasons: he stood out due to his odd features marking him as a demi-human, his preference for wearing women's clothing, his own lacking combat abilities and lastly dissatisfaction of his unusual and sudden appointment despite all that from the other knights. However, on the first day, he also came to be acquainted with Reinhard van Astrea and Julius Juukulius which would be the first step in breaking the wall between Ferris and his new environment. Through his good relationship with both of them and the subtle opportunities to display his worth crafty granted by Marcos Gildark, Ferris would come to earn the respect of the other knights for saving their lives with his magic. This would come to give him a sense of his abilities and place there.

Around ten days after he joined the Royal Guard, before he became a permanent member, dark rumors surrounding his old family would reach his ears via Fourier. After speaking to an official about Crusch's solo investigation into his family, they learned that Crusch had not emerged from the manor and that her soldiers were encountering the undead. After leaving for his manor with Fourier and Julius, Ferris received a message from his father that would demand he came to Argyle estate alone in exchange for Crusch's life. Returning to Argyle mansion for the first time in nearly a decade, Ferris would confront his father and Hannah Regret, who he felt a familiar connection to. Following a cold reunion, Ferris would acquiesce to his father's demand to revive his mother with the Argyle family's ancient spell called the Sacrament of the Immortal King. However, when Ferris was brought to the master bedroom, and examined his mother's corpse he would come to the shocking conclusion that she was murdered due to numerous and frenetic stab wounds in her body, partially thanks to Biehn's meticulous preservation. After a tense argument between Ferris and Biehn, the later would lose his composure and admit his guilt in the matter. Eventually realizing any further discussion was pointless, Ferris revived the woman. The spell, however, ended up being a partial failure as despite his mother seemingly coming back with some part of her personality, she was but a walking corpse without her former soul. Moreover, his now undead mother would kill Biehn as they embraced, then she crumbled into ash a moment later. The maid would then reveal to Ferris where Crusch was being held and that she had already freed her from her bonds. Just as Ferris raced out of the room, he would hear the locking and smoke coming from the room. Despite his protest, the maid would not open the door, choosing to die along with her master and mistress. The event marked a scar on Ferris' heart, and he developed deep hate for those who easily gave up their lives. He would meet Crusch and Julius in the foyer of the manor, relieved but utterly distraught by the whole event and escape the burning building with them.

After the incident, Fourier would collapse from a mysterious illness and Ferris would spend over a month looking after him. Desperate and frustrated at the lack of progress, Ferris would consider using the Sacrament of the Immortal King to revive him after death, but Fourier would forbid it, as he wanted to be allowed to die on his own terms if that was the case. They share a somber heart to heart moment and Fourier would pass away a couple of days later. On that same day, Ferris would take his oath of knighthood to Crusch to support her and Fourier's memory.

The Travelogue of the Finest
Roughly 4–5 months before the events of Arc 1 and a couple of months after the mysterious illness took the lives of the entire Royal Family, Julius, Reinhard, and Ferris were tasked with escorting two members of the Council of Wise Men, Miklotov McMahon and Bordeaux Zergev, on a diplomatic mission to the neighboring Sacred Vollachia Empire. During their stay, the Ninth ranking Divine General, Balleroy Temeglyph, was seemingly killed, and Reinhard was blamed for it, forcing the Royal Guard trio to "kidnap" the seventy-seventh emperor, Vincent Vollachia, and flee the Crystal Palace. In a nearby forest, they were ambushed by the Eighth and Sixth ranking Divine Generals Moguro Hagane and Groovy Gumlet respectively. As Reinhard held back the two Generals, Julius and Ferris fled further ahead with the emperor, but they encountered the First ranking Divine General, Cecilus Segmunt. Julius and Cecilus fought but the Royal Knight was no match for the Divine General. After successfully breaking Cecilus' one of his swords, the Blue Lightning decided to fight him a bit more seriously. Just as he was about to decapitate the Spirit Knight, Reinhard came to the rescue. A short duel between the two strongest swordsmen of their respective nations followed, and Reinhard came out victorious.

After successfully escaping from the three Divine Generals, Julius, Reinhard, Ferris, and Vincent finally had some time to breathe and plan out their next steps. Vincent revealed that Balleroy most likely stands behind the ongoing coup d'état. Before they could devise a plan, however, a group of 30 assassins from the Insect Cage Clan engaged the three Knights and the emperor. However, Reinhard stayed behind and swiftly defeated all thirty of them. Meanwhile, while making their escape from yet another serious threat, Julius, Ferris, and Vincent fell into an ambush created by the thought-to-be-dead Divine General Balleroy Temeglyph, who managed to snipe off Vincent's right arm by the shoulder while riding on his flying dragon Carillon. While Ferris healed the mortally wounded emperor, Julius continued deflecting Balleroy's magical snipes, keeping him at bay and defending his friends. After devising a plan and using Ferris as a decoy, Julius was able to pinpoint Balleroy's location despite the man's invisibility, and he hit them with Al Clauzeria, killing Carillon and seriously wounding Balleroy. Julius and Balleroy then engaged in their final duel, which ended with the Spirit Knight's blade piercing the Divine General's chest, killing him. After the threat was finally dealt with, Julius, Vincent, and Ferris regrouped with Reinhard and returned to the Crystal Palace, resolving the conflict. As a token of gratitude, the emperor signed a non-aggression pact between the Empire and the Kingdom, marking the Kingdom's ambassadors' mission as successful.

Roughly a month after Balleroy's rebellion, Julius and Ferris encountered Cecilus in a tavern located in the Royal Capital. Due to the danger that the Divine General presented, the duo accompanied him to a tea house located on the outskirts of the city, where Cecilus informed them of his plans to fight with the Sword Saint Reinhard van Astrea. However, because of Reinhard's absence due to him being on a mission at the Holy Kingdom of Gusteko's borders with Lugunica, Julius had no other option but to secretly accept the Divine General as a guest in his mansion, since his presence in the Royal Capital was illegal. After four days of hiding a Divine General inside House Juukulius, Julius and Ferris were suddenly called to Captain Marcos Gildark's office, where the Fourth ranking Divine General, Chisha Gold, was waiting. The two knights were then given a task to accompany Chisha to his needs in the Royal Capital, and the trio set out to find the person Chisha was after. Arriving just in time, they were able to prevent Cecilus from beheading the High Count Gramdart Holstoy who was behind the failed coup d'état and had fled the Empire. Having fulfilled their mission, Chisha and Cecilus were prepared to return back to the Empire with High Count Holstoy, but they were stopped by Marcos, who arranged a proxy match between Cecilus and Reinhard.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
Ferris has at one point been called one of the weakest characters in the series by the author. Due to his constitution and Divine Protection, although he would be among the hardest characters to kill, he has no combat capabilities. He lacks all talent with the blade, and though he has a strong aptitude with water magic and can effectively paralyze a person with his magic, he has no true offensive capabilities. However, he makes up for this by being the greatest healer in the world, his healing magic entirely unmatched by anyone.

Divine Protection
Divine Protection of Water (水の加護, Mizu no Kago): Ferris's Divine Protection grants him a strong aptitude for healing magic.

Magic
Ferris has a strong natural affinity for the water attribute and a deep connection to water mana as a whole, and according to the author, he has one of the deepest wells of mana to draw from. He has extraordinary capabilities and talent with healing magic thanks to the combination of his bloodline and his Divine Protection of Water. He is so exceptional with it, in fact, that in his desperation to heal his master, in three months, he had elevated the field of healing magic in the Kingdom by "three whole levels," and his already impressive healing magic had improved tremendously, enough so that it was capable of surprising a Great Spirit capable of healing magic like Beatrice. In the two months that followed, that, Ferris even rewrote the very principles of healing magic, such that he could even heal said spirit if needed. However, he has no aptitude for attack magic.

Spells:
thumb|275px|Ferris using healing magic.
Healing Magic (治癒魔法, Chiyu Mahō): Ferris can summon Water Mana through a person's body which stimulates an individual's natural healing capabilities and speeds up wound recoveries. Healing magic can help restore an injured body or cure a target of any ailment they might have within an instant. That being said, healing magic can only treat physical wounds and ailments whilst having no effect on mental afflictions. The skill, talent, and raw power of the mage using healing magic naturally affects the effectiveness of the treatment. Ferris is a healing prodigy who is considered to the greatest healer in the Kingdom if not the world, earning him the alias of Blue. He can, with little effort, instantly bring someone back to perfect health from the brink of death, and even a gravely wounded person can be completely healed by Ferris without so much as a scar to show after the healing procedure. Ferris can even seamlessly reattach lost limbs such as when he reattached Crusch's cut-off right forearm after it had been cleanly severed by the Sin Archbishop of Greed. There are, however, at least two known afflictions that not even Ferris can heal: the illness that felled the Kingdom's entire Royal Family and the curse caused by Sin Archbishop of Lust's Dragon's blood. Additionally, the target of Ferris's healing magic needs to still have an ember of life within them for him to be able to save them, as even someone who had only recently passed away cannot be rejuvenated by Ferris.
Perpetual Healing: Ferris is capable of using his magic on a person in order to force their body to heal at a rapid rate on its own, even once Ferris has stepped away. However, this is entirely dependent on the amount of mana available to the target, and if their mana is exhausted, then the healing will not work. When he used this on Aldebaran, whose gate was connected to Volcanica's and was providing him a practically inexhaustible amount of mana, even after Ferris had been moved away from him and Al was even slashed in half by Reinhard, he rapidly healed from the fatal damage, as if it had never happened before.
thumb|275px|Ferris destroying the circulatory system.
Bodily Function Manipulation: Ferris can also use his magic in order to tamper with a target's internal functions. For example, Ferris can make someone's body go out of control, enabling him to do things such as using their body like a puppet or destroying the circulatory system of their Gate from inside. Likewise, he can use his magic to mostly nullify a target's pain, though he typically avoids doing this so that his target doesn't overextend themselves and make their injuries worse.
Sacrament of the Immortal King (不死王の秘蹟, Fushiou no Hiseki): Sacrament of the Immortal King is an ancient and incredibly powerful spell created by an unknown Witch long ago. The spell, when cast correctly, will allow the user to reanimate corpses of the dead and make them do their bidding. Sadly, the technique to properly cast the spell has been long lost to time, and only an incomplete incantation exists which was transcribed in an old and withered book regarded as the most important heirloom of House Argyle. Originally, the spell was thought to be capable of fully reviving a dead person, and there are legends of the aforementioned Witch being supposedly capable of bringing back people exactly as they were before their demise. Effectively, the written chunks of the spell's full passage is incapable of producing anything more than walking corpses with no soul of their own, creating "corpse soldiers" whose flesh slowly withers away and decomposes through time. To further limit the usefulness of this mostly-lost spell, a caster with an extremely rare natural affinity for it must be found in order to recreate even the most basic effects of this forbidden spell. Ferris used this spell once, roughly a year before the start of the main story, on the two-year-old corpse of his mother — who had been repeatedly stabbed and killed by her husband and Ferris' father Biehn Argyle. Upon chanting the incomplete incantation, a faint blue light transferred from his palms and seeped into the dead body, springing it back to life almost immediately. In total, the corpse had remained "alive" for no more than a couple of seconds as almost immediately after opening her eyes, Hannah strangled Biehn and — after killing him — dissipated to dust. Perhaps the most enigmatic thing about the whole ordeal was Hannah's faint but genuine smile upon laying her eyes on her husband and her supposed son — something that was not a possible reaction from one of Biehn's countless reanimated corpses.

Physical Traits/Flow Method
Due to his deep connection to water mana and his regenerative capabilities, his body is considerably weak, and he cannot use the Flow Method.

Heightened Senses: Due to the demi-human blood flowing through his veins, Ferris sensory organs were significantly enhanced past the limitations displayed by most humans. His cat-like ears in particular were able to detect the slightest change in his surroundings to the point that he could tell when someone turned to look at him. Because of his excellent hearing, he could always tell when someone was approaching him, with the exception of Reinhard van Astrea.

Accomplished Cook: According to the author, Ferris is an outstanding cook who personally serves for Crusch.

Other
Pseudo-Immortality: One way Ferris' body differs from most humans and demi-humans is his extraordinary connection with Water Mana, which imbues it with the passive effect of rapid cellular regeneration. With this in effect, it means he can resurrect from death. However, in exchange it further weakens his ability to fight, and it is unknown if he has a limit to how many times he can do this.

Equipment
Sword: Ferris owns a short sword he received from Crusch, but as he doesn't like to damage his skin, he generally refuses to wield it. He has wielded it once in an effort to intimidate an unimpressed Capella, but he otherwise has not talent with the blade.

intro: Echidna (エキドナ), commonly known as Eridna (襟ドナ), is an artificial spirit created by the Witch of Greed, Echidna, who is currently in service of Anastasia Hoshin. First introduced in Arc 5, she later plays a pivotal role in Arc 6 and a minor supporting character in Arc 8.
appearance: Echidna takes the appearance of a white fox with snow white hair and sharp black eyes, though she usually takes the form of Anastasia's scarf.
personality: Similarly to her creator, Echidna speaks, sounds, and acts just like the Witch herself. However, she has no memories of her past aside from her name. Because of this, Subaru nicknamed her Eridna (Scarfidna). She's also shown to deeply care about Anastasia, going to extreme lengths to make sure no one would find out about their condition. According to the author, she is the equivalent of Echidna in personality if she had a heart.
history:
Whilst it is known that the Witch of Greed created Echidna, the exact purpose of her creation and what happened prior to her meeting Anastasia is unknown. However, Echidna states that she felt like the purpose of her birth was completed the second she was born.

Kararagi Girl & Cat's Eye
Nine years prior to Subaru’s arrival to the world, Mother tasked a former slave named Reisel with retrieving an object relating to the legacy of the Witches. He visited Ricardo Welkin, asking for help with stealing a meteor inside a cart. They ambushed the fleet but were stopped by Shiroro Tonerico. While Ricardo was fighting with Shiroro, Reisel stole the target carriage and abandoned his old friend. However, his plan was inadvertently thwarted by Anastasia, who exchanged the carriages. In the carriage, Anastasia met Echidna, and the two formed a bond. Reisel came back to take the true cart, but he was defeated by Anastasia, Echidna, the Pearlbaton siblings, and Ricardo, who formed a ceasefire with Shiroro.

Camp Formation Stories
Anastasia initially sought to join the Royal Selection after learning she had the qualifications to be a candidate, but refused to enter the race once she learned that Julius would not become her knight. However, in time, Julius eventually decided to become Anastasia's knight, and the two performed a ritual of knighting. Anastasia and Echidna spoke once he left, with the former telling the latter that she would show her the end destination of her greed.

Julius Juukulius's Promise Keeping Notebook
After the Battle for Priestella, Subaru, accompanied by Julius and "Anastasia", were visiting wards of hospitals, seeing if Subaru could recognize any of those were made Nameless. The trio lamented about how the "Sleeping Beauty" state that had been discovered prior to these events was caused by the Authority of Gluttony and how it could affect make others forget them completely. However, they believe that Subaru, who was unaffected by Gluttony's effects, was proof that there was hope. Anastasia apologized to Subaru for taking him all over the place, but Subaru didn't mind, though he regretted not seeing more people. Though Julius attempted to reassure him, Subaru claimed that if he were in Subaru's position, he'd be the same, which Julius agreed with. As the group was preparing to leave and go to the next ward, however, another stretcher passed by, and Subaru recognized the person on it, turning to the others and telling them that it was Joshua Juukulius, Julius's brother.

Beatrice's Everyone is Troublesome, I Suppose
A few days after the Battle for Priestella, as they were making preparations to leave Priestella, Subaru informed Beatrice that Anastasia had been possessed by the artificial spirit Echidna and asked what they should do. Deciding to observe the flow of mana surrounding the girl, she quickly realized that Anastasia's gate was defective. As she was observing her, however, Emilia appeared and asked why she was watching Anastasia. Although not wanting to lie to her, due to Subaru not wanting Anastasia's condition to spread, Beatrice struggled with what to tell her. Mistaking her observations as nervousness to meet Anastasia, Emilia brought Beatrice over to meet her. After a little bit of small talk, "Anastasia" mentioned to Beatrice that she figured the Subaru had already talked to her about her state, much to Emilia's confusion.

Julius Juukulius's Promise Keeping Notebook II
A few days after the Battle for Priestella, as they were on the road, Julius could often be seen offering his assistance to "Anastasia", who had forgotten him thanks. Subaru noticed the awkwardness between them, though Emilia was glad to see that they were close, and Subaru expressed his gratitude for her being able to say something like that even if she did know the current circumstances. Before long, he asked Emilia to take Julius aside so he could talk to "Anastasia", who had silently asked for help. Taken aside, she quietly complained about Julius being too intimate and that she didn't know how to deal with him, even using what she knew about Anastasia's etiquette and personality. Despite his own frustrations at dealing with her due to her similarities to her creator, he told her he'd help about Julius and talk to him. Moments later, he returned to Emilia and Julius. Despite having an emotional reaction towards her interactions with Julius, he asked Emilia to see to "Anastasia" since she seemed a little tired while he spoke with Julius. Though Emilia thought he was hiding something, he covered that up with a confession of love to her, causing her to call him a dunderhead and go with "Anastasia".

Julius Juukulius's Promise Keeping Notebook III
A few hours after Subaru's group was separated from the others, Shaula returned to the Pleiades Watchtower with Subaru's group, and Julius reunited with "Anastasia", who claimed that their side had also gotten dangerous. This being said, she also mentioned that something seemed to have happened between the woman and Subaru, and when Julius looked in the woman's direction, he noticed that the only thing in her eyes seemed to be Subaru. "Anastasia" claimed that she had saved them and that there seemed to be only one-sided negotiations between her and Subaru, and though she had only intended to take Subaru, "Anastasia" convinced her to guide the others to the tower. Afterward, "Anastasia" mentioned they'd managed to finally step foot inside the tower before chiding Julius for thinking negatively. Shortly after, they approached the woman, and though Julius attempted to thank her and ask for her name, she turned her back to him, as she only intended to speak if Subaru had been involved. Nearby, Emilia and Beatrice were trying but failing to pry Subaru's arms off of Ram, as he had been holding her tight to protect, and though Julius went to help them, he questioned if Subaru was more worthy of the title of Knight, as he was trying to protect others even while unconscious.

Beatrice's Everyone is Troublesome, I Suppose! In Fact!
The next day, after observing the first trial of the tower, Emilia and Beatrice spoke with "Anastasia" and Julius, Beatrice accidentally sounding malicious with her joke towards the effect of Julius's Divine Protection. After Emilia and "Anastasia" talked about Emilia's worry for Subaru, Ram exited the carriage. After asking about Rem, she asked for the details about their current circumstances, only to learn that Subaru had been holding her tightly. Embarrassed, Ram walked toward the carriage with her wand out, claiming she would erase Subaru, leading Emilia to stop her.

Kararagi Reaper Incident
Shortly after the events of the Great Disaster, Anastasia, accompanied by Julius, Halibel, and Echidna, returned to Kararagi, where they decided to report their discoveries to the mayor of the Third City Ivada, Orgo Hayata. Unfortunately, there was yet another problem: the windstorm created by the Slasher, Zarestia, that was thrust upon Banan. After learning of this, she, Anastasia, and Julius made their way to Banan to meet up with Ricardo. Sometime after Ricardo quelled Zarestia's rage, Anastasia's group arrived and were led to the holding cells in Riften Magoji's mansion, where Zarestia was being held. During their conversation, Anastasia learned that Riften went missing, Julius noticed that Zarestia was a Great Spirit and introduced himself, and Halibel unintentionally riled her up by noticing her strange constitution, that something was missing. However, when Anastasia mentioned Zarestia being responsible for other such town-destroying wind cataclysms, Zarestia declared otherwise, saying that she only rampaged in Banan. Shortly afterward, this is confirmed when a massive tornado appeared outside of Banan, not made by Zarestia. After giving her orders and securing Zarestia's assistance, the group made their way to stop the tornado.

After leaving Riften’s mansion, Anastasia’s group and Zarestia managed to quell the winds. However, in the process, Anastasia and Echidna were kidnapped. When Anastasia later woke up, she found herself in Zarestia’s Bed, and Echidna had left her side to ensure her safety, as she was the main target behind their enemy’s actions. Anastasia spoke with said enemy, a woman identical to Zarestia who she referred to as Black Tia, and after a one-sided conversation, Anastasia promised to help Black Tia, as otherwise, everyone who would come to find Anastasia, Black Tia, and Anastasia herself would find themselves likely killing each other. Not long after, Echidna appeared after realizing Anastasia would be safe, and despite her concerns, Anastasia convinced her that everything would be fine. A full day after being taken, she and Anastasia were brought back to Banan by Black Tia, and shortly after, likely due to her exhaustion catching up with her, Anastasia passed out with a fever.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
Although she is capable of using magic by drawing on the Od of who she possesses, Echidna is not necessarily powerful, nor is she really much of a combatant. Though about as crafty as Anastasia herself, she is not truly meant for combat and can be prone to making panicked actions. Furthermore, because she only possesses Anastasia and must draw from her Od instead of her gate, she cannot freely use magic as she likes without putting Anastasia in danger and severely exhausting her body, further limiting her overall capabilities.

Magic/Spiritual Arts
Echidna has a natural affinity for the yang attribute. She also has enough knowledge with magic to be able to recognize the spatial distortions created by the Sand Time barrier that covered the Augria Sand Dunes. By her claim, she already naturally had the knowledge that could allow her to approach the Pleiades Watchtower when even Reinhard van Astrea couldn't bypass the barrier. It is likely that said knowledge is in reference to said distortions. It is unclear, however, if the knowledge she was born with extends beyond her attribute and the barrier. This being said, Echidna lacks in certain ways compared to a normal spirit. Though considered a great spirit, she lacks the ability to contract with humans and it is difficult for her to use magic to defend herself with, and in exchange, she is skilled at concealing herself. She is also a low-consumption spirit.

Spells:

Jiwald (ジワルド): Jiwald is a yang attribute spell that allows Echidna to fire heat rays from her fingers.
El Jiwald (エル・ジワルド): Echidna can fire several rays from her fingers which are then brought down in a claw-like motion.
Cognitive Disruption (認識阻害, Ninshiki Sogai): A built-in mechanism within Echidna that can prevent others from being able to recognize her true form. This ability doesn't work on certain people with defective Gates, such as Anastasia.

Other
Possession: In emergencies, Echidna can overwrite her existence onto Anastasia's Od, making her able to temporarily borrow her body, and by doing so, she can draw on Anastasia's Od to use magic at the former's expense. Furthermore, due to Anastasia's deficient gate, it would be incredibly difficult for even a master of magic such as Beatrice to notice the possession if one wasn't purposefully looking into her flow of mana. However, it is possible to be stuck possessing Anastasia's body if Anastasia locks herself away in her Od, in which case, Echidna can only wait for her to come out willingly or force her out.

intro: Echidna (エキドナ) was the Witch of Greed. Mentioned throughout the series, particularly for her connection to Roswaal and Beatrice, she formally debuted in Arc 4 as a major supporting character and later secondary antagonist.
appearance:
Echidna's barely exposed skin was porcelain-like and pure white, so white that it seemed any semblance of color had been completely bleached from her existence. Her black eyes shone with intellect and were the only part of the woman that looked alive. Her long straight hair reached down to her back and was as white as her skin, and it also had a black butterfly hairpin (jade green in the anime). Anyone who saw her would be instantly captivated by her striking beauty, although the sight of her would also inject overwhelming fear into a person's soul. Although her spirit in the Castle of Dreams was in her late teens, Echidna's slender body appeared as though it was in its mid-twenties. 

The only parts of her body that were visible were her head, neck, and hands, as the rest of her figure was usually wrapped in black clothing. The contrast between her black clothing and the whiteness of her skin helped express her striking beauty. During her meeting with Subaru in the trial of his past, Echidna wore clothing fabricated from Subaru’s memories. The outfit she donned was the female version of the school uniform worn at Subaru's high school in Japan. The ensemble consisted of a white dress shirt, a navy-blue blazer with the school's crest sewn onto the left breast, a red ribbon tied around the shirt's collar, a grey pleated short mini-skirt, knee-high white socks, and white uwabaki slippers with brown soles. Instead of her usual hair ornament, Echidna wore a smaller red butterfly clip in her hair.

Despite her extraordinary beauty, Echidna induces overwhelming fear known as miasma in everyone "lucky" enough to meet her to the point people start vomiting in her presence. If exposed to her miasma for too long, the people in her presence would die. It is worth mentioning that, while he somehow did not receive that side effect, Subaru did note her presence felt as dangerous or more so than the White Whale or the Sin Archbishop of Sloth.

In actuality, Echidna from four centuries ago and Echidna from the Castle of Dreams were stated to be two separate entities. Accordingly, their appearances slightly vary. While being mostly identical, Echidna from four centuries ago was noted to be in her mid to late twenties, rather than late teens. Her face was almost the exact same as the Trial Echidna, save for a much calmer and wise air it gave off. 

She was often seen smiling and acting very nonchalantly, until the topic shifted to something she was genuinely interested in. Due to her beautiful appearance, she often gave off a maidenly impression.
personality:
Echidna's curiosity toward the unknown and thirst for knowledge were the two things that defined her behavior, and she has once referred to it as love and directed those feelings toward Subaru's Return by Death, which she was interested to the point that she longed to become his advisor to record the many possibilities created with Subaru’s Authority. At first glance, she was polite, soft-spoken, understanding, and even a bit childish. However, she was not very good at tidying up after herself, and she was stated by the other Witches to be quite clumsy like the time when she accidentally set a forest on fire, nearly burning to death, as she was trying to warm herself. She was also somewhat forgetful in regards to daily tasks; the other Witches mentioned that she once forgot to change from her nightgown, and accidentally went out in public without properly dressing. Echidna also seemed to have pride in being a Witch, as, according to Beatrice, she would desire seeing a reaction of awe and fear from those who bore witness to her laboratory. Likewise, she was not above handing out information to those who could successfully reach her palace, though she was also selective about information that she gave out, especially in regards to her research, something which Beatrice claims may have been in response to an unpleasant experience.

Described as being black-hearted, she could not understand the feelings of others and could be seen as a sociopath by normal standards. According to herself, she learned many negative emotions such as contempt and ridicule from her parents, and because she was never given a proper example of how love was meant to feel, she could not understand her own emotions of love or other such positive emotions. If it was to get a hold of more knowledge, she had no problems with employing sophistry, lying, and deceiving others. She was reasonably polite and even jovial to Subaru, whenever the two interacted. Even after the reveal that she was black hearted and after Subaru called her a monster, she kept acting like an affable individual. Though Echidna ultimately respected Subaru's decision to press on in his struggles without her help, she revoked his qualifications for entering her Castle of Dreams, as payback for not taking her hand. While Echidna does have some trouble with certain emotions, she isn't actually as emotionless as she made herself out to be to Subaru. It also is notable that she does maintain elements of the personality she showed Subaru even when she isn't around him. This being said, Al noticed that, despite not being able to understand the hearts of others, she was not heartless herself, as at times, he would catch glimpses of sadness, guilt, and loneliness in her.

As Echidna from four centuries ago and Echidna from the Castle of Dreams were stated to be two separate entities, the two also differ somewhat in personality. The original Echidna is much more considerate, empathetic, and helpful than her counterpart from the Castle of Dreams. This being said, however, the Castle of Dreams version of Echidna seemed to originally share the same traits with her alternative counterpart four centuries ago, and following her and Al's defeat against a certain enemy, she sacrificed her love and a good portion of what made her the "Witch" in order to become the "Witch of Greed", turning her into the Witch seen in the present day. According to Beatrice, the Echidna that she knew was not an evil person, and Subaru speculates that the difference between the personalities may stem from the fact that the Castle of Dreams version of Echidna was a representation of her younger self. However, whether this is true remains to be confirmed.
history:
Echidna is the daughter of the Warlock of Melancholy, Hector, and the Witch of Vainglory, Pandora. Unlike any other Witches across history, Echidna was the only person who was born as a Witch. Echidna's parents were responsible for her birth, having supposedly produced her with a specific goal in mind, that goal being unknown. By Echidna's claim, her parents were good-for-nothings, and she learned negative emotions such as contempt and ridicule from them. However, she believed that, from their perspective, her existence was a failed imitation to them. She despised her parents, and at some point in time, she parted ways with them.

Echidna has claimed that she experienced the pains of having excess mana in her body when she was younger. In the years predating the Great Calamity, Echidna travelled alongside Satella, Flugel, Reid Astrea, Farsale Lugunica, and Alec Hoshin for unknown reasons, though according to Alec, it was a journey to save the world. According to Echidna, at the time of their travels, they needed to keep their identities secret. However, at one point during their travels, they ended up in the country of Magrizza. Despite attempting to hide their identities, Farsale declared his own name, resulting in a noble discovering them and inviting them to a banquet of nobles. The nation's crown prince, who was also in attendance at the banquet, became enamored by Echidna and went behind the scenes to arrange a marriage between the two of them, with Echidna's party going along with them after they were split from their capable fighters. However, at some point, for reasons yet to be explained, Reid and Volcanica went on a rampage, ultimately resulting in the marriage being cancelled and them being driven from the nation. It was a short time later that they learned that the Black Serpent destroyed Magrizza. According to Echidna, it was likely that they were being chased by the Black Serpent.

Over four centuries ago, Echidna acted as a tutor for a young Roswaal after saving him from suffering inflicted on him by mana poisoning. In the following years, she created three artificial spirits, with Puck being the first created by Echidna and Beatrice being the last.. She also started researching means of immortality by transferring her soul into a body which belonged to someone else. Throughout the years, she gathered humans and demi-humans alike, in order to create a perfect "sanctuary" which would be able to support the barrier, and after the Sanctuary was created, she would often travel back and forth between her castle, Kugelschreiber Castle, with Beatrice. When Roswaal was 16 years old, he faced off against Hector and after being defeated and nearly killed, Echidna saved his life and engaged Melancholy. After Ryuzu Meyer, the Apostle of Greed, sacrificed herself in order to bypass the requirements and instantly activate the barrier, she successfully fended Hector off and saved the lives of everyone in the Sanctuary.

At some point during her immortality experiments, she made numerous copies of Ryuzu, one of which was given the name Sphinx after the mythological monster. However, despite having obtained her knowledge of the magical arts, Echidna disposed of her as a failure, unintentionally setting her upon the world with barely the ability to survive.

According to her, royals of every country came to visit Echidna to borrow her wisdom at some point in the past when she was alive. Echidna mentioned that she has a connection with Kararagi since she "helped found it". She also became acquainted with the Divine Dragon and Emilia's Mother. She also hired Petelgeuse at one point to act as some form of mentor to Beatrice.

At an unknown point, Echidna became the mentor and parent-figure to Aldebaran. He was taught various kinds of knowledge, different types of magic, forbidden arts, such as Ol Shamak, and even how to use his Authority all by Echidna. Their relationship was one where he could not entirely dislike her, they interacted with each other regularly and carefreely, and he questioned whether her relationship was one that could be classified as parental or not, ultimately coming to refer to her as Teacher out of apparent spite. Because of her methods, the other Witches seemed to object to them, and even Al noticed at times that she seemed to feel guilt, though she never backed down. Numerous times during their training, she mentioned that nobody could defeat Al, who she created, and with that resolve in the two of them, they went to confront the task that Echidna had for Al, something which seemed to be connected to Satella. In the end, however, Echidna found herself heavily injured, and Al arm was taken by the shadow. While Al's spirit was shattered, Echidna, deciding there was some other form of damage that could be handled, sealed Al away in Ol Shamak. What she did after that is unknown. However, for reasons unknown, this resulted in her becoming compatible with her Witch Factor and being reduced to the Witch of Greed in exchange for her love.

After the deaths of Typhon, Minerva, Daphne, Carmilla, and Sekhmet, Echidna, who was purportedly 19 at this time, later collected their souls before her body was destroyed so as to not lose them, and was sealed away by Volcanica, coming to reside in the Castle of Dreams within her tomb at the Sanctuary.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
Echidna was an incredibly powerful Witch whose mastery of magic allowed her to effortlessly take down the likes of Dragons with ease. Also, thanks to her clumsiness, she can also become a threat accidentally, as her clumsiness has led to her unintentionally burning down a forest in a simple attempt to warm herself. Although not considered one of the stronger Witches, Sekhmet has mentioned that she feared the day that Echidna became bored of the world, and she claimed that she could very easily become capable of destroying the world.

Authority
Despite being a Witch, unlike the other Witches of Sin, she was an applicable candidate for her theory of inheritance, which hypothesizes that someone without a Witch Factor by birth who shares a profound connection to someone who was compatible with a Factor could innately unlock the door to an Authority. This being said, Echidna claims that it is difficult to explain the Authorities of someone in this position, as they had their door "half-open by birth". It is unknown why Echidna differs from the Witches of Sin. After failing to make a Factor hers for an unknown length of time, upon the failure of her student, placing her on the verge of death, she became compatible with and was chosen by her Witch Factor, losing her love in exchange and becoming the "Witch of Greed" in the process. Upon returning to the world as Omega, she has not yet shown to have access to her Authority of Greed outside of the Castle of Dreams. However, since a Witch Factor is not required after it has already unlocked a user's Authority, it is unknown whether or not she still retains said Authority even with her new body.

Authority of Greed (強欲の権能, Gōyoku no Ken'nō): Echidna was a previous holder of the Witch Factor of Greed and can use its Authority of Greed, which has granted her the abilities related to peering into all of the world's knowledge, past, present, and future. According to No Stella No Life 3, while Echidna was the "Witch", she had been chosen by the Witch Factor of Greed due to her intense thirst for knowledge and attained the title of Witch of Greed as a result.
Book of Wisdom (叡智の書, Eichi no Sho): In the web novel, Echidna's Authority was a white Book of Wisdom, which she called the Memories of the World (世界の記憶, Sekai no Kioku), that allowed her to draw knowledge from the world's memory at any point in time, sending the knowledge directly into her mind and skipping the learning process she enjoys. It allowed her to see any event in the past, present, and future, which she considered uninteresting and monotonous. It has been said that the Book of Wisdom provided to Beatrice is an imperfect copy of her Authority of Greed. However, the mind of an ordinary person attempting to read her book would be fried by the sheer amount of knowledge flowing into the reader's mind. It is unclear whether this book is the entirety of her Authority or merely one manifestation of her Authority.

Magic
Echidna was able to use all six elements and was extremely skilled in all of them with–at the time–unparalleled mastery. She was capable of using every spell that existed at the time and even created her own spells to use. Even following her death, no one ever came close to her overall skill with manipulating magic, until Roswaal L. Mathers became the first and only person who would rival and even surpass her in magical knowledge and proficiency. It should also be noted that there exist individual beings who are stronger in the usage of a specific magical element, such as Puck, who was noted as the most powerful Fire Magic user in the series, with the raw power of his spells even surpassing that of Roswaal's. She has been claimed to be capable of using high level multiplefold magic, with the only other people said to be capable of doing so being Roswaal and Myonmyon. Her mastery and skill with magic is claimed to be powerful enough to get past Volcanica's halo, which provides with extremely high-level magical defenses, and it is claimed by the author that she remembers every ancient magic that has not been handed down, not written down, or forgotten. According to Beatrice, although she lacked the mana necessary, if she was able to overcome that, Echidna could have been akin to a deity of creation.

Spells:
Goa (ゴーア): Echidna was able to manifest a blaze of fire to incinerate foes.
Healing Magic (治癒魔法): Echidna summoned water mana to heal the wounds of herself and others, however it only affected physical ones.
Jiwald (ジワルド): Jiwald allowed Echidna to fire heat rays from her fingers which would effortlessly pierce her enemies.
Ol Shamak (オル・シャマク): An anti-Witch spell that was originally created by Echidna. It is a forbidden art that immobilizes its target, preventing them from moving and ceasing the activity of their body's gate. When activated on a target without a Witch Factor or Authority, they are bound in a black light with a contradictory force. The spell can only be used to its full potential when cast on someone with a Witch Factor or Authority, encasing them in a completely black orb. Anyone else who enters the vicinity of the spell while it is being used on a Witch Factor or Authority bearer will also find themselves captured within the orb. The orb can vary in strength, and it has the capability to become so tough that it cannot be destroyed by outside interference or simple brute strength, to the point that only something like a slash from the Dragon Sword Reid can destroy it. It unusually uses an "Ol" prefix, meaning it classifies as separate from the typical prefix classifications.
Soul Transcription (魂の転写): A lost magic technique that allows a person to transcribe their own soul over another's. By doing this over and over to extend their life indefinitely, the user can achieve what Beatrice termed as "subjective immortality". However, it has one major restriction in that for it to work, the person whose soul is overwritten must usually be of blood-relation to the caster. The spell was originally created by Echidna to gain immortality, but she could not complete it before her demise. Instead, it was finished by Roswaal, who had been using it to survive until the present era. After the Sanctuary's fall, it is revealed that Echidna has slowly been latching more and more of her soul onto Ryuzu Shima, until she successfully hijacked her body, later renaming herself into Omega.
Al Shario (アル・シャリオ): Echidna was capable of casting a forbidden spell that literally brought stardust down to earth, massacring her opponents. The speed of the stardust was described to be almost impossible to evade. She once used this spell to massacre a swarm of around 100 Silver Dragons.
Dream Arts: Echidna is capable of utilizing a lost type of forbidden art known as dream arts which allows its user to manipulate the minds of the target. Though her level of skill with it is not on the same level as someone such as Shion, she still had enough proficiency with it to create the Castle of Dreams.
Castle of Dreams (夢の城, Yume no Shiro): A special space outside the world, which Echidna from the Castle of Dreams has control of, is mentioned to be her dream. Echidna's and the other five Witches' souls manifest within this space after their deaths. The Castle of Dreams primarily takes the form of a seemingly limitless empty grassland with a little hill in the middle, although Echidna can change its appearance at will, being able to turn it into a dark empty void as if a curtain had fallen upon the world. She is capable of creating portals in and out of the Castle of Dreams. Due to it being outside of the world, Subaru suffered none of the penalties from Return By Death while within the Castle of Dreams though Echidna had stated that if he died in the Castle of Dreams, his soul would shatter, resulting in his real body's death as well. 
Memory Manipulation: Echidna from the Castle of Dreams was capable of searching through the memories of others, shown in Arc 4 where she rummages through Subaru's memories to recreate a Japanese high school girl uniform, and she even became aware of Subaru’s memories and meetings from previous failed loops. She was also capable of erasing memories, as seen in Arc 4 where she temporarily seals away Subaru's memories of their meeting in the Castle of Dreams to follow the rule about it being forbidden to talk about their "little tea party" until his trial went underway.
Teleportation: Like Beatrice, Echidna was capable of teleportation magic, with no one else holding the capabilities to display such type of magic, not even her genius disciple Roswaal.

Magic/Forbidden Arts Creation: Echidna is responsible for making numerous techniques, forbidden or otherwise. Three of her most notable creations in this regard are the Soul Transcription technique, which both she and her pupil Roswaal utilized; Ol Shamak, which was made to combat Witch Factor wielders such as the Witches and Sin Archbishops and was taught only to Aldebaran; and Al Shario.

Intelligence
Vast Intellect: As the embodiment of the thirst for knowledge, Echidna was obsessed with gaining knowledge and was in possession of The Book of Wisdom which could show her the world's memory. Echidna possessed one of the greatest intellects in the world, and had conducted numerous experiments with magic, creating powerful meteors. Numerous people from every nation used to come to her, seeking her knowledge when she was alive. She possessed vast knowledge about the older era, to the point she could boast there is nothing she didn't know.

Other
Item/Life Construction: During her lifetime, Echidna created a variety of items and beings due to her vast intellect and absolute mastery of magic.
Artificial Spirit Creation: Echidna has created three artificial spirits: Puck, Beatrice, and Echidna. It is unknown how she created them but they were created via an unspecified mechanisms.
Clone Creation: Echidna was capable of creating Ryuzu Meyer copies by using the original Ryuzu Meyer as a basis for an experiment to research immortality. They were created by crafting an artificial Od through a special spell and creating the rest of the body through mana, adding that all Ryuzu copies created were given enough intelligence to follow orders from birth.
Meteor Creation: Echidna could create meteors, which are items that allow people to use magic without utilizing a gate. However, the only meteors she was known to have forged in her lifetime were Conversation Mirrors and the Star Staff.
Gospel/Book of Wisdom Creations: Echidna researched ways to recreate her Book of Wisdom for others to use. Though they were all considered failures, several of them ended up in the hands of the Witch Cult, guiding them toward their desires, albeit vaguely. The two most advanced versions were passed on to Roswaal and Beatrice, which gave them more accurate looks into the future towards their desires, but still did not show them everything. In fact, Beatrice’s book eventually became void of any words at all.

Miasma: According to Echidna from the Castle of Dreams, she was known for emitting intense miasma that caused people to throw up in her vicinity. If exposed to it for too long, one would be at risk for falling into madness or suffering a mental breakdown, and even dying. Omega used this miasma to kill eighteen bandits in thirty seconds, as soon as she left the Sanctuary. She also noted that someone with the qualifications to become a Sage Candidate would be able to resist her miasma. While he did not receive that side effect, Subaru noted her presence felt as dangerous or more so than the White Whale or the Sin Archbishop of Sloth.

Unknown Ability: During a failed loop of Arc 4, Echidna was capable of modifying Petra Leyte's handkerchief that Subaru had given Echidna earlier, allowing Subaru to harden it in accordance to his will and use it as a weapon to cut away Satella's shadows trying to absorb him. A light shone from the handkerchief. The process which she does this by is unknown.

intro: Daphne (ダフネ) was the Witch of Gluttony. Mentioned throughout the story, she formally debuted in Arc 4 as a supporting character.
appearance:
Daphne had shoulder length ashen hair which she had tied in two tails. Her appearance was that of a 13- or 14-year-old child. She was dressed in a pitch-black straitjacket which she wore over her white clothing, that were chained to her coffin. Both of her eyes were completely covered by a blindfold, wrapped to cross over the center of her face, which lent to her appearance having a more witch-like aura as opposed to other Witches of Sin. Despite her eerie and off-putting aura, she could be quite adorable at times. Her eyes were golden yellow, with her left eye resembling a closed mouth with teeth, whereas her right eye had a visible pupil and resembled an open mouth.

Daphne herself was chained to a black coffin which was mostly seen standing vertically. Daphne named it the Centipede Coffin. On her command, the coffin's lower part would open up and reveal eight crab-like legs that would move itself and its host anywhere Daphne wished to go. She stated her coffin operated on her sweat, saliva, and other bodily wastes produced by her. Subaru described it as a living being, similar to crabs or spiders but more repulsive. The coffin itself was actually a witchbeast created by Daphne long ago, for the sole purpose of serving her as transport.
personality:
As the Witch of Gluttony, Daphne's reason for living was to feel full, causing her to care about the amount more than taste and hunger. She is also anorexic. She was also stated to repeatedly vomit out food and eat it again, although she seems to have indulged in such acts only when there was no more food left. If that option failed, she would resort to eating objects she could chew, such as rugs, curtains, clothes, etc. In an effort to try and get rid of the never-ending hunger, Daphne created witchbeasts but soon after lost control of them and accidentally released them into the world. Despite the threat the witchbeasts present, they were created with a positive mindset - to save the world from hunger. Her view on hunger was bizarre, as to her, those who try to eat others should be wary of being eaten themselves. Because of it, she was unable to comprehend Natsuki Subaru's counterarguments to her self-serving theory. 

Daphne's speech was described as incoherent and surreal. Talking with her eye to eye was practically impossible for anyone who wasn't suffering from extreme hunger, as she did not understand the basic human mindset and values. Her only goal was to save the world and herself from hunger, no matter the cost. Subaru described her mentality as animalistic and not something a person should possess. Her manner of speech was usually cheerful and childish, indicating her age. She also likes to give nicknames to people, such as Subarun to Subaru, Dna Dna to Echidna, Met Met to Sekhmet, Ner Ner to Minerva, Mila Mila to Carmilla, and Tyu Tyu to Typhon. She regarded Gluttony as the most important craving in life, saying that a person is unable to live without eating. She rarely showed emotions or the will for basic human functions apart from indulging in her gluttony. The author has stated that Daphne doesn't care about other people.

Following her death, Daphne accepted her demise and didn't care much about "dying again". Hence, she was perfectly willing to go against Echidna in her Castle of Dreams, even if it meant her one last destruction, most likely by Sekhmet's hands.
history:
A long time ago, a man was afflicted with an incurable disease, and, as he was afraid of dying, he began using various methods to try and prolong his life. Daphne was one of the many people he used in his experiments, and eventually he succeeded in achieving his goal by using her body. In his joy, he forcibly undid her binds, and when she came to her senses, she found herself all alone in the man's castle, suffering from hunger. To satisfy her hunger, she began eating everything in the castle, including things like the throne and the carpets, and resorted to eating what she threw up when necessary. Her body could supposedly not die; however, she felt like she was going to die from hunger. Eventually, she somehow began creating witchbeasts in the castle, which she considered to be illusions at the time, and started to use them as a food source. After a while, her binds broke from the fighting between her and the beasts, allowing her to leave the castle. The witchbeasts also left and spread across the world.

At some point in the past, Minerva and Daphne found themselves in the same location, where they found themselves in an infinite loop of eating and healing, angering each other. However, the context for why this is is unclear.

It was claimed that over 400 years ago, Daphne died of starvation in an unnamed desert. Echidna later proceeded to locate and collect her soul, allowing Daphne to manifest in Echidna's Castle of Dreams.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
Considering Daphne is ranked just behind Typhon in terms of strength, it's safe to assume she holds considerable power. The author has stated that Daphne cannot create anything stronger than herself, meaning she is individually stronger than any one of the Three Great Witchbeasts. She could eat the entire White Whale in a single bite.

Authority
Authority of Gluttony (暴食の権能, Bōshoku no Ken'nō): As the Witch of Gluttony, Daphne was a user of the Authority of Gluttony and was a compatible holder of its corresponding Witch Factor. Her Authority granted her abilities related to consumption.
Consumption: According to the author, Daphne is capable of devouring the entire White Whale in a single bite, and later, she was shown to be able to eat even spirits with ease. According to Echidna, she was a terror if she decided to "devour" someone. It should be noted that while she is capable of eating spirits, this is not the same as the Spirit Eating employed by the Spirit Eater tribe.
Magic Eyes: In the web novel, Daphne could be seen using her Authority of Gluttony and making people feel extreme hunger by touching or looking at them. She had two so-called “magic eyes”: her left eye, the magic eye of famine, and her right eye, the magic eye of apastia. This ability has been removed from the light novel, hence should not be considered as canon until stated or proven otherwise. That being said, an illustration from the second art book displays two labels of famine and apastia alongside Daphne's eyes, though the eyes are reversed from what they were in the web novel.
Famine (飢餓, Kiga): The magic eye in Daphne's left eye. Just a single glance from this eye was enough to force the target to experience extreme famine, causing them to eat their arm and try to lick their own blood while ignoring everything other than the thought of eating. Despite this, Echidna described Daphne's left eye as "nothing much" when compared to her right eye.
Apastia (拒食, Kyoshoku): The magic eye in Daphne's right eye, which Echidna claimed was a terror if she used.
Life Creation: Daphne is able to create living things out of nothing. She creates witchbeasts when her mood is "woozy" from her "Third Mouth". Through her ability, she created all witchbeasts, including the Three Great Witchbeasts: the White Whale, Great Rabbit, and Black Serpent. The White Whale had the ability to erase anything it touched with its mist of elimination from existence. The Great Rabbit had an insatiable hunger and only ate living things, and there were as many of them as there are water droplets in mist as it could multiply infinitely so long as at least one of them was left alive. It left no trace of the people it ate, and it was said to be able to reduce land to a barren wasteland. The Black Serpent can plague its victims with a hundred diseases just by touching them, and any ground that it slithers over becomes cursed, making anything except witchbeasts unable to live on it. A person that came into contact with its tongue was scarred with reddish black burns, another had their skin from the neck up covered in reddish black spots that gushed black blood, and another had their body dried up to the point that touching them might break their body apart.

name: Flugel
alias: Sage (賢者, Kenja)
nickname: Great Sage (大賢人, Dai Kenjin) (by Shaula) ; Master (お師様, Oshi-sama) (by Shaula) ; Instigator (扇動者, Sendōsha) (by Echidna) ; The Wisest One (by Otto Suwen) ; Astrophile/Monster (by Natsuki Subaru)
previous_affiliation: Japan ; Kingdom of Lugunica ; Witch Era Party ; Pleiades Watchtower
intro: Flugel (フリューゲル) was the Sage, a member of the Witch Era Party, and a key figure in the sealing of the Witch of Envy 400 years ago. Though mentioned throughout the series, his identity as the Great Sage is not revealed until Arc 6, his name having been mostly erased from history and his exploits instead credited to his disciple, Shaula.
appearance: Not much is known about Flugel or what he looked like, despite his face being engraved on the Lugunican currency. It is presumed that his outfit resembled Shaula's in some way as she mentioned she dressed similarly to him.
personality: Shaula mentioned that Flugel was a very smart and intelligent person. He apparently stated how tiring it was to talk to Shaula multiple times, implying he was also exasperated of her antics. Both Petelgeuse and Volcanica spoke of him with respect and fondness respectively, indicating he was rather likeable. According to Alec Hoshin, Flugel was the most likely person to die in their travelling group, ahead of Alec himself.
history:
Approximately 400 years before Subaru's arrival, Flugel was summoned to the world from Japan. Later, he would go on a journey with Satella, Echidna, Reid Astrea, Farsale Lugunica, and Alec Hoshin. He and Daphne would also create the unique witchbeast, Shaula, for currently unknown reasons at an unknown point in time. He also formed a partnership of sorts with Echidna. According to Echidna, at the time of their travels, they needed to keep their identities secret. However, at one point during their travels, they ended up in the country of Magrizza. Despite attempting to hide their identities, Farsale declared his own name, resulting in a noble discovering them and inviting them to a banquet of nobles. However, the nation's crown prince, who was also in attendance at the banquet, became enamored by Echidna and went behind the scenes to arrange a marriage between the two of them, with Echidna's party going along with them after they were split from their capable fighters. However, at some point, for reasons yet to be explained, Reid and Volcanica went on a rampage, ultimately resulting in the marriage being cancelled and them being driven from the nation. It was a short time later that they learned that the Black Serpent destroyed Magrizza. According to Echidna, it was likely that they were being chased by the Black Serpent.

At some point, the Pleiades Watchtower, which Flugel is said to have built, was constructed. The Sage is said to have met the first generation's Sword Saint, Reid Astrea, and the Divine Dragon, Volcanica, in one of the Kingdom's five regional capitals, Flanders, located in southern part of the Kingdom, and blessed the grounds of Flanders so Earth Dragons would be born. After Satella, the Witch of Envy, suddenly went out of control and went on a rampage across the world, Flugel met with Reid and Volcanica in Flanders, forming an alliance with the heroes. The three heroes set their goals on defeating the rampaging Witch who mercilessly killed thousands and thousands of innocents and toppled one country after another. After realizing they were unable to kill her, Flugel and the rest managed to defeat her and seal her away in the Augria Sand Dunes at the very east of the Dragon Kingdom of Lugunica. 

At the Pleaides Watchtower, which was in the vicinity of the Evil Sealing Stone Shrine, Flugel gave Shaula the task of watching over the Witch of Envy's seal, giving her the order to indiscriminately kill anyone who attempted to approach the area. He also erased himself from history, giving Shaula all the credit for his role in the fight against the Witch for an unspecified reason. Sometime after, the Sage was said to have planted a seed in the middle of the Lifaus Highway; a seed that would later grow into a giant tree dubbed Flugel's Tree. The tree would later be destroyed by Natsuki Subaru in order to defeat the White Whale.

At some point, he entrusted Petelgeuse Romanée-Conti with a box containing the Witch Factor of Sloth. The Kingdom of Lugunica also engraved his purported face on their silver coins.
abilities_text:
Great Power: As Flugel potentially had the power to kill Shaula and played a role in the sealing of the Witch of Envy, Flugel is rumored to have had a considerable amount of power. However, it is not known if Flugel actually fought the Witch herself.

Vast Intellect: Considering his title as the Sage and numerous legends surrounding him, Flugel was known for having been a very intelligent person, considered by many to rival the Divine Dragon himself, in terms of intellect. Throughout the centuries following Satella's defeat, numerous countries dispatched envoys to the Tower in order to make contact with the Sage and gain knowledge that was unable to be obtained in any other way.
