intro: Julius Juukulius (ユリウス・ユークリウス) is Anastasia Hoshin's knight and a member of the Royal Guard. He played major roles in both Arc 3 and Arc 6 and supporting roles in Arc 5 and Arc 8. Julius was also one of the main protagonists of The Travelogue of the Finest, as well as a supporting character in The Dream the Lion King Saw.
appearance:
Julius is a tall young man of a well-built muscular stature with yellow eyes and gleaming light purple hair that is arranged neatly with a strand hanging down his face. He almost exclusively wears the formal Royal Guard uniform. When he fought with Subaru, he took off his Royal Guard's coat and wore a black suit with blue borders.

In the Water Plumage Inn in Arc 5, he wore a yukata, and for a short period later, he wore a cloak that protected him from the sands of the Augria Sand Dunes. After his fight with Reid Astrea in Arc 6, Julius received a cut directly under his left eye. Due to the nature of the cut, the scar is permanent.

During the events of Arc 8, Julius wore Kararagian fashioned clothing: a kimono with a black nagagi and white hakama, a haori the same shade of purple as his hair, a red scarf, his sword at his waist, and a pair of sandals.
personality:
As a member of Lugunica's nobility, Julius acts in a proper fashion, always having an air of nobility and conviction. He is also considerate and doesn't forget to show care toward others. He also shows a strict side, giving out accurate assessments of others whether they're good or bad, which is a result of his upbringing as an elite, whilst currently, he believes that he and others can do better than they currently are. Julius also appears to be somewhat of a history buff, and he tends to display hints of excitement when a situation involves people who have left their mark on history. In fact, a part of him felt excited by the prospect of confronting such people during the Great Disaster, albeit he tempered his expectations after having already met Reid Astrea prior, who both lived up to and betrayed the image he had of the first Sword Saint.

Despite his demeanor, which clashes with Subaru's modernized world view, Julius tends to worry about others, even those who do not like him. When Subaru lashed out during the Royal Selection Ceremony, despite agreeing with Subaru, because he feared that Subaru would be executed for his remarks by the Royal Army, Julius made an example of him in order to save his life and to quell the army's anger, while resulted in a one-sided and publicly humiliating beating and his own temporary house arrest. Ferris later points out that despite these actions, he held out hope in the young man, even when later they decided they would never be friends. Of course, despite this, Julius still wishes to befriend people such as Subaru, and despite early rocky relationships, he is more than willing to listen to their accounts of important matters, such as believing Subaru on everything he had to say regarding the Witch Cult before the Subjugation of Sloth.

However, as pointed out by Reid Astrea, beneath his noble demeanor, Julius is actually a very insecure person who desperately holds on to his bonds with others. This mindset seems to be the result of his parents' deaths, causing him to seek attention to fill the void in his heart. During his final duel with Reid, Julius acknowledged his flaws and gained mutual respect with the first-generation Sword Saint. He then began working to remake the bonds he lost when after his name was eaten. During said duel with Reid, he also claimed that maintaining his appearance as a noble and chivalrous knight was something he kept up for others. As he was once inspired by such a knight, he wished to keep up his appearance as one of a similar kind so that others may have something to strive for, something which Reid acknowledged and claimed was very similar to a friend of his. It is thanks to his interactions with Reid, Subaru, who made him question who would be more worthy of the title of knight, and the reforging of his bonds after his name was devoured that he was able to restore his confidence and steel his resolve to one day ask for a proper spar with his friend, Reinhard van Astrea, whose strength he was fully aware of. Likewise, it also strengthened his ambition to become stronger, going as far as to request training from another of the world's strongest citizens, Halibel, to attain strength so that he could become a better knight that could protect the people around him.

Julius is also as idealistic as Subaru and Emilia, believing that goodness exists in everyone, even those who are classified as evil. In fact, it is for this reason that Julius assists Subaru with handling Spica, who had originally been the Sin Archbishop of Gluttony of the Witch Cult, people who are criminals and hated by everyone in the world, as he believed that she was an inherently new person as she was at this point.
history:
Joshua Juukulius's Careful Encyclopedia (Early Life)
Julius was born as the son of Klein Juukulius, who had run away from his noble family and married a commoner woman. Sometime later, his parents died while saving people in a flash flood, and Julius was taken in by his uncle, Alviero Juukulius. One day, Alviero explained the situation to his son, Joshua Juukulius, asking him if he had any questions about it since it would affect his life. After claiming that he had no questions, he had Julius introduce himself. When Julius introduced himself, he offered a handshake which led to him mistakenly giving an introduction meant for a lady and causing Alviero to laugh. However, Joshua started to cry, causing Julius, Alviero, and the servants of the house to panic.

The next morning, Julius had started practicing swordsmanship with Alviero, which Joshua had awoken to hear. It did not take long for Julius to be disarmed and lose to Alviero, causing him great frustration, which Alviero said to treasure and recalled how his own frustration and sense of loss to swing the sword had faded away at some point. With morning practice over, Julius noticed Joshua and asked if he slept well. Not long after, Julius visited Joshua in his room and explained that he hadn't been taught about being a knight before and that he wished he had been more serious. When asked what he did when he lived with his parents, Julius told him that he would either help them or play with his friends, and he wasn't aware of being a member of House Juukulius until Alviero came to adopt him. Joshua recalled that Julius's parents died in a flash flood while saving people, and he called them great people. However, Julius asked if it was weird that he just wanted his parents to be alive and worried about whether it was fine to do as Alviero said. After thinking about it, Joshua said he needed to become a hero to become worthy of his parents. Desperate, he asked what a hero was, and Joshua looked to a bookshelf where his favorite story was, which would be Julius's ideal. From that point forward, they met regularly in Joshua's room to read those epics.

In the month that followed, Julius's studies and training continued, and he discovered his Divine Protection and that he was beloved by spirits. He and Joshua had also gone to Julius's debut, where Julius first saw a young Reinhard, and he realized that he was a real hero. Joshua, however, who felt humiliated, suddenly had an attack and blacked out, and his health deteriorated. When Julius visited him, worried about him, he asked if he wanted him to do anything, and Joshua pointed towards that appas on a tree. When Julius went to get one, Joshua got a reminder of the differences between them and laughed and cried, questioning why he was even still alive.

At some point after this, about a month after Julius first arrived in the manor, Julius went to Joshua's room, where Joshua was waiting with the next chronicle of Reid Astrea, which he was looking forward to. After Julius noticed his strange expression, Joshua said he was just happy that Julius was interested in the book, and he asked if his training, both with the sword and Divine Protection, was tough, and though Julius said it was hard, he didn't say it was tough, though he admitted that these were the kinds of things that the heroes they read about experienced, something which made Joshua recall what happened with Reinhard.

It is unknown if it was during that month or after, but one day, a group of spirits approached Julius, and they eventually made a contract with him.

First Mission
Five years before the Royal Selection, Julius was involved in the investigation of the organization led by Reiner Wahrheit alongside Bikram Edditz and Helaine Gatness. With assistance from Reinhard, who had infiltrated the organization by disguising himself as a girl named Adelheid, they were able to bring him down and arrest him.

The Dream the Lion King Saw
Roughly 8 to 9 months before the start of the Arc 1, Julius, together with Reinhard van Astrea, formed a friendly bond with a new knight of the Royal Guard, Felix Argyle. The two knights stood behind Ferris' back, supporting him on his endeavors in the Royal Guard. One faithful day, Julius was tasked with escorting Prince Fourier Lugunica to the Argyle Manor, in order to rescue Crusch Karsten, who has been taken hostage by Biehn Argyle, the lord of the manor. After retrieving the Duchess, Julius swiftly dispatched the remaining undead, who had been resurrected via the Sacrament of the Immortal King.

The Travelogue of the Finest
Roughly 4–5 months before the events of Arc 1 and a couple of months after the mysterious illness took the lives of the entire royal family, Julius, alongside Reinhard and Ferris, were tasked with escorting two members of the Council of Wise Men, Miklotov McMahon and Bordeaux Zergev, on a diplomatic mission to the neighboring Sacred Vollachia Empire. During their stay, the Ninth ranking Divine General, Balleroy Temeglyph, was seemingly killed, and Reinhard was blamed for it, forcing the Royal Guard trio to "kidnap" the seventy-seventh emperor, Vincent Vollachia, and flee the Crystal Palace. In a nearby forest, they were ambushed by Eighth and Sixth ranking Divine Generals Moguro Hagane and Groovy Gumlet respectively. As Reinhard held back the two Generals, Julius and Ferris fled further ahead with the emperor, but they encountered the First ranking Divine General, Cecilus Segmunt. Julius and Cecilus fought but the Royal Knight was no match for the Divine General. After successfully breaking Cecilus' one of his swords, the Blue Lightning decided to fight him a bit more seriously. Just as he was about to decapitate the Spirit Knight, Reinhard came to the rescue. A short duel between the two strongest swordsmen of their respective nations followed, and Reinhard came out victorious.

After successfully escaping from the three Divine Generals, Julius, Reinhard, Ferris, and Vincent finally had some time to breathe and plan out their next steps. Vincent revealed that Balleroy most likely stands behind the ongoing coup d'état. Before they could devise a plan, however, a group of 30 assassins from the Insect Cage Clan engaged the three Knights and the emperor. However, Reinhard stayed behind and swiftly defeated all thirty of them. Meanwhile, while making their escape from yet another serious threat, Julius, Ferris, and Vincent fell into an ambush created by the thought-to-be-dead Divine General Balleroy Temeglyph, who managed to snipe off Vincent's right arm by the shoulder while riding on his Flying Dragon Carillon. While Ferris healed the mortally wounded emperor, Julius continued deflecting Balleroy's magical snipes, keeping him at bay and defending his friends. After devising a plan and using Ferris as a decoy, Julius was able to pinpoint Balleroy's location despite the man's invisibility, and he hit them with Al Clauzeria, killing Carillon and seriously wounding the Balleroy. Julius and Balleroy then engaged in their final duel, which ended with the Spirit Knight's blade piercing the Divine General's chest, killing him. After the threat was finally dealt with, Julius, Vincent, and Ferris regrouped with Reinhard and returned to the Crystal Palace, resolving the conflict. As a token of gratitude, the emperor signed a non-aggression pact between the Empire and the Kingdom, marking the Kingdom's ambassadors' mission as successful.

Roughly a month after Balleroy's rebellion, Julius and Ferris encountered Cecilus in a tavern located in the Royal Capital. Due to the danger that the Divine General presented, the duo accompanied him to a tea house located on the outskirts of the city, where Cecilus informed them of his plans to fight with the Sword Saint Reinhard van Astrea. However, because of Reinhard's absence due to him being on a mission at the Holy Kingdom of Gusteko's borders with Lugunica, Julius had no other option but to secretly accept the Divine General as a guest in his mansion, since his presence in the Royal Capital was illegal. After four days of hiding a Divine General inside House Juukulius, Julius and Ferris were suddenly called to Captain Marcos Gildark's office, where the Fourth ranking Divine General, Chisha Gold, was waiting. The two knights were then given a task to accompany Chisha to his needs in the Royal Capital, and the trio set out to find the person Chisha was after. Arriving just in time, they were able to prevent Cecilus from beheading the High Count Gramdart Holstoy who was behind the failed coup d'état and had fled the Empire. Having fulfilled their mission, Chisha and Cecilus were prepared to return back to the Empire with High Count Holstoy, but they were stopped by Marcos, who arranged a proxy match between Cecilus and Reinhard.

Pre-Royal Selection
Anastasia Hoshin, having met Alviero several years prior, decided to hold talks with the Juukulius family, seeking to expand into Lugunica's market. As the meeting began to progress towards a fruitless result for both sides, Mimi happened to find a Dragon Insignia. Anastasia told her to give it back, and she claimed it from Mimi, apologizing for the hassle after Julius told her it was a valuable artifact. However, as she held it, the insignia shone brightly. This designated her as a candidate for the Royal Selection. At that time, Julius asked himself what he would choose to do if Anastasia decided to become involved with the Royal Selection. After learning of its meaning, she soon set her mind on participating.

Camp Formation Stories
Anastasia and Julius went to a meeting at the Royal Castle with the knights, the noble civil servants, and the Council of Wise Men, with Crusch Karsten also in attendance. She declared her intent to participate in the Royal Selection, and Julius explained how she was discovered as a candidate. Bordeaux Zergev lashed out at Julius for bringing a foreigner into the mix, but Miklotov McMahon reprimanded him, causing him to back down. Anastasia agreed to sign a non-disclosure contract and proved her candidacy to the audience by making the Dragon Jewel shine. Following the meeting, Crusch spoke with Anastasia and recognized her as a rival for the throne. Afterwards, Julius and Reinhard van Astrea went to Conwood Melahau's tavern, the Silver Shield, where he requested the Sword Saint to become Anastasia's knight. That night, Julius returned to his mansion and spoke with Anastasia again, and upon learning of his request to Reinhard from him, she immediately became upset and said she would return to her home country, quickly leaving the mansion.

Julius was troubled and did not realize the mistake he had made, but after receiving encouragement from Joshua, who said the Kingdom's number one knight was the Finest of Knights and that Anastasia needed the best knight, even if it meant that House Juukulius would face opposition for supporting a foreigner, he resolved himself to meet her. At an inn, Anastasia told Ricardo and the triplets to not allow anyone through to her. Julius encountered them and fought with Ricardo without a sword, easily beating him, although he had not been in top condition because he had been drinking. Julius then spoke to Anastasia through her door, retracting his request to Reinhard and offering his services instead, after which she opened the door and they performed the ritual of knighting, and in the end, the Finest of Knights became the merchant's knight.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
Though not nearly on the same level as Reinhard or Marcos Gildark, Julius is among the strongest individuals of the Dragon Kingdom of Lugunica. At one point, he was stated to be skilled and powerful enough to be able to reach the title of a Second-Class General in the Imperial Army of the Vollachia Empire, a position reserved for individuals who are either unparalleled tacticians, have distinguished themselves with excellent leadership capabilities, or stand out from the rest in terms of overall strength and skill in combat, but are not walking monsters capable of single-handedly turning the tide of a major battle. Though almost completely outmatched in both instances, Julius displayed enough strength to survive battles with legends of such strength as the Blue Lightning and the first Sword Saint and even withstand their onslaught of attacks for a short time. After the contract with his spirits was renewed, his strength was enhanced significantly further to the point that he was able to easily defeat the undead Sphinx with little resistance. He continues to improve his skill and has even trained with the strongest man in Kararagi, Halibel, following the Great Disaster, and Halibel has acknowledged his skill as being one of the most powerful people in the Kingdom.

Divine Protection
thumb|250px|Julius encased in the power of his spirits.
Divine Protection of Gathering Spirits (誘精の加護 Yūsei no Kago): This enables Julius to see, talk, and be liked by spirits, though he has to work hard to actually get liked by spirits. The effect is so prominent that most lesser and quasi-spirits are willing to fight with each other to approach him, while more powerful spirits, though not so blinded by this Divine Protection, become fond or at least have a positive impression of him. Likewise, this makes him one of the few people within the Kingdom to have a gift to form contracts with spirits.

Magic/Spiritual Arts

Julius has an affinity for the wind attribute. However, he does not practice ordinary magic. Instead, Julius, who is contracted with the six spirits, Ia (イア, red/fire), Kua (クア, blue/water), Aro (アロ, green/wind), Iku (イク, yellow/earth), In (イン, orange/white/yang), and Nes (ネス, purple/black/yin), excels in using spiritual arts, making him one of only two Spirit Knights (精霊騎士, Seirei Kishi) in the Kingdom of Lugunica. By entrusting his spirits with the use of magic in his place, he is able to combine different attributes of magic simultaneously and weave it into his swordplay, whether that is to cast offensive spells, to boost his weapon's or his own abilities, to heal, or to impair his opponent's abilities. Although he was forced to sever his contract at one point with his spirits, because he was able to renew it, his spirits, which had previously been quasi-spirits, managed to evolve, making both them and himself stronger and capable of a wider array of strong spells. When they are not in materialized, they reside within their own crystal which Julius keeps on his person.

Spells:
Healing Magic (治癒魔法, Chiyu Mahō): Julius can use water mana via Kua to heal his allies' wounds.
thumb|250px|Julius using Aro as a propeller and cushion.
El Fura (エル・フーラ, Eru Fūra): With assistance from his wind spirit Aro, Julius can unleash the second level of Fura in which he can create a burst of wind, with uses ranging from several slashes, cushioning a fall, or churning the air and ground to create dust clouds.
Strength Enhancement: Julius can call on In to boost his strength and agility, granting him superhuman abilities for a period of time.
Strength Impairment: Julius can call on Nes to impair the power of his opponent. The full extent of this impairment is unknown, but at the very least, it does seem to affect his opponent's physical abilities to an extent.
Yin Magic Sealing: Julius is able to employ a type of seal made of yin magic that can both prevent the target from dying and keep them from moving. It is the same kind of seal that was used to seal the Witch of Envy. According to Al, it works similarly to Ol Shamak, and according to Roy Alphard, anyone sealed this way can still somewhat sense the outside world. It required the combined efforts of Beatrice and Julius to create, and the only way to undo the seal would require that the one breaking the seal is skilled in Yin Magic as well.

Combined Spells: Since he can call on more than one spirit to use magic, he can have them combine their respective attributes in order to create or combine spells together, either enhancing their effectiveness or using spells rarely used by other mages. Likewise, depending on how he times his spells, he can activate two separate spells simultaneously onto different targets or with very different purposes.
thumb|250px|Julius using Ul Gora.
Ul Gora (ウル・ゴーラ): Julius calls on Ia and Aro to produce a powerful magical firestorm by combining both Fire and Wind magic.
thumb|250px|Julius and Subaru using Nect.
Nect (ネクト): A high-level magic that enables people to share senses within the effect area by connecting their gates. It is considered to be difficult to use, however, In and Nes can use it by pairing Yin and Yang Magic together and tuning the interference of mana between people. If it is too weak, the thoughts won't get through, yet if it's too strong, people won't know where the line between them and other people begins. Performed with In and Nes.

Unique Spells: Although he does not generally create spells, he is one of only a few capable of using all six elements. Furthermore, with his contracts, he can activate them all simultaneously without suffering the same kind of backlash as a non-spiritual arts using mage. As such, he is effectively one of the only people capable of casting these spells, and freely, in the world.
thumb|250px|Julius using Al Clarista.
Clarista (クラリスタ): Julius imbues his sword with the power of his six spirits, empowering it. Clarista and its different levels are Julius' original magic.
Al Clarista (アル・クラリスタ): Al Clarista allows Julius to imbue his sword with the power of his six quasi-spirits (after his fight with Reid Astrea, he can do that with his newly bloomed spirits), cladding his blade in a brilliant rainbow light. According to him, when this spell is in use, he can cut almost everything with his sword, no matter the toughness. Julius displayed this ability two times, roughly half a year before the start of the Royal Selection on his diplomatic journey to the Sacred Vollachia Empire. There, he fought the First and Ninth ranking Divine Generals on separate occasions, and managed to break the former's 5th best sword, and kill the latter. Julius is also capable of using the long-range version of Clarista where the spell takes the form of a beam of pure destructive energy. The light is capable of cutting through anything and everything in its path. After Julius reforged his contract with his quasi-spirits, the power and range of the attack greatly increased, surprising even Julius. During his battle with the Ninth ranking Divine General of the Vollachia Empire, Julius used this spell to melt away the General's spear and pierce his chest, killing him.
thumb|250px|Julius using Al Clauzeria.
Al Clauzeria (アル・クラウゼリア): When Al Clauzeria is casted, six different colored spirits start circling around Julius and join into one whirling rainbow-hued vortex of light which is shot out from the tip of his sword. Immediately following the impact of the rainbow light, the torrent of light explodes in a sizeable shock wave that sends his opponents flying. The wall as well as the vortex are composed of six elements, which are able to repel any sort of magic that is casted against it as well as any and all physical attacks. Furthermore, in the novelization of Julius' duel with Petelgeuse Romanée-Conti, the rainbow shockwave started expanding directly from his own body, rather being shot out from the tip of his sword, easily purifying away close to a hundred unseen hands that enveloped the Knight from all sides, just seconds prior. Despite the small difference in execution, both versions have the same effect. Following the evolution of his quasi-spirits into spirits, this attack has enough power to completely wipe away one of the heads of a Dragon the caliber of Valgren. By tweaking the spell, Julius can use this spell to create a dome-like barrier around himself and his targets. Ordinarily, this is used for defense, but it can also be used to trap aerial opponents such as Balleroy Temeglyph near the ground. Following the evolution of his spirits, his barrier has shown to be able to extend to cover up to half of the entirety of the Fortified City of Garkla.
Al Cranvel (アル・クランヴェル): Al Cranvel is Julius' secret technique he developed long ago but never managed to properly utilize, due to his lack of experience. After he forged a new contract with his newly bloomed spirits, Julius called upon their power and clad himself in their sixfold power, greatly increasing his speed and overall power. To the other party, Julius appeared as if he was swallowed alive by a rainbow. This sword skill is noted as Julius' ultimate attack. Debuting this trump card during his final duel with legendary Reid Astrea, it played a vital role in helping him overcome the obstacle known as the first generation's Sword Saint.

Physical Traits/Flow Method

Master Swordsman: Julius is a master of swordsmanship who is considered one of the greatest practitioners within the Kingdom. He uses an orthodox style of swordsmanship that is fast and precise, and though he is not very fond of using underhanded tricks with his attacks, he more than makes up for it with pure skill. His skills can be further augmented with his spiritual arts.

Intelligence
Keen Strategist: Julius is rather knowledgeable in various matters. With such knowledge at his disposal, he is able to come up with various strategies in order to counter his target. In one notable example, during the Reaper Disaster, Julius used his knowledge of how tornadoes are formed in order to counter one created with the power of a great spirit, using large pieces of rubble to slow the wind and use fire to counteract the fronts that were giving the tornado its momentum and destructive force. In another case, he used a barrier, ordinarily used for defense over a limited area, to trap his enemy, Balleroy, and prevent him from taking to the skies and regaining the advantage.

Equipment
Heirloom Sword: Julius wielded a sword, which was a prized heirloom of House Juukulius. He spent years mastering its use. During the events of Arc 6, however, the sword broke when Julius fought against Reid for the first time.
Spare Sword: Following his duel with Reid, Julius resorted to using a spare sword he brought with him. According to Subaru's observation from one of the failed loops, Julius' new sword looked like a cheap and mass-produced weapon, a model likely used by many of the other knights.

name: Kadomon Risch
relatives: Raksha Risch (wife) ; Plum Risch (daughter) ; Grimm Fauzen (father-in-law) ; Carol Remendis (mother-in-law) ; Flam Remendis (niece) ; Grassis Remendis (niece)
intro: Kadomon Risch (カドモン・リッシュ) is a fruit seller in the Royal Capital of Lugunica.
appearance:
Kadomon is a muscular and firmly built fruit seller and often carries a twig in his mouth. He has green hair which he bands back into a slicked-back style, with a hairband to hold it tightly together. He wears a black vest with a golden outline and two bracelets line his wrists.

His face is dominated by two large scars running down from his forehead to his chin and right below his left eye, given to him by his wife Raksha. He also has a small goatee and two sky blue eyes.
personality: Despite his rough looks, Kadomon is actually a kind and good-natured person, though he gets annoyed with people's antics when they happen in front of his store since it usually detracts from his business. When it comes to his family, he shows gratitude toward those who help them and is willing to repay them however he can, which he did for Emilia in spite of her appearance. Furthermore, he will immediately move to assist others when an accident happens, and he is willing to go against the Royal Army to protect others who are doing what they can to help others, such as what he did for Natsuki Subaru.
history:
At an unknown point in time, Kadomon met Raksha, and she gave him his scar. The two worked as part of the same mercenary troupe for a time, and at some point, the two got married and had their child, Plum.

Behind the Scenes of Life in Another World from Zero
On the day of Subaru's arrival into the world, sometime after Subaru left his stand, his wife arrived at his stand, and at some point after, Emilia appeared with his daughter, who had gotten lost after being separated from her mother. When Kadomon asked her how he could repay her, though she didn't give the full explanation, she asked about Felt and how something she had was stolen, leading him to tell her about the Loot House and warning her not to go there. Emilia still resolved to go there, and before she could go, Plum offered her a red flower ornament as thanks for her help.

intro: Joshua Juukulius (ヨシュア・ユークリウス) is Julius Juukulius's cousin and adoptive younger brother, and he is a member of the Anastasia Camp. He played a lesser supporting role in Arc 5.
appearance: Joshua is an elegant and handsome young man with a clear and slender face and long, light purple hair that he regularly ties into a tail, leaving it to elegantly fall down his shoulders. He has bright and sparkling, yellow slant up eyes that give off a sharp look which left a pretty bad first impression on Subaru. His black clothes are well tailored and perfectly fit his slender physique; paired with his monocle, they give off a strict and scholarly impression, and one can easily figure out his social standing. He's described to give off an impression of a boy who would best fit into a quiet room, immersed in literature - which coincidentally was how he spent most of his childhood. Despite that, Joshua is extremely well mannered, and his posture is elegant and befitting of a noble.
personality:
Unlike his brother Julius, Joshua does not have the same composed personality, as shown when he gets flustered with the antics of the Emilia Camp members and can be quick to fear others based off of rumors. Despite this, he has a serious yet amiable personality, and Natsuki Subaru considers him easier to get along with than Julius. He respects his brother to the utmost degree and cannot stop when he starts talking about him, and likewise, he has a great respect for spirits and the people who are able to contract with them, which he displayed upon meeting Subaru and Beatrice. He has also developed a passion for art and painting.

Even with his utmost calm and collected personality, he was previously subtly racist towards demi-humans, with Julius describing that Joshua had a narrowed view towards the world. Since then, he has shed his prejudice, and he has shown not to be fazed when dealing with either members of the Anastasia Camp, which is comprised of many demi-humans, or even Emilia, someone who was hated and feared for being a silver-haired half elf who bore a resemblance to the Witch of Envy, though in the case of the latter, he had to be convinced that his lingering fear was baseless.

Despite all this, due to his frail condition, Joshua was jealous of his brother, even bordering on a slight hatred, which Roy Alphard stated using Joshua's memories.
history:
Joshua Juukulius's Careful Encyclopedia (Early Life)
Joshua was born sickly, and he would regularly have coughing fits and would be forced to be bedridden. Because of this, he was physically very weak and quickly ran out of stamina. As such, unable to train himself or learn combat skills, he spent his childhood buried in books. One day, Alviero explained the situation to his son regarding the adoption of his cousin, Julius, into the family, asking him if he had any questions about it since it would affect his life. After claiming that he had no questions, he had Julius introduce himself. When Julius introduced himself, he offered a handshake which led to him mistakenly giving an introduction meant for a lady and causing Alviero to laugh. However, Joshua started to cry, causing Julius, Alviero, and the servants of the house to panic.

The next morning, Julius had started practicing swordsmanship with Alviero, which Joshua had awoken to hear. It did not take long for Julius to be disarmed and lose to Alviero, causing him great frustration, which Alviero said to treasure and recalled how his own frustration and sense of loss to swing the sword had faded away at some point. With morning practice over, Julius noticed Joshua and asked if he slept well. Not long after, Julius visited Joshua in his room and explained that he hadn't been taught about being a knight before and that he wished he had been more serious. When asked what he did when he lived with his parents, Julius told him that he would either help them or play with his friends, and he wasn't aware of being a member of House Juukulius until Alviero came to adopt him. Joshua recalled that Julius's parents died in a flash flood while saving people, and he called them great people. However, Julius asked if it was weird that he just wanted his parents to be alive and worried about whether it was fine to do as Alviero said. After thinking about it, Joshua said he needed to become a hero to become worthy of his parents. Desperate, he asked what a hero was, and Joshua looked to a bookshelf where his favorite story was, which would be Julius's ideal. From that point forward, they met regularly in Joshua's room to read those epics.

In the month that followed, Julius's studies and training continued, and he discovered his Divine Protection and that he was beloved by spirits. He and Joshua had also gone to Julius's debut, where Julius first saw a young Reinhard van Astrea, and he realized that he was a real hero. Joshua, however, who felt humiliated, suddenly had an attack and blacked out, and his health deteriorated. When Julius visited him, worried about him, he asked if he wanted him to do anything, and Joshua pointed towards that appas on a tree. When Julius went to get one, Joshua got a reminder of the differences between them and laughed and cried, questioning why he was even still alive. Though he never said so out loud since, seeing Julius climb that tree to get an appa stirred his jealousy and made him feel a small sense of hatred.

At some point after this, about a month after Julius first arrived in the manor, Julius went to Joshua's room, where Joshua was waiting with the next chronicle of Reid Astrea, which he was looking forward to. After Julius noticed his strange expression, Joshua said he was just happy that Julius was interested in the book, and he asked if his training, both with the sword and Divine Protection, was tough, and though Julius said it was hard, he didn't say it was tough, though he admitted that these were the kinds of things that the heroes they read about experienced, something which made Joshua recall what happened with Reinhard.

As he watched Julius's feats growing up, observing him practicing with a sword and often wishing he could join him, his admiration long since outweighed his envy, and he started learning clerical duties.

Pre-Royal Selection
At some point before the Royal Selection's start, Anastasia Hoshin visited House Juukulius in an effort to expand her business into Lugunica. While Joshua was concerned over her presence as well as the presence of demi-humans, he shared these concerns with his brother, though he was scolded for his narrow sightedness. After meeting Anastasia and her party, he came to respect her and her business-oriented mind. After learning of Anastasia's qualification to become Lugunica's monarch and her official induction into the Royal Selection, Julius and Joshua, alongside other members of the Iron Fang, began helping her set up her business in Lugunica, and he joined his brother in joining the Anastasia Camp. He also came to look up to Tivey Pearlbaton after meeting him, and he began mimicking him by wearing a monocle.

Joshua Juukulius's Careful Encyclopedia
As Mimi, Hetaro, and Tivey had entered his room the moment they realized that there was food, Joshua, who was honored to have finally been chosen to do something for Anastasia, was concerned that he had to act as a messenger to invite Emilia to Priestella, nervous and somewhat fearful of her due to her race and the rumors of her appearance being a match for the Witch of Envy. However, Mimi declared that Emilia wasn't scary, and recalling that Hetaro and Tivey had interacted with the Emilia Camp for the Subjugation of the White Whale and the Subjugation of Sloth, he asked for their opinions. While Tivey claimed that Emilia didn't seem to be scary, Hetaro declared that he only ever talked with her knight, Natsuki Subaru, someone else that Joshua had heard rumors and was wary of, as his origins were unknown and he had no known power. He also recalled the other worrisome rumors about the camp, which only increased his worries.

Deciding to directly ask Anastasia her intentions of sending him, Joshua shared his thoughts with her and asked her outright. Though she said that Emilia and Subaru wouldn't be scary, she had called for Julius and told him that Joshua was worried about coming off as rude toward the members of the Emilia Camp, which Julius agreed with since he said that they were nothing like the rumors claimed them to be. However, he also said to watch out for Subaru, who was more than what he seemed, was very loyal and determined, and had earned his position as her knight as a spiritual arts user himself. After a moment of silence, Joshua thanked Julius for sharing that with him, knew to be wary if Subaru, and left the room, leaving Julius and Anastasia to speak with each other. After leaving them, he encountered Ricardo who came to check on him, and he was relieved to see that Joshua was doing better.

In Priestella, after Anastasia gave him a letter to pass along, Joshua, who had dropped it at some point, encountered Schult, who had given him the letter, much to his gratitude. Wanting to thank him, he asked what the boy, Schult, wanted in return, to which Schult said he was lost. Walking together, Schult gave an explanation of his history and the respect that he shows to the members of his camp, and he asked Joshua if there was someone he respected, to which Joshua replied that that person was his brother, though after recalling something in the past, his feelings became a little complicated. Schult looked forward to meeting him, and Joshua claimed that Julius would treat him kindly, but soon after, they noticed a commotion ahead. Realizing the danger, Joshua gave Schult his letter and told him to run, telling him to convey it Schult's master to pass along to his brother. After Schult ran, Joshua stepped in the way of Lye Batenkaitos as he was about to attack a defenseless woman, allowing her to escape while Lye became interested in him and devoured his name and memories.

Julius Juukulius's Promise Keeping Notebook
As he was being brought into a hospital ward, Subaru stopped the stretcher, having recognized him, and he told Julius and "Anastasia". Later, as Julius was lamenting having forgotten even forgotten his own brother, apologizing to him for it at his bedside, Ricardo came into the room and confirmed that the two were related through his sense of smell. Though he had forgotten Julius, he claimed that in spite of that, he could tell that he was still one of them, and he patted his head. Julius's gaze sank to Ricardo's severed arm, and Ricardo scolded him for it, stating that it was his own problem. The lack of change in the man gave Julius a sense of relief, and Ricardo mentioned that thinking in such a way naturally comes to someone who live for a long time, including Julius. Afterward, Ricardo entrusted Anastasia to Julius, as he was aware of their next journey, and he claimed he would not forget it and that Julius must not forget either. After accepting his trust and entrusting Joshua to him in return, Julius pulled out a notebook, which he claimed that he would be writing his experiences and words he's spoken with in, that way he wouldn't forget again, which brought relief to Ricardo.

relatives: Mimi Pearlbaton (older triplet sister) ; Tivey Pearlbaton (younger triplet brother) ; Roshi Pearlbaton (previous adoptive/foster father) † ; Anastasia Hoshin (current adoptive/foster mother) ; Ricardo Welkin (current adoptive/foster father)
intro: Hetaro Pearlbaton (ヘータロー・パールバトン) is one of Anastasia Hoshin's followers and is one of the three vice captains of the mercenary group known as the Iron Fang.
appearance: Hetaro has aqua green eyes and medium-length orange hair. He has orange cat ears along with a tail and wears a white robe. Unlike his sister Mimi, he has differently shaped eyebrows and slightly droopy eyes. He is described to be a boy with big round eyes who is easily mentally fatigued.
personality: Unlike his cheerful sister, Hetaro has a more cautious personality, which comes from his experiences of taking care of his sister. As he is a siscon, he generally tends to let his sister do whatever she wants, leading her to grow into her current personality, though because of this he is attentive and is sensitive to changes in mood. Despite this, he is also on good terms with his younger brother Tivey, who listens to what he has to say. Due to Ricardo's habit of heading straight into the battle, he is virtually the commander of the Iron Fang while in battle.
history:
Early Life
Sometime in the past, Mimi, Hetaro, and Tivey were abandoned by their parents. When they were two, Tivey was about to be kidnapped. Mimi attempted to fight off the kidnappers, but she was stabbed four times in the process, and Hetaro was also injured. As they were running away, they ran into Roshi Pearlbaton, who healed them, and after taking them in, he taught them how to survive.

Kararagi Girl Meets Cats and Kararagi Girl & Cat's Eye
Mimi and Hetaro attempted to rescue Anastasia, but they were incidentally captured instead by Razcrew. Razcrew planned to sell them on the slave markets in the north of Kararagi. However, his plan was thwarted, and he ended up being enslaved himself. After the defeat of Reisel, Anastasia vowed that if anything happened to Roshi, she would take the Pearlbatons under her care.

Eventually, Roshi made a kamikaze attack while on a mission, blowing up with an enemy in the process. Ever since, the siblings have lived with the Iron Fang under Anastasia and Ricardo's care.

Joshua Juukulius's Careful Encyclopedia
As Mimi, Hetaro, and Tivey had entered his room the moment they realized that there was food, Joshua Juukulius, who was honored to have finally been chosen to do something for Anastasia, was concerned that he had to act as a messenger to invite Emilia to Priestella, nervous and somewhat fearful of her due to her race and the rumors of her appearance being a match for the Witch of Envy. However, Mimi declared that Emilia wasn't scary, and recalling that Hetaro and Tivey had interacted with the Emilia Camp for the Subjugation of the White Whale and the Subjugation of Sloth, he asked for their opinions. While Tivey claimed that Emilia didn't seem to be scary, Hetaro declared that he only ever talked with her knight, Natsuki Subaru, someone else that Joshua had heard rumors and was wary of, as his origins were unknown and he had no known power. He also recalled the other worrisome rumors about the camp, which only increased his worries, and then, he went ask Anastasia about her intentions directly.

Kararagi Reaper Incident
Sometime after the Battle for Priestella, the Pearlbatons returned to Banan in Kararagi. However, at some point after the events of the Great Disaster, the Slasher, Zarestia set a windstorm on the town, destroying half of it and raising everyone in town sans Ricardo into the sky - an event that would be remembered as the Shinigami Disaster. Believing Ricardo to have stolen her Light Sphere, the two confronted each other, worrying the Pearlbatons. However, after withstanding all of her attacks, she stopped attacking him, made the windstorm dissipate, and lowered everyone to the ground. Later, everyone went to counter a black tornado that had started to assail Banan, and though they managed to quell it, Anastasia and Echidna had gone missing.

intro: Heinkel Astrea (ハインケル・アストレア) is the current Patriarch of House Astrea and the Deputy Commander of the Royal Guard. He plays a supporting role in Arc 7, Arc 8, and Arc 10, and an antagonistic role in Arc 5 and Arc 9.
appearance:
Heinkel is a muscular man with short red hair, blue eyes, and, initially, a stubble beard. He wears a black tabard with brown shoulder plates and chest armor, along with a dark cape, brown pants, gloves, and black boots, and he carries a sword at his hip.

After later becoming Filore's knight, Heinkel's stubble is shaved, leaving a small beard on his chin. He also begins to wear vestments of the Divine Dragon Church, which is comprised of a blue suit with golden lining and a white collar, similarly covered shoulder armor and bracers, white gloves, a dark blue cape held in place by a symbol of the church, a belt with a medallion hanging from it, and his sword hanging from his waist.
personality:
When he is first introduced, Heinkel is shown to be a slovenly, arrogant, and brash man who outwardly has no care for what others think about him, is not ashamed to throw around his position to intimidate others for petty reasons, and is regularly seen drinking alcohol regardless of the time of day or the events taking place. He is quick to insult others and intentionally acts malicious for no reason, and he is fully aware that others despise him. Likewise, he appears to be a cowardly man who is willing to take hostages in order to ensure that extremely mighty figures, such as his son, will remain nearby and assure his own safety. Likewise, he is seemingly fully willing to use his son as a tool to maintain his position within the Royal Guard, while fully refusing to give up his title as the patriarch of House Astrea despite not caring to perform his responsibilities.

Despite his rough attitude, Heinkel is actually typically heavily bitter and depressed, and he is more negative toward himself than to others, loathing his own personality and weaknesses. Likewise, he has always had the bad habit of fretting over things that could not be helped and that he would not have been able to do anything about even if he thought long and hard about it. Despite currently being decently skilled with a blade, he does not find swinging his sword enjoyable, seeing it as a shackle. He is also heavily fearful of those with great power, visibly freezing when forced to confront them. He has shown to be uncomfortable with taking other people's lives or seeing them taken in front of him, even if it is deemed necessary. Likewise, he is not very fond of hurting children and is reluctant to do so, even when said children are visibly and easily beating him within an inch of his life. When Al stated that there was no need to kill anyone during his scheme, Heinkel showed visible relief. Likewise, it has been noted by several people that despite his bitterness, he does consider the consequences of his actions, and according to Volcanica, whose mind had been overwritten by Al, Heinkel is actually a decent person, as evidenced in how he always considers fear, and would never be like the many demented people that he has met. Despite this, he himself does not believe so, and he believes that his actions following Priscilla Barielle's demise prove as such. He also becomes extremely hostile and defensive when someone pokes into the issues surrounding Heinkel and his family's predicament, and this hostility can become so great that Al was unable to prevent him from killing Felt several times for it.

In the past, Heinkel was not always bitter and resentful. On the contrary, he was typically happy, and he both deeply respected the Royal Family and loved his family. He admired his father, Wilhelm van Astrea, more than anyone else in the world, and looked up to his strength, power, and unwillingness to give up, even if he wasn't able to understand Wilhelm's teachings about the sword. He loved his mother, Theresia van Astrea, who loved him dearly. His love for his wife, Louanna, filled his heart, and he was always fiercely protective of his son, Reinhard. However, things took a dramatic turn when Louanna was inflicted with Sleeping Beauty for unknown reasons related to Reinhard. Because of this, Heinkel regularly prayed at the Divine Dragon Church, and he looked into remedies for every recognized illness, and he would jump at any opportunity he had to rescue her, even if they were rumors, such as a meteor that could "cure any illness". He became desperate enough that, despite having initially been called upon to challenge the White Whale, aside from his fear in challenging it, he was more than willing to suggest his mother take on the role while he would be willing to effectively betray the Royal Family by sneaking into the Royal Castle and steal the Dragon's blood in their stocks.

Despite his desperation, this tremendously backfired, and his family was further broken apart. Because his mother was killed in the Great Conquest, it caused his father to lash out at Reinhard, and Heinkel, who still cared for his son, decided to completely sever ties between them, not allowing the man to even apologize. Furthermore, because of his own failure and his own body's resulting near invincibility, his depression and desperation increased, and he stopped praying at the church, unable to face the Divine Dragon or its followers. Likewise, his alcoholism intensified. Although he still loved his son and was willing to protect him from the Six Tongues in spite of the child's already tremendous strength, when Reinhard started acting as the Sword Saint, Heinkel came to want to basically destroy the relevance of the title for his son's sake, so he started acting spitefully toward him as well, often throwing negative remarks and comments Reinhard's way. Over time, these fractures only deepened, and his bitterness and depression increased, and even though he hurled abuse towards even the doctor meant to help cure his wife, he hit his lowest point after that doctor's murder. Furthermore, thanks to the Battle for Priestella, the fractures in his family increased further with the battle against the undead Theresia serving as the catalyst, causing Heinkel to lash out even more harshly at both his father and son. Eventually, his desperation grew to the point of apparent opportunism, willing to join whichever group he had to find a cure and destroy the "Sword Saint", whether that be joining the Priscilla Camp or attempting to jump to Emilia's camp after the former's demise. Likewise, even if it means completely betraying and making an enemy of the entire world, Heinkel would be willing to do it if there was a real chance of curing his wife. This being said, even though he is willing to take such actions, he is still shown to worry of his son, especially when he was forced to confront the Witch of Envy.

Despite all of this, after he was retrieved by Filore and was convinced to become her knight, despite initially treating her with outward skepticism to make her reconsider her choice, Heinkel started to display pieces of his former kindness by properly advising Filore and scolding her when need be, and he believed that his becoming Filore's knight only served to shackle her, as he was fully aware of how he was perceived, something which he seems to feel regretful about. Likewise, he sympathized with the people who had to deal with Filore's decision to make him her knight, claiming that he'd react the same way as them. Furthermore, despite internally complaining, he has shown willing to follow her lead when she acts carelessly, dealt with any of the extensive amount of paperwork as part of the responsibilities of being her knight, and, despite being fully aware of just how reckless her intentions were, even decided to help Filore when she was dead set on infiltrating the castle to help her friends. Later, despite being repeatedly beaten by Marcos Gildark, who despised who Heinkel had become after his wife fell asleep, even though he was terribly afraid and did not want to fight, not only did he act to serve as Filore's shield, but, unconsciously, he also would not drop his sword, unable to give up despite his precarious and terrifying predicament.
history:
Early Life
Heinkel was born to his father, Wilhelm, and to his mother, Theresia. In his younger days, he was a much more earnest and kind man who seemed to have aspirations of becoming the next Sword Saint like his mother and worked quite hard. He fell in love with a woman named Louanna at first sight and sometime later the two had an arranged marriage. They had a son, Reinhard Astrea. However, things would soon begin to go awry for the Astreas, first with Louanna suddenly falling into deep sleep two years after Reinhard's birth and left in an inanimate state without any cure for such condition. He began to take up drinking alcohol during this time but still showed care for his other family members.

On the night of the Royal Abduction Incident, in which the daughter of Ford Lugunica was kidnapped, Heinkel committed an unspecified grave sin, having perpetrated an unknown betrayal and a terrible mistake that rendered said betrayal pointless, the result being with Heinkel becoming doused in Dragon's blood and becoming an "immortal knight". In the time afterwards, when the White Whale appeared in the Kingdom of Lugunica, Heinkel was requested to lead a group of men to eliminate it in a subjugation that would come to be known as the Great Conquest, but he refused. Theresia took Heinkel's place at his request, but she ended up dying.

When Wilhelm returned from the search for Filore Lugunica, the kidnapped royal princess, he was as upset with Heinkel for his irresponsibility as he was with Reinhard for taking the Divine Protection of the Sword Saint from Theresia during the battle. However, Heinkel also chided Wilhelm for publicly blaming Reinhard for Theresia's death, and he refused to allow Wilhelm to see Reinhard, as Heinkel believed that he had no right to apologize to him. With Heinkel swearing to prove that Reinhard's acquiring the Divine Protection of the Sword Saint was not the cause of his mother's death, a rift was born in the Astrea family. Heinkel continued working for the Royal Guard, and Wilhelm left them and concentrated all of his efforts on slaying the White Whale to avenge Theresia. Heinkel inherited the estate and domain of House Astrea after this. Shortly after this, Heinkel lost a duel to a five-year-old Reinhard, resulting in unsavory rumors about the two's relationship which suggest that Reinhard was being treated like a slave. Over the years, he became a bitter alcoholic with such a deep hatred for himself that he started taking it out on the world around him. He began to admonish Garitch, Louanna's doctor, over the years, due to him not being able to cure Louanna. Soon after Garitch's murder by a resentful disciple of his, Heinkel fell into grief as a result of the doctor's death, realizing that nobody could treat his wife.

First Mission
Five years before the Royal Selection, while Reiner Wahrheit's drug operation was running rampant, Heinkel was placed under house arrest on suspicion of aiding and abetting in the former knight's organization. In an attempt to clear Heinkel's name, Reinhard decided to crossdress and take up the identity of a young girl named Adelheid to infiltrate and bring down Reiner's organization. After Reiner and his collaborator, Count Easley Oruon, were incarcerated, the Commander of the Royal Guard, Marcos Gildark, came to notify Heinkel that the Council of Wise Men had decided to promote him to Deputy Commander, much to his bewilderment and vexation. That night, he went down to a bar in the Commoner District and encountered Reinhard there. Suspecting that Reinhard had pulled strings to get him promoted, Heinkel asked him if he had done so, which his son denied. Being reminded from Reinhard that accepting the position could help Louanna, he accepted his new role and told his son to join the knights when he turned fifteen. He then proceeded to return to Marcos to accept his appointment, unaware that Reinhard had conspired with the Six Tongues to prompt his promotion. Reinhard eventually joined the Royal Guard and would earn a reputation as the Knight Among Knights as he was told to, while Heinkel, dishonored, further languished and rotted in his own self-hatred, continued to grow more bitter, at some point ceasing calling his son by his name and instead calling him a brat or by his title of Sword Saint.

Felt-chan Rises to the Center Stage
In response to Reinhard's arrival to the castle, Heinkel entered the room that Felt was getting changed in, much to Carol's anger and Felt's annoyance. Afterward, Carol informed Heinkel of Felt's reason being in the castle was for the Royal Selection, which he laughed at. Though Felt was ready to attack him, Heinkel stepped in front of her quickly and claimed that they were both in the same position before leaving.

Priscilla's Cheers for Me, Drunk Father Part
A couple of months after the incident at the Sanctuary, hearing of rumors of a meteor that could cure any ailment of the one who drinks out of it, Heinkel set out for a bandit den, and he slew all of the bandits there. However, this was in vain, as the cup turned out to be a sham. While here, he met Priscilla Barielle who offered to form an alliance of sorts with him so that in exchange for helping her take the throne, he would obtain the Dragon's Blood so that he could cure his sleep-bound wife, acting in opposition to Reinhard and Felt's efforts in the Royal Selection.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
Although he will tremble and panic before the mass majority of powerful warriors, Heinkel is a strong fighter in his own right, capable of easily killing a den of bandits, an army of golems, or a horde of flying dragons. Although his skill with the sword pales in comparison to his overpowered son and experienced war veteran father, Heinkel's abilities are such that he could fight against just about anyone and almost always survive, even if he doesn't win.

Physical Traits/Flow Method
Expert Swordsmanship: Despite being overshadowed by his more famous relatives, and his insecurity in his own abilities, Heinkel is still rather skilled with a sword. He was able to defend himself against Theresia's attacks, albeit for a short period of time, and easily dispatch assassins that outnumbered him, with Al even commenting his swordplay could be described as beautiful. To further exemplify his sword abilities, he is capable of changing his stance and the way he attacks according to whichever enemy he faces, and it should be noted that Heinkel easily slaughtered an entire camp of bandits, slayed hordes of flying dragons, and handily dealt with Moguro Hagane's golems. This being said, his personality inhibits him from being capable of performing the same level or feats as his other relatives, something which has resulted in Heinkel not receiving the title of van in his name.

Supernatural Survivability: After his failure on the night of the Royal Abduction Incident resulted in him being doused in Dragon's blood, Heinkel has become someone who is almost impossible to kill through ordinary methods or attacks; as described by Filore, this has turned him into an "immortal knight". His durability is such that he can withstand the strikes of incredibly powerful opponents, such as Priscilla, Madelyn Eschart, Moguro Hagane, Groovy Gumlet, the Cloud Dragon Mezoreia, the Divine Dragon Volcanica, and Marcos Gildark, as well as blasts from weapons as powerful as the Star Staff, and not only take minor overall damage, but even stand up shortly after as if nothing had happened to him. Similarly, he is also seemingly immune to diseases or poisons, even if they come from a source as immediately lethal as the Black Serpent. Even standing upon its corrupted land and being swallowed by it, something that would kill others, including a witchbeast as strong as a Guiltylowe, in seconds, Heinkel was capable of not only surviving but also without any form of pestilence. So far, the only known way for Heinkel to die is through starvation.

Enhanced Strength: Heinkel has great physical might. He is able to lift trees without much effort, and when combined with Yae's steel wires, he was able to turn them into impromptu cannonballs. Likewise, he has enough leg strength to easily bound leap up to the top of Lupugana's ramparts.

Skilled Hand-to-Hand Combatant: Even without using his sword, Heinkel carries enough skill that he can swiftly and easily bring down a pair of knights before they have time to react to him.

Intelligence
Skilled Tactician: Despite his usual demeanor, Heinkel is proficient in coming up with and preparing for plans. Although not usually seen, he used this in order to infiltrate the Royal Castle not just once, but twice.

Pharmaceutical Knowledge: Due to the predicament with his wife, Heinkel scoured over every conceivable way to cure her. As such, he has greater knowledge in this subject than the average healer does.

Equipment
Holy Sword Astrea (聖剣アストレア, Seiken Asutorea): Heinkel's sword was once given to him by his father who wielded it in his youth, receiving it as a wedding gift from his father-in-law.

intro: Hector (ヘクトール) was the Valiant and the Warlock of Melancholy. A supernumerary Warlock who, along with the Saintess, was considered separate from the rest of the Witches, he consistently pursued Echidna for unknown reasons.
appearance:
Hector had the look of a young man with a tall body and a slender frame. His long messy charred-brown colored hair was tied into a braid that trailed below his waist. His brown eyes had heavy bags under them that gave off the impression of a sickly person. Although he was described as appearing to be around twenty years of age, as the effects of the Authority of Melancholy in users other than him could allow them to suspend their body from aging, it is unknown whether or not he did the same or if he even had the capacity to do so. His mouth was slightly puckered, and his cheekbones were fairly pronounced. The color of his face was poor, and his posture was crooked, which, when coupled with his worn eyes, gave the impression of someone who found it demanding to put on clothes and leave the house. Indeed, every part of Hector's demeanor portrayed lethargy and a general lack of vitality. Rather paradoxically, despite the lack of joviality conveyed by his attitude and posture.

Contrary to his facial features however, Hector wore a rather colorful attire; that of a jester. Half of it was purple and half of it was white. The suit was extremely skinny, left his shoulders visible, and had a red and black tail on it. In the anime adaptation, he is shown to be surrounded by a purple distorted hue which somewhat resembles a force field.
personality: As the Warlock of Melancholy, Hector has a negative personality, frequently expressing his negativity in words. His manner of speaking is similar to Roswaal, who started to speak like Hector after getting beaten. Hector is stronger than Echidna, but despite that, his existence was left unknown for future generations to know. It should be noted that his mind was corrupted by his Witch Factor, so this personality may be different to what it was prior to the corruption. According to Beatrice, he was obsessed with Echidna due to a warped sense of love for her as her father.
history:
More than 400 years ago, Hector was known as the Valiant. Though it is unknown for what reason he bore this title, he willingly took in the Witch Factor of Melancholy, something which was tailor-made for his usage, and became counted as a supernumerary Witch Factor holder alongside the Saintess, Pandora. According to Clind, however, despite being compatible with their respective Factors, the Valiant and the Saintess were unable to avoid the mental corruption that came with Witch Factors. By Roswaal's claim, even if Hector's way of life grew twisted, he chose to become the person he ended up being from his own limited choices, which he himself has affirmed. Hector was also once married, and his wife deemed it suitable to refer to him as a Warlock of Melancholy as a pet name, which stuck with him over time.

Hector and the Witch of Vainglory, Pandora, had a daughter together, that being Echidna. Hector and Pandora were responsible for her birth, having supposedly produced her with a specific goal in mind, that goal being unknown. By Echidna's claim, she never learned anything positive from her parents, having only learned negative emotions such as contempt and ridicule from them. However, she believed that, from their perspective, her existence was a failed imitation to them.

Later on, Hector began to pursue his daughter, Echidna, out of his obsession for her. During this period, he chased her down to Kugelschreiber Castle, and the ensuing conflict left the whole building in ruin. Eventually, Echidna was forced to flee to the Sanctuary located in the Kremaldy Forest. In order to prevent him from entering the Sanctuary, Echidna tried to create a magical barrier but failed, resulting in Hector successfully accessing the hiding place and facing off against Roswaal A. Mathers, swiftly defeating him without breaking a sweat. Just before delivering the finishing blow, Echidna intercepted him, saving Roswaal's life. The Witch and the Warlock clashed with the outcome of their fight being unknown, though both survived the ordeal. An unknown amount of time after this, Hector engaged in a battle with Roswaal and Clind. In the end, his Witch Factor of Melancholy was assumed by Clind, who took the role of its custodian. Sometime following this battle, Hector died.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
Hector has at one point been called among the upper echelons of strength in the series by the author. Hector was incredibly powerful, capable of not only defeating a young Roswaal, but even requiring preparations to repel by someone of the caliber of the Witch of Greed. This being said, the full extent of his power is currently unknown.

Authority
Authority of Melancholy (憂鬱の権能 Yū'utsu no Ken'nō): Hector was the previous wielder of the Witch Factor of Melancholy and could use its respective Authority. As the Valiant, Hector was compatible with the Factor of Melancholy, allowing him to unrestrainedly exercise its abilities until his death.

Crushing Force Field: Hector surrounds himself in an invisible force field that is able to crush both living things and magic alike. The more he closes his distance with the target, the stronger the damage is. As Hector himself seems to be the very center of this force field, the damage has the highest magnitude when in direct contact with him; by simply jabbing his finger into Roswaal's chest, he shattered his bones, completely crushed his chest and organs and twisted and crumbled his limbs, completely destroying the mage's body beyond repair.
Long Range Force Field: Hector also seems to be able to create force fields outside his reach by looking at a place or pointing his open palm towards it, as seen when he destroyed a hut in which Ryuzu was hiding, several tens of meters away from where Hector was standing.

intro: Kurgan (クルガン) was a hero of the Sacred Vollachia Empire who was regarded as its strongest warrior. Debuting in Arc 5, he played the role of a secondary antagonist, after the Witch Cult resurrected him as a corpse soldier and he was used as a pawn of the Sin Archbishop of Lust to wreak havoc in the Watergate City of Priestella. He was defeated by Garfiel Tinzel.
appearance:
Kurgan was a giant who stood around seven feet tall and towered above most other people. His huge body was armored by thick, twisting muscles and his fists were said to be as large as a child's head. The trait that distinguished Kurgan as a member of the Many-Armed Tribe and earned him the legendary appellation "Eight Arms" was his eight powerful arms. His blue skin and black eyes gave the impression of a vengeful demon. The warrior's physical appearance and combat might bestowed Kurgan with a legendarily intimidating presence. Even the likes of the previous Sword Saint, Theresia van Astrea, failed to suppress a shudder upon gazing at Kurgan for the first time.

Reflecting his barbarism, Kurgan wore scant clothing. His ensemble consisted of a tattered black loincloth, black bracers on each forearm that had golden bracelets attached to their bottom hems, and black hosiery that covered his legs below the knees and had the same golden bracelets adorned at the bottom. Kurgan had various pieces of gold jewelry traipsing down his body, including his neck, face, and waist area. He has no shoes as he states that he prefers nature's ground.
personality:
Kurgan had a rough and straightforward personality but spoke in a surprisingly sophisticated manner. He was also highly perceptive and seemed to have above average intelligence despite his otherwise brutish appearance. However, he was ever eager to battle strong opponents in order test his strength and go beyond his limits, thus Kurgan was never one to turn down a fight. He deeply admired the peak of martial arts mastery, such as the one that Reid Astrea once achieved, holding deep admiration for the "Heavenly Sword".

He had a fascination with the darkness within Stride, this being the reason why Kurgan initially took an interest in him. Witnessing a dark emotion such as despair in an individual was enough to spur Kurgan to act in alignment with them. The emotions within Stride influenced Kurgan into taking on the role of his father, growing to unconditionally love and serve him in the wake of the devastation he brought with him. Despite the paternal care he bore for Stride, Kurgan possessed a corrupt, brutish mindset. He frequently taunted his enemies and was not above threatening their loved ones, at one point boasting to the Sword Demon during their first duel that he would kill him, abduct and impregnate his wife Theresia, and name his son with her after Wilhelm.
history:
Kurgan was born to the Multi-Arm Tribe. Despite their main characteristic of having more arms than normal, even in their tribe, having eight arms was unheard of. In his youth, Kurgan managed to raise his clan's status and protect their land from a Vollachian lord who sought to claim it, which marked the start of his world-renowned exploits. He rose in strength to become the Vollachia Empire's strongest warrior, achieving a legendary status tantamount to receiving an order of merit from the Vollachian emperor himself. 

More than half a decade ago, Kurgan was given responsibility over Stride Vollachia, who was given up by his family due to his frail constitution. Kurgan felt jubilated at seeing the darkness within the boy's eyes, growing to care for him and eventually considering himself Stride's foster father. While attempting to participate in the Imperial Selection Ceremony, an unknown culprit poisoned Stride with a powerful poison, causing Stride to drift between life and death for three arduous and agonizing months. When Stride beat his illness, he awoke to tell Kurgan that he saw entities known as the Observers in the heavens, toying with people as if they were mere pieces on a board. At that moment, Kurgan determined that he would not obey the Vollachia Empire that sought Stride's death, choosing instead to prioritize the love that he, as a father, felt for his foolish son. From then on, Shasuke, Raizo, and Melinda, the other three who came to pledge themselves to Stride, all walked together to see where the Destruction Wish would arrive at. 

Sword Demon Love Story
Approximately forty years prior to the start of the story, aiming for Sword Saint, Stride used the gift of Veltol Astrea as an excuse to meet with him in the Suwen Company in Picoutatte, where he openly insulted him and his daughter. With Veltol challenging him to a duel, he claimed to be unable to fight due to his illness, which Theresia had noticed, and he decided to have Kurgan act as his champion. Further antagonizing the two with insults to them and Theresia's husband, Veltol struck him, leading to his brutal beating by Kurgan and being cursed by Stride. Leaving Yaktol Suwen with a message that he would be waiting at a great bridge in the city's west district with the source of the curse, he left. The next morning, he met with Theresia and Wilhelm, who challenged him to a duel. Despite being irritated that the rumors he heard regarding her award ceremony were true and that Wilhelm had equivalent battle aura to Kurgan, the duel ensued. Despite this, both sides took great damage, and seeing that he was in danger of losing his pawn, he stopped the duel and claimed it their loss, tossing his ring to them, and using another to turn the bridge beneath them into sand, allowing him and Kurgan to escape. Sometime later, the two arms that were severed during this fight were reattached.

Sword Demon Battle Ballad
He was eventually defeated once more by Wilhelm in the city during the Subjugation of the Blight Dragon and lay dying on the streets of Picoutatte until Volcanica's miracle healed him. Having been the only survivor of the Stride Faction, Kurgan was then extradited back to the Vollachia Empire and reduced to a mere slave in the Fortified City of Garkla, willingly accepting this fate despite having the power to resist.

Finale of the Eight Arms
Decades later, Kurgan was involved in the defense against Regulus Corneas's rampage in Garkla. He was initially ordered along with his fellow laborers to attack the Sin Archbishop by an Imperial Soldier supervising them. Defeated with just a single attack and having no will to fight back, he was spurred to act by the voice of a young prince whose desperation reminded him of his foster son's. Gathering the motivation to prevent the prince from dying, he was granted his old arms of choice, Demon Cleavers, which happened to be in Garkla, and took up arms against the Sin Archbishop of Greed. Although the Fortified City fell in just a single hour, without the intervention of Kurgan, who singlehandedly impeded Regulus's path, allowing the city's survivors to be evacuated in time, it would have fell in half that time. His final word being the same commendation he had offered twice to the Sword Demon in Picoutatte, he met his end as Regulus delivered a speech that fell on deaf ears. In commemoration of Kurgan's achievement at Garkla, the prince exhausted all efforts to restore Kurgan's reputation, and successfully managed to do so after enough time, with his Demon Cleavers being restored and put on display on the uppermost floor of Garkla's Great Fortress.
abilities_text:
thumb|right|250px|Kurgan demonstrating his swordsmanship against Garfiel Tinzel.
Master Swordsmanship: As noted by Theresia, she saw Kurgan as an enemy that was far, far stronger than the usual crop with swordsmanship that rivalled Wilhelm's. His sword strikes can create a fierce gale, which raged at tremendous speeds.

Enhanced Physicality: Kurgan has a powerful body that is both incredibly strong and tough to damage. With just his physical strength as a corpse soldier, he was able to easily overwhelm Garfiel, and in life, by simply flexing his muscles, he was able to halt bleeding from missing limbs. A single one of his strikes, with or without his blades, is enough to deal massive damage to his opponents and cause severe internal injuries. Likewise, even in the face of losing his limbs, Kurgan is unflinching, acting essentially unbothered after losing two of his arms in combat.

Equipment: Kurgan wielded four large greatswords that required even Kurgan to use two hands to wield, and he called them his Demon Cleavers (鬼包丁). They were his favorite weapons, but two of them were later destroyed by Wilhelm during their duel. Despite this, all four weapons seemed to be in perfect condition by the time of the Battle for Priestella.

Great Power: By mastering and taking full advantage of his body's unique features and developing techniques to suited it, Kurgan became one of the strongest fighters of the Vollachia Empire. He was easily able to parry and deflect blows from a Dragon. As a corpse soldier, however, despite retaining incredible strength, it was but a shadow of his former self, compared back to when he was still alive, to the point that Wilhelm gauged he would have easily killed Garfiel if he had been at his complete strength in life.
