intro: Kiritaka Muse (キリタカ・ミューズ) is a trade representative of Priestella and the owner of the Muse Company. He is the last survivor of Priestella's Council of Ten. Though initially making his debut in a side story, Kiritaka played a passive, yet rather strong supporting role throughout Arc 5.
appearance: Kiritaka has pale gold hair that's carefully smoothed toward the back of his head. He has a tall and thin body and wears well-tailored clothes with a limited number of adornments which make him look refined.
personality:
As one of the major merchants of Priestella, Kiritaka has a sense of dignity and self-worth, and is shown to be educated based on his words and actions. He is skilled as a merchant, making him constantly busy. Every morning, he uses the broadcast meteors in the city center building to broadcast in order to let the citizens know that it would be used in emergencies.

Kiritaka has a strange obsession with younger girls and puts emphasis in whether a woman looks young rather than their actual age or mentality. Currently, he claims that his heart has been stolen by Liliana Masquerade and tends to get out of control when things involve her, such as the time he attacked Subaru when he saw him with conversing with her.

Despite this, Kiritaka is shown to have honorable qualities, as when the Witch Cult attacked his company during the Battle for Priestella, he was intent on sacrificing himself to let Anastasia escape.
abilities_text:
White Dragon's Scales (白竜の鱗, Hakuryū no Uroko): Kiritaka hired a mercenary group, known as the White Dragon's Scales, to be his personal bodyguards. The group consists of highly skilled individuals, who are more than capable of protecting Kiritaka, when needed. During the fight with the Sin Archbishop of Gluttony, most of the members had their names eaten and were put in suspended animation, with Dynas Trussardi and some others managing to escape the same fate. Following Lye's death, it's unknown if they have already regained their names.

Leadership: Although normally a merchant, Kiritaka has shown to be an excellent leader, which has allowed him to rise up to the Priestellan Council of Ten. Despite being the only member active throughout the Battle for Priestella due to the deaths of the others, he quickly responded to the Witch Cult’s attack by leading everyone to shelters and deciding to make use of his company as both a medical station and the temporary headquarters of the resistance. Likewise, he had the foresight to have everyone moved after a short period of its use to counter a surprise attack.

intro: Grimm Fauzen (グリム・ファウゼン) is a servant for House Astrea alongside his wife, Carol, and he is the former second and final Deputy Commander of the Zergev Squadron. He played a primary supporting role in the Sword Demon Trilogy.
appearance:
In the past, Grimm Fauzen wore the standard outfit and armor of the Royal Army and wielded a shield. He was a man with short, messy purple hair, and dark yellow brown eyes. Having suffered burns in his youth during the war, he has burn scars on his hands and wrists.

In the present, Grimm is an old man and is shown to have a scar on his throat due to an injury he got during the Demi-Human War. He has short white hair, a strong jawline, a white beard, and sharp eyes. He appeared wearing a pretty and chic butler outfit, similar to that of Wilhelm van Astrea. It is mentioned that he aged better than his beloved Carol Remendis.
personality:
Grimm is a strong-willed man, shown to be extremely stalwart and loyal to the Kingdom's Army. He placed great faith in others to act as the sword, whilst he acted as their shield. Despite that, he was quite a jocund person, who was easy to get along even on the brink of disaster. When adversity affected his loved one, Grimm was shown to be less easy-going, and in continuous blame of himself for the situation that had occurred. As he grew older, Grimm became more serious, and after marrying Carol Remendis, he swore absolute loyalty to the Astrea family.

In his younger days, Grimm, having grown up in a small town, was somewhat idealistic and sought excitement that his small town could not offer, and as such, he became independent as he became of age. He also sought glory and to become a hero, which, in place of patriotism, is what initially inspired him to join the Royal Army when they were recruiting during the Demi-Human War. However, following his survival during his first battle and his multiple near-death experiences, Grimm became realistic and shed himself of those dreams, knowing that neither dreams nor facing reality were not what fills a person's stomach. Despite his attitude, he decided to keep with the army, filled with the trauma of the deaths and cries of his allies. This being said, thanks to his interactions with Wilhelm, which at first were rocky, he was able to overcome his trauma and push forward.

Due to a throat wound inflicted on him during the Demi-Human War, Grimm temporarily lost the ability to speak. Later, he began communicating more from his expressions and through paper, though he can still talk in brief intervals.
history:
Sword Demon Love Song
Grimm was born in a small village called Fleur, situated north-east of the Royal Capital. When he was fifteen, Grimm moved out of Fleur out of boredom and into the Royal Capital to become independent, and for the next few years, he worked at several shops and taverns, performing menial work. One day, the Royal Army sought new recruits to join the army in an effort to fight in the Demi-Human War. Wishing to become a hero and attain glory, Grimm joined the army, where he met Tholter Weasily and was trained alongside him and the other knights by the commander, Razak Gildark. Six months after he joined, Grimm participated in his first battle, the Battle for Redonas Plateau, where a noble had also sought to make a name for himself. However, soon after the battle began, he, alongside many others in Grimm's unit, were all quickly killed. Having barely survived by being just outside the blast and being blown away, Grimm ran away, and he encountered a violet-skinned demi-human. As he was facing death, however, he was saved by the arrival of Wilhelm Trias, who easily beheaded him. Grimm, wanting to survive, followed after him, and he bore witness to the mountain of corpses that Wilhelm had created. Shortly after, the army signaled their victory, due in no small part to Wilhelm's efforts. His experience here greatly changed his beliefs, and instead of resigning in fear or clinging to his dreams, he remained in the army to keep himself fed, and soon after, Wilhelm was adopted into his squad.

After sharing drinks with his comrades and returning to the barracks early, he found Wilhelm training behind the barracks. After a short conversation with Wilhelm, who claimed that he didn't understand how the others couldn't devote themselves to their training instead of pleasures and calling Grimm a coward for making excuses, Grimm left to sleep, and in the following days, he continued to mask his trauma. Shortly after this, the Royal Army was baited into Castour Field, where they found themselves handily dealing with the demi-humans that they had struggled with prior. While Wilhelm was cutting down his enemies and bringing awe to friend and foe alike, both he and Grimm, who was protecting Tholter with his shield as he fired his arrows, had a bad feeling. It wasn't long after that their premonitions came true and the earth shook through magic, causing chaos among the army. Realizing the plot, Wilhelm moved forward to fight his enemies while the others retreated, much to his chagrin. Grimm, having dropped his sword, chased after him to bring him back, and along the way, he damaged a magic circle. After speaking with Wilhelm, who appeared and dispatched an attacking demi-human, he was told what the idea, crafted by Valga Cromwell, was meant for and that retreating was part of the trap. Despite Grimm's misgivings, Wilhelm continued to fight, and Grimm chased after him. Witnessing his carnal display against his enemies, Grimm called him the Sword Demon. Soon after, a massive cry from his allies could be heard as they fell for the trap, and Grimm was left sobbing for his decision. That day, the Battle of Castour Field ended in the army's defeat.

After being taken back by the rest of the army and given treatment, Grimm and Wilhelm joined the Zergev Squadron, with Grimm becoming akin to Pivot Arnancy's shadow. With the great defeat at Castour Field, the Kingdom decided to call in the magic specialist Roswaal J. Mathers to analyze the magic circles used. On the way there, Grimm and Wilhelm argued about when the latter called him a coward for his trauma, and before long, alongside the rest of the squadron, they arrived at Castour Field, where they officially met Roswaal and her bodyguard Carol. After once again getting into an argument with him, he, Wilhelm, and a few other members of the squadron moved on as a group to the magic circle. Along the way, he kept Carol company so that there would be any problems with Wilhelm. After arriving and allowing Roswaal to check the circle, after she claimed it would be a threat to the Kingdom, Grimm had a bad feeling that he thought Wilhelm might share. That feeling turned out to be correct when the undead Tholter fired arrows at them and corpse soldiers began rising. Covering Roswaal alongside Carol, Wilhelm went to fight the undead, where he met Sphinx. With Roswaal intending to join the fight, furious, Sphinx decided to retreat, leaving everyone to clean up the undead. With some help from Roswaal, Wilhelm realized that Tholter was the main corpse soldier to defeat, and after giving him the push he needed to overcome his trauma and fight, Grimm ran forward and put his old friend to rest. Though still fearful, after a conversation with Carol shortly after the fight, he fell in love with her. Afterward, meeting up with the commander Bordeaux Zergev and Pivot, Roswaal relayed Sphinx's identity and the threat she bore. Later, he, Wilhelm, Roswaal, Bordeaux, and Pivot all reported to the Kingdom's officials, including Miklotov McMahon, about the threat.

For the next three years, Grimm and the rest of the Zergev Squadron, as well as Roswaal and Carol at times, fought in some of the most dangerous battlefields of the war, where they both lost and obtained new members of the squadron. At one point, Grimm alleviated her fears in regards to both Wilhelm and her master, and afterward, she offered to train him with his shield. Over time, the two would regularly meet so that Carol could train him, and his relationship with Carol also grew. One day, the squad was set to go to Aihiya Swamp, where Valga, Libre Fermi, and possibly Sphinx were. Speaking with Wilhelm, they compared this to Castour Field, with Roswaal confirming his suspicions that their superiors took this into consideration. Carol appeared soon after, and as she spoke with Grimm, she gave Grimm a locket as a good luck charm. Soon after, they met their new commander, Leip Barielle, who struck Wilhelm for being disrespectful. Roswaal managed to pacify the man, and they walked away alongside Carol. With Wilhelm abating any concern for him, conversation soon turned to the locket Grimm received, in which was a flower that was given to Carol by her master. Not noticing Wilhelm's surprise, the squad soon moved to Aihiya Swamp.

During the Battle of Aihiya Swamp, Grimm fought alongside the rest of the Zergev Squadron as the fighting progressed, soon deciding to move toward the center of the fighting to remove the root of the war itself. There, they came across Libre, who challenged Wilhelm to a duel. Although putting up a good fight, Libre was able to corner Wilhelm and push him back, and in response, Grimm, Bordeaux, and Pivot surrounded Libre to cut him off. However, they were all put under the effects of a wide spanning magic circle, left at the mercy of the demi-humans. With Libre pointing his blade at Bordeaux, Wilhelm attempted to fight him off, only for Libre to nearly kill him. Pivot, instead, jumped in the way of his blade, and as he lay on the ground, he yelled at everyone not to let Wilhelm die, rousing them to take arms against Libre. However, they were all nearly slaughtered, and Grimm, who was able to defend himself for longer than the others, sustained a wound to his throat. Before he could be finished off, Wilhelm pounced Libre and fell into away from the others. With Pivot dying in Bordeaux's arms, he soon revived as an undead and attempted to strangle Bordeaux. However, the barely conscious Grimm managed to push him away, allowing Bordeaux to put him to rest. After this, the army retreated, with Grimm managing to survive his terrible wound, unable to speak.

Within the month that followed, Grimm remained in the Royal Treatment Center. Though he met with Bordeaux once, he was unable to speak with him again since the man found himself busy. Carol visited him and apologized profusely for allowing this to happen, leading to their kiss and their becoming lovers. During one of her later visits, she gave Grimm a new shield as a present for surviving the battle. Later on, because of Carol's insistence, Wilhelm came to visit him, somewhat surprising Grimm. During their conversation, in which Grimm used writing to communicate, after he said that Bordeaux had clearly changed, much to his frustration, Wilhelm questioned why everyone gave their lives for him and why Grimm sacrificed his voice. Grimm responded to him by claiming that his ideals and sword were the squad's as well and that he represented hope. Despite being envious of his abilities and will to push forward where other can't, that was the reason he could not be allowed to die. Afterward, Grimm thanked him for his actions when Tholter had risen as an undead when Wilhelm gave him the push he needed.

After returning to duty, uprisings began across the country. With the rebuilt Zergev Squadron wondering where they should go, Wilhelm realized that their enemies were targeting the castle, and Grimm backed him up. Trusting his judgment, Bordeaux led everyone to the castle, and with assistance from Roswaal and Carol, they were allowed into the castle. Shortly after arriving inside, Bordeaux left for the audience chamber while Wilhelm's group left for the chapel. After meeting with Valga and Sphinx, Wilhelm decided to handle Valga while the others chased after Sphinx. The group managed to corner her with Roswaal's techniques and Carol's midair combat, and Grimm even managed to deflect one of her strongest attacks thanks to the shield. After the appearance of Bordeaux and Libre thanks to this, Libre cut off Sphinx's other arm before fading away, and Sphinx ran away, followed by Roswaal. The others went to help Wilhelm, who eventually managed to defeat Valga.

In the following year, Wilhelm became much friendlier with everyone, and he would also start sharing drinks with Grimm, even teasing him about his relationship with Carol, while Grimm found it amazing about his changes. However, after Wilhelm left to go save his lands in the Battle of the Trias Domain, Grimm, Theresia, and the rest of the Zergev Squadron made their way to save him. After this, Wilhelm would not be seen with the army until after the Demi-Human War was over. In this time, Grimm received a home of his own, where Carol would often visit. During the ceremony to award the Sword Saint, Grimm attended and bore witness to the battle between Wilhelm and Theresia, and after witnessing his victory and his kissing Theresia, he and the other members of the Zergev Squadron reunited with him.

Sword Demon Love Story
After Theresia dragged Wilhelm to her mansion and forced him to take a bath, he spoke with Carol and Grimm, the former of which lashed out at him, and he learned of her position as Theresia's attendant. After this, they informed him that he was unemployed, leading him to finding a way to rejoin. Later, upon Carol and Grimm's return to the mansion, Carol chided Wilhelm for upsetting Theresia and went to speak with her while Wilhelm and Grimm finished all of the food that Theresia prepared. The next day over breakfast, Carol warned him not to do anything that would upset Theresia. The day after that, Wilhelm found himself face to face with the best warriors the country had to offer, including Bordeaux, Carol, and Grimm. With Gionis and Miklotov overseeing the battle, Wilhelm fought and defeated all forty soldiers. However, after Theresia arrived and chided the king for allowing this, it was revealed that she would have been let go of her position if she married Wilhelm, much to everyone's but the king and Miklotov's shock. Wilhelm accepted this, and they embraced, Theresia calling him Wilhelm van Astrea.

Three months later, Veltol Astrea used his authority to move the Zergev Squadron to patrol the towns around the capital, despite there being only three days before Wilhelm and Theresia's wedding. After Wilhelm joined up with Grimm and the rest of the squadron, who all wanted to wrap up the patrols as quickly as possible to let Wilhelm make it in time for his wedding, Bordeaux and Theresia, who had made him food for the journey, saw them off. Though they intended to pass quickly through the towns on Fleur, Millgray, Bonobo, and Cramlin, they faced a setback in Fleur due to Grimm's homecoming for the first time since he joined the army. Despite this, they managed to pass quickly through Millgray and Bonobo, but on the day before Wilhelm's wedding, the squad was tasked with finding the missing children in Cramlin. Though they found them inside the Nest of the Earth Serpent, a cave network beneath Mount Cordor, Wilhelm, Grimm, and the last child were all caved in. Trying to find their way out, the kid, who had passed out, eventually awoke and provided the two with a lagmite crystal, providing them light. However, shortly after, they were set upon by the Earth Serpent, a large earth sandworm. Being forced to confront it, Grimm, who was only able to block one of its strikes, was tasked with taking the kid and running while Wilhelm held it off. Grimm eventually found a hole for the kid to pass through and had him inform the rest of the squad of his location. Afterward, he signaled Wilhelm to rush back to him, where a trap was waiting and triggered when the giant worm punched a hole into the outside world, where the rest of the squadron was waiting, and they successfully killed it. With it being the morning of the day of the wedding, everyone quickly rushed to return back to the capital, Conwood Melahau and the others feeling guilty for failing to recognize her as a regular girl during their time with her and saying that Theresia should not be on the altar alone, deciding to postpone their after-action report. Though unable to clean themselves or change, they managed to return in time, and afterward, he attended his wedding. With Veltol entrusting her to him, Wilhelm and Theresia were finally married. As the two prepared to leave, Theresia tossed the bouquet to Carol, leaving her flustered. Grimm took this chance to pull her in, take the bouquet, and hold it in the air, showcasing that he and Carol would be next.

Felt-chan Forms a Hooligan Squad
Felt sat with the trio of thugs to discuss with them, and after some talk and a bit of resistance from them, she eventually convinced them to help destroy the country, as she thought they had similar views to her. Later on at night, Reinhard had a secret meeting with Grimm and Carol, commenting how the events that transpired confirmed that his choice to follow Felt was the correct one and that he felt a little guilty that he would use her to make the Astrea family name rise to glory again. Changing the main subject, the old lady asks if they really should allow their master to get near Reinhard's mother, as they feared what could come of the encounter. Reinhard stated that he cannot deny him this, as it was his right, and he mentioned that he would soon leave with Felt to take care of other matters, thanking the both of them for everything they had done.
abilities_text:
Powerful Instincts: Aside from his skill with the shield, one of Grimm's most notable traits is his ability to sense danger. According to Grimm, he gets a feeling of fear on the nape of his neck when danger is near. His instincts are the main reason that he has managed to defend himself and survive hopeless situations, such as the Battle of Castour Field. In fact, his ability to sense danger is superior to Wilhelm's, getting bad feelings when Wilhelm initially couldn't until the danger was already at his feet, and this had led to Wilhelm trusting this feeling as something that signifies true danger.

Equipment:
Great Shield: Grimm's primary weapon of choice is a large shield with the crest of House Remendis engraved on it. The shield was given to him by Carol Remendis during the Demi-Human War. He displayed great skill with it, even being capable of deflecting attacks from Wilhelm, an Al Jiwald fired by Sphinx, and even an attack from an Earth Sandworm. His skill with the shield allows him to evenly match the skills of Carol while being manipulated without hurting her. The shield he wielded before this bore the symbol of the Kingdom's flag on it.
Sword: Although he wasn't very effective with it and was considered hopeless with it, Grimm wielded a standard sword in his first few battles.

intro: Gramdart Holstoy (グラムダート・ホルストイ) was a High Count and a former minister of the Sacred Vollachia Empire. He was one of the main antagonists of The Travelogue of the Finest, where he targeted Emperor Vincent Vollachia's life, stole the secret imperial flying dragon tamer technique, and fled the nation. Following his capture, Gramdart was escorted back to the Empire by Cecilus Segmunt and Chisha Gold due to his treason.
appearance: Gramdart is described to be a middle-aged man.
personality: Gramdart was a greedy and ambitious man who allegedly wanted to steal the emperor's throne for himself. He was also mentioned to have stolen the secret Imperial flying dragon taming technique, which would cause great trouble for the entire Empire. Gramdart was also a coward at heart, avoiding a direct confrontation with Vincent at all costs, and fleeing the Empire after his plans were foiled.
history:
The Travelogue of the Finest
Roughly half a year before the start of Royal Selection in Lugunica, Gramdart, alongside Balleroy Temeglyph, conspired against the seventy-seventh emperor of the Vollachia Empire, Vincent Vollachia. After his plan ended in failure with Balleroy's death, Gramdart faked his own suicide to serve as a cover for his escape into the neighboring Dragon Kingdom of Lugunica. Trying to achieve diplomatic immunity by giving an unspecified souvenir (likely the aforementioned Imperial secret) to the Six Tongues, Gramdart secluded himself in the heart of the kingdom. Not long after, his men spotted Cecilus Segmunt in the Royal Capital, which caused Gramdart to hire fourteen thugs (Ton, Chin, and Kan, among others) to tail the Divine General; however, the group was swiftly dispatched by him. Naturally, it didn't take long for Cecilus to locate Gramdart himself. Slaughtering his guards with ease, Cecilus was about to take Gramdart's head off; however, Chisha Gold intruded just in time to prevent his death. The two Divine Generals then restrained the High Count and took him back to the Empire to be granted punishment for his treason.

alias: Sixth (陸, Roku) ; Master of Curse Tools (呪具師, Jugushi)
occupation: Fifth of the Nine Divine Generals

intro: Groovy Gumlet (グルービー・ガムレット) is the Fifth ranking Divine General of the Sacred Vollachia Empire. He played a major supporting role in Arc 8, and he also played a small antagonistic role in The Travelogue of the Finest.
appearance: Groovy has a small body covered with brown fur with black spots and whiskers on his face. He has cream-colored fur on his chest, his muzzle, and on the tip of his tail. Groovy also wears numerous belts across his body, which he uses to carry his weapons. For defense, he wears a bronze left breastplate and a small shoulder plate on his left shoulder. In addition, Groovy dons both a yellow scarf around his neck and dark olive-green toeless leather pants.
personality: Despite his small stature, Groovy is a hothead who speaks in a rather vulgar manner and is very short-tempered. He is loyal to the emperor and has a sense of camaraderie with his allies, including other Divine Generals like Balleroy and Moguro. Despite his temperament, he is not above apologizing to others when he is in the wrong. In his free time, Groovy restores old buildings or ruins with historic value and tended to the gardens of the Crystal Palace before its destruction.
history:
The Travelogue of the Finest
Roughly four to five months before Arc 1, a rebellion in Vollachia was started by Gramdart Holstoy and Balleroy Temeglyph. Together, Groovy and Moguro Hagane were dispatched from the Imperial Capital of Lupugana by Goz Ralfon to retrieve the emperor, Vincent Vollachia, while Cecilus Segmunt left on his own accord to accomplish the task. Vincent was kidnapped by Reinhard van Astrea, Julius Juukulius, and Ferris, then in the Empire to negotiate a non-aggression pact alongside Council of Wise Men members Miklotov McMahon and Bordeaux Zergev. Although Moguro initially took Ferris captive, the Sword Saint later freed him and began turning the tables against the two generals, which allowed for the other two knights to escape with Vincent. Groovy and Moguro were later forced to retreat from Reinhard due to his sheer power, and after running to Cecilus, Reinhard was given a chance to render the Blue Lightning unconscious, forcing the pair into submission and causing them to fall back with the unconscious general. After the rebellion was quelled, Groovy met with Vincent in Lupugana's Crystal Palace alongside Moguro, Goz, and Chisha Gold, where they discussed the incident.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
As one of the Nine Divine Generals, Groovy is impressively strong. Although he is aware that he cannot compete with his fellow generals in terms of their respective specializations, his particular strength comes from not only his assortment of weapons, but his sheer willful dedication and methods by which to kill his enemies. In fact, in the words of Eugard Vollachia, Groovy is stronger than all of the Nine Divine Generals of his own era.

Curses
Extensive Curse Knowledge: Groovy excels in the understanding of curses and curse tools. He knows how to make these tools and can even determine how curses work. It was with this knowledge that he managed to uncover the working of the Curse of Thorns. It is precisely because of this knowledge that Groovy was first sought out by Vincent Vollachia to become a Divine General, and it is the reason he is known as the Master of Curse Tools.
Curse Tool Creation: Utilizing his knowledge of curses, Groovy has learned how to create curse tools. One such tool is an unnamed black orb-shaped tool that was put into use at the Gladiator Island Ginunhive. It takes the lives of people engraved with a curse mark if they exceed a fixed distance from the orb, although the exact distance is unknown.

Physical Traits/Flow Method
Enhanced Strength: Despite his small stature, Groovy has considerable physical strength. With a single strike, he was able to send a fully grown man of Heinkel Astrea's stature flying, his fist creating a shockwave on impact.

Enhanced Durability: Groovy is also rather tough. Despite being poisoned, taking severe throat damage, going for days on end without food, drink, or sleep, taking the Curse of Thorns into himself, taking a wound to the gut from the Yang Sword, and tanking an attack from the Fiend Sword to rid himself of the aforementioned curse, he kept himself alive and still seemed lively despite his heavy injuries.

Enhanced Olfaction: Groovy has an enhanced sense of smell that is considered to be the best in Vollachia, allowing him to sniff out the locations of living things or inanimate objects and differentiate between them from a great distance. The one object Groovy cannot smell is the Fiend Sword Murasame, an Enchanted Sword with a will of its own. Out of hatred directed towards Groovy for reforging it into a katana, Fiend Sword used its ability to sever the perceived “point” of its own scent, thereby deterring anyone from being able to track it through scent again. It has even been implied that his nose can pick up on residual mana that has been used against another person.

Intelligence
Anatomical Knowledge: Groovy has a great understanding of the bodies of humans and demi-humans, and this knowledge complements his usage of curse tools, poisons, and the like. On top of this, he understands even the tiniest aspect of his own body, and he uses that knowledge when handling curses and poisons, knowing when his body becomes incapable of withstanding said detriments.

Other
Expert Blacksmith: Groovy has made many weapons while studying curses and curse tools. His skill is great enough that he was able to completely reforge the Fiend Sword from a regular sword to a katana.
Killing Tool Creation: Groovy is also capable of creating unique armaments besides swords, such as Yae Tenzen's special steel thread rings.

Equipment
Groovy wields an assortment of weapons and curse tools in his arsenal. He is described as a walking venerable armory of weapons and is extremely skilled at using them. He possesses much less a traditional fighting style than he does a high level of instinct, natural physical power, and speed, which all work well with his various tools. As a result, he can turn into a nearly literal and lethal whirling blade of death. 
Blood Hatchets (血斧, Chi Ono): These are curse tools that send an intense vibration through the target upon impact. They were originally made to deal with opponents who wore armor over themselves. They also use their holder’s blood to acquire a target. If a target gets Groovy's blood on themselves or their clothes, the hatchets, when thrown, will proceed to lock on to a target and attempt to land a blow on them. The hatchets are also capable of exploding if necessary.
Magic Knuckles (魔手甲, Ma Tekkō): Groovy's Magic Knuckles are gloves with magic stones embedded within which allow him to use non-elemental spells simply made up of mana.
Gauntlets: Groovy wears a pair of gauntlets on his person.
Poison Daggers: Groovy has several daggers that are covered in a lethal poison. A unique characteristic of this poison is that it will nullify the target’s sense of pain. Sometimes, Groovy uses this poison on himself when he is at risk of being overrun by intense pain caused by others, such as the case with the Curse of Thorns. This allows him to fight for a set period of time before his body can’t handle it.
Kusarigama: Groovy uses a kusarigama with a fist-sized weighted ball at the end of the roughly thirty or so meter chain which is made of unique materials. The weight is able to knock opponents back with impressive force. The weight is also filled with the explosive “sands” of the Crimson Hills Girall, and the explosion that comes from the weighted ball, which is triggered by absorbing mana from the surroundings, is powerful and has a wide range.
Snakewhip Sword: The waistband that Groovy wears is an urumi, a flexible sword that bends like a serpent, and it was made from the fangs of snake humans.
Grappling Hooks: Attached to Groovy's trousers are cuffs which can fire off grappling hooks. Used against an opponent, they have the capacity to break a person's shoulders.
Sonic Magic Crystal: Groovy has a magic crystal embedded in his throat. After flicking it, Groovy can use it to amplify his roar and bombard his opponent with a blast of sonic pressure.
Werewolf Cloak: A cloak made of the skin of werewolves. Due to the method used to make this cloak, it has the Divine Protection of Ambushing built into it, making it harder for one to be detected by others in the vicinity.

intro: Goz Ralfon (ゴズ・ラルフォン) is the Fourth ranking Divine General of the Sacred Vollachia Empire. He played a supporting role in Arc 7 and Arc 8. He also played a small antagonistic role in The Travelogue of the Finest and The Tale of the Scarlet Princess.
appearance: Goz is a tall, burly man, slightly taller than Halibel with battle scars covering most of his rough face, brown eyes, and orange-brown hair. He has a beard and clads himself in golden armor that has a red cape attached to the back. In combat, Goz wields a giant golden mace.
personality:
Despite his intimidating physique, Goz is extremely loyal to the Empire and the emperor himself. So much so that he's willing to risk his life for the emperor's safety, despite Vincent losing his title as the emperor of the Vollachia Empire. From what he has shown, Goz always obeys every word from his emperor, which often irritates him and subjects Goz to a barrage of insults. Similarly, he does not abide listening to other people disrespect his emperor, getting unreasonably angry because of it. Most of the time, he is often compared with a dog or an ape, especially when one takes into consideration his habit of using his voice’s excessive volume when speaking. Of course, with his loyalty comes an excess of pride in being a Vollachian soldier. It is because of this pride that he believes that the country should take care of its own problems, leading him to being heavily against forming alliances with other countries, especially Vollachia’s bitter enemy Lugunica, even if it means the country might survive.

Goz is an honorable man, and he will treat anyone who he recognizes as an ally or his savior with respect. Shortly after Rem broke him free from his cuffs and gave him food, he expressed great respect for her and even wished to greet her to his family for what she had done. It has been claimed that in Vollachia, where anyone called to the Crystal Palace's throne room was due to their abilities, if one were to be called for their humanity, it would be Goz. As expected from his rank, Goz is well-respected and professional in his work, looking after the Imperial Army by serving as a Divine General and even suggesting replacements for the fallen Divine Generals when asked for feedback. When forced to go against his own soldiers after breaking out of his imprisonment, who were following their own loyalty, he respected their decision and willingly left said soldiers alive because he was aware of the position they were in. He also places great trust in his soldiers, believing that despite whatever hardships there may be that they can crush their foes with combined efforts. In addition, Goz has a passion for music plays with musical instruments. His love of music led him to meeting his wife at a recital.
history:
At an unknown point in time, Goz's love of music led him to meet his future wife at a recital. The two eventually got married, and they had children. Goz was also a Second-Class General of the Imperial Army, but at some point following the death of Lamia Godwin, he was promoted.

The Tale of the Scarlet Princess
Around seven years before the main story, Goz and Arakiya were dispatched to the Pendleton estate in an attempt to take custody of Jorah Pendleton and his wife, Priscilla, for a scheduled execution. However, Jorah fended Goz and his escorts off for Priscilla's sake, knowing that he would meet his end in just mere moments.

The Travelogue of the Finest
Roughly four to five months before Subaru's arrival, the seventy-seventh emperor of the Vollachia Empire was targeted by Gramdart Holstoy and Balleroy Temeglyph. In the ensuing chaos, the three Lugunican Royal Guards Reinhard van Astrea, Julius Juukulius, and Ferris, who accompanied the two members of the Council of Wise Men, Miklotov McMahon and Bordeaux Zergev, kidnapped the emperor and fled Lupugana with him. While the Eighth, Sixth, and First ranking Divine Generals were dispatched to locate and bring the emperor back to the Crystal Palace, Goz organized the troops, took the two Lugunican diplomats hostage, and kept the Crystal Palace in as much order as possible. Following Vincent's safe return and the departure of the Kingdom's diplomats, Goz took part in a secret meeting between him, Vincent, the Fourth ranking Divine General Chisha Gold, Moguro, and Groovy, with whom he discussed the incident.

Sword Identity
About two to three months afterwards, Goz took place in a meeting between some of the Divine Generals, the emperor, and the Imperial Prime Minister, Berstetz Fondalfon. The group discussed who should be appointed as the next Ninth ranking Divine General following Balleroy Temeglyph's death. Goz suggested a capable Second General from the Insect Cage Clan by the name of Kafma Irulux, but his suggestion was contested by Berstetz, who hoped to give the seat to a Flying Dragon commander by the name of Madelyn Eschart. 

When the Empire's Stargazer prophesized Yorna Mishigure's rebellion, Goz accompanied Cecilus and Arakiya in order to awake Kafma from his pupa and also witnessed Madelyn bring her dragons to the Imperial Capital. Goz and Kafma later joined the other generals in assaulting Chaosflame. While there, Kafma relinquished the idea of becoming a Divine General due to not believing that he was fit enough, putting Goz in a position where he lost credibility due to Kafma's choice.

Imperial Coup
Sometime before the events of Arc 7, he learned of the upcoming Great Disaster. Unfortunately, since his immense loyalty and pride would get in the way of his plans to prevent the disaster, Chisha and Berstetz, the latter of which was unaware of said disaster, had him defeated and locked away beneath Berstetz’s mansion, giving him just enough food and water not to die.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
Goz is an incredibly powerful warrior whose strength is among the top of the Empire's hierarchy. He is capable of going toe to toe with combatants on the level of Hornet and easily dispatch hordes of combatants with ease. What makes him even more dangerous than his combat prowess, however, is his ability to command large forces, which is second only to Chisha among the Nine Divine Generals.

Physical Traits/Flow Method
Herculean Strength: Goz has considerable strength. A single punch from him has the might to create shockwaves and the power to instantly fell a large-sized witchbeast. More than that, however, a strike delivered by Goz is so mighty that not even another one of the Nine Divine Generals can stop it easily. It is thanks to his strength that he is capable of wielding his primary weapon, and he has shown to be easily capable of throwing an axe with such ferocity that whoever is stricken by it will be sent flying backward with terrific momentum.

Enhanced Endurance: Goz has an incredible level of endurance. During his imprisonment, Chisha and Berstetz effectively starved Goz in order to drain his strength. Despite this, Goz was still extremely lively and fighting against the chains binding him, even after months with barely any food.

Excellent Hearing: Goz has an incredible sense of hearing, which enables him to recognize sound on a level higher than the average person and to discern even the nuances in the wind.

Techniques
Howl (遠吠え, Tōboe): Using his extraordinary hearing and herculean strength, Goz can discern vibrations that are unique to every organism and strike someone with the very same vibrations that his opponents have in the form of a deadly "howl" that is created with a shockwave of sound from his mace. The "howl" only damages the targets whose vibrations match the sound of Goz's mace. This technique was what led Goz to become known as the Lion Knight.

Leadership
Exceptional Leadership: Among everyone in the Imperial Army, Goz is well-known not just for his attitude, but also for his skills as a leader. Aside from his combat capabilities, his best quality is in being able to command a massive number of forces even while on the frontlines, something which, among the Nine Divine Generals, is said to be second only to Chisha. He commands respect from everyone beneath him and can easily boost their morale, and he has an eye for particular talent among his comrades and is willing to vouch for them for better standings both in rank and on the battlefield. Vincent highly values this even over his martial skill. It is precisely because of this quality that Vincent left him to lead the army in Garkla during the Great Disaster rather than taking him to Lupugana.

Equipment
Large Mace: Goz wields a large golden mace in combat. This mace can be disassembled via twisting the spear-like shaft from the striking head of the mace. This mace, so heavy that only someone of Goz's size and strength could wield, is unique in that slamming the shaft into the separated head can generate a powerful sound, allowing Goz to use his "howl".
Golden Armor: One of the most distinguishing traits of Goz is the golden armor that he wears in battle.

name: Halibel
alias: Admirer (礼賛者, Raisansha) ; Eternal Playboy (永遠の遊び人, Eien no Asobinin)
intro: Halibel (ハリベル) is a shinobi of Kararagi who is known throughout the world as the Admirer, one of the three people said to be on par with the Kingdom's Reinhard van Astrea in terms of overall martial skill, alongside the Empire's Cecilus Segmunt and the Holy Kingdom's Vague Adgard. He made his main story debut in Arc 8, where he played a supporting role.
appearance: Halibel is a wolf human with relatively long black fur clad in a disheveled black kimono possessing worn-down purple accents. His large height makes him tower over a fully-grown Subaru like a black statue covered in fur, and his golden eyes are usually narrowed into two slits. He often likes biting on his golden kiseru with his teeth. More often than not, Halibel gives off a rather laid-back air through his appearance.
personality:
Halibel has a casual behavior and likes the taste of liquor and free alcohol. In spite of the nature of his line of work, Halibel is outwardly friendly towards others and is rarely shown to display anger or disapproval towards other and their opinions of him, and he often makes jokes to keep the mood light. He'll even offer to share candy with children, though he'll also forget that he doesn't have any candy on him. It is because of this positive nature and his habit of bestowing praise unto others that he earned himself the epithet of the Admirer. In fact, in the rare times that Halibel expresses his disapproval, it is claimed that those who knew him would be surprised to hear such words leave his mouth. Likewise, he is somewhat whimsical. With his rather free position as a shinobi for hire and his personality, it is Halibel's motto that he will help those that he wants to help while turning his nose from things that do not interest him, something which tends to give other people two different extremes in terms of their impressions toward him.

Although he shows total respect towards others, he can be a bit too serious when talking about his race, since his race is rather rare and on the verge of extinction, often mentioning that he feels like carrying the pride of his kind. Likewise, he also considers himself a masterless ronin and is not under the control of his country. Although he has gratitude toward his country and is willing to allow himself to be hired by people in power, he is averse to the idea of being owned by the country and being used as a bargaining chip for political negotiations.

Though a friendly man, he takes his job seriously. If someone hires him to do a job, whether that be Kararagi’s League of Cities themselves, a friend like Anastasia Hoshin, or especially from his fellow wolf-human tribesmen, he will do what he can to accomplish his task, listening and respecting the requests of his contractors. Likewise, he also believes that one should not break their promises or oaths, as when he was once tasked by his fellow tribesmen to take the life of Ricardo Welkin for breaking his oath to them, Halibel believed that he brought it on himself. This being said, he does not enjoy having to take the lives of his friends, and he will show visible relief if he is able to avoid doing so.
history:
Halibel was born in the hidden settlement of the wolf people in Kararagi. He was childhood friends with Ricardo, who he was the same age as. By his teenage years, Halibel's strength among the wolf people in the village was peerless. While he wished to live out his days peacefully, Ricardo, who was unsuited to life in the village, left the village on his fifteenth birthday, making an oath with the village's leader that he would renounce his identity as a wolf person. In the event that he broke his oath, the chief swore to Ricardo that Halibel would come to kill him. Eventually, as the strongest wolf human and the strongest man in Kararagi, Halibel was allowed by his fellow tribesmen to make himself known and proclaim himself as a wolf human. That said, as a member of their tribe, he would oft be requested to handle their requests.

Around fifteen years after Ricardo's departure, Halibel was tasked with carrying out his assassination, as the wolf people believed he had broken his oath to hide his lineage. Though he found the task unfortunate, Halibel still accepted it nonetheless, believing that Ricardo brought it upon himself. When he eventually met Ricardo and was prepared to take his life, a young Anastasia protected Ricardo, and she managed to find a compromise to keep Halibel from having to kill Ricardo. Afterward, Halibel maintained friendly relations with Anastasia and Ricardo.

At some point in the past, Vollachia’s strongest warrior, Cecilus Segmunt, was given the task of slaying Halibel, as being a wolf human put his head on the chopping block for his race’s involvement in the betrayal of the Emperor of the Briar and his lover. The two clashed, but rather than killing Halibel, Cecilus returned home. Sometime after this, Halibel lived in Banan.

Anastasia's Companion Searching Chronicle
Sometime around the events of the Pleiades Watchtower Expedition, Halibel was hired by the League of Cities to investigate the goings-on of one of the towns that borders Vollachia, Nanou, whose income of food and other such supplies had dramatically reduced. There, he discovered that the living were completely replaced by the undead. Though he found the events strange, as the undead were acting as though they were alive yet without purpose, Halibel dispatched them all and reported to the League of Cities. Though they attempted to pass judgement on him, thinking he had gone too far in his actions, Anastasia and Julius Juukulius interrupted the mock conference they were holding, with the former using her words to give Halibel the chance to explain his actions in Nanou. She managed to convince the League of Cities to send her and Halibel as emissaries to Vollachia, to which they accepted. As it aligned with his goals to investigate the occurrence, he accepted it as well. Along the way, he spoke with Julius and explained his connection to Anastasia and Ricardo.

Kararagi Reaper Incident
Shortly after the events of the Great Disaster, Anastasia, accompanied by Julius, Halibel, and Echidna, returned to Kararagi, where they decided to report their discoveries to the mayor of the Third City Ivada, Orgo Hayata. Unfortunately, there was yet another problem: the windstorm created by the Slasher, Zarestia, that was thrust upon Banan. After learning of this, she, Eridna, Julius, and Halibel made their way to Banan to meet up with Ricardo. Sometime after Ricardo quelled Zarestia's rage, Anastasia's group arrived and were led to the holding cells in Riften Magoji's mansion, where Zarestia was being held. During their conversation, Anastasia learned that Riften went missing, Julius noticed that Zarestia was a Great Spirit and introduced himself, and Halibel unintentionally riled her up by noticing her strange constitution, that something was missing. However, when Anastasia mentioned Zarestia being responsible for other such town-destroying wind cataclysms, Zarestia declared otherwise, saying that she only rampaged in Banan. Shortly afterward, this is confirmed when a massive tornado appeared outside of Banan, not made by Zarestia. After giving her orders and securing Zarestia's assistance, the group made their way to stop the tornado. Although they managed to quell the winds, however, they soon realized that Anastasia and Echidna had gone missing.

A full day after being taken, Anastasia and Echidna were brought back to Banan by Black Tia, their captor, and shortly after, likely due to her exhaustion catching up with her, Anastasia passed out with a fever. Though Julius tended to her and attempted to help heal her with his spirits, he was unable and settled for practicing with Halibel to become stronger. Over the course of the day, Julius fought and lost against Halibel ten times, though after their tenth fight, Halibel mentioned that Julius was definitely improving, claiming that he was likely one of the strongest people in the Kingdom. As evening approached, they decided to have another clash, in which Halibel claimed that he would be able to display his full potential at nighttime.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
Halibel is famously known to be one of the few people in the world who is able to employ martial skill on a similar level to the Kingdom's Reinhard, effectively making Halibel one of the strongest people in the world, matched only by a bare few, and the most powerful military asset in Kararagi. Halibel is highly skilled at using various types of techniques, and as a shinobi, he excels at eliminating his targets. Even without using his myriad techniques, he has many other ways of combatting opponents, both with his physical might and his knowledge of curses, giving him a wide array of methods to fight, even when his opponent is unfavorable towards him. Even when forced into melee combat with a warrior on the level of a polished Eugard Vollachia, he displayed such skill in martial arts that he was able to defend, attack, and counter with ease, even without using special techniques and tricks. Furthermore, by his own claim, he is able to show his full potential at nighttime. Even among shinobi, he is considered exceptional, to the point that Olbart Dunkelkenn would reluctantly attest it.

Curses
Curse Arts (呪術, Jujutsu): Halibel is an expert in curse arts. Killing curses are his trump card, and he fuses pieces of his own fur or nails that he cursed into his weapons to cast a curse that, no matter what, will kill his opponent. However, these curses are not compatible with beings that are already dead, such as the zombies in Vollachia.

Extensive Curse Knowledge: As an expert in using curse arts himself, Halibel is quite versed in the workings of curses. It was with this knowledge that he, alongside another curse expert, was able to determine the inner workings of Eugard Vollachia's Curse of Thorns.

Techniques
As a shinobi, Halibel has access to numerous abilities and techniques exclusive to shinobi, and his mastery with them is second to none. Most of his techniques center around deception, high lethality, targeting weaknesses, avoiding damage, and movement, giving him many options:
Dead Spot (死穴): Halibel has shown the ability to perceive the flow of power in various techniques and abilities, and by aiming at these "dead spots", he is able to completely nullify powerful attacks, such as a great laser, and he is even capable of halting the regeneration of the zombies of the Great Disaster for a time.
Cloning (分け身): Halibel is able to use his fur to clone himself into four, using both physical and hollow clones to confuse his opponent. Perhaps the biggest upside to his cloning ability is that each and every clone is identical to the original specimen, including their strength, meaning that rather than splitting his fighting strength into four "pieces", he quadruples it. The clones are also able to act independently.
Swapping (変わり身): Used only in the alternate events of Re:IF, Halibel has the capacity to swap his place with an object's place. He utilized this technique in order to swap places with a log and have it sustain the damage of Reize's wind attacks in his place.
Unnamed Burying Technique: During his battle with Eugard Vollachia, Halibel displayed an ability to drag his opponent into the ground. Apparently, the technique leaves the target’s head poking out of the ground, but those of considerable power and resistance do not get dragged into the ground all the way. Eugard managed to get away with only his lower half being dragged beneath the earth. He is also capable of slipping into the ground himself, using it as a means of evasion.
Unnamed Walking Technique: Using a certain walking technique, Halibel is able to leave behind afterimages to confuse his opponents. Unlike his clones, these afterimages vanish like mist.
Unnamed Dissipation Technique: Halibel is capable of catching attacks with his finger and dissipating the strength of the attack into the ground, making the ground ripple like water in the process.

Physical Traits/Flow Method
Halibel is highly proficient in melee combat, and thanks to his traits as a wolf human, he has physical capabilities beyond most humans, as well as enhanced senses that most humans do not have. He is also a master of the Flow Method, increasing his already impressive physical might by leaps and bounds.

Enhanced Strength: Halibel's physical strength is top notch. He is capable of releasing devastating power with palm strikes which are capable of damaging castle walls or creating a small windstorm that can blow away fire from even the Yang Sword, while an elbow strike can hit someone with the power of a battle axe, with whoever got struck potentially leaving a crater in the ground. Even just grazing someone with his fingertips has the potential to leave a fist sized hole in his enemy.

Enhanced Speed: Halibel is incredibly fast. When he kicks off of the ground, he can propel himself at such a speed that the ground behind him shatters, and most are incapable of keeping up with him.

Claws: As a wolf human, Halibel has sharp claws on his finger, and they are very easily capable of rending flesh. Combined with the Flow Method's enhancement, his claws can become sharp enough to compare to any famed sword.

Heightened Olfaction: As a wolf human, Halibel's sense of smell is higher than the average human's. With it, Halibel was able to smell the faint traces of poison with Groovy's blood.

Stealth: Halibel is a master of stealth and can completely erase his presence, including his scent. He could be sitting in a room filled with a large number of people of Divine General level, and nobody would even realize he was there until he’d either killed everyone or purposefully made himself known. He is also able to prevent those with a keen sense of smell, such as Ricardo, from noticing his scent. During combat, he has a habit of using his clones while scattering his own presence, and if one is particularly observative, they can take advantage of this, assuming they last long enough against.

Others
Poison Knowledge/Recognition: Having been trained as a shinobi, Halibel is familiar with all kinds of poisons, and he is able to determine whether a person had been poisoned by the scent in their blood, even if the smell is faint.

Equipment
Kunai: Halibel’s primary weapon of choice are kunai. When thrown, his kunai are described to travel at beyond human speeds.
Throwing Daggers: He uses these alongside his kunai.
Kiseru: Halibel is regularly seen smoking out of a kiseru, burning the special herbs within to keep himself alive.
Katana: Halibel carries a katana. However, as he has yet to draw it, it is unknown how proficient he is with it in combat.

name: Hannah Regret
intro: Hannah Regret (ハンナ・リグレット) was the only maid of House Argyle. She played a supporting role in The Dream the Lion King Saw.
appearance: Hannah had flax hair and amber eyes much like Ferris. She dressed in an unremarkable maid outfit. From Crusch's perspective, she had a resemblance to Ferris.
personality: Hannah was a rather solemn person who had a quiet dignity about her. She seemed especially warm toward Ferris, although she tended to mask it with a fairly detached disposition.
history:
The Dream the Lion King Saw
Little is known about Hannah's history with the Argyles and how deep her relationship ran with them. However, she was the only servant to remain with them after the family become fallen nobility out of affection.

Hannah did not approve of the dark situation around Biehn and Miles. Thus, seeking outside aid to deal with it, Hannah had contracted House Karsten and began acting as a double agent. Later, she met with Crusch Karsten again after the poison had worn off and loosened her restraints so that Crusch could meet Ferris and escape. However, Crusch would question her reasons for helping them, and Hannah returned the query with a question of her own, suggesting it was out of her own love for Biehn. She would also bear witness to Biehn's wife being revived by Ferris and the killing her husband moments later in the master bedroom. After questioning Ferris and looking strangely relieved, she was the one who told Ferris where Crusch was. Just as Ferris left to go find her, the Hannah told Ferris goodbye and locked herself in the room along with Biehn and his wife's corpses, committing suicide by setting the room on ablaze.

relatives: Dudley Miload (husband) ; Annerose Miload (daughter) ; Roswaal L. Mathers (distant relative)
first_light_novel: The Oni Sisters of the Hidden Village
intro: Grace Miload (グレイス・ミロード) was the mother of Annerose Miload. She died during childbirth during the Attack on Miload Manor.
appearance: Grace was described to be a slender woman.
personality: Grace seemed to be a friendly woman who was prone to teasing others and a sharp woman who instantly realized that Ram was interested in Roswaal. She was also decisive. After realizing that she was in danger, she was quick to listen to Ram's orders and follow her lead.
history:
The Oni Sisters of the Hidden Village
Grace was unable to control mana properly since birth until it was fixed when Roswaal corrected it. She became friends with him soon after and later became distant relatives when she married Dudley. During the final month of her pregnancy, Roswaal, Rem, and Ram visited her while Dudley was away for work. Over the course of three days, she became friendly with the twins. However, when Dudley was late to come home, Roswaal and Rem went to retrieve him, leaving Ram to keep Grace company. When Faust attacked, Ram ordered Limrear to help Grace so they could escape. However, after the group came across some of the corpses of the servants, Grace's water broke, and Ram left Limrear to help her deliver the baby while she fended off Faust. After the battle concluded, she delivered her baby but had unfortunately lost too much blood. Dying, she told Roswaal that she loved him, named her baby Annerose, and asked Roswaal to watch over her.

name: Kalifa
relatives: Ilya (daughter)
appearance: Kalifa is a beautiful woman with long grey-brown hair and green eyes. She gives off a gentle aura.
personality: Although she cannot speak, making her day-to-day tasks more difficult, Kalifa is a kind and protective woman who cares for the safety of her daughter and, despite her young age, strives to diligently raise Ilya. In the time since she moved to Hakuchuri, she has become close with Gaston.
history:
Some time in the past, Kalifa became Doltero Amule's mistress and birthed their daughter, Ilya, several months before the Royal Selection. Doltero revealed his relationship with them to only one person, his closest and most loyal confidant, Safis.

The Golden Lion and the Sword Saint
Recognizing that Kalifa and Ilya were Doltero's weaknesses, Safis attempted to have them killed out of loyalty to his boss and a desire to remove the "vulnerabilities" he had. As a result, Kalifa was attacked by an assailant Safis sent and had her larynx destroyed, inhibiting her from ever being able to speak again. She and her daughter both survived, and she entrusted Ilya to the Astrea Manor for protection. Doltero sent one of his men after the two, but he was discovered by Felt and Reinhard and revealed his affiliation with the Black Silver Coin once the candidate threatened with the Sword Saint. Shortly afterwards, Gaston, Rachins, and Camberley located Kalifa and brought her back to the mansion, where they discovered that Doltero was Ilya's father. Deciding to visit Doltero in Flanders, Rom used his connection to Doltero to hold a meeting with him. When Felt, Reinhard, and Rom, alongside Kalifa and Ilya, met with Doltero, he discovered that his confidant was responsible for ordering the attack on his mistress and daughter. Safis revealed his intentions, preparing to commit suicide to atone for his misdeeds, only for Doltero to suddenly assault him to keep him alive and demote him to a simple lackey position in the Black Silver Coin unless he could work to regain the Pig King's trust. Understanding Safis's argument, he disowned his mistress and his daughter, much to the displeasure of Felt and Rom. Before leaving, Kalifa turned to Doltero and bowed, showing him the face of his sleeping baby one last time, and Doltero murmured Ilya's name once the room was clear of everyone besides him.

Following the incident, Felt prepared a sum of money for Kalifa to use for her new life with Ilya in Hakuchuri, and helped secure a live-in job for her at a ranch, having Reinhard speak with the owners about it. Flam and Grassis prepared household goods for her, while Gaston, Rachins, and Camberley were assigned to move them. As Kalifa and Ilya departed, Felt told the baby to live strong.

intro: Grassis Remendis (グラシス・レメンディス) is the granddaughter of Carol and Grimm Fauzen and the younger twin sister of Flam Remendis. She later joined the Felt Camp along with her sister. She plays a supporting role in Arc 9.
appearance: Like her sister, she is a short girl and has peach hair with yellow ribbons in her hair. She wears white and pink clothes. Unlike her sister Flam, her fringe is straight.
personality:
According to Ezzo Cadner, she is very much like her sister in personality, who does not mind speaking of things she does not want to do and has a sharp mouth. She and her sister are also mischievous, habitually teasing others.

She and her sister also hold grudges towards those who wrong the members of House Astrea, particularly when it comes to Heinkel Astrea, and they will show no qualms in delivering ruthless beatings towards their enemies.
history:
Born to one of Carol and Grimm's children, servants of House Astrea, she and her sister Flam have been trained by the family they've served since birth.

Meili’s Witchbeast Observation Record
A short time after the successful Pleiades Watchtower Expedition, members of the Felt Camp, which included Flam and Grassis, were tasked with reaching the Pleiades Watchtower and investigating it. During their travels through the Augria Sand Dunes, the Divine Dragon attacked them to protect the tower, leaving Reinhard to defend the party. Fortunately, Meili Portroute, who was protecting the party from witchbeasts as they made their way toward the tower, presented Volcanica’s talon, and they were allowed passage into the tower. There, they came across the Books of the Dead, which Meili explained to them, much to the fascination of Ezzo. Understanding their importance, Felt suggested Reinhard find the book of his grandmother, and though he was hesitant to do so, when Felt persuaded him to find it at some point, he was grateful.

Shortly after, they noticed the same birds that Subaru and Eridna had witnessed before. With one captured for study, Ezzo quickly discovered its true nature, and the crimson scorpion being carried by Meili killed it in his hands. Realizing the birds were being used to spy, Ezzo and Reinhard set to killing them all. Deciding to return to the capital, they left Ezzo and Flam at the tower.
abilities_text:
Divine Protection (加護 Kago): Grassis and her sister both have the Divine Protection of Mindspeak (念話の加護 Nenhanashi no Kago), which allows them to speak to each other through their mind. The distance between them does not matter, but it can only be used once a day. According to Petra's observations, the once-a-day condition seems to be connected to the amount of time that she sleeps rather than a full 24-hour time period.

Flow Method (流法): Despite being young, Grassis is an expert in using the Flow Method, giving her access to increase strength and a greater recuperation speed. She is shown to be powerful enough to beat the three thugs, Gaston, Rachins, and Camberley, with ease. Grassis is also mentioned to be stronger than Felt, Rom, and the other Felt Camp members except Ezzo Cadner and Reinhard van Astrea.

Stealth: Like her sister, Grassis is good at stealth. During the conflict with Al, she managed to stay hidden throughout all of his loops, and she even managed to successfully sneak up on him once without his noticing until it was too late.

intro: Helaine Gatness (へレイン・ガットネス) is the former leader of the Golden Beetle's office in Flanders and a member of the Six Tongues, acting as a subordinate of Russell Fellow.
appearance: Helaine is a small woman with narrow eyes and twin pigtails in her dark green hair that, depending on the light, can look black. Her right eye is covered by a diagonal fringe. She wears a well-made black suit, a black tie, black gloves, as well as black socks and shoes, qualities that make her appear to be an authentic professional. Perhaps most strikingly, Helaine can often seen with a forced, pasted-on smile that conceals her true thoughts and intentions.
personality:
Helaine has a condescending and audacious demeanor, a lack of humanity and remorse, an unyielding nature, and a stoic exterior that masks her true intentions and emotions from others. She is willing to investigate people's backgrounds or thoroughly research a particular skill in order to excel at it. For example, Helaine thoroughly analyzed all of the games in Flanders' gambling quarter, with her sheer gambling prowess being why nobody from the Big Three could outmaneuver her in bets. Although highly capable, she views her talents with vain, this being what led her to instigate the unrest in Flanders in an attempt to gain a foothold in the Big Three, failing because she gauged herself as more in control of the situation and mistakenly underestimating the shrewdness of her opposition.

She exhibits a strong loyalty and captivation for Russell to the point that she would end her own life if he ordered her to. Rather than strictly adhere to his orders exactly as presented to her, however, Helaine had the inclination to disobey her assignment, believing he would be pleased if she achieved success. When an associate of hers is put at risk, she will not hesitate to let them be if it is advantageous for her interest, recommending against saving Belmont when he was faced with the threat of murder and assessing his life as a tool to ward off the exposure of her side's involvement. Helaine also feels hostile towards Lugunica's knights, considering them inefficient compared to the Six Tongues.
history:
First Mission
Having been the youngest individual among the ranks of the Six Tongues five years before the start of the Royal Selection, Helaine worked alongside Bikram Edditz and Julius Juukulius to topple Reiner Wahrheit's organization, which dealt in several illicit activities, most notably the sale of the illegal drug Hexcel. Under the pseudonym Helena, she introduced Julius to Blau, a member of the organization, providing the man a false story about the rookie knight's identity. When they reconvened after Julius's first day infiltrating the group, he spoke of how he pretended to slay Blau and sought to have him healed, only for Bikram to deny his request. Helaine provided a sample of the Hexcel drug they found, with Bikram saying it was her task to identify their source. When Belmont, a spy in the organization and her colleague in the Six Tongues was detained by Reiner's people on suspicion of leaking information, Helaine was against rescuing him. Julius attempted to convince Helaine and Bikram otherwise, and though she resisted, after she confirmed his view that Belmont would be more beneficial to keep than Blau, they hatched a plan to save him. Using the injured Blau, she drugged him with Hexcel of potent quality, sending him on a rampage, ending with his life being cut short by Reiner's hand. With her mission complete, she prepared herself to move to her next task, briefly conversing with Belmont after his reunion with Marcos Gildark.

Riot in Flanders
Several years later, Helaine was assigned with the task of managing the Flanders branch of the Golden Beetle, a moneylending loan shark organization with strong links to the underworld. Around the start of the Royal Selection, Mozolite, the second-in-command of the Balance, allied himself with Helaine in an attempt to snatch the position of his boss, Manfred Madison, orchestrating attacks on the Big Three and her own Golden Beetle organization with assassins and leveraging his position in his group to do so. Helaine, perceiving Mozolite's ambition and detecting that he could be easily exploited, supported his goal, believing it would be in the interest of the Six Tongues. Two months later, during a meeting with the representatives of the Big Three concerning the attacks that had been taking place, she proposed the one responsible was Felt, the Royal Selection Candidate being housed by the Sword Saint of Hakuchuri, having received reports that she contacted Doltero Amule and the Black Silver Coin before. As a result, the leaders of the Balance and the Flower Prison Garden, Manfred and Toto, went on to seek courtesy visits from her as a means to verify her intentions, with Doltero sending his former confidant Safis to inform her of their wishes.

On a night following Felt's courtesy visits with Toto and Doltero, a subordinate of Mozolite's with an Excess Mana Circulation Constitution attacked Mimosa, a student of Ezzo Cadner who worked for the Flower Prison Garden, setting the brothel she was in on fire. Although Ezzo rushed to the scene, he was rendered unconscious and framed for the arson. With the Big Three after him, he escaped from his predicament with Camberley's help and sought Helaine for his safety, offering unpublished magic theories he had created to her in exchange for an abandoned mansion to use as a safe house. Felt, Reinhard, Flam Remendis, and Rachins Hoffman visited the Golden Beetle to inquire his whereabouts. Hoping to establish a professional relationship with Felt, she willingly divulged Ezzo's location. Acting as a representative of Ezzo, Rachins, accompanied by Flam, paid a visit to the gambling quarter to directly confront Helaine, who revealed she was aware of his origins as the son of the Royal Instructor, Rickert Hoffman. Initially making a bet with the unreasonable request that the name or power of the Sword Saint be lent to her, she changed her condition to something more relaxed and what was her true goal: to send a single letter to the Hoffman family with the contents of her choosing. Rachins accepted her bet and selected Shatranj as their game of choice.

During the game of Shatranj, Helaine easily outmaneuvered Rachins. However, Manfred arrived in the middle of it, calling Helaine by the same derisive Golden Pest nickname that he used to refer to her and what Rachins had said just earlier, making Helaine quickly realizing that her opponent had greeted the Tattoo Face prior to the game, with Ezzo removing the cognitive disruption mask that concealed his identity to verify that his status as a fugitive among the Big Three had been put on hold. Furthermore, she misunderstood that Rachins's condition should he win the game had been to arrange for Ezzo's escape, when in reality he never provided her with any condition. He then made six clicks of his tongue, indicating his awareness of Helaine's allegiance while simultaneously exposing it to Manfred, declaring "Shatzbort" to signal his victory in an off-board game. With her loyalty to the Six Tongues revealed, and Manfred there to ensure that she fulfilled her end of the bargain, her only option was to minimize her side's losses and take accountability for her own failure. As compensation for her loss, she provided Ezzo with the information that would allow him to avenge his fallen student, Mimosa. The Balance took Helaine into custody afterwards, quickly learning the identity of her collaborator, Mozolite, and his betrayal of their organization.

Once everything was said and done, the Golden Beetle's influence and reputation in Flanders plummeted, with its place being succeeded by Felt, and in exchange for a large compensation, the Six Tongues managed to retrieve her from the Balance, with her being taken in and imprisoned underground at an unknown location, likely in a building at the Royal Capital. She personally reported the whole situation to Russell and was subjected to torture from her curse mark in response to her insubordination, vowing to herself that she would overcome the intense pain dealt to her in order to serve him again.

intro: Lamia Godwin (ラミア・ゴドウィン) was an Imperial Princess of the Sacred Vollachia Empire who participated in the Imperial Selection Ceremony. She played an antagonistic role in The Tale of the Scarlet Princess, Arc 7, and Arc 8.
appearance:
Lamia had orange hair, glossy drooping eyes, and an alluringly shaped body with large breasts. She wore a long black dress with an outer crimson garment that matched the color of her eyes. The top had long sleeves that extended down from the elbow, and they had a crest on them. Additionally, Lamia had a penchant for accessories. She could be seen wearing a black head accessory and a green necklace.

As a zombie, she possessed a vessel of earth, pale skin bereft of color, various cracks that ran across her body, pitch-black sclera, and radiant golden irises.
personality:
Lamia was a confident and self-assured woman who used cunning and manipulative methods to fulfill her ends. She was cruel, ruthless, and vicious, willing to use any means necessary to achieve her goals, including deceit and violence. Her words sounded as sweet as honey while dripping with malice and sarcasm. She was adept at manipulating others with charm and using them as resources when necessary. Lamia was also blessed with great intellect and had a talent for political tact, yet she also had the foresight to listen to the recommendations of her former advisor, Berstetz Fondalfon. Likewise, she was gifted with an intelligent mind able to quickly put things together once she understands the concept behind it, as well as to immediately judge roles suited for the abilities for herself and others and duties befitting their positions.

As shown, Lamia, never really had much attachment to her half-siblings and was fine with manipulating them for her own ends. As shown where she lied to her half-brother Barthroy Fitts in order to give her an edge in the beginning of the Selection Ceremony by pretending that she genuinely hated the idea of killing her half-siblings for the throne, only to then poison him to death when his guard was down. As revealed, the only half-brother Lamia genuinely cared about and admired was Vincent and that she had originally wanted to befriend him and team up together with him when she was younger. But upon seeing the close relationship he had with Prisca, Lamia immediately realized she wouldn't be able to gain Vincent's absolute loyalty unless she died first. Although Lamia was thrilled by those who pose a challenge to her, like Vincent and Prisca, she ultimately came to hate Prisca in particular, even laughing with regret that she had not previously killed her younger sister moments before her own death.

As Lamia willingly cooperated with Sphinx after becoming a zombie, her mind was not subject to the manipulation that many of the other undead experienced during the Great Disaster.
history:
Lamia was born as part of the Godwin family, a family which held the rank of Counts in the Vollachia Empire. At the age of nine, Lamia turned the tide of an internal rebellion against the Godwin family with her personal force, the Pruning Corps. As a result, she became the head of the family.

At the age of sixteen, Lamia took part in the Imperial Selection Ceremony. She perished at the hands of Prisca Benedict after the attempted Siege on the Abellux Castle failed with Cecilus Segmunt's elimination of the Pruning Corps.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
Although Lamia is combat capable in her own right, her strength does not surpass that of most accomplished warriors. However, she makes up for this with her genius intellect, something which made her not just dangerous, but also made it so that she wasa one of the people most likely to win the final Imperial Selection Ceremony. As an undead, although her physical capabilities does not improve, it is because of Lamia that the threat posed by Sphinx grew so much.

Intelligence
Keen Intellect: Lamia had been recognized as a genius since her earliest days, being able to quickly understand concepts after being given the barest of explanations. It is thanks to this that she was able to not only quickly understand the truth of souls and use the Sacrament of the Immortal King's replication ability to her advantage when she was undead, but she was also quick to understand who should be considered the largest threats during large-scale skirmishes like the Imperial Selection Ceremony. In particular, Lamia excels at cornering her opposition with schemes and traps, something that was partially responsible for epithet, Poison Princess.

Other
The Pruning Corps (剪定部隊, Sentei butai): Lamia commanded an elite and loyal force known as the Pruning Corps. The Pruning Corps wore black armor from head to toe and wielded a pair of shears as their weapons of choice. They were renowned for their cruel and feral nature in battle, and only Lamia and Berstetz were capable of commanding them; even as undead, their instinct is to halt at either of their commands, regardless of their respective affiliations. However, the Pruning Corps were single-handedly decimated by a young Cecilus Segmunt in a battle that later engraved the Blue Lightning's name in history.

Equipment
Yang Sword Vollachia (陽剣ヴォラキア, Youken Vorakia): As a member of the Imperial Family of Vollachia, Lamia was capable of summoning and using the Yang Sword Vollachia, otherwise known as the Yang Sword, an ornate crimson sword with light that shines like the sun. The sword appears out of thin air when the user wishes to use it, and it cuts and burns whatever the user desires.
Poison: Lamia commonly used poison to eliminate her enemies, and she became known as the Poison Princess because of her association with it.
