name: Great Rabbit
relatives: Daphne (creator)
intro: The Great Rabbit (大兎) is one of the Three Great Witchbeasts created by the Witch of Gluttony, Daphne. It was one of the main antagonists of Arc 4.
appearance: A typical rabbit of the Great Rabbit closely resembled the rabbits found on Earth and were even similarly named. Just like real-world rabbits, every Great Rabbit had a short fluffy tail, large hind legs, long ears, and a coat of fur. They were adorned with a pair of sharp front teeth that could cleave through flesh and bone with astounding ease. Their fur was as white as snow, and their eyes, that lit up when filled with murderous intent, were red. Although small in size (roughly twice as large as a clenched human fist), the Great Rabbit more than made up for its lack in strength due to the insurmountable numbers. It had several physical traits common to witchbeasts, including a fluorescent pink wheel-like sigil and a horn. The rabbits' sigils were small and located on the lower right side of their backs and their singular horns, which were small and had a drill-like shape, were located on their foreheads.
history: Following its birth 400 years ago, the Great Rabbit terrorized the world for centuries, becoming infamous for leaving behind no remains after ravaging various towns and villages. Due to its unstoppable nature, it was treated as a natural disaster, and groups of people called scavengers started to trail after its wake, stealing any valuables left behind by the beast's victims. Nearly four hundred years after its creation, the Great Rabbit's rampage brought it to the Foutour Plains within the lands of the noble House Karsten in the Kingdom of Lugunica. Luckily, the forces of Duke Meckart Karsten led by the duke's daughter, Crusch Karsten, who employed her One Blow, One Hundred Felled technique to dispatch a number of individual rabbits, were able to drive the Great Rabbit out of the Karsten Duchy with minimum casualties beyond wildlife and environmental damage, with her attendant Ferris also healing the duke after he received a battle wound.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
Despite its kill count, each individual rabbit is not particularly strong, and combatants can slay individual rabbits rather easily, whether physically or with magic. However, its threat comes with the sheer number that the Great Rabbit produces. The numbers are so overwhelming that most cannot withstand the endless torrent of rabbits, and eventually, they would be eaten. Like the White Whale, this is the reason that they stayed alive for centuries and brought ruin to many, effectively making them closer to a natural disaster than anything else. In fact, even during the incident where it was finally defeated, it required a combined effort just to seal them away, which could only be done after quelling a certain number of them first.

Physical Traits

Powerful Bite: Despite their small sizes, a single Great Rabbit had enough jaw strength and a sharp enough pair of teeth that it could tear through flesh and bone with minimal effort. A single bite of a single rabbit was enough to completely tear a person's hand from their body, as if the bone had not been there in the first place. If the entire horde were to attack a single person, there would not be a single trace of them left.

Other
Multiplication: The Great Rabbit's biology allowed for it to naturally itself multiply instantly and infinitely, and the collective consciousness would only die when every single rabbit was destroyed. It is for this reason that it was considered practically impossible to kill the Great Rabbit. The highest known limit of individual rabbits that the Great Rabbit seems to be capable of splitting into is 80,000, and it is unknown if the total amount of rabbits at any one time can go higher.

Mana Sensing: In order to find new prey, the Great Rabbit could sense large amounts of mana and tended to follow its to its source. This often led the Great Rabbit discovering living creatures, as living creatures generally had the highest concentration of mana that could be found. Because of this, it was possible for a skilled magician to lure the Great Rabbit to a specific location by providing a strong magic spell for it to follow.

intro: Jamal Aurélie (ジャマル・オーレリー) is a Low Count of the Sacred Vollachia Empire and the sole Escort General of the Imperial Army, acting as the bodyguard of the emperor and the empress consort. He played both supporting and antagonistic roles in Arc 7 and a supporting role in Arc 8.
appearance: Jamal is a tall and very well-built man wearing an eyepatch with Vollachia's Sword Wolf symbol over his scarred right eye. He has rough blue eyes, messy and unkempt dark brown hair, as well as a small stubble beard. As per all Imperial Soldiers who are not Generals, Jamal could be seen sporting Vollachia's standard military uniform, consisting of a red undershirt with short sleeves, a grey overshirt, black pants, black boots with red stripes, black gloves, and a chest protector and shoulder pads. He retains the same uniform upon his promotion to Third-Class General. He also has two twin swords which are usually stationed on his back when they're not drawn.
personality:
Jamal tends to be an openly hostile and aggressive man. Likewise, he has a tendency to quickly resort to violence. Despite being initially stopped by Todd, Jamal continued to with his oppressive and rough attitude towards Subaru, going as far as to stomp on Subaru's broken fingers and badly beat him, and he even lifted Spica by the hair and slammed her into the ground in order to "teach her a lesson". Despite these rough traits, however, Jamal has a sense of honor. He can fight alongside his comrades without complaint, and he becomes enraged on their account if someone was responsible for causing them harm, as in the case with Rem. In a similar way, he has shown willing to take injuries meant for his comrades in battle, and he recognizes when he needs to defend someone because of their importance to the given situation. He pushed Subaru and Spica out of the way of an attack meant for them while taking the injury himself, realizing that they were key for taking down the Great Disaster.

Jamal is a loyal man, showing his emperor the utmost respect, and he is even willing to punish those he believes are being disrespectful towards the man. This loyalty even extends to people he is willing to take into his family, such as Medium O'Connell, who became the Imperial Empress Consort. The same can also be said for his own only family. Though he always acts tough in front of his sister Katya, he feels sad when she is hurt, and he is willing to martyr himself during battle so that all of the proceeds of his death would be sent to her, believing that that was the best way to help her aside from being there himself. This side of him also quite characteristic of most Vollachian soldiers, who all wish to fight in meet their end in battle, as Vincent himself attests to.
history:
Five years before the start of the main story, Jamal was stationed in the Fortified City of Garkla. After the destruction of the city resulting from the Sin Archbishop of Greed some years prior, numerous factions of bandits came into the city under one union and interfered with the rebuilding process. However, Jamal fought and slew one of the bandit's leaders in order to make his enemies lose morale at the cost of his right eye. Later, Jamal met Todd, who had quit being a bandit at that point, and introduced him to his younger sister, Katya.

Sword Identity
Roughly two to three months before the start of the main story, Jamal and Todd were talking about the revolt that had started at that point in time by Yorna Mishigure, the Seventh ranking Divine General. During this conversation, Jamal talked about how he heard a rumor about testing people in the subjugation of Yorna's rebellion in order to see who would take the place of the former Ninth ranking Divine General. After Jamal was asked about his source, he revealed that he had heard it from a few people who fled from a fortress that Yorna had attacked. After taking the time to gather more information, the two later captured the fled soldiers to turn them in as prisoners and helped to bring an end to the rebellion, though they received no reward for their contributions.
abilities_text:
Skilled Swordsman: Jamal is a dual-wielding swordsman with surprisingly graceful skill. He is easily capable of dispatching strong opponents, be it witchbeasts, other soldiers, or flying dragons, as well as deflecting a storm of arrows shot at him with high speed and precision. After Subaru led Todd, Jamal, and the rest of their group into the Elgina's ambush, Jamal was the one who fought it almost single-handedly and even decapitated it without much trouble, a feat not many can pride themselves with. Later, he was able to easily dispatch someone as strong as Holly Shudrak with relative ease. Jamal had risen to his rank as a First-Class Soldier in the Empire for his skill with the sword and fighting prowess, which is said to be on par with roughly ten regular Imperial Soldiers, and was thought by Todd to be able to reach the status of Third-Class General in time, which he successfully reached by the time of the Great Disaster. However, he still cannot compare himself to truly strong individuals such as the Nine Divine Generals.

Above-Average Reflexes: Jamal displayed above average reflexes in battle, as he was easily able to run long distances and deflect incoming arrows with his twin swords without getting hit or even grazed by them.

Enhanced Strength: While not possessing even a fifth of the strength of the individuals such as the Divine Generals, Jamal is very strong for a normal person.

Enhanced Speed: Jamal is shown to be fast enough to easily outpace a Galewind Horse.

Leadership: Despite his crude demeanor, Jamal is rather charismatic with imperial soldiers, and he is capable of making quick decisions and leading them, giving him the makings of a general.

Equipment
Twin Swords: Jamal masterfully wields twin swords in battle, using either for offense or defense as needed with surprising skill.

intro: Jorah Pendleton (ジョラー・ペンダルトン) was a Mid-Count of the Vollachia Empire and the first husband of Priscilla Barielle. He played a supporting role in The Tale of the Scarlet Princess.
appearance: Jorah was an old man with a decently tall stature, a wrinkled face with sky blue eyes and ashen grey hair. He was usually dressed in fine turquoise clothes and wore a hat of the same color pallet.
personality: Jorah was a cowardly man who didn't have the strength nor the ambition to behave as the Vollachian code demands of its denizens. Though he had a weak side, he also had a caring personality when it came to Priscilla despite their age difference, taking care of her for as long as he could until his untimely death.
history:
The Tale of the Scarlet Princess

Sometime later, Serena Dracroy sent her servants Balleroy Temeglyph and Miles to the Pendleton Estate in order to invite him and Priscilla to the Gladiator Island Ginunhive. While they were there, the gladiators attempted to spark a revolution that would render the island independent from the mainland, which later ended up failing thanks to the intervention of the Imperial Army.

Soon afterwards, Jorah was accused of attempting to overthrow the emperor of Vollachia, Vincent Vollachia, from his position. As a result, Goz Ralfon visited his manor in an attempt to take custody of him and Priscilla for a scheduled execution. Jorah fended Goz and his escorts off for Priscilla's sake, knowing that he would meet his end in just mere moments.

Hornet is a tall woman over two meters in height, towering over her opponents. She has short black hair with her sides shaved and colored light purple, deep purplish-red eyes, and tends to dress herself in a black and yellow body suit. Finally, before battle, Hornet always put on her two black and light-purple swords which she wears as prosthetics. The blades were so heavy that she was required to have at least two people put them on.

As a zombie, she possesses a vessel of earth, pale skin bereft of color, various cracks that run across her body, pitch-black sclera, and radiant golden irises.
personality: Hornet tended to often tease or flirt with people she either respected or was relatively close with, such as Al and Ubilk. However, in combat, Hornet was a nasty and brutal fighter who disregarded a fair fight. Contrary to expectations, Hornet's most fervent and desired wish was to gloriously die in combat against someone who could overpower her.
history: At some point in time, Hornet came to the Gladiator Island Ginunhive, where she spent the rest of her life fighting in the arena. In an incident four years prior to the uprising, all of the gladiators on the island fought a large witchbeast. The only two survivors of this battle were Hornet herself and Al. After the incident, she grew an interest in Al after having initially thought of him as small fry. Right before the uprising at Ginunhive, she joined Ubilk's rebellion in the hopes that she would get to fight Al. Although she easily overpowered him when they finally crossed blades, he used his ability in order to cheat death 79 times, nearly bleeding out in the process until Arakiya saved him. In the end, after Al returned and tried to defeat her 713 more times, totalling to 792 deaths in all, Hornet died a non-honorable death from poisoning after Al asked Arakiya to burn the body of a shinobi who used a technique known as the Poison Hand.
abilities_text:
Considerable Strength: Hornet is an extremely skilled fighter. Before meeting Olbart Dunkelkenn, Al described her as the third or fourth strongest person he had met in his life. Her strength was renowned enough that when she revived as an undead, Goz Ralfon considered her a worthy opponent.

Equipment: As she had lost her arms during her time on the Gladiator Island, Hornet wielded two giant prosthetic arm swords which she wielded as her main weapons.

name: Kafma Irulux
alias: Seventh (漆, Nana) ; Fighting Insect General (闘蟲将, Tōmushishō)
relatives: Unnamed father † ; Unnamed uncle
intro: Kafma Irulux (カフマ・イルルクス) is the Seventh ranking Divine General of the Sacred Vollachia Empire. He plays both a supporting and antagonistic role in Arc 7 and a supporting role in Arc 8.
appearance: Kafma is an average-sized man with brown skin, yellow eyes, short, bristling yellow-green hair, green tattoos on his arms and torso, a scar on his left eyebrow, and a red jewel-like object or body part on his forehead. Kafma is usually seen in a cropped sleeveless shirt that leaves his entire toned abdomen exposed, a yellow collar piece atop his shoulders, a grey cloak torn around the hem, black loose-fitting pants, a purple sash around his waist, and black shoes that leave the tops of his foot exposed. His facial expressions, physique, and the overall air he gives off have all been described to be as sharp as a wire.
personality:
Most of the time, Kafma acts professional and follows orders without many complaints. However, his temper is rather short, which makes him appear very tense and quick-to-blow-up, often causing him to make impulsive decisions mere moments after hearing an unwanted reply. When subjected to scenarios he isn't fond of, Kafma doesn't refrain from speaking his mind, be it to someone of a lower rank than him or to the very Divine Generals who command him. This being said, he is not above admitting his faults, and it is for this very reason that he believes himself unworthy of being one of the Nine Divine Generals despite being given the chance. As with most of the other members of the Imperial Army, he is also very patriotic, and he holds the Empire as well as the emperor in very high regards. Despite his short temper, Kafma is a virtuous man, and he holds shame as a result of his clan's involvement in a previous rebellion against the emperor and doesn't always hold himself in high regards, and he seeks to atone for his clan's involvement in their rebellion. Due to the way he was isolated growing up and considered a monster by everyone around him, Kafma came to understand that he did not want to feel the loneliness that could not be shared or understood by others.

Kafma is also very respectful towards those beneath him, something that made him immensely popular with other soldiers. He has also displayed this quality to people he believed to be citizens of the Empire. Before he realized that Natsuki Subaru’s group was actually his enemies, he displayed outward frustration on their behalf, stating that having an audience in the same place as the emperor when this ordinarily should not have happened was extremely troubling for them and highly discomfortable.

During combat, Kafma typically respects his opponent. During the Battle for the Imperial Capital, when he confronted Garfiel Tinzel, despite being on opposite sides, Kafma showed respect towards him, and he even expressed sadness when he was forced to try and implant an insect in him, claiming he did not like doing so but that he couldn't afford to let Garfiel win due to them being at war. He even disliked watching the agony he suffered as a result of his attack, and he told him somberly that he would remember his strength and prowess after he died. This being said, while duking it out with him and seeing Garfiel survive his deadly attack, Kafma displayed great joy at fighting him like an equal, and he became elated and smiled at being able to fight with everything he and his insects had. Likewise, despite him knowing that there are other commendable warriors in the Empire, he prides himself on being the bravest among them when in the face of death, and he will willingly push himself to the brink of death in order to assist his comrades.
history:
Kafma grew up as a member of the Insect Cage Tribe, a tribe where members would form symbiotic bonds with insects to gain power. Typically, most members of the tribe were meant to train their mind and body until the age of twelve, where they then receive their first insect. However, Kafma's father, the older brother of the tribe's chief who lost his mind due to being inferior to his younger brother, declared his son dead a few days after birth. In reality, Kafma was forced to take in his first insect a few days after his birth, and from then on, he was forced to take in one insect a year until he was twelve. At the age of twelve, his existence was discovered, his father was executed, and his uncle, the tribe's chief, chose to take responsibility for him. Despite being avoided and feared by others his age, he actively interacted with others, learned how to be a warrior from his chieftain uncle, and showed that he was not different from them by being tenacious in his interactions with all generations. Eventually, Kafma chose to take in a fourteenth insect in the face of opposition from tribe's elders, and after three days and nights of suffering, he took in the insect to become recognized as a full-fledged member of the Insect Cage Tribe. Thus, he became the strongest member the tribe had ever seen.

Although he tried to show a virtuous sense of camaraderie to his fellow tribe members, they could only see him as a monster, and he left his homeland to escape this perception. He found the people of the outside world to see him in the same way, and he came to believe that there was nowhere he could escape from being a monster by the time he became a General in the Imperial Army. Despite this, he was told to disregard that he was a monster by a comrade of his who thought of himself the same way, and he realized that he was okay with being considered one on the condition that he wasn't excluded from being understood by other people.

Roughly two to three months after the death of the former ninth ranking Diving General, Balleroy Temeglyph, a meeting was held in order to determine who would take his place. The fifth ranking Divine General, Goz Ralfon, quickly suggested Kafma as a suitable candidate due to his deep loyalty to the Empire and its emperor, as well as his very well-honed skills as a warrior which let him ascend to the rank of a Second-Class General at a very young age.

After Yorna Mishigure began a revolt, Kafma was released from his house arrest in order to handle the rebellion and prove his usefulness against the other candidate, Madelyn Eschart. However, before confronting the citizens of Chaosflame with Goz, Kafma ultimately concluded that he was not fit to become a Divine General and gave up his chances of taking the ninth seat after admitting that he was unqualified for the position to the emperor, Vincent Vollachia.
abilities_text:
Insect Cage Clan Attacks: As a member of the Insect Cage Clan, Kafma can masterfully use a variety of his Clan's trademark attacks and weapons. Although he originally had 32, he now holds a total of 33 different insects inside himself, each with unique abilities. As the relationship between Kafma and his insects are meant to be symbiotic, his insects typically require mana or lifeforce for the use of their power. However, should those prove insufficient, they will begin to eat flesh and blood instead. When being forced to use a vast quantity of insects to fire off thorns, bullets of light, and blades of wind simultaneously over an extended period of time without proper nourishment, he could feel the insects eating away at him from the inside, causing him intense pain. It is also possible to frighten the insects inside of him, preventing them from continuing to devour him from the inside. However, it is unknown whether or not this can affect Kafma's fighting strength.
Thorns: Kafma can skillfully fire countless purple thorn-like insects towards his enemies with extreme precision and speed, and the thorns can all be as long as a human arm. With this attack, Kafma easily breaches the distance between him and his enemies, skewering them before they have the chance to retaliate. Likewise, these thorns can come attached to strong vines. Kafma can use these insects both to protect people over a wide area and to grab onto multiple targets at once. He can also create footholds for his allies with this ability. The vines are often used in defense and support rather than for offense, though that doesn't mean they can't be used for offense. In fact, when the vines charge at an opponent, the pressure generated has been compared to an entire forest crashing into an opponent. It even has enough binding strength to hold back a Dragon of Valgren's level for a short period of time. This being said, as the thorns are part of the insect, if they get damaged, it can hurt the insect, causing them to scream out in pain, and as such there will be backlash.
thumb|right|250px|Kafma's wings.
Wings: Kafma can sprout six insect wings that enable him to fly. By making his speed vary with the movement of his wings, he can confuse his enemy by moving in and out of their awareness. He can also unleash slashes from his wings.
Ribs: By protruding his ribs from his body, the golden insect within can create a powerful attack that can hollow out anything his ribs aimed at, including the top of the reinforced walls of Lupugana's ramparts, and once the attack is done, his ribs close again. This being said, the use of this insect wears on Kafma's mind and body and is not meant for rapid firing.
Carapaces: Kafma can generate black carapaces one his arms like gauntlets and use them for self-protection like Garfiel's gauntlets.
Antennae: By transforming his shoulder bones into red antennae, he can fire them off like cannonballs that can send a transformed Garfiel flying backward. However, doing this causes Kafma an intense amount of pain, as he needs to snap the antennae off at the base to do this.
Other Insects: Among his collection of insects, some of them allow him to fire off blades of wind and bullets of light, among other abilities.
Insect Implantation: Aside from the technique he uses to implant insect inside his own body, Kafma can force his target to take an insect egg into their body through a special tube that he uses in close combat. When fighting, this tube allows a white insect to implant an egg through a wound that hatches inside the target's body. Since most people’s bodies are not capable of withstanding these insects, not to mention the intense preparation time required for the body to be able to adapt to their insect, it is not uncommon for his target to die in agony as the insect transfigures its host. Likewise, healing magic is ineffective against it as, while said magic can heal wounds, it cannot stop the transfiguration caused by the insects. He typically avoids using this technique unless he is forced to take his opponent down as quickly as possible. It is possible, however, to burn the insects that were implanted in the target’s body, albeit at the risk of burning oneself.
Pupa State: When Kafma decides to take another insect into his body, he can put himself into a cocoon-like state so that he can adapt to his new insect. It is unknown if this is inherent to Kafma or something shared among all the Insect Cage Clan members.

Enhanced Physicality: His body is incredibly durable. Whereas most of his clan can only handle a few of their insects, Kafma not only survived taking in his absurd number of insects, but he also managed to completely adapt to them. He is also highly resistant to pain, capable of withstanding the pain of his ribs bursting through his skin and his antennae being snapped off at the base. Even excluding this and the power that his insects provide him, Kafma has impressive physical might. He is capable of going head-to-head with someone as strong as Garfiel and dealing considerable damage to him. Similarly, he is capable of withstanding a beating from said warrior, even including being dragged through stone and his wings being torn to shreds, as well as withstanding the intense drawback from being forced to fight for more than fifty hours without food or drink and allowing his insects to devour his insides, all while continuously holding back an entire army.
Extra Organ: Kafma has developed an extra organ, not as a result of a particular insect but of the symbiosis between him and all of his insects. This organ can be exposed by Kafma's chest opening up. Once exposed, it can be used to send out a shockwave that is said to reduce any warrior into red mist.

name: Katya Aurélie
name_jp: カチュア・オーレリー
relatives: Jamal Aurélie (older brother) ; Picard Aurélie (eldest brother) ; Todd Fang (husband)
first_light_novel: The Land of Wolves / Death unto the Weak, No Mercy 4 (side story) ; Volume 30 (main story)
intro: Katya Aurélie (カチュア・オーレリー) is Jamal's sister and Todd's wife. She is a noble from the Aurélie family and has been prone to illnesses from a very young age. She played a supporting role in Arc 7 and Arc 8.
appearance:
Katya is a fair-skinned woman who possesses a weak and slender body resulting from her poor health. Much like her brother, she has messy and unkempt dark brown hair parted in two pigtails on both sides of her head and a rough blue-eyed gaze. She wears formal grey and white clothes with multiple decorations, including a yellow and cyan triangular emblem just below her neck, patterns composed of the same colors in stripes or diamonds, and a purple floral design at the bottom of her dress.

As a consequence of her constitution, Katya is required to use a wheelchair. The wheelchair's primary color is black, its cushions are purple, and the chair itself also has golden motifs alongside its edges. In order to facilitate her forwards or backwards navigation, Katya can turn the rims of the wheelchair in order to move around.
personality:
Katya's behavior while being held hostage in Berstetz Fondalfon's mansion is timid, fearful, and cautious. She appears cold, easily flustered, and quick to anger; often biting her fingernails, chewing on her lips, muttering to herself, and stammering when under stress. 

She habitually conceals her true emotions behind a mask of arrogant indifference, deliberately trying to appear harsh and cold to those around her. Despite her longing for companionship and love, she tends to distance herself from those who try to get close to her. Hence, it took persistent effort on Rem’s part to get Katya to become more comfortable and trusting around her. 

She isn’t bold and is often unsure if her own opinions are valid. She is terrified of death and desperately avoids dangerous situations, always trying to take the safest path. Although Katya cannot be described as a courageous person, her mentality is not one of cowardice but rather that of a kindhearted and peace-loving person who has been traumatized by her circumstances. When she sensed that Madelyn might harm Rem in anger, she found the strength to speak up and attempt to de-escalate the situation, despite being terrified of the divine general. Her actions were a testament to her selflessness, as she put herself at risk to protect her friend. 

Katya is possibly an example of the psychological toll that growing up in the Vollachia Empire, with its fervent belief in strength above all else, can have on an average person who isn’t blessed with physical strength. While in the mansion, she seems to be in a perpetual state of stress and anxiety, and is vigilant against revealing any weakness that could be exploited, especially when talking about those close to her. While her past remains mostly shrouded, her life thus far appears to have been one of great suffering and heartbreak, including the loss of those who were close to her. She attributes these misfortunes to her own terrible luck and incompetence, even blaming herself for any harm that befalls those around her. Her self-esteem is painfully low, viewing herself as selfish, helpless, and undeserving of love and companionship. Despite her fear of death and desire for survival, Katya's actions show compassion and concern for others. Though she refuses to admit it openly, she is deeply in love with Todd Fang and trusts him wholeheartedly.

name: Gustav Morello
previous_occupation: Governor of the Gladiator Island Ginunhive
relatives: Kurgan (relative)
intro: Gustav Morello (グスタフ・モレロ) is the former governor and Island Chief of the Gladiator Island Ginunhive. He played a supporting role in Arc 7 and Arc 8 as an advisor of sorts for the Pleiades Battalion. Following the Great Disaster, Gustav was promoted to a position that would keep him situated in Lupugana.
appearance: As a member of the Multi-Arm Tribe, Gustav bears blue skin, black eyes, and white hair in addition to the thick muscles, four arms, and towering height as is typical for his clan. He wears a dark grey uniform which is worn by others on Ginunhive and bears an armband with the symbol of the Empire on his left arm.
personality:
Gustav is an intelligent man who strives to be honest and transparent over being deceitful. Unlike his kin, who were predisposed to violence, he detests warfare, is nonviolent, and fears that his death will bring about nothing. He is fiercely loyal and grateful to Vincent Vollachia for his personality rather than his position, causing Gustav to not tolerate disrespect towards the emperor. Befitting of his position, he enforces order and fairness at Ginunhive to fit his assignment of training the minds and bodies to use Ginunhive's gladiators in case if an emergency were to plague the Empire.

Unlike the rest of the men in his tribe, which craved violence in emulation of Kurgan, Gustav prefers peace and maintaining said peace. Though most of the men died due to their nature, it was this nature of Gustav's that not only kept him alive but even allowed him to defend the rest of his people. He is also somewhat pacifistic compared to the rest of his tribe. After someone attacked his tribe in an effort to get rid of them, when the man and his subordinates were captured and held in place, despite being given the chance to take revenge for his fallen tribesmen, he decided not to kill him and instead have him sentenced to hard labor, much to the dismay of his people.

Gustav also respects old customs such as Sparka, as well as the people he considers his friends. It was for this reason rather than his loyalty that he followed Subaru alongside the other gladiators and soldiers in the Pleiades Battalion.
history:
In the past, Gustav resided at the Multi-Arm Tribe's homeland, where he read books, raised livestock, and protected the homes. He was viewed as a coward, for the other men of his tribe all sought valor in combat due to the legacy of the legendary Eight-Arms Kurgan. This path led to Gustav's grandfather, father, siblings, and friends dying for naught whilst sparring with others across the Empire. The tribespeople of the Multi-Arm Tribe increased their harsh treatment towards Gustav, as in their eyes, the one whom they perceived as a coward remained alive while their loved ones had all perished. On one fateful day, “bandits” who had believed all of the tribe's men were slain chose to assault the village. Its houses were burned, belongings were pilfered, women and children were killed for sport, and the tribespeople could do nothing to stop it. Gustav decided to spar with the “bandits” on his own, despite not having the strength to stand a chance against them. Just as he was about to lose his head, the Blue Lightning saved his life. 

After Gustav's life was saved, he was approached by the emperor of Vollachia, who questioned his beliefs and shared in them. The ringleader of the attack, a local feudal lord that had his private army dress up as bandits to eliminate the Multi-Arm Tribe, was arrested, and Gustav was chosen to decide his fate. Sensing that the lord was frightened of death, Gustav levied hard labor unto the man instead of death, much to the dissatisfaction of his living tribespeople. However, Gustav's dignity was recognized, and the emperor offered patronage to him. Over time, he carried out his duties and increased his court rank, and on the day he became a High Count, the emperor gave Gustav the order to work as the governor of the Gladiator Island Ginunhive. From then on, he began serving his newfound position as the Island Chief honestly, and under Gustav's leadership, the Gladiator Island would be remade from its previous lawlessness into a more orderly place where there were less unnecessary deaths.
abilities_text:
Enhanced Strength: As a member of the Multi-Arm Tribe, Gustav's physical strength is much greater than the average person's. Though not a warrior like the rest of his tribe, his physique alongside his shields makes him tough to push back.

Wise Leader: As his position demands, Gustav is excellent at commanding order, managing to keep an entire island full of ruffians and soldiers in order by providing them with their needs, invoking Sparka, and using the threat of a curse tool to keep people in check. The only people this does not seem to work on are extreme examples such as Subaru and Cecilus, but it still invokes respect in them.

Equipment:
Shields: Gustav has wielded shield that he has used in tandem with his arms in order to block strong blows.
Curse Tool: Gustav has a curse tool, created by Groovy Gumlet, embedded in his body that was originally used to curse everyone residing on the Gladiator Island, and anyone cursed by it who left its range would lose their life. It seems that he has some control of the curse it creates, as all those who joined the Pleiades Battalion were freed of the mark. However, even if he were to die, if the curse tool was still active while others were cursed by it, it would still kill them if they left its range or it left theirs.

name: Idra Missanga
intro: Idra Missanga (イドラ・ミサンガ) is a former gladiator at the Gladiator Island Ginunhive and a member of Subaru's Unit during the latter's stay on the island who later joined the Pleiades Battalion. He made his debut in Arc 7.
appearance: Idra is a man with rust-colored hair, golden eyes, and a pleasant face. He dresses in baggy rust-colored jeans, a white undershirt, and a golden necklace. Moreover, he also wears a matching headband and vest composed of purple and yellow designs.
personality: Idra is a socially anxious man who usually stays calm, level-headed, and honest to a fault. However, when he was put into danger at the Gladiator Island, he lied to the other members of his Unit, put up a determined front to look fearless, and attempted to control everyone around him. Despite coming off as a fraud, Idra's wish is to be a man who prevents shame from being brought onto his father and his family. For these reasons, Idra attempts to work hard and repay the debt he feels for those who choose to believe in him.
history:
Hailing from a small farming village in the northwestern part of the Sacred Vollachia Empire, Idra worked at a family mill that had been around since the time of his grandfather's grandfather. He was entrusted by the territory's lord to manage a local waterwheel built alongside a river in his village, and he was also in charge of milling all of the grains from the village. Although his family was privileged, they chose to help fellow villagers in times of need and acted humble, which Idra learned for himself.

One day, Idra met a man at a travelling mercenary who would come to the village's local bar and came to know him over time, listening to the man's stories and holding a yearning for the lifestyle of those outside his village. The man eventually expressed his interest in Idra's cousin, and Idra himself chose to set up a meeting between the man and his cousin out of kindness. This kind gesture was short-lived, as the pair would attempt to steal Idra's family business by falsifying the results of his milling to the village. Although he attempted to convince the village of his innocence, they chose to plant preparations for an insurrection within his home because they prioritized profits that the mercenary and Idra's cousin brought, and Idra was brought to a trial before the village's lord. Failing to prove his innocence without anyone to believe in him, Idra was punished and sent to the Gladiator Island by slave traders.

name: Hiain Yatz
intro: Hiain Yatz (ヒアイン・ヤッツ) is a former gladiator at the Gladiator Island Ginunhive and a member of Subaru's Unit during the latter's stay on the island who later joined the Pleiades Battalion. He made his debut in Arc 7.
appearance: Hiain is a green lizard human who has blue eyes, long nails, and a tail. He wears a dark yellow cloak attached in place by a belt.
personality: Hiain is loud, impulsive, easily frightened, and a short-tempered sweet-talker. He is a scaredy-cat quick to express fear or rage when put in an unfavorable situation, which causes him to create his own problems. Hiain once participated in a fight and ran away to escape the consequences, and his impulsiveness caused his friends to abandon him for their own safety. He later convinced himself that they were cowards in spite of knowing that it was in his nature to take advantage of people and attempted to justify himself regardless. Although he often runs away when put into trouble to save himself, there are some cases where Hiain will attempt to help others.
abilities_text: Camouflage: As a lizard human, Hiain has the ability to change the color of his scales and appear as if he blends in with his surroundings. Hiain's ability to remain camouflaged is reliant on staying motionless. However, due to his nature, he tends to get frightened and move out of fear.

intro: Jawsrough (ジョズロ) is a former gladiator at the Gladiator Island Ginunhive. He later became a member of the Pleiades Battalion.
appearance: Jawsrough is a man with dark skin, thick lips, ashen brown hair, and a single left eye. His right eye is covered by a white scar, and behind the closed eyelid is an artificial prosthetic eye made of wood. However, his replacement eye does not substitute for the eyeball he lost.
personality: Jawsrough had an infamous celebrity-like reputation at Ginunhive as a “lone wolf”. He disagreed with the notion of the Gladiator Island being a utopia for savages where physical strength is esteemed, a conception he believed many people possessed. His reputation was not simply because he did not associate with others. Instead of following the established order of trusting other people in a Unit with his life, Jawsrough discarded any gladiator he viewed as a despicable criminal and felt at ease with cutting one down if they were not worth looking out for. Nevertheless, under the surface of Jawsrough's outward cynical attitude, he holds intense expectations for other people regardless of their age or appearance.
history:
Brotherhood of Pleiades
Before being sent to Ginunhive for unknown reasons, Jawsrough was a mason. There, he became known as a lone wolf for his mentality and actions. At an unknown time in the future, Subaru arrived at the Gladiator Island, and Jawsrough was the last person who he convinced to become his comrade. In order to help Subaru compete against Gustav, Jawsrough used his skills as a mason by creating a board and pieces for the game of Reversi that the two used for their Sparka match.

name: Izmail
alias: Giant Eye (巨眼, Kyogan)
intro: Izmail (イズメイル) was a member of the Cyclops Tribe. Once considered to be the hope of his tribe, he participated in a battle at the Imperial Capital of Lupugana, but was ultimately slain with a sweeping fire attack from Arakiya.
appearance: Izmail was a strong man with a large blue-colored eye. As a zombie, he possessed a vessel of earth, pale skin bereft of color, various cracks that ran across his body, pitch-black sclera, and a radiant golden iris that replaced his sole blue eye. Izmail's form evolved after sustaining lethal damage, causing him to gain tentacle-like fingers, a swelled frame larger than his original physique, and numerous limbs with various lengths that rapidly multiplied across his body.
personality: A prideful and ambitious warrior, Izmail relished honor in combat. He held no favor for people he believed were cowards or fools who desecrated the battlefield and thought of them as enemies.
abilities_text:
Eye (眼, Gan): Like the other members of the Cyclops Tribe, Izmail possessed a single eye with multiple abnormal powers. Notably, this allowed Izmail to “switch” his sight and perceive the emotions of people on the battlefield in colors. Individuals with a strong fighting spirit had a red light, those who were abundant in anxiety had a yellow light, and those who harbored panic or fear had a blue light.

Equipment: Izmail wielded an enormous and ardently forged battle axe that was taller than his own body. He carried the axe on his back and used it to eliminate his foes on the battlefront. According to Todd Fang, Izmail's skill was so great that he had the potential to become a Second-Class General in the Imperial Army.

name: Gudda Dialmo
alias: Tiger Hunter (虎狩, Tora Kari)
intro: Gudda Dialmo (グッダ・ディアルモ) is a Second-Class General of the Sacred Vollachia Empire.
appearance: Gudda is a large and muscular man with white scar marks made by claws left across his upper body.
personality: Gudda is a brave man who feels pride at being a Second-Class General, and he is genuinely loyal to his emperor, to the point that he was enraged at the rebels for being traitors.. He is willing to put his life on the line in battle. He trained his soldiers with such a mentality that they would not lose their wills to fight. After his defeat by the Pleiades Battalion during the Battle for the Imperial Capital, his self-confidence and pride as a general were wiped away.
history: While Gudda was still a Third-Class General, he engaged in warfare with a group of tiger humans who were tyrannizing a part of Vollachia. He witnessed his superior, a Second-Class General, being crushed to pieces before his eyes. Despite Gudda's distress at this, his will to fight remained adamant and he threw himself into combat with the enemy leader who killed the Second-Class General, ultimately succeeding in decimating them and their faction. As a result of the clash, his torso was scarred by claws from the tiger humans, which led to him to gain his alias, the Tiger Hunter. He was also eventually promoted to Second-Class General.
abilities_text: Equipment: Gudda wields two metal clubs that weigh nearly a hundred kilograms each.

name: Hayden Garo
race: Beast Human/Lion Human and Human Hybrid
intro: Hayden Garo (ヘイデン・ガロ) is a demi-human separatist in the Kingdom of Lugunica.
appearance: Hayden is a wild-looking man with slicked-back, dark blonde hair, a well-groomed beard, and blue eyes. He has a tall, strong frame, as well as sharp nails and teeth. In addition, Hayden has a scar in the form of a claw mark above his left eye that was carved onto him by Frederica’s fingernails.
personality:
Hayden is a conceited and belligerent man who prides himself on his rare blood. He has a rigid, domineering personality, unshakeable beliefs, and the tendency to utilize force when he does not have his way. For unknown reasons, Hayden utterly despises humans, going so far as to dub them “inferiors”. His ambition is to create a country where all humans are exterminated and he is crowned king. He also has a habit of meticulously filing his nails.

After discovering Frederica possessed rare blood and meeting with her, Hayden began to desire her not only for her blood but also for her body, strong-willed spirit, and judiciousness, offering her compliments on each of these traits. In spite of his craving for her, he was unwilling to tolerate when she spoke her mind and disagreed with his mindset toward humans.
history:
Born as a halfbeast demi-human with rare blood, Hayden would eventually come to determine that humans were inferior beings who needed to be exterminated, and he sought to take the places of the demi-human leaders in the Demi-Human War and create a new nation in his image where he would be king. To achieve this, he started working with Leonardo Baroness to discover the secrets of rare blood. One day, Hayden found Frederica Baumann, a fellow halfbeast who also had rare blood, and plotted with Leonardo to manipulate the lightbugs of Costuul and orchestrate an incident in the city that allowed him to kidnap her for his plans.

Hayden briefly met Frederica near of one of Costuul's magicreation tool factories and caused a lightbug within a magicreation tool to go haywire. When Frederica and Garfiel reported the incident to Mayor Leno Rex, he caused the collapse of the city hall with a lightbug using a larger magicreation tool and successfully kidnapped Frederica when she was alone, taking her to a cave he and Leonardo had made as their base. He then divulged both his philosophy his reason for kidnapping Frederica to her and planned to take her back to his “castle” once Leonardo finished working with her blood. However, the duo was interrupted by Clind and Garfiel Tinzel, who discovered the cave by pursuing a trail of blood Frederica left. Hayden and Garfiel fought, ending in the former’s loss. Following his loss to Garfiel, Hayden escaped from the cave where the two had battled and made himself known to Frederica when she was by herself, admitting to her that although he would retreat for the day, he intended on returning so as long as she continued to participate with her camp in the Royal Selection. He proceeded to make his escape, but not before allowing Frederica to scar the region above his left eye as a token of gratitude for remembering his name.
abilities_text: Beastification (獣化, Kemonoka): As a halfbeast of lion human lineage, Hayden has the ability to transform himself into a large lion beast.

name: Gwain Merette
name_jp: グウェイン・メレテー
nickname: The Faker (食わせ物, Kuwase-mono)
affiliation: Kingdom of Lugunica ; Chamber of Commerce
relatives: Gwain (father)
intro: Gwain Merette (グウェイン・メレテー) is a representative of the Kingdom of Lugunica's western regions for the country's Chamber of Commerce.
appearance: Gwain is a scrawny man who is unconcerned with maintaining appearances. He has long, light-brown hair, gold eyes, an unshaven beard, and a face that could cause him to be mistaken for a woman, if he would shave his chin.
personality: Gwain is a man of great tolerance with a keen intuition. When he was younger, he had a more aggressive attitude that was influenced by his circumstances.
history:
Once Upon a Time in Lugunica II
Gwain was born as a werewolf by the name of Alagar (アラガル, Aragaru). Due to his lineage, he faced peril from Vollachia's policy of executing all people of wolf human descent. He came under the service of Galahau Dracroy and was tasked with assassinating his daughter, Serena Dracroy, along with three other assassins. While a fugitive, Alagar singlehandedly managed to vanquish an entire fortress and escaped to Lugunica's Royal Capital, where he was subjugated by Marcos Gildark. An emissary from the Empire, Serena, was sent to retrieve Alagar and bring him to certain death. However, the group transporting Alagar to Vollachia was ambushed by the other assassins sent to kill Serena. Quickly deducing that Alagar was one of the assassins, Serena made an offer to aid him in faking his death and continue surviving if he chose to spare her life and stop working with Galahau, to which he accepted, making a promise with her and later Roswaal to not use his Beastification again. After the incident, Alagar took on the name of his dead father, Gwain, and was employed by the Fellow family.

The Three Idiots Set Out! Cursed Goddess Statue Episode
In the years following his employment to the Fellow family, Gwain managed to become a representative of Lugunica's Chamber of Commerce. He began to hold lavish auctions for the wealthy to acquire rare items, such as meteors. One night, when holding an auction attended by a crossdressing trio of Subaru, Otto, and Garfiel, some of the items were stolen. The case was eventually solved, and in the end, Clind managed to retrieve a statue missing from Gwain's inventory for Roswaal.

Petra's Emilia Camp Struggle
During the events of Arc 5, Gwain took part in the Western Margrave Domain Meeting.
abilities_text:
Divine Protection (加護, Kago): As a half-wolf human, Gwain possesses the Divine Protection of Ambushing (騙し討ちの加護, Damashiuchi no Kago). Although its exact effects are unknown, it enables werewolves to be difficult to find by other people.

Beastification (獣化, Kemonoka): As a halfbeast of half-wolf human lineage, Gwain has the ability to transform himself into a large dark brown wolf beast, though he does not make use of this transformation due to his promise with Serena Dracroy and Roswaal L. Mathers.

name: Lehare Yvsant
first_light_novel: Sword Demon Battle Ballad: Finale of the Eight Arms
intro: Lehare Yvsant (レハレ・イヴサント) is the governor of Garkla.
appearance: Lehare's appearance was never described.
personality: In the past, Lehare abused the captive workers he supervised and had a sadistic desire to inflict pain on them when he could. He grew a respect for Kurgan in the years following his defense of the city, despite the Eight Arms having been a prisoner he viewed with scorn and pity.
history: Lehare was a supervisor of the construction of Garkla's city walls. Unaware of the legend of the Eight Arms due to it fading into obscurity, Lehare saw Kurgan as an easy target to direct his sadism towards. When Regulus Corneas arrived within the city of Garkla and instantly destroyed a third of it, the then-governor and their aides were caught and killed in the destruction. As a result, Lehare was appointed as the interim governor by a young prince known for his wisdom who happened to be in Garkla for an inspection, obeying his instructions. Although bewildered why the prince sought the Eight Arms, he affirmed the old hero's presence in the city. In the aftermath of the incident, Lehare, who officially became the governor of Garkla, as well as the other survivors of the city, passed on that Kurgan had emerged victorious. He restored the Demon Cleavers that had been destroyed in the clash between the Eight Arms and the Sin Archbishop of Greed, displaying them on the top floor of the great fortress as a symbol of the Fortified City's sturdiness.

name: Hamayal Wesmi
intro: Hamayal Wesmi (ハマヤル・ウエズミ) was a shinobi from the Vollachia Empire who was tasked to assassinate Priscilla Barielle.
appearance: Hamayal's appearance was never described.
personality: As a shinobi, Hamayal had been perfected as a puppet who lacked a sense of free will, focusing single-mindedly on tasks assigned to him without question. He regarded the task of assassinating a Royal Selection Candidate as the culmination of his work and something to celebrate at the end of his time as a shinobi. Because he adhered so carefully to the idea of acting with the idealized idea of a shinobi with resolve as he and the others from his village believed, he was enraged upon learning of Yae Tenzen's betrayal, which quickly turned to alarm when he realized she had been broken. After his mind was shattered by Al, although he was reduced to a pawn who did as the knight told, he failed to become the same type of loyal pawn Yae was.
history:
In his childhood, Hamayal met and began coexisting with his Phantom Wolf. At some point, he completed his training in the shinobi village and became a shinobi. With his Phantom Wolf at his side, he found prolonged success in the livelihood of assassination. He had known Yae Tenzen while she was developing a reputation as a genius prodigy in their village, lamenting that someone with her temperament had the essence of a shinobi despite her personality deviating from his ideal expectations.

After Yae's failure to assassinate Priscilla Barielle, a suicide squad comprised of Hamayal and nine other shinobi were tasked by Chisha Gold with achieving what the Crimson Sakura could not. Using the nine shinobi as a decoy, he was the one entrusted with the duty of assassinating Priscilla while her knight, Al, was dealing with the others. His plan came to a halt when Al intercepted him in the hidden passages under the Barielle Manor. Realizing his comrades were dead, he set his Phantom Wolf on Al. However, he was then attacked by Yae, who survived her failed assassination attempt, having been made to know "terror" and broken by Al, becoming his pawn in the process. The Phantom Wolf suddenly become subordinate to Al, and feeling anxiety, he attempted to attack the knight, only to fall victim to the Aggressor side of his Authority. On Al's orders, he sent his Phantom Wolf through the letter that was to report how the mission had went. The Phantom Wolf was set on Chisha as soon as he opened said letter, but Cecilus Segmunt, who was in the room with him, eradicated it in a flash, ending Hamayal's life.
abilities_text:
Phantom Wolf (幻狼, Genrō): A shadow beast with a will of its own that Hamayal coexisted with. Having fed his shadow to the beast as a child, it grew up alongside him until it took on the form of a humongous quadruped with the silhouette of a wolf, lacking any proper body parts like eyes or a nose. Losing his own shadow, the Phantom Wolf would fold itself into appearing as Hamayal's shadow and had the ability to break off independently from it to attack a prey or sneak into all sorts of crevices, returning to appearing as his shadow once finished with a task. He cooperated with his Phantom Wolf to easily execute any enemy he came across. However, Hamayal's utilization of the Phantom Wolf came at a price. Because the lives of a shadow beast and a shadow master are connected with each other, if one perishes, the other will follow. When destroyed, a Phantom Wolf disperses as a phantom would. Hamayal's Phantom Wolf was disposed of by Cecilus Segmunt, immediately ending his own life.

Shinobi Techniques (シノビの術技, Shinobi no Jutsugi): As a shinobi, Hamayal was apt in the use of shinobi techniques. The only skill he displayed was a technique of tightening his muscles to stop his body's bleeding.

name: Ia
relatives: Julius Juukulius (contractor) ; Kua, Aro, Iku, In, and Nes ("sisters")
intro: Ia (イア) is a spirit of the fire attribute that is contracted with Julius Juukulius. Once a quasi-spirit, she managed to evolve into a proper spirit during the events of Arc 6.
appearance:
As a spirit, Ia has a small, red spherical form that emanates red light.

In the Re:Sacrificing Life In Another World from Zero IF story, as Lumera, she has taken on a human form, appearing as a tall, beautiful woman with flowing red hair and red eyes, a curvaceous figure, and a flashy, extravagant red dress.
personality: As a quasi-spirit, Ia's thoughts are comparable to that of a young child. Although Ia and the other five contracted spirits are unable to understand words, Julius is able to transmit emotions, his impressions of people, and other similar things to them. As the six spirits became Julius's contracted spirits after a fierce fight with many other lesser spirits, they have almost become like sisters who endured a shared struggle together, and so they only bicker on occasion.
history: Because of Julius's Divine Protection of Gathering Spirits, a number of lesser spirits found it easy to like his nature, and they sought to have contracts with him. Unbeknownst to Julius, a fierce fight ensued to decide who would become his contracted spirits, with Ia, Kua, Aro, Iku, In, and Nes being the six lesser spirits who were victorious in the end. They proceeded to diligently guard Julius from then on, at some point becoming quasi-spirits. Eventually, when Julius was at the age where he was ready to make contracts with them, with a simple “Nice to meet you”, he formed contracts with the six of them.
abilities_text:
Magic/Spiritual Arts
Ia is a spirit that commands fire mana and can thus use fire magic. As Julius's contracted spirit, Ia makes use of her magic to aid him when necessary. She and Julius's other spirits each have appropriate crystals for themselves, where they reside when they are not materialized.

Spells:
thumb|240x240px|Ia creating a barrier to protect Subaru.
Barriers: Ia is able to quickly generate barriers to protect against damage such as explosives. While it is unknown just how large her barriers can become or the extent of damage they can withstand, they were able to protect someone as weak as Natsuki Subaru from a relatively large explosion and left him with only minor injuries.
thumb|250px|Julius Using Ul Gora.

Combined Spells:
Ul Gora (ウル・ゴーラ): Julius can call on Ia and Aro to produce a powerful magical fire storm by combining both fire and wind magic.

Unique Spells:
thumb|250px|Julius Using Al Clarista.
Clarista (クラリスタ): Julius imbues his sword with the power of his six spirits, empowering it. Clarista and its different levels are Julius's original magic.
Al Clarista (アル・クラリスタ): Al Clarista allows Julius to imbue his sword with the power of his six quasi-spirits (after his fight with Reid Astrea, he can do that with his newly bloomed spirits), cladding his blade in a brilliant rainbow light. According to him, when this spell is in use, he can cut almost everything with his sword, no matter the toughness. Julius displayed this ability two times, roughly half a year before the start of the Royal Selection on his diplomatic journey to the Sacred Vollachia Empire. There, he fought the First and Ninth ranking Divine Generals on separate occasions, and managed to break the former's 5th best sword, and kill the latter. Julius is also capable of using the long-range version of Clarista where the spell takes the form of a beam of pure destructive energy. The light is capable of cutting through anything and everything in its path. After Julius reformed his contract with his quasi-spirits, the power and range of the attack greatly increased, surprising even Julius. During his battle with the Ninth ranking Divine General of the Vollachia Empire, Julius used this spell to melt away the General's spear and pierce his chest, killing him.
thumb|250px|Julius using Al Clauzeria.
Al Clauzeria (アル・クラウゼリア): When Al Clauzeria is casted, six different colored spirits start circling around Julius and join into one whirling rainbow-hued vortex of light which is shot out from the tip of his sword. Immediately following the impact of the rainbow light, the torrent of light explodes in a sizeable shock wave that sends his opponents flying. The wall as well as the vortex are composed of six elements, which are able to repel any sort of magic that is casted against it as well as any and all physical attacks. Furthermore, in the novelization of Julius' duel with Petelgeuse, the rainbow shockwave started expanding directly from his own body, rather being shot out from the tip of his sword, easily purifying away close to a hundred unseen hands that enveloped the Knight from all sides, just seconds prior. Despite the small difference in execution, both versions have the same effect. Following the evolution of his quasi-spirits into spirits, this attack has enough power to completely wipe away one of the heads of a Dragon the caliber of Valgren. By tweaking the spell, Julius can use this spell to create a dome-like barrier around himself and his targets. Ordinarily, this is used for defense, but it can also be used to trap aerial opponents such as Balleroy Temeglyph near the ground. Following the evolution of his spirits, his barrier has shown to be able to extend to cover up to half of the entirety of the Fortified City of Garkla.
Al Cranvel (アル・クランヴェル): Al Cranvel is a secret technique Julius developed long ago but never managed to properly utilize due to his lack of experience. After he made new contracts with his newly-bloomed spirits, Julius called upon their power and clad himself in their sixfold power, greatly increasing his speed and overall power. To the other party, Julius appeared as if he was swallowed alive by a rainbow. This sword skill is noted as Julius' ultimate attack. Debuting this trump card during his final duel with legendary Reid Astrea, it played a vital role in helping him overcome the obstacle known as the first generation's Sword Saint.

Conditional Spells:
thumb|240x240px|Subaru using "Rental Goa" against Petelgeuse.
Rental Goa (レンタル・ゴーア, Rentaru Gōa): Not being one of the spells Subaru made after forming a formal contract with Beatrice, this was instead a Goa used on the spot during the former's provisional contract with Ia, hence why he chose to call it a "rental" spell. It was used against Petelgeuse Romanée-Conti to set him on fire after being doused in oil.

name: Hogey Marshepo
relatives: Unnamed wife (deceased) ; Azla Eastern
intro: Hogey Marshepo (ホギー・マルシュポ) is a painter and the father of Azla Eastern.
appearance: Hogey is a thin, middle-aged man with a beard.
personality: Hogey is a man who is not above engaging in the creation of forgeries to support his family. He has an interest in forging famous paintings to see if he is capable of recreating them. Having said that, he believes that his reproductions fall short compared to the original works.
history:
When Hogey was younger, he met a woman and had a son, Azla Eastern, with her. However, due to his financial difficulties as an unsuccessful painter, he was unable to support her, and so the couple could not marry. He was eventually approached by Amilét Megis, who requested him to create more forgeries to support her business, to which he accepted. Thus, Hogey was responsible for creating countless forgeries of numerous famous art pieces, and was eventually able to marry his lover and support his family. After Hogey's wife passed away, Azla learned the truth of his father's profession, and was not only angered by the fact that he had been raised by tainted money, but that his father was not using his talent to create his own original works. He attempted to tell Hogey to quit, but failed to make him budge. As a result, Azla began to expose Hogey's forgeries by reporting them to their owners. When this did not give him his desired result, he decided to report it Baron Nico Olsen, the owner of one of the counterfeits.

Two years after the death of Hogey's wife, a forgery of the Sleeping Miderine, a distinguished work of art that was painted over a century ago, had arrived in the hands of Baron Nico Olsen. Though he was initially angered to learn it was a forgery, he respected Azla's plea and became intrigued by Hogey's circumstances. Baron Olsen hatched a scheme to aid Azla, including preemptively staging a kidnapping to protect him from being targeted. Olsen also decided to assess Anastasia Hoshin by having her evaluate the piece, and she determined that it was a fake. After researching the case, Anastasia, Julius, and Joshua found Hogey, who explained his past. Having created forgeries for over twenty years, Hogey did not believe he could change. However, Joshua spoke up and conveyed that Hogey had enough talent to create art that rival renowned works, and that his son wanted him to create his own paintings. Joshua then began to explain that Azla had been abducted, but when he started the story by mentioning Olsen, Anastasia realized that Hogey's son was safe and the baron was the "mastermind" behind the abduction. Afterwards, Hogey and Azla had a reunion.

name: Meckart Karsten
name_jp: メッカート・カルステン
relatives: Helena Karsten (wife) ; Crusch Karsten (daughter)
intro: Meckart Karsten (メッカート・カルステン) is Crusch Karsten's father and the former head of House Karsten.
appearance: Meckart has amber eyes. Despite trying to look dignified with his eyes, his drooping eyebrows and gentle looks prevent it. Unlike his wife, Helena Karsten, he has nothing in common with his daughter except for their eye color.
personality:
Much like his daughter, he is a highly loyal, honest, and dutiful man. However, in contrast to her fiery traits, he is a much more mild mannered individual who often errs on caution. That said, his convictions are no less weaker than Crusch’s which makes his disposition more well rounded than her.

He is often seen under a lot of stress, due in part to his daughter’s behavior despite her position, as seen during a conversation with Ferris.
history:
Ex 1
Around the time of his daughter’s 17th birthday, Meckart was conflicted about how to get his daughter to attend her party while wearing a dress and acting as a noble daughter’s should, not wishing her to be looked down upon or mocked for her demeanor and habit of wearing men’s clothing. He stated his concerns to Ferris, and soon after, he witnessed a mock duel between Crusch and Prince Fourier Lugunica. When Fourier won and managed to get Crusch to concede to wearing a dress, Meckart was grateful to him.

On the night of her birthday, however, a village in the duchy was under attack by the Great Rabbit. Deciding to leave his daughter in the dark about the attack, he led a unit to confront the great witchbeast and save as many people as he could. Contrary to his wishes, however, Crusch found out, and she found her way to the battle, where she successfully managed to drive it away, which would end up earning herself the nickname “The Valkyrie”. After this incident, Meckart retired and passed his title onto his daughter, entrusting her his duties.

After the Subjugation of the White Whale, it is rumored that Meckart has returned to his post to assist his memoryless daughter in running the duchy.

intro: Marcos Gildark (マーコス・ギルダーク) is the captain of the Royal Guard and the Knight Commander. Although he only played a minor role in Arc 3 during the Royal Selection Ceremony, he later plays a supporting role in Arc 10.
appearance: Marcos has a chiseled face that is often compared to a boulder or a craggy cliff. He is a large man with an abundancy of muscles which are usually concealed underneath his armor. Thanks to his bulging muscles, his neck and shoulders are impossibly thick, in comparison to an average person's. His eyes are blue, and his green-colored close-cropped hair is cut into the shape of a square. Unlike most members of the Knights of Lugunica, Marcos wears a suit of plate armor with gold trimmings. Transfixed to his waist is a sword he uses in battle. Overall, his appearance exudes the martial spirit of a disciplined warrior.
personality:
Marcos is a stern and strict man who takes his position as the captain of the Royal Guard seriously. He is composed and brave at all times, allowing him to calmly deal with emergencies. In addition to being an astute thinker, he is also surprisingly thoughtful and perceptive which has allowed him to look for his soldiers on and off the field. He is respectful towards others, shown to apologize for any disrespect shown either purposefully or unintentionally, and he does not allow bias or emotions to cloud his judgment or interfere with his work, even if it includes effectively detaining a person of importance. He is also not unwilling to calmly explain any circumstances in relation to said detainment, though he is also described as being immoveable in this regard. Likewise, though he bears no prejudice towards any of his knights and will treat them fairly, he will not tolerate his knights being disrespectful, especially in tense situations, willing to use his own aura to silence them if necessary.

This being said, while he typically acts stoically and with respect and not the type of person to act in blind rage, for those he despises, he has no issue glaring at them with a certain level of hostility while holding back his rage, chiding them for their behavior, and if given an appropriate chance, he is not unwilling to unleash a vicious beating upon his target of scorn, and he will keep pummeling that person until they are unwilling to keep fighting. In particular, he dislikes how people such as Heinkel Astrea continue to drown themselves in their sorrows and continue to waste away what little they have, as well as their willingness to drag others down with them if necessary, and not only does he show visible disappointment in such people if they refuse to grow up and move past such hardships, but he will actively tell people associated with them to refrain from letting themselves be used by such people.

As one might expect from his neutral and stoic standing, because of his position as the commander of the Royal Guard, he believes that it is undesirable for him to back a single Royal Candidate. This being said, in times where the state of affairs becomes undesirable, Marcos is willing to go against the government if need be and act on his own, working with those very people if need be. Likewise, he believes that if the rot cannot be removed without bloodshed, then one must not shy away from it, and he will even allow himself to leave his station and place his trust in his knights that they know why they swing their swords.

Roughly 15 years before the events of the main story, Marcos held a strong grudge against the Royal Knights, despite being one of them. According to him, all he did was imprison poor and starving people, and he believed that jail should be a place where people's hearts change for better. The unfairness he was forced to participate in resulted in Marcos joining The Brotherhood, which he was originally ordered to suppress on a mission. This allowed him to give people from the slums hope and help them change their lives.
history:
Before the start of the main story, Marcos was approached by Crusch Karsten who voiced her request to accept Ferris into the Royal Guard and make a knight out of him. Due to Ferris' unparalleled healing magic, he accepted him among the ranks of Royal Guards and employed him many times in the following year.

The Travelogue of the Finest
Not long after the collective deaths of the entire Royal Family, Marcos assigned Reinhard van Astrea, Julius Juukulius, and Ferris to accompany the two Council of Wise Men members Miklotov McMahon and Bordeaux Zergev to the neighboring Empire of Vollachia. Roughly a month after their return, he arranged a proxy fight between the Lugunican Sword Saint Reinhard van Astrea and the Vollachian First ranking Divine General Cecilus Segmunt.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
Marcos is currently regarded as the second strongest fighter in Lugunica, only falling behind Reinhard, with strength said to be enough that, if he wasn't overshadowed by Reinhard, his name would be the one that rivals the strongest people from each nation. He is powerful enough to make someone of Garfiel Tinzel's level wary, and even though he has enough control over his aura to direct it at specific parties, said aura was powerful enough that when he accidentally felt it, Garfiel had to fight off his instincts to beastify and fight.

Physical Traits/Flow Method
Expert Swordsman: Although it is unclear just how skilled he is, his skill is such that those who witness it can attest to it to his unbelievable might.

Incredible Strength: Marcos's physical strength is incredible. By placing his hand against a sheathed sword, he can easily prevent even a sliver of it from being unsheathed, and with just a single strike of his bare hands, he can cause immense damage to whomever he hits. He can easily swing a grown man around like a doll, and by simply placing his fist in a person's mouth and opening his hand, he can easily break a person's jaw and remove teeth. Even Heinkel Astrea, whose constitution is among the sturdiest, felt himself on the verge of death after being assaulted by his might.

Techniques
Fa Jin (発勁, Hakkei): Marcos can use fa jin, a martial arts technique that deals a single crushing blow to the internal organs behind muscle. Marcos utilized his skill to readily absorb and perfectly replicate this technique from Roswaal after having only seen him use it twice.

Magic
At present, it is unclear what attribute Marcos has an affinity for, and it is unknown how proficient he is with ordinary magic. This being said, he seems to have enough knowledge of magic that he can work together with the likes of Ram to rewrite spells that prevent magic from being used to spells that can prevent noise from escaping a specified area.

Forbidden Art (禁術, Kinjutsu): Marcos has an unnamed forbidden art that was attached to him through an El Goa cast by Roswaal during an incident where assassins were targeting the life of an envoy from Vollachia. It creates a magical armor made of grey, bedrock-like stones that he can use to defend a specific part of his body, or covers his whole body, increases his height to three meters, and makes him immune to things like poison gas.

Other
Discerning Eye: By making his blue eyes glimmer slightly, Marcos can check for dangerous magic reactions and/or any equipment people may have.

Stealth: In spite of his hulking frame and the fact the wears heavy armor, Marcos is capable of moving silently and catching experienced fighters like Heinkel Astrea by surprise.
