previous_affiliation: Four Great Spirits ; Kingdom of Lugunica
relatives: Chap (temporary contractor)
intro: Melakuera (メラクェラ) was the Arbitrator, a former member of the Four Great Spirits. He was a judgmental spirit who viewed Emilia's existence as a sin because she possessed the same physical characteristics as the Witch of Envy, leading him to try and exterminate her. Seven years prior to the beginning of the story, he was eliminated by Puck in a battle that came to be known as the Day of Red Earth and Sky.
appearance: Melakuera did not have a true corporeal body, but he had the ability to possess bodies and split his form. In his unadorned form, Melakuera appeared as a red clump of heat and energy. But, when he manifested himself into a familiar form, Melakuera took the form of a winged horse completely covered by crimson flames. All of Melakuera's bodies appeared as fiery horses, even when one of his bodies had possessed Chap. Melakuera ended up turning him into half a manifestation of a man garbed in flames, and half of a fiery horse.
personality:
Arbitrator Melakuera cared about nothing more than maintaining peace and order. He cared greatly about the ancient rules he adhered to, as he refused to break them even if they were an inconvenience to him. He neglected to intervene in the sacred contracting between Emilia and Puck despite the problems he likely knew it would cause him. He was willing to go to any lengths in order to protect the world from darkness, even if it meant sacrificing the lives of innocents to do so. Melakuera seemed to only care about inflicting his brand of justice when the world was in danger, as he cared little for minor injustices committed by petty criminals. He was even willing to work with criminals to further his goals, such as when he formed a contract with the bandit Chap.

He felt no remorse towards the victims he deemed as necessary losses and would not hesitate to execute those who stood in the way of his warped sense of justice. During his pursuit of the half-elf Emilia, Melakuera mercilessly executed the lesser spirits that came to her defense and released the venom of the Black Serpent, knowing it would wreak havoc upon the entire forest and the innocent people that populated it. The Arbitrator spoke in a very robotic, matter of fact manner, favoring the archaic pronouns thou (汝 nanji) and mineself (我 ware). His voice reflects his role as an arbitrator of the world, not wasting any time on connectives or other basic sentence structuring.

Despite his long life, Melakuera still suffered from the same blind paranoia that afflicted lesser beings. For instance, he, like the common folk of the world, showed abject fear and revulsion to silver-haired half-elves as he believed they were descendants of the infamous Witch of Envy who destroyed half of the world centuries ago. So firm was his disgust towards silver-haired half-elves that he actively sought them out wherever they appeared and destroyed them under the delusion that he was keeping the world safe from the legacy of the Witch. Even if the half-elf was nothing more than an innocent crying child, Melakuera would show no mercy, such was the case when he tried to kill Emilia.
history:
Early Life
A long time ago in the distant past, a spark from a campfire created an "it" which did not possess any intelligence or self-awareness. Near the campfire "it" was born from, there was a completely average family consisting of a father, a mother, a daughter, and a son. The father of the family passed down the role of managing their campfire on the family's travels, and whenever the boy lit the fire, "it" would appear from the flames. Following the family for decades, the boy eventually became a father, and then a grandfather. However, the man would eventually come to the end of his life, and he would pass away while praying for his family's continued safety. After the man's death, the being which had been following him for his entire life would gain self-awareness for the first time. Remembering how the man called "it" a friend, the being, a lesser spirit, resolved itself to fulfill the final prayer of its friend. Seeing the man's grave, the nameless lesser spirit took the name engraved on it, Melakuera, in order for the man's name to live on until its death. As the sole friend of the man, Melakuera would follow the wishes of its friend by maintaining peace and tranquility, protecting the world from all dangers, and saving all others from suffering.

Eventually, Melakuera grew to be one of the four most powerful spirits in the world that were collectively known as the Four Great Spirits. Each of the Four Greats represent one of the four primary elemental attributes. Melakuera, as the bearer of fire, became known as the Arbitrator.

Great Calamity Era
Many years after Melakuera's birth, the Witch of Envy used her terrible power to decimate half of the entire world. Although she was defeated and imprisoned by heroes, Satella's dark deeds ensured that her name was never forgotten. Half-elves, particularly female ones with silver hair and bluish-purple eyes, faced prejudice because the Witch of Envy purportedly fit that description. Many beings, including Melakuera, believed that silver haired half-elves were descendants of the Witch and should therefore be destroyed in case they followed in her footsteps.

At some point, Melakuera clashed with another spirit whose might rivalled that of the Four Greats. This beast-like spirit used fire Magic to generate and manipulate ice in stark contrast to Melakuera who summoned actual flames. Their fearsome battle torched an entire city and became well known across the world as an example of what the Four Great Spirits were capable of. The beast-like spirit escaped Melakuera's wrath and later became known as the "Beast of the End" for his capability to rival the Four Greats.

Bonds of Ice
Hundreds and hundreds of years later, seven years before the story, Melakuera sent some of his eyes into Elior Forest to scout the forest in search of Emilia, but they were always defeated by Puck. Eventually, after sensing immense magical power coming from the forest, Melakuera decided to make his appearance there. Puck and Melakuera fought at Elior Forest, ending in Puck's victory. Ironically mirroring the fate of his friend, after Melakuera's death, Emilia felt the need to make a grave with his name on it, despite him leaving no body to bury.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
As a great spirit, Melakuera was an incredibly powerful existence within the world. It was so powerful that during its battle with Puck, one of the characters proclaimed as among the strongest of character in the series in the past, not only did the battle destroy part of the terrain it took place in, it took everything Puck had to defeat him, and he still nearly died in the process.

Magic/Spiritual Arts

As the great spirit presiding over fire, Melakuera had a great command over fire magic. Melakuera was able to launch scorching fireballs that reduced everything in their path to ashes, and he was capable of manifesting flaming wings said to be hot enough to burn the soul to launch massive heatwaves that affected a large area, turning everything within the area into scorched remains.

Physical Traits
thumb|200px|Melakuera splitting himself against Emilia.
Division: Melakuera was able to divide his existence into multiple parts. He used this ability to divide himself into seven bodies, each on the level of Puck's normal form, controlling them individually to monitor the world and deter calamity. Although the bodies that appeared as separate beings with equal power, the divided Melakeruas were all one being. He also used this ability to create small “eyes”.

Intelligence
Keen Intellect: Melakuera was deceptive and cunning. He deceived others in order to trick the barrier Puck set up over Elior Forest. He also intentionally released the Black Serpent's poison into the forest in order to see if Emilia would use her power.

Other
Possession: By forming a contract with someone, Melakuera was able to take control of their body, using it as an anchor.

intro: Moguro Hagane (モグロ・ハガネ) is the former Eighth ranking Divine General of the Sacred Vollachia Empire. They are a living meteor who governed the Imperial Capital of Lupugana's Crystal Palace. They played an antagonistic role in Arc 7 and a lesser supporting role in Arc 8. They also played a small antagonistic role in The Travelogue of the Finest.
appearance: Moguro usually appeared as a large being who is nearly three meters tall. They had a thick body and long limbs that were covered with a hard bronze substance, which was of an inorganic mineral. Their head was a large bronze helmet with green glass in the center and green vertical highlights. They also had several green orbs which resembled mana stones that are attached to the joints around its body and feet. Moguro's true form was the green jewel that acted as the magic core of the Crystal Palace, located in the castle's top floor.
personality: Moguro was a reserved individual who spoke in a monotone voice and limited their words, which made it hard to understand their thoughts. Despite that, they were excellent at sifting out essential information and always remained attentive to conversations. They most often expressed themself through combat and even offered words of praise to their opponents. Although Moguro was a meteor who was influenced by the one who sits on the Crystal Palace's throne, this did not stop them from being friends with people like Groovy and having the wish to bring peace to the Vollachia Empire. Their accumulated personality and memories were completely reset after the events of the Great Disaster.
history:
At an unknown point in time, the Crystal Palace and its meteor, including the magic core (魔核, ma kaku) that acted as the heart of it, controlling the palace from within, were created. After its construction, due to the high density of mana absorbed by the rare mana stones used in the citadel's makeup, the magic core controlling the Crystal Palace eventually gained a spirit. The living meteor would later come to be named Moguro Hagane, and in order to hide their true identity from all but a select few within the Empire, Moguro began to proclaim themself as the Steelman and took advantage of their appearance to appear as a member of the Steelfolk tribe. They would eventually meet Groovy Gumlet, who had initially mistaken them for furnishing of the Crystal Palace and attempted to place them into storage, and they ended up becoming close with him.

The Travelogue of the Finest
Roughly four to five months before Arc 1, a rebellion in Vollachia was started by Gramdart Holstoy and Balleroy Temeglyph. Together, Moguro and Groovy Gumlet were dispatched from the Imperial Capital of Lupugana by Goz Ralfon to retrieve Vincent while Cecilus Segmunt left on his own accord to accomplish the task. Vincent was kidnapped by Reinhard van Astrea, Julius Juukulius, and Ferris, then in the Empire to negotiate a non-aggression pact alongside Council of Wise Men members Miklotov McMahon and Bordeaux Zergev. Although Moguro initially took Ferris captive, the Sword Saint later freed him and began turning the tables against the two generals, which allowed for the other two knights to escape with Vincent. Moguro and Groovy were later forced to retreat from Reinhard due to his sheer power, and after running to Cecilus, Reinhard was given a chance to render the Blue Lightning unconscious, forcing the pair into submission and causing them to fall back with the unconscious general. After the rebellion was quelled, Moguro met with Vincent in Lupugana's Crystal Palace alongside Groovy, Goz, and Chisha Gold, where they discussed the incident.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
Moguro is incredibly powerful. Due to their unique form as a meteor, they can employ themselves as an army of golems, a colossal titan, and even the Crystal Palace itself. Because the only way to bring Moguro down is to destroy the core, it is effectively impossible to kill Moguro, no matter how damaged they become, allowing access to greater and more numerous methods of attacking and defending that no other person would be capable of utilizing.

Physical Traits
Colossal Toughness: Moguro's external bodies possessed enough strength that they could easily kill their opponents with a glancing blow, and their attacks could send shockwaves of earth to crush opponents with ease. It has been said that around the world, Reinhard was the only person who was capable of breaking Moguro's hard metal with his bare hands.

Whirlwind Fighting Style: Moguro could drill with both of their hands as well as by spinning their external bodies at incredible speeds. They could move underground as easily as a fish in water can. Using this technique, Moguro overtakes their opponents by hiding underground. The whirlwind style allowed them to perform techniques that were fatal to humans with colossal strength. Even when their body is enlarged to giant proportions, Moguro is still keen, nimble, and precise.

Reconstruction: Moguro could alter the shape of their body to various sizes and shapes. They could change the structure of a body part, such as a limb, into something more sharp or dull, they could elongate themself to a colossal size, or they could even change the form of their external body into the bastions surrounding the Imperial Capital. They could even create numerous golems of varying toughness and strength as if they were their own miniature army. So long as they have the material to work with, they can even repair their body with ease. As long as Moguro's true body, the magic core of the Crystal Palace of Lupugana itself, is intact, they could not be completely defeated.

Giant Magic Crystal Soldier: Being connected to the Crystal Palace, Moguro can, if necessary, transform the entire palace into a massive soldier that takes a similar appearance to Moguro's usual form. In this state, it wields one of a certain number of giant pillars as large as itself reshaped into a greatsword with a fifty-meter blade, from its hands, it can fire a blast similar to but weaker than the Magic Crystal Cannon, still bearing enough power to destroy half of the Imperial Capital, it can emit an undodgeable mist of light from its body, and it can gyrate its body to deal with attacks that surround it. However, Moguro is not the only one able to do this. Due to the meteor being directly connected to the palace, others are capable of triggering this form. Once it entered this state, it was no longer possible to revert the soldier to its palace form.

intro: Melinda (メリンダ) was Stride Vollachia's wife and a member of the Evil Eye Tribe. She was one of the secondary antagonists of Sword Demon Battle Ballad.

However, she was very quick to become angry when people went against her ideals and placed innocent and unborn babies in danger. She was also willing to go out of her way and put her life at stake just to protect someone's unborn child.

abilities_text:
thumb|200px|Melinda's Evil Eyes
Evil Eyes (魔眼, Magan): As a member of the Evil Eye Tribe, Melinda, rather than having a third eye located somewhere on her body as is common for her tribespeople, was uniquely the owner of two Evil Eyes in the place of conventional eyes. Her right eye was the Evil Eye of Pride, and her left eye was the Evil Eye of Vainglory. The effect of an Evil Eye was activated when someone looked into it, forcing her to keep her eyes shut until she was ready to utilize its power, and, according to Kurgan, they could only ensnare the weak.

Activated when someone peered into it, the Evil Eye of Vainglory created hallucinatory illusions, presenting a counterfeit reality to its target. This is the ability Melinda used to induce an illusion in Wilhelm's mind, which manifested as a hallucination of Pivot Arnancy, and to control the citizens of Picoutatte.

intro: Marone Lisbon (マローネ・リズボン) is a former citizen of Guineb. She later started to help Regin Suwen at his hospital.
appearance: Marone is the most beautiful woman in Guineb with bright red hair in a ponytail. She has light brown eyes and wears a white ribbon in her ponytail. Like Felt, she has a yaeba that becomes prominent when she laughs. She has a golden necklace around her neck, a big chest, and wears a light green and white outfit.
personality: Marone is an assertive, impulsive, and emotionally driven person with a big determination to do what she wants. While she is an optimist, she is very perceptive and does not ignore when a situation is not actually favorable. She is also shown to be compassionate and empathic.
history:
Otto's Peddling Record of Joy and Sorrow
Marone was born and raised in Guineb. One day, Aheem Lavril, the son of Guineb's mayor, Colin, deceived her and gave her to slave traders. Later on, Otto Suwen was also entrapped by Aheem and locked away with Marone. When she awoke, she explained the situation to him, referred to him as Number Two, and introduced herself. After Otto was given a chance to confirm his earth dragon Frufoo's whereabouts, he told Marone that he had the "Divine Protection of Guidance" and made an agreement with her. Afterward, when they were put on his dragon carriage, he was told to reveal his path through the mountains. The deal with Aheem was that he would provide the traders women in exchange for not disrupting Guineb. With Frufoo leading the carriage, Otto directed the traders where there was a supposed path that they could use. Then, after calling out to Marone as part of their agreement, they held on tight as Frufoo was signaled to crash the carriage.

Otto and Marone had their injuries treated in a hospital in a nearby town, where he revealed that Guineb's mayor and son were likely to be investigated for the incident and Aheem likely arrested. Upon asking if she would return to Guineb, Marone refused. When Marone asked for his name, he said she could keep calling him Number Two and gave her his own savings, enough for her to start a new life anywhere she wanted, lying to her by saying it was a reward for taking down the slave traders.

The Three Idiots Set Out! Earth Spider Episode
After separating from Otto, Marone moved to Pappelt, where she became Regin Suwen's assistant. When Otto and his group arrived at Pappelt, Otto and Marone were reunited.

While attempting to escape Flanders once his plan to take Manfred's position was foiled, he was captured by the Anastasia Camp and delivered back to the city. Afterwards, he was tortured by his former boss while being forced to hold his eyes in his hands. His current status is unknown.
appearance: Mozolite is a large man with a flat face reminiscent of a crushed frog. He had tattoos on his eyeballs, each of which were gouged out by The Balance following his betrayal.

history:
Mozolite hailed from the same hometown as Mimosa. Around the start of the Royal Selection, Mozolite, who was the second-in-command of the Balance, allied himself with Helaine Gatness in an attempt to snatch the position of his boss, Manfred, orchestrating attacks on the Big Three and her own Golden Beetle organization with assassins and leveraging his position in his group to do so. Helaine, perceiving Mozolite's ambition and detecting that he could be easily exploited, supported his goal, believing it would be in the interest of the organization she served.

When Felt attempted to make a courtesy visit to the Balance after visiting the Flower Prison Garden first, Mozolite and Manfred's men were there to relay their boss's refusal to see her and Reinhard van Astrea. Felt ultimately accepted the result, and simply by looking around, Mozolite made the men who had surrounded the pair disperse, allowing them to leave. After Manfred's meeting with Felt, he recognized that she had a keen nose and ordered Mozolite to keep a close eye on them. 

While attempting to escape from Flanders after Helaine exposed Mozolite's involvement in the conspiracy once she lost her bet to Rachins Hoffman and his subordinate with an Excess Mana Circulation Constitution was defeated by Ezzo Cadner, he was met by the Anastasia Camp. While attempting to flee from them, Reinhard threw a tometo at him all the way from the city, which landed a blow on him, causing him to faint. When he awoke, his eyes had been gouged out, and he was tortured by Manfred while in the presence of Toto and Doltero Amule.

name_jp: メルティ・プリスティス
alias: Clumsy Nun (不器用な修道女, Bukiyōna Shūdō On'na)

first_game: Re:Zero − Starting Life in Another World: The Prophecy of the Throne
intro: Melty Pristis (メルティ・プリスティス) is the former sixth candidate to become the 42nd monarch of the Kingdom of Lugunica. After being exposed as an imposter for the throne, she stepped down from the Royal Selection and fled Lugunica with Tiga, Salum/Wolf, and Pooka, intending to pay a visit to Tiga's old group of travelling entertainers.
appearance: Melty is a beautiful young lady with long indigo hair in twin tails that reaches a centimeter off the ground, a small ahoge, and yellow eyes. She wears a nun outfit with Arabian aesthetic. Her attire consists of a blue dress with a slit and white knee-high boots. Both tails of her hair are wrapped around with gold chains, and she adorns a gold pendant that is the shape of the Divine Dragon.
personality: As a nun who worked under the Divine Dragon Church, she believes in the Divine Dragon. She is a polite and soft-spoken girl who is always low profile, and she is somewhat protective. Melty is reserved, but she's also very modest and compassionate. She tries her best to do everything, but because she tends to rush, she can be a bit of a screw-up.
history:
Before arriving in Lugunica, Melty lived in Faradar, the village of the Evil Eye Tribe. Ever since she was a child, she intuitively realized that she was different from normal people, but she did not mind because everyone accepted her for who she was, and she accepted that kindness in turn. However, what she had not realized was that her Evil Eye of Bewitchment was the cause of people's kindness toward her. While taking an exam to determine her Evil Eye's strength, she wished for the voices urging her to quit scaring her, and as a result, those around her began to fight each other until they collapsed. Although nobody died, as a result of this, she was imprisoned far away from the village. Although her brother Salum was told to never visit her, he frequently slipped by the tribe's adults to meet with her, bringing her information about her Evil Eye, such as that someone else from hundreds of years ago had possessed the same power as her, for her sake.

One day, she met a young boy named Tiga when he was still a traveling entertainer, and the two became good friends. Salum also happened to meet Melty shortly after her first encounter with Tiga. While initially wary of Tiga's presence, he accepted the young boy's assertion that he was Melty's friend and would never leave her side. Due to the effects of her Evil Eye of Bewitchment, she came to believe that she had used her power to change the course of his life and make him into her friend. Unbeknownst to her, however, Tiga's Divine Protection allowed him to resist her power. Nevertheless, Melty felt guilt over her belief that her Evil Eye had ensnared him, and this guilt went on to weigh on her conscience for many years to come.

Sometime in the past, Faradar was attacked, resulting in Melty being separated from her family, including Salum. She met Mother, who sealed her Evil Eye and closed her throat, making it so she was unable to eat food. From then on, the only way she could digest food was via injection through the Mana Wasps that are thought to have been created by Mother. Her and Tiga went to Lugunica and joined the Divine Dragon Church, being overseen by Sakura Element, who possessed a power allowing her to control Mana Wasps.
abilities_text:
Evil Eye (魔眼, Magan): Melty has the Evil Eye of Bewitchment (人誑しの魔眼, Hitotarashi no Magan). It is a very rare ability among the Evil Eye Tribe that is considered to be too dangerous, since it can affect its own kind. For that reason, Melty was locked up. Her eye can manipulate someone unconditionally, just by touching the person. Whoever is touched follows her orders as long as she commands them. It was originally on her hands; however, when she met Mother, her eye was hidden so that no one could see it when used.

Magic (魔法, Mahō): Melty has enough skill in magic to use water magic.
Healing Magic (治癒魔法, Chiyu Mahō): Melty summons water mana to heal the wounds of herself and others. She can also heal someone's illnesses.

Equipment: Melty wields a long staff that contains a book of spells within.

name: Lilac
relatives: Shion (main personality/separate soul)

intro: Lilac (ライラ) is a wandering dream arts user. She, alongside Shion, later joined the Omega Party.
appearance:
Lilac has purple and pink eyes with purple pupils, and as the phantom of an elf, she has pointed ears. She has long purple hair with two black Mariposa lily on her hair. Her clothes are almost similar to Shion's; however, unlike Shion, her attire is more revealing as it consists of a short black sleeveless dress. She adorns herself a crimson red rose on her left arm, a dagger wrapped around on her hips, and a small gold locket around her neck with a purple bow as a choker.

Since Lilac shares the same physical vessel as Shion, whenever her personality manifests in their vessel, its appearance instantly shifts to match hers.
personality: Unlike her counterpart, Lilac is slightly more aggressive and stubborn, as well as very protective of Shion, to the point that, despite accidentally taking a whole town hostage, she is willing to keep people asleep to keep them away from her. That said, she does not seem to like dragging unrelated parties into her own mess if she can help it, as shown when she wanted to prevent anyone from coming to harm while in her dream world. Due to being a Dream Arts User, however, her sense of self is somewhat fuzzy, and because she is so synchronized with others, she can find herself becoming influenced by other people's memories, including taking on their speech quirks. It is because of this that she can often be heard speaking with numerous loan words, having picked them up from passing memories of a person who uses them. She is somewhat driven by her goal to find the person who uses these words, even being willing to follow Omega as part of her party for the chance to learn of the person who uses them.
history:
At an unknown point in time and for unknown reasons, two separate souls, Shion and Lilac, came to possess the same vessel. When the two souls first confronted each other, they were in conflict and fought for control over their shared body. However, one day, that changed, and they now share their body peacefully, speculating that, having entered another person’s dream, they were deeply affected. As time passed, they came across the dream of a man who spoke with English loan words, and ever since, they have been searching for the person whose dream they entered in order to fill the void that lingered in their hearts.

Omega in Wonderland
At some point, she and Lilac appeared in Gusteko. However, they were deemed heretics by the Gustekan Church, causing them to send a Temple Knight after them. At some point after entering the town of Sylphoa, they confronted Mikli, and Lilac, having had no time to aim, used her Dream Arts to put her, and accidentally, the entire town, to sleep. Because of this, however, Shion lost contact with Lilac.

Sometime later, after Omega and Colette appeared in her dream space, she stopped the former from destroying it with Al Shario, and she sealed her magic while within the dream. After getting into a small dispute with Omega, Colette spoke with her about letting all of the townspeople go, and though she was hesitant to do so and seemed standoffish, Omega stated that Colette's words got through to her. However, upon hearing Omega's use of a loan word, Lilac wanted to know where she heard it, leading to negotiations. Despite becoming frustrated with her and even slapping her, she decided to give Omega a chance to take care of the Temple Knight who had come after her, breaking the seal that she'd placed. The fight that followed was short lived as the Witches of Sin quickly dispatched her, much to Lilac's shock. Shortly after, Palmyra entered the dream space with a message from Shion.

Following this, after Omega spoke to the other Temple Knight who had come for Mikli and had him leave with her and report the death of the heretic, Lilac released the people of Sylphoa from her dream world, and Omega offered Shion and Lilac to join her party. Since she couldn't quite trust the two, having just met them, she would give them a chance to look into her memories with their Dream Arts, giving them a chance to find the person from which the loan words they speak come from. The two accepted her offer and joined the party.

Witch Trials
One day, having moved on from Sylphoa, the Omega Party was walking in a snow field, where they encountered a Snow Blight. However, Omega swiftly dispatched it with Minya. Soon after, they arrived at Limbus, where signs claiming it was forbidden to go out at night and to comply with the "vows of the faith". Though slightly concerned about the town's eeriness, as the group was low on supplies, they decided to enter Limbus, where after a few minutes, they found themselves surrounded by the townsfolk who were armed with farming tools. Though they attempted to calm the townsfolk and offer them a gift in the form of the Snow Blight's crystallized head, they instead accuse her of being a Witch after seeing it, leading Omega to warn Colette against using her bracelet's transformation and Lilac from turning back into Shion, else they be declared Witches. Thanks to the appearance of Nananna Pezza and speaking with Noelle Tuérico, she was able to vouch for them and clear them of being Witches.

Omega's group finds an inn to reside in where they discussed the issue at present, warning everyone about how easily they could be made into scapegoats whether for their abilities, race, or even the look in their eyes, and Noelle explained about Witch Hunts and Witch Trials being rare occurrences in Gusteko that Itinerant Preachers were sometimes sent to deal with. Although wanting to leave the town quickly, the group decides to stay in the town to help Noelle repay her debt to Nananna, and soon after, they meet with Nananna when she arrived to ask for the group's assistance. That night, the Witch Hunt is for a person named Piditz who had been tipped off as a Witch, and Nananna wanted him taken into custody only. When they later spotted Piditz and chased after him, Omega split off to corner him, only to find Mireille Hetia using her spiritual arts to kill Piditz. Thanks to being near the body, Omega was quickly turned into a scapegoat and declared a Witch so that Mireille could cover up her kill and at least prevent her from getting in the way of her and Nananna's revenge, and Omega was taken into custody.

At the inn, the party discusses how if the scale of this event expands, they will be unable to prevent the spread of the news this time, which could result in the party's persecution, even abroad, and their possible extradition back to the church. To clear their names, Colette states that they should find the real culprit for the murders. Lilac and Colette go to gather information around the town, and they meet with Mireille, who explained to them how the hunts started. Likewise, Omega explained this to Palmyra, as she learned it while imprisoned. Shion used her dream arts to peer into the minds of the townsfolk, and she warns Lilac that the "Witch" is just a conspiracy by the council to get rid of political enemies. After learning of this, Lilac informs the Colette and Palmyra, and the elves suggest sowing division in the people to uproot the conspiracy. Though wanting to talk to Noelle, she does not come back that night, and Lilac and Shion decide to use their dream arts to nudge the townsfolk to attend the upcoming.

The next day, the Witch Trial is being held for Omega, overseen by Nananna and the Town Hall, while Palmyra acts as Omega's attorney. Despite her arguments, Edmon Quayle counters with his supposed knowledge of the Witches and Omega's chatter does not help. Colette speaks up and claims that she believes that things will not go as the council claims, as people will begin to notice that the entire event seems off, which resounds with the townsfolk. Because of this, Palmyra claims that there is a conspiracy, which Edmon fights against and asks for Nananna's assistance. Because she sides with the town, Lilac and Shion believe her to be part of the conspiracy, and they decide to use their dream arts to influence the people's mental states. Palmyra then claims that the council is using the Witch rumors to get rid of inconvenient people, which Edmon also fights against, though is quickly silenced when she states she heard it herself from a council member and declares that there is no Witch. Unfortunately, Omega claims otherwise.

Despite angering Palmyra, Omega decides to clear things up by declaring that there were two conspiracies taking place in town. Despite Nananna trying to prevent her from talking, Omega ignores her and explains that many of the victims were relatives of council members, and she claims that Nananna is the second conspirator, calling her the bastard child of Edmon whose mother was banished from the town, and as a result, she despised the town. Noelle later appears and confirms that her actions were in response to the death of an elderly healer, and she claims that Nananna tried to remove her from the trial by knocking her out since her only ire was with Limbus. Afterward, Noelle declares that the secretary, Mireille, was helping Nananna, as she was a bastard child of Edmon as well, and she stated how the corpses of Piditz and other people connected to the council and other outside officials were already dumped in a hole. Omega also declares that she witnessed Mireille killing Piditz. Enraged, Mireille uses her spiritual arts to char Edmon's arm with blue fire, and with the intent of killing the entire council, surrounds the council with blue fire, and she and Nananna stand against them. Although Omega is fine with leaving things as they are and taking their leave, Colette states she doesn't want things to end like this, and Omega decides to end the fighting in response to her plea, burning through her restraints and declaring herself a Witch.

Later, as Omega's party begins to leave the town, Noelle says her goodbyes to Nananna, and it is declared that the evil spirit accompanying Mireille will be disposed of. Likewise, it is claimed that Edmon's position is under threat with both his severe injuries and the loss of the citizens' trust, and Mireille claims she was mistaken about real Witches. Despite Colette believing that things were settled peacefully, however, Omega thinks to herself that Limbus would soon face its destruction, as since Omega, Nananna, and Mireille were not executed, there would be continuous Witch Hunts and deaths for scapegoats for the whole incident. Although considering telling Colette about this, she decides against it.
abilities_text:
Magic (魔法, Mahō): Lilac is skilled at using dream arts.
Dream Arts: A type of forbidden art that is all but lost from the world in the present that allows its user to meddle with the mind. It is trained by using people as test subjects. After the person falls asleep, the practitioner must learn to sense and attune themselves to the person's Od before they die. Her proficiency with Dream Arts is considered impressive by Omega, who herself can use Dream Arts, and even surpasses her, being able to put an entire town to sleep for long periods of time and create a dream space larger than the Castle of Dreams.
Hypnosis Magic: A form of magic that temporarily stops mana from flowing into the target's Od, severing their consciousness from reality. Hypnosis Magic is considered the specialty of Dream Arts Users.
Thought Implantation: Using Dream Arts, it is possible to place a thought into another person's head and leave them to act on it, such as making a person think of the user as an ally and making them stop any pursuers chasing after them.
Memory Scouring: As a Dream Arts user, Lilac is attuned to other people and is influenced by their memories. Likewise, if she chooses to, she can look into another person's memories to extract specific information. However, their target may show resistance, preventing her from reaching the memory she is looking for.

Possession: As Shion's phantom, Lilac is able to take over her body in the real world, appearing as she does in the dream world. It is likely that her possession is limited only to Shion.

Equipment: Shion carries a dagger around on her hip. However proficient she is with it is unknown.

name: Mizelda Shudrak
name_jp: ミゼルダ・シュドラク
nickname: Mii (ミー) (by Utakata)

relatives: Taritta Shudrak (younger sister) ; Flop O'Connell (brother-in-law) ; Medium O'Connell (sister-in-law)
intro: Mizelda Shudrak (ミゼルダ・シュドラク) is the Chieftain of the People of Shudrak located in the depths of the Buddheim Jungle, in the Empire of Vollachia. She played a supporting role in Arc 7.
appearance: Mizelda is a tall, strong woman with brown skin and green eyes. Her hair is black, but the top is dyed red and parted to one side. Due to the hot and somewhat moist weather, Mizelda, like most of her other people, wears minimal clothes. She also sports a pair of big, round golden earrings. After her fight with Arakiya, it is revealed that she lost a leg and uses a wooden prosthetic leg as a replacement.
personality:
Mizelda is shown to be rather hostile towards outsiders and especially towards those who trample on their pride as proud hunters. While she does exhibit these traits, she is willing to listen to the pleas of Subaru and Vincent and even allow them to take the Ritual of Blood, albeit having them partake in the hardest and most dangerous ritual they have. After Subaru and Vincent successfully complete the ritual, Mizelda treats them as fellow hunters and agrees to help Subaru save Rem and Rui.

She is quick to judge how a combatant fights, and she enjoys watching when someone triumphs in battle, such as when she witnessed Subaru's actions in the Lifeblood Ritual. She is also very protective of her tribe and very loyal to people that she considers her allies. She also tends to have some favoritism towards men who she considers has handsome faces, such as Vincent and Otto Suwen. This being said, she does not allow this to cloud her judgment, and as the chieftain of her tribe, she is willing to let go of her attraction in favor of leading her people within their jungle; this being said, she is not averse to someone she is attracted coming to stay with her people. While she herself would choose this, she is also willing to help her own people should they be conflicted about whether to remain within the jungle or choose life outside of it, as she did for her sister.

However, she is particularly brutal towards her enemies. During the events of the Great Disaster, shortly after the defeat of the Witch Sphinx, disliking the deceptive words she was spouting, she took her dagger and slit her throat before repeatedly stabbing her. She also dislikes being treated like someone to be protected simply because of her gender. Like the rest of the Shudrakians, they were annoyed when Zikr Osman requested them to stay back while the rest of the army was prepared for a massive sacrifice during the Battle for the Imperial Capital.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
Mizelda is a powerful and prodigal combatant whose strength is renowned among her people. Likewise, she was capable of putting up a fight against Arakiya for a time, and her strength was acknowledged by Vincent to be worthy of the Nine Divine Generals. Even after having lost her leg and replacing it with a prosthetic, her strength does not appear to have diminished.

Physical Traits/Flow Method
Melee Fighter: Mizelda is also highly skilled at using her knife in combat. She used it to effectively fight Arakiya for a short time in close quarters, and later, she showed such skill with a pair of daggers that she was able to swiftly handle numerous golems created by Moguro Hagane with ease.

Skilled Archer: As is the case with most other members of her people, Mizelda is extremely skilled with her bow and its usage.

Enhanced Eyesight: Mizelda has excellent eyesight, easily surpassing a beastified Frederica Baumann's, allowing her to see across a battlefield with ease.

Equipment
Hunting Tools: As a hunter, Mizelda is typically armed with a bow and arrows or a knife. 
Club: During the Battle for the Imperial Capital, she used a club.
Daggers: During the aforementioned battle, she also used a pair of glossy black daggers.

name: Medium O'Connell
name_jp: ミディアム・オコーネル
alias: Sword Consort (剣皇妃, Ken Kōhi)
nickname: Medi (ミデ, Midi) (by Balleroy) ; Midii (ミディー) (by Utakata)
relatives: Flop O'Connell (older brother) ; Vincent Vollachia (husband) ; Taritta Shudrak (sister-in-law) ; Mizelda Shudrak (sister-in-law)
intro: Medium O'Connell (ミディアム・オコーネル) is the sister of Flop O'Connell. She played a supporting role in Arc 7 and Arc 8.
appearance: Medium is a tall woman with long cream blonde hair, which is the same color as her older brother. She wears her hair in a unique style. She is also described to be taller than her brother. She wears clothes that reveal her shoulders and legs, and she carries two barbarian swords on her waist.
personality:
Medium is a bubbly, cheerful, and overall positive person who has a tendency to try to befriend and help the people around her. She very rarely exhibits sadness, and she is almost always seen smiling and interacting with others, even if some of those people come off as cold and standoffish, like Vincent. She is the type to think with her heart more than her head, and when her brother pointed this out, said words became a guiding light to her. She is also quick to feel praise, as a single compliment from Flop was enough to give her enough motivation to fight against experienced soldiers. She also believes quite heavily in her brother's dream, and since she wants to make his wish of "revenge" come true, alongside their strong bond built up in their harsh early life, Medium decided to accompany her brother and act as her bodyguard, and the two often worked together to leave strong impressions in the places that they visited, intent on leaving positive marks across the Empire. She also seems to have fun with children, as after she met Spica, who was called Rui at the time, she could be seen fixing her hair and taking care of her.

While Medium is usually a positive thinker, on rare occasions, she can be seen with short bursts of particularly strong negative emotions. Following the deaths of Miles, Balleroy, and Carillon, she was so saddened by their deaths that she wouldn't stop crying about it for a little while. She felt the same way after she learned that Balleroy and Carillon were revived in the Great Disaster as zombies. When she and Flop were saved from the orphanage's caretaker by Miles and were given a chance to take out their grudges, Medium was quick to start stomping and beating on the caretaker alongside the other children out of payback for what the man had done. After she learned of Spica's history as Rui Arneb of the Witch Cult, she froze and trembled in fear. In fact, in the non-canon Azamuku IF side story, after Flop was killed and his death blamed on the country's usurper, Medium was terribly distraught, angry, and dead set on vengeance. Azamuku aside, despite the tribulations her life has given her, she was able to quickly pick herself back up and keep fighting; in fact, in the case of Spica, she was terribly apologetic and wanted to fix their relationship, while in the case of Balleroy's "revival", it even inspired her so greatly that she experienced the greatest amount of strength she ever had.

As stated before, Medium is very quick to offer her assistance to people, just like her brother. Shortly after meeting with Natsuki Subaru, the amnesiac Rem, and Spica, she was immediately friendly and positive with them, leaving a strong impression on them. Likewise, she and her brother were quick to trust and believe in them, as they both assisted the group in escaping Guaral after they were discovered by one of their enemies. Not only did she and her brother assist them with this escape, but she was even willing to join the rebellion on their side after meeting with Vincent after her brother negotiated with the man.

Because she is so trusting in her brother, she more often than not goes with his flow and almost always agrees with him when he makes a decision, often neglecting to use her head since her brother is the thinker between the two. That said, she can still be caught off guard by his decisions, especially when the concern her. During a discussion he had with Vincent regarding the future of the country, when he offered his sister's hand in marriage to the emperor, even though she had fallen for the man by this point, she was still stunned and didn't know how to react. This being said, she still went along with his decision out of both trust in Flop and love for Vincent.

Medium also has a strong conviction in being a positive influence on people. After meeting the cold and cruel Vincent, she often tried to get through his tough exterior and be more emotional. Likewise, when she met Roswaal L. Mathers and learned of his similar nature, Medium vowed to become a positive influence on the two of them so that they would become friendlier and learn how to be more social and caring, intent on becoming something of a role model.
history:
When she was young, she and her brother Flop grew up in an orphanage in a small town called Averyk, where they were routinely beaten by adults. One day, an imperial soldier named Miles arrived at the orphanage and promptly beat and tied up the adults in charge of the orphanage. Along with the other kids, aside from Flop, she beat the tied-up adults out of rage from her abuse. 

Soon after, she and Flop were brought to the Dracroy Domain, where Serena Dracroy resided. Understanding their circumstances, she became an older sister figure to the two of them and allowed them to reside in her domain. A few years after this, they met Balleroy Temeglyph, and they helped him raise the newborn Carillon. At some point, when Carillon lost some of his baby teeth, they were made into a necklace that he started to wear. At some point, Medium fell in love with Balleroy.

Some years after this, Flop decided to set out from the Dracroy Domain to become a merchant to achieve his revenge, with Medium acting as his bodyguard. During their travels, however, they heard of the demise of Balleroy, Carillon, and Miles, each of which saddened them and left Medium crying.

Undead Busters
During her time as the new empress, rather than subjecting herself to typical royal behavior, she had been sparring with the imperial soldiers, which Flop had praised her for. However, as she was insecure about how to be a good wife to Vincent, she asked for advice from Yorna Mishigure, Serena, and Madelyn Eschart. Soon after, Cecilus Segmunt's group, who had been tasked to deal with the remaining undead, returned to speak with Vincent about Volcas. Soon after, Yorna and Volcas, who had recognized her as Iris, engaged in combat, though Volcas mostly did not fight back. Following the events of the battle, Volcas sought to be executed by Vincent with the Yang Sword, whereas Yorna obstinately did not want to accept that outcome. Realizing that there was a possibility Yorna could revolt again, Medium, Vincent's new empress consort, suggested to Vincent that Volcas should be chosen to fill the vacancy in the Nine Divine Generals. She believed her proposal would not only cater to Yorna and fill the vacancy left by Chisha Gold, but with Volcas being the direct cause behind Eugard Vollachia's decree to execute the wolf people and mole people, forgiving him and having him join their side would show that Vincent was serious about keeping the decree rescinded. Vincent took the proposal seriously, and when Medium accidentally let slip that the suggestion was her brother's, she told Vincent that she just wanted to improve Vincent's view of her as his empress. Regardless, after hearing Medium out, Vincent proceeded to meet with Volcas in person to discuss her proposal with him, walking with Medium hand-in-hand.
abilities_text:
Divine Protection (加護, Kago): Medium possesses the Divine Protection of Morale (高揚の加護, Kōyō no Kago). The more excited or motivated Medium feels, the more her physical abilities increase in response. At its best, Medium can become strong enough to counter even the magic bullets fired by Balleroy. However, the Divine Protection is a double-edged sword, as since it is affected by Medium's mood, it also diminishes her abilities if she feels sad or enters a depressive state. It has been said that usually, she's practically immoveable, yet while she is at her weakest, she can be toppled over with ease. Additionally, Medium is unaware that she owns this Divine Protection. Her physical strength is not the only thing affected by her Divine Protection. Her other senses are also improved; her sight, when influenced to its best by her Divine Protection, achieved the same level as Balleroy's scope.

Equipment: Medium carries two barbarian swords on her waist which she uses to fight with, and she is talented enough with them to not only delay the Imperial Army long enough for Flop and Subaru to escape from them, but also to regularly spar with them and come out almost always victorious.

intro: Madelyn Eschart (マデリン・エッシャルト) is the Sixth ranking Divine General of the Sacred Vollachia Empire. She played an antagonistic role in Arc 7 and Arc 8 and a small supporting role toward the end of the latter arc.
appearance: Madelyn is a young girl with golden eyes and light blue hair, the tips of which are a darker and tied into two long braids. She has blue wings that sprout out of her back and two deep black horns that rise from her head. Additionally, a bright purple bow is wrapped around her left horn. She wears a bright blue dress with white-colored circles and is usually seen with her Flying Winged Blade, which is folded upon her back when sheathed.
personality:
Madelyn is childish, prideful, and often emotional. She looks down on most people while expecting them to obey her orders. As a result of viewing herself as superior for being a dragonkin, she expects to be both respected and feared, only seeming to show care to those who abide by her standards. When she is put in a situation where she doesn't get her way, Madelyn lashes out in frustration and sometimes lampoons herself for bringing shame to her tribe. Although she is not fond of humans making so much noise despite their weakness and fragility, as a dragonkin, she also seems to like treasures and human craftsmanship, and she seems to feel the urge to hoard them, even if it means obeying humans to receive them as a reward.

However, when it comes to the ones she loves, Balleroy, she shows a softer side, and she often refers to them as hers. She also shows this side of herself to Carillon and is typically friendly with him. Similarly, her love for Balleroy is so strong that she is even willing to change sides during a war if he is on the opposing side, such as during the Great Disaster, and she is willing to kill people who cause him trouble. Likewise, when it comes to the people connected to Balleroy, although she still exhibits her temperamental attitude, she is not unwilling to ignore an invitation from them; when she was regularly invited by Medium O'Connell to have tea and snacks with her, she often accepted, and she was even willing to explain her experiences with Balleroy to her when she needed marital advice.
history:
Madelyn was created by Mezoreia, and for many years, she lived alone at the summit of Mount Palzoa with the Dragon. After some time, a stranger and his flying dragon, Balleroy and Carillon, found Madelyn and Mezoreia after breaking through the cloud sea, something no other human had done before. Balleroy was surprised to see the girl, and he started coming to spend time with her after this, giving her the name Madelyn after someone he once knew and giving her clothes, other gifts, and teaching her how to speak. Over time, the two became close with Madelyn coming to love Balleroy, and he sought to bring her outside of Mount Palzoa. This resulted in a fight between him and Mezoreia, though they made peace in the end. Balleroy stopped trying to take her away from the mountain, and eventually, he stopped visiting the summit altogether.

One day, Madelyn decided to go out of the mountain summit on her own, and after realizing how big the world was, she began searching for Balleroy of her own accord, with Mezoreia flying in the sky to watch over her. Following his scent, she eventually learned of Balleroy’s death through Berstetz, which set her on a path to understand why he was killed and get revenge on the person who did it, with Berstetz offering her Balleroy’s position as the Ninth Divine General and the name Eschart after a fallen noble family. During a meeting that took place two to three months after Balleroy's death, Madelyn was suggested by Berstetz to inherit Balleroy's position as the Ninth ranking Divine General despite not having any concrete accomplishments and being largely unknown to the other Divine Generals.

Sword Identity
When Yorna Mishigure began an uprising after the death of Tanza's sister, Madelyn attempted to confront her and failed to give Yorna or Tanza any damage due to the Soul Marriage Technique. After being unable to achieve any results, Madelyn later reiterated a message that Yorna gave her to the other Divine Generals stating the conditions for ending the ongoing rebellion after surprising some of the other Divine Generals and entering a brief clash with them. After her performance alongside Chisha Gold in searching for the escaped soldiers and Kafma Irulux's resignation from the offer, the emperor was given no other choice but to accept Berstetz's proposal and appoint her as the Ninth ranking Divine General.

From then on, she continued searching for any hints into Balleroy that she could, feeling worse as she felt that she was tainting his memory and the position he once held in the process.

Undead Busters
After Medium O'Connell became Vincent's empress consort, she would sometimes visit Medium due to her connection with Balleroy. Eventually, Medium invited her, Yorna, and Serena Dracroy to visit her for marital advice. Despite her confusion about why she was invited, she nonetheless gave her experiences with Balleroy to help advise Medium. Before long, Cecilus Segmunt's party returned to Garkla, intending to speak with Vincent about how to handle Volcas.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
Madelyn is an incredibly powerful warrior. Despite being at the bottom of the Nine Divine Generals, she is capable of ignoring most damage and even fighting against incredibly powerful warriors on the level of Emilia and Priscilla Barielle. Furthermore, should she find herself desperate, she can summon forth a Dragon and even take over its body, providing her with significantly more power than she would ordinarily possess.

Physical Traits/Flow Method
Inhuman Strength: Madelyn has immense physical strength due in part to her race as a dragonkin. She can effortlessly throw her Flying Winged Blade with ease. By comparison, someone as physically strong as Emilia struggled to lift it and failed to throw it properly. On top of which, she has enough strength to easily break through a glacier-like wall of ice with ease with a simple grip of her hands, as well as generate shockwaves while swinging her weapon.

Inhuman Durability: Madelyn is also incredibly physically tough. During her fights with Emilia, she seemed to take no damage at all despite having had glaciers dropped on her multiple times. Similarly, almost none of Emilia’s attacks seemed to affect her either.

Sharp Claws: Though she typically doesn't use them in combat, Madelyn has very sharp claws that are easily capable of rending flesh. A single swipe from her claws nearly killed Flop O'Connell when she hit him, and they were easily capable of ripping through Emilia's ice. Even a slight graze can cause heavily shake a person and disorient them.

Body Heat Increase: Madelyn seems to be able to increase her body’s heat to the point that snow instantly evaporates around her. However, what this does for her abilities, if it does anything for them at all, is unknown. This being said, it allows her to resist cold-based attacks and fight in spite of it.

Enhanced Olfaction: As a dragonkin, Madelyn's sense of smell is greater than a human's. With it, she can follow a person's scent, even after their death.

Other
Possession: As a dragonkin, Madelyn has the ability to possess the Dragon who created her, Mezoreia, and by doing so, she gains access to the full power held by it. However, her original body remains unconscious while doing this, and attempting to disturb it will not end her possession of a Dragon.
Shared Senses: Even when not possessing Mezoreia, Madelyn seems to be able to share senses with Mezoreia. It does not seem that she physically shares one of the five senses, but that she immediately becomes aware when Mezoreia becomes aware of the presence of other beings.

Wind Strikes: Madelyn is capable of gathering wind around her claws and firing it off as a projectile alongside a swipe of her claws. It is unclear if this kind of attack is inherent to her claws, based in her physical strength, or if she can freely manipulate the wind; regardless, it easily has enough strength to damage the ground and send someone of Emilia's caliber flying and bouncing off of the ground.

Dragon Command: As a dragonkin, Madelyn has the ability to make emotional connections with dragons. However, she has only demonstrated use of this ability with Flying Dragons in order to give them commands. During the Flying Dragon Cataclysm in the Fortress City of Guaral, Madelyn was able to command a flock of dragons to converge at the city and wreak havoc on it. It is unknown if there is a limit to how many dragons she is able to command at once, and likewise, it is unknown if she is the only dragonkin capable of doing this. However, she cannot command random undead flying dragons, as they will attack her merely for possessing life.

Equipment
Flying Winged Blade (飛翼刃): The Flying Winged Blade is a heavy boomerang-like weapon that can return to its wielder once it is thrown. However, it is a difficult weapon to use and master, as even someone as physically capable as Emilia was unable to throw it right after attempting.

intro: Mariuli Shudrak (マリウリ・シュドラク) was a member of the People of Shudrak and a former Stargazer. She was first mentioned in Arc 7 as Taritta's soul sister, since both of them were born on the same day, and she was also Utakata's mother.
appearance: Mariuli was described to be a beautiful woman with black hair of which the tips were died pink.
personality: She was said to be a gentle and calm person. Kind at heart, she spent much of her days helping around the village and looking after the kids, singing to them. According to Taritta, her voice was so beautiful that every time the tribe had a feast, everyone would ask her to sing to them, which she happily obliged. Unlike most other Shudrakians, however, Mariuli did not feel at peace by simply living, breathing and dying the Shudrakian way, and sought meaning to her birth and life. When on her death bed, the thing she most lamented wasn't the impending doom or the fact she won't see her child anymore, but the fact she had lived out her life without fulfilling her supposed destiny and killing the one who was supposed to bring the Empire to ruin years following her death.
history:
Having been born on the same day as Taritta, the two have therefore been named soul sisters; an ancient Shudrak tradition dictating that two individuals born on the very same day are connected via their souls. Hence, ever following their birth, Taritta and Mariuli were inseparable. Throughout her early life, however, Mariuli had been plagued by ill health, spending much of her days bedridden and was therefore bestowed the role of a guardian; one of the two jobs widely claimed throughout the tribe, subserving her status amongst the tribeswomen as someone who's in charge of cooking, taking care of the kids and defending the settlement if necessary. At some point in her life, however, Mariuli had been blessed by the stars and was chosen as a Stargazer which granted her a very special task to fulfil, which she kept referring to as her "commandment". Following her revelation, Mariuli started to change according to Taritta; she started singing new songs unfamiliar to her fellow members of the tribe and continuously blessed the village with knowledge inaccessible to someone who was yet to set food outside the jungle and interact with the outside world. At some point, she had a child and gave birth to Utakata.

Due to her ill health, however, she soon found herself bedridden, this time however, on death's door. In her final moments, Mariuli conveyed her commandment as a Stargazer to Taritta, asking her to find the black haired and black eyed traveller who was supposedly about to trigger the Great Disaster which will plunge the Empire into ruin, and kill them, before plunging Taritta's knife deep into her chest, dying soon afterwards.
abilities_text:
Weak Constitution: Due to her frail body and ill health, Mariuli wasn't a very capable warrior. In fact, she was so incapable with the bow that if she was given one and was told to shoot a hundred arrows towards a target, she'd likely miss all hundred of them.

Stargazer (星詠み, Hoshiyomi): As a Stargazer, she was given commandments by the observers. It is due to this that she was granted bits of knowledge that she should not have been privy to, such as the songs sung by other stargazers. That said, it is also the cause of her seeming change in personality and nigh fanaticism.

intro: Mezoreia (メゾレイア), also known as the Cloud Dragon (雲龍 Unryū), is a Dragon that resides in the Sacred Vollachia Empire, and it is the Dragon responsible for the creation of the dragonkin, Madelyn Eschart. It played an antagonistic role in Arc 7 and Arc 8.
appearance: Mezoreia is a colossal Dragon with a white body said to be clad in pure white clouds and black eyes.
personality: As a dragonhusk, Mezoreia has lost most of its personality and capability of speech after creating a dragonkin. However, because Madelyn is still alive, Mezoreia has not lost its spirit, and it retains traces of its personality. It is shown to be highly protective of Madelyn, treating her as a daughter figure, and it has also shown to be friendly toward any visitors it may receive atop Mount Palzoa, assuming they were not hostile towards it or Madelyn. This being said, it has also shown to be willing to fight anyone who wants to take Madelyn away from it. Even after Madelyn left the mountain, it followed her around, hidden above the clouds, and though it ordinarily did not interfere in actions on the ground, it displayed no issues in following her commands or allowing her to take over its body. Also, similarly to Volcanica, Mezoreia appears to speak in a deific manner.
history:
At some point, Mezoreia used its power to create a young Dragonkin girl in exchange for becoming a dragonhusk. Alongside its kin, it lived on the peak of Mount Palzoa, and it spent its days caring for the girl.

After some time, a stranger and his flying dragon, Balleroy Temeglyph and Carillon, found Mezoreia and its Dragonkin after breaking through the cloud sea, something no other human had done before. Balleroy was surprised to see the young girl and the Dragon, and he started coming to spend time with her after this, giving the girl the name Madelyn after someone he once knew and giving her clothes, other gifts, and teaching her how to speak. Despite being initially wary of him, Mezoreia grew used to his presence and allowed him to keep returning to visit. Over time, Balleroy and Madelyn became close, with Madelyn coming to love Balleroy, and he sought to bring her outside of Mount Palzoa. However, disapproving of this, it resulted in a fight between him and Mezoreia. After a grueling fight, they made peace, and Balleroy stopped trying to take her away from the mountain. Eventually, however, he stopped visiting the summit altogether. When Madelyn decided to leave Mount Palzoa, rather than try to stop her, Mezoriea decided to follow her, hiding itself within the clouds above wherever she went.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
As a Dragon, Mezoreia is a naturally powerful being, capable of overwhelming the majority of warriors within seconds and bringing an end to a large number of people in an instant. Despite not being as old, nor nearly as powerful, as some others of its kind, it is still incredibly difficult to survive an encounter with Mezoreia, and only some of the most powerful of warriors can pose a threat to its might.

Physical Traits
Overwhelming Physical Might: As a Dragon, Mezoreia is incredibly strong and resistant to damage. Its natural physical might and size are powerful enough that it can deal tremendous damage with small movements, and it can even deal enough damage to kill most lesser beings with ease.

Talons: Mezoreia's talons are extremely sharp, said to be sharper than any run-of-the-mill blade. It has shown to be easily capable of tearing through Emilia's Ice Soldiers, which were made of ice so dense that they could be compared to steel.

Tail: Mezoreia can use its long tail to rupture the ground beneath it, and it can easily deal enough damage that someone of Garfiel Tinzel's strength would feel as if they were on the verge of death multiple times over.

Wings: Although ordinarily meant for assisting it with flight, Mezoreia's wings can easily be used to cause damage over a wide span, including handily dealing with densified ice created by Emilia.

Body Heat Increase: Mezoreia seems to be able to increase its body heat to the point that snow instantly evaporates around her. It allows it to resist cold-based attacks and fight in spite of it.

Dragon Scales: Mezoreia's scales are tremendously tough and grant it resistance to physical strikes. Although nowhere near as refined as Volcanica's scales, Mezoreia's are strong enough to allow it to resist the majority of damage dealt its way, including from strikes as powerful as Emilia's kicks armed with her ice weapons, and though he was eventually able to deal significant damage to Mezoreia, it was even capable of reducing how much damage a warrior of Garfiel's standing was able to deal it, such as escaping a powerful strike with only a nosebleed.

Dragon Halo: Mezoreia's halo allows Mezoreia to withstand strikes from magic. Although nowhere near as refined as Volcanica's halo, it provides enough defense to easily protect it from magic as strong as Emilia's.

Magic
Heavenly Mana: The mana held within Mezoreia is so powerful and vast that it is both highly destructive as well as capable of extending its command over the very skies.

Flight: Dragons use their mana to fly while using their wings to assist in their flight. Mezoreia flight speed is rather high, being compared to an arrow shot at full force, and moments after taking off, it was able to cross the entirety of the Imperial Capital and reach the Crystal Palace from the bastions in mere moments.

Dragon Breath: Mezoreia’s breath creates a white beam of light that can easily alter terrain. Upon hitting its target, the beam creates a powerful shockwave that makes the ground rise and causes buildings to rip from their foundations. If necessary, Mezoreia is capable of firing off multiple weaker but consecutive blasts.

Weather Manipulation: As the Cloud Dragon, it could spread its mana across the heavens in order to generate and manipulate clouds. It usually uses this to hide its form while it flies in the sky. However, it is also capable of concentrating all of its mana through the clouds and making them converge at one point, creating a funnel of thunderclouds that contained enough power to erase both the Imperial Capital. The full extent of this, however, was not revealed, as it was prevented prematurely.

Wind Manipulation: Mezoreia is capable of manipulating the wind, generating attacks with such force that it can easily gouge out the ground and kill anything caught up in it.

history:
Omega in Wonderland
Mikli grew up in the same village as Zank Metley, and the two joined the Gustekan Church, raising their strength and ranks together until eventually, the two became Temple Knights. After meeting the Holy King, they suggested that the two marry, which they accepted. However, before they could do so, Mikli was ordered to hunt a heretic, leading her to confronting them in Sylphoa. Later, after Omega's party arrived in town, Lilac let Omega confront Mikli, leading to a small scuffle between her and the Witches of Sin, which ended in both a quick loss and the loss of her blessing. Afterward, Zank, who had volunteered to retrieve her, took her with him, where she supposedly would lose her position as a Temple Knight for losing her blessing.

name: Maqueena
intro: Maqueena (マクウィナ) is a bard who previously masqueraded as a con artist.
appearance: Maqueena is a young woman with wavy brown hair.
personality: Maqueena is an eccentric girl who is easily frightened, overly judgmental, and quick to complain or deride people if they are not to her liking. However, she possesses a cunning and shrewd wit, having been the only known individual who discovered Coatl's past profession. She puts her self-interest first, being open to mistreating, blackmailing, and even drugging strangers for her own benefit. Despite trying to be a bard, her singing capabilities are completely lacking.
history:
One Wild Night
To get by as a resident of Gusteko, Maqueena chose to become a con artist. She outwardly pretended to be a bard as a front for her true profession, and at some point, she perceived the connection between Coatl and the Ice Thieves that accidentally caused an avalanche in the town of Leanotte. She blackmailed the man in the wake of her discoverey and extorted money from him countless times, becoming more adjusted to the layout of the church he resided in as well as the route to and from it with each visit. One day, she arrived at the church to seek out Coatl, only to discover that he was nowhere to be found. Over the course of the day, a blizzard would form, and several more people would enter the church; the second to enter was Podoso, the third was Admonsah, followed by Omega and her group with Noelle Tuérico.

After a near death encounter with one of Admonsah's throwing knives, Maqueena acquainted herself with everyone and told the story of Coatl's heroism with her subpar skills as a bard. Since the ongoing blizzard left the group stuck in the church, she attempted to retrieve Coatl's money by herself, but was accompanied by Podoso, much to her reluctance. Trellock arrived at the church around the time she was entering the church's hidden basement, and shortly afterward, she screamed upon the discovery that Coatl had been murdered, inciting a sense of horror in her and everyone else, and quickly took the key to his safe before the others could arrive. As Omega attempted to piece together the circumstances of Coatl's death, Maqueena was in shock to learn of the recent serial murders and objected to the group's quick acceptance of Admonsah when his background and his killing done in self-defense were deduced.

Shortly after Maqueena heard Omega's supposition that Coatl's murderer had the key to his safe, she used pollen from the sleeping flower, Muskrim, to make everyone fall unconscious and quickly attempted to make a getaway. However, she was pursued by Noelle, a survivor from Leanotte's avalanche who joined the Gustekan Church as an Itinerant Preacher to seek revenge against the Ice Thieves for their actions. She was under the misconception that Maqueena was one of their members and made an attempt on her life until Omega prevented her from being killed. Omega revealed Maqueena's true profession and gave Noelle an ultimatum while manifesting her true form, ultimately resulting in nobody dying. The next day, Maqueena was bound by a rope for her crimes and taken to Leanotte by Podoso and Admonsah, swearing that she would live a simple life and practice being a bard from then on.

intro: Leonardo Baroness (リオナルド・バロネス) is a doctor who specializes in working with blood.
appearance:
Leonardo is a scrawny bat human with lifeless grey hair, morbidly pale, dry skin, and visible bones, all of which give him the impression of appear like a moving corpse. He has thin fingers and wears a cloak with countless vials of blood within. His erratic eyes contain a sinister gleam that, by intuition, is only held by people who are not sane.

Upon absorbing the vials of rare blood he had on his person, Leonardo was transformed into a monster-like large mass of liquid blood that assimilated its surroundings into its body.
personality: Leonardo is a doctor who obsesses over unravelling the hidden mysteries of blood to bring the world salvation. He prides himself on his research. As a bat human, Leonardo has fondness for sucking blood and dislikes wasting it to the point that he will lick up any drops of blood from the ground without hesitation.
history:
Golden Siblings
The Blood Sample Collector Leonardo Baroness dedicated his research to understanding the mysteries quality of rare blood. He eventually started to work closely with Hayden Garo and discovered how to manipulate the lightbugs of Costuul.

When Hayden brought the kidnapped Frederica Baumann to their base, Leonardo introduced himself to the woman and openly his feelings on the importance of blood. As a consequence for intimidating Frederica, Hayden grabbed Leonardo's face for a short period of time and rushed the doctor to finish his duty. However, before Leonardo could finish his job and allow Hayden to return to his castle with Frederica, Garfiel and Clind arrived to save her. Clind then confronted Leonardo after ensuring Frederica's freedom. As a result of his obsession with acquiring Frederica's rare blood, the doctor was driven to absorb the vials of blood he had collected into his body, transforming him into a giant liquid mass of blood.
