name: Lynek
first_light_novel: Iris and the King of Thorns
intro: Lynek (リネック) was the teacher of Iris. A mole person who once obeyed Eugard Vollachia after he and the pack of demi-humans he belonged to were forced into servitude, he was attributed as having “assisted” Volcas in the murder of Iris, leading the emperor to decree the execution of all wolf people and mole people. To avoid his murder as a result of Eugard's decree, he spent the rest of his life in exile on the Gladiator Island Ginunhive.
appearance: Lynek was a mole person who had round eyes and a large nose that took up half of his face.
personality: Lynek was a knowledgeable man with the skill to act as a tutor and a healer. Greatly considerate of people and their feelings, he regularly made an effort to acknowledge and accommodate them. He downplayed his own expertise and skills, emphasizing that, with his knowledge, other people could easily fulfill his roles. Despite recognizing himself as Iris's enemy, Lynek treated her with the utmost sincerity, feeling gratitude and profound regret towards her as a result of her forgiveness of his and his pack's actions. Over time, he grew concerned for her wellbeing and began to prioritize her and Eugard's happiness over his own pack, going so far as to ask for Iris's forgiveness when he perceived himself as the cause of their rift and to brew what was effectively a poison that would slowly kill her because she wished for it.
history:
Lynek was one of the members of the “pack” led by Volcas. He was among the bandits who attacked a village within the Elcanti Domain in a retaliatory attack to avenge their comrades that had been slain by the domain's forces. Given the role of directly managing their food supply and stolen goods, he never laid hands on any of the villagers. Rather than facing execution, Iris forgave the pack members and implored Eugard to spare their lives, which he accepted. As a consequence of their defeat, Lynek and the others were bound by Collars of Subservience and conscripted into a disciplinary unit obligated to serve the Elcanti Domain. On top of having the position of a healer in the disciplinary unit, Lynek was given the additional role to act as Iris's teacher, frequently spending his time with her. He educated her in subjects such as proper etiquette. Volcas often abruptly disturbed the two, chiming in by bantering with Iris. After Terriola Goldario joined their faction, he observed the two women developing a positive relationship with one another.

As the Imperial Selection Ceremony began, Iris was afflicted with a fever, leaving Lynek to temporarily act as her nurse while the others he delegated his healing knowledge to took his place in the disciplinary unit. He was ordered by Eugard to contact him with any updates about Iris's status, no matter how trivial. Although he offered her the opportunity to speak with Eugard over a Conversation Mirror, she refused because of how they had contributed to his isolation. They were paid a visit by Whitaker Goldario, who had brought valuable medicinal herbs as a gift for Iris, entrusting their use to Lynek. At Whitaker's request, Lynek exited the room, and Iris was given an explanation of the Battle Craze Syndrome she had contracted and that the herbs would be used to cure her.

Lynek boiled the herbs to brew the medicine that would cure Iris. Upon being cured, Lynek cried tears of relief, and Iris set her sights on reuniting with Eugard. Unbeknownst to them, the Battle Craze Syndrome had been what prevented Iris from falling victim to Eugard's Curse of Thorns, and she was assaulted by the binding of thorns upon their reunion. Lynek blamed himself for Iris's newfound inability to approach Eugard, earnestly apologizing to her. Some time later, while Volcas and Iris were speaking, Lynek bore news to her, revealing that Whitaker Goldario had launched a rebellion in tandem with the Nine Divine Generals against Eugard, intending to murder him by setting fire to the Imperial Residence in the Imperial Capital.

To return to Eugard's side and encourage him to take arms against Whitaker, who planned to install himself on the throne once the King of Thorns was killed, Iris requested Lynek to use the herbs he had been gifted to create a medicine that would simulate the effects of Battle Craze Syndrome, which he reluctantly accepted after Volcas demanded an explanation from her. With Iris's encouragement, Eugard swiftly extinguished the lives of the Nine Divine Generals and Whitaker, putting a stop to the revolt, and his coronation proceeded as planned, being crowned as emperor by his beloved. Having been within the range of the Curse of Thorns for an extended period of time, Iris began to cough up blood when she returned to her quarters. Lynek warned her that she was pushing herself too hard, feeling guilty for creating a poison that was whittling down her life. Volcas, who was with the two, told Iris he was siding with her above all else, rather than with the Vollachia Empire, and that Eugard had no issue with his loyalties, giving her a cup of water after saying this. Though tolerating her selfishness despite the risk to her life, Volcas expressed genuine concern for her mind and body. Lynek rejected her proposal to teach her how to brew it herself, as she would not have been able to make it even if she had learned how to, yet he also had the responsibility of complying with her selfish request in order to remain with Eugard, placing him in a predicament where he would have had to continue bestowing her with poison out of obligation. Volcas delivered her a gentle insult, and Iris proceeded to rest in order to conserve her energy in order to interact with her beloved Eugard.

To prevent Iris from having to suffer from the poison, Volcas murdered her, and he was promptly eliminated by Eugard upon his discovery of the scene. As a result, Eugard would come to decree the execution of all wolf people and mole people, attributing Lynek as having purportedly aided in Iris's murder even though Volcas made his decision alone. Following a conversation with Eugard at Iris's funeral, Terriola spoke with Lynek, whom she had kept hidden to brew poison for her and to protect him from the imminent policy that decreed the execution of all wolf people and mole people. Despite the decree, Lynek had no words of apology for his brethren, as he and Volcas had made their decisions, and he chose to prioritize Eugard and Iris over his pack. She prepared a refuge for him at the Gladiator Island surrounded by Lake Violane and considered turning it into a prison for convicts to act as a distraction for him. Affirming to him that she had not spoken of her feelings for Eugard to him so she would not be a thief like her brother, the Thief Emperor, she wished Lynek well, and he set off for Lake Violane. For the rest of his life, Lynek made various poisons and medicines at the Gladiator Island.
abilities_text: Healing Skills: Although not trained in magic, Lynek had the skill to be considered a healer with an irreplaceable role in the disciplinary unit. He could brew various medicines and poisons and had the knowledge to create even complex brews. With the rare herbs he was given by Whitaker, he was able to brew both a medicine that cured Iris's Batte Craze Syndrome and a poison that simulated its effects.

name: Mireille Hetia
relatives: Edmon Quayle (father) ; Nananna Pezza (half-sister)
first_light_novel: The Witch's After Tea Party / Witch Trials Part 2
intro: Mireille Hetia (ミレイユ・ヘティア) is a former secretary of Edmon Quayle.
appearance: Mireille is a woman with long blue hair who gives off an intelligent impression.
history:
Early Life
Mireille was born to an affair between the Limbus council representative, Edmon Quayle, and her mother. However, Edmon banished her mother, and she came to despise both Edmon and the town of Limbus. When she was young, she met an elderly healer who lived on the outskirts of Limbus. There, she received her guidance, similar to her half-sister, Nananna Pezza. Because of this, she later became a civil official. At an unknown point in time, she received an evil spirit.

Witch Trials
One day, because of an illness that had taken hold of Limbus, numerous people found their lives in danger, but thanks to the elderly healer coming up with an appropriate medicine, lives were saved and the illness vanished. However, a rumor declared that she started the illness in order to provide the solution and increase her reputation. She was then declared a Witch and burned to death. Following the healer's death, the council members began to get rid of anyone the council considered inconvenient, including the noble who had once taken the healer's cure, and they declared it the response of a Witch, resulting in the subsequent Witch Hunts. At some point around this time, Mireille was appointed to be a subordinate to a government official in Limbus, where she learned of the healer's execution, and she began committing murders with her spiritual arts in the town against relatives of the council members. Later, Nananna was sent to deal with the strange killings in Limbus, where, having heard about the execution of the elderly healer as well, Nananna conspired with Mireille to bring down their father and the people of Limbus for their transgressions, with Mireille getting rid of any other officials who came to the town.

On the night that the Omega Party appeared, they decided to assist in the Witch Hunt for a person named Piditz who had been tipped off as a Witch, and Nananna wanted him taken into custody only. When they later spotted Piditz and chased after him, Omega split off to corner him, only to find Mireille using her spiritual arts to kill Piditz. Thanks to being near the body, Omega was quickly turned into a scapegoat and declared a Witch so that Mireille could cover up her kill and at least prevent her from getting in the way of her and Nananna's revenge, and Omega was taken into custody. Later, Colette visits Omega, and they point out that killings began before the party arrived, which should clear Omega's name, but instead, Mireille decides to have her executed anyway, and Palmyra objects to Edmon. To clear their names, Colette states that they should find the real culprit for the murders. Lilac and Colette go to gather information around the town, and they meet with Mireille, who explained to them how the hunts started.

The next day, the Witch Trial is being held for Omega, overseen by Nananna and the Town Hall, with Mireille present as well, while Palmyra acts as Omega's attorney. Despite her arguments, Edmon counter with his supposed knowledge of the Witches and Omega's chatter does not help. Colette speaks up and claims that she believes that things will not go as the council claims, as people will begin to notice that the entire event seems off, which resounds with the townsfolk. Because of this, Palmyra claims that there is a conspiracy, which Edmon fights against and asks for Nananna's assistance. Because she sides with the town, Lilac and Shion believe her to be part of the conspiracy, and they decide to use their dream arts to influence the people's mental states. Palmyra then claims that the council is using the Witch rumors to get rid of inconvenient people, which Edmon also fights against, though is quickly silenced when she states she heard it herself from a council member and declares that there is no Witch. Unfortunately, Omega claims otherwise.

Despite angering Palmyra, Omega decides to clear things up by declaring that there were two conspiracies taking place in town. Despite Nananna trying to prevent her from talking, Omega quickly ignores her and explains that many of the victims were relatives of council members, and she claims that Nananna is the second conspirator, calling her the bastard child of Edmon whose mother was banished from the town, and as a result, she despised the town. Noelle Tuérico later appears and confirms that her actions were in response to the death of the elderly healer, and she claims that Nananna tried to remove her from the trial by knocking her out since her only ire was with Limbus. Afterward, Noelle declares that the secretary, Mireille, was helping Nananna, as she was a bastard child of Edmon as well, and she stated how the corpses of Piditz and other people connected to the council and other outside officials were already dumped in a hole. Omega also declares that she witnessed Mireille killing Piditz. Enraged, Mireille uses her spiritual arts to char Edmond's arm with blue fire, and with the intent of killing the entire council, surrounds the council with blue fire, and she and Nananna stand against them. Although Omega is fine with leaving things as they are and taking their leave, Colette states she doesn't want things to end like this, and Omega decides to end the fighting in response to her plea, burning through her restraints and declaring herself a Witch.

Later, as Omega's party begins to leave the town, Noelle says her goodbyes to Nananna, and it is declared that the evil spirit accompanying Mireille will be disposed of. Likewise, it is claimed that Edmon's position is under threat with both his severe injuries and the loss of the citizens' trust, and Mireille claims she was mistaken about real Witches.

However, this spirit was capable of corrupting her. Following the events in Limbus, she disposed of the evil spirit.

name_jp: メルティ・プリスティス

intro: Melty Pristis (メルティ・プリスティス), also known by her codename White Sheep, is a member of the Six Tongues and a defector of the Beloved Children. She plays a supporting role in Arc 10.
appearance: Melty is a young woman roughly a year or two younger than Natsuki Subaru. She has indigo hair done up on both sides, large, round, golden eyes emanating a powerful will, a well proportioned face with an air of fragility to it. She wears a black suit with a white collared shirt and a thin tie. Before joining the Six Tongues, she would ordinarily wear clothes reminiscent of the cognitive disruption cloak. Later, she briefly wears a light blue evening dress.
personality:
Melty is a somewhat timid young woman who is willing to apologize for her comrades behavior. Though she tries to restrain the changes in her expression, she is not suited to it and has a bad poker face, and she is aware of it. Furthermore, she is quick to worry about the safety of other people, and when people are injured, she wants to assist however she can, agreeing with the sentiments of Subaru that it is best to have as few casualties as possible. She does not like conflict, and from the perspective of Subaru, the inherent good nature he perceives her as having is not very suited to an organization like the Six Tongues.

At times, when Melty becomes excited, she becomes somewhat impatient, has a hard time controlling her heightened emotions, and becomes somewhat talkative. This is particularly the case after meeting Subaru, who was indirectly responsible for allowing her to escape from her oppressor, as she was quick to display her gratitude toward him and started speaking excitedly over what he had done for her. Similarly, she has also been moved by his behavior and decisiveness to assist other people.

Despite her kind-hearted nature, Melty has been deeply traumatized by her time serving under Capella Emerada Lugunica, who has not only become the object of terror for her, but also cannot break the habit of calling her Mama, even after escaping from her. Due to her influence, Melty had low self-esteem. However, though it was forced out of her by Black Dog, she was able to build up her courage to escape from her, something that she wishes she could have recognized sooner. Similarly, she is reluctant to use her power on people, having hesitated to use it on Subaru multiple times and feeling guilty afterward. Because of the way her ability works, it makes her hesitant to touch or get close to people, as she feels as though she is overwriting their will with what she wants. This being said, she is willing to use her power on her own allies if need be in order to help people, having almost attempted to do so against her employer, Russell Fellow, if not for Black Dog's interference.
history: At an unknown point in time, Melty, alongside Black Dog, became subservient to Capella, who forced them to refer to her as Mama and work as part of her Beloved Children. It is unknown how long they worked for her, but Melty was stationed within the Divine Dragon Church. However, following the Subjugation of Sloth led by Subaru, they were provided a chance to escape from the Beloved Children as Mama was panicked. Afterward, they joined the Six Tongues, taking on the names of "Black Dog" and "White Sheep", and for the next year, the managed to thwart several of the Beloved Children's plans.
abilities_text:
Magic
According to Melty, she is capable of performing magic. However, it is unknown what attribute she has an affinity for and how proficient she is with magic.

Other
Bewitchment (人誑し, Hitotarashi): Melty's power allows her to leverage already existing emotions within a person and nudge them toward making a decision in accordance with her wishes or needs. This can allow those she targets to make decisions much faster than they ordinarily would. In order for her to use her power, she must first place her hands on the target, and then she must speak to them, either casually asking questions or pleading with them her desires. However, her power cannot force a person to do something that they would absolutely refuse to do. Furthermore, it is possible for someone to completely overcome her power's influence through outside stimulus, whether directly or indirectly.

Equipment
Conversation Mirror (対話鏡, Taiwa-kyō): Melty has a Conversation Mirror on her person which allows her to get in touch with her allies.
Cognitive Disruption Cloak: Melty has been lent a cloak with cognitive disruption built into it, allowing her to obscure her features from others.
Staff: Melty owns a staff that is roughly the length of a baton which she uses for defense.
Dagger: Melty keeps a dagger on her person for self-defense.

relatives: Lye Batenkaitos (son) ; Roy Alphard (son) ; Rui Arneb (daughter)
intro: Leilani Alnair (レイラニ・アルナイル) was a Sin Archbishop of the Witch Cult, representing Gluttony.
appearance: Leilani had brown hair cut to shoulder length, shihaku eyes, and a loose, black robe that concealed her figure. She had a defined bump size as a result of her pregnancy. From the perspective of Shaula, Leilani's appearance was ordinary and she had no physical features that stood out. However, from Leiliani's own point of view, she saw herself as an ugly woman.
history:
At some point in time, Leilani inherited the Witch Factor of Gluttony and was selected to be the Sin Archbishop of Gluttony. For over 3 years, she was pregnant with her children, preventing them from being born from sheer force of will.

Scorpion Tale
At some point, following her gospel, a group of over 900 people crossed the Augria Sand Dunes with her in an attempt to reach the Pleiades Watchtower. However, the group faced complete annihilation at the hands of witchbeasts, leaving only Leilani after she was saved by Shaula. Afterward, she was brought to the tower, and Shaula would allow her to stay until she gave birth. Although she attempted to dismiss Leilani, she consistently acted self-deprecatingly humble before her, and her Authority attempted to work its way toward replacing her memories with "Leilani". Over time, once Leilani believed that her Authority had fully consumed her, she attempted to have Shaula listen to her and claimed that she was the most important person in Shaula's life. However, her Authority did not overwrite Shaula's devotion toward Flugel, and as punishment, Shaula shot her with one of her needles in her midsection, killing one of her unborn children. Afterward, she removed her from the tower and left her just outside of the Sand Time barrier with some provisions in an attempt to leave her a chance to survive. When she was found by travelers, she attempted to have them save her by getting rid of her children, believing that she could always just have others if necessary. However, because of her injuries, her words were misunderstood, and the travelers instead saved her remaining two children at the cost of Leilani's remaining life, and she died while continuing to call herself pitiful.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
Despite being a Sin Archbishop, Leilani was rather weak, with minimal combat skill and had to rely on outside help to survive against the likes of witchbeasts. However, she was still incredibly dangerous thanks to the brainwashing effect of her Authority, and because of that, she had the capacity to bring ruin to the lives of many just by existing, in a way similar to Carmilla.

Authority
As the Sin Archbishop of Gluttony, Leilani was a user of the Authority of Gluttony (暴食の権能, Bōshoku no Ken'nō) and was a compatible holder of its corresponding Witch Factor.

Overeating (過食, Kashoku): The prerequisite to trigger Leilani's Authority was for someone to show her pity. Once she was pitied by someone, the Authority of Overeating would activate, continually coercing pity from its victims. Those who were subjected to Overeating were left with “bite marks” that, little by little, gradually expanded until every single person within the memories of a victim's life was painted over by the existence of “Leilani”. That being said, as Leilani's presence only gradually grew within a target, the process of Overeating was required take place over a prolonged period of time. The process of Overeating began by overwriting a target's memories of an insignificant acquaintance, and over time, it incrementally painted over people with increasing significance in a target's life until “Leilani” replaced the most important people who were connected to a victim's reason for living and whom the victim treasured. By the time the process was complete, “Leilani” painted over every person in a victim's memories, regardless of whether they were someone the victim disliked, someone the victim was close to, or someone whom the victim exhibited love towards. Her existence also replaced every aspect of people from a victim's memories, including their faces, voices, and scents. Those who were subjected to Overeating saw Leilani as a friend, a mentor, a lover, and the most important person to them, and as such, they would unhesitatingly follow her wherever she went, using their bodies as shields and sacrificing their lives to protect her from any danger that came her way.

When the process of Overeating had progressed far enough, the memories within a victim would have every emotion lined with the memory of “Leilani” and likely contained multiple versions of her at once within them, but due to the Authority's effects, Leilani's victims failed to notice it, as they never doubted the validity of the precious memories within themselves, even though they had been revised. Furthermore, to cause people to pity her as a means to invoke her power, Leilani used her pregnancy to take advantage of people's pity towards pregnant women, going so far as to even prevent her children from being born for over three years through sheer force of will all to maintain her state. However, Leilani found opponents who were not susceptible to words and common sense, such as Shaula, to be the greatest danger to her by nature. In the case of Shaula, Overeating's ability was unable to overwrite her sheer devotion and love toward Flugel. Once Shaula was separated from Leilani, the Authority's effects came undone, though it is unknown if it was brought about by the user's death or if Overeating's effects stopped when the two were apart.

Equipment
Gospel (福音, Fukuin): As a member of the Witch Cult, Leilani was the owner of a copy of a Gospel. Each Gospel was a replica of the Book of Wisdom, a book that had been in the possession of the Witch of Greed, Echidna. The Book of Wisdom would provide exact details of future events concerning the Witch of Greed, essentially bestowing Echidna with a form of precognition. Unlike the original Book of Wisdom, the Witch Cult's Gospels are imperfect replicas, meaning that, although they detail the future of its owner, the events conveyed are subject to change and the information provided was often up for interpretation. The Gospels take the form of small black books that can only be read by their owners.
