intro: Regulus Corneas (レグルス・コルニアス) was a Sin Archbishop of the Witch Cult, representing Greed. He debuted in a small scene of Arc 3 alongside Lye Batenkaitos as a tertiary antagonist, where he took on Crusch's military convoy, completely decimating it alongside its passengers, which included Rem. Later, he appeared in Emilia's first trial during the events of Arc 4, where he played an antagonistic role under Pandora's in the lead-up to the Permafrost of Elior Forest, and he also appeared as one of the main antagonists of Arc 5.
appearance:
Regulus's face had no eye-catching features, and he had golden eyes that were usually murky and disinterested but started to sparkle when he passionately engaged in his long monologues. His modestly handsome face wasn't particularly attractive or unattractive, while his hair was neither short nor long and without a distinct style, however, it was naturally white despite his youthful appearance. Regulus' white skin that lacked any semblance of a tan, coupled with his white hair and predominately white clothing, made him seem as though he was the epitome of the color white. In fact, the complete devoid of color exhibited by Regulus' physical appearance gave him the impression of a sickly person of which all color had drained away.

Regulus' primary attire primary piece of clothing was a pure-white greca-style overcoat that reached down to his ankles and had golden-edged cuffs, a set of five golden buttons running down the torso of his center front that usually ensured that the coat was closed above the hipline, and golden-highlighted edging. The inside of the coat was black and featured vertical golden stripes travelling down the entire coat. The most striking part of his coat was the opulent gold and black high-neck collar it sported that had the symbol for infinity inscribed on it, perhaps reflecting the nature of Regulus' Authority. Under his coat, he wore a long-sleeved deep-blue-colored dress shirt, white snow-white trousers, and a pair of white shoes, the latter two of which were both the same shade as his hair and overcoat. Usually, only the cuffs of the dress shirt could be seen as Regulus's long overcoat tended to obscure it almost completely. Regulus had a single deep-blue teardrop-shaped earring that was the same color as his dress shirt and dangled from his right earlobe thanks to a thin gold chain attaching it.

During the wedding that he attempted to have with Emilia in Arc 5, Regulus displayed himself in a far more formal wedding uniform. He chose to wear a white tuxedo with a white color palette, the same as his normal uniform. The tuxedo had a long cape-like backside that nearly went down to his heels. In addition, Regulus wore a blue and white striped undershirt adorned with a black and gold striped ribbon, white gloves, and white shoes.
personality:
Regulus was talkative, and tended to describe himself as unselfish, despite representing Greed. He would often go on and on about trivial matters in the most incoherent ways, usually leaving the other party confused and/or unable to follow his thoughts, ideals and values. Due to his extremely prideful personality, however, he often forced his own selfishness on others and tried to justify it. If his opponents had said something that went against his opinions and beliefs, he would find unreasonable faults in them, gradually becoming angry while accusing them of "violating his rights", before attacking and killing them without mercy or second thought. Despite his self-proclaimed pacifistic nature, he would not hesitate to attack, harm or kill someone, as to him, the act of taking away what is his was the most abhorrent and disgusting thing a person could do. He often showed complete ignorance for other individuals' values and exercised extremely selfish behaviors. This is best showcased when Regulus became unreasonably infuriated at Rem when she prepared to defend herself after explicitly telling her that he abhors fighting, which contradicts the fact that he mercilessly slaughtered multiple convoys full of wounded people just minutes prior to Rem's battle with him and Lye Batenkaitos. Regulus is incredibly hypocritical and wouldn't hesitate to renege his own words and promises, giving further evidence of his sociopathic nature.

He was extremely prideful and viewed himself as a "divine being" or "the most satisfied existence in the world", which greatly hindered his assessment of people, no matter if they were his enemies or allies, to the point he would make light of the Sword Saint, mocking him and calling him "a moniker of some guy who knows of nothing but swinging a sword". He often pointed out his dislike for needlessly involving himself with others and vice versa, stating he would be perfectly happy if people never paid attention to him and/or bothered him. Despite that, he has been shown to have conversed with people without initiating a conflict with the opposite party, until he got his "rights violated", which instantly changed his mood for the worse and prompted him to take action against them. His hot-tempered personality often resulted in unneeded fights. However, due to his overwhelmingly powerful Authority of Greed, he always came out victorious and unharmed, even against ridiculously strong opponents such as the Vollachia's strongest Kurgan. Due to his long life as a Sin Archbishop without ever getting his life seriously threatened, he never matured intellectually or emotionally; he disclosed his secret to Subaru, who in turn was able to connect all the dots and unravel his formidable Authority, allowing Reinhard to deal the finishing blow. In his final moments, Regulus revealed how he hated being looked down upon or laughed at, going even as far as saying he became a Sin Archbishop just so he could protect himself from such people; whoever offended him or his wives would ultimately be slain for the transgression, no matter their acquaintanceship with him. Regulus never realized his "sins", even in the final moments leading to his demise. His view on the world was corrupt and distorted from the very beginning until the bitter end. His final cries were full of hatred, wishing for the whole of humanity to disappear forever.

Having been born with a corrupt and distorted mindset, Regulus seemingly did not perceive kindness, love and affection in the same way as a normal person would have; it was strongly suggested that he lacked empathy and was impulsive, narcissistic and sociopathic. He took everything as a personal assault and critique, never developed a "human side", which in turn made him feel like everyone was against him, pitying and loathing his very existence. With time, Regulus himself seemingly developed a paranoid personality which completely dulled his perception of the world around him. After receiving the Witch Factor of Greed, Regulus gained an extreme form of escapism; he slaughtered everyone who pitied him, destroyed everything that bothered him and protected only the things he deemed important and necessary for his ideal and dream life. With that, Regulus was given an opportunity to be able to escape the dull, depressing and detested world he was brought into, and create a new world with himself at the top and surrounded by his subjects/wives; his "cherished kingdom". He spent the following century trying to fulfill his Greed, which he never achieved. He insistently attempted to justify to himself that he was not greedy and denied any faults towards his character, until his bitter and watery end.
history:
Early Life
More than 100 years ago, Regulus used to live with his family in a village of a country outside the Four Great Nations. His father was an alcoholic yet tried to be a good father, his mother complained about bad earnings but apologized for it occasionally, and his two brothers who were sometimes mean to him but gave him their share of their meal if he accidentally spilled his. At an unspecified point in his life, Regulus was chosen as a Sin Archbishop and obtained the Witch Factor of Greed. In accordance with his deepest desires, he developed the overpowered Authority of Greed, which he used in the following century of his life. Regulus subsequently killed his entire family, then the villagers who looked down on him, followed by the people from the nearby town who pushed his family into such peril, and finally, his entire home country. He broke the mind of his childhood love, slaughtered her family, and forced her to marry him, thus compelling her to become his wife. Only after having committed such atrocities did Regulus finally see a way to live: free of all worries, not needing anything as he considered himself satisfied as he was. However, she eventually committed suicide, sneering in her last moments. Happening across this, Regulus buried and made a grave for her, and began to take many wives after her, forcing each and every one of them to remain expressionless and never smile like his childhood friend did.

At some point in the past, Regulus got hold of a small black box, similar to the one Petelgeuse Romanée-Conti used. It is unknown if it was the exact same box or a different one. Regulus, however, did know what was inside of it when Petelgeuse showed it to him during the events of the Elior Forest battle, suggesting the box Regulus once held contained either the Witch Factor of Greed or Sloth.

In the following years, Regulus became the Sin Archbishop of Greed, joining the Witch Cult where he became the leader of the radical faction. Familiarizing himself with the doctrine of the Cult and its members, Regulus met Petelgeuse, the leader of the now-forgotten moderate faction. It's safe to assume the two didn't harbor a friendly relationship although they occasionally cooperated along with the other Sin Archbishops. Just like other high-ranking members of the Witch Cult took care of their own eccentric goals, Regulus spent his free time carefully and meticulously search of beautiful women he'd forcefully marry and spend his days with, before eventually watching them die, be it from natural or unnatural causes, more often than not being the one who delivered their deaths.

Permafrost of Elior Forest
Roughly 100 years before the events of the main story, Regulus participated in the attack of the elven village in Elior Forest along with Pandora, cooperating with her to collect the elf Fortuna as his 79th wife. With the pair revealing their malicious intentions, Petelgeuse, who was helping the elves in the forest, ordered Fortuna to run with her niece Emilia. Regulus then proceeded to have a one-sided battle with Petelgeuse who just took in the Witch Factor of Sloth, cutting Petelgeuse's right arm off and severely wounding and ruining his legs by throwing dirt at him, in a relatively short notice. Just before he was about to deal the finishing blow by smashing Petelgeuse's head open, Fortuna interrupted him, which greatly angered him. When Pandora calmly asked him to spare Petelgeuse's life, he lashed back at her, throwing dirt at her, killing her instantly. Soon after, Pandora used her Authority of Vainglory to erase her death from ever happening and proceeded to remove Regulus's presence from the forest and sent him back to his mansion, which reverted the damage he had dealt to Petelgeuse and Elior Forest.

Finale of the Eight Arms
More than a decade before Subaru's arrival, Regulus single-handedly took down a heavily fortified Vollachian city of Garkla, housing thousands of soldiers, as well as the Vollachian hero Kurgan. Rumor has it that at the time, a meteor supposedly belonging to one of the Witches of Sin was located in the city itself. It is not known if the Meteor was actually present or if it was only an excuse to drive the Witch Cult to take action.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
Regulus is easily one of the strongest characters introduced in the series, a threat capable of going toe to toe with even Reinhard van Astrea due to the effective invincibility and generally highly destructive and surprisingly versatile power granted to him by his Authority. In fact, if not for Subaru and his knowledge of the stars, it is highly likely that Regulus would never have been killed, even with Reinhard as his opponent. According to the author, not only is he one of the strongest characters in the series, but he has even claimed that he would be the sole survivor in the event that the calamitous Authority wielding Witches and Sin Archbishops ever clashed.

Authority
Regulus was the previous holder of the Witch Factor of Greed and was able to use its respective Authority. His Authority granted him abilities related to the time of a person or object and the ability to pass his heart unto the people who are a part of his "kingdom".

Lion's Heart (獅子の心臓, Shishi no Shinzō): With Lion's Heart, Regulus was allowed to stop the time of his own body, and of anything he touched. By applying Lion's Heart to his body, he became unaffected by any physical phenomena, including age, hunger, thirst, excretion of bodily waste, getting wet, being frozen, or taking damage, whether physically or magically. Essentially, his power made him both un-aging, invincible, and prevented all physical phenomena from interacting with him, granting himself freedom from the constraints of concepts like gravity, air resistance, conservation of momentum, and effectively any physical rules and concepts of the world. The same thing was true of anything else he applied his power to, as by preventing the concepts of the world from interfering with these objects, they could pass through and destroy anything, creating absurdly powerful attacks capable of completely bypassing any defense while simultaneously moving at speeds beyond comprehension. The aftereffects of such attacks could easily sever flesh, and entire convoys could be destroyed by a single attack. Traps like pitfalls with some form of cover also become ineffective, as by standing on the cover and stopping its time, he could walk on it as if it were solid ground. While he was in this state, he could be somewhat interacted with, and once he began to fight seriously, he was capable of rejecting and completely ignoring everything. By simply walking into a building or even a massive wall of ice, he would breeze through them, leaving only a hole behind. In the event he attempted to walk or properly interact with other physical constructs or bodies, he needed to stop the time of the ground or said things around him. Likewise, by stopping time on his own body, it was capable of piercing right through anything, including buildings, the ground, his clothes, or other people. The main drawback to Lion's Heart was that, by stopping the time of his body, Regulus's heart stopped beating, limiting how long he could stop his own body's time. Thus, Regulus was required to pair Lion's Heart with his second ability, Little King, in order to maintain his invincibility. Keeping Lion's Heart active for longer than five seconds without Little King made him experience excruciating pain, and although he never went beyond five seconds, going as long as ten seconds was likely impossible. Furthermore, it became difficult for Regulus to manipulate objects beyond his own body when Little King was not in use.
thumb|right|250px|Regulus cutting Petelgeuse's arm off by simply lifting his own right hand.
Wind imbued with Lion's Heart: Regulus is able to apply his power to even the small gusts of wind typically generated by nature or movement. By doing so, he can weaponize it like a flying slash that can easily sever limb from body, as he did to both Petelgeuse and Crusch. On a larger scale, he can even create a bomb-like effect that could easily kill a large number of people at once and completely destroy things like dragon carriages with ease. However, one of the most dangerous applications of this ability is that he can stop the time of his own breath, allowing him to leave invisible traps in the air. Anyone who gets caught in these traps take tremendous damage. Even Reinhard lost an entire leg because of this.
thumb|250px|By kicking the ground beneath his feet, Regulus was able to hurl stones at Reinhard and Subaru with incredible speed.
Earth imbued with Lion's Heart: Regulus often used his power to stop time on the ground around him, allowing him to walk. Likewise, he had a tendency to use this on handfuls of dirt and sand, making them become minuscule bullets capable of completely shredding through whoever is unfortunate enough to receive his attack, effectively turning them into nothing more than a bloody mist. He also applied his power to stones, turning them into bullets that punched through anything in their path, leaving holes the size of the stones in any construct in their way, and even causing numerous buildings to collapse all at once. Using this on even one small object, such as a tile, could easily tear a person's limb from their body, like he did when he nearly severed Subaru's leg from his body.
thumb|250px|Using a massive pile of water, Regulus fires hundreds of water droplets at Emilia and Subaru.
Water imbued with Lion's Heart: By stopping time on water while he was touching it, he could walk on water as if it were made of earth. Like with earth, Regulus could use his power to weaponize water droplets and splashes like bullets, and they bore similar effects. However, unlike earth, he could weaponize water much more fluidly. By kicking at a canal within Priestella, he was able to create a miniature tsunami that could not be stopped. Any falling drops also had their time stopped, making the rain dangerous and easily capable of punching through the ground. He could also pick up a massive amount of water with his hands after freezing its time. By then throwing it at his enemy, he can create yet another unstoppable wave of attacks just like the tsunami. He could also propel himself into the sky by stepping into the water, using the pillar generated afterward to fling himself.
Other people imbued with Lion's Heart: While he primarily uses it on himself, Regulus is also capable of stopping the time of other people and making them temporarily invincible. However, he usually does not do this, and instead, he will utilize the constraint freeing aspect of his Authority to send his enemy flying in another direction, leaving comical man shaped holes in any construct they pass through. Ignoring the constraints of the world, the person will not stop naturally, and they must wait for the Authority to wear off from their body. He can also do this while sending a person into the sky, effectively shooting them into space. Even Reinhard could not stop himself while in this state, and the only reason he was able to return was the fact that he was sent flying to the moon.

Little King (小さな王, Chīsana Ō): With Little King, Regulus was capable of sharing a small "heart" that resided in and resonated with the hearts and heartbeats of his wives, or in other words, anyone he believed to be a “subject” of his “little kingdom”. He could keep the heart within his body from beating while pseudo-hearts that were within all of his wives was beating for him. By pairing this with Lion's Heart, he was able to circumvent its five second time limit, allowing him to maintain his constant invincibility at all times. Likewise, it was next to impossible for most of his wives to notice this pseudo-heart themselves as they felt no change within themselves nor bore any consequence to bearing this heart, making them completely ignorant of it. This only lasted, however, for as long as his wives' own hearts kept beating. If they all died, his Little King would effectively stop working. It was also possible to remove his pseudo-heart from his wives by either putting them in a very near-death state, stopping their hearts from beating via cryostasis, or by using another method to sever and crush the pseudo-heart, such as Subaru's Invisible Providence. The range of Little King was unknown, though according to the author, Regulus' wives had to be close enough for him to feel their love nearby.

Equipment
Gospel (福音): As a member of the Witch Cult, Regulus was the owner of a copy of a Gospel. Each Gospel was a replica of the Book of Wisdom, a book that had been in the possession of the Witch of Greed Echidna. The Book of Wisdom would provide exact details of future events concerning the Witch of Greed, essentially bestowing Echidna with a form of precognition. Unlike the original Book of Wisdom, the Gospels of the Witch Cult were imperfect replicas, meaning that, although they detailed the future of its owner, the events conveyed were subject to change and the information provided was often up for interpretation. The Gospels took the form of small black books that could only be read by their owners.
Conversation Mirror: A meteor that allows the user to get in contact with people who hold other such mirrors.

name: Pandora

relatives: Echidna (daughter)
intro: Pandora (パンドラ) is the Saintess and the Witch of Vainglory. A mysterious Witch regarded as taboo to both the Witch Cult, which she seemingly presides over, as well as the world, she is a supernumerary Witch considered separate from the rest of the Witches.
appearance:
Pandora has the outward appearance of a young woman with a small, delicate body. She has long, straight platinum hair, which is said to be seemingly transparent, to give off a soft glow akin to the shine of the sun, and to have a radiance that creates the effect of a glistening waterfall that travelled down her slender shoulders and rested slightly below her knee line. She has blue eyes with slit pupils that are framed by long eyelashes. She is described as having inhuman beauty that is terrifying enough to make any person who set their eyes upon her incapable of stopping themselves from trembling. Likewise, it is stated that Pandora's charming facial features are considered the ideal image of the word "beauty" accepted by human beings, that her beauty is enough to make others tremble or rouse happiness within them, and that if it were possible to kill through beauty alone, it would be her radiance that would be capable of doing so. However, it has been declared that it is possible to tell at a glance that Pandora is a dangerous being who can not be allowed to exist. Although she may appear to have a gentle smile and a gaze filled with compassion towards a stranger, suggesting she could feel love for them, that sense of love seemed so distorted and overwhelming to the point that it was terrifying.

Pandora's clothing is incredibly simplistic. The only thing the Witch wears was a single sheet of white fabric that covers her torso and traipses over her. The decoration the fabric has a line of deep blue stitches at the top and a matching blue ribbon. Aside from her gown, the other sole piece of material she has is a blue ribbon tied into her hair that is similar to the one that decorated her dress.
personality:
At first glance, Pandora is dignified and graceful, with a generally calm demeanor. This calm exterior hides an extremely selfish and sociopathic personality, willing to do anything to achieve her goals. She had no problem with manipulating Petelgeuse Romanée-Conti into killing his beloved Fortuna and driving him into insanity, and she even told Emilia that she would rip up Elior Forest to open the Seal if she did not comply with her demands. Despite these traits, she never showed anger toward anyone, sending Regulus Corneas away when he turned on her and speaking calmly toward Emilia despite the latter repeatedly killing her.

She had an abject lack of guilt stemming from her actions, showing no form of remorse when she caused someone mental or physical pain or even when she killed innocent people and concocted catastrophes. The Witch only saw the people around her as pawns or pets, not actually viewing them as intelligent creatures worthy of being considered her equals in any way.
history:
More than 400 years ago, Pandora was known as the Saintess. Though it is unknown for what reason she bore this title, she willingly took in the Witch Factor of Vainglory, something which was tailor-made for her usage, and became counted as a supernumerary Witch Factor holder alongside the Valiant, Hector. According to Clind, however, despite being compatible with their respective Factors, the Saintess and the Valiant were unable to avoid the mental corruption that came with Witch Factors.

Pandora and the Warlock of Melancholy, Hector, had a daughter together, that being Echidna. Pandora and Hector were responsible for her birth, having supposedly produced her with a specific goal in mind, that goal being unknown. By Echidna's claim, she never learned anything positive from her parents, having only learned negative emotions such as contempt and ridicule from them. However, she believed that, from their perspective, her existence was a failed imitation to them. Many years after Echidna's birth, Pandora, as the head of the Saintess Sect, was an enemy to the Witch Era Party.

Although according to Beatrice's knowledge, Pandora was supposed to have died sometime in the past, in reality, she remains alive to this day. As such, Pandora was the only Witch who roamed the world freely after the Great Calamity and the Witch of Envy's subsequent sealing. Over the next four centuries, Pandora sowed various seeds of chaos across the world for reasons currently unknown. At some point, the Witch Cult was effectively subsumed into the Saintess Sect, and due to their preexisting name not being very well known, the Sect switched to operating under the Cult's name, leading to the modern Witch Cult. Although the exact position that Pandora has in the modern Witch Cult remains unknown, the Sin Archbishops that lead the group treated Pandora with respect, indicating she held a position outranking theirs. Furthermore, her existence was a well-kept secret among members of the Witch Cult who neglected to talk about her.

Permafrost of Elior Forest
Approximately 100 years ago, intending to open the Seal in the Great Elior Forest that was guarded by the forest's elves, she instructed Regulus Corneas, the Sin Archbishop of Greed, to accompany her there. Moreover, she used her Authority to direct the Black Serpent there. Pandora and Regulus arrived to find Fortuna, the Guardian of the Seal, and Petelgeuse Romanée-Conti, the leader of the moderate faction of the Witch Cult. Pandora explained to the pair her intentions of opening her Seal. After their initial hostile interactions, Petelgeuse ordered Fortuna to escape and make sure Pandora doesn't get the chance to interact with Emilia and use her for her vile plans. After the pair successfully escaped, Petelgeuse then revealed a box containing the Witch Factor of Sloth, and despite being incompatible with the Factor, took it in, gaining the Authority of Sloth. Pandora commended him for his efforts, giving him the title of the Sin Archbishop of Sloth, but the spirit rejected it, saying he accepted the power only to protect what he loved. Petelgeuse then dueled Regulus, however, Greed easily defeated Sloth, severing off his right arm and utterly destroying his legs, rendering him unable to even move. Just as Regulus was about to stomp Petelgeuse's head, ending the spirit's life forever, Fortuna came back to save him. As Regulus prepared to slaughter the pair, Pandora intervened, stating that she would not allow him to harm him as they held significant importance for her plans. Regulus, enraged, hurled dirt at her, which blew her into bits of gore, however, Pandora brought herself back to life and removed Regulus' presence from the forest which automatically reverted all the damage he had done, including disfiguring Petelgeuse.

Pandora then managed to escape from Fortuna and Petelgeuse, and she made her way to the Seal where she met Emilia. Pandora revealed that she had been controlling the lesser spirits that Emilia followed and told her how no one had to be hurt and that all she had to do was open the Seal. To the Witch's disappointment, Emilia told her that she had made a promise to Fortuna not to open the Seal, to which Pandora replied she would tear the forest apart and open the Seal forcefully. Seconds before Pandora succeeded in convincing the child, a heavily injured Fortuna attacked Pandora, killing her time after time after time, but to no avail. As Fortuna yelled at her to stay away from Emilia, Petelgeuse joined the fight. The newly promoted spirit and the Guardian of the Seal then prepared to finish the Witch once and for all however, Pandora used her Authority to confuse Petelgeuse who accidentally used his Unseen Hands to rip a hole into Fortuna's chest, destroying her vital organs and sending her to death's door. With the illusion broken, Petelgeuse realized what he had done, and was subsequently driven completely mad due to the unbearable guilt. Pandora then asked Emilia to open the Seal again. Pandora then revealed she had been controlling the lesser spirits that had played with Emilia and led her to the Seal. Emilia, witnessing these events, unleashed her magic, and continuously killed Pandora in her rage, as Pandora came back repeatedly and attempted to calm her down. Emilia then lost control and froze the entire forest, thus ending Pandora's assault.

Great Conquest
Fourteen years before Subaru's arrival, Pandora made an appearance during the Great Conquest, the Lugunican army's attempt to slay the White Whale. She then approached Theresia van Astrea, the former Sword Saint, who had recently lost her Divine Protection. Theresia attempted to attack Pandora, but with her Authority, she was ultimately unaffected. After Pandora's death was rewritten, Theresia lost consciousness and soon died.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
Thus far, as she has yet to show how capable she is in combat, it is unclear just how powerful she is. However, she is still incredibly dangerous, capable of manipulating the likes of Regulus, Petelgeuse, and even the Black Serpent with ease, taking actions that lead to the deaths of the likes of a Sword Saint and the guardian of Elior Forest's seal, as well as easily evading death.

Authority
Authority of Vainglory (虚飾の権能, Kyoshoku no Ken'nō): Pandora is the current holder of the Witch Factor of Vainglory and is able to use its Authority, granting her abilities related to the manipulation of natural phenomena. As the Saintess, Pandora is compatible with the Factor of Vainglory, allowing her to unrestrainedly exercise its abilities.

Phenomenon Manipulation: Though Pandora's Authority remains largely unexplained, the apparent main application of the Authority of Vainglory is the power to manipulate phenomena at will, although there are conditions in place for the ability to come into effect. One example of Pandora manipulating phenomena was when she first buried Regulus into the ground with no effort, and then removed him from Elior Forest, which effectively made it so that he never entered the forest in the first place, reverting all the damage done by him including him badly wounding Petelgeuse. The moment Pandora used her power, Regulus was no longer in the forest, and instead, he found himself frolicking in his mansion with his wives. As Regulus had never technically attacked, the wounds on both Petelgeuse and Fortuna ceased to exist. Despite the newly forged fact that Regulus had never attacked, however, Petelgeuse, Fortuna, and Pandora all retained memory of the lost event. Likewise, it seems that she can pick and choose which events still take place, as despite removing Regulus, Petelgeuse maintained his hold on the Witch Factor of Sloth. When manipulating phenomena, Pandora would usually state what she wanted to happen similar to a narrator and whatever she said would come to pass.
Memory Manipulation:thumb|250px|Pandora rewriting Emilia's memories Using her Authority, Pandora could seemingly manipulate the memories of another person to a certain extent. By making contact with her victim's head, the Witch could erase memories of her choice and also implant fabricated ones. She demonstrated her power of memory manipulation when she made Emilia forget any knowledge of the Witch of Vainglory's existence. However, this aspect of the Authority wasn't all-encompassing, as Emilia in her later years would occasionally remember disjointed fragments of the memories she had lost.
Self-Resurrection:thumb|250px|Pandora negating her own death. In the event that Pandora was somehow killed, her demise would somehow be rewritten. Ultimately, this application of Vainglory's power that the Witch could evidently use posthumously ensured that Pandora would never be permanently felled by any known physical attack. Her power to self-resurrect was best demonstrated during her attack on Elior Forest. During the assault, she resurrected without a scratch on her after the Regulus used his Authority to turn her into bloody paste. Later, she suffered numerous brutal deaths at the hands of Fortuna and young Emilia, only to instantly return each time.
Sense Manipulation:thumb|250px|Pandora tricking Fortuna into thinking she's holding Emilia while she was actually holding Pandora. Pandora was capable of utilizing her ability to seemingly manipulate phenomena to alter her target's senses to potentially perceive things differently to how they were. In this way, Vainglory could manipulate her targets into believing she was somebody else. Similarly, she could also alter people's senses into believing that other people were her. During her attack on Elior Forest, Pandora was able to make Fortuna mistake her as Emilia by making Fortuna perceive Pandora as the young girl. The Witch was also able to trick Petelgeuse into mistaking Fortuna as herself and Emilia as Fortuna, therefore goading him into killing the former.
Witchbeast Manipulation: Pandora is able to manipulate witchbeasts and bring them to locations of their choosing. In the web novel version of Arc 4, according to one of Petelgeuse's fingers, although she cannot control the Black Serpent with her Authority, she is able to direct it to wherever she wants.

intro: Reala Thompson (リアラ・トンプソン), née Reshia Tinzel (リーシア・ティンゼル), is Garfiel and Frederica's mother. First appearing in a flashback in Arc 4, she formally debuted in Arc 5, where she played a pivotal role in Garfiel's character arc.
appearance: Reala has green eyes and long golden hair which she braids into a ponytail. After reuniting with her son in Priestella, she wears brown and black. She has a glintstone necklace, a plain white shirt, and black shoes.
personality: She was considered a rather luckless person by those who knew her due to having lived a life a of much hardship, and despite that, she was known to carry strange but kindly disposition. After surviving in a rock slide, Reala has no memories about Garfiel Tinzel and her past as Reshia, but her affectionate personality did not change.
history: Reala's family suffered from a crushing debt, which forced her parents to sell her off into an illegal slave trader at a very young age. Not long after, she was kidnapped by a group of demi-human bandits who raided her slaver trader's camp. Several years later, she was abandoned by the demi-human bandits after she became pregnant with Frederica, and spent the following years of her life hopping from one slave caravan to another. At an unspecified point in time, she moved to the Sanctuary, where she gave birth to Garfiel, roughly seven years after giving birth to Frederica. Then, roughly 10 years before the start of the main story, she left the Sanctuary in pursuit of Garfiel's father. Almost immediately after departing, she was involved in a rock slide accident, which led her to be found by Garek Thompson with seemingly no memories of her past. He took care of her and brought her to Priestella. A few years later, they married and had two kids, Fred Thompson and Rafiel Thompson.
abilities_text: Equipment: Reala used to carry a necklace of two glintstones (輝石). However, she took the two stones off the necklace and gave one each to her two children.

intro: Randohal Lugunica (ランドハル・ルグニカ) was the 41st King of Lugunica and Ford Lugunica's older brother. Like the rest of the Royal Family, he fell victim to the mysterious plague that had wiped out the entire Royal Family.
appearance: As a member of the Royal Family, it can be assumed that Randohal had gold hair and crimson red eyes.
personality: Randohal lacked political ability and was often admonished by the Council of Wise Men when he tried to carry out his ideas, but he was a good person who was trying to help the people of his Kingdom. He was respected by his people for his pacifism and kindness.
history:
Randohol was Lugunica's King for at least fourteen years. He presided over the coronation of Roswaal L. Mathers as the head of House Mathers when the mage was still a teenager.

Following the sudden mysterious illness that first plagued Zabinel Lugunica and soon Fourier Lugunica as well, Randohal was soon to follow. He, like the rest of his family, battled the illness for an entire month, until he finally passed away on the same day as his fourth son Fourier, and only a couple of days after his first son Zabinel.

intro: Omega (オメガ) is a copy of Ryuzu Meyer who contains the soul of the Witch of Greed. Before the fall of the Sanctuary, the clone was known under the name Shima (シーマ), one of the original four clones who were tasked with overseeing the Sanctuary.
appearance:
After possessing the body of Ryuzu Shima, Echidna naturally took on the physical form of her host and named herself Omega. In terms of her appearance, Omega is a petite young girl around ten to twelve years of age, though in reality, she's well over four centuries old, predating even the Great Calamity. Her beautiful yet pale face is adorned with a long, refined nose and almond-shaped cyan eyes. After encountering and killing a group of bandits, she stole what clothes and shoes of theirs could fit her, opting to wear them over her original white robe. As Ryuzu Meyer was a half-elf, Omega's ears are inhumanly pointy. Her long fluffy pink hair flows down her back and is slightly curved outwards. Befitting a girl of her physical age, Omega is rather short, failing to reach even halfway up Subaru's chest.

Omega can choose to project her soul as Echidna, temporarily giving her the Witch of Greed's physical appearance. However, she shies away from using it for too long to prevent herself from being found by an unknown enemy of herself and the other Witches. Currently, her appearance has gradually begun shifting over time to match that of her original self, with her pink hair having turned grey while in the process of becoming white.
personality:
Ryuzu Shima was against freeing the Sanctuary due to seeing the original Ryuzu's memories 10 years in the trial and had partly been manipulating Garfiel behind the scenes to make sure it didn't happen. She entered the grave in an attempt to rescue Garfiel but was forced to take the trial. In the end this meant she broke her contract with Echidna. As punishment Shima was duly stripped of her position as an overseer and was made to live with other mindless clones in the forest, donning the white robe as a result.

After being possessed by Echidna's soul, Omega is essentially Echidna from the Castle of Dreams, but in a different body. She retained all of her memories and thoughts, but she was forced to forsake most of her magical power in order to retain her full self. Having been born anew, Omega mostly spends her time observing and adventuring, trying to learn as much as possible about the world she is so unfamiliar with, and she has also retained the clumsiness that Echidna was known for, which has led her accidentally set fire to an entire forest, nearly drown in a river, and almost pass out in the cold snowfields of Gusteko. It should be kept in mind, however, that Omega is in fact the Witch of Greed from the Castle of Dreams, rather than the Witch of Greed who roamed the world before the fall of the Witches.

After starting her journey, she has shown a rather friendly, if somewhat shrewd side of herself, both getting back at people who have wronged someone she has taken a liking to by giving them nightmares or taking others along with her on her journey after either helping them or being saved by them, stating that it was primarily to ward away a common enemy of the Witches. That said, when she was told to be mindful of causing too many deaths for the sake of the people she travels with, she decided to take that advice to heart, which has led to her preventing the deaths of the people around her and even threaten others to prevent such deaths with their own.
history:
Roughly 10 years before the events of Arc 4, Garfiel ran into the Tomb and challenged the Trials. Out of concern for him, one of the Ryuzu copies–Shima–followed suit and accidentally underwent the first Trial. Seeing this as a good opportunity to yet again kick off her experiments with Soul Transcription, Echidna used that occasion to latch a tiny bit of her soul onto her. For the following ten years, she slowly filled the host with her soul, bit by bit. A decade after kickstarting her new plan, Echidna was finally given an opportunity to escape–and so she did. Toward the end of the Sanctuary Incident, Echidna somehow managed to pour in the last bits of her soul and escape the Sanctuary after four long centuries. 

The Witch's After Tea Party
After the fall of the Sanctuary, Echidna managed to completely transfer her soul into Shima and renamed herself Omega, which means "the end", based on Subaru's memories of his original world. She then decided to take it slow and first get accustomed to the new body. Following her reincarnation, Omega left the Sanctuary, taking with her a glintstone anchor that housed the souls of Typhon, Daphne, Carmilla, Minerva, and Sekhmet. She unintentionally burned down a forest when using a fire magic spell to heat herself up. Later, she encountered a group of thieves, killed them with her miasma by projecting her true appearance, and stole their clothes for herself.

The Requirements to be a Witch
Sometime later, Omega accidentally fell into a river and was saved by Colette, a young girl who lived by herself just outside of a local village in the forest. The two of them spent several days together, getting to know one another and exchanging stories from their pasts. When Omega decided to take a walk on another day, Colette informed her to not travel to the eastern side of the forest to avoid a witchbeast that had been attacking people there. Omega went anyways and met Palmyra, who also warned her of a "Beast". That night, she travelled to the eastern side of the forest and attempted to murder the beast herself until Palmyra came and revealed that it was Colette. Learning of the young girl's ostracization as a Witch for being the only survivor caused by a "Beast", Omega came to the conclusion that Colette had accepted the discrimination she faced and decided to try and "become" a Witch by killing the girl she had only recently met. Omega took off a bracelet that Colette had owned since she was very young, the Beast Protection Bracelet, the meteor that was behind her transformation into a beast. Manifesting her true form to Palmyra and an unconscious Colette, Omega set off for the village in hopes of setting things straight with the villagers. However, this only made things worse for Colette, as she was forced to leave the area as a consequence for being acquainted with a "Witch". Seeing as how Colette had nowhere else to go and Palmyra had used up all of her courtesy for the village, the two of them were invited by Omega to join her, officially forming their party.

The Witches' Evaluation Meeting
Once the Omega Party was formed, in the Castle of Dreams, the six Witches had a meeting together where they discussed Echidna's reasoning for allowing Colette and Palmyra to travel with her. To avoid being found by an unnamed enemy of the Witches, Echidna chose to blend in with other humans and avoid being discovered by them. As a result of this reasoning, Minerva set a two-year deadline for Echidna to regain her full powers. It was decided by Echidna that they should leave Lugunica. Believing Gusteko was out of the question, between Vollachia and Kararagi, she set her sights on the latter.

One Wild Night
Ironically, the trio then proceeded to cross over into Gusteko. One day, they were caught in a severe blizzard and rescued by Noelle Tuérico, an Itinerant Preacher of the Gustekan Church, after Omega launched a fire spell into the distance. They wait for Omega to regain her energy in a makeshift snow house Noelle created and speak with her in the meantime, learning about the term Silver Blessing, her position in the Gustekan Church and the nearby church building they can use as a refuge. They visit the church once Omega is rejuvenated and acquaint themselves with Podoso, Admonsah, and Maqueena, each of whom had come to the church to meet the pastor who lives there, Coatl. The trio learned of Coatl's history of having saved a local town from the effects of an avalanche unintentionally caused by the Ice Thieves and how he took up a position of the town's watcher following his charity towards its people, becoming known by the moniker Saint of the Avalanche. Maqueena and Podoso split off from everyone else to visit another part of the church, and another visitor named Trellock arrives while they are out. Eventually, Maqueena discovers something and screams, prompting everyone else to follow after her to find what has caused her fear. They all stumble upon Coatl's corpse, prompting Omega to say that there was a cold-blooded killer among them.

Omega took charge of the situation, using detective work to determine the killer's identity. She heard from Podoso that there had been a string of serial murders, with Coatl being the eighth known victim. The other victims were peddlers and travelers. Querying him about the seventh victim, Omega then sets her sights on Admonsah, whom she was certain was associated with them. They learn Admonsah was a former slave who unexpectedly killed his owner in self-defense. He was unequivocally forgiven by a majority of the group. Omega tries to ascertain why Coatl would be murdered, searching for any hidden savings. Suddenly, everyone but Maqueena in the room fell asleep to the effects of the Muskrim flower, and she made her getaway with Coatl's collection of magic stones, not wanting to stay and fall victim to his murderer. She was stopped outside by Noelle, who says she could not be affected by such a simple drug and had killed Coatl out of revenge for his former membership of the Ice Thieves and his part in causing the avalanche that devastated Leanotte, her town. Omega arrives to stop Noelle before she could kill Maqueena, outlining that she was only a con artist who perceived Coatl's connection to the Ice Thieves rather than an outright member before giving the ultimatum that she would die if she caused another death, yet again manifesting her true form while saying so. Meanwhile, the culprit responsible for the serial murderers, Trellock, attempted to murder Colette, but her Beast Protection Bracelet activated, severely injuring him. In the end, they pretended that Noelle had apprehended Trellock and left, Podoso decided to take in Admonsah, and Maqueena was forced to stop conning people. With her revenge foiled, Noelle was left aimless. Colette proposed for her to join their group to which she accepted upon Omega's approval.

One Wild Night Extra
Later, the party decided to head to the town Podoso had told them about. Eventually, they set up camp, and while Colette and Noelle set up the camp, Palmyra decided to talk with Omega about including Noelle in their travels, worried about getting her involved in their troubles, which included Omega being a half-elf Witch and Colette's bracelet. Omega believed that there was nothing to worry about, and shortly after, Noelle, who had heard part of their conversation appeared and said that she already knew about Omega's secret and chose to follow them regardless. Though Palmyra asked if she had a thing for odd people and Noelle's joking reply that she did, just like Palmyra, she claimed to be just as odd, as she was an itinerant preacher from the Gustekan Church who had decided to leave. Though Palmyra thought it wasn't as bad as Omega's secret, Omega told her that she was underestimating the Church and what they bestowed Noelle, and the two claimed that they would not be amicable toward her effectively breaking a contract, something which might end up leading to them falling into her mess. Though Palmyra told Omega to be prepared to fight, when Noelle told her to feel free to kick her from the party if she ever became a burden, to which she replied by saying not to underestimate her and spoke of her own circumstances, basically unintentionally cornering Noelle into staying in the party after saying not to use Colette as an excuse. Colette arrived shortly after, and the group decided not to talk to her about their conversation. Instead, they ate, and Noelle explained repairs that she had made to their equipment and offered her knowledge of how to use their equipment and how to survive in Gusteko, including knowledge on the Gustekan Church, to which Palmyra and Omega realized that they wouldn't be able to survive in Gusteko without Noelle.

Omega in Wonderland
The party continued to trudge to the snows of Gusteko, with Palmyra and Omega becoming exhausted. Attempting to give Palmyra some more energy, Colette attempted to let her use her bracelet, but when Palmyra tried, it left her weak and vomiting. Omega explained the reason for this, claiming she allowed it to happen because she wanted to see the look on her face. Afterward, she had Noelle carry Palmyra while Colette carried her. As the got closer to the town of Sylphoa, Omega dispelled a barrier, and eventually they reached the town, where she and Colette fell subject to the Dream Arts spell that had been cast over the town.

Impressed with the size of the space and likening it to her Castle of Dreams, even claiming it as superior to herself, Omega cast Al Shario in order to lure out the caster. The caster, Lilac, appeared shortly after, erasing the star Omega summoned and questioning who they were. After a small dispute, she left convincing her to take down the spell to Colette. Despite her standoffish attitude, Omega claimed that Colette's words were getting through to her. However, upon hearing Omega's use of a loan word, Lilac wanted to know where she heard it, leading to negotiations. Despite becoming frustrated with her and even slapping her, she decided to give Omega a chance to take care of the Temple Knight who had come after her, breaking the seal that she'd placed. The fight that followed was short lived as the Witches of Sin quickly dispatched her, much to Lilac's shock. Shortly after, Palmyra entered the dream space with a message from Lilac's partner, Shion.

Following this, after Omega spoke to the other Temple Knight who had come to retrieve Mikli and had him leave with her and report the death of the heretic, Lilac released the people of Sylphoa from her dream world, and Omega offered Shion and Lilac to join her party. Since she couldn't quite trust the two, having just met them, she would give them a chance to look into her memories with their Dream Arts, giving them a chance to find the person from which the loan words they speak come from. The two accepted her offer and joined the party. Afterward, Omega realized that they must have skimmed across Subaru's memories at some point, and she claimed that combing through those memories would be dangerous for them, assuming they could see them after bypassing all six Witches' resistance.

Witch Trials
One day, having moved on from Sylphoa, the Omega Party was walking in a snow field, where they encountered a Snow Blight. However, Omega swiftly dispatched it with Minya. Soon after, they arrived at Limbus, where signs claiming it was forbidden to go out at night and to comply with the "vows of the faith". Though slightly concerned about the town's eeriness, as the group was low on supplies, they decided to enter Limbus, where after a few minutes, they found themselves surrounded by the townsfolk who were armed with farming tools. Though they attempted to calm the townsfolk and offer them a gift in the form of the Snow Blight's crystallized head, they instead accuse her of being a Witch after seeing it, leading Omega to warn Colette against using her bracelet's transformation and Lilac from turning back into Shion, else they be declared Witches. Thanks to the appearance of Nananna Pezza and speaking with Noelle, she was able to vouch for them and clear them of being Witches.

Omega's group finds an inn to reside in where they discussed the issue at present, warning everyone about how easily they could be made into scapegoats whether for their abilities, race, or even the look in their eyes, and Noelle explained about Witch Hunts and Witch Trials being rare occurrences in Gusteko that Itinerant Preachers were sometimes sent to deal with. Although wanting to leave the town quickly, the group decides to stay in the town to help Noelle repay her debt to Nananna, and soon after, they meet with Nananna when she arrived to ask for the group's assistance. That night, the Witch Hunt is for a person named Piditz who had been tipped off as a Witch, and Nananna wanted him taken into custody only. When they later spotted Piditz and chased after him, Omega split off to corner him, only to find Mireille Hetia using her spiritual arts to kill Piditz. Thanks to being near the body, Omega was quickly turned into a scapegoat and declared a Witch so that Mireille could cover up her kill and at least prevent her from getting in the way of her and Nananna's revenge, and Omega was taken into custody.

Later, Colette visits Omega, and they point out that killings began before the party arrived, which should clear Omega's name, but instead, Mireille decides to have her executed anyway, and Palmyra objects to Edmon Quayle. As part of Omega's plan, Noelle persuades Nananna to speak up, and Nananna insists on the town holding a Witch Trial for Omega, and Palmyra declares that if she is a Witch that she would burn with her. While remaining in the prison, she continues to talk to the guards and annoy them, gathering information all the while.

The next day, the Witch Trial is being held for Omega, overseen by Nananna and the Town Hall, while Palmyra acts as Omega's attorney. Despite her arguments, Edmon counter with his supposed knowledge of the Witches and Omega's chatter does not help. Colette speaks up and claims that she believes that things will not go as the council claims, as people will begin to notice that the entire event seems off, which resounds with the townsfolk. Because of this, Palmyra claims that there is a conspiracy, which Edmon fights against and asks for Nananna's assistance. Because she sides with the town, Lilac and Shion believe her to be part of the conspiracy, and they decide to use their dream arts to influence the people's mental states. Palmyra then claims that the council is using the Witch rumors to get rid of inconvenient people, which Edmon also fights against, though is quickly silenced when she states she heard it herself from a council member and declares that there is no Witch. Unfortunately, Omega claims otherwise.

Despite angering Palmyra, Omega decides to clear things up by declaring that there were two conspiracies taking place in town. Despite Nananna trying to prevent her from talking, Omega ignores her and explains that many of the victims were relatives of council members, and she claims that Nananna is the second conspirator, calling her the bastard child of Edmon whose mother was banished from the town, and as a result, she despised the town. Noelle later appears and confirms that her actions were in response to the death of an elderly healer, and she claims that Nananna tried to remove her from the trial by knocking her out since her only ire was with Limbus. Afterward, Noelle declares that the secretary, Mireille, was helping Nananna, as she was a bastard child of Edmon as well, and she stated how the corpses of Piditz and other people connected to the council and other outside officials were already dumped in a hole. Omega also declares that she witnessed Mireille killing Piditz. Enraged, Mireille uses her spiritual arts to char Edmon's arm with blue fire, and with the intent of killing the entire council, surrounds the council with blue fire, and she and Nananna stand against them. Although Omega is fine with leaving things as they are and taking their leave, Colette states she doesn't want things to end like this, and Omega decides to end the fighting in response to her plea, burning through her restraints and declaring herself a Witch.

Later, as Omega's party begins to leave the town, Noelle says her goodbyes to Nananna, and it is declared that the evil spirit accompanying Mireille will be disposed of. Likewise, it is claimed that Edmon's position is under threat with both his severe injuries and the loss of the citizens' trust, and Mireille claims she was mistaken about real Witches. Despite Colette believing that things were settled peacefully, however, Omega thinks to herself that Limbus would soon face its destruction, as since Omega, Nananna, and Mireille were not executed, there would be continuous Witch Hunts and deaths for scapegoats for the whole incident. Although considering telling Colette about this, she decides against it.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
Since Shima's body was not the most suitable host for Echidna to possess, she was forced to leave out her experience with magic. Despite this, she is still incredibly knowledgeable, and she can still use magic to easily defeat and kill most of her enemies. Furthermore, she could kill most beings with her miasma alone if she so chose, making her dangerous just by being close to her. According to her estimates, it will take her roughly two years to regain all her skills and powers. Furthermore, as she has not exhibited it as of yet, it is unknown if she retains her Authority of Greed. As it is unknown how much time has passed by the time of the Witch Trials side story, it is unclear how much of her power that Omega has recovered.

Magic
Although she is currently limited from using her full capacity of spells, Omega is still familiar with the usage of magic and is capable of using fairly powerful spells without needing incantations and effectively using all affinities to her advantage against an opponent, even retaining her ability to dispel "blessings" placed by a Temple Knight. Although she hasn't shown it off, she is capable of using all six attributes of magic, and at least within a dream realm, she has shown the capacity to use a forbidden art. Presently, she is unable to properly cast the more advanced spells in her arsenal.

Spells:
Goa (ゴーア): Omega is able to manifest a blaze of fire to incinerate foes.
Dona (ドーナ): Omega can summon one wall of earth, which she uses as a defensive spell.
Minya (ミーニャ, Mīnya): A basic yin magic spell in which the user creates purple stakes of crystallized mana with light purple flames. The spell can ignore defenses, and when it hits, it can stop time on a part target, crystallize them, and cause them to shatter. Any stakes in the air explode and release smaller stakes that fly in all directions which then rips targets apart.
Dream Arts: Omega is capable of utilizing a lost type of forbidden arts known as dream arts. Though her level of skill with it is not on the same level as someone such as Shion, she still had enough proficiency with it to create the Castle of Dreams.
Al Shario (アル・シャリオ): Omega was capable of casting a forbidden spell that literally brought stardust down to earth, massacring her opponents. As of right now, she has shown to be able to use this spell within a dream realm, but as it is unknown how much of her full strength has recovered by the time she exhibited this spell, it is unknown if she can presently use it in the real world.

Intelligence
Vast Intellect: Omega has retained the knowledge that she had acquired in her life as Echidna. She possessed one of the greatest intellects in the world, and had conducted numerous experiments with magic, creating powerful meteors. Numerous people from every nation used to come to her, seeking her knowledge when she was alive. She possessed vast knowledge about the older era, to the point she could boast there is nothing she didn't know.

Other
Miasma: Omega can project the soul of the Witch of Greed, making it appear as if she was physically standing by Omega's side. By doing so, Echidna starts emitting an intense aura of wickedness and madness which is enough to drive people mad and kill them in thirty seconds. It's mentioned by Echidna that a Sage could endure her aura.

Miasma-Attuned Olfaction: Shima can smell the Witch's miasma, something that only a few individuals in the series so far are capable of doing. This is likely due to her connection with Echidna before she completely took over Shima's body.

Equipment
Glintstone (輝石 Kiseki): Omega uses a necklace to carry a glintstone with her. This glintstone is an anchor that contains the five souls of the other witches, Minerva, Carmilla, Typhon, Sekhmet, and Daphne in it. She can freely converse with them, but she is unable to bring them out of the stone and have them materialized in the world.
