intro: Petra Leyte (ペトラ・レイテ) is a former inhabitant of Arlam Village who currently lives and works at Roswaal Manor as a maid. She plays a major role in Arc 4 and Arc 9, a supporting role in Arc 7, Arc 8, and Arc 10, and a lesser supporting role in Arc 2 and Arc 3.
appearance:
During her life as a village child, Petra wore common clothes that consisted of a pair of brown shoes, green leggings with horizontal stripes that were shorn just above the ankles, a white long-sleeved shirt, an open short-sleeved cream-colored cardigan with red outlining, and a red ribbon fastened to her collar. She has medium length reddish brown hair that, as time progressed, has grown to reach her shoulder in Arc 9, she has cyan eyes, and she has continued to grow taller since her introduction.

In Arc 4, Petra switched to a maid uniform for her job, keeping her ribbon tied in her hair. During Subaru's knighting ceremony, Petra wore a light green dress with a ribbon of the same shade in her hair along with her red ribbon. From Arc 7 and on, she wore a long-sleeved yellow and white shirt, a green skirt with white frills, a green cloak held together by a red ribbon, a red ribbon in her hair, white leggings, and brown boots. By Arc 9, she has also fashioned part of her hair into a braid.
personality:
Petra is a pure-hearted, innocent young girl who often tries her best to help and nurture others, regardless of whether doing so was detrimental to her. Her sweet personality is enough to mellow the hearts of those who interacted with her, particularly Subaru and Frederica, whose moods brightened just from talking with her. Unlike many people in Lugunica, Petra harbors no xenophobic tendencies towards demi-humans, instead judging people off of their deeds and personalities. Alongside the other children in Arlam Village, Petra held no prejudice against Emilia. In a similar vein, Petra is able to fairly judge a person's abilities and is unable to unfairly demean a person she doesn't like.

For someone so young, Petra is incredibly brave, choosing to prioritize the lives and wellbeing of others above her own in situations of crisis. When the disguised Wolgarm fled into the Wolgarm-infested woods, Petra, who was unaware of the creature's true identity, steeled her nerves and traversed into the forest to rescue the animal from danger. When Elsa Granhiert took her hostage and brought her before Subaru and her fellow maids, Petra, although terrified at the prospect of dying, told her friends to flee and save themselves rather than rescue her. Similarly, she is even willing to put her life on the line if it means helping others, as shown when she placed an oath bound curse mark on herself as a promise to let Musica meet Emilia while negotiating to let them pass into Vollachia to save Subaru. She was even willing to read a Book of the Dead, despite knowing the risks involved, in order to understand her opponent's possible goals, as well as use a Witch Factor in spite of the risks.

Originally, Petra was a rather self-centered young girl, believing the world to be small and simple. Being rather smart for her age and having known that she was cute, she fully exploited that fact and used it as a means of getting out of trouble, believing that apologies were essentially just a tool to obtain forgiveness. Likewise, this gave her an excuse to be slightly mischievous. Because she was adored by the adults, admired by the boys, and relied on by the girls, she had become excessively spoiled and her ego had bloated sharply, and she had begun to harbor rather harsh opinions of other people. This also led to her feeling a sense of loneliness when she realized nobody seemed to approve of her dreams of becoming a tailor, and her not getting her way simply by her appearance became her first real setback. However, after she was saved during the Wolgarm Incident by Subaru and seeing what became of him because of her actions, she felt tremendous guilt, to the point that she was crying about what she had done, and after speaking with her parents and apologizing to Subaru, she came to understand that she misunderstood everyone's kindness, and because of this, she mellowed out. Thanks to Subaru, she began to admire kind people and strived to be kind herself, no longer wanting to take the kindness of others for granted, while she came to dislike herself and believe being sly was inappropriate.

Following the incident in the Sanctuary, Petra has become somewhat bolder, aspires to the ideal that she must at all times achieve what is expected of her, and speaks her mind more often, especially when it comes to the safety of her friends and, in particular, Subaru, who often worries her with his constant recklessness of turning head-first into danger. That said, she has shown to be quite harsh with those that she cannot stand. Because of the actions that Roswaal took that nearly led to the death of not only everyone in the Emilia Camp but also the villagers of both the Sanctuary and Arlam Village, she has shown to be very critical and unforgiving toward him, often using blunt and cruel statements when talking with him or even wringing out dirty rags in his drinks. Of course, she doesn’t go too far with her resentment, and she is even willing to work with him at times if it means victory, but alongside Otto Suwen, she refuses to trust him, and she makes sure that she stays an anchor in the camp in the case that Roswaal does something suspicious again.

Because of everything he had done for her, saving her, forgiving her, and showing her the error of her original attitude, Petra has come to harbor a deep crush on Subaru. Because of this, Petra changed her wish of wanting to be a seamstress at the Royal Capital to being a good wife, and in an effort to place herself in a position from which she could provide her help to Subaru, when Roswaal Manor was putting up a notice for new servants, Petra went out of her way to ask the other villagers to turn down the offer so that she could become one herself. It is for the goal of assisting Subaru and remaining by his side that she is now learning maid duties, politics, and magic, and though she has times in which she feels like she is powerless compared to the other members of the camp, she is willing to trust those people to help and keep an eye on Subaru in her place.

Petra is often shown to be anxious over Subaru and his reckless actions as well, pouting when he actively decided leave for the Pleiades Watchtower, which even the Sword Saint was unable to reach and was in one of the most dangerous locations in the world, and even felt frustrated with his decision to accept Spica in spite of her past. However, she looks up to him for being willing to take such risks, and she has taken after him somewhat in taking similar risks. When she feels anxious, she even calls his name to rid herself of said anxiety, which allows her to take action when necessary. However, although this is exclusive to the events of Arc 9, after reading Subaru's Book of the Dead, despite becoming incredibly upset after learning his secret, her boldness, confidence, and willingness to stay by his side and help him was greatly amplified, to the point that she was willing to give up something precious of hers to Clind in order to use his Authority to gather everyone to help save him, as well as to take on his Witch Factor and proclaim herself a Witch, despite the negative connotations of Witches around the world, in order to both help and be like Subaru, who she recognized as essentially being a Warlock by bearing his own Authority, and Petra was willing to sacrifice many possible futures in order to use her Authority in order to assist Subaru, including returning to her original home or various other sacrifices, so long as she could stay by and help him.

Petra considers herself to be quite mentally strong as well, as despite knowing that his eyes were on Emilia and Rem, who practically shone so bright that they were all he could see, she did not give up her love for him and intended to make herself stand out just as much to get his attention. On top of being intelligent and headstrong, the love she feels for Subaru also allows her to maintain her sense of self and resist the temptations brought about by a Witch Factor, which Petra described as being highly attractive.

Exclusively to the events of Arc 9, because she read Subaru's Book of the Dead, she started to understand Subaru significantly better, and she could feel herself being influenced by him, began thinking in a similar manner to him, speaking with his loan words, and when she is around Emilia and Rem, the influence is even stronger thanks to Subaru's immense passion for desperation for them, leading her to speak to them in a somewhat similar fashion to Subaru. Likewise, she was willing to break any promises to people she didn't like.
history:
The World Petra Saw
Petra is a young girl who formerly lived in Arlam Village, a small rural village located in the lands of the noble Margrave Roswaal L. Mathers. As she grew up, she came to realize that she was cute and was willing to use that to get out of trouble, and in the process, she was practically the center of attention in the village. However, she also came to harbor the feeling that the people around her were terribly simple-minded and naive. Even after meeting the margrave in charge of the area, she came to find talking to him a complete waste of time. When she turned ten, a merchant stopped by the village. Upon seeing the fabrics he was selling and buying some for herself, she had started to aspire to move to the Royal Capital and become a tailor when she grew up. Over the next two years, Petra started to realize that she felt somewhat lonely when the other children didn't seem to approve of her dream and merely talked about their own dreams.

At one point after becoming enthralled with fabrics, Frederica, who was still working with House Miload, had been summoned to the manor and asked to deliver a message to the mayor of Arlam Village. There, Petra, who she asked for directions and was taken by her cuteness. There, she claimed that she would have liked to be Frederica's friend, though unbeknownst to Frederica, she was thinking of her pinafore as reference rather than thinking too much of Frederica. Afterward, she led her to the mayor.

One day, two years later, a new butler in training, Subaru, visited the village. Upon his visit, while the other kids played with him, Petra was wary of his demeanor, especially as he knew her name despite not introducing herself. Leading him to the village, she decided to lead him to Rasphum, intending to prank him by making him believe that he was the village head. That same day, she met Meili, who claimed to have been visiting for a short time, and she showed Petra a small dog that did tricks. The next day, when Subaru appeared, more relaxed than the day before, she gained a slightly better impression of him, though that was drowned out when he dragged the village into doing radio calisthenics. Later, she and the kids were playing with the dog, which had bitten Subaru earlier that day. When the dog ran off, she and the other children followed Meili when she went to retrieve him. However, after an hour without finding the dog and worrying about the other children, Petra, still afraid, decided to try and turn everyone around, only for Meili to use a Wolgarm to knock them out.

When she woke up the next day, she learned that she and the kids were saved by Subaru, who got hurt in the process, and that Meili had supposedly left the village, which she instinctively knew to be a lie. Along with the other kids, she went to the manor to show her gratitude to him. After the maid Ram led her to his room, however, upon seeing how badly injured he was, she recalled what she had asked of him and realized that her actions led to this. After freezing up, she ran back home and locked herself away in her room in guilt to cry. That night, after she calmed down, she spoke with her parents about her actions that led to Subaru's injuries, and though slightly scolded for it, they told her that she should apologize.

Two days later, the day after the incident was fully resolved, Subaru visited the village again, and though the kids pulled him around, Petra, who scolded them for it, ran away when Subaru looked at her. After he caught up, he and Petra sat down, and despite Subaru nearly misunderstanding that she might have gotten injured because of the whole mess, she apologized and sobbed to him. Ultimately, Subaru forgave her, which led to her to reconsider why she was forgiven, at which point she realized that it was because Subaru, as well as everyone else she wrote off as naive, were just kind. A short time later, Petra showed off an outfit that she made with fabrics she had bought, wanting to hear Subaru's thoughts. After hearing his positive opinions and how he believed that she would make an excellent tailor when she told him about her dream, her dreams of becoming a tailor changed to wanting to be a good wife to a kind man, and she had begun to harbor a crush on Subaru.

Some Like it Cold
One day, while the village was feeling the effects of Puck's magic release period, Subaru and the residents of Roswaal Manor visited the village, and Subaru announced that they would be having a competition during this snow festival. Whoever was able to make the best snow sculpture would win a prize, and the judges were Subaru, Roswaal, and Rasphum. As the kids were playing in the snow, Petra made a snow sculpture of a rabbit. Subaru, though impressed, touched it up, and he was reprimanded by Petra for it. In the end, Petra was the one who won the competition.

Frederica and Petra's Maid-san Days
A couple of months after the Wolgarm Incident, Petra decided to give up her dream of becoming a tailor, instead choosing to look for work in Roswaal Manor when posters asking for new maids at the manor were posted, where she could be closer to Subaru. After pleading with the other village girls not to take on the request, Petra went to accept the request. Though Frederica, who was conducting her interview, wanted to turn her down due to the lack of time to trains new maids in the basics, she received favorable responses from Petra that made Frederica want to hire her. Warning Petra that her behavior would reflect on Roswaal, Frederica accepted when she was told that Petra would not give up for the person she cared for, and afterward, had Petra refer to her as her big sister.

After being hired, Frederica began instructing her, only to find that Petra was already excellent at completing her tasks. Commenting on how a young Ram could have learned from Petra, the two headed to the village. While there, Frederica shopped for what she could while the half of the villagers were still gone, while Petra spoke with her friends. On their way back to the manor, however, Petra was in a bad mood, having been defending Frederica after they said her mouth was scary. Moved, Frederica urged her to speak with her friends again, who looked like they wanted to apologize.

One night, she and Frederica shared a bath, in which Frederica told Petra about Clind and warned her to stay away from him due to his proclivities. Recognizing the complicated emotions in Frederica's voice, she asked to stay the night in her room. Later, after leaving food out for Beatrice, she appeared in Frederica's room, where she learned of one of Frederica's old bad habits. After laughing about it, the two went to bed, hoping that by the next morning, the food left for Beatrice would have been gone. The next morning, as Frederica was preparing breakfast, Petra spoke to her, apologizing for her behavior on the day that the two first met. Though Frederica said there was nothing to apologize about since she had almost forgotten, she recalled Petra mentioning wanting to be friends, and now they were. Asking Petra what made her think of apologizing, Petra claimed that something had been bugging her and she had remembered. Believing she believed what caused her to remember, Frederica began to panic, only for Petra to say it was because of something she had said the night before. Afterward, she helped Frederica prepare breakfast.

The Emilia Camp's Great Evaluation Meeting
Following the Sanctuary Incident, Annerose Miload and Clind, who had been tasked with making preparations by Roswaal, arrived at the Sanctuary to board all the villagers on their carriages, intent on leading them out of the snow-covered and heavily damaged forest. Annerose was quick to scold Roswaal for his behavior and approved of his being struck, claiming to Garfiel that she would be his ally should he hassle him again. Moments later, the pair introduced themselves to Subaru and Otto, who had been claimed to be the new internal affairs minister for the Emilia Camp, surprising Subaru with their behavior and titles, and thanks to Clind, Subaru realized that Roswaal had their appearance already prepared. Though Clind claimed that they were a step closer to freeing Roswaal from the "spell" he was under, he teased Subaru when he exclaimed how he thought he said something important. Frederica then appeared and scolded Clind, claiming to Subaru that she knew him and that he was flawed despite his abilities, something which was seemingly proven when Petra said that the villagers had gathered together. Frederica attacked him, though Clind dodged her attacks with ease, and with Otto claiming that he would handle things there, he told Subaru that he should go see Emilia.

Approaching the tomb, where Annerose was talking with Emilia, Beatrice stood by his side, and Subaru warned her not to get too close to Clind. Noticing his state, Ram appeared and claimed that his nature hadn't changed since the last time she met him and that he behaved this way towards her in her youth and even thought that Rem had experienced it. After a warning that Clind did not differentiate between male and female, Annerose approached Subaru and questioned if he was willing to take responsibility for forcing a kiss onto Emilia, though Emilia appeared and defended Subaru by saying it was consensual. Acting like a "rival in love", the two argued, with Annerose even calling Subaru a homewrecker, Beatrice getting angry, and Ram stirring things up. Seeing them all, Emilia touched her crystal where Puck slept and called everyone there precious to her.

Poltergeist Story
Two months after the Sanctuary Incident, Roswaal called for the maids of Roswaal Manor. Intending to begin making allies with other nobles with Emilia for the Royal Selection, he set his sights on first targeting Viscount Torion Aruz, he tasked the girls with cleaning a villa that was once the workshop of his father, Roswaal K. Mathers. Two days later, the girls arrived in the evening, birds attempting to steal their luggage having delayed their arrival. There, they found that the workshop was covered in ivy and vines and was practically falling apart from disuse. As nighttime approached, despite Frederica starting to panic over the workshop's creepy atmosphere, they decided that they would have to stay the night there.

While Ram remained out front for a while, Frederica and Petra went to the back of the workshop, which is in even worse condition than the front. However, after a hole just large enough for the two to slip into, Petra walked inside, followed shortly after by Frederica. Unable to see Petra, she instead saw a doll in the darkness, shortly before the lights came on. Soon after, she reunited with Petra and Ram, afraid of the doll. Despite Ram's insistence that it was Frederica's imagination, Frederica and Petra heard an explosion-like noise in the distance while Ram heard nothing. Wanting to leave, Frederica clung to Ram as they headed for the front door, only to find that it was storming outside, and Petra had to stop Frederica from beastifying and running away.

Deciding they would investigate the strange sounds and dolls, Petra headed upstairs, hoping to catch sight of a hollow. Frederica, still sticking with Ram, tried to follow after her, only to fall through the floor of the stairs. Shortly after, Frederica became a target of harassment for the doll, and before long, she ended up latching onto one in fear, having mistaken it for one of the other two. In a panic, she beastified and ran off, the doll gripping her tail. She eventually smashed it away with her tail on the roof, only to find others that made her fall. Ram, who recognized what they were, ordered the dolls to catch her. Shortly after, Frederica, her clothes destroyed, and Petra were told that the dolls had been magicreation tools that were defending the manor, and they treated Petra and Frederica as intruders, treating them differently because due to their different sizes. First claiming the dolls could help them clean the place up with them, Petra then thought to dress up the dolls and fix their makeup before calling Roswaal to the workshop.

Before long, Roswaal had flown over to the workshop and wondered how long it had been since he'd been there. Meeting up with the maids, he found 111 of those dolls dressed up and fixed. Surprised that they were still, having created more of themselves to continue protecting the place until the master could return, he thanked them, causing them to bow and finally shut down. Afterward, facing the confused Petra, he thanked them for allowing him to right a wrong, upsetting Petra for his attitude. With Roswaal deciding to help them, Frederica told Petra she could work him hard, while Ram had knelt down and gently thanked the dolls for their service.

Otto Suwen's Internal Affairs Struggle
Shortly after the decision to visit the Watergate City of Priestella was made, Petra was being extremely petulant because she was not one of the people who would be going to the Watergate City and was instead accompanying Roswaal. Otto listened to her complaints for a bit, even suggesting he would talk to the Margrave himself about it, which Petra refused. Otto asked Petra to baby-sit Roswaal whilst he was away, to which Petra agreed, saying she would have done that even if he had not asked. In return, she asked him to take care of Subaru and the others. Otto asked if Petra was worried about him, to which Petra replied that she saw no need to do so.

Petra’s Emilia Camp Struggle
Occurring simultaneously with the Battle for Priestella, Petra took part in the meeting with the western nobles alongside Roswaal, Annerose, Frederica, and Clind. After a short confrontation with the renowned chef, Dias Fatsbalm, she witnessed as Roswaal attempted to convince the other nobles into backing Emilia of their own accord. Shortly after the meeting began, Roswaal had Petra speak on his behalf regarding Emilia, as if he were to do so, it may sound insincere or manipulative. She did as she was asked and gave her opinion and facts on Emilia, and she successfully managed to convince the other nobles to back her. Later, after learning some dishes from Dias, they returned to Roswaal Manor.

Beatrice's Everyone is Troublesome, I Suppose!
After returning to Roswaal Manor, Beatrice was invited by Petra to sleep in her room. Having tea together, Beatrice told the curious Petra what happened in Priestella, to which Beatrice described the battle. Eventually, she asked about how Beatrice was during that fight, as she had barely brought herself up during the explanation, and she said that she was worried as Beatrice had started to imitate Subaru lately. Petra then dragged Beatrice into the bed with her, and they fell asleep.

Stand by me Pleiades and Missing Child Search
Following the successful Pleiades Watchtower Expedition, the expedition team returned to Roswaal Manor, carrying the news of Subaru and Rem’s disappearance. Following the revelation, Anastasia Hoshin and Julius Juukulius decided to enter Vollachia through Kararagi, and Roswaal decided to have Clind use his Authority to take everyone else where they needed to be. Leaving Meili in the Royal Capital with Annerose, the rest of the camp arrived in Picoutatte. After settling an issue between Otto and Diadora Regundra and making a deal with the Suwen Company, the group decided to pass through the Everlasting Darkness with the assistance of the mole people.

As they passed through the area, however, they were forced to speak with the representative of the mole people, Musica, who expressed concerns on behalf of his people about the emergence of a second Demi-Human War because of Emilia’s partaking in the Royal Selection. Since Emilia was disguised as a bodyguard while wearing her recognition obstruction robe and Petra was acting like a noble lady being escorted into another country on the camp’s behalf, Musica and Petra entered discussions, where she deduced his true intentions to sacrifice their race in order to bring down Emilia. Musica agreed to back off from the mole people's preexisting plan to meet and discuss things with Emilia when their business in the Empire was concluded, willingly bearing an oath bound curse mark in the process to show her intentions were genuine. Afterward, they were brought into Vollachia.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
Petra has once been declared one of the weakest characters in the series. However, she makes up for her lack of physical strength with her intelligence, cunning, will, and adaptability. Despite her youth, she has shown herself to be a formidable enemy whose tactical and political prowess, despite her youth, are not to be underestimated.

Although it is exclusive to Arc 9 and the Sasageru IF, Petra was once a formidable enemy as a Witch. Although in Arc 9 she pushed the limits of what she could do and sacrificed everything about her life to achieve victory, in the Sasageru IF, she held enough strength to contend with Vague Adgard and was feared as a centuries old Witch in a similar manner to the Witch of Envy.

Intelligence
Keen Intellect: Despite her youth, Petra is intelligent and a fast learner. As a child, she was quick to realize that she could use her cute appearance to get others to do as she wanted, and later on, when Subaru first appeared, she immediately recognized that something was different about him, which gave her a sense of caution that neither the other kids nor adults of the village had. Later on, after joining the Emilia Camp, she was quick to learn maid duties, magic, and politics, and she, alongside Otto, with their intelligence and realistic views of the world and the people around them, became an important anchor in the camp filled with idealists. Her intellect has shown itself the most when interacting with Musica and Vincent Vollachia, where, in the case of the former, she was able to negotiate and come to a compromise with him, while in the case of the latter, she was able to see through his attempts to manipulate the camp with both his words and lack of words. Later on, during the Battle for the Imperial Capital, she showed exemplary display for strategies, to the point that while working alongside Otto, their presence was perhaps the most significant on the battlefield, while during the Pleiades Sealing Conflict, she was not only able to see through Al's Authority after taking in Subaru's memories for the arc, but she was able to discover and overcome his weaknesses, come up with various applications for the Authority of Melancholy, and even completely direct people to the point that they could force Subaru to use Return by Death. According to Otto, her inclusion into the camp might have been the most significant and was perhaps Subaru's greatest achievement.

Magic
Petra has an affinity for the yang attribute. She has learned magic techniques from Roswaal, which she has used for offensive purposes in the form of Jiwald and support purposes to boost one’s physical resilience. However, she is inexperienced with magic, making it inferior to the magic used by others.

Spells:
Jiwald (ジワルド): Using yang magic, Petra is able to conjure and manipulate visible light into beams of scorching heat that attack whatever stands in its way. Due to her inexperience in magic, her version of Jiwald is underwhelming, producing enough heat to leave small burns on the skin or ignite fire magic stones. This being said, it does seem to have enough power to pierce through someone's body at point blank range.
Healing Magic: Petra has claimed to be able to heal others. However, she has yet to display this ability.

Physical Traits/Flow Method
Self-Defense: Frederica gave Petra lessons in physical combat in order for her to learn how to defend herself.

Curse
thumb|150px|An oath bound curse mark carved onto Petra’s chest
Oath Bound Curse Mark (誓約の呪印, Seiyaku no Juin): Following a confrontation with Musica and the mole humans in Stand by me Pleiades, Petra upheld her oath and had a curse mark carved onto herself. According to her oath, if she is to ever break her promise and not allow them to meet Emilia, she shall be engulfed in a purifying flame, scorching her body and tainting her soul, never allowing it to return to Od Lagna. Petra's curse mark appears as a light circle with a carving of the crest of House Mathers displayed in the circle's center.

Authority
Exclusively to the events of Arc 9, before its events were undone by Return by Death, Petra bore the Witch Factor of Melancholy and its respective Authority during Arc 9. Clind, the other user of Melancholy and the person who assumed the responsibility of managing it, bestowed to Petra a black box containing the Witch Factor from which she has employed the Authority. Although she was incompatible with Melancholy, Petra did not succumb to the Factor's mental corruption, and she was limited in making use of its full power unless it is in exchange for a price.

Compression (圧縮, Asshuku): Using this Authority, Petra possessed the power to compress space, time, sensations, processes, and concepts. She primarily wielded Compression as a form of teleportation by compressing the distance that would be required to travel from one point to another, or to compress intangible things such as the time of thought and discussion processes or the sensations of agony within people in order to support her allies. As any individual besides Hector is incompatible with Melancholy due to its nature, Petra was required to bypass Od Lagna to wield Compression. In order to do this, she had to take from people something with the possibility to influence the world as compensation to offer to Od Lagna in order to use the Authority, whether that is the existence of a spell that could open up many futures or something else with a similar influence. Likewise, compensation can be given by different parties depending on one's intention. If one wanted the user of the Authority to move them, then that person would give compensation; alternatively, if the user decided to use the Authority on a different person of their own accord, the user would offer compensation. Though the totality of the compensation that the Witch Factor's custodian, Clind, has exchanged to wield Melancholy is unknown, he has been provided compensation by Roswaal L. Mathers, who gave up "four magics" to allow him to use his power, and in one failed loop, Petra, who gave up the possibility to become Subaru's bride. She also forfeited various sacrifices, including to never imbibe, pen a missive, clutch a stuff toy, and so on. When she invoked the Authority, despite claiming during the battle between Roy Alphard and the Aldebusters that the people of the Royal Capital had offered compensation for them to use, Petra was later shown to have offered a great deal or all of the compensation on her own. Once the price was paid, an incompatible user of the Witch Factor could unrestrainedly exercise Compression until the provided compensation was used up.
Instant Teleportation: With this utilization of Compression, Petra could seemingly instantaneously transport herself and other people alongside her if necessary in the blink of an eye from a place she started at to another place of her choosing by compressing the time and distance that would be required to travel from one point to another. In Clind's case, it can be employed so long as it is within the Kingdom of Lugunica, while in contrast, Petra was not forced to abide by the same limitation, being able to transport people to the Agzadd Canyon in Kararagi. However, using this form of Compression becomes significantly more difficult on wary and resistant opponents, and it is considered a herculean task to perform it on foes such as a Sin Archbishop or the Divine Dragon. To use this manner of Compression effectively, either the target must give their consent, or the opponent must be caught off guard.
Compress Agony (コンプレス・アゴニー, Konpuresu Agonī): As opposed to Clind, who never innovated on the way he utilized the Authority of Melancholy, only employing it for instant teleportation and going on the offensive to attack opponents, Petra developed her own original applications of Melancholy to use on conceptual things. These applications, which she had collectively given the name Compress Agony to, allowed her to compress the time it took for her targets to experience various mental faculties, emotional problems, discussions, sensations, and other similar things.
Process Compression: Petra was able to compress the time it took for people to gather their thoughts together and discuss with each other. Doing this eliminated the time that it would ordinarily take for people to think over a situation and talk to each other, as well as the time it would take to speak with their allies, effectively making it to where any such talks and discussions were immediately understood by each person affected and allowing them to respond to things with the most optimal course of action immediately. From the perspective of someone whose thoughts have been compressed, it appears as if they instantly reach a judgement and they are left in the dark as to why they attained said judgement. While typically seen in an advantageous light, using this could have the opposite effect on someone who was forced to push their minds far beyond the norm, such as someone like Aldebaran, whose Authority essentially already pushes his mind into overdrive. By using this against such a person, it can cause that person's mind to practically overheat, making it so that they are unable to respond or react appropriately to their surroundings. However, this also provided the risk that the target would be able to adapt to the compression and use it to their own gain, making it a double-edged sword.
Sensation Compression: Petra was able to compress the time it took for one to experience things such as pain, trauma, hesitation, and other such sensations like unconsciousness. By doing so, she could force her target to go through all of their emotions, even if they tried to suppress them in the back of their minds or hearts. Every such feeling would be felt in a mere instant and all at once, seemingly amplified due to how long it would ordinarily have taken to process such feelings. Trauma could be overcome in an instant; pain became a momentary passing that would not hold back or stall those experiencing it, which she displayed against Roy Alphard's Eclipsing Binary; and, though it was not shown, it was implied that Petra could even use this compression to awaken anyone who had fallen unconscious by having the time it took for them to ordinarily wake up pass in an instant.

intro: Pivot Arnancy (ピボット・アーナンシー) was the first Deputy Commander of the Zergev Squadron and a knight of the Royal Army.
appearance: Pivot was a man with long brown hair and a monocle. He usually wore his Royal Guard uniform.
personality: A capable, sophisticated, and intelligent man. history:
Pivot was one of the old guards of the Zergev Squadron whose dependable and shrewd nature kept the somewhat ragtag squad running smoothly behind the scenes. He was one of few people who could handle Wilhelm's standoffish behavior when he was younger without losing his cool.

He would take part many battles in war with the Zergev Squadron until the fateful Battle of Aihiya Swamp where he and most of the squad would be killed by Libre Fermi when defending an injured and immobile Wilhelm with their lives while under the effects of one Sphinx's magic circle spells. He and the fallen Zergev Squadron were later revived as corpse soldiers in that very same battle, used by Sphinx to help her escape, and were ultimately finished off by Bordeaux.

name: Natsuki Kenichi
nickname: Ken (ケン)
relatives: Natsuki Naoko (wife) ; Natsuki Subaru (son)
intro: Natsuki Kenichi (菜月 賢一) is Subaru's father and Naoko's husband. Though a minor character overall, he is pivotal to Subaru's story.
appearance: Kenichi is a good-looking, relatively tall, middle-aged man with short, combed-back black hair similar to Subaru's. He has drooping black eyes with angled eyebrows, and for his age, he's surprisingly well built and athletic. Most of the time, he's seen wearing average-looking, rectangular glasses that complement his usual laid-back smile and positive demeanor perfectly. One could immediately recognize his blood connection with Subaru.
personality: Kenichi is sociable, usually talking with acquaintances while outside, and, coupled with his good looks, tends to get the email addresses of high school girls. He is usually in high spirits, but can be moody at times, and also enjoys teasing his son Subaru when he wakes up. As a mayonnaise lover, he collects the caps of empty mayonnaise bottles.
history:
At some point, Kenichi met Naoko when she was being tricked by a bad adult and skillfully talked her out of the situation. When he discovered her being tricked the same way the next day, he realized that just a warning wouldn't be enough, which set off his instincts and caused him to grow attached to her. Kenichi married Naoko and had a son with her: Subaru. Kenichi was something of a local celebrity in their community, getting along with everyone from high schoolers to the elderly, resulting in his phone having thousands of contacts.

Subaru idolized his father and wanted to be like him. However, after this proved to be impossible, he went through a downward spiral that ultimately resulted in him becoming a shut-in. While the self-hating Subaru wanted his parents to reprimand him, the couple saw that their son was just going through something and instead subtly encouraged him to go back to school every day. Kenichi also saw that Subaru was using exaggerated gestures in his attempts to be noticed, which only caused him to make a fool of himself; a bad habit his son inherited from him that he knew he had to correct.

According to the author, after Subaru went missing (was transported to Lugunica), a police investigation was launched but ended up empty-handed. As a result, Kenichi and Naoko now spend their days praying for their son's safety.

appearance: Plum typically wears a pink dress with a small ribbon attached onto it. She has her bright green hair styled in a bob style haircut, and she has light blue eyes.
personality: Being a young child, Plum is easily scared when separated from her parents. Despite this, she is quite cheerful, easily warming up to Emilia and Subaru while they helped find her mother. She also tried to show gratitude to those who help her, as in both the failed loop and the main timeline, she gave her hair ornament to Emilia as thanks for bringing her back to her parents.
history:
Behind the Scenes of Life in Another World from Zero
On the day of Subaru's arrival into the world, Plum was in the Royal Capital with her mother. However, she got separated from her and started to cry when she couldn't find her. Despite her own problems, Emilia noticed her and tried to help her, but because she was taught not to talk to strangers, she instead cried. In order to help her open up to her, she offered her name and created ice sculptures and had Puck dance. Afterward, the two walked through the capital until they arrived at an appa stand, where the girl's parents were. When Kadomon asked her how he could repay her, though she didn't give the full explanation, she asked about Felt and how something she had was stolen, leading him to tell her about the Loot House and warning her not to go there. Emilia still resolved to go there, and before she could go, Plum offered her a red flower ornament as thanks for her help.

name: Odglass
alias: Sacred Beast (霊獣, Reijū) ; Benevolent Mother (慈母, Jibo)
nickname: Virtuous Monster (善意のお化け, Zen'i no Obake) (by Echidna)
affiliation: Four Great Spirits ; Gusteko ; Gustekan Church ; Sacred Mountain Pardochia
intro: Odglass (オドグラス) is the Sacred Beast, one of the Four Great Spirits. She is known as the mother of Gusteko and the Benevolent Mother of the Gustekan Church.
appearance: Odglass is said to have the appearance of a large, white bear.
personality:
Odglass is a spirit who, unlike most other spirits, interferes with the world by watching over the people of the Holy Kingdom of Gusteko, where she resides, with affection and benevolence from her abode, the Sacred Mountain Paradochia. She is a powerful great spirit who has scores of spirits and lesser spirits under her control, which she uses to help humans live in the permafrost-covered nation.

As the Benevolent Mother, Odglass is the one responsible for causing Gusteko's perpetual snow. She knows everything that happens within the snow's reach, and as part of her contract with the Holy King, the monarch is able to be aware of everything within the nation and deal with anything bad that appears. According to Beatrice, it is also said that the Sacred Beast is the one who does not really listen among the Four Great Spirits, and she claimed that Echidna called Odglass a virtuous monster.
history: When the Holy Kingdom of Gusteko was founded, Odglass exchanged a contract with a spiritual arts user who followed her, bestowed the title of Holy King onto them, and from then on, she was involved in choosing successive Holy Kings, who were selected out of the citizens regardless of their bloodline or origin. This process created an established and long relationship with Odglass and Gusteko, as the tradition to select the Holy King is something she has held from the beginning of the country’s history. Because of this, she is heralded as the Gustekan Church’s Benevolent Mother.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
As one of the Four Great Spirits, Odglass has tremendous power that puts her on a similar level to others of her kind. Though, the full extent of her power is unknown, as the one responsible for Gusteko's permafrost, her reach seems to be immense.

Other
Climate Manipulation: It has been stated by the author that Odglass is the one responsible for covering Gusteko in snow and leaving it permanently cold. Although her snow does not cover the country from one tip of the country to the other, it still has immense range, and since the Gustekan Church's goal is to cover the world in her snow, it is implied that she can extend her reach even farther.
Limited Omniscience: It has been stated by the author that Odglass is aware of anything that takes place under the falling snow. While the exact specifics are unknown, this implies that Odglass is able to perceive the majority of events in the country. This being said, it is unknown if she requires people to directly be beneath the snowy skies or if this allows her to perceive events within buildings and vehicles such as carriages as well.
Shared Omniscience: Through her contract with the Holy King, she is able to share her ability to perceive the nation with them, allowing them to act however they see fit in response.

name: Muspel
alias: Stone (石塊, Ishikure)
intro: Muspel (ムスペル) is the Stone, one of the Four Great Spirits. It was said to roam freely within the Sacred Vollachia Empire, but in actuality, the spirit was secretly granted convicts to use as anchors by Vollachia and distributed across the country to provide a number of regions with its benefits. Despite not making an official appearance, Muspel's influence played a major role during the events of Arc 8.
personality:
Muspel is thought to have no will, words, or philosophy, and appears to exist solely as a deific being. Records from the Empire state that Muspel moves on a grand scale every 12 years, leading to various earthquakes after its movement.

However, when Arakiya devoured the rest of Muspel, it temporarily gained a sense of self-preservation, which resulted in Arakiya’s uncontrolled rampage in the Imperial Capital.
history:
Sometime around the events of Vollachia's most recent Imperial Selection Ceremony, Vincent Abellux found a method to trap Muspel within its territory. By using Muspel's power, he was able to fend off the Siege on the Abellux Castle carried out by one of his younger half-sisters, Lamia Godwin. When Prisca and Vincent's lives were in danger due to Lamia's artillery, Arakiya devoured a small portion of Muspel in order to defend her princess.

According to Vincent, at least throughout his time as emperor, convicts were used to connect to Muspel and preserve its connection to the Empire. The effects of the contract made convicts experience death of the mind while the Stone remained at its contractor's location; Vollachia took advantage of Muspel's tendency of being at its contractor's location in order to move it around and distribute its positive effects on the land to various areas in the nation where it was needed while continually replenishing their supply of convicts so as to prevent the possibility of losing track of it.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
As one of the Four Great Spirits, Muspel has a tremendous amount of power and mana, and its power is embedded into the very earth of Vollachia. By Vincent's description, the land upon which it rests receives its protection, providing fertile lands and a positive impact on the recuperation of those who land on those lands. On the other hand, precisely because its power is so deeply connected to the country’s lands, if its connection was suddenly removed, Vollachia would cease to exist, and the land would become uninhabitable. Similarly, though it is possible to make a contract with humans, its power is so great that it robs its contractor of their mind. In fact, it has been stated several times that Arakiya, who had devoured the Stone on two different occasions, should have exploded from the sheer amount of power flowing through her body. Due to its unique state of having no presence of mind and never having been shown in combat, it is currently unclear exactly how powerful Muspel is in its entirety.

Magic/Spiritual Arts
As the great spirit presiding over earth mana, Muspel is capable of using earth magic. However, as it has not shown sentience, it is unclear how proficient it is in casting magic.

Spells:
Restoration Magic (復元魔法, Fukugen Mahō): A type of magic that can recover objects to their original state. Although Muspel never consciously cast restoration magic of its own accord, its mana was siphoned by Sphinx during the Great Disaster in order to cast this spell as a means of creating vessels for the undead resurrected across Vollachia.

intro: Orphe (オルフェ) was the former Director of the Six Tongues. Once a con artist, Orphe met Wilhelm Trias in the Prison Tower when the latter was arrested. Later, when Wilhelm came to visit him, Orphe gave the Sword Demon advice on how to deal with Theresia's situation after receiving a guarantee that a good word would be put in for him. Upon Orphe's release, at Wilhelm's recommendation, Bordeaux Zergev began making use of his skills, resulting in the foundation of the Six Tongues.
appearance: Orphe is a handsome man with long hair, a neat and tidy appearance, and a pale complexion that suggests a touch of high society. He is described as having a sweet face and voice that could charm anyone regardless of gender.
personality: A sharp smooth-talker not above acting on his desires, Orphe gained a reputation as a philanderer as a result of swindling six noble women at once. Despite his habits, he is an intelligent man who is skilled with gathering information in a short period of time. He was trusted and capable enough to be appointed as the leader of the Six Tongues. He spoke highly of his smooth-talking, saying it was the only skill he had in his life, and could use it to navigate the Kingdom and get people to reveal to him things that officials would not be told.
history:
In the past, Orphe was seeing six different women in the Noble District of the Royal Capital and gave each of them different stories, which resulted in him being called Six Tongues because it was as if he used a different tongue with each of them, and eventually being incarcerated and sent to the Prison Tower. When Wilhelm Trias was imprisoned for invading the ceremony commemorating Theresia van Astrea's achievements in the Demi-Human War at the Royal Castle, Orphe was in the cell directly across from him, and the two briefly spoke before the Sword Demon was released. Sometime later, after speaking with Miklotov McMahon about Theresia's circumstances as the Sword Saint, Wilhelm returned to meet Orphe, receiving advice on what to do in regard to her situation and promising to put in a good word for him and release him sooner upon his readmittance into the army. After Orphe's release from the Prison Tower, Bordeaux had the conman come under his service at Wilhelm's recommendation. In no time, Orphe proved himself a worthy intelligence gatherer, leading to the foundation of the secret intelligence organization bearing his alias, the Six Tongues, becoming its leader.

With his new position under Bordeaux's supervision, using his tongue as his primary resource, he had been permitted to do a wide range of things throughout the Royal Capital and the Kingdom as a whole, procuring information that officials such as knights would have been unable to. When meeting with Bordeaux and Wilhelm to discuss the Stride Faction after they had begun attacking Lugunica, he requested permission to contact remnants of the Demi-Human Alliance and interrogate them if necessary. Later, he obtained the information that they had been spotted at Abiate, and discovered that those responsible for sheltering them while they were staying hidden from view were thugs, broke mercenaries, or those who bore hostilities towards the Kingdom, the demi-humans from across the country with lingering negative sentiments against it after the Demi-Human War. He relayed Cragrell Dawson's request to speak with the Sword Saint to Wilhelm and, with the Six Tongues presided over by him, he continued to keep an eye on the remnants of the Demi-Human Alliance. In preparation for Raizo's attack on Gionis Lugunica's life, Roswaal J. Mathers suggested using Clind to counter the shinobi, to which Miklotov approved and Orphe arranged the preparations for to ensure his defeat as smoothly as possible.

Although Orphe's status is unknown in the present, Russell Fellow has succeeded his leadership position to become the current Director of the Six Tongues.

name: Palmyra
intro: Palmyra (パルミラ) is Colette's friend. She, alongside Colette, later joined Omega and formed the Omega Party.
appearance: Palmyra is a teenage girl with long black hair and piercing brown sanpaku eyes. She wears a dark grey coat along with a short black skirt and long dark boots. She and Colette have matching hairpins.
personality:
A headstrong, sensible girl with a caring nature, Palmyra is loyal to and protective of her younger friend Colette. She is prone to openly, bluntly voicing her frustrations, often briefly bickering or bantering with Omega as a result of her choice of words or actions. While having an aggressive exterior and being wary of strangers, she has a kind heart and behaves mindfully.

Despite her usual attitude, Palmyra tends to think ahead, worrying about the future of the party and planning for eventual problems to crop up. She will keep an eye on others who have joined the group and try to talk in secret from them in preparation for how to deal with them. That said, she is still quick to accept newcomers after a brief conversation, and she will feel somewhat guilty for suspecting them. She is also quick to act in events when her friends are in danger, though she will openly express her annoyance when her friends also interfere with her attempts to help. This is usually the case with Omega, leaving Palmyra regularly frustrated. Most prominently, however, she is also willing to keep secrets from Colette in order to keep her innocence intact and not worry her, often colluding with other members of her party to do so.
history:
The Requirements to be a Witch
Palmyra is Colette's friend who stuck by her side when she was outcast from their village, despite being aware of her past and her identity as a "Beast". When away from her home village, in which she lived within its largest house, she maintained a graveyard for the animals that were mauled by Colette's transformed form. When Palmyra first met Omega, she warned the half-elf girl to leave the forest they were in, or else the "Beast" would eventually tear her apart. Omega did not heed her warning and challenged the "Beast" herself, almost managing to successfully slay it until Palmyra stopped her and revealed that it was Colette, who she wanted to help. She proceeded to explain Colette's history of being ostracized as a Witch due to her connection with a "Witchbeast" which slaughtered everyone that took her in. Omega reveals that Colette had transformed into a beastly form due to the Beast Protection Bracelet, a meteor her parents unknowingly gifted to her when she was young with the effect of enhancing its user's mana and transforming its user in exchange for their sense of reason. Soon after, the Witch unveiled her true appearance to Palmyra and an unconscious Colette, sensing promise in the former for being able to withstand her presence. She then made her way to Colette's village in an attempt to straighten the situation out with them. However, this only made things worse for Colette, as she was forced to leave the area as a consequence for being acquainted with a "Witch". Seeing as how Colette had nowhere else to go and Palmyra had used up all of her courtesy for the village, the two of them were invited by Omega to join her, officially forming their party.

One Wild Night
The trio then proceeded to cross over into Gusteko. One day, they were caught in a severe blizzard and rescued by Noelle Tuérico, an Itinerant Preacher of the Gustekan Church, after Omega launched a fire spell into the distance. They waited for Omega to regain her energy in a makeshift snow house Noelle created and spoke with her in the meantime, learning about the term Silver Blessing, her position in the Gustekan Church, and the nearby church building they can use as a refuge. They visit the church once Omega is rejuvenated and acquaint themselves with Podoso, Admonsah, and Maqueena, each of whom had come to the church to meet the pastor who lives there, Coatl. The trio learned of Coatl's history of having saved a local town from the effects of an avalanche unintentionally caused by the Ice Thieves and how he took up a position of the town's watcher following his charity towards its people, becoming known by the moniker Saint of the Avalanche. Maqueena and Podoso split off from everyone else to visit another part of the church, and another visitor named Trellock arrives while they are out. Eventually, Maqueena discovers something and screams, prompting everyone else to follow after her to find what has caused her fear. They all stumble upon Coatl's corpse, prompting Omega to say that there was a cold-blooded killer among them.

Omega took charge of the situation, using detective work to determine the killer's identity. She heard from Podoso that there had been a string of serial murders, with Coatl being the eighth known victim. The other victims were peddlers and travelers. Querying him about the seventh victim, Omega then sets her sights on Admonsah, whom she was certain was associated with them. They learn Admonsah was a former slave who unexpectedly killed his owner in self-defense. He was unequivocally forgiven by a majority of the group. Omega tries to ascertain why Coatl would be murdered, searching for any hidden savings. Suddenly, everyone but Maqueena in the room fell asleep to the effects of the Muskrim flower, and she made her getaway with Coatl's collection of magic stones, not wanting to stay and fall victim to his murderer, and Noelle followed after her. While Omega, who had woken up, took care of them, the culprit responsible for the serial murderers, Trellock, attempted to murder Colette, who Palmyra had wrapped her arms around before falling unconscious in an attempt to protect her, but her Beast Protection Bracelet activated, severely injuring him. In the end, they pretended that Noelle had apprehended Trellock and left, Podoso decided to take in Admonsah, and Maqueena was forced to stop conning people. With her revenge foiled, Noelle was left aimless. Colette proposed for her to join their group to which she accepted upon Omega's approval.

One Wild Night Extra
Later, the party decided to head to the town Podoso had told them about. Eventually, they set up camp, and while Colette and Noelle set up the camp, Palmyra decided to talk with Omega about including Noelle in their travels, worried about getting her involved in their troubles, which included Omega being a half-elf Witch and Colette's bracelet. Omega believed that there was nothing to worry about, and shortly after, Noelle, who had heard part of their conversation appeared and said that she already knew about Omega's secret and chose to follow them regardless. Though Palmyra asked if she had a thing for odd people and Noelle's joking reply that she did, just like Palmyra, she claimed to be just as odd, as she was an itinerant preacher from the Gustekan Church who had decided to leave. Though Palmyra thought it wasn't as bad as Omega's secret, Omega told her that she was underestimating the Church and what they bestowed Noelle, and the two claimed that they would not be amicable toward her effectively breaking a contract, something which might end up leading to them falling into her mess. Though Palmyra told Omega to be prepared to fight, when Noelle told her to feel free to kick her from the party if she ever became a burden, to which she replied by saying not to underestimate her and spoke of her own circumstances, basically unintentionally cornering Noelle into staying in the party after saying not to use Colette as an excuse. Colette arrived shortly after, and the group decided not to talk to her about their conversation. Instead, they ate, and Noelle explained repairs that she had made to their equipment and offered her knowledge of how to use their equipment and how to survive in Gusteko, including knowledge on the Gustekan Church, to which Palmyra and Omega realized that they wouldn't be able to survive in Gusteko without Noelle.

Omega in Wonderland
The party continued to trudge to the snows of Gusteko, with Palmyra and Omega becoming exhausted. Attempting to give Palmyra some more energy, Colette attempted to let her use her bracelet, but when Palmyra tried, it left her weak and vomiting. Omega explained the reason for this, claiming she allowed it to happen because she wanted to see the look on her face. Afterward, she had Noelle carry Palmyra while Colette carried her. As they got closer to the town of Sylphoa, Omega dispelled a barrier, and eventually they reached the town, where she and Colette fell subject to the Dream Arts spell that had been cast over the town.

Meanwhile, Noelle and Palmyra, who were unaffected thanks to Noelle's seal, met with a Temple Knight named Zank Metley, who was there to hunt a heretic. Noelle and Palmyra, carrying the others' unconscious bodies, followed him into an empty tent, where he explained the situation. However, after entering into conflict with Palmyra, who does not follow the Church's teaching, Colette's bracelet senses danger and transformed her body into a beast. After Zank deemed her a heretic, Colette ran away with Omega and Palmyra. Elsewhere in town, she came across the person responsible for the town's predicament, Shion who, after she introduced herself and explained the situation to her, asked for Palmyra's assistance. Soon after, she used her hypnosis magic to put Palmyra to sleep, giving her a message to pass on to Lilac. After passing it along to her, she woke up and told Zank, who was in a fight with Noelle, that Mikli Yulitô, the other Temple Knight, was alive.

Following this, after Omega spoke to Zank, who had in reality come to retrieve Mikli, and had him leave with her and report the death of the heretic, Lilac released the people of Sylphoa from her dream world, and Omega offered Shion and Lilac to join her party. Since she couldn't quite trust the two, having just met them, she would give them a chance to look into her memories with their Dream Arts, giving them a chance to find the person from which the loan words they speak come from. The two accepted her offer and joined the party.

Witch Trials
One day, having moved on from Sylphoa, the Omega Party was walking in a snow field, where they encountered a Snow Blight. However, Omega swiftly dispatched it with Minya. Soon after, they arrived at Limbus, where signs claiming it was forbidden to go out at night and to comply with the "vows of the faith". Though slightly concerned about the town's eeriness, as the group was low on supplies, they decided to enter Limbus, where after a few minutes, they found themselves surrounded by the townsfolk who were armed with farming tools. Though they attempted to calm the townsfolk and offer them a gift in the form of the Snow Blight's crystallized head, they instead accuse her of being a Witch after seeing it, leading Omega to warn Colette against using her bracelet's transformation and Lilac from turning back into Shion, else they be declared Witches. Thanks to the appearance of Nananna Pezza and speaking with Noelle, she was able to vouch for them and clear them of being Witches.

Omega's group finds an inn to reside in where they discussed the issue at present, warning everyone about how easily they could be made into scapegoats whether for their abilities, race, or even the look in their eyes, and Noelle explained about Witch Hunts and Witch Trials being rare occurrences in Gusteko that Itinerant Preachers were sometimes sent to deal with. Although wanting to leave the town quickly, the group decides to stay in the town to help Noelle repay her debt to Nananna, and soon after, they meet with Nananna when she arrived to ask for the group's assistance. That night, the Witch Hunt is for a person named Piditz who had been tipped off as a Witch, and Nananna wanted him taken into custody only. When they later spotted Piditz and chased after him, Omega split off to corner him, only to find Mireille Hetia using her spiritual arts to kill Piditz. Thanks to being near the body, Omega was quickly turned into a scapegoat and declared a Witch so that Mireille could cover up her kill and at least prevent her from getting in the way of her and Nananna's revenge, and Omega was taken into custody.

Later, Colette visits Omega, and they point out that killings began before the party arrived, which should clear Omega's name, but instead, Mireille decides to have her executed anyway, and Palmyra objects to Edmon Quayle. As part of Omega's plan, Noelle persuades Nananna to speak up, and Nananna insists on the town holding a Witch Trial for Omega, and Palmyra declares that if she is a Witch that she would burn with her. At the inn, the party discusses how if the scale of this event expands, they will be unable to prevent the spread of the news this time, which could result in the party's persecution, even abroad, and their possible extradition back to the church. To clear their names, Colette states that they should find the real culprit for the murders. Lilac and Colette go to gather information around the town, and they meet with Mireille, who explained to them how the hunts started. Likewise, Omega explained this to Palmyra, as she learned it while imprisoned.

The next day, the Witch Trial is being held for Omega, overseen by Nananna and the Town Hall, while Palmyra acts as Omega's attorney. Despite her arguments, Edmon counter with his supposed knowledge of the Witches and Omega's chatter does not help. Colette speaks up and claims that she believes that things will not go as the council claims, as people will begin to notice that the entire event seems off, which resounds with the townsfolk. Because of this, Palmyra claims that there is a conspiracy, which Edmon fights against and asks for Nananna's assistance. Because she sides with the town, Lilac and Shion believe her to be part of the conspiracy, and they decide to use their dream arts to influence the people's mental states. Palmyra then claims that the council is using the Witch rumors to get rid of inconvenient people, which Edmon also fights against, though is quickly silenced when she states she heard it herself from a council member and declares that there is no Witch. Unfortunately, Omega claims otherwise.

Despite angering Palmyra, Omega decides to clear things up by declaring that there were two conspiracies taking place in town. Despite Nananna trying to prevent her from talking, Omega ignores her and explains that many of the victims were relatives of council members, and she claims that Nananna is the second conspirator, calling her the bastard child of Edmon whose mother was banished from the town, and as a result, she despised the town. Noelle later appears and confirms that her actions were in response to the death of an elderly healer, and she claims that Nananna tried to remove her from the trial by knocking her out since her only ire was with Limbus. Afterward, Noelle declares that the secretary, Mireille, was helping Nananna, as she was a bastard child of Edmon as well, and she stated how the corpses of Piditz and other people connected to the council and other outside officials were already dumped in a hole. Omega also declares that she witnessed Mireille killing Piditz. Enraged, Mireille uses her spiritual arts to char Edmon's arm with blue fire, and with the intent of killing the entire council, surrounds the council with blue fire, and she and Nananna stand against them. Although Omega is fine with leaving things as they are and taking their leave, Colette states she doesn't want things to end like this, and Omega decides to end the fighting in response to her plea, burning through her restraints and declaring herself a Witch.

Later, as Omega's party begins to leave the town, Noelle says her goodbyes to Nananna, and it is declared that the evil spirit accompanying Mireille will be disposed of. Likewise, it is claimed that Edmon's position is under threat with both his severe injuries and the loss of the citizens' trust, and Mireille claims she was mistaken about real Witches. Despite Colette believing that things were settled peacefully, however, Omega thinks to herself that Limbus would soon face its destruction, as since Omega, Nananna, and Mireille were not executed, there would be continuous Witch Hunts and deaths for scapegoats for the whole incident. Although considering telling Colette about this, she decides against it.
