intro: Olbart Dunkelkenn (オルバルト・ダンクルケン) is the previous Third ranking Divine General of the Sacred Vollachia Empire and the chieftain of Vollachia's shinobi village. He played an antagonistic role in Arc 7 and a supporting role in Arc 8. He also played a minor supporting role in The Tale of the Scarlet Princess.
appearance:
Olbart is a wrinkled old man with a stooped-over physique, natural for someone bearing over 90 years of life on their shoulders. His seemingly glowing yellow eyes are usually covered with very thick and long eyebrows which happen to be of the same color as his relatively long greyish-white hair. Perhaps his most characteristic feature are his two white and black antennas sprouting out of his forehead. Incidentally, these two antennas happen to add another 30 centimeters to Olbart's high, elevating the old man from mere 100 centimeters to a much more respectable height of 130 centimeters. Additionally, Olbart sports a long and thin beard, which can sometimes be hard to spot due to his color palette, and two golden earrings per each ear. Following the false Great Disaster that struck Chaosflame, Olbart lost his right hand from the elbow down, having it be absorbed by the shadows just after he pierced Subaru's abdomen with his hand for the second time. Later, his left hand from the elbow down was lost in his encounter with Sphinx amidst the Conquest of the Undead Capital.

Olbart clads himself in a tight white and black body suit that strongly resembles a kimono. Half of the suit is white, while the other half is black, creating a pattern that strongly resembles yin and yang. The sleeves of his suit are large enough to allow Olbart to hide his hands inside of them and are adorned with a half-circular pattern which completes itself when both sleeves are put together. To finish off his look, the old man wraps a purple scarf around his neck, which fits the body suit perfectly as the sleeves have purple accents. The scarf itself also has a yellow-colored motive drawn on it, as well as a yellow star. Finally, to hold the suit in place, Olbart uses a purple belt which he ties around his waist.
personality:
At first glance, Olbart appears as a friendly and energetic old man, who often makes light of the situations and predicaments he finds himself in. He usually likes to stay away from the center of attention, until his presence is needed, either for de-escalation or to put the situation under control by force. Whatever the case may be, Olbart never fails to seize the opportunity to crack jokes and lighten up the mood with his mostly light-hearted view on situations, though it should also be worth mentioning that some of his remarks can be strangely morbid, sending chills down his enemies' or allies' spines, such as when he threatened Kafma Irulux that he'll chop his head off on the spot, for deeming his remarks a bit overly egotistical. Due to his old age, Olbart has a habit of forgetting or mixing up different dates. Such an example can be seen when he mistakenly thought the gladiator rebellion took place two or three years prior to Arc 7, when in fact, it happened over eight years prior. As a member of the Nine Divine Generals and occupying the rank of Third, Olbart seemingly appears loyal to the emperor and the Empire, following his orders without much question and being prepared to lay down his life for the emperor. 

In reality, however, Olbart is a vicious and selfish old man with no concrete morals or loyalty. Being loyal only to himself, Olbart tends to act in a way that primarily benefits him. Though he faithfully follows his emperor's orders, he has no trouble disregarding them if he sees a better outcome in picking a different route than the one he was told to follow. Likewise, he has no trouble using deadly force on innocent people and children, as seen when he murdered Subaru, despite them taking the appearance of a ten-year-old child due to his "infantilization" technique, or Rui, despite appearing just as young. Furthermore, he is willing to do anything for victory, whether it means sabotaging one’s supplies, slashing apart his enemies’ limbs to prevent them from fighting entirely, or using an entire town as a decoy against a strong opponent, further cementing himself as the “Vicious Old Man”. He is not above even using his allies as decoys and body shields against his enemies. Of course, even in spite of the viciousness he is known for, there are some things that Olbart considers being taken too far, one example being the group that used sacrifices to turn Arakiya into a spirit eater, while another was the experimentation of souls that led to undead monstrosities born of mutated and mixed souls. In the case of the former, while he was unwilling to dispose of Arakiya, he did bring an end to the group responsible for her, while in the case of the latter, he believed it was better to bring an end to such monstrosities.

By not holding anything precious and refusing to devote his heart to anyone, Olbart has achieved the pinnacle of shinobi techniques, reigning as the indisputable strongest shinobi the Empire has to offer and climbed all the way up to the rank of Third among the Nine Divine Generals. With his unusually long life spanning over nine decades, Olbart has achieved pretty much everything he wished for. However, despite his being a perfect representation of what a shinobi should be, Olbart has always had his misgivings about how he had lived as a shinobi, and at times, he even attempted pass his teachings and beliefs onto the other shinobi of his village, albeit mostly meeting with failure, and at times, he would openly and brazenly disobey the village's doctrine. For example, Olbart does not believe that it is good for the shinobi to specialize in one technique and must be capable of exploiting their targets' weaknesses, and thus, the shinobi must be capable of using multiple techniques. Though, he failed to cultivate shinobi toward this direction, and with the supposed death of one of the village's most talented shinobi, Yae Tenzen, he came to believe the idea a lost cause. He also believes that, despite the teachings of the shinobi, living without finding something that one could hold precious holds back the true potential of the shinobi. Like Yae, because he is capable of doing almost anything without a second thought, most of life loses its spark, making it so that the idea of keeping something precious becomes more desireable. In fact, he has even pestered Yae regularly about such issues, claiming that she should also go against the shinobi's teachings. In particular, although he is aware that living as a shinobi means living in the shadows without the chance for fame, he holds the ambition of making his own death glamorous so that he can have posthumous fame, thus leaving a mark on the Empire's history and uprooting the very concept of shinobi. This is mainly because he believes that dying as a shinobi would leave their death as empty. Knowing that he was close to death in his old age, he decided to follow this strong ambition and decided to set his sights on murdering Emperor Vincent Vollachia, who he has regarded as the greatest emperor of all time.
history:
Olbart hails from the shinobi village located in the Sacred Vollachia Empire. Having been seemingly raised by the shinobi, Olbart has lived the life of one ever since an early age. He did not believe in the doctrine of specializing in only a single technique, instead training in using strategies that thwarted an opponent's strong points and learning techniques to guide a battle to a favorable result. By the time he reached middle-age, he had gained a reputation as the most formidable and deadly shinobi of all. When Shasuke and Raizo became runaway shinobi and fled from the village, he permitted them to escape on a whim, and revealed to them his secret, the ambition that led him to becoming a shinobi: to die an unimaginably flashy death. Eventually, Olbart became the chieftain of the shinobi, abandoning the single-technique doctrine in favor of his own philosophy. During the reign of Drizen Vollachia, Olbart meddled in the affairs of Kararagi and came to clash with Halibel. In the end, he was beaten half to death by Halibel, proving the Admirer was the strongest shinobi in the world, much to Olbart's chagrin. At another point in time, Olbart also came into contact and dealt with the people responsible for turning Arakiya into a spirit eater.

The Tale of the Scarlet Princess
Shortly after Vincent Vollachia's coronation as the seventy-seventh emperor of the Sacred Vollachia Empire roughly 7 years before the start of the main story, a large uprising took place on the Gladiator Island Ginunhive, with the gladiators led by Ubilk wanting to become independent from the mainland. In order to squash the rebellion, Vincent had dispatched a regiment of the Imperial Army led by the Divine General Olbart and Arakiya, who had yet to be indicted as one of the generals. While Arakiya infiltrated the island in order to lower the bridge and let the main force inside the island, Olbart patiently waited outside the island. After Arakiya and a gladiator named Al took back the Gladiator Island, Olbart offered a reward to the gladiator, but he denied it.

Years during Vincent's rule
There were few who were properly molded by Olbart's ideology, the most recent of them being Yae Tenzen, a girl who gained a reputation as a genius prodigy who blossomed as a shinobi from childhood. She became Olbart's most valued pupil, earning unreserved praise from him. Often, Olbart would speak to her, giving her advice that he had learned over the course of his long life while also tempting her to go against the very teachings that the village espoused. Having caught wind of her talents, Chisha Gold tasked her with infiltrating the Barielle Manor in the Kingdom of Lugunica to observe, and later, to assassinate Priscilla Barielle, which she ultimately failed, seemingly resulting in her purported death. Although Olbart referred ten more shinobi to the White Spider for him to deploy to Lugunica and fulfill the same task with, all ten of them failed at their tasks and met their ends, and no more shinobi were sent after her once one of the shinobi's techniques was turned against Chisha. In the aftermath of the situation, believing that Yae had truly died, Olbart felt regret that the cultivation of capable shinobi had seemed to end up a lost cause.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
Olbart is a tremendously powerful man with an incredibly long lifetime of surviving impossible odds and opponents more powerful than himself. His skills are such that he has been considered one of the most dangerous warriors in the Vollachia Empire. More than that, however, he is considered to be the pinnacle of being a shinobi, and he is the second most powerful shinobi in the world behind the Admirer, Halibel. Among Vollachian generals, if one did not include Cecilus's overwhelming strength and Arakiya's sheer firepower, Olbart, alongside one other general, are considered to be among the most dangerous elements in the event that a nation was to enter war with Vollachia.

Physical Traits/Flow Method
Skilled Martial Artist: As the leader of Vollachia's shinobi village and its strongest member, Olbart has mastered the art of being a shinobi. He can masterfully bend his body to his own will, perform attacks seemingly impossible for an aged man, and dish out monstrous damage to his surroundings and enemies. His speed, strength, and accuracy are nigh unmatched among all Nine Divine Generals of the Empire. Even while missing an arm, he seemed rather unaffected by it and even used it to his advantage while in combat. Olbart is shown to use misdirection while in combat, making his opponent think that he is ducking or attacking from one direction while in reality, his attack is coming from elsewhere. He is also particularly knowledgeable of the weaknesses of the human body and can accurately target those spots; even should he be forced to fight without killing his opponents, he can strike at pressure points to instantly incapacitate them. Even ignoring that, he has enough physical might that his hand is capable of piercing straight through his enemy's chest, and a kick from him holds enough power that it could not only send someone as strong as Garfiel flying away, but it could easily behead the average soldier.

Superhuman Speed: As a master shinobi, Olbart can move at insane speeds, seemingly teleporting and flying around the battlespace. During his fight with Yorna Mishigure, his speed is described as that of a fighter jet, moving around at speeds surpassing that which can be followed by a normal human eye. His speed, in application with his mastery of primarily shinobi-used martial arts and deadly precision achieved only by a select few individuals around the world, make him one of the most deadly and efficient fighters hailing from the Empire. 

Techniques
Shinobi Techniques (シノビの術技, Shinobi no Jutsugi): Over the course of his long life, Olbart has become the pinnacle of the Empire's shinobi, making him the second strongest shinobi in the world, inferior only to Halibel, and one of the country's strongest living fighters, able to easily overpower most people facing him. By holding nothing precious to him, Olbart has managed to achieve the peak of shinobi techniques, and due to his belief that a shinobi should not specialize in merely one technique and must be capable of exploiting their opponents' weaknesses, Olbart has achieved mastery over many techniques, which, when combined with his vast experience, has allowed him to survive to the present day while able to overcome nearly every kind of opponent. After living for so long, he has mastered the bare basics of being a shinobi: stealing his opponents' attention, clouding their mind, immobilize them, and kill them. His skill is so great that when he is forced to enter combat, he is able to deceive even the minds of experienced warriors such as Garfiel Tinzel and attack from directions different from his body indicates, even while lacking an arm.
Infantilization (幼児化, Yōji-ka): One of his trademark skills that played a considerable role throughout Arc 7 and Arc 8 was Olbart's Infantilization technique. Essentially, by making contact with a person and altering their Od, Olbart can effectively rejuvenate the target's body and make them physically younger. By doing so, most of his enemies are effectively rendered powerless against him, as they're usually left in the body of a ten-or-so year-old child. Furthermore, after being "infantilized", the target's deduction skills and overall intellectual capabilities slowly diminish over time, reflecting their sudden rejuvenation in both body and mind. Olbart later revealed this to be one of his most rare techniques and that it was employed to extort or quickly depose of enemies and their bodies.
Energy Redirection: Olbart is capable of using the energy from his opponent's attack and redirecting as he pleases, including back into the core of the attacker's body or the ground.
Unnamed Earth Diving Technique: Through an unknown method, Olbart is capable of sinking into the ground and appearing elsewhere on the battlefield. He is also capable of taking things from the environment and flinging them at his enemy from beneath the ground.
Unnamed Poisoning Technique: Through an unknown method, Olbart is capable of leaving behind poison with little more than a handprint. Those afflicted bleed, and their skin, flesh, and bone face being burned while steaming. It is unknown if this poison can spread to the rest of the body, as Garfiel, who was once hit with the technique, tore out the affected area before it could deal too much damage.
Unnamed Burial Technique: By giving a tap to a solid surface, he can make said surface ripple like water, softening it to the point that he can hide bodies within it, and afterward, the surface hardens again.

Other
Stealth: As a shinobi, Olbart is a master of stealth. He is able to completely erase his presence if he so wishes, to the point that others will forget that he is in the same room, and he can remain hidden until he has either killed everyone nearby or purposefully makes his presence known. Though it is unclear if his statement is true, he has claimed himself to be able to go invisible. Likewise, by keeping his presence hidden, he can also bypass the effects of specific curses, such as Eugard Vollachia's Curse of Thorns, which covers a relatively large radius.

Keen Battle Experience: Due to his long lifespan, Olbart has seen many fights and toppled countless opponents. This allowed him to become quite proficient at figuring out his opponents' tricks and tactics, allowing him to form destructive counters to incoming attacks. Olbart immediately recognized Al's use of his unknown Authority, noting he had some strange tricks up his sleeve, something that completely flew over Kafma Irulux's head, and after seeing Rui use Leaper once, he was able to determine how it worked. Likewise, he used this experience to expertly target his enemies’ weaknesses while on the battlefield, something that allowed him to even wipe out an army by himself. It was this habit and viciousness that earned him the moniker Vicious Old Man, and it is thanks to this that he has managed to survive fighting against even opponents who were stronger than himself.

Keen Orientation: Olbart has mastered the ability to grasp a scene by looking at a map and never forget a location upon a single visit. It is thanks to this ability that he was able to traverse the Crystal Palace, which he had visited many times prior, with ease, despite its hallways and rooms being distorted.

Equipment
As a shinobi, Olbart carries many traditional weapons associated with them, such as kunai and shuriken, as well as compressed spirit stone bombs, keeping them stored away safely inside his sleeves:
Kunai & Shuriken: Olbart can use his kunai knives and shuriken with terrifying speed and precision, killing very skilled opponents without them even realizing it. It is not uncommon for him to flood the area around him with his weapons in order to cut off his opponent's movements, and he can use shinobi techniques to disguise when he threw them. He also has his shuriken coated in poison that is capable of exploding even if the target dodges.
Ration Balls: Olbart keeps ration balls, small balls filled with nutrients without regard for taste, on his person. Despite their awful taste, by Olbart's words, they are capable of keeping a person going for an entire day.
Compressed Fire Stone Bombs: During his fight with Yorna, Olbart demonstrated a deadly and brutal weapon; compressed fire stone bombs. Taking a similar shape to his emergency food rations, Olbart is equipped with small black balls which have chunks of fire stones embedded inside of them. Though their size is miniscule, the potential damage dealt by their explosions is no laughing matter. By simply throwing them in the air and forcing Yorna to try and destroy them in order to prevent a bombardment of the city below, Olbart managed to catch Subaru in a brutal death loop with there being no seeming way to avoid the blast and having his eyes and ears destroyed.
Book of Techniques: Olbart has a book which he uses to keep track of and record as many different combat techniques and skills as possible.

name: Null
nickname: Old Man Null (ヌル爺さん Nuru-jīsan)
intro: Null (ヌル), commonly known as Old Man Null (ヌル爺さん), is a healer who previously resided at the Gladiator Island Ginunhive for many years. He later became a member of the Pleiades Battalion.
appearance: Null is an elderly man with a thin and wrinkly body. He has protruding white hair near his ears, and a circular symbol above his right ear, and an elongated head. He wears a light vest and a long scarf wrapped around his neck.
personality: Prior to leaving Ginunhive, Null often cooped himself up in the island's healing room, where he had the free time to occasionally doze off when he was not working. He also dislikes when others use his medicine for harm, befitting his position as a healer.
history:
Many years ago, Null was sent to the Gladiator Island Ginunhive for unknown reasons at a time when the island was much more deadly. One day, his life would change when he put a cloth over the wound of a gladiator who lost their arm. This would lead to more instances where he would be called to heal people. Null was consequently ordered to work as a healer in Ginunhive's healing room, and he would become more acquainted with bloody scenes over the years.

While Null lived peacefully as a healer, a gladiator would escape the Gladiator Island and the Chief at that time was promptly fired. To fill up the new position, Emperor Vincent Vollachia would appoint Gustav Morello as the new Island Chief. Under Gustav's leadership, the Gladiator Island was remade from its previous lawlessness into a more orderly place where there were less unnecessary deaths. As a result, the number of people who died from injuries or illnesses decreased.
abilities_text: Amateur Healing Skills: Although Null was formerly a healer at Ginunhive, he lacks the skills to properly treat other people, effectively making him a healer in name. Null can stitch wounds and concoct simple medicinal drugs. However, because he was not allowed to use effective drugs by the Gladiator Island's administrators, he couldn't create anything more than adverse concoctions, such as the poison he made for Subaru.

name: Noelle Tuérico
nickname: Big Breasts (でか乳, Deka Chichi) (by Maqueena)
intro: Noelle Tuérico (ノエル・トゥエリコ) is a former Itinerant Preacher of the Gustekan Church. She later deserted from her position to join the Omega Party.
appearance: Noelle is a fair-skinned woman with a curved body and plump chest. She has long, braided gold hair that reaches down past her shoulders, clear blue eyes, and wears a thick, black church vestment.
personality: Noelle is a friendly and cheerful girl who is willing to help those in need. That said, she is also smart and is properly wary of the people she is around, especially when it comes to fellow members of the Gustekan Church. Furthermore, she also has a vengeful side, born the day her village was crushed. She is patient and diligent enough to wait for years so that she can find her target. Likewise, she can also be rather brutal towards her enemies, and she is quick to resort to violence if anyone she deems her enemy doesn't meet her demands.
history:
Early Life
When she was young, Noelle lived in the village of Leanotte in Gusteko. However, after an avalanche caused by the Ice Thieves, many of the village's people died, including her family, her friends, and her neighbors. As a result, Noelle joined the Gustekan Church, seeking to use her induction into the faith as a means to pursue revenge against those responsible for the avalanche. For twelve years, she awaited the day she could exact her revenge, and she eventually managed to become an Itinerant Preacher. At one point, she was saved by Nananna Pezza's medicinal knowledge, and she later assisted her in regard to Leanotte.

One day, Noelle was forwarded a letter from Coatl, a pastor who used his savings to restore Leanotte in the aftermath of its avalanche and took up residence at a nearby church on a mountain, by the Gustekan Church. In the letter, he confessed that he had belonged to the Ice Thieves and had been among those who caused Leanotte's avalanche. When Noelle arrived at the church he resided in, Coatl welcomed her, affirming the sins he had committed, and requesting that retribution be limited only to his life. However, Noelle, whose reason for joining the Gustekan Church had been to seek payback on all of the Ice Thieves, refused to accept the result. She tortured Coatl in an attempt to force him to divulge the identities of his peers, but he refused, leading Noelle to murder him by dealing a killing blow to his head with her gloves. She then fled from Coatl's church, travelling down the mountain despite an ongoing blizzard until she caught a glimpse of a fire spell.

One Wild Night
After having seen a fire spell in the distance, Noelle found a party of girls in the snow, with one of them, Omega, passing out from the cold of the active blizzard. They waited for Omega to regain her energy in a makeshift snow house Noelle created and spoke with her in the meantime, learning about the term Silver Blessing, her position in the Gustekan Church, and the nearby church building they can use as a refuge. They visit the church once Omega is rejuvenated and acquaint themselves with Podoso, Admonsah, and Maqueena, each of whom had come to the church to meet the pastor who lives there, Coatl. The trio learns of Coatl's history of having saved a local town from the effects of an avalanche unintentionally caused by the Ice Thieves and how he took up a position of the town's watcher following his charity towards its people, becoming known by the moniker Saint of the Avalanche. Maqueena and Podoso split off from everyone else to visit another part of the church, and another visitor named Trellock arrived while they were out. Eventually, Maqueena discovered something and screams, prompting everyone else to follow after her to find what has caused her fear. They all stumbled upon Coatl's corpse, prompting Omega to say that there was a cold-blooded killer among them.

Omega took charge of the situation, using detective work to determine the killer's identity. She heard from Podoso that there had been a string of serial murders, with Coatl being the eighth known victim. The other victims were peddlers and travelers. Querying him about the seventh victim, Omega then sets her sights on Admonsah, whom she was certain was associated with them. They learn Admonsah was a former slave who unexpectedly killed his owner in self-defense. He was unequivocally forgiven by a majority of the group. Omega tries to ascertain why Coatl would be murdered, searching for any hidden savings. Suddenly, everyone but Maqueena in the room fell asleep to the effects of the Muskrim flower, and she made her getaway with Coatl's collection of magic stones, not wanting to stay and fall victim to his murderer. She was stopped outside by Noelle, who says she could not be affected by such a simple drug and had killed Coatl out of revenge for his former membership of the Ice Thieves and his part in causing the avalanche that devastated Leanotte, her town. Omega arrives to stop Noelle before she could kill Maqueena, outlining that she was only a con artist who perceived Coatl's connection to the Ice Thieves rather than an outright member before giving the ultimatum that she would die if she caused another death, yet again manifesting her true form while saying so. Meanwhile, the culprit responsible for the serial murderers, Trellock, attempted to murder Colette, but her Beast Protection Bracelet activated, severely injuring him. In the end, they pretended that Noelle had apprehended Trellock and left, Podoso decided to take in Admonsah, and Maqueena was forced to stop conning people. With her revenge foiled, Noelle was left aimless. Colette proposed for her to join their group to which she accepted upon Omega's approval.

One Wild Night Extra
Later, the party decided to head to the town Podoso had told them about. Eventually, they set up camp, and while Colette and Noelle set up the camp, Palmyra decided to talk with Omega about including Noelle in their travels, worried about getting her involved in their troubles, which included Omega being a half-elf Witch and Colette's bracelet. Omega believed that there was nothing to worry about, and shortly after, Noelle, who had heard part of their conversation appeared and said that she already knew about Omega's secret and chose to follow them regardless. Though Palmyra asked if she had a thing for odd people and Noelle's joking reply that she did, just like Palmyra, she claimed to be just as odd, as she was an itinerant preacher from the Gustekan Church who had decided to leave. Though Palmyra thought it wasn't as bad as Omega's secret, Omega told her that she was underestimating the Church and what they bestowed Noelle, and the two claimed that they would not be amicable toward her effectively breaking a contract, something which might end up leading to them falling into her mess. Though Palmyra told Omega to be prepared to fight, when Noelle told her to feel free to kick her from the party if she ever became a burden, to which she replied by saying not to underestimate her and spoke of her own circumstances, basically unintentionally cornering Noelle into staying in the party after saying not to use Colette as an excuse. Colette arrived shortly after, and the group decided not to talk to her about their conversation. Instead, they ate, and Noelle explained repairs that she had made to their equipment and offered her knowledge of how to use their equipment and how to survive in Gusteko, including knowledge on the Gustekan Church, to which Palmyra and Omega realized that they wouldn't be able to survive in Gusteko without Noelle.

Omega in Wonderland
The party continued to trudge through the snows of Gusteko, with Palmyra and Omega becoming exhausted. Attempting to give Palmyra some more energy, Colette attempted to let her use her bracelet, but when Palmyra tried, it left her weak and vomiting. Omega explained the reason for this, claiming she allowed it to happen because she wanted to see the look on her face. Afterward, she had Noelle carry Palmyra while Colette carried her. As they got closer to the town of Sylphoa, Omega dispelled a barrier, and eventually they reached the town, where she and Colette fell subject to the Dream Arts spell that had been cast over the town.

Meanwhile, Noelle and Palmyra, who were unaffected thanks to Noelle's seal, met with a Temple Knight named Zank Metley, who was there to hunt a heretic. Noelle and Palmyra, carrying the others' unconscious bodies, followed him into an empty tent, where he explained the situation. However, after entering into conflict with Palmyra, who does not follow the Church's teaching, Colette's bracelet senses danger and transformed her body into a beast. After Zank deemed her a heretic, Colette ran away with Omega and Palmyra, Noelle stood in his way and negotiated working with him to take care of the problem at hand, to which he complied. Soon after, Noelle encountered Shion who had just put Palmyra to sleep. Not listening to her, Noelle threatened Shion with violence, only to be warned that Zank had killed his allies. Shortly after, alongside the beastified Colette, she had a small fight with Zank, until Palmyra awoke and claimed that the other Temple Knight, Mikli Yulitô, was alive.

Following this, after Omega spoke to Zank, who had in reality come to retrieve Mikli, and had him leave with her and report the death of the heretic, Lilac, Shion's phantom, released the people of Sylphoa from her dream world, and Omega offered Shion and Lilac to join her party. Since she couldn't quite trust the two, having just met them, she would give them a chance to look into her memories with their Dream Arts, giving them a chance to find the person from which the loan words they speak come from. The two accepted her offer and joined the party.

Witch Trials
One day, having moved on from Sylphoa, the Omega Party was walking in a snow field, where they encountered a Snow Blight. However, Omega swiftly dispatched it with Minya. Soon after, they arrived at Limbus, where signs claiming it was forbidden to go out at night and to comply with the "vows of the faith". Though slightly concerned about the town's eeriness, as the group was low on supplies, they decided to enter Limbus, where after a few minutes, they found themselves surrounded by the townsfolk who were armed with farming tools. Though they attempted to calm the townsfolk and offer them a gift in the form of the Snow Blight's crystallized head, they instead accuse her of being a Witch after seeing it, leading Omega to warn Colette against using her bracelet's transformation and Lilac from turning back into Shion, else they be declared Witches. Thanks to the appearance of Nananna and speaking with Noelle, she was able to vouch for them and clear them of being Witches.

Omega's group finds an inn to reside in where they discussed the issue at present, warning everyone about how easily they could be made into scapegoats whether for their abilities, race, or even the look in their eyes, and Noelle explained about Witch Hunts and Witch Trials being rare occurrences in Gusteko that Itinerant Preachers were sometimes sent to deal with. Although wanting to leave the town quickly, the group decides to stay in the town to help Noelle repay her debt to Nananna, and soon after, they meet with Nananna when she arrived to ask for the group's assistance. That night, the Witch Hunt is for a person named Piditz who had been tipped off as a Witch, and Nananna wanted him taken into custody only. When they later spotted Piditz and chased after him, Omega split off to corner him, only to find Mireille Hetia using her spiritual arts to kill Piditz. Thanks to being near the body, Omega was quickly turned into a scapegoat and declared a Witch so that Mireille could cover up her kill and at least prevent her from getting in the way of her and Nananna's revenge, and Omega was taken into custody.

Later, Colette visits Omega, and they point out that killings began before the party arrived, which should clear Omega's name, but instead, Mireille decides to have her executed anyway, and Palmyra objects to Edmon Quayle. As part of Omega's plan, Noelle persuades Nananna to speak up, and Nananna insists on the town holding a Witch Trial for Omega, and Palmyra declares that if she is a Witch that she would burn with her. At the inn, the party discusses how if the scale of this event expands, they will be unable to prevent the spread of the news this time, which could result in the party's persecution, even abroad, and their possible extradition back to the church. To clear their names, Colette states that they should find the real culprit for the murders. Lilac and Colette go to gather information around the town, and they meet with Mireille, who explained to them how the hunts started. Likewise, Omega explained this to Palmyra, as she learned it while imprisoned. As for Noelle, she joined Nananna, who had been speaking with Edmon about finding Piditz. As she is intent on finding out about the real culprit, Nananna knocks her out and hides her in a pit where all the bodies of the dead "Witches" were dumped. Meanwhile, Shion used her dream arts to peer into the minds of the townsfolk, and she warns Lilac that the "Witch" is just a conspiracy by the council to get rid of political enemies.

After learning of this, Lilac informs the Colette and Palmyra, and the elves suggest sowing division in the people to uproot the conspiracy. Though wanting to talk to Noelle, she does not come back that night, and Lilac and Shion decide to use their dream arts to nudge the townsfolk to attend the upcoming. The next day, the Witch Trial is being held for Omega, overseen by Nananna and the Town Hall, while Palmyra acts as Omega's attorney. Despite her arguments, Edmon counter with his supposed knowledge of the Witches and Omega's chatter does not help. Colette speaks up and claims that she believes that things will not go as the council claims, as people will begin to notice that the entire event seems off, which resounds with the townsfolk. Because of this, Palmyra claims that there is a conspiracy, which Edmon fights against and asks for Nananna's assistance. Because she sides with the town, Lilac and Shion believe her to be part of the conspiracy, and they decide to use their dream arts to influence the people's mental states. Palmyra then claims that the council is using the Witch rumors to get rid of inconvenient people, which Edmon also fights against, though is quickly silenced when she states she heard it herself from a council member and declares that there is no Witch. Unfortunately, Omega claims otherwise.

Despite angering Palmyra, Omega decides to clear things up by declaring that there were two conspiracies taking place in town. Despite Nananna trying to prevent her from talking, Omega ignores her and explains that many of the victims were relatives of council members, and she claims that Nananna is the second conspirator, calling her the bastard child of Edmon whose mother was banished from the town, and as a result, she despised the town. Noelle later appears and confirms that her actions were in response to the death of an elderly healer, and she claims that Nananna tried to remove her from the trial by knocking her out since her only ire was with Limbus. Afterward, Noelle declares that the secretary, Mireille, was helping Nananna, as she was a bastard child of Edmon as well, and she stated how the corpses of Piditz and other people connected to the council and other outside officials were already dumped in a hole. Omega also declares that she witnessed Mireille killing Piditz. Enraged, Mireille uses her spiritual arts to char Edmon's arm with blue fire, and with the intent of killing the entire council, surrounds the council with blue fire, and she and Nananna stand against them. Although Omega is fine with leaving things as they are and taking their leave, Colette states she doesn't want things to end like this, and Omega decides to end the fighting in response to her plea, burning through her restraints and declaring herself a Witch.

Later, as Omega's party begins to leave the town, Noelle says her goodbyes to Nananna, and it is declared that the evil spirit accompanying Mireille will be disposed of. Likewise, it is claimed that Edmon's position is under threat with both his severe injuries and the loss of the citizens' trust, and Mireille claims she was mistaken about real Witches. Despite Colette believing that things were settled peacefully, however, Omega thinks to herself that Limbus would soon face its destruction, as since Omega, Nananna, and Mireille were not executed, there would be continuous Witch Hunts and deaths for scapegoats for the whole incident. Although considering telling Colette about this, she decides against it.

Stimulant Resistance: Although Noelle has not been bestowed with a Blessing, as an Itinerant Preacher, she can resist drugs and poison.

name_jp: パラディオ・マネスク
relatives: Drizen Vollachia (father) ; Vincent Vollachia (half-brother) ; Prisca Benedict (younger half-sister) ; Lamia Godwin (younger half-sister) ; Rommel (half-brother) ; Barthroy Fitts (half-brother) ; Stride Vollachia (relative) ; Eugard Vollachia (ancestor) ; Terriola Goldario (ancestor) ; Radkain Vollachia (ancestor)
intro: Palladio Manesque (パラディオ・マネスク) was an Imperial Prince of the Sacred Vollachia Empire. He played an antagonistic role in both Arc 8 and The Tale of the Scarlet Princess.
appearance: Palladio was a man with long, wavy green hair. His Evil Eye was located on his forehead. As a zombie, he possessed a vessel of earth, pale skin bereft of color, various cracks that ran across his body, pitch-black sclera, and radiant golden irises.
personality:
Palladio was a timid and foolish person who lacked the intelligence and supporters to make the most of his Evil Eye throughout the Imperial Selection Ceremony. He was unable to realize that Lamia had planned to use him and his abilities as an asset to help dispatch Vincent and Prisca, and he believed that he could defeat her when it was impossible for him to do so. He was also quite arrogant and looked down on his siblings, particularly Lamia, who had died without having left behind any lasting accomplishments, and Vincent and Prisca, who he referred to as cowards and weaklings who only engaged in collusion and schemes.

Palladio was inspired by the rule of a previous emperor, Eugard Vollachia, and he believed that his rule with fear was extremely effective and intended to walk in his footsteps. However, he despised the works of fictions with "foolish" rumors that the Emperor of the Briar lived for the sake of a village girl, believing they were false. Even as an undead, he intended to take over his country and incinerate every written account of Eugard's loving side so that only his rule of fear would be remembered.
history:
Palladio was among the eleven children of Drizen Vollachia that possessed the qualifications to use the Yang Sword, earning him the right to participate in the Imperial Selection Ceremony. He made an alliance with Lamia to kill their brother, Vincent Abellux, on the condition that she give away a body part of hers for him to pursue her with if their plan succeeded. At the beginning of Lamia's Siege on the Abellux Castle spurred by Lamia, he briefly spoke to Prisca, and she swore to take his head. After the attack failed and his alliance with Lamia crumbled when Prisca killed her, Palladio retreated to his castle.

Two months after Palladio and Lamia failed to take Vincent's life, he was confronted at his castle by Prisca, who came to fulfill her promise of taking his head. He tried to attack her with his Yang Sword, but Prisca swiftly defeated and decapitated him with her own Yang Sword, turning his corpse into ashes.
abilities_text:
Evil Eye (魔眼, Magan): As a descendant of the Evil Eye Tribe, Palladio's Evil Eye gave him the unique ability to enter the mind of others, enabling him to telepathically communicate with and track people with incredible accuracy, so long as he possessed a part of a target's body. Anyone targeted by Palladio's eye experiences a sharp pain in their chest and are branded with an eye-shaped mark. According to Vincent, Palladio had grown complacent with his ability in life, but his precision seemed to have improved after his death. The telepathic communication made it hard for one to conceal their emotions, and the more fragile one's mind was, the more obvious their thoughts were. However, this applied to Palladio too. He was also able to observe precise surroundings of other locations from a distance, though the extent to which he was able to do this is unknown. By closing his eyes, he is also able to view a large area around him as if looking down from the perspective of the sun.

Equipment: 
Yang Sword Vollachia (陽剣ヴォラキア, Youken Vorakia): As a member of the Imperial Family of Vollachia, Palladio was capable of summoning and using the Yang Sword Vollachia, otherwise known as the Yang Sword, an ornate crimson sword with light that shines like the sun. The sword appears out of thin air when the user wishes to use it and it cuts and burns whatever the user desires.

name: Podoso
intro: Podoso (ポドソ) is a guard in the town of Leanotte.
appearance: Podoso is a stern-looking middle-aged man with short, green hair.
personality: Podoso is a responsible and friendly man who carries out his guard duties with diligence. He is genuine with his work and people, showing empathy and kindness.
history:
As a guard who has worked in Leanotte for some time, Podoso is familiar with the town and Coatl's deeds to assist the townspeople during the avalanche that occurred ten years prior. Although it is not known if Podoso was a resident of Leanotte at the time of the avalanche, he knew of Coatl's actions and found him admirable. While dutifully fulfilling his role as a guard, seven serial murders occurred over the span of several weeks. Recognizing the danger of Coatl's solitude life, Podoso decided to visit the church to warn the pastor of the murder, only to discover that he was nowhere to be found and that a young woman, Maqueena, had entered before him. Later in the day, Admonsah arrived at the church, a blizzard began to form, and a party of four girls, consisting of Omega's group and Noelle Tuérico, also entered.

Podoso acted respectfully to the other visitors in the church, openly discussing topics such as Coatl's deeds or the Ice Thieves. He accompanied Maqueena when she attempted to go to another part of the church by herself, with Trellock arriving during their absence. Podoso and Maqueena were the first to discover the church's hidden basement and that Coatl had been murdered there. He proceeded to participate in the discussions revolving around the murder, revealing the serial murders of victims who had their faces ripped to the rest of the group and admitting that he had came to the church to warn Coatl. He also divulged that the circumstances of the seventh murder was different and was quick to accept Admonsah for his background as a slave, understanding that his murder was in self-defense. 

When Maqueena was close to having her true profession exposed, she used Muskrim to escape the church, rendering everyone apart from Noelle unconscious. In the end, Maqueena was exposed for her crimes as a con artist, Trellock was revealed to be the serial killer, Podoso offered Admonsah to become his assistant, and he left was unaware that Noelle, who purportedly took custody of the serial killer, was Coatl's true murderer. He and Admonsah parted ways with Omega's group on friendly terms, taking Maqueena with them to Leanotte.

name: Nikola Suwen
relatives: Unnamed younger brother ; Lumera Ia Juukulius (wife) ; Yaktol Suwen (ancestor) ; Mazeran Suwen (ancestor) ; Framir Suwen (ancestor) ; Otto Suwen (ancestor) ; Oslo Suwen (ancestor) ; Regin Suwen (ancestor)
first_light_novel: Re:Sacrificing Life In Another World from Zero
intro: Nikola Suwen (ニコラ・スーウェン) is the descendant of Otto Suwen who realizes the Suwen family's 400 year wish to free Natsuki Subaru and Beatrice during the events of the Re:Sacrificing Life In Another World from Zero IF story.
appearance:
Upon his introduction, Nikola, much like Otto, dressed in green, wears a green hat, has grey hair, and appears with androgynous traits. However, he was slightly younger than Otto, appeared to be more of a slender man, and had longer hair that was tied near the middle of his back, which gave him an air closer to that of a scholar than a merchant.

As a consequence of trespassing onto the territory of the Eternal Agzadd Glacier, the Witch of Melancholy removed Nikola's left leg below the knee, forcing him to employ a prosthetic leg. By the time forty years passed, Nikola grew a beard and had long since become accustomed to and mastered using the prosthetic magic tool.
personality:
From Subaru's point of view, Nikola's nature is much like Otto's. By Nikola's own claim, he is an eccentric member of the Suwen family. Compared to his siblings and relatives, he considers himself as someone who seems to be unsuited to the mature way of thinking that they have. As such, he was told that he would either die successful or penniless. Unlike Otto, he does not have the courage to stay unfazed while under pressure, as in the case of when he first faced off with Vague Adgard. Having said that, he was crafty enough to expect his arrival and utilize a means to bring the Witch of Melancholy to the battlefield, even being readily willing to suffer the consequences of doing so in order to fend the Mad Prince off.

Similarly to Otto, Nikola has a habit of snapping his fingers as a signal to trigger a scheme. Although he is not shown to have as much of an interest in history as Rosalind, he has knowledge of a variety of things, ranging from the aftermath of Aldebaran's successful attempt to seal Subaru away, to Vague's status as the world's one and only spirit human, and even to quotes from Hoshin, despite how they have fallen out of use. He can be careless and accidentally break a promise, as he did with the promise he made to the six Juukulius sisters to not reveal the deaths of the five spirits other than Lumera to Subaru and Beatrice. Furthermore, due to believing that he accomplished something of value by fulfilling the Suwen family's long-cherished wish, Nikola stresses to Subaru that he is not in debt and has no reason to pay anything in return.

Ever since he was a child, Nikola was in love with Lumera, who was acquainted with the Suwen family, and he wished to become a man who was worthy of being with her. However, as her promise with her master took precedence, he dedicated himself to ensure it could be resolved within ten years and made the necessary arrangements to save Subaru and Beatrice for his own interests, rather than a sentimental desire to fulfill the Suwen family's long-cherished wish. Despite being driven by his love for Lumera, Nikola strived to genuinely help Subaru and Beatrice after their rescue, going so far as to provide a house for them and willingly staying by their side for over 40 years.
history:
Following the Kingdom of Lugunica's downfall, the Suwen family established itself in the Unified Empire of Vollachia and was given the special position of a purveyor for the imperial family. Born as the eldest son of the family, Nikola was expected to inherit their business. As a child, he fell in love with Lumera Ia Juukulius, who often visited his family, and confessed his love to her. In response, she told him that she could not reply to his confession until her promise with her master was fulfilled. As a result, a fire lit within Nikola and he resolved himself to fulfill the long-cherished desire of his family to recover Subaru and Beatrice from the Grand Mogolade Geyser, swearing that he would achieve it within ten years. Motivated by his love for Lumera, he relinquished his right of succeeding the family business to his younger brother, managed to eventually finish all of the necessary preparations to recover the orb, and made a direct appeal to Rosalind Vollachia, who was amused by his actions and accepted his proposal in accordance with Vincent Vollachia's promise to an oni girl that the imperial family would aid Subaru.

When the time came, the “Grand Mogolade Geyser Black Orb Recovery Plan” was sprung into action. As locating the black orb within the geyser required time and effort from Lumera, and the process of searching for it would cause Vague Adgard to notice, they decided to set up a diversion to draw the Mad Prince's attention elsewhere. While Lumera would be accompanied by Nikola, Rosalind, and Madelyn Eschart, Arakiya and Lumera's sisters engaged Vague in combat, which resulted in Lapicha, Soyone, Dorena, Kiara, and Sinica allowing Arakiya to devour them once they each sustained fatal damage, thereby sacrificing their lives while fulfilling their promise with Julius in the process. Their sacrifices allowed Arakiya to repel Vague and gave Lumera the time she needed to recover the black orb. Once she found it, Rosalind used the Yang Sword to break it open, freeing Subaru and Beatrice. However, due to the aftereffects of being trapped within the orb for 400 years, Subaru was on the verge of death upon waking up. While Nikola and Lumera were left in shock, unable to assist him, Rosalind noticed that Beatrice could be of help to him.

Waking up again soon, an immobile Subaru found himself in another room, where he was able to speak with Beatrice. Nikola spoke up and proceeded to introduce himself to Subaru as Nikola Suwen, a man with many titles, with the title of merchant being the most familiar to him. He then informed Subaru that 400 years had passed since Aldebaran sealed him and Beatrice away, and conveyed a message from his ancestor, Otto, which had been passed down in his family. After learning of the Suwen family's 400 year old undertaking, how Otto's unyielding determination had allowed him to achieve his goals in the end, and realizing that he would never be able to speak with his friend again, Subaru began to sob, understanding that the majority of people he knew no longer existed in the world. He asked Nikola about Emilia, who confirmed she was alive, but that he did not know if she was safe because she had encased the Agzadd Valley in ice, freezing herself and Aldebaran in the process, and that the Witch of Melancholy had settled at the glacier and attacked anyone who encroached on the territory. Later on, Nikola provided Subaru and Beatrice with a house, telling the two that he could help them with anything they needed and that he did not believe Subaru had to repay any debt to him, as it was because his own hard work paid off and he was able to fulfill the Suwen family's 400 year wish by saving them that he had accomplished something of value.

Believing an attack from the Mad Prince, Vague Adgard, was bound to happen, Nikola preemptively prepared a spell that could be remotely activated to create an interference within the bounds of the Eternal Agzadd Glacier, cognizant that the Witch of Melancholy would pursue him. Sure enough, Vague intruded into Subaru and Beatrice's provisional home while Nikola, Lumera, and Arakiya were over for dinner. Over the course of many loops, Subaru, despite still being immobile from the aftereffects of his sealing, was able to influence the situation enough to the point that he and the other three combatants managed to prevent Vague from killing any of them. Once enough time had passed, Nikola raised his right hand and snapped his fingers, invoking the same gesture Otto used when enacting a plan. A few moments later, a voice spoke up, stating their request that no one was to meddle with the glacier, and white lights surrounded the house in all directions, completely obliterating it. As Subaru and the others were protected by EMM, they withstood it, and he and Beatrice recognized the source of the white lights, which had been the Crimson Scorpion's needles.

The Witch of Melancholy then made her appearance, activating Compress Agony on Vague, allowing the needles of the Crimson Scorpion, which was fighting alongside her, to pierce him. Despite this, he was unscathed by the ensuing explosion because he switched to his mana body, and he exchanged words with the Witch of Melancholy, before instantly vanishing from the scene. Once he disappeared, the Witch's attention turned to Nikola, as she had determined he had intruded on the glacier through his magic signature, and pointed to his left leg, which had been severed at the lower half, and then attempted to leave. Subaru tried to call out to her, but discovered that he was unable to pronounce her name, and as he continued trying to speak with her, she activated Compress Agony on him.

Following Vague's attack, Nikola began to employ a prosthetic leg. Subaru was finally released from Compress Agony's effects two weeks later and spoke with Nikola about what had happened. From Nikola's perspective, it was a stroke of luck that he only lost a leg and hardly found his prosthetic leg an inconvenience due to the advancement of magic tools since Subaru's time 400 years ago. He conveyed that the Witch of Melancholy did not kill people and that he trespassed into the region of the glacier to attract her attention, having done so to preemptively counter Vague. Moreover, he explained that Vague commenced his objective to purge the world of spirits by murdering Odglass, followed by Zarestia, has trying to target Arakiya, and was even responsible for killing Lumera's sisters. However, he realized he had made a mistake by telling them that Lumera's sisters had been eradicated, asking Subaru and Beatrice to pretend that they had not heard him, which the former of the duo rejected. Nikola then disclosed that Vague killed Lumera's sisters, who had been fully aware of the potential outcome and that they made a diversion to lure the Mad Prince away from the others when they were enacting their plan to rescue Subaru. Suddenly, Lumera entered the room, declaring that it had been a natural decision for them. She then admonished Nikola for not abiding by the final plea of her sisters, though she quickly understood that he would want to mention what they had achieved to Subaru and Beatrice and gently stroked his head while he remained dejected for having revealed it.

Over the course of forty years, Subaru recovered from the aftereffects of his sealing and prepared to confront the Witch of Melancholy and the Mad Prince, Vague Adgard. During this period, Lumera continued to not reciprocate Nikola's feelings for her because she was concerned about Subaru's recovery process. However, once Subaru had recovered his spirit and he bluntly told them that they should get together, Nikola and Lumera began a relationship. With the backing of the unified emperor of Vollachia, the couple had a grand wedding ceremony held for them, although it was interrupted by Vague, forcing Subaru to repeatedly utilize Return by Death in order to deal with him. Nikola also managed to master using his prosthetic leg. Once the time came for Subaru and Beatrice to set off for the Eternal Agzadd Glacier, Nikola checked to see if they were ready. Lumera joined them, also asking if their preparations were complete, as she was accompanying the duo to the glacier. Once the four of them exited the house they had been in, they were met by Rosalind's daughter, who had succeeded her mother after she succumbed to illness. The unified emperor voiced her intent to lend two of her daggers, the Nine Divine Generals, to Subaru. With the additions of the Diamond Princess, Arakiya, and the Cloud Dragon, Madelyn Eschart, to the group, Subaru called out everyone's names and set off for the glacier with his allies.

name: Reborn
intro: Reborn (リボーン) is a member of the Beloved Children. He plays an antagonistic role in Arc 10.
appearance: Reborn is a youth with spiky, bright blue hair that is swept to the side on the top of his head while the sides are buzzed short, red eyes that have a nasty look in them, and a small frame. His outfit consists of a sleeveless blue top with a high collar that reaches his chin and a vertical red stripe on the right side and matching blue trousers. His detached sleeves and boots are a darker shade of blue with red straps on them, he wears a pair of red X-shaped earrings, he has an ornament with the Mark of the Beloved Children pinned to his collar, and he carries his oversized weapon on his back. He gives off the atmosphere of a small, hot-blooded animal.
personality: Reborn is described as having a big attitude and a loud voice for his small build who gives off the atmosphere of a small hot-blooded animal, and he has a vulgar manner of speech, unwilling to praise others. He can be restless, as seen when he repeatedly and roughly hit his feet around the meeting table made by Arbalest. Moreover, he is prone to anger and will not hesitate to take it out on his own comrades, whether by trying to kill them, threatening them, or by using his power of silence on them. He is equally quick-tempered when fighting enemies and becomes easily infuriated when put on the back foot or when things do not go his way. Furthermore, he has complained about generally everything being far too noisy and wanting to silence everything.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
Although it is unclear exactly how powerful he is, it has been stated that Reborn is the strongest member of the Beloved Children. Even without his primary power, he is still a force to be reckoned with, and the other members of the Beloved Children recognize that they stand no chance against him. At present, he is known to at least be capable of clashing with the likes of a emotionally disrupted Crusch Karsten, though ultimately, she is still stronger than he is.

Physical Traits/Flow Method
Expert Swordsman: Reborn is an excellent swordsman who can easily fight against Crusch with large blades.

Heightened Agility: During combat, Reborn has a habit of fighting three-dimensionally, kicking off of the walls and ceiling while attempting to attack from various angles.

Techniques
Silence Generation: Reborn is capable of stopping sound from escaping a specified area. It is capable of preventing any speech from reaching one’s allies, even when they are close to each other, or preventing the sounds of a battle from reaching anyone’s ears. Furthermore, by alternating between using silence on specified targets and deactivating it, the audio discord can disrupt and break the concentration of his opponents. This being said, it does not necessarily stop sensory type abilities, as Natsuki Subaru was still able to detect Crusch’s battle with him through his Cor Leonis. Furthermore, the area afflicted with silence is limited to everything within his line of sight. As such, if someone is out of his vision, they will not be affected. This also means that if he is blinded, he cannot use his power.

Equipment
Shear-like Greatswords: Reborn uses a giant pair of shears as his primary weapon. The shears can separate into two blades, and he can easily use them like greatswords. At present, he has only used one of them, so it is unclear if he is capable of dual wielding them or using them while they are attached. They are easily sharp enough to carve right through stone with little apparent resistance.
