intro: Reid Astrea (レイド・アストレア) was the first Sword Saint, a member of the Witch Era Party, and a key figure in the sealing of the Witch of Envy 400 years ago. Mentioned throughout the series, he formally debuted in Arc 6 as a secondary antagonist.
appearance: Reid had waist length, fiery red hair, sky blue eyes, and was mentioned to be a head taller than Subaru with a muscular body. He wore a half a crimson kimono, which only covered the left side of his torso, a white sarashi wrapped around his waist, and a black eye patch over his left eye. He often put his eyepatch on his right eye as well, since it was merely aesthetic.
personality:
Reid was shown to have a very frank and rather crude personality, as Subaru was easily able to imitate his method of speech, and tended to speak in short sentences, frequently ending them with you (オメエ omee). He had no interest in titles, stating that he was himself, others were themselves, and that he was strong not because he wielded a sword, but simply because he was strong. He was also lustful, mentioning that he would have had Emilia in bed if he was still alive.

Despite being somewhat frank and abstract, Reid was quite clever. In addition to this, he also had a great amount of knowledge regarding how to fight with the sword and once spent three months lifting nothing but his sword. His effort led him to be the first person in history who attained the Heavenly Sword.

In Re:Zero Prequel: Loving the Days Gone By, it was revealed that Reid did not discriminate against those he pointed the tip of his sword at. Be it an evil spirit, a witchbeast, or a Blight Dragon, Reid cut them down one by one. Due to his campaigns against Dragons in particular, some of them retaliated and decided to avenge their fallen brethren to no avail. They were either cut down by Reid himself or by other powerful individuals of that era.
history:
Reid Astrea was born around 400 years ago. Throughout the years, he trained relentlessly and soon achieved the very zenith of swordsmanship, becoming the only person in history who reached a level of swordsmanship known as the Heavenly Sword. He became famed for a plethora of his activities, such as slaying one hundred Dragons in a fight, his achievement of 6,000 undefeated victories at the Gladiator Island Ginunhive in the Vollachia Empire, his victories in drinking competitions, and other varying exploits.

In the years predating the Great Calamity, Reid travelled alongside Satella, Echidna, Flugel, Farsale Lugunica, and Alec Hoshin for unknown reasons, though according to Alec, it was a journey to save the world. At an unspecified point in time, he also met the Divine Dragon Volcanica. Reid was known in history for being the one responsible for the eradication of the Blight Dragons which used to roam the world back then. According to legends, he cut down numerous dragons with a single swing of his Dragon Sword, having primarily done so because Dragon meat was his favorite meal. He had even battled with Volcanica at least once before in order to eat it, having left a wound on its neck in that battle that would later become Volcanica's inverted scale. According to Echidna, at the time of their travels, they needed to keep their identities secret. However, at one point during their travels, they ended up in the country of Magrizza. Despite attempting to hide their identities, Farsale declared his own name, resulting in a noble discovering them and inviting them to a banquet of nobles. The nation's crown prince, who was also in attendance at the banquet, became enamored by Echidna and went behind the scenes to arrange a marriage between the two of them, with Echidna's party going along with them after they were split from their capable fighters. However, at some point, for reasons yet to be explained, Reid and Volcanica went on a rampage, ultimately resulting in the marriage being cancelled and them being driven from the nation. It was a short time later that they learned that the Black Serpent destroyed Magrizza. According to Echidna, it was likely that they were being chased by the Black Serpent.

Later in Reid's life, in his middle years, once Satella, the Witch of Envy, suddenly went out of control and went on a rampage across the world, he is said to have met with the Dragon and the Sage in the city of Flanders, forming an alliance with the other two. The heroes set their goals on defeating the rampaging Witch who mercilessly killed thousands and thousands of innocents and toppled one country after another. After realizing they were unable to kill her, Reid and the others managed to defeat her and seal her away in the Augria Sand Dunes, located in the Dragon Kingdom of Lugunica's easternmost region.

It is not known what Reid did after the Great Calamity, but after an unspecified amount of time, the first Sword Saint died. According to the author, a child of Reid's younger brother succeeded him, becoming the second Sword Saint and the first person to bear the Divine Protection of the Sword Saint.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
Reid has been noted as one of the most powerful people to exist in Re:Zero, capable of killing others who have been called among the strongest with ease, only being outclassed by Reinhard van Astrea in sheer overall power. According to the author, Reid was such a genius that he surpassed every swordsman in the world after only three months of wielding a sword. Even when he was barehanded, he was already the world's strongest. He was easily able to defeat Julius and Eridna. He was one of the only beings in the world capable of going toe to toe with Satella, though like with Reinhard, he would have been unable to kill her due to their incompatibility. Combined with his prideful and arrogant personality, his soul was capable of overwriting Roy Alphard's Authority of Gluttony, effectively hijacking his body and achieving complete rebirth 400 years after his death; although in his fight against Julius, his body began to "crack" because Roy's body couldn't contain Reid's soul.

Physical Traits/Flow Method

Master Swordsman: Reid was known for having peak sword mastery and the martial arts of his time. As a testament to his peerless skill, Reid was said to be the first person to reach the "Heavenly Sword". To this day, he is the most powerful swordsman that has ever lived, as he alone reached the zenith of swordsmanship. According to himself, he doesn’t even need an actual sword to use techniques or cut through things, and he repeatedly demonstrated as much by using primarily his own hands or a pair of chopsticks rather than the sword that was available to him during his fight against Julius and Emilia. His sheer sword skill is said to surpass even that of the current generation's Sword Saint, Reinhard, who's stated to be the most powerful character in the series. A swing of his weapon is capable of unleashing torrents of light that can blow away or vaporize anything caught up in it, and he is even capable of slashing through the intangible: light, the atmosphere, space, magic, and even concepts manipulated by Authorities. Such attacks are considered beyond understanding and a true testament of the first Sword Saint.

Inhuman Strength: Even ignoring his swordsmanship, Reid's physical strength was still tremendous. In one display of his strength, he was able to hold up a block of ice so massive that it covered the entire ceiling of the Pleiades Watchtower's second floor, Electra.

Inhuman Durability: Reid was also considerably tough. Though he rarely ever seemed to let an attack reach him, when they did, they did minimal damage. When Emilia struck him with a weapon made from her Ice Brand Arts, which are said to be denser than steel, he seemed to take no damage, merely complaining that she hit him instead.

Techniques
Energy Channeling: Reid was capable of a technique where he channeled the full power of his opponents' attacks harmlessly out of his body. It is hinted at that he could channel it out of any part of his body but had only done it through his feet. This technique effectively made him immune to attacks from clubs, hammers, punches, kicks or anything blunt.

Other
Excellent Intuition: Reid is rather adept when it comes to combat involving things besides swinging his sword. In one failed loop, he was able to recognize that some ability was keeping Ram active despite her condition, and he immediately recognized what it was, deciding to slash through it to sever its influence.

Equipment

Dragon Sword Reid (龍剣レイド, Ryūken Reido): Four centuries ago, Reid received a special sword which was dubbed the Dragon Sword after Reid often went on rampages with it, killing numerous Dragons with a single swing. The sword is said to be unbreakable and is supposedly able to cut through any material, no matter the toughness or density. According to some legends, the sword even brought the Witch's end. After Reid's death, the Sword was given to his offspring who inherited the Divine Protection of the Sword Saint. As a tribute to the achievements Reid had achieved with this legendary weapon, the Sword inherited his name.
thumb|180x|Reid taking on Julius Juukulius with nothing but a pair of chopsticks.
A pair of chopsticks: In Arc 6, Reid can be seen with a pair of chopsticks. In his hands, the chopsticks are extremely durable and are able to withstand repeated sword slashes without chipping or breaking despite being made of ordinary wood. Reid even cut Subaru's Authority of Greed with them.
The sword in Electra: Reid temporarily used the available sword in the Pleiades Watchtower’s second floor, Electra, during his fight with Julius.

name: Sphinx
alias: Witch (魔女, Majo) ; Witch of Greed (強欲の魔女, Gōyoku no Majo) ; Great Disaster (大災, Taisai)
nickname: Creator (造物主, Zōbutsushu) (by "Edda")

intro: Sphinx (スピンクス) is the first copy of Ryuzu Meyer who was created in the Sanctuary by the Witch of Greed, Echidna. Initially serving as a main antagonist of Sword Demon Love Song, she made her first main story debut in the final scene of Arc 7 and later became the main antagonist of Arc 8 as the culprit behind the Sacred Vollachia Empire's Great Disaster.
appearance:
Although she was around four hundred years old as a result of her artificial existence and mana body, for the majority of her life, Sphinx perpetually maintained the body of a girl who was twelve years of age. As she was a copy of Ryuzu Meyer, she shared her long, fluffy pink hair, dark cyan eyes, and distinctively pointed ears with the other clones. Despite her innocent and girlish physical appearance, Sphinx radiated an abominable aura that denoted her as a wicked monster. Originally, she displayed a lack of expressiveness as a result of her incomplete emotions.

Sphinx wore a black robe with large sleeves that were too long for her arms and a high collar that partially concealed her face. Due to the long length of the sleeves, they each have holes that allowed her to extend her arms out. However, after the Demi-Human War, Sphinx lost her arms and legs, barely escaping death with only her head, torso, and robe. 

By the time of the Great Disaster, Sphinx regained all of her limbs via unknown means and came into possession of a staff with a glowing orb. Following her demise at the hands of Cecilus Segmunt, she became a zombie. In this form, she possessed a vessel of earth, pale skin bereft of color, various cracks that ran across her body, pitch-black sclera, and radiant golden irises. Her lack of expressiveness began to change as well, with her face beginning to display various emotions. Upon being brought to the brink of death by Vincent's Yang Sword and managing to complete the missing parts of her soul, Sphinx took on the Witch of Greed's physical appearance, gaining long white hair that stretched to her back, black eyes that housed an intellectual spirit, and porcelain-like white skin, while continuing to don her black cloak that had become too small to cover her full body.
personality:
As a result of being created from one of the Witch of Greed's failed experiments and not fully inheriting a complete soul, Sphinx, although possessing a distinct self-identity from Echidna, was born with a mostly emotionless demeanor and little attachment to her own life, only primarily inheriting the greed to understand and learn things. A self-proclaimed Witch, Sphinx could not understand emotions from birth because of her defective personality and desired to gain a "complete" soul like Echidna, who she originally viewed as a mother figure. She viewed herself as a vehicle whose sole purpose of creation was to attain completion in order to fully recreate the Witch of Greed and replace her incomplete self with that of the complete Echidna, in accordance with the original desire her creator had for her. As such, she had no desires that she could call her own, believing she would become Echidna once she completed herself.

For most of her life, Sphinx lacked the ability to properly feel and comprehend emotions, struggling to understand outcomes in which attachment and irrationality triumphed over rationality. Although she attempted to speak kindly or tried to maintain an air of courteousness when talking to other people, she sounded disinterested and robotic, often manipulating or exploiting other people for her own interests. No matter who she faced, as long as it advanced her goals, Sphinx showed little concern in murdering others or gathering corpses to guarantee her own safety or use for her own experiments. This, alongside her use of the Sacrament of the Immortal King to raise numerous corpse soldiers, led her to be branded a Witch by the human faction during the Demi-Human War. Despite this, she had already introduced herself as a Witch to the Demi-Human Alliance in an attempt to become the “Witch of the Kingdom”, a disaster prophesized to bring ruin to Lugunica in the future.

Following her failures at Priscilla's hands, unknowingly to her, she began to harbor a desire for vengeance against the woman, to the point that she decided to scheme the destruction of the entire Vollachia Empire to get back at her. During the Great Disaster, when she had captured Priscilla, Sphinx often came to speak with Priscilla as an undead. During this time, there was a visible shift in her personality. Whereas she was initially quite stoic, she began displaying more expressions, and the more she talked with Priscilla, the more that she realized the emotions that she was feeling such as frustration, anger, confusion, curiosity, and fixation. While her stoicism was not completely gone when confronting people other than Priscilla, the range of her emotions rapidly expanded nonetheless. Furthermore, this understanding of emotions expanded to include other people; due to her increased understanding of attachment and emotions of both herself and others, she was even able to determine how to use the emotions of other people to her advantage. Even after her vessel changed into the form of the Witch of Greed, she began recognizing more and more of her emotions.

In her final moments, when Priscilla managed to escape the space of her prison, Sphinx became convinced that her plans had come crumbling down. However, she refused to give up her desire to exact revenge upon Priscila as she fell from the sky and finally displayed her full wrath for the first time as she shouted the name of the Sun Princess and directed all of her selves to attack her. Due to the ambiguous nature of her identity as the one born as Sphinx and the soul born from the Witch of Greed, she was not able to fully grasp her identity until Subaru and Spica confronted her. She also claimed in this time that she believed that no matter what path she took, things would have always turned out this way for her, as she had achieved an objective of her own will, outside of what her creator intended for her. In the end, after being recognized by Priscilla as her enemy despite her own failure, Sphinx let go of her sternness and asserted that Priscilla was her enemy, finding her own purpose and affirming her own desire rather than following the purpose of creation she had been intended to fulfil, and smiled at her enemy as she met her end.

Sphinx had a habit of saying "required" (要 you) with a verb in accordance to something she believed was necessary, such as using "observation: required" (要・観察 you: kansatsu) when observing other people's actions, "deliberation: required" (要・熟考 you: jukkō) when pondering something, or other a variety of other words that reflect what she believed she must have done in the moment. Once she took on Echidna's form, she attempted to discard this way of speaking, but as she met her end and accepted her individuality, she used it one final time.
history:
Early Life
Ryuzu Meyer was a young half-elven girl who became indebted to the Witch of Greed, Echidna. The Witch, with Ryuzu's permission, began experimenting on her in a secret laboratory. Echidna sought to unlock immortality by cloning Ryuzu and transferring her consciousness to the copy, meaning she could live forever via a long line of copies. She was able to create the first five copies of Ryuzu, the first of which she decided to transfer her consciousness into. However, Echidna chose to shave off parts of her soul in order to fit in the receptacle, resulting in an emotionless girl with a body made of mana, a fractured mind, and a vast amount of magical knowledge, albeit not at the level of Echidna herself, as the receptacle of Ryuzu Meyer hindered the girl from wielding the Witch's techniques. Bestowed the name of an impure monster, Sphinx, the Witch of Greed's failed creation, managed to escape being disposed through some twist of fate. She wandered throughout the world to fulfill the purpose of her creation, replicating the Witch of Greed, while Echidna's disciple, Roswaal, pursued her.

The body of Ryuzu Meyer was unfit for surviving in the harsh conditions of the world; whether it was with bad weather, extreme temperature changes, or encounters with malicious witchbeasts or humans, Sphinx was often threatened by circumstances outside of her control. The discrepancy between receptacle and soul had required her to exert effort akin to learning how to walk, breathe, and beat her heart again. Her body of mana could not allow her to grow or train, so she pursued knowledge and skills that did not depend on the state of her body while facing persecution for appearing as a half-elf, choosing not to alter her appearance to not run the risk of being unable to fulfill her purpose. To continue living, Sphinx reduced herself to the status of a spectacle, a slave, and the servant of a lavish master. Taking advantage of her memory and her greed to understand and learn more, for one hundred and fifty years, Sphinx made her abilities into a utility that allowed her to gain the protection of and live under various people who could provide her safety until she attained the means to protect herself. To avoid suffering Roswaal's fury or extreme persecution due to sharing the same race as the Witch of Envy, she did not opt to stay in one location for too long.

Becoming a magician required Sphinx to exert nearly one hundred times the effort it would take someone of average ability to. The first spell she cast unleashed naught but a small, flickering flame at her fingertips, disappointing her greatly. There were no sudden changes to her life upon gaining the capabilities to use magic. After using one spell, Sphinx stabilized using the gate of her mana-based body and was successful in reproducing the majority of magic attained by the Witch of Greed's soul. She continued to conceal herself, using her magical prowess to make the job easier. For the next one hundred years, she devoted her time to learning about Echidna, but the Witch Cult's efforts at erasing the existence of Witches other than the Witch of Envy hindered her progress and made results difficult to acquire. Ultimately, this path failed to produce major results for Sphinx, so she attempted to fill in the missing pieces of the Witch of Greed's soul herself for another hundred years, only for this venture to result in failure as well. After spending three hundred and fifty years without making a breakthrough that could assist her in fulfilling her purpose, Sphinx chose to make a major alteration to her methods.

Sword Demon Love Song
When the opportunity conveniently presented itself after the tensions between humans and demi-humans and Lugunica reached a boiling point, Sphinx joined the Demi-Human Alliance, a large insurrectionist force based within the Kingdom of Lugunica. The Alliance, made up entirely of marginalized demi-human tribes in Lugunica, sought to reap the blood of their oppressors, consequentially beginning a civil war that came to be known as the Demi-Human War. With her appearance as a half-elf being the only justification she needed to ally with their cause, she happened to meet Valga Cromwell and Libre Fermi, the principal leaders of the Demi-Human Alliance, and unveiled her knowledge from the Witch of Greed to support the former's stratagems. With their resources, she also managed to reproduce the Sacrament of the Immortal King. While her involvement was kept relatively secretive, Sphinx was considered to be Alliance's backbone, and alongside Valga and Libre, she became the one of the three people most responsible for their successful advancements, despite having no interest in their victory. Throughout the war, she would observe the quality she was lacking most, love, in demi-humans and humans alike, assuring the actuality of its existence and understanding that it was missing from herself.

During the Demi-Human War, Sphinx set up testing grounds at Shamrock Valley, which would only be opened with a glintstone of her creation, and she tested the efficacy of her Magic Circles there at the behest of Valga. These Magic Circles exploded when triggered by a person walking over them much like a landmine. During the Battle of Castour Field, Sphinx's Magic Circles worked with brutal efficiency. Her usage of Magic Circles to set soldiers from the Royal Army ablaze led to the Demi-Human Alliance's victory. A few days after the victory, she went to Castour Field and used the Sacrament of the Immortal King, an ancient spell that she used to resurrect and create mindless "corpse soldiers" from the deceased forces on both ends. However, while she was trying to create corpse soldiers, she encountered Wilhelm Trias, Grimm Fauzen, Carol Remendis, and Roswaal J. Mathers, her existence became known to the Kingdom, and she was branded as a Witch. After her first known appearance in the civil war, Valga and Libre began to disagree over whether her methods were justified or not until she stopped it with a Jiwald. After Libre left, she asked Valga if Libre needed to be eliminated, to which he suggested that they should avoid it if possible.

Sphinx eventually began working on a much more complex system of Magic Circles with Valga's help, and three years after the conflict at Castour Field, the Battle of Aihiya Swamp brought the duo's efforts come to fruition. Knowing that the Royal Army would work to dispel any Magic Circle they came across, a hidden one across the entire swamp was created, being charged activated with the energy of the smaller circles after being destroyed. Under the Magic Circle's effects, humans were felt a heavier pressure as if they were underwater while demi-humans remained unaffected. Its powers affected those who had differences in their mana cycles, meaning that became more potent on those who were more adept in magic, which costed many human casualties in the battle. Unfortunately for Sphinx, the Roswaal of that generation did not hold any magical abilities and instead used steel gauntlets to take her on, which made the Witch withdraw from Roswaal and her attendant, Carol. After finding Libre, who Valga needed regardless of his survival to advance the Alliance's cause, Sphinx used her magic to kill him, turning him into a corpse soldier who covered her escape.

Around this time, Sphinx designed a forbidden art that negated the users of Divine Protections from utilizing their abilities and nullified the Kingdom's covenant with the Divine Dragon from by creating a blind spot in Od Lagna. The forbidden art never saw any use in the Demi-Human War, however, and it was instead used a few years later during the Subjugation of the Blight Dragon by Stride Vollachia, who discovered the means to enter Sphinx's Testing Grounds in Shamrock Valley to replicate and utilize the forbidden art for his own schemes.

Not long after the battle at Aihiya Swamp, Sphinx, Valga, and the reanimated corpse of Libre enacted an attack on Lugunica Castle by entering it via one of its many hidden passageways. While Wilhelm fought Valga and Bordeaux fought what remained of Libre, Sphinx was confronted by Grimm, Carol, and Roswaal. Carol successfully managed to cleave off her left arm, and not long afterwards, Libre cut her right arm off. Attempting to prioritize her own life while still possessing little attachment to it, Sphinx followed her instincts to run and barely escaped death by entering another hidden passageway within the castle to escape to the sewers. Upon her escape attempt, she was confronted by Leip Barielle and captured. A short time later, Roswaal arrived and questioned Leip about her whereabouts, and he lied about her death. Once Roswaal left satisfied after receiving a necklace with a ring that Leip had taken from the Witch, he picked up Sphinx's body and would come to keep her alive for his own benefit. At an unknown point in time, he would confine her under an abandoned wooden house in the Barielle Domain and remove her legs.

Imprisonment
Though he would usually keep her under watch by regularly replaced guards, Leip would rarely speak to her aside from one-sided commands. Twenty years after her imprisonment, however, Leip had asked Sphinx about her goal for the Demi-Human War, which Sphinx replied her goal given to her by her creator. Leip scoffed at this and told her that such a goal was pointless, that allowing her own name to die while attempting to become someone else had no value, and he told her that she was to work for his purposes. A long time later, she learned through him that the Lugunican Royal Family was to one day face the tragedy of disease, and he wanted to take advantage of that by breaking the mind of his future wife so that he could manipulate her and rule through proxy, commanding Sphinx to craft a spell to break said woman's mind. Though she realized it was dark, she felt something dazzling about the way he reached for his own desires rather than someone else's, as she had never once felt any form of passion or desire to accomplish her goal, and she hoped that he would succeed so that he could teach her the passion she so lacked.

The Day I Gave Up on Being a Following Star
Several months before the beginning of the main story, Leip formulated a plan to gain control over Lugunica. After the beginning of the Royal Selection, Leip aimed to take away the will of his wife, Priscilla Barielle, who was a candidate to become the country's next monarch. By using Sphinx's powers to make her into a puppet, Leip would effectively rule the country if Priscilla won. However, after Leip was incapacitated by Al, this plan fell through. Sphinx continued to wait for Leip's success, but ultimately, he never returned. Breaking her shackles, she somehow left her imprisonment and learned the fate of Leip, and with his death, Sphinx felt a strange "ardor" and began to harbor feelings of revenge toward his wife, Priscilla, for causing his death.

Pride and Prejudice and Zombies
A few months later, after the Royal Selection had begun, she attempted to take over Priscilla's body again by luring her to a trap. Using parasites that she had created, Sphinx would spread an infection from a waterwheel along a river in the Barielle Domain in order to coax Priscilla into showing up there. However, this tactic would also come to fail when the infected waterwheel manager and host of the parasites' queen, Edda Rayfast, was put out of commission by Al, who would remove a parasite within Priscilla after she burnt Edda to ash. After this event, Sphinx began waiting in silence for time to pass while deliberating on her next course of action.

Eventually, driven by her failure and wishing to take revenge on Priscilla, Sphinx decided to set her sights on Priscilla's homeland, Vollachia, as both a part to complete herself and to attain her revenge. At an unknown point in time after this, she managed to regain all of her lost limbs, experimented with the town of Nanou in Kararagi, and she set forth toward Vollachia, creating various different countermeasures to ensure her victory.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
Although she was initially considered a failure and was so incredibly weak that she had to scrape by as being used as a tool or slave by others, after having lived for centuries, Sphinx became an incredibly competent and dangerous magician. By the time of the Demi-Human War, ~360 years after her birth, her magic, widespread use of forbidden arts, ability to create an instant army from the dead, knowledge, and ruthlessness were enough to classify Sphinx as a Witch and one of the most dangerous people in the war, having been among the reasons that the war lasted so long and so many casualties had built up over the decade. Four decades later, despite having been locked away without her limbs, her danger level grew tremendously by somehow learning the Flow Method and martial arts, and by the time of the Great Disaster, she had become so dangerous that she almost managed to wipe out Vollachia and threaten its neighboring countries. Even after becoming undead, her strength and threat level was enhanced much further by her inability to die and her ability to gather knowledge, as well as by connecting to the mana stores of the Crystal Palace.

Magic
By utilizing the knowledge she inherited from Echidna, Sphinx could make use of spells from multiple affinities, as well as the Sacrament of the Immortal King, a powerful forbidden art she uses to create undead. She has also mastered magic to such a degree that she can create multiple variations of different kinds of spells, and she can use spells from different parts of her body besides the hands, such as from her eyes. She is capable of weaving mana masterfully enough to generate a large white cloth capable of defending large targets. Likewise, she has also shown to use the various unique properties of each element to her advantage while using her magic: using the reflectivity of ice like a mirror to bounce her light spells off of, projecting displays of other locations on water, instantly freezing the water from previously used spells to steal the heat from her target and slow them, weaponizing water droplets like endless minuscule blades, and other such variations and combinations.

Magic Circles (魔法陣, Mahō-jin): Magic Circles are a type of geometric magic algorithm used to perform complex spells and rituals that can be drawn on objects or living beings. These can produce great kinds of effects, such as regular spells, large-scale magic that completely alter the state of a battlefield, imbuing an individual with extreme power, or even distorting the space inside of a building as large as the Crystal Palace in Lupugana. However, once Magic Circles are found drawn on the ground, their effects can be nullified by damaging the circle, so hiding them until activation is necessary. Though, it is also possible to use the destruction of magic circles against her enemies by connecting their destruction to the activation of a different magic circle, effectively deceiving and trapping the enemy. Since this is an ancient form of magic, very few people know about them, and even fewer are capable of using them.

Spells:
Goa (ゴーア): Sphinx manifested a blaze of fire, which incinerates a foe.
El Goa (エル・ゴーア): Though its exact effects are unspecified, Sphinx could use it to rain down fire on an opponent.
Ul Goa (ウル・ゴーア): Sphinx fired a large number of powerful fire bullets. A powerful flame scatters when the bullets land.
Al Goa (アル・ゴーア): Sphinx could let loose a massive fireball, scorching away everything in its path. 
Ul Huma (ウル・ヒューマ): Sphinx could generate a barrage of water that shot to the sky from the ground. This provided a good defense against fire spells.
Jiwald (ジワルド): Using Yang Magic, Sphinx was able to conjure and manipulate visible light into beams of scorching heat that laid waste to whatever object stands in its way. Jiwald was Sphinx's preferred method of combat. Like most spells, there are four levels that increase in intensity and amount depending on the level. The most basic offensive light spell is Jiwald, which allows the caster to project a single beam of concentrated light out of a finger so fast that even the trained human eye can barely register it.
El Jiwald (エル・ジワルド): Sphinx could fire several swords of light that melted through anything in their path.
Al Jiwald (アル・ジワルド): The most powerful offensive spell in Sphinx's arsenal consisted of a single ray of light projected from the Witch's entire palm. The spell is much faster and larger in scale than any of other Jiwald variation and was easily her most destructive, usually annihilating anything in its path. That being said, the soldier Grimm Fauzen was still able to deflect Al Jiwald with his shield. Although capable of casting normally as of the Great Disaster, during the Demi-Human War, she cast it through magic circles she had drawn on her body. It is unknown if these were required at the time or if they were used for a separate reason.
Sacrament of the Immortal King (不死王の秘蹟, Fushiō no Hiseki): The Sacrament of the Immortal King is an ancient spell created by an unknown Witch long ago. The spell, when cast correctly, will allow the user to reanimate corpses of the dead and make them do their bidding. Sadly, the technique to properly cast the spell has been long lost to time, and only an incomplete incantation exists which was transcribed in an old and withered book regarded as the most important heirloom of House Argyle. Originally, the spell was thought to be capable of fully reviving a dead person, and there are legends of the aforementioned Witch being supposedly capable of bringing back people exactly as they were before their demise. Effectively, the written chunks of the spell's full passage is incapable of producing anything more than walking corpses with no soul of their own, creating "corpse soldiers" whose flesh slowly withers away and decomposes through time. In a given group of undead under her control, Sphinx could choose a "core" to act as a control point between all of them. Tholter Weasily is the only known individual who this power has been used on. If one corpse soldier is neutralized, then the rest of them become more powerful. However, if the core corpse soldier was dispatched, then this effect wore off. The main difference between the "core" corpse is that its abilities were closer to what they were in life compared to others, which can easily distinguish them. To further limit the usefulness of this mostly-lost spell, a caster with an extremely rare natural affinity for it must be found in order to recreate even the most basic effects of this forbidden spell. As the version Sphinx originally used was incomplete, she was only able to reanimate corpses and turn them into corpse soldiers until she began using parasites and corebugs. However, Sphinx was also able to use it in combination with her Magic Circles and a bone belonging to one of Valga's ancestors to increase his height to how tall the giants of old were. However, by the time of the Great Disaster, Sphinx was able to create a more perfected version of the Sacrament of the Immortal King. By using restoration magic, in tandem with immense mana of the Stone, Muspel, as well as by setting up numerous magic circles across the entirety of the Imperial Capital, she was able to call the dead into vessels made of earth that could move by utilizing a corebug; the vessels retained the strengths of the souls that inhabited them, and with the effect of the restoration magic, the bodies that were destroyed could be "revived", bearing knowledge that the destroyed copy had obtained. When turned undead herself, Sphinx used this method to gather and relay information, a method which Subaru dubbed Escape by Death. Furthermore, thanks to the assistance of the undead Lamia Godwin, whose insight was somewhat greater than Sphinx's when it came to the truth of the soul, an undead created this way could have multiple copies of themselves be reproduced at a time. By Lamia's words, if such vessels can be created endlessly, then by diluting the source of those receptacles and filling them all, copies of the same person can be recreated. However, the vessels produced this way had a particular weakness to the destructive nature of fire magic and the time-based properties of yin magic, and furthermore, Spica's Astral Eclipse and the Yang Sword could also permanently prevent souls from being reproduced as an undead, either by interfering with or destroying the soul completely.
Al Shario (アル・シャリオ): Sphinx was capable of casting Al Shario, a spell that literally brought stardust down to earth, decimating opponents who were not strong enough to counter the falling stardust. The speed of the stardust is described to be almost impossible to evade. The star contains enough power that, even without touching the ground, it is capable of splitting the ground and burning the atmosphere.
Forbidden Art (禁術, Kinjutsu): An unnamed forbidden art and, aside from the Sacrament of the Immortal King, was the only one Sphinx was known to have experimented with. Designed by Sphinx herself, it went unused by her in her lifetime. It could create a blind spot in Od Lagna, invalidating its constraints. This was effective for nullifying the effects of Divine Protections and the Kingdom of Lugunica's covenant with Volcanica. In the period ensuing the Demi-Human War's end, Stride Vollachia acquired the means to replicate it and unleashed it during the Subjugation of the Blight Dragon.

Combined Spells:
Flying Magic (飛行魔法, Hikō Mahō): Sphinx could use flying magic, a spell executed with a combination of the earth, wind, and yang affinities, allowing her to float in the sky. She can also use the winds from this magic to protect herself from a certain level of strength from attacks.

Unclassified Spells: Sphinx has used spells that have not been classified under any category or magic, nor have they been deemed forbidden arts. 
Spatial Distortion: Sphinx could alter the space around her person, and if she was attacked and killed by her opponent, the distortion of space would explode outward, killing everyone in the vicinity in a bright flash of white light.
Unnamed Dimensional Spell: Sphinx was able to take a certain part of the world and place it within a pocket dimension, where it would remain completely unaffected from events in the outside world. She used this spell to separate the dungeon from the Crystal Palace and hold Priscilla prisoner.

Physical Traits/Flow Method
Martial Arts: Following her loss to Roswaal J. Mathers during the Demi-Human War, Sphinx began training in martial arts. She interlaced her magic with an elegant martial art technique. However, according to Sphinx, there was a limit to the level of enhancement that the Flow Method could yield for her replicant body when she was an undead.
Wind-Based Destructive Grip: By enshrouding wind magic on her palm and combining that with martial arts, Sphinx can catch attacks with her hand and use the intense vibrations of the wind to shatter anything caught within her grip.

Undead Physiology: After Sphinx met her demise, thanks to having used Sacrament of the Immortal King prior, Sphinx had risen as one of the undead herself. In this state, she could receive damage and easily repair it so long as the corebug within did not break. Furthermore, with the assistance of Lamia Godwin, she was able to multiply herself with undead copies by spreading out her soul, making it almost impossible to permanently end her. Similarly, because of this, if one of her copies died, the knowledge that one obtained would be shared with each other copy.

Intelligence
Keen Strategist: Sphinx is incredibly thorough when creating her plans. Throughout the Great Disaster, simply to prevent her plan from collapsing, she created numerous strategies and counterstrategies that she could put into play in the event that any prior strategies collapsed: using the undead against the country least compatible with life, using Muspel's mana stores up to ensure the country's collapse, using the core of Moguro Hagane as a bomb, using the Crystal Palace itself as a back-up power source, nudging Arakiya to take in Muspel and potentially using her death to trigger the country's collapse, etc. Likewise, she is not above using the unused strategies once proposed to her by Valga Cromwell.

Other
Zombie Creation: To create zombies, Sphinx used two kinds of lifeforms as a base from which two different zombie types were made. She has been described as the creator of one of them, while her relation to the other type is unknown. Similarly, it is not known if they were produced by magic or other means.
Corebug Creation: Sphinx could utilize corebugs (核虫, kaku mushi), small, round red bugs that appeared similar to caterpillars, which served as the core of a "zombies" and kept them intact. A corebug acquired the data of a deceased person to turn them into a zombie, and reproduced the victim's original form with a vessel of earth. This process could be finished near instantaneously, meaning that someone who died could immediately become a zombie following their own demise. The corebug, which could be located in a variety of body parts, impacted the durability of a zombie; they could be impervious to damage if stricken in areas that the corebug was not present in, but if the corebug itself was destroyed, the zombie broke apart and was immediately destroyed.
Parasite Creation: Sphinx could create parasites that took over a living target's body and turned them into "zombies". While their manner of creation is unknown, they completely followed the will of their creator, Sphinx, and sought to create a "paradise" for her. They initially formed in a host's body as a living tentacle-like appendage that was capable of physical movement. Upon taking control of a host's body, the host was killed, and the parasites were able to use the leftover brain's intellect and thought processes. Though it is not known if their process of taking over human hosts was selective, they were only observed to take over adult males despite being able to nest themselves within women and children, with the exception of one female host who was established as the parasites' queen. They also had the ability to take over non-human animal hosts, such as rats. Similarly to the Sacrament of the Immortal King's effects, the zombies' bodies slowly decomposed over time after being taken over. Although it was unknown if there was a limit on how many parasites can be created, it was possible for more than two thousand of them to exist at the same time, with each one loyal to Sphinx's desires.

Equipment
Staff: Sphinx held a black staff with red accents that was slightly longer than she was tall. The jewel inlaid in the main part of the staff can shine with bluish-white light and act as a light source, and should she choose to do so, she can use this jewel to project images of distant locations and events, similar to the functionality of a Conversation Mirror.

intro: Roswaal J. Mathers (ロズワール・J・メイザース), formerly known as Julia (ジュリア), was the grandmother of Roswaal L. Mathers, the mother of Roswaal K. Mathers, and the head of House Mathers two generations before the current Roswaal, and she was a key figure in making the study of magic prevalent within Lugunica. She played major roles in the Sword Demon Trilogy.
appearance:
Like previous generations, she had heterocromatic eyes, with the left eye being yellow and the right eye being blue. Her long straight indigo hair was partially tucked behind her left ear and reached down past her shoulders. Roswaal's skin was as fair as porcelain and her bust was considerably large. Despite the fact that this iteration of Roswaal wore little makeup, her astounding beauty was still enough to captivate men.

Although her clothing was fairly different from previous and succeeding generations, she still stayed true to the general taste maintained by every Roswaal. Her ensemble, that was a uniform of sorts in deference to the Demi-Human War that was ongoing at the time, consisted of a pair of long black boots, white tights, a white long-sleeved shirt, and a purple jacket with golden lining and rolled cuffs that was worn over the shirt, essentially obscuring the white garment from view. Her cleavage was not covered by the shirt nor the jacket, essentially meaning that it was exposed. Like her grandson, Roswaal wore a long black cloak that nearly trailed along the ground and had a red interior
history:
Julia was born with a Gate that could only hold and produce a small amount of mana, leaving her incapable of casting magic, unlike her previous bodies. However, Roswaal still took this chance to learn martial arts. At some point in time, Julia had a child, Karl, with Garitch Fabless in an attempt to bear a child who was apt in healing magic. Though she had siblings in this incarnation, they and their parents had all perished around the time of the Demi-Human War's end, if not earlier. At some point, she started researching how to create artificial gates in order to overcome gate problems, inspired by her maximum mana capacity being minimal and leaving her with subpar magic capabilities as a result. However, she never managed to accomplish this feat.

Sword Demon Love Song
Following the Battle of Castour Field, Julia was called in to examine the magic circles used. Accompanied by Carol Remendis, the two joined the Zergev Squadron out into Castour Field. Accompanied by Wilhelm Trias, Grimm Fauzen, and a few other members in a small group, they made their way into the field, with Roswaal speaking to Wilhelm while Grimm kept Carol company. After arriving at the site, she muttered that the Kingdom was certainly at threat, and soon after, the undead Tholter Weasily fired an arrow at her, which Wilhelm defended against. Though he managed to take care of most of the undead, he came face to face with Sphinx, who Roswaal decided to help fight against. However, Sphinx decided to retreat, leaving them with the undead to fight. Roswaal mentioned that one of the corpse soldiers should stand out as the main one to defeat, and with a push from Wilhelm, Grimm was able to slay that one soldier, Tholter. Soon after, Roswaal informed the others of Sphinx's identity and the threat she bore. They later reported the same to the Kingdom's government, and later, she claimed that she would likely being seeing the Zergev Squadron often moving forward as the war progressed.

For the next three years, she often found herself fighting alongside the Zergev Squadron on the frontlines, in order to pacify any magic circles. Before long, their sights were set on Aihiya Swamp, which Wilhelm compared to Castour Field. Roswaal appeared and confirmed his suspicions that the Kingdom did take into consideration that this was a trap, but they figured that the other side would surely fatigue. Accompanying her was Carol, who spoke with Grimm and gave him a good luck charm. With the arrival of Leip Barielle as their new commander, he struck Wilhelm for his disrespect, leaving Roswaal to pacify him and take him elsewhere alongside Carol. Later, during the Battle of Aihiya Swamp, she went to investigate a certain magic circle, only for it to activate right before her. Though she could have handled it with ease, Sphinx appeared and got in her way, killing a few of the nearby knights in an effort to get Roswaal to join her. However, this failed, and instead, Roswaal cornered her with her martial arts skill, forcing her to retreat. Afterward, Roswaal destroyed the magic circle, giving her allies a chance to retreat.

About a month later, she had the king hide elsewhere besides the castle while she went to assist the Zergev Squadron to corner the attackers. After allowing them into the castle, she went with Wilhelm's group and confronted Valga Cromwell and Sphinx in the chapel. With Wilhelm taking care of Valga, she, Carol, and Grimm chased after Sphinx, who they managed to successfully corner and sever one of her arms. When the ceiling was destroyed by one of her deflected attacks, Bordeaux and the undead Libre appeared. After Libre cut off her other arm and disintegrated, Roswaal chased after Sphinx and struck her back to the ground. However, using the secret passageways, Sphinx managed to escape her. As Roswaal searched for her, she encountered Leip, who claimed to have completely incinerated her, showing Roswaal a ring on a string as proof of her demise. Asking for the ring, she promised Leip his credit for killing Sphinx, while she smiled that things would be going according to plan to her teacher. When Wilhelm vanished to train himself, Roswaal would be the only one to manage to find him, and because of her, he managed to learn about the ceremony to award the Sword Saint Theresia van Astrea for her contributions to the war. On the day of the ceremony, Roswaal provided her with a ceremonial sword and gave her words of advice as she left.

Sword Demon Love Story
A couple of days after the ceremony, Roswaal appeared in the auxiliary Astrea Manor, where she assuaged the jealous Theresia's fears. Deciding to interfere one last time, Roswaal brought Theresia to the castle, despite Wilhelm requesting her not to come.

Sword Demon Battle Ballad
Julia sacrificed her life to save Carol, even though she hadn't expected to die at that point in time since it was not written in her Gospel.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
Despite lacking in the magic that each previous Roswaal had, Julia was still incredibly knowledgeable of magic and powerful in combat, having extensively trained herself in martial arts in order to fight and defend herself. Thanks to this, she was able to fight and easily overwhelm the likes of Sphinx and shinobi, making her one of the key figures in winning the Demi-Human War and the Subjugation of the Blight Dragon.

Physical Traits/Flow Method
Master Martial Artist: In order to counter the powerful magical abilities of Sphinx, Roswaal cultivated the body of Roswaal J. Mathers to be a master martial artist rather than a master mage. From a young age, Roswaal painstakingly trained her body in the martial arts. Over twenty years, her training coupled with her natural talent forged her into a true fighting genius. Anyone who saw her in combat could tell that she was an accomplished practitioner with a flawless technique. Her style was based around landing lightning quick and precise punches that sowed ruin upon the bodies of her enemies. Although his later bodies like Roswaal L. Mathers probably weren't as physically powerful as Roswaal J. Mathers, they still maintained the fighting techniques Roswaal had coalesced during that particular life, meaning Roswaal remained a true master of the martial arts. 

Superhuman Strength: The physical strength of Roswaal J. Mathers vastly surpassed that which was accepted as possible for a human being. Her mighty blows were powerful enough to snap bones, rupture internal organs, shatter boulders, and split large trees in half. She could throw small-yet-heavy steel balls with enough force to shatter bones and organs.

Magic
As she carries the knowledge of every previous Roswaal that came before her, Julia is has extensive knowledge in regard to magic, having made numerous headways in magic theory, recognizing the intricacies of spells and magic circles used by others, making the Royal Magic Research Institute, and being named as the country's court mage. However, due to her gate being inferior to every previous Roswaal, she is incapable of using her magic.

Yellow Eye: Roswaal is able to use a yellow eye to break magic apart. However, this ability does not seem to be instant, as when she used it to destroy a powerful magic circle, she first had to slightly tamper with the circle and then concentrate for a short time to allow her eye to cancel it. When it cancels magic, it seems to flicker slightly.

Spells:
Soul Transcription (魂の転写): A lost magic technique that allows a person to transcribe their own soul over another's. By doing this over and over to extend their life indefinitely, the user can achieve what Beatrice termed as "subjective immortality". However, it has one major restriction in that for it to work, the person whose soul is overwritten must usually be of blood-relation to the caster. The spell was originally created by Echidna to gain immortality, but she could not complete it before her demise. Instead, it was finished by Roswaal who had been using it to survive until the present era.

Equipment
Book of Wisdom (叡智の書): Just like Beatrice, Roswaal was given one of the two complete copies of the Book of Wisdom Echidna created before her ultimate demise. It allows Roswaal to use a limited version of the original Book of Wisdom, as it shows her a detailed path to her desired future. For four centuries, Roswaal strictly acted upon the Book's writ, doing exactly as it was written. 
Steel Mittens: Alongside her pugilistic fighting style, Julia wore a pair of black steel mittens to enhance the damage that she could cause to her enemies.
Enchanted Cloak: Roswaal wore a cloak that ensured that any offensive magical attack that struck the cloak would dissipate and leave its wearer unharmed. However, it is only effective for singular usage, as after negating an attack the cloak would dissipate.
Metal Throwing Balls: A type of projectile Julia specifically used for fighting Sphinx. Despite their small size they contained a lot of mass that allowed them to penetrate deep into the target's body, dealing significant damage.

name: Setanta
intro: Setanta (セタンタ) was the chief of the Oni Village Ram and Rem lived at when they were young, and the last chief of the onis.
appearance: Setanta was elderly in appearance with brown eyes and grey hair that goes down to his neck, a large build, and an intimidating presence. He tended to wear a montsuki haori jacket similar to many of the other members of the tribe. Like other members of his tribe, he was capable of producing two horns from his forehead.
personality: He strictly followed the law in the village and was shown to be willingly (albeit grimly) take the responsibility of removing the taboo of twins as an Oni himself. However, he changed his view when Ram unveiled her powers with just a single horn in order to protect Rem. He saw Ram as a child prodigy and ultimately accepted the Oni twins as members of the village, and he would often remind Rem that the only reason she wasn't killed was because of Ram's power. The only time he would treat Ram as a child was only when it was convenient. He seems to have a certain unique view on strength as well; when he met with his old friend, Valga Cromwell, he seemed to respect his mentality from when he was younger, and he spat at how he had gotten weak and soft with age.
history:
At an unknown point in time, Setanta met and befriended Valga Cromwell.

The Oni Sisters of the Hidden Village
Immediately after the birth of Rem and Ram, Setanta decided to kill the two for tainting the oni bloodline, rebuking their mother, Temae for birthing them and trying to protect them. Ordering to have her held back, he took his blade and prepared to kill them, only to be stopped by the infant Ram's power. Seeing her power, he and the rest of the onis knelt, calling her the reincarnation of the Oni God. Over the years, he had Ram join the onis on hunts and in various meetings. Some years later, Valga came to visit, and after being escorted to Setanta's house, he called himself Rom. Though Setanta told Ram to stay for the discussion and Rem to go home, Ram declined his order and left with Rem. A few hours later, he and Rom were leaving the village, having come across the twins. As he spoke to Ram, Valga scolded him for treating Ram as a child only when it was convenient. After Rom told the twins to be good sisters and left, Setanta spat that he had gotten weak with age before returning to his home. Sometime later, when the village came under attack by the Witch Cult, Setanta fought them off for a long time, until he was the last man standing, and in the end, he was set ablaze and killed.
abilities_text:
Oni Bloodline: As that chief of the Oni Tribe, he had access to the same traits that the rest of his tribe had. His strength was exceptional enough that, aside from Ram, he was the final oni standing during the Witch Cult's raid on his village.

Equipment: Due to his strength, Setanta was the only among the Oni Tribe who could wield an incredibly heavy, dulled, and over 2 meter long sword that had mainly been used as a decoration.

intro: Ryuzu Meyer (リューズ・メイエル) is the name of the original Ryuzu Meyer, whom her copies are based on. They played supporting roles throughout Arc 4.
appearance:
Like the original Ryuzu Meyer, all of the copies look the same. Ryuzu is a petite girl with long, fluffy pink hair that curves outward at the ends. She wears a large black robe (white for Shima) that drags along the ground and is too big for her hands to show completely through the sleeves. The bodies of the copies are revealed to have been created with an artificial "Od" that is surrounded and bound together with mana, forcing them to change places in order to recharge once they reach their daily limit.

Following the Sanctuary Incident, Garfiel and Subaru have begun styling each Ryuzu's hair differently in order to tell each of them apart, with the exceptions of the main three Ryuzus.
personality:
Out of all of the clones, only four have an actual personality, as a necessity to perform their duties as main managers of Sanctuary. Although they share the first name with the original they are given different last names as part of their roles, personality quirks, hobbies and interests. The rest of the copies are devoid of any ego and act as simple workers who obey the 4 main Ryuzu or take care of other duties. Those that are recognized to be an Apostle of Greed by Echidna are allowed to gain command over the clones if they touch the crystal the original Ryuzu resides in. Each of the four main Ryuzu take on the role as Ryuzu every four days.

Ryuzu Meyer (original): By her own will, she sacrificed her life to enact the Sanctuary's Barrier by using her own Od which sealed her body in a crystal in order to stop the Warlock of Melancholy from destroying the Sanctuary. She also agreed to be a part of Echidna's experiment as long as the witch promised to maintain the Sanctuary.
Ryuzu Alma (リューズ・アルマ, Ryuuzu Aruma): Alma was in favor of freeing the Sanctuary. She was the one who clarified Subaru over various aspects of the conflict within the Sanctuary.
Ryuzu Bilma (リューズ・ビルマ, Ryuuzu Biruma): Like Alma, Bilma was also in favor of freeing the Sanctuary. She is the 2nd clone Subaru meets and speaks the most with. Bilma also has the most playful disposition among the main overseers.
Ryuzu Shima (リューズ・シーマ, Ryuuzu Shīma): Shima was against freeing the Sanctuary due to seeing the original Ryuzu's memories 10 years prior to the start of the story in the trial, and she had been partly manipulating Garfiel behind the scenes to make sure it didn't happen. She entered the grave in an attempt to rescue Garfiel but was forced into taking the trial. In the end, this meant that she had broken her contract with Echidna. As punishment, Shima was duly stripped from her position as overseer, and she was made to live with the other childlike clones in the forest, donning the white robe as a result. After the Sanctuary's fall, it is revealed after that incident from a decade prior, Echidna had been planning to use her to escape once the barrier had been lifted, and to that end, she had been slowly latching more and more of her soul onto Shima, until eventually, she successfully hijacked her body. Echidna, now in Shima's body, calls herself Omega.
Ryuzu Delma (リューズ・デルマ, Ryuuzu Deruma): One of the copies with an actual personality. She was also in favor of lifting the barrier. She acted as Shima's support when the latter was telling the story of the Sanctuary's past.
Pico (ピコ, Piko): Pico is a copy that Subaru named when he first discovered the original Ryuzu's body. She is able to follow simple orders, but other than that, she is like a baby. She was the clone most oddly attached to Subaru throughout the arc.
Others: The other copies don't have knowledge or experience, and they can only obey broad orders. The copies act as eyes and use their telepathy to relay messages if needed. They need others to order them to eat food once in a while and curl up when they reach their limit in the forest. Following the events in Arc 4, the main clones, alongside Subaru and Garfiel, have been giving names and new hairstyles to the numerous clones in order to help them gain a proper sense of self. The same goes for Pico.
Sphinx (スピンクス, Supinkusu): The first clone created. Due to the imperfect method of Soul Transcription, she could not inherit all of Echidna's memories, personality, and power, which left her with a fragmented mind, and as a result, she was discarded. Centuries after her creation, she became a leading figure in the Demi-Human War and the instigator of the Great Disaster. She ultimately perished by the hands of Cecilus Segmunt, Priscilla Barielle, Subaru, and Spica.
history: The Ryuzu copies were created by Echidna in an experiment to research immortality. She copied her memories and knowledge to the copies. However, her experiment was never completed because of her death. The main copies took over in order to manage the other copies in Echidna's place and to take on Ryuzu's role within the Sanctuary when the Mathers family supported them.
abilities_text:
Note: This section will only detail the abilities shared by the clones. For the individual abilities of characters like Sphinx or Omega, see their respective pages.

Telepathy: The Ryuzu copies are able to transmit their thoughts to each other.

Self Destruction: If ordered to do so, the clones can blow themselves up and inflict magical bomb-like damage on their enemies.

intro: Sylphy Elmart (シルフィ・エルマート) is a maid working at Roswaal Manor and the former 184th wife of Regulus Corneas.
appearance: Sylphy is a woman with golden blonde hair and dark blue eyes. She has similar hair to that of Emilia and noticeable cute features. She wore a dress with a similar design to the one most of Regulus's other wives wore, but with features distinguishing it from the others. When employed as a maid, she starts to wear a maid uniform.
personality:
Due to years and years of having to live in fear of being killed for even smiling in front of Regulus, Sylphy developed a cold and emotionless facade which made her look like apathetic and uncaring. However, Sylphy does care about the others who were forcefully taken by Regulus, and she does not want to see them end up like many of his previous wives. This led her to taking the position of the representative of the other wives, willing to take his brutal punishment in place of the others. Likewise, she also believed that anyone who was able to escape from him should never come back, regardless of herself and the other wives, as she displayed to Emilia after she returned following her own “escape”. She even showed determination to end her own life if necessary in order to assist Emilia in defeating the man when she learned about the weakness of Regulus’s Authority.

In the aftermath of Regulus's defeat, she developed profound feelings of loyalty to Emilia, dedicating herself to serving the Royal Selection Candidate upon her employment as a maid in the Roswaal Manor.
history: At some point in the past, Sylphy lived in a small village in a mountain valley. However, when Regulus came and decided to take her as his 184th wife, he slaughtered her family, friends, and other villagers, just for knowing her face and name, leaving her to take on the emotionless facade that she and the other wives were forced to wear.
