intro: Stride Vollachia (ストライド・ヴォラキア) was a former prince of the Sacred Vollachia Empire and a Sin Archbishop of the Witch Cult, representing Pride. He was a younger Wilhelm van Astrea's mortal enemy. He was the main antagonist of Sword Demon Love Story and Sword Demon Battle Ballad.
appearance:
From a mere glance, Stride Vollachia could easily be recognized as a man of status around thirty years of age. His features, which helped distinguished his importance, were uncommonly sharp and noble. He had grey eyes and long, rich deep-purple hair that had a silky look to it and reached past his shoulders. His slim body had, ever since his youth, been riddled by illness that made even the simplest of physical activities grueling for him. His voice betrayed his imperialism and thus also his connection to the meritocratic Sacred Vollachia Empire.

In reflection of his physical appearance and noble carriage, Stride wore clothing of princely refinement. His outfit, that was primarily black, consisted of black trousers, black shoes, a light grey shirt, a black cravat, a white waistcoat over the shirt, and a black long coat over the waistcoat that had notched lapels and rolled cuffs. Some of his clothing had purple lining that matched the color of Stride's hair. On his left shoulder, similarly to what future emperor Vincent Vollachia would come to bear, Stride had many large feathers with purple tips, denoting his remaining connections to the Imperial Family. On each of his ten fingers, Stride wore his rings, the Hubristic Ten Commandments, that he could use to afflict curse-like effects on his enemies.
personality:
As the Sin Archbishop of Pride, Stride was vain and prideful, disliking being told what to do by others, as shown when he rebuked Yaktol Suwen for trying to restrict his actions or doing the same to Kurgan for talking back to him. He was openly rude to those he viewed to be lower than himself, and Theresia noted that he fluently insulted others. He seemed to underestimate fighters that aren't well known, as when Wilhelm and Kurgan first fought, he didn't think the former would stand a chance. Despite this, he was a quick thinker and praised things he found to be satisfactory. He was willing to ignore formalities to stop Wilhelm and Kurgan's first duel in order to prevent himself from potentially losing a valuable pawn. He plotted against the Kingdom of Lugunica knowing full well the power of Volcanica's protection, earning him his alias, the Destruction Wish.

Stride bears a powerful hatred of the Observers, as he has written in his journal. Likewise, many of his actions were done in accordance with this hatred.

Stride spoke in a very archaic, regal and scornful manner. He favored using the pronoun mine venerable self (余, yo) when speaking, which is a pronoun used only by kings or emperors. He also referred to people using thou (貴様, kisama) with it having connotations of Stride treating everyone he spoke to as an inferior.
history:
Early Life
Stride Vollachia was born as one of the sons of the emperor. However, he was born sick, and his family quickly proposed to offer the renunciation of his inheritance rights to another family, exchanging him for a suitable recompense. On the surface, Stride was sent to train under the strongest warrior in Vollachia, Kurgan, in order to improve his strength in mind and body, however, he was fully expected to die under Kurgan's harsh training regime. Luckily for Stride, though, Kurgan grew strangely attached to the bottomless darkness that was cultivating inside of the young boy's eyes, quickly taking a liking to Stride. Against all odds, he grew into adulthood under Kurgan's supervision. With strong ambition and insight, Stride had the potential to rise to a position where he could compete for the imperial throne. However, he had no backers for the Imperial Selection Ceremony. Shortly after, an unknown culprit poisoned Stride with a powerful poison, which caused Stride to drift between life and death for three arduous and agonizing months. The illness utterly destroyed him, to the point he more resembled a walking corpse, than a man. However, his eyes shone with newly-found determination–as he had found the very truth of the world, in the midst of his battle for life. On that day, Stride relayed to Kurgan what he saw: that there were entities called "Observers" who sit in the heavens, toying with everyone as if they were mere pieces upon a board.

With Kurgan at Stride's side, wanting to support his "son", the Destruction Wish began carving his path forward. He met and recruited the runaway shinobi Shasuke and Raizo, the Twin Shura, appointing them as his "Generals". Not long after, he encountered his future wife, the Ashen Bride, Melinda, a survivor of the Evil Eye Tribe, a people nearly erased from existence due to their Evil Eye abilities. At some point in this timeframe, he acquired a Witch Factor, joined the Witch Cult, and received his Gospel from a diligent knave who introduced himself as a Sin Archbishop and assisted Stride with the handling of his Hubristic Ten Commandments. At an unknown time, he hid his journal within the Crystal Palace.

Sword Demon Love Story
Approximately forty years prior to the start of the story, aiming for Sword Saint, Stride used the gift of Veltol Astrea as an excuse to meet with him in the Suwen Company in Picoutatte, where he openly insulted him and his daughter. With Veltol challenging him to a duel, he claimed to be unable to fight due to his illness, which Theresia had noticed, and he decided to have Kurgan act as his champion. Further antagonizing the two with insults to them and Theresia's husband, Veltol struck him, leading to his brutal beating by Kurgan and being cursed by Stride. Leaving Yaktol Suwen with a message that he would be waiting at a great bridge in the city's west district with the source of the curse, he left. The next morning, he met with Theresia and Wilhelm, who challenged him to a duel. Despite being irritated that the rumors he heard regarding her award ceremony were true and that Wilhelm had equivalent battle aura to Kurgan, the duel ensued. Despite this, both sides took great damage, and seeing that he was in danger of losing his pawn, he stopped the duel and claimed it their loss, tossing his ring to them, and using another to turn the bridge beneath them into sand, allowing him and Kurgan to escape. 

Sword Demon Battle Ballad
In the following months, he conducted a series of attacks, targeting seemingly random locations across the Kingdom, such as the Astrea Manor, where he had his wife Melinda ensnare Wilhelm with her Evil Eye of Vainglory through a Conversation Mirror and bound Carol Remendis to the curse of the Amethyst Thumb on his left hand. During this period, he went to Sphinx's refuge in Shamrock Valley to retrieve a forbidden art of hers that disabled people's Divine Protections and nullified the covenant between the Kingdom and the Divine Dragon. Roughly eight months into Theresia's pregnancy, Stride delivered a swift blow to the Kingdom by invading the Royal Lugunica Castle and killing Veltol by forcing Carol, who he had cursed before, into doing his every bidding with the Amethyst Thumb. Carol kidnapped Theresia and Stride, after cursing the surviving Tishua Astrea with his remaining Scarlet Pinky Finger, took the both of them back to Picoutatte, where he would begin an incident that later became known as the Subjugation of the Blight Dragon.

There, Stride set the forbidden art he previously retrieved across Picoutatte, situated himself in the city's main tower, and began collecting sacrifices, including a great deal of demi-humans with a grudge against Lugunica who volunteered their lives in an attempt to aid Stride in bringing the nation's ruin. Using the skull of a deceased dragonkin, which drunk the blood of the sacrificed people he forced Carol to slay, he was able to summon the dragonkin's parent, the Black Dragon Valgren, through its survival instincts, binding its will to his with the Jade Index Finger, Amber Middle Finger, and Azure Ring Finger on his left hand. He ordered Melinda to use her Evil Eye of Vainglory on the city's guards, sending them to the Subjugation Force and pinning them down, allowing Kurgan to attack the knights. Shasuke then brought forth Roswaal J. Mathers and Grimm Fauzen, the latter of whom arrived by error. Grimm had an arduous battle with Carol, who was still under Stride's curse, and Shasuke, one of Stride's shinobi. Roswaal, at the cost of her life, sacrificed herself to save the pair of Grimm and Carol from Shasuke. 

After attempting to defend himself from Grimm's attack by summoning the Yang Sword, it rejected him and began the process of burning his body, but he was quickly saved by Shasuke, who cut off his left arm, to stop the spread of the sword's flames. With the rings on his left hand reduced to ash, terminating their effects and leaving him with only the four rings on his right hand, Stride revealed his Gospel and his position as the Witch Cult's Sin Archbishop of Pride. Due to his left arm being scorched to nothingness and five of his nine remaining rings being destroyed, however, Valgren regained its senses and promptly attacked the four people on the top of the tower. Barely being saved by Shasuke, Stride jumped in the air while being carried by his "General" but was intercepted by Carol. A duel between her and the shinobi followed, resulting in Carol bisecting Shasuke, leaving Stride unprotected. Realizing he had lost, Stride fell off of the Dragon's back, towards the streets of the city below. Before he could hit the ground, the Black Dragon sprung towards him. Just before it could swallow Stride, Melinda, utterly burnt due to being scorched by one of Valgren's previous attacks, lunged towards her husband, embracing him. Seconds later, Valgren's heads chewed their two bodies into chunks and swallowed the pair.

However, even after his body was devoured, Stride's rings continued to influence Valgren. The Dragon was confronted by Wilhelm and Grimm, who both dealt a great deal of damage to the Dragon. During combat, Grimm and Wilhelm were both seriously wounded and could barely continue the fight. Just as the battle was about to close on a disastrous end, the fortieth King of the Dragon Kingdom of Lugunica, Gionis Lugunica, appeared in the city, and with him, the Divine Dragon descended from the skies above. In a couple of minutes, Volcanica scorched Valgren's body away, effectively marking the end of Stride Vollachia's influence over the world. After this, Vollachia erased him from their history, with his sole remaining physical legacy, the journal he concealed in the Crystal Palace's library, being discovered by Vincent Abellux as a child.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
Due to his weak physical condition from childhood, Stride's physical power is effectively non-existent. He primarily binds people to his will by employing his Authority in order to face off with his opponents, using this power to turn the swordswoman Carol Remendis against her friends. He also uses the skills of his four subordinates, including the combat prowess of his surrogate father, the Eight Arms, Kurgan, the Evil Eyes of Pride and Vainglory belonging to his wife, Melinda, and shinobi techniques of the Twin Shura, Shasuke and Raizo, having them fight and use their powers for his sake when his condition prevents him from engaging in a duels or he does not apply the effects of his Authority onto an opponent.

Authority
According to himself, Stride “obtained a Witch Factor and the manifestation of an Authority” despite proclaiming himself a “sham” and there being no recognizable inheritor to the Witch Factor of Pride after his death. He was assisted in handling his Authority by the same diligent knave who provided him with his Gospel.

Hubristic Ten Commandments (傲れし十戒, Ogoreshi Jikkai): Stride is the previous wielder of the Witch Factor of Pride and could use its respective Authority. Stride’s Authority produced a set of ten different rings that could “curse” any targets of Stride’s choosing. There were five unique rings, each corresponding to the five fingers on Stride's hand and having their own color assigned to them, as well as two copies of each unique ring for use on both hands. The rings shared the curse of binding a target's soul to adhere to Stride’s will, effectively turning them into a puppet that abode by his every whim. The eyes of a target changed change to the color corresponding with the ring Stride cursed them with. Furthermore, the rings had a last-resort technique that allowed Stride to manipulate a target’s body in such a way that their maximum potential was drawn out, but the burden this placed on their body was so immense, it could destroy the target if it was not terminated as soon as possible. It is unknown if Stride had a means to manufacture more rings or if the Authority could only manifest a total of ten rings. Similarly, it is unclear if the curses he could produce were related to those cast by curse arts or are otherwise entirely separate.
The Scarlet Pinky Finger (朱色の小指, Akeiro no Koyubi), the ring variety on Stride's pinky fingers, had the secondary effect of casting a limb-rotting curse on its target. It exhausted the gate and rotted the limbs of the target it was placed on, and eventually led to death. Its curses were cast on Veltol and Tishua Astrea. The Scarlet Pinky Finger on his right hand was sliced in half by Wilhelm at the conclusion of the Silver Flower Dance of Picoutatte, leaving Stride with a total of nine remaining rings.
The Amethyst Thumb (紫紺の親指, Shikon no Oyayubi), the ring variety on Stride's thumbs, had the secondary effect of casting an asphyxiation curse on its target. This curse activated when the cursed target touched a loved one, at which moment a dark red bruise left on their chest would begin to strangle them, hindering their capacity to breathe. Its curses were cast on Carol Remendis and an unborn Heinkel Astrea.
The Jade Index Finger (翡翠の真指, Hisui no Mayubi), the Amber Middle Finger (琥珀の中指, Kohaku no Nakayubi), and the Azure Ring Finger (空色の環指, Sorairo no Kanyubi), each corresponding to their respective fingers, were not observed to have any secondary effects. The three rings on Stride's left hand were used to bind the Black Dragon Valgren, which required three rings for its three souls, to his will. Its curses were also cast on the Twin Shura, Shasuke and Raizo, and assumedly on an unnamed member of the Safeguarding Chamber.

Equipment
Yang Sword Vollachia (陽剣ヴォラキア, Youken Vorakia): As a member of the Imperial Family of Vollachia, Stride was capable of summoning and using the Yang Sword Vollachia, otherwise known as the Yang Sword, an ornate crimson sword with light that shines like the sun. However, Stride was unworthy of summoning the Yang Sword, and shortly after materializing the blade, Stride's left arm began to burn, incinerating his left hand and all five rings on it, prompting Shasuke to cut it off in order to save his life. 
Gospel (福音): As a member of the Witch Cult, Stride was the owner of a copy of a Gospel. Each Gospel was a replica of the Book of Wisdom, a book that had been in the possession of the Witch of Greed, Echidna. The Book of Wisdom would provide exact details of future events concerning the Witch of Greed, essentially bestowing Echidna with a form of precognition. Unlike the original Book of Wisdom, the Gospels of the Witch Cult were imperfect replicas, meaning that, although they detailed the future of its owner, the events conveyed were subject to change and the information provided was often up for interpretation. The Gospels took the form of small black books that could only be read by their owners.
Conversation Mirror (対話鏡, Taiwa-kyō): A meteor that allows its user to communicate with others over a long distance by connecting with a separate Conversation Mirror, similar to a cell phone. Stride used a pair of Conversation Mirrors with his wife, Melinda, to have her ensnare Wilhelm with her Evil Eye of Vainglory over a long distance.

name: Sergei
first_light_novel: The Oni Sisters of the Hidden Village
intro: Sergei (セルゲイ) was one of the Witch Cultists that attacked Ram and Rem's village. After his defeat, he was killed by the sisters.
appearance: Sergei was a young man with a frivolous and innocent appearance.
personality: Sergei was almost always shown to be calm and composed. He was also sadistic, believing it to be fun to strangle his victims, whether or not they were children.
history:
The Oni Sisters of the Hidden Village
Around ten years before Natsuki Subaru's arrival into the world, Faust, Sado, Sergei, and Fogg attacked the Oni Village. Three months later, Sergei ambushed and murdered Dudley Miload on his way home from Costuul. Afterward, he left for the Miload Manor to lure away Roswaal L. Mathers and one of the sisters. After the group arrived, he showed Rem the brutalized corpses on the convoy and tricked her into using her horn, effectively incapacitating her with his mana poisoning. After then unleashing an explosion on the carriage Roswaal was in, he summoned the other nearby cultists, and he tried to strangle Rem. However, Roswaal attacked with magic and retrieved Rem. After sending her off to the Miload Manor to save Ram and Grace, he faced off with the cultists, effectively slaying them all and breaking all of Sergei's limbs. Sergei was presumably killed by the sisters a short while later.
abilities_text:
Mana Poisoning: Sergei was born with a nature that randomly interferes with and poisons the atmospheric mana around him. This makes him the natural enemy of the Onis, and it is the primary reason why they were able to be so easily defeated. This trait makes it troublesome for magic users to use magic, capable of reducing the power of high-powered spells of someone like Roswaal and reducing the freedom to use it in general.

Explosion Technique (爆裂術式): Sergei was able to use the Explosion Technique; however, he admits that he's terrible at it.

name: Sado
first_light_novel: The Oni Sisters of the Hidden Village
intro: Sado (サド) was one of the Witch Cultists that attacked Ram and Rem's village. He was later killed by Ram.
appearance: Sado was a sluggy, short, and somewhat fat man. Neither his appearance nor his clothes were unique; they appeared so normal that if he slipped into a crowd, it would be easy to lose sight of him.
personality: Sado was shown to be extremely careful person who does not work on his own, willing to abandon any plan the moment things look bad for him, even being willing to leave the country he is in, something which has allowed him to stay alive. To him, everything that the wind tells him is most important, and he will act according to the way the wind blows. Sado was not very expressive, and as he was dying, he did not beg for his life, merely pitying his enemy and offering his name in his final moments.
history:
The Oni Sisters of the Hidden Village
Around ten years ago, Faust, Sado, Sergei, and Fogg attacked the Oni Village. Three months later, he set upon a scheme to cause mayhem in the Royal Capital involving the use of magical miasma stones. However, when the wind turned bad for him, he decided to abandon his plan, only to be confronted by Rem and Frederica Baumann. Deciding to leave other cultists to hold him off, he avoided the girls' attacks and rode the wind to escape. As he was escaping, however, Ram was able to shoot him down with her magic, severing his limbs. As he was bleeding out on the ground, Rem and Frederica found him, and Rem began interrogating him. However, he merely claimed to pity Rem, and he gave her his name before he died.
abilities_text:
Wind Reading: Sado was taught how to read the wind by Faust, something which allows him to determine if good or bad things are coming his way. Because of this, he has an extremely sharp intuition.

Wind Riding: Sado was able to float and ride on the wind at high speeds. However, it is not flight magic, and it is unclear if this ability is related to magic. Due to its nature, he can only move windward and downwind, giving him less freedom to maneuver himself.

Equipment: Sado kept magical miasma stones on his person to use in a certain scheme. It is unknown if he had any other uses for them.

name: Safis
alias: Snake Eyes (蛇目, Janome)
affiliation: Kingdom of Lugunica ; Flanders ; Black Silver Coin
appearance: Safis is a slender man with dark green hair and eyes reminiscent of a snake's.
personality: Safis is absolutely loyal to Doltero and his organization, the Black Silver Coin. He will do anything to ensure the livelihood and power of his boss, even if it means offering his own life or having the lives of his Doltero's family murdered so as to ensure that he has no weaknesses.
history:
The Golden Lion and the Sword Saint
Upon learning about the existence of his boss's mistress, Kalifa, and daughter, Ilya, from Doltero himself, Safis took it into his own hands to have them killed out of loyalty to his boss, having the desire to remove his "vulnerabilities". As a result, Kalifa was attacked by an assailant Safis sent and had her larynx destroyed, inhibiting her from ever being able to speak again. She and her daughter both survived, and she entrusted Ilya to the Astrea Manor for protection. Doltero sent one of his men after the two, but he was discovered by Felt and Reinhard and revealed his affiliation with the Black Silver Coin once the candidate threatened with the Sword Saint. Shortly afterwards, Gaston, Rachins, and Camberley located Kalifa and brought her back to the mansion, where they discovered that Doltero was Ilya's father. Deciding to visit Doltero in Flanders, Rom used his connection to Doltero to hold a meeting with him. When Felt, Reinhard, and Rom, alongside Kalifa and Ilya, met with Doltero, he discovered that Safis was responsible for ordering the attack on his mistress and daughter. Safis revealed his intentions, preparing to commit suicide to atone for his misdeeds, only for Doltero to suddenly assault him to keep him alive and demote him to a simple lackey position in the Black Silver Coin unless he could work to regain the Pig King's trust. Understanding Safis's argument, he decided to disown his mistress and his daughter, much to the displeasure of Felt and Rom. Following the incident, Safis was stripped of his executive position in the organization, but was allowed the chance to prove his loyalty and regain Doltero's trust.

Riot in Flanders
Two months later, Doltero had a meeting with Toto and Manfred Madison, the other heads of the Big Three, and Helaine Gatness, the leader of the Flanders branch of the Golden Beetle. The meeting concerned a series of murders that had been committed against members of the Big Three organizations, as well as the Golden Beetle, with Helaine proposing that Felt was responsible, having received reports that she contacted Doltero and the Black Silver Coin before. As a result, Manfred and Toto went on to seek courtesy visits from her as a means to verify her intentions, with Doltero sending Safis to inform her of their wishes. Meeting Felt and Reinhard in Hakuchuri, he told them of the circumstances in Flanders and relayed Doltero's message that the Flower Prison Garden and the Balance were awaiting courtesy visits from her.

Several days after Felt's courtesy visits, the Big Three started began pursuing Ezzo Cadner, who was framed for burning down a brothel in the red-light district and killing members of the Big Three, including a veteran of the Black Silver Coin and Mimosa, a prostitute from the Flower Prison Garden. Once Felt discovered his location at an abandoned mansion and heard his side of the story and Reinhard defeated a hundred members of the Black Silver Coin who had gathered at the mansion to catch the dwarf while using the name of the Masked Knight Veltol, the candidate and the Sword Saint proceeded to Doltero's mansion. Reinhard defeated another hundred men from Doltero's group, and him and Felt met with the Pig King and Safis. Felt suspected that the Black Silver Coin was responsible for the strife in Flanders, having learned that Kalifa and Ilya were targeted again. Neither Doltero nor Safis claimed responsibility, and nobody else in the organization had realized the truth about their relation to the Pig King. However, Safis mentioned that the veteran of the group who died on the night of the brothel's arson had been present when Kalifa and Ilya visited Doltero with Felt, and had revealed this information to Mimosa, who then relayed it to someone else. Ultimately, the incident's mastermind attempted to pit Felt and her group and the Black Silver Coin against each other, and succeeded in guiding her faction's actions. Despite that, Felt maintained confidence and relied on her comrade's approach to resolve the strife in Flanders. In the end, the true culprits were discovered and the incident was resolved, and the Black Silver Coin continued operation.

intro: Reize (レーゼ) is a resident of Kararagi who stole the Light Sphere of the Slasher, Zarestia. Though she has yet to appear in the main story, she first appears in the Kararagi Reaper Incident side story.
appearance:
After taking part of the Light Sphere, Reize's appearance would mirror Zarestia's. Reize has milky-white shaggy hair with a magenta strand, white eyebrows, and sharp almond-shaped eyes with a bright yellow color. She wears an immaculate pure black kimono with a magenta sphere and the right side over the left, giving the impression of burial clothes, but with the skirt shortened to the mid-thigh and freely exposing her long, slender legs.

In Re:IF, Reize was a young woman who had short, dark brown hair, and light blue eyes. Upon being exposed to alcohol, she was reverted to her true appearance, having dark circles around her eyes and bearing a physique smaller than that of Zarestia's.
personality:
After taking part of the Light Sphere, Reize gained the desire to murder people akin to how Zarestia had. While her true form and age have not been stated in the main canon, due to her impulsive behavior, it is suggested that she could be on the younger side. She was also intent on killing Anastasia's longtime companion, the artificial spirit Echidna, for unknown reasons, until the former convinced "Black Tia" that she could help her.

In Re:IF, she was easily angered by members of the Witch Cult as they were the ones that destroyed her village. This consequentially made her extremely vengeful and ruthless towards anyone who emits miasma. Moreover, she showed an envy towards someone for living a positive life that she could not have. She also acquired Zarestia's aversion to alcohol.
history:
Reize lived with her mother within a village for outcasts that lay in a remote area near the city of Azamiki. However, the peaceful life she had in her village was brought to an end when it was attacked by Capella Emerada Lugunica. By some chance, she survived and sought the power to take revenge. Sometime later, Reize received a part of Zarestia's Light Sphere and is currently seeking revenge.

Kararagi Reaper Incident
At some point after taking a part of Zarestia's Light Sphere, she unleashed a black tornado toward Banan, which the Anastasia Camp, Halibel, and Zarestia all fought off. However, the moment they overcame the tornado, Reize kidnapped Anastasia Hoshin and Echidna. When Anastasia later woke up, she found herself in Zarestia’s Bed, and Echidna had left her side to ensure her safety, as she was the main target behind their enemy’s actions. Anastasia spoke with Reize, who looked effectively identical to Zarestia, and after a one-sided conversation, Anastasia promised to help her, as otherwise, everyone who would come to find Echidna, Reize, and Anastasia herself would find themselves likely killing each other. Not long after, Echidna appeared after realizing Anastasia would be safe, and despite her concerns, Anastasia convinced her that everything would be fine. After this, Anastasia learned Reize's name, history, and goals, chose to help her achieve them, and returned a full day later to Banan, where Reize allowed herself to quietly sit in a cell.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
When using Zarestia's Light Sphere, Reize's power becomes immense, capable of easily destroying towns. However, it is unclear just how much power Reize is capable of or is proficient in utilizing, making the full extent of her capabilities unknown. Similarly, it is unknown whether or not she is capable of combat without the Light Sphere.

Magic/Spiritual Arts
Although it is unknown what attribute that Reize has an affinity for, with Zarestia's Light Sphere, Reize can utilize the Slasher's immensely powerful wind magic. However, it is unclear if she is capable of using ordinary magic or if the Light Sphere enables Reize to naturally use spiritual arts.

Physical Traits
Miasma Attuned Olfaction: On the night her village was destroyed, Reize was approached by a mysterious figure, who poured "something" into her ear. Following that incident, Reize was able to smell the miasma. With this ability, Reize can easily locate people who are emitting a strong miasma, similarly to how Rem can smell Subaru's miasma after the latter Returns by Death. It is revealed by Echidna in Re:IF Kasaneru that this is a natural ability of the Oni tribe as well as their purpose for existing. However, as her race in the main canon is unknown and it is unclear if Capella has done anything to her, it is unknown whether Reize retains this ability.

Equipment
Light Sphere (光珠, Mi Tama): Reize received a part of Zarestia's power from the Light Sphere, a gem that serves as Zarestia's anchor, the source and store of her power. For unknown reasons, after acquiring it, she assumed Zarestia's appearance. This effect could be reverted, however.

appearance: Shasuke was a man with white hair parted to the left, blue eyes, and a single right eyebrow. He was described to always wear a black cloak that covered his entire body. He also wore a mask on his face, and a hachigane on his forehead. When he took off his cloak, his body was described to be quite pale, with an eerie blue mottled pattern covering his torso.
personality: Shasuke had quite a humble personality, serving his master without complaint. He did not feel any emotions until the very end due to the Shinobi training process stripping them from him. Just before his death, he was described to have finally been happy, and was finally able to laugh louder than he ever had in his life.
history: Raizo and Shasuke were born in Vollachia's shinobi village. The two of them were twins who were subject to the training process of a shinobi. The process was cruel, and involved body modifications using drugs, curse marks, all kinds of magic, and heavy training. It was mentioned that only one in a million could survive this process. Both he and Raizo survived and reborn as shinobi. However, despite their promise, the two of them were deemed as imperfect by the shinobi for being twins. As a result, they killed the grown-ups who had deprived them of everything, the comrades who followed them, and became runaway shinobi. Before they fully escaped, they had a run-in with the most formidable and deadly shinobi of all, Olbart Dunkelkenn, who decided to let them live on a whim. Eventually, the twin shinobi encountered and devoted their services to Stride, accepting his offer to use and dispose of them in the most extravagant way possible.

Following the unexpected death of his mother, Karl was possessed by the original Roswaal, and inherited the Roswaal estate, along with its assets.

At some point, Karl began researching numerous things regarding magic. He’d come up with a theory to imbue objects with Yang Magic, and he created numerous magic dolls which he used to guard his home.

name: Reisel
intro: Reisel (ライゼル) was one of Ricardo Welkin’s colleagues back when he was a slave.
appearance: Reisel is a brown Tanuki-human who wears traditional Japanese-style clothing.
history:
Reisel was originally a slave who was forced to work in the mines doing hard labor. He met Ricardo there, forming a friendship with him. Reisel organized numerous slave rebellions, and in one of them, he and some others escaped, though Ricardo was not invited to it. 

Five years after that, in Kararagi Girl & Cat's Eye, Reisel entered a bar and met with Ricardo. He requested Ricardo to do him a favor by stealing from a cargo full of goods. Ricardo asked what his aim was, and Reisel replied that he intended to steal a Meteor from it. 

On a mountainside outside of Banan, both Ricardo and Reisel tried to ambush the cargo, Shiroro emerged from the cart and attempted to cut off Ricardo's head. Whilst that happened, Reisel stole the cart, leaving Ricardo behind as he battled against Shiroro.

However, the cargo had been switched with empty boxes, thus Reisel wasn't able to recover the meteor he was looking for. In rage, he used his own meteor that Mother had given him to create shadows to locate the real shipment and kill those who stole them. His plan was thwarted by the combined efforts of Anastasia Hoshin, Echidna, and Ricardo.

As a result of his defeat, Reisel destroyed the meteor that was given to him by Mother. She came to the scene, where the weak and sprawling Reisel was in front of her. He begged that he wanted a second chance, but she did not tolerate his failure. She touched his forehead, causing Reisel to lose all of his limbs, his eyes, nose, mouth, ears, and transformed him into something inhuman.

relatives: Lilac (alternate personality/separate soul)

intro: Shion (シオン) is a wandering dream arts user. She, alongside Lilac, later joined the Omega Party.
appearance:
Shion has orange eyes with blue pupils, and as an elf, she also has pointed ears. She has long green hair with a ponytail on her right side. Her attire consists of a short white cloak with a green diamond-shaped pattern in the inside, a white and brown dress that is like a huntress wears, and white high-end boots. She also adorns an orange rose on her left shoulder, a dagger wrapped around on her hips, and a small gold locket around her neck.

Since Shion shares the same physical vessel as Lilac, whenever her personality manifests in their vessel, its appearance instantly shifts to match hers.
personality: Shion is a rather friendly person who is easy to talk to, and she does not like dragging others into her messes if she can help it, even going as far as to ask a stranger to help her speak to her other half, Lilac. Due to being a Dream Arts User, however, her sense of self is somewhat fuzzy, and because she is so synchronized with others, she can find herself becoming influenced by other people's memories, including taking on their speech quirks. It is because of this that she can often be heard speaking with numerous loan words, having picked them up from passing memories of a person who uses them. She is somewhat driven by her goal to find the person who uses these words, even being willing to follow Omega as part of her party for the chance to learn of the person who uses them.
history:
At an unknown point in time and for unknown reasons, two separate souls, Shion and Lilac, came to possess the same vessel. When the two souls first confronted each other, they were in conflict and fought for control over their shared body. However, one day, that changed, and they now share their body peacefully, speculating that, having entered another person’s dream, they were deeply affected. As time passed, they came across the dream of a man who spoke with English loan words, and ever since, they have been searching for the person whose dream they entered in order to fill the void that lingered in their hearts.

Omega in Wonderland
At some point, she and Lilac appeared in Gusteko. However, they were deemed heretics by the Gustekan Church, causing them to send a Temple Knight after them. At some point after entering the town of Sylphoa, they confronted Mikli, and Lilac, having had no time to aim, used her Dream Arts to put her, and accidentally, the entire town, to sleep. Unable to contact Lilac after this, Shion remained in Sylphoa, where eventually, another Temple Knight and his cohorts arrived. However, shortly after arriving, she felt her connections to them start to vanish, despite attempting to bring them into the dream world.

Sometime later, after having witnessed a beast escaping with two girls, Shion spoke with one of them, Palmyra, and while introducing herself, she asked for Palmyra's assistance. After explaining the situation to her, she used her hypnosis magic to put Palmyra to sleep, giving her a message to pass along to Lilac. Shortly after, she came face to face with Noelle Tuérico, who was making hostile remarks and threatening violence toward her if she didn't undo her spell, not listening to anything Shion would say. Just before Noelle flew into violence, however, she warned Noelle that the person she was working with, the other Temple Knight, killed his allies and might do the same to her. This led to a fight immediately afterward between said Temple Knight and Noelle and the beastified Colette. However, this did not last, as Palmyra awoke and told the man that his fiancée Mikli, the other Temple Knight, was still alive.

Following this, after Omega spoke to the man and had him leave with Mikli and report the death of the heretic, Lilac released the people of Sylphoa from her dream world, and Omega offered Shion and Lilac to join her party. Since she couldn't quite trust the two, having just met them, she would give them a chance to look into her memories with their Dream Arts, giving them a chance to find the person from which the loan words they speak come from. The two accepted her offer and joined the party.

Witch Trials
One day, having moved on from Sylphoa, the Omega Party was walking in a snow field, where they encountered a Snow Blight. However, Omega swiftly dispatched it with Minya. Soon after, they arrived at Limbus, where signs claiming it was forbidden to go out at night and to comply with the "vows of the faith". Though slightly concerned about the town's eeriness, as the group was low on supplies, they decided to enter Limbus, where after a few minutes, they found themselves surrounded by the townsfolk who were armed with farming tools. Though they attempted to calm the townsfolk and offer them a gift in the form of the Snow Blight's crystallized head, they instead accuse her of being a Witch after seeing it, leading Omega to warn Colette against using her bracelet's transformation and Lilac from turning back into Shion, else they be declared Witches. Thanks to the appearance of Nananna Pezza and speaking with Noelle, she was able to vouch for them and clear them of being Witches.

Omega's group finds an inn to reside in where they discussed the issue at present, warning everyone about how easily they could be made into scapegoats whether for their abilities, race, or even the look in their eyes, and Noelle explained about Witch Hunts and Witch Trials being rare occurrences in Gusteko that Itinerant Preachers were sometimes sent to deal with. Although wanting to leave the town quickly, the group decides to stay in the town to help Noelle repay her debt to Nananna, and soon after, they meet with Nananna when she arrived to ask for the group's assistance. That night, the Witch Hunt is for a person named Piditz who had been tipped off as a Witch, and Nananna wanted him taken into custody only. When they later spotted Piditz and chased after him, Omega split off to corner him, only to find Mireille Hetia using her spiritual arts to kill Piditz. Thanks to being near the body, Omega was quickly turned into a scapegoat and declared a Witch so that Mireille could cover up her kill and at least prevent her from getting in the way of her and Nananna's revenge, and Omega was taken into custody.

At the inn, the party discusses how if the scale of this event expands, they will be unable to prevent the spread of the news this time, which could result in the party's persecution, even abroad, and their possible extradition back to the church. To clear their names, Colette states that they should find the real culprit for the murders. Lilac and Colette go to gather information around the town, and they meet with Mireille, who explained to them how the hunts started. Likewise, Omega explained this to Palmyra, as she learned it while imprisoned. As for Noelle, she joined Nananna, who had been speaking with Edmon about finding Piditz. Shion used her dream arts to peer into the minds of the townsfolk, and she warns Lilac that the "Witch" is just a conspiracy by the council to get rid of political enemies. After learning of this, Lilac informs the Colette and Palmyra, and the elves suggest sowing division in the people to uproot the conspiracy. Though wanting to talk to Noelle, she does not come back that night, and Lilac and Shion decide to use their dream arts to nudge the townsfolk to attend the upcoming.

The next day, the Witch Trial is being held for Omega, overseen by Nananna and the Town Hall, while Palmyra acts as Omega's attorney. Despite her arguments, Edmon Quayle counter with his supposed knowledge of the Witches and Omega's chatter does not help. Colette speaks up and claims that she believes that things will not go as the council claims, as people will begin to notice that the entire event seems off, which resounds with the townsfolk. Because of this, Palmyra claims that there is a conspiracy, which Edmon fights against and asks for Nananna's assistance. Because she sides with the town, Lilac and Shion believe her to be part of the conspiracy, and they decide to use their dream arts to influence the people's mental states. Palmyra then claims that the council is using the Witch rumors to get rid of inconvenient people, which Edmon also fights against, though is quickly silenced when she states she heard it herself from a council member and declares that there is no Witch. Unfortunately, Omega claims otherwise.

Despite angering Palmyra, Omega decides to clear things up by declaring that there were two conspiracies taking place in town. Despite Nananna trying to prevent her from talking, Omega ignores her and explains that many of the victims were relatives of council members, and she claims that Nananna is the second conspirator, calling her the bastard child of Edmon whose mother was banished from the town, and as a result, she despised the town. Noelle later appears and confirms that her actions were in response to the death of an elderly healer, and she claims that Nananna tried to remove her from the trial by knocking her out since her only ire was with Limbus. Afterward, Noelle declares that the secretary, Mireille, was helping Nananna, as she was a bastard child of Edmon as well, and she stated how the corpses of Piditz and other people connected to the council and other outside officials were already dumped in a hole. Omega also declares that she witnessed Mireille killing Piditz. Enraged, Mireille uses her spiritual arts to char Edmon's arm with blue fire, and with the intent of killing the entire council, surrounds the council with blue fire, and she and Nananna stand against them. Although Omega is fine with leaving things as they are and taking their leave, Colette states she doesn't want things to end like this, and Omega decides to end the fighting in response to her plea, burning through her restraints and declaring herself a Witch.

Later, as Omega's party begins to leave the town, Noelle says her goodbyes to Nananna, and it is declared that the evil spirit accompanying Mireille will be disposed of. Likewise, it is claimed that Edmon's position is under threat with both his severe injuries and the loss of the citizens' trust, and Mireille claims she was mistaken about real Witches. Despite Colette believing that things were settled peacefully, however, Omega thinks to herself that Limbus would soon face its destruction, as since Omega, Nananna, and Mireille were not executed, there would be continuous Witch Hunts and deaths for scapegoats for the whole incident. Although considering telling Colette about this, she decides against it.

Magic (魔法, Mahō): Shion is skilled at using dream arts.
Dream Arts: A type of forbidden art that is all but lost from the world in the present that allows its user to meddle with the mind. It is trained by using people as test subjects. After the person falls asleep, the practitioner must learn to sense and attune themselves to the person's Od before they die. Her proficiency with Dream Arts is considered impressive by Omega, who herself can use Dream Arts, and even surpasses her, being able to put an entire town to sleep for long periods of time and create a dream space larger than the Castle of Dreams. Likewise, if she chooses to, she can look into another person's memories to extract specific information. However, their target may show resistance, preventing her from reaching the memory she is looking for.

intro: Salum Pristis (サルム・プリスティス) is Melty Pristis's older brother. As his alternative personality, Wolf (ウォルフ), he was an assassin who attempted to dispatch the five Royal Selection Candidates other than Melty. After Wolf and Pooka's defeat, Salum, Wolf, and Pooka joined Melty and Tiga in fleeing from the Kingdom of Lugunica, intending to pay a visit to Tiga's old group of travelling entertainers.
appearance:
Salum wears a Middle Eastern-inspired uniform with a black, short shirt, gold eyes-like belts around his chest waist, a blue bandana on his head, and bandages on his hands, covering the Evil Eyes engraved on his hands.

As Wolf, he dons a yellow uniform with a black overcoat that touches the ground, black gloves and boots, and switches between several masks with different expressions. However, as opposed to the two sharing the same vessel but having different appearances, Wolf's body is the same as Salum's, and thus without the uniform that obscures his appearance, the two appear identical, with only their voices changing. Initially, Salum puts a black robe over himself as a ritual of sorts to give control of his body to Wolf, but after the two of them came to terms with one another, they could switch between each other at will without the use of the robe.
personality:
Serious and humorless, Salum is a man of few words. He is a vagabond on a journey, traveling around the world with his spirit partner Pooka. He is an unsophisticated yet kind-hearted person who steps forward and takes on danger in place of others. Although Pooka describes him as a man of common sense, he has trouble communicating with other people. He has a soft spot for younger people and always carries sweets with him to distribute to younger children. Because of his intimidating appearance and quiet nature, people sometimes react with suspicion.

As opposed to Salum, Wolf is significantly more talkative, has a haughty temperament, and enjoys toying with his opponents. His mercilessness towards targets and his capacity to be cold-hearted in order to fulfill a task distinguish him from Salum. Wolf frequently admonishes his other half for his weakness, and is far more powerful than Salum when he is in control. While he still covered his body with a black robe, he showed off his emotions by wearing one of his eight masks to express himself. Due to his purpose to act in Salum's place, he convinced himself that he had to play the role of a villainous evildoer, hurting himself in the process. Unlike Salum, he lacked a bond with and did not care for Pooka, though in spite of this, he panicked as she approached death and refused to let her die. After Wolf's defeat, he was recognized by Melty and Salum as their other sibling, and changed his ways, calling himself Pooka's friend and declaring that he would spoil his little sister.
history:
Salum hailed from Faradar, the village of the Evil Eye Tribe, which was home to him and his younger sister, Melty. When it came time for Melty to undergo an exam to determine her power's strength, she was found to have the Evil Eye of Bewitchment and unintentionally caused the people at the exam to fight each other until they collapsed. Although nobody died, as a result of this, she was separated from the rest of the village, and Salum was told to never visit her. However, he frequently slipped by the tribe's adults to meet with her, bringing her information about her Evil Eye, such as that someone else from hundreds of years ago had possessed the same power as her, for her sake. Salum also happened to meet Melty shortly after her first encounter with Tiga. While initially wary of Tiga's presence, he accepted the young boy's assertion that he was Melty's friend and would never leave her side.

Following an attack on Faradar, Salum was separated from his sister. Desperate to reunite with her, Salum joined with Mother's faction, working to ensure his sister's safety. Around this time, he met and formed a contract with Pooka, who was tasked by Mother to keep an eye on him. However, Salum could not fully embrace the power of his Evil Eye, which made him fail at even the simplest of jobs. As a result of his weakness and his inability to fulfill his role, the personality of Wolf was born. Wolf made a deal with Salum to perform the dirty work in his place. Salum accepted this and deferred control of his body to Wolf in order to accomplish the work he was tasked with.

intro: Rudar Iglesia (ルダール・イグレシア) is an exclusive character from the video game Re:Zero Lost in Memories and is the younger brother of Zelga Iglesia.
appearance: Rudar is a tall and slim middle-aged man with long dark purple hair, blue eyes and a short mustashe. He wore a white shirt with a necklance under a indigo coat and a red vest with yellow outlines.
personality: Rudar is shown to be a selfish and greedy man who always think himself as a king. He also had planed to coup d'etat against the Kingdom of Lugunica and the Royal Candidates as he thinks so highly of himself that he is fit to be king.
history: Rudar used to live with his two brothers. One day, he killed his older brother and almost killed Zelga and sent him to prison. Years later, after Subaru and Zelga escaped from Grimour Prison, he was dethroned by his brother and was sent to prison.
abilities_text: Engraving Seal of the Blue Flame (青炎の刻印 Aoi Honō no Kokuin): It's an ability that has been passed down from the Iglesia family for generations. It gathers light within his body and shows the seal on their back.

intro: Sithonia Featherrun (シトニア・フェザーラン) was the eldest daughter of the Featherrun Sisters and a "child" to Mother.
appearance: Sithonia was a beautiful young woman of around twenty in age, of tall stature, and with long blood-red hair flowing all the way down to her waist. Her irises were also red, and she wore a matching red dress of the same colour.
history:
At some point in time, Sithonia ended up under the control of Mother, and was tasked with bringing her a curse doll. As a result, by some means, Sithonia ended up becoming the eldest daughter of the Featherruns sisters by surviving being made into an imperfect curse doll. Sithonia cherished the time she spent at the Featherrun mansion, and was distraught when the process to make a completed curse doll was set into motion after Holosseo was killed, with the Featherrun Sisters being resorted to slaughter each other.

Adamant that she would win out in the slaughter and complete herself fully as a curse doll so she could escape from Mother's influence, Sithonia secretly plotted against her sisters. She tried to kill her main adversary, Elsa Featherrun after all of the other sisters were out of the picture, however she was easily defeated, and chose to be killed by her so she could be finally free of her abominable Mother.
abilities_text: Curse Doll (呪い人形): As an imperfect curse doll, Sithonia possessed immense regenerative capabilities giving her a pseudo-immortality. Sithonia was also able to control the shades of the girls who had failed to become curse dolls via her ability, and use them in attack. In addition, she could also transform into and imitate people with exceptional accuracy.

name: Ryuzu Meyer
status: Deceased (body sealed in a mana crystal)
relatives: Ryuzu copies (clones) ; Omega (clone) ; Sphinx (clone)
intro: Ryuzu Meyer (リューズ・メイエル) was a half-elf girl who lived in the Sanctuary during the era of the Witches, four centuries ago. She was used by Echidna in order to activate the Barrier and protect the Sanctuary from the Warlock of Melancholy.
appearance: Ryuzu was a petite girl with long, fluffy light pink hair that curved outward at the ends. She wore a large black robe that dragged along the ground and was too big for her hands to show completely through the sleeves. Due to her race, she had a pair of pointy ears which were usually concealed by her pink hair. Her face was very adorable and innocent. Due to the high collar of her attire, her mouth was usually blocked from view, giving the girl a shy and timid air.
personality:
Ryuzu acted similarly to how her copies acted during the events of Arc 4, but more lively. She was a diligent girl who was always happy to give a helping hand to everyone in the Sanctuary who needed some help. Despite her timid and shy appearance, she was perfectly capable of forming bonds with people even as troublesome and hard-to-come-close-with as Beatrice.

According to Echidna, the girl's Od possessed great compatibility with the Sanctuary, making her a perfect candidate to use as the core for the Sanctuary's barrier. Sadly, however, her Od first needed to get accustomed to the environment. Before she could get the chance to do so, the Warlock of Melancholy began his attack on the Sanctuary, forcing the Witch of Greed to find other solutions. In such times of peril, Ryuzu showed immense courage and volunteered herself to physically merge her Od with the catalyst which would allow Echidna's plan to work. In her final moments, she confessed her fondness of Beatrice and merged with the mana crystal which acted as the catalyst for the barrier.
history:
In the years predating Hector's attack on the Sanctuary, Ryuzu was somehow saved by Echidna, who brought her to the Sanctuary in order to test her compatibility with the land.

On the day of Hector's attack, she established contact with a high-grade magic crystal, which allowed her Od to sync with the lands of the Sanctuary and set up an impenetrable barrier which effectively fended off the intruder. She spent the next four centuries encased in the same magic crystal, until Emilia overcame the three trials and lifted the barrier. Her current status or location remain unknown.

name_jp: ロウアン・セグムント

intro: Rowan Segmunt (ロウアン・セグムント) was a mercenary-for-hire from the Sacred Vollachia Empire, the former bodyguard of the Emperor of Vollachia, and the father of First ranking Divine General Cecilus Segmunt. Initially debuting as a minor character during one of Subaru's failed loops in Arc 7, he later reappeared with both a supportive and antagonistic role in Arc 8.
appearance:
Rowan was a tall and grizzled-looking middle-aged man with blue eyes, greying navy blue hair styled in a bun and a bit of shaven facial hair covering his face. He was a self-proclaimed rōnin and dressed like one, wearing a rather large kasa-style hat, a lilac kimono, a black cloak which was decorated with vertical stripes of gold color on the outside and a darker lilac on the inside, as well as hot pink sandals. He had a katana at his white waist, which had a black scabbard and a hot pink rayskin. Due to him being an alcoholic, he also stunk of booze.

As a zombie, Rowan possessed a vessel of earth, pale skin bereft of color, various cracks that ran across his body, pitch-black sclera, and radiant golden irises. He also discarded his hat.
personality:
Rowan was shown to have been quite a drunkard, usually spending his time and money in different pubs, drinking copious amounts of alcohol. He could hold his alcohol surprisingly well, as he was able to easily cut down Gaoran Peitiet despite being drunk. As expected from a mercenary, Rowan sought money, and he is prepared to do nearly anything for an appropriate compensation. However, Rowan was willing to offer praise to his opponents in battle. He was also noted to be rather rough but straight to the point. 

Rowan's dearest wish was to attain the Heavenly Sword, something he was obsessed with doing before, during, and after his time as a Stargazer. He lived a life full of bloodshed and slaughter with the hopes of attaining his long-cherished desire. Whether they were a stranger, a family member, or even himself, Rowan would unhesitatingly extinguish the life of anyone standing in his way if it had allowed him to proceed further on the path to the Heavenly Sword, and even his own son believed that he did not have any human emotion left within him. As his son was reaching the Heavenly Sword, Rowan was even willing to tempt him to slay the emperor so that the entire country would become his enemy, intent on having his son polish his sword skills with the endless assault of the numerous soldiers coming at him without end. He was even willing to extinguish his own life and become an undead to use the endless revival and a worthy enemy to polish his skills and reach the Heavenly Sword himself once he believed it was achievable for him again.

Due to his goal of reaching the Heavenly Sword, Rowan also believed that he was born in the wrong era. He had even pondered about life during the era of the Great Calamity, when all things feared the Witch of Envy. Likewise, he was also of the belief that chaos and disaster should be widespread, as such an environment was ideal for improving his own skill. As such, he did not care whether or not a country would fall, and he would only focus on his own goals.
history:
In the distant past, Rowan fervently desired to improve his skills with the sword to attain the Heavenly Sword. With his sword, he systematically slayed those who sought to improve their skills like him, formidable witchbeasts, the people in villages destroyed by witchbeasts, scourges who terrorized others, and saintly people that provided charity, producing few results. He then studied and learned techniques from sword schools, eventually going on to murder their heads and attempt to combine all their techniques together, but he abandoned this path too when it threatened the balance of his own skills. Striding on a trail of blood and failing to achieve the deep-rooted conviction he obsessed over, right when Rowan began to contemplate suicide, he was chosen to become a Stargazer and was bestowed with the commandment to produce a being who could reach the Heavenly Sword.

Rowan believed he may have been able to achieve his commandment by producing a being qualified to attain the Heavenly Sword, but he gave up on the path of fostering and growing hidden talent. He continued to butcher person after person in hopes of achieving his goal. However, once Rowan came to the conclusion that he could not reach it, he determined that his progeny should be the one to do so. Over the next several years, after much trial and error of raising eight children and murdering them when they were not talented enough, Cecilus, a transcendental being with the potential to grasp the Heavenly Sword, was born. Rowan determined that his commandment was fulfilled with Cecilus's birth and was then freed from his role as a Stargazer. Because he had spent his prime years to create Cecilus, he felt the conviction to end his own life again when he lost sight of his goal once more. However, Cecilus clutched his father's finger, making his thoughts disappear. At that moment, Rowan realized that if a baby so small could climb the stairs of the Heavenly Sword, an old swordsman could also tiptoe across the stairs. Forgetting his sorrows, he began to chase the Heavenly Sword once again.

A couple of months following the Imperial Selection Ceremony and the failed uprising at the Gladiator Island Ginunhive, Rowan acted as Emperor Vincent Vollachia's bodyguard. At the time, High Count Gaoran Peitiet orchestrated an attack on the Crystal Palace, using the absence of the First-Class Generals and Lupugana's weakened defenses to his advantage–however, to no avail. With his forces being swiftly defeated by a retaliating force led by then-Third-Class General Zikr Osman, the High Count was then killed by Rowan, who deflected his halberd strike aimed at the emperor's chest, and diagonally slashed Gaoran, ending his life then and there.

At some point during Vincent's reign, Rowan attempted to convince Cecilus to murder Vincent in order for the Imperial Army to perpetually chase after him and hone his sword skills in a state of turbulent chaos on the border of life and death. Cecilus, however, refused this offer because it was something that only a villain would do, told Vincent of Rowan's plans, and endeavored to slay his own father on the emperor's behalf. Gravely injured from his son's attack, Rowan promised that when Cecilus reached the Heavenly Sword, he would come to kill the Blue Lightning. This proposal caused Cecilus to turn a blind eye to Rowan's survival, dropping him in a river to allow his escape. Following this incident, Rowan continued to hone his skills with the hope that, one day, he could cut down his son. This eventually led to him becoming a mercenary, and a bounty was put on his head.
abilities_text:
Master Swordsman: Rowan was very skilled with his katana, having been mentioned by the barista to be by far the strongest individual from the pub Subaru and Flop found him. Subaru also noted that Rowan's sword technique was similar to that of a martial art style known as "iai", a real life Japanese-specific martial art that involves quickly drawing one's blade to attack and then immediately resheathing it right after. In his earlier days, Rowan frequented many schools of swordsmanship and attempted to blend the techniques together with his own swordsmanship, but he ultimately abandoned doing this when it threatened his balance as a swordsman; regardless, due to this experience, he is a master of numerous sword styles and has masterfully blended them to improve on his own skill. After becoming an undead and fighting with Yorna Mishigure, his skill with the blade improved dramatically, leaving even his son impressed. It should be noted that his skill could be considered the peak of what an ordinary person can achieve without being what Rowan considers “transcendental”.
Cloud Cutting (雲切, Kumokiri): Rowan could use a technique called Cloud Cutting, a powerful slash of the sword so lightning-fast that it leaves no sound behind and creates a force that can rise to the sky, literally allowing it to cleave clouds in two. For people who lack uncommon courage, the sheer strength of the technique is enough to make them feel as if their own flesh has been cleaved. Rowan created the technique himself, having spent his lifetime to devise it. Although considered something of a parlor trick by other practitioners of the blade, it is still capable of slashing at aerial opponents.

Excellent Teaching Abilities: While Rowan's skill with the blade was top-class, he was also an extremely good tutor who was capable of producing beings with extreme skills with the blade.

Equipment: Rowan wielded a katana called the Onibami (オニバミ, Onibami). It was unnamed in the light novel.

intro: Serena Dracroy (セリーナ・ドラクロイ) is a High Countess hailing from the Sacred Vollachia Empire. She is one of the most prominent nobles in the Empire, and she helped Priscilla Barielle into the Empire following the events of Arc 5. She played an important role in The Tale of the Scarlet Princess. She played a supporting role in Arc 7 and Arc 8.
appearance: Serena is a tall woman with a stocky physique. Her hair is of rust red color, and she has a big scar on the left side of her face, which she received from an assassin sent to kill her in the past. She bears a long coat as her nobles' attire, but she prefers to place it atop her shoulders rather than wearing it normally.
personality: The embodiment of the word fierce, Serena is a bold woman that talks with a kick to her voice. She is strong, prideful, and enjoys talking with others, and by her own claim, she is greedy when it comes to attaining victory. She is fierce, progressive, and courageous, and when necessary, she would even snap at her emperor, and she is smart, quickly able to discern things from minimal information. Though she typically assumes an approachable demeanor, during stressful situations, such as being held at wand-point by Ram, she remains calm and composed, and during battle situations, she remains wary and keeps her guard up, and she will not hesitate to cut down an unarmed man depending on the circumstances. She is also rather prideful of her Flying Dragon Squadron, to the point that their removal from the Imperial Army due to a farce schemed by the emperor led her to joining the rebel army during the Imperial Civil War in order to get back at him.
history:
Once Upon a Time in Lugunica II
When she was a teenager, Serena became the head of her family. Her business required her to travel to the Kingdom of Lugunica, where she sought to resolve a dispute. However, assassins were sent to follow her to Lugunica in a targeted attempt to kill her. Before she could be killed, she was saved by several people, among them Roswaal L. Mathers, who found out that the assassins were sent by her father, Galahau Dracroy, who wanted revenge for losing his position. In the resulting conflict, she received her characteristic scar from one of the assassins. Upon defeating three of the assassins and convincing the fourth to turn against them for his survival, she would eventually return to the Empire, where she confronted her father. In the resulting conflict, it is said that Galahau carved a large scar onto her face, but she ultimately proved victorious and proceeded to burn him alive, which led her to be known as the "Scorching Lady"; because she received her scar from one of the assassins who attempted to murder her, the extent to which this story is true is unknown. Sometime after these events, Jorah Pendleton helped her bring her family together as she was having a hard time doing so by herself. 

Sometime later, one of her subordinates, Miles, brought Flop and Medium O'Connell back to the domain with him, and they befriended Serena, viewing her as a benefactor. Some years after Flop and Medium befriended Balleroy Temeglyph when he decided to start raising the flying dragon Carillon, the two decided to depart from Serena's domain to fulfill their goal of "revenge". Balleroy opted to stay in Serena's domain and became one of her subordinates alongside Miles.

The Tale of the Scarlet Princess
Seven years before the main story, Serena sent her servants Balleroy and Miles to the Pendleton Estate in order to invite Jorah and his wife, Priscilla, to the Gladiator Island Ginunhive. While they were there, the gladiators attempted to spark a revolution that would render the island independent from the mainland, which later ended up failing thanks to the intervention of the Imperial Army. After the group left Ginunhive and returned to Serena's estate, Priscilla thanked her for the invitation in the stead of her resting husband.

At an unknown point in time after Jorah's execution, Serena ordered Balleroy and Miles to look for Priscilla, as there was a rumor going around about some bandits who kidnapped a girl looking like her. The duo successfully found her and managed to bring her to the estate. Afterwards, Serena found a way to smuggle Priscilla out of the Empire and into the Kingdom of Lugunica.

Undead Busters
After Medium became Vincent Vollachia's empress consort, she sought marital advice from her, Yorna Mishigure, and Madelyn Eschart to visit her. Before long, Cecilus Segmunt's party returned to Garkla, intending to speak with Vincent about how to handle Volcas.
abilities_text:
Excellent Strategist: Serena has shown to be an excellent tactician during battle. During the Battle for the Imperial Capital, she kept her allegiance hidden from the heads of state and claimed that she would not participate in the rebellion or the army so that she could catch them off guard and act as a trump card for the rebels, and during Defense of Garkla, she easily outsmarted the enemy commander and was able to fully counter his sneak attack.

Flying Dragon Squadron (飛竜隊, Hiryūtai): The Flying Dragon Squadron is an attack force owned by Serena. It is comprised of an elite group of flying dragons and dragon riders that possess complete mastery over the air, and their strength is the reason the Dracroy Domain is revered in Vollachia. The current squadron under Serena is said to be the strongest it has ever been.

Equipment: Serena keeps a sword at her hip.

relatives: Unnamed parents (deceased) ; Zoey (older sister)
intro: Tanza (タンザ) is a servant of Yorna Mishigure who once resided within Chaosflame's Crimson Lapis Castle. She plays a supporting role in Arc 7 and Arc 8.
appearance: Tanza is a young girl with pale skin, purple eyes, and tan hair. Due to her lineage as a deer human, she sports a pair of antlers and has one decoration below each antler. She dons a blue and purple kimono with a floral pattern with its collar, sleeves, and bow being a bright shade of green, reminiscent of Yorna's kimono.
personality:
Tanza was initially presented as a doll-like girl who does not show her emotions. Despite her cold exterior, she holds immense love for Yorna and is herself cared for by the residents of Chaosflame. She often appears reserved, but she is able to understand the thoughts and feelings of those around her. Although she mostly shows respect to the people around her, Tanza is straightforward, supportive, and honest, to the point of speaking bluntly when asserting her opinion. In reality, though she is highly intelligent for her age, she has always been highly self-deprecating and often thinks of herself as selfish, bearing no confidence in herself. At times, she felt glad that it is not in her nature to show her emotions on her face, and because of the way that her country stole the lives of her family away, she came to hate the Empire.

She has also shown great loyalty to those she follows. For Yorna, who she is highly protective of, she was willing to go against someone as dangerous as Abel and even set a large number of citizens on his party so that they would leave and not involve Yorna in his war, willing to give up her own life so that Yorna would not be punished or involved, and she later entered an extremely dangerous battlefield just to reunite with her. She even displayed her deep loyalty to Natsuki Subaru during the events in Ginunhive, willing to sacrifice her life to make sure he lived. Likewise, despite her own retorts to his apparent non-serious behavior, she did not abide by others mocking him, and she often sulked when he unknowingly upset her, displayed a competitive streak with Beatrice when it came to wanting to assist him, and was even willing to threaten anyone who she thought wanted to hurt him. Thanks to her travels with Subaru, she has been able to gain more confidence in herself, to the point that it shocked Yorna when they reunited, and despite rarely showing emotion on her face or camaraderie, she seemed to be proud to be a member of the Pleiades Battalion.
history:
The birthplace of Tanza and her sister, Zoey, was ravaged and destroyed by bandits who sought to earn profits when the spread of a superstition claiming that boiling the antlers of deer humans could create a panacea. Their parents were murdered by the bandits, and the two of them barely escaped with their lives. From that point onward, the sisters lived a harsh life of suffering while attempting to evade those who sought to kill them for their antlers or to prey on their weakness, as has been customary for the Vollachia Empire. Zoey put herself through harsh circumstances to even obtain a plate of soup for her and Tanza, who detested her reliance on her older sister and felt the desire to end her own life. After they had continued to flee for a long time, the two of them eventually heard rumors of a paradise called Chaosflame. Despite Tanza's doubts toward its existence, Zoey managed to lead her there. Yorna greeted the sisters when they arrived at Chaosflame and embraced them. Although Zoey had not cried when her parents died, when a spectacle was made of her so she could obtain soup, or when Tanza levied curses towards her, she began to sob as she embraced Yorna. Tanza, too, cried at this scene, thinking that she must never lose Yorna or her paradise.

In Chaosflame, the sisters were provided with suitable meals and a bedroom. Being the most hardworking of Yorna's servants, Zoey carried out her responsibilities dutifully. However, two years after arriving at Chaosflame, while Zoey was guiding demi-human tribes into the city, she passed a fortress of Imperial Soldiers who were conducting a military exercise. They attacked the demi-humans under the guise that they were potential enemies. Zoey was unfortunately be murdered and tortured for sport by the soldiers, who would then disgrace her corpse. Following this incident, Tanza, who had begun to hate the Empire, requested to take on Zoey's old responsibilities, which Yorna accepted. She was also comforted by Yorna while feeling rage, sorrow, and anguish stemming from Zoey's murder, while Yorna told her that she also hated the Empire.

As a direct result of Zoey's death, Yorna attacked the fortress and killed a majority of the soldiers there for revenge, and when a few of them escaped, she carried out a full-scale rebellion against the Empire to retrieve the escaped soldiers. During this rebellion, Madelyn Eschart arrived at Chaosflame and attempted to hold Tanza hostage, though this ultimately failed with Yorna's use of the Soul Marriage Technique.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
At present, it is unclear how strong Tanza is without her being subject to outside techniques. However, with the enhancement she received from Yorna's Soul Marriage, Tanza had the power to defeat large-sized witchbeasts. Furthermore, when her power was increased with Subaru's Cor Leonis, she was the strongest combatant within the Pleiades Battalion, able to defeat common undead with her feet and bare fists and create shockwaves that broke through the bastions of Lupugana reinforced with earth magic, as well as the walls of the Prime Minister's mansion that were reinforced with a Divine Protection.

Physical Traits/Flow Method
Augmented Physical Capabilities: Tanza typically fights by using the physical might given to her by Yorna's Soul Marriage Technique, and instead of using weapons, she usually uses her hands and feet in combat.
