intro: Theresia van Astrea (テレシア・ヴァン・アストレア) was Wilhelm van Astrea's wife and the previous generation's Sword Saint who fought and single handedly brought an end to the Demi-Human War roughly 40 years before the start of the main story. Though a minor character overall, she is pivotal to the character arcs of her relatives and later serves as a secondary antagonist in Arc 5. She also plays major roles in the Sword Demon Trilogy.
appearance:
She was fairly short and had long red hair with flowers attached to it, tying it in two ponytails, while a big part of her hair stayed loose. She had blue eyes and a fair complexion. In her free time, she wore a long green and white off-the-shoulder dress with shoulder straps decorated with flowers. Theresia's common outfit had white trimmings and pink patches on the dress in a form of bows, with one of them being on her chest. She also used to wear small red shoes.

When operating as a knight of the Royal Guard, she used to wear a short white dress with armor and a white cloak over it, with a pair of dark purple gloves and tights of the same color. In her uniform, she wore high white boots and tied her hair in a high ponytail.
personality:
Theresia was a very social, open-minded, overly kind person who often found herself very worried about others, to the point that she would push aside her own personal feelings in favor of others'. She loved flowers, and she cared very deeply about life, to the point that despite being the next Sword Saint, she could not bring herself to raise a sword to harm another. She was even fearful of her own ability to harm others. Thanks to one of her Divine Protections, these feelings were even greater amplified, and if she ever did hurt someone, she would cry and apologize profusely for having done so, even if it was reflexive. Oftentimes, she would find herself confused as to why she was chosen as the Sword Saint, and those feelings only grew over time. During the era of the Demi-Human War, these feelings were particularly relevant, as despite others wanting her to take up the sword and fight, she could not do so, resulting in the deaths of several family members who fought in her place, much to her terrible sadness, causing her to cry often and lose her smile for years.

After she met Wilhelm, her feelings began to change. She began to smile more often, looking forward to meeting him, despite his rude demeanor. Aware though she was that she had fallen in love at first sight, she did not fight these feelings, and as she met with him, she found herself influenced by the way he diligently devoted himself to the sword, often asking why he did so. Eventually, sometime after he claimed his reason to fight was to protect others, she started reflecting on the reason she was given the title of Sword Saint again. It wasn't until she learned that Wilhelm was in danger that she finally found the resolve to raise her sword and do harm unto others: to protect Wilhelm. Despite this, she effectively pushed aside all of her feelings and took part in the war, despite the fact that doing so hurt her terribly. This said, when Wilhelm took her reason to wield the sword away from her, she finally started acting like her true self in front of others again: cheerful, easily flustered, strong willed, annoyed by others' when they acted rudely or foolishly, jealous to and pouty of matters revolving around Wilhelm, who she trusted and loved implicitly.
history:
Sword Demon Love Song
Theresia was born to her father, Veltol Astrea, and her mother, Tishua Astrea. Since she was born with a Divine Protection, she refused to use a sword, fearing that she would hurt others. However, at the age of twelve, she obtained the powers of the Sword Saint from her uncle, Fribal van Astrea. Eventually, House Remendis offered Carol Remendis to attend her. Though initially she found herself dismayed by Theresia's attitude towards wielding a sword, after an incident where Carol found herself swiftly defeated by Theresia and caused the Sword Saint to cry, the two became much closer. In the following year, the Demi-Human War broke out, and in the year that followed, Theresia was taken to her first battle, where she was expected to draw her sword for the first time. However, she could not bring herself to do it, caring far too much for life to bring harm, and as a result, one of her brothers died, leaving Theresia heartbroken and unable to smile anymore. As the years passed, her other brothers and even her uncle were killed during the war, wounding her heart further, and because she didn't have the heart to raise her sword, Carol would take her place in assisting Roswaal J. Mathers throughout the war.

One day, Carol told her that instead of being stuck inside and having to deal with people trying to convince her to join the army, she should go outside somewhere, leading to Theresia finding an isolated spot in the slums where she could be by herself, and eventually, she planted flowers there. Later on, she one day met another young man who had come to this place to train on his own. Intrigued by the young man and having fallen for him at first sight, she spoke with him, showed him her flowers, and asked if he liked them, to which he replied negatively. Annoyed by this, she scared him off. Despite this, when Carol came to pick her up later that day, she was genuinely smiling, saying that she met a rude boy that day. For the next several weeks, the two continued to meet each other here, and Theresia would ask the same question, only to retrieve the same answer.

In the month following the Battle of Aihiya Swamp, during one of her meetings with the young man, they exchanged names for the first time, her lack of fear at hearing his name surprised him, and she asked for the reason he wielded his blade, to which he replied that it was all he had. After this, those two questions would be something she asked every time they met, each with the same answers. He continued to ignore this request and kept one with his duties and training, answering the very same questions from Theresia every time. Sometime after this, he met with Theresia again, where he was once again made to question why he wielded his sword, even though he claimed that he would continue to wield his sword, even if it caused him pain, and she hoped to him that he would find that reason one day. After the Invasion of the Royal Castle was over, he went to meet Theresia again, where Wilhelm claimed he no longer hated flowers, and his reason for the sword was to protect others. At some point during or after this time, she learned exactly who he was and even congratulated him.

Within the following year, she and Wilhelm would meet more often, using their sword and flowers as excuses to see each other. However, one day, after Wilhelm learned that his lands were in trouble, he walked towards the flower garden that night and spoke with Theresia, who had been there all day. After a conversation and walking back with her in the direction of the main road, she inspired him to fight, albeit unintentionally. Later, having been told by Carol that Wilhelm had gone on his own to fight for his lands, Theresia, for the first time, willingly picked up the sword, and with the resolve to protect Wilhelm, she left with the Zergev Squadron to retrieve him. Upon arriving, Theresia began slaughtering the demi-human attackers who destroyed the Trias Domain, despite the immense heartbreaking pain it caused her, and after racking up over 1000 kills, everyone returned to the Royal Capital. A few weeks later, the two confronted each other in the flower garden, where she swiftly and easily defeated him. Saying that she would not return, she claimed to have found a reason to swing her sword, to protect others, and as she walked away, having borne a sad expression, Wilhelm claimed that he would take that sword away, as he regretted having given her a reason to have to swing her sword. Thanks to this, Wilhelm was not seen fighting with the Royal Army again until after the Demi-Human War was over.

Thanks to Theresia joining the war efforts, she was given the auxiliary Astrea Manor for her triumphs in the Battle of the Trias Domain, yet due to her fighting, she often did not find herself returning to the building. Though starting out on bad terms with Bordeaux Zergev, she fought together alongside him, and after two years, she managed to deal great damage to the Demi-Human Alliance, gathering more than ten thousand kills, much to her sadness. With the war over after Cragrell Dawson met with the king, Theresia was to be awarded for her contributions. After being given a ceremonial sword from Roswaal, she made her way to the ceremony hall, and soon after, Wilhelm, who had been training himself for two long years, appeared to challenge her. Happy to see him again and that he had gotten so strong, she displayed her immense strength to all of those present, completely erasing any doubts of her skills. However, she ultimately lost to Wilhelm. Claiming to be stronger than her, he said that she no longer had a reason to fight, that he would fight in her place in order to protect her. After sharing a kiss, he was reunited with the Zergev Squadron on one side and dealing with a pouting Theresia on the other, saying that he'd tell her he loved her when the mood hit him.

Sword Demon Love Story: Their Later Tale
Following the ceremony, Wilhelm was taken to the Prison Tower. Meanwhile, speaking with the king about her reward, she decided to use it to free Wilhelm, and after that, they made a deal that Theresia would be allowed to retire from the military if she managed to marry Wilhelm. Shortly afterward, she reunited with Wilhelm outside of the Prison Tower. After dragging him to her mansion and forcing him to take a bath, Wilhelm spoke with Carol and Grimm, the former of which lashed out at him, and he learned of her position as Theresia's attendant. After this, Theresia informed him that he was technically unemployed, leading to him to go and find a way to get his job back. While he was gone, Theresia prepared food for him, Grimm, and Carol for that night, which he saw when he returned to the mansion. In the conversation that followed, he told her about how the only person he talked to during the two years he was gone was Roswaal, who would often find him, and out of jealousy and irritation, she threw him to the ground and locked herself in her room. Upon Carol and Grimm's return to the mansion, Carol chided him and went to speak with Theresia while Wilhelm and Grimm finished all of the food that Theresia prepared.

The next day, after an argumentative breakfast with Carol and Grimm, Wilhelm informed Theresia of where he was going and left her breakfast. While he was gone, though still pouting about his interactions with Roswaal, she prepared food for the two of them. When he returned to the mansion, he told her about his returning to the army and for her not to go to the castle the next day. The next day, after Wilhelm left, Theresia found herself fretting over whether or not to go to the castle. As she did, Roswaal appeared, assuaged her jealous doubt, and decided to bring her to the castle. However, after Theresia arrived and saw what was going on, she chided the king for allowing this, and it was revealed that she would have been let go of her position if she married Wilhelm, much to everyone's but the king and Miklotov's shock. Wilhelm accepted this, and they embraced, Theresia calling him Wilhelm van Astrea.

Sword Demon Love Story: The Bride's Father
After the two decided to get married, Wilhelm and Theresia left for the Astrea Domain so that Wilhelm could ask her parents for her hand in marriage. After arriving there, Wilhelm was nervous to meet them, which made Theresia happy. Soon after, Veltol and Tishua arrived in the meeting room, and Veltol immediately put pressure on Wilhelm. The four sat down and spoke, Theresia talking about some things with her mother while Veltol decided to determine if Wilhelm was worthy of Theresia. Despite the man's apparent disapproval, Wilhelm was about to ask for Theresia's hand, but Veltol was quick to explode, resulting in him and Theresia getting into an argument. Tishua apologized for it and noticed his tea was empty, and though she was about to offer to refill it, Veltol did instead. However, Theresia stopped him, as Veltol had drugged his tea. Cornered, Veltol mentioned that it wasn't poison but a drug that made one lose control of their bladder, leading to Theresia snapping at him. After Tishua told him the way to the bathroom, she asked if Wilhelm would be able to adjust to their family, to which he answered by calling them mother and father and saying that it would probably be hard to get along with Veltol. Receiving a positive response from Tishua, he left to use the bathroom.

Sword Demon Love Story: Wedding Day
In the three months that followed, Theresia brought Wilhelm to meet her parents. However, thanks to Veltol, their upcoming wedding faced numerous setbacks and obstacles. Thanks to his interference, three days before their official wedding date, he used his authority to force the Zergev Squadron to patrol a few towns around the capital, knowing full well that it would take three days to accomplish. Suspicious that this was her father's fault, she asked Bordeaux to look into it. Later, despite her frustrations, Wilhelm decided to take on this challenge, and as he prepared to leave, Theresia, who had fixed him food for on the road, saw him off. Afterward, speaking with Bordeaux, he confirmed her suspicions, and she resolved to meet with and scold her father.

Two days later, she and Carol went to confront Veltol. When they met, Theresia was quick to chide her father for his actions, and she even threatened to leave House Astrea because of him. Even Carol and her mother joined in to chide him. However, she believed in Wilhelm, and she knew that he would arrive on time for their wedding, despite her father's meddling. The next day, wearing her wedding dress, she waited patiently for the return for the Zergev Squadron with Carol and her parents. Eventually, Bordeaux arrived and informed her of the squad's return, and soon after, her wedding took place. Despite Wilhelm being unable to clean himself off after the mess he went through, the wedding went off perfectly, and the two were married. In the month that followed, Veltol made numerous appearances, much to Theresia's frustration, and eventually, he even suggested going along on the honeymoon as well, leading to another argument. However, with help from Tishua, they were able to get him to leave. Given two months for their honeymoon, they prepared to leave, taking Carol as Theresia's attendant, and they decided to visit the cities to the south of the capital.

Sword Demon Love Story: Earth Dragon Capital, Flanders
After their marriage, Wilhelm and Theresia went on their honeymoon with Carol accompanying them, and they first visited Flanders, the Earth Dragon Capital, where Theresia was going to ride an earth dragon for the first time. After experiencing one for a moment, Carol interrupted them after Wilhelm got a little intimate with Theresia, to which Theresia scolded Carol. Though Carol was heavily reluctant, partially due to her own misgivings and Veltol's request to not let him take things too far with her, she entrusted Theresia to Wilhelm's care. As they rode atop one earth dragon, Theresia told Wilhelm about how the different species of earth dragons were named after flowers, which Wilhelm was curious about. As they rode, Wilhelm was reminded of his family, and after Theresia grabbed his attention, she described them to her. After a few hours time, Theresia improved her riding to the point that she surpassed Carol, and she and Carol ran around on their respective earth dragons. Wilhelm, watching them from a distance as a rancher watched approached him and said the earth dragon she was riding became attached to her. After he offered it to Wilhelm, he was told its name was Diana, which Wilhelm laughed at.

Sword Demon Love Story: Silver Flower Dance of Picoutatte
After leaving Flanders, because Theresia insisted they not visit her home in Hakuchuri, they made for Picoutatte, where her father was waiting, leading to another argument. However, with his reason for visiting to collect the present for his wife, they accompanied him to the Suwen Company. With Veltol asking Wilhelm and Carol to allow him and Theresia to shop together, they left to observe the town. Inside the shop, however, they were met by a disrespectful Stride Vollachia, who was targeting the Sword Saint. Leading Veltol to challenging him to a duel, he introduced Kurgan, who would serve as his champion, as Theresia had noticed Stride's apparent illness. After further insulting him, her, and Wilhelm, Veltol struck Stride for his remarks, leading Kurgan to ruthlessly beat him down and Stride to curse him. Taken to the hospital, she met with Wilhelm and was informed of Veltol's condition by the healer Garitch Fabless. Accordingly, the only way to remove the curse was to cut it off at the source. Soon after, Yaktol Suwen, who ran the shop, informed the group of the message given by the Stride that they would be waiting at a great bridge in Picoutatte's west district with the source of the curse. Impatient, Carol ran off with Yaktol in search of the man while Theresia resolved herself to go to the bridge with Wilhelm.

The next morning, Carol returned, unable to find Stride. After Yaktol then provided Wilhelm with his new sword that Veltol picked out for him, he and Theresia left for the bride where Stride and Kurgan were waiting. Despite Stride's annoyance with Wilhelm's appearance, Theresia challenged him, and the two chose their champions, Wilhelm and Kurgan, on their behalf. Stride was further annoyed at learning that the rumors of what happened at her ceremony were true and that Wilhelm showed as much dangerous fighting spirit as Kurgan. Soon after, the fight began on the bridge. Although both sides took great damage, Stride decided to step in when he realized that Kurgan was in danger. Not wanting to lose his pawn, he declared the duel his loss, tossed them one of his rings, and then used something to turn the bridge into sand, dropping everyone on it into the river and allowing for him and Kurgan to escape. Destroying the ring and allowing others to help the people out of the water, they left for the hospital where Carol informed them that Veltol was better, and Wilhelm was admitted. At some point after this, she informed her mother, who decided to visit Picoutatte herself, and she and Carol went and bought the accessory that Veltol wanted to buy her as a present. However, after getting into an argument with her father later, she went to go meet her mother alongside Carol.

Sword Demon Love Story: The Other Side of the Honeymoon
Following the Silver Flower Dance of Picoutatte, Theresia and Carol wandered the streets of Picoutatte while Wilhelm and Veltol were recovering from their injuries. As they walked, they came across Garitch and spoke with him. Theresia apologized to him for having destroyed the bridge and creating more work for him, but he waved it off. Still worried about it, Carol tried to pin the blame on the one responsible for the challenge while Garitch said that Veltol could pay for the damages and treatment and nobody would be upset. However, he also asked her if she could get Veltol to reconsider his recommendation of Garitch to the Royal Capital, as he did not want to go to the capital since the mother of his son was there. Though he believed that it would probably be for the best that he didn't go, Theresia claimed that happiness was up to the individual to choose, which ultimately cemented that Garitch did not want to go, saying it wasn't the right time yet, and the girls left his going to the capital to Veltol. Afterward, they asked about the mother, which he described, leading to Garitch telling her that someone so immoral should not be recommended and telling her that Wilhelm was fastidious, so she didn't have to worry, triggering an emotional response from Carol. After he recommended the sherbet, he left, and the two had a bowl for themselves.

Great Conquest
In the years after Heinkel's birth, Theresia remained outside of the Royal Guard while Wilhelm served as its captain. Eventually, Heinkel joined the ranks of the knights, married Louanna Hartley, and their son, Reinhard, was born. After five years had passed since Reinhard's birth, the Kingdom of Lugunica's effort to bring down the White Whale, the Great Conquest, was being prepared for. Since Wilhelm was tasked with another mission, Theresia took the place of Heinkel, who refused to join the subjugation, to lead a group of knights to defeat the witchbeast once and for all. However, during the Great Conquest, she lost her powers as the Sword Saint, encountered Pandora, and passed away.
abilities_text:
Divine Protection (加護, Kago): Theresia possessed two Divine Protections: the Divine Protection of the Death God (死神の加護, Shinigami no Kago) she was born with and the Divine Protection of the Sword Saint (剣聖の加護, Kensei no Kago), which she gained when she was twelve. With the former, slashes imbued with the Divine Protection's power left curse wounds that were unable to be healed. It also increased the closer she was to the target and she could even reopen wounds others have if they were close enough and were originally inflicted by her. If the wound expanded, so did the effect of the protection. If the wound was a light cut on the finger and the target cut off said finger, this new wound became the target of the protection. The effects disappeared if she died.

thumb|209x209px|Theresia's swordsmanship.
 Sword Saint (剣聖, Kensei): The power of the Sword Saint gifted her with inhuman intuition and insight while maximizing her latent swordsmanship talent and knowledge of combat towards a level that only a few could reach. This allowed Theresia to break down any kind of technique or attack directed at her while simultaneously showing gaps in them for the most optimal counter. These manifested as spectral "white lines" that only she could see, which were implied to be guidance from the "Sword God". However, if someone possessed equal or greater skill relative to hers, the lines would distort, making her opponent's attack paths difficult to read.

Master Swordsman: Theresia was highly skilled at using the sword. Contrast to Wilhelm's defter and measured style, her swordplay was more momentum based, employing a lot of acrobatic flourish. It was described as if she was doing a beautiful deadly dance.

Equipment: As the Sword Saint, Theresia wielded the Dragon Sword Reid (龍剣レイド, Ryūken Reido). The sword could only be drawn against opponents it deemed worthy for it to be used against, and it was later given to her grandson, Reinhard. After her death and being revived as a puppet of the Witch Cult, Theresia used a different sword in combat.

intro: Volcanica (ボルカニカ), also known as the Divine Dragon, is a key figure in the sealing of the Witch of Envy 400 years ago. Mentioned throughout the series, it is the guardian of the Kingdom of Lugunica and is worshiped by its inhabitants as it is the very symbol of hope and trust for the entire nation. It plays both a minor antagonistic and supporting role in Arc 6 and an antagonistic role in Arc 9. It also played a pivotal supporting role in Sword Demon Battle Ballad.
appearance:
Volcanica is an enormous Dragon who is covered in shiny pale blue scales which are said to gleam like jewels and seem sharper than a forged treasured sword. Its thick paws are equipped with black, rock-like claws. Volcanica's face greatly resembles that of an earth dragon with two large milky-white horns sticking out of each side of its head. Finally, Volcanica has a pair of intelligent looking gold eyes which emit a wise and awe-inspiring aura. Its presence is so great that one feels like he isn't even allowed to breathe without the Divine Dragon's permission. Another notable feature is the presence of a mysterious white scar located directly underneath Volcanica's jaw. When touched by someone other than Volcanica, the Divine Dragon will fall in a state of shock and will desperately try to kill whoever touched it. 

In its crouched position, it is said to be about 16 meters in height, but its actual size is unknown, though it is much larger than Valgren who was about 10 meters tall.
personality:
Volcanica was described as a benevolent and wise entity, one which defended Lugunica from many threats in the past and brought peace to the Kingdom. It bore a strong envy towards those with unrealized potential. Having been born among the race of what could be considered the absolute strongest, it highly esteemed the potential held within humans as radiant as they could grow and develop themselves as they reach for their goals, thus validating their existences.

In complete contrast to its reputation, by the events of Arc 6, Volcanica has fallen into a dragonhusk state, operating purely on instinct. Beatrice and Eridna speculated that Volcanica in its current state exerted about 10% of its former strength even though its condition is nothing physical, but rather a "spiritual death". The Divine Dragon has lived for so long that most things have lost its meaning, though it still feels obliged to uphold the covenants it forged with Dragon Kingdom of Lugunica and Flugel respectively. Before falling into a dragonhusk state, Volcanica was mentioned to be a cynic by Shaula. During its fight with Valgren, about four decades before the main story, it was mentioned to feel pity for the state in which the Dragon had ended up in, implying it had a strong sense of pride.

After temporarily awakening in Arc 6, Volcanica has shown to be rather fond of those it has formed a good relationship with, such as Satella, Flugel, or Farsale. Likewise, it even hesitated to harm Satella as she started to become the well-known Witch of Envy. It also feels tremendous regret for allowing itself to falter in the past and allowing such a tremendous disaster to occur on its watch, and upon remembering the disaster, Volcanica was likely to become violent and agitated. When coming into contact with Felt on her trip to the Pleiades Watchtower with Meili Portroute and several other members of her camp, it became docile and willingly abided by her requests because it conflated her with Farsale.

During the Arc 9 loop, Aldebaran used his Book of the Dead on Volcanica, filling its empty dragonhusk with his own consciousness and effectively turning it into a second version of himself. Due to Volcanica's latent soul and vessel differing from that of Aldebaran's, the Dragon "Aldebaran" had a more optimistic outlook and other personality differences compared to its counterpart and retained residual feelings acquired from its time as "Volcanica". The strongest of these feelings were its favor for Farsale and dislike of Reid, and the remainder of it was blurred. With its personality differences, it was able to determine the cause behind Heinkel Astrea's unusual durability and piece together the truth behind Clind's abilities, whereas the original Al did not reach either conclusion immediately. It was strongly attached to Felt and also conflated her with Farsale, maintaining the same attachment Volcanica's dragonhusk exhibited towards her. As such, its loyalty towards Al and Felt was split half and half. In the end, Aldebaran's overwriting of Volcanica's dragonhusk was undone alongside the rest of Arc 9's events, returning the Divine Dragon to its normal self before it was ever hijacked.

Volcanica speaks in a deific manner favoring the archaic pronouns thou (汝, nanji) and mineself (我, ware) and its voice conveys its omnipotence. Its gender is also unknown, as it uses a neutral pronoun (我, waga). When Al's consciousness overwrote it, Volcanica spoke exactly like he did.
history:
Great Calamity Era
Volcanica is a Divine Dragon who several centuries ago made a covenant with Farsale Lugunica to help safeguard and guide the country in times of turmoil. For this reason, it is worshiped as a national deity and became the symbol of Lugunica's Royal Family.

Over 400 years ago, Sekhmet drove Volcanica past the Great Waterfall just so she could rest. The two eventually had a major fight, and at its conclusion, Sekhmet fell to her death from the Great Waterfall. At an unknown point in time, it also fought against Reid Astrea, who wanted to eat its flesh, and their bout, Reid left Volcanica with a wound on its neck, which later became its inverted scale. According to Echidna, at the time of their travels, her party needed to keep their identities secret. However, at one point during their travels, they ended up in the country of Magrizza. Despite attempting to hide their identities, Farsale declared his own name, resulting in a noble discovering them and inviting them to a banquet of nobles. The nation's crown prince, who was also in attendance at the banquet, became enamored by Echidna and went behind the scenes to arrange a marriage between the two of them, with Echidna's party going along with them after they were split from their capable fighters. However, at some point, for reasons yet to be explained, Reid and Volcanica went on a rampage, ultimately resulting in the marriage being cancelled and them being driven from the nation. It was a short time later that they learned that the Black Serpent destroyed Magrizza. According to Echidna, it was likely that they were being chased by the Black Serpent. Later, Volcanica sealed Echidna off in her tomb within the Sanctuary as a deterrent to Satella.

Volcanica was said to have met with Reid and the Sage in Flanders. Around the same time, the Divine Dragon supposedly used an unknown type of blessing ability to create earth dragons. When the Great Calamity began, the three heroes set their goals on defeating the rampaging Witch of Envy, who mercilessly killed thousands and thousands of innocents and toppled one country after another. After realizing they were unable to kill her, Volcanica and the others managed to defeat her and seal her away in the Augria Sand Dunes at the very east of Dragon Kingdom of Lugunica. 

At some point in the era 400 years ago, Volcanica's dragonkin, Clind, whose time of creation is unknown, began to serve Roswaal L. Mathers. Volcanica has also seems to have history with Patrasche as well, even knowing her name despite her being named in the present day. 

Sword Demon Battle Ballad
Roughly 40 years before the Royal Selection, and about a year after the end of the Demi-Human War, Stride Vollachia, with the skull of a three-horned dragonkin, summoned Valgren, who proceeded to ravage through Picoutatte. When Gionis Lugunica arrived at the city, Volcanica arrived not long afterwards, possessed by Clind. Recognizing that Valgren was a mere dragonhusk, Volcanica scorched the Black Dragon to nothing with its purifying breath, healed all of the citizens and combatants who had been injured, and put out the fires that were spreading through the city, confirming the validity of the four centuries long covenant that had been into question before.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
As the Divine Dragon and the safeguard of the Kingdom of Lugunica, Volcanica has considerable power. It was able to defeat Sekhmet, the second strongest Witch after Satella, and is stated to even be able to put up a competitive fight against Reinhard while the latter uses the Dragon Sword. While being 90% in a hibernating state and operating purely on instincts, Volcanica was easily able to overwhelm Emilia and her Ice Soldiers, scorch away Satella's Shadows within seconds, and contend with the full power of both Roswaal and Clind at the same time, emerging completely unscathed in a practically one-sided battle. Even against other Dragons, such as Valgren, Volcanica’s strength is on another level. According to Garfiel Tinzel, its strength and presence are significantly greater than that of the Cloud Dragon Mezoreia.

Physical Traits/Flow Method
Overwhelming Physical Might: Although it is unclear if Volcanica uses the Flow Method or even needs it, all of its physical capabilities are immeasurably powerful. The slightest of attacks can easily crush a man and most likely kill them.

Talons and Fangs: Volcanica's talons are said to be much harder and much sharper than the majority of swords in existence. Likewise, its fangs are said to be even sharper than that, and combined with its jaw strength, anything bitten by the Divine Dragon is unlikely to survive. There also seems to be power embedded in its fangs, even when removed from its body. When Aldebaran used one of them, he was able to easily destroy certain devices in Lugunica's Prison Tower with seemingly minimal effort. However, what exactly this power is or what it does precisely is unknown.

Wings: On Volcanica's back is a massive pair of wings that it uses both for its flight and in offense. By unfurling and flapping its wings, Volcanica can unleash a powerful gust of blade-like winds that can carve through a large area at once.

Tail: Volcanica can also use its long and powerful tail to attack. A single swing is enough to cause great damage to the environment around it, and most people would not survive being struck by it.

Dragon Scales: Volcanica's scales are immeasurably hard, surpassing even the toughness of diamonds. As a Dragon, these scales provide Volcanica an incredible physical defense, and the only known weapon said to be able to ignore this defense is the Dragon Sword Reid, according to Clind. Even the might of the Sword Demon, one of the most renowned swordsmen in the world, cannot easily pierce its scales.

Dragon Halo: The halo atop Volcanica's head provides it with immeasurable magical defense. Spells of the Al level are incapable of bypassing its defense, and even with Roswaal L. Mathers using his multiplefold magic with multiple Al level spells combined together, up to five simultaneous spells, he could not injure Volcanica at all, and it always came unscathed. Like with its scales, the only known weapon that can ignore this halo is the Dragon Sword.

Magic
Divine Mana: Volcanica has an enormous amount of mana in its body, and it is even able to "cleanse" the world with it. By exerting its mana, it is able to extinguish great flames or heal the injured all at once over an area at least as wide as the city of Picoutatte. Likewise, though it is not seen doing so of its own will, it is capable of casting incredibly powerful magic that would otherwise be inaccessible to most, and the sheer power of the magic that it can cast is much greater when compared to a human's.

Dragon Breath: The Divine Dragon's breath, which when let loose, rushes straight towards its target and envelops it in a white and bluish light. When the light envelops its opponents, they are instantly turned into dust, as if they had been purified. It is so powerful and hot that it instantly destroyed Emilia's Ice Soldiers, which were said to be tougher than steel, and, according to Emilia, it even killed sound itself. Using this, even the Blight Dragon Valgren was completely erased from existence. It can also change the type of breath it has depending on the circumstances; it has shown to be able to generate a large watery mist from its breath which can then be used to freeze its wet targets. Likewise, it can generate both fire and water together in this manner to create a devastating shockwave with immense destructive force.

Flight: As a Dragon, Volcanica is capable of flight. According to Emilia's observations, however, it actually uses the ability through magical energy rather than its wings which help it to fly. By channeling magical power throughout its body, Volcanica can make itself float in a similar way as Puck and Roswaal do. It uses its pairs of wings to help it glide and control the direction of its flight in a manner similar to a rudder.

Other
Elemental Manipulation: Although the extent of the manipulation is unknown, Volcanica seems to be able to manipulate multiple various elements. It is unknown whether this is merely a trait of its as a Dragon or if this is magic. By manipulating the wind, Volcanica can keep any person who rides its back from being affected by the wind as it moves, and it can fasten them in place so that they do not fall off due to its immense speed. It also makes it to where being at higher altitudes than the body is meant to handle becomes moot for the people on its back. It has also shown to be able to generate massive fists made of earth and control them with ease.

Spatial Rupturing: Volcanica is able to twist space and cause it to rupture, destroying anything or anyone caught in it, completely ignoring defenses. Volcanica can seemingly do this at will, with immense accuracy, and without warning.

Life Creation: Through unknown methods, Volcanica was apparently responsible for the creation of earth dragons. However, at one point, it was mentioned that they were made via a blessing.

intro: Zabinel Lugunica (ザビーネル・ルグニカ) was the First Prince of the Dragon Kingdom of Lugunica. He has yet to appear in any side stories or flashbacks, and he was the first to fall ill to the mysterious plague that struck the Royal Family. He was the first to die to the disease, roughly a month after contracting it.
appearance: Zabinel has yet to appear in the story, but as a member of the Royal Family it can be assumed he had gold hair and red eyes.
personality: Due to not appearing in any of the side stories, flashbacks or in the main story, it's unknown what kind of man Zabinel Lugunica was.
history:
While he was still alive, Zabinel held hunting festivals at the Hyclara Plateau. Bikram Edditz was the last known person to have achieved the highest record at these festivals. Around seven years ago, he was set to be engaged to the granddaughter of Azah Febry, a member of the Council of Wise Men.

First Prince Zabinel Lugunica was the first one to have been fallen ill with the mysterious illness that soon buried the entire Royal Family of Lugunica. First being thought to be the result of the First Prince overworking himself, Zabinel soon became more and more ill. Roughly a month following his initial symptoms and becoming bedridden, Zabinel was the first of the Royal Family of Lugunica to succumb to the unexplained illness. intro: Tholter Weasily (トルタ・ウィズリー) was a common soldier of the Royal Army and a close friend of Grimm Fauzen. He died early on in the Demi-Human War at the Battle of Castour Field.

His and Grimm's first battle was the Battle of Redonas Plateau. Tholter handled the events during and after better emotionally than Grimm did. Tragically, Tholter would become one of many causalities of the Royal Army at the Battle of Castour Field where the main army would fall to demi-human forces' large-scale magic after choosing to obey the orders of Grimm's old squadron leader instead of following Grimm and Wilhelm. A fierce clash would ensure between the two groups before Tholter—who acted as the "core" corpse soldier controlling the others like him—would be cut down by his old friend Grimm and put to rest.

intro: Vincent Vollachia (ヴィンセント・ヴォラキア), also temporarily known by the alias Abel (アベル), is the seventy-seventh emperor of the Sacred Vollachia Empire. He played major roles in Arc 7 and Arc 8, and he played supporting roles in both The Travelogue of the Finest and The Tale of the Scarlet Princess.
appearance:
Vincent is a young and very handsome man in his mid-twenties. He has relatively short black hair and almond-shaped brown eyes which emit an aura of high intelligence. With a pale complexion, Vincent gives off a sense of fragility if one were to quickly glance at him, but when one is in his presence, his charisma emits an overpowering sense of dread and power that makes even the finest of soldiers cower in fear. As noted by Subaru, when first laying eyes on him, one cannot help but to feel like kneeling down before him.

Vincent is dressed in a long, red elegant coat with its collar and the front edges being black. The coat's edges are gold in their color, just like the buttons on the front and on the coat's sleeves. On its left side, there's an insignia with a wolf impaled by swords, the symbol of Vollachia. Underneath his coat, Vincent can be seen wearing a grey tuxedo, and underneath that, a white long-sleeved shirt can clearly be visible. Vincent does not wear any special ornaments or jewelry as he doesn't seem to like being seen as ostentatious. Additionally, there are black feathers with red tips on his left shoulder.

When he and Subaru first met one another at the start of Arc 7, Vincent covered his face with a rag, which he used to conceal his face and identity. Only his dark brown eyes were visible underneath them. After removing the rag and revealing his true identity to Subaru, he donned a red mask that resembled an Oni. It covered the top half of his face and had two large horns protruding from the top of it. The Oni mask was woven with a cognitive disruption spell that prevented him from being recognized by those who were familiar with him but unaware he had been deposed from the imperial throne, making it a far more effective way of hiding his identity than the tattered rags he resorted to using before obtaining it.

While he participated in the Bloodless Siege of Guaral, Vincent dressed as a dancer while under the alias Bianca with Subaru's help. He wore crimson and black clothing, black and golden ornaments, a light purple cloth wrapped around his waist, makeup and nail polish applied by Subaru and fine-tuned by himself, and used a long, black braided wig adorned with a floral decoration. In addition, he wore several pieces of jewelry across his upper body, including a gold face chain and gold earrings.
personality:
Vincent is shown to be extremely prideful, fastidious, and perfectionistic. He is shown to be cold and has little superficial compassion and mercy for the people who haven't earned it, but despite that, one cannot call him a bad leader as he's loved by some and feared by a majority of his subjects, and he is even capable of turning terror into admiration and servitude into adoration. Even when visibly worn out, wounded and on death's door, his people bowed their heads and kneeled before him, and no one dared to look at him with even a hint of pity or any other negative emotion. Perhaps one of his most important virtues is his rationality and his ability to make very quick decisions which almost always turn out in his favor, no matter the odds. As mentioned above, Vincent is very cold and lacks unnecessary compassion for his soldiers as in Vollachia, everything and everyone is owned by the emperor. Despite the overwhelming political power he has, he's very resourceful and does not treat people's lives as possessions. Having said that, he had no problems in ordering one of his guards to chop off his own head (despite Balleroy Temeglyph later explaining how the knight would not have left the hall with his life as he showed weakness which strictly goes against the core teachings of Vollachian Empire). Likewise, he is not above using death to inspire fear in others to prevent rebellions, and he believes that if one must die, that death should be efficient and exploited to the utmost. This being said, despite not being above having people killed, he seems to detest killing to a certain degree, which he displayed upon coming across the undead Viva, an infamous serial killer responsible for countless murders and dismemberments in his search for the soul, and in response, Vincent showed a rare display of outrage by purposefully burning his soul when he had the option to pass on peacefully.

He's shown to be extremely smart and capable of making the entire Empire dance in the palm of his hand. He's easily able to manipulate people, even those who are a cut above others in intelligence. At the end of Imperial Diplomacy of Bloodshed, it's revealed that Vincent stood behind the coup itself, tricking the High Count, Prime Minister, the Divine Generals, the Lugunican diplomats and the whole Imperial Army into an elaborate and stretched-out plan all for the sake of signing the non-aggression pact with the Kingdom of Lugunica, as he had no desire to start a war but due to the Empire's age-old teachings, he couldn't allow himself to hastily accept the treaty. His is likewise skilled at wordplay, even being capable of outsmarting Miklotov McMahon in a verbal battle and making a fool out of Bordeaux Zergev, deceiving him into thinking he's simply belittling him when in fact, he was just citing a passage from Magrizza's Guillotine. He's easily capable of manipulating people to fall into his traps, using them for his own goals and plans. He's normally calm but does not shy away from showering his subordinates with insults or straight up ordering them to commit suicide or to not speak a word. Vincent was also noted to emit a strong presence, different from anything Julius Juukulius has ever felt; it was neither joy nor terror but something far more sinister.

According to Cecilus Segmunt, Vincent has a way of seeing the true potential of the people that he meets, usually even better than the person themself does, and when giving orders, he does so "recklessly", making it difficult for others to keep up with his ideal of them. He tends to have certain expectations of the people he meets or commands, typically criticizing one as slothful if they are unable to meet those expectations. However, he does not disrelish solely for being incompetent; in his own words, one ought to perform the vocation that corresponds to their own caliber, and he believes that everyone must live with all of their might without respite. Likewise, Vincent strongly believes in rewarding or punishing people for their deeds. Everyone should give their all and be treated accordingly. Even though it was more than 8 years after being a crucial benefactor in squashing Gladiator Island Ginunhive's uprising, upon learning of that he was the one who participated against the rebels, Vincent swore to reward Al for his outstanding work all those years ago.

Vincent also has a hatred and disgust for the Stargazers. Though he understands that their prophecies are true, he is disgusted by how they are twisted into fanaticism and abandon their “selves”, not to mention how their words lead people down paths that they do not want, such as his own prophecy regarding the Great Disaster. This is most clear in his interactions with Ubilk, and because of how he mistakenly understood Natsuki Subaru as a Stargazer after noticing the effects of Return by Death, combined with Subaru’s emotional attitude and decisions, that hatred and disgust slipped into his view of Subaru. Ordinarily, because he tends to take a tolerant approach to digesting and evaluating things, it is rare to see Vincent display truly genuine negative emotions, with the rare few moments being when discussing things related to the Stargazers or Stride Vollachia.

After the death of Chisha, Vincent reveals that while he was prepared for his life to end, which is why he kept people at a distance regardless of who they were, he was not prepared to lose someone dear to him. Because of this, Vincent became colder and more emotional for a time, getting into a brawl with an infantilized Subaru after refusing to listen to what he had to say. He also claims to hate arguments based in emotion, as they have the least potential, and yet, after his temporary ousting from the throne, he had been both tormented and rescued by those very arguments time and again.
history:
Early Life
Vincent Abellux (ヴィンセント・アベルクス, Vinsento Aberukusu) was born as the son of Drizen Vollachia, the seventy-sixth emperor of Vollachia. As a child, Vincent discovered Stride Vollachia's journal in the Crystal Palace's library, where he learned of the madman's delusions, the possibility of him being a Stargazer, and his knowledge of a coming Great Disaster which would occur following the death of the emperor of Vollachia. Because of this, believing that the Empire would not be saved if the emperor were anyone else, Vincent resolved himself to become the emperor and make preparations to prevent the destruction of the Empire. The wisdom he acquired at a young age allowed him to quickly establish a reputation for himself in the time he was only about ten years old. Around this time, Vincent witnessed the fall of Garkla, spurring on the legendary hero Kurgan to take up arms one last time to give the surviving residents in the Fortified City enough time to evacuate from the Sin Archbishop of Greed's rampage. After the Eight Arms succeeded in his mission and died in the process, Vincent spent years restoring the heroic reputation he had before the circumstances that led him to becoming a slave.

Before his birth, the Abellux family was one that was neither high-ranking nor prestigious, and they began to have ambition after his birth. When Vincent was eleven, a rebellion against his family was started by a vassal of theirs who conspired with a separate family. Despite their brilliant tactics, Vincent was able to trounce them and eliminated every conspirator, and he had the advance troops dismembered and displayed on the road to inspire fear and prevent further rebellions. The incident became infamously known as the Miracle of Abellux. Because of this incident, Vincent himself had rumors spread about him, and his reputation became feared by the public. By the age of twelve, he took over his own household, which had fallen into disarray during the rebellion, and they were eventually eliminated too.

When he was twelve, as he was traveling along in his carriage, it got stuck in a ditch. Thanks to the nearby Chesha Trim, they were able to free the wheel with the young man's calculative skills. As a means to thank him for his assistance and to bring him to the mansion, Vincent had Chesha board the carriage. Afterward, Vincent asked him Chesha if he would die for him, which Chesha declined on impulse. Despite expecting to be executed for his insolence, his answer impressed Vincent, and telling him to keep that outlook, decided to hire him. His confusion led him to question Vincent's decision, as he was aware of the events of the Miracle of Abellux, to which Vincent merely replied that his actions were to prevent any future rebellions through fear. As Vincent asked what Chesha thought he expected of him, Vincent claimed that the road he walked was one filled with ditches, and he believed he would need Chesha's abilities to get out of such problems.

After being hired, Chesha started to go by the name Chisha Gold, adopting the surname of a certain house that Vincent had exterminated. Thanks to the adoption of the Gold name, rumors began to spread that Vincent left one descendant from the family alive to serve him in order to condemn the family to endure the humiliation to escape his control, further reinforcing his own reputation. From then forward, Chisha helped Vincent get out of various "ditches", and once he was well learned about the flood control systems, he decided to finally be rid of the administrator and have him executed for embezzlement. As more time passed, Vincent eventually told Chisha about Stride Vollachia and his journal. However, he did not tell him what he read within it. At an unknown point after this, Vincent picked up Cecilus.

The Tale of the Scarlet Princess
Roughly 7 years before the events of the main story, Drizen Vollachia became incapable of ruling the nation, which was confirmed when he drew the Yang Sword and burned to ash in an instant. In the following year, Vincent waged war against his half siblings in an event known as the Imperial Selection Ceremony. Two months before its conclusion, his younger half-sister Lamia Godwin laid Siege on the Abellux Castle, which Vincent successfully repelled, ending in her demise. Vincent won the Imperial Selection Ceremony by slaughtering a majority of his siblings. The only one he spared was Prisca Benedict, who he kept alive after he convinced her servant and foster sister, Arakiya, to betray her. After successfully faking Prisca's death, he became the seventy-seventh emperor of the Sacred Vollachia Empire.

Post-Imperial Selection Ceremony
Following his coronation, Vincent scrubbed clean Vollachia's corruption, purging nobles who had clung onto their power only by their history despite becoming a shell of themselves, and despite the initial similarity of his changes to other previous emperors, it was quickly recognized that Vincent had entirely reformed the Empire in a manner quite different from any previous emperor. Thanks to his actions, unnecessary bloodshed and conflict ceased, fights to the death would no longer be applauded, and proof of strength was no longer determined solely by the person's respective overall strength, giving those with ambitions the drive to strive with their lives to achieve them. Vincent also revived the Nine Divine Generals system, deciding that Cecilus would be ranked as first, Arakiya second, Olbart Dunkelkenn third after his retrieval, and Chisha fourth, and he already had an eye on others he wanted for the other positions. He had also given positions to the servants of his fallen siblings, including making Berstetz Fondalfon, the most direct follower of one of his greatest rivals in the Imperial Selection Ceremony, Lamia, the Prime Minister.

Death unto the Weak, No Mercy ZERO Vincent
One day, Ubilk, who had become a Stargazer, appeared before Vincent, forewarning him of an attack from Gaoran Peitiet, a High Count of Vollachia. Thanks to this, Vincent successfully led his defeat, and his personal bodyguard at the time, Rowan Segmunt, cut him down. Afterward, he gave Ubilk the official title of Stargazer in the Crystal Palace, and since then, his commandments have been useful in quelling numerous problems.

The Travelogue of the Finest
Roughly six months before the beginning of the story, Reinhard van Astrea, Julius Juukulius, and Ferris escorted Miklotov McMahon and Bordeaux Zergev on a diplomatic mission to the Imperial Capital of Lupugana. They met Vincent in the Crystal Palace, but after an unfortunate turn of events, the trio of knights and the emperor had to flee to a nearby forest in order to save their lives. Soon after their battle with the Divine Generals who were trying to retrieve the emperor, the squad realizes that the perpetrators were after Vincent's life. After successfully defeating the traitors who turned out to be Balleroy Temeglyph and Gramdart Holstoy, the Lugunican diplomats manage to secure a non-aggression treaty. On their way back, they came to the conclusion that Vincent was the one who perpetrated the entire coup in order to create a scenario in which he'd be "forced" to sign the pact with the Kingdom of Lugunica.

Imperial Coup
During one of Ubilk's visits to the castle, he spoke with Chisha and Vincent, saying that the Great Disaster had been foretold by the stars, something that he brought up with the intention of informing Chisha about. When Chisha began questioning him, having not heard of this Great Disaster, Ubilk claimed that it would bring ruin, also mentioning Yang Sword's glow, implying he knew about what went down with Prisca and resulting in Chisha nearly killing him for it. Afterward, he claimed that it would be the death of Vincent Vollachia that would trigger the Great Disaster. After Ubilk left the room, Vincent and Chisha discussed why he kept it secret from Chisha, which Vincent claimed was futile and something that Chisha could not prevent anyway, something that Chisha disagreed with and claimed his intentions to go against, which Vincent refuted. When asked for how long he had known about the Great Disaster and its trigger, Vincent brought out the journal, and he stated that everything he had done was to minimize the damage, including preparing Chisha for the future.

Later, after Chisha started working behind the scenes to take Vincent's place as the one to die, he and Berstetz initiated a coup which resulted in Goz Ralfon being defeated and captured and Vincent retreating to the Buddheim Jungle that linked him near the graveyard of nameless monarchs, which contained several bare necessities for survival. Deciding to take a stand, Vincent decided to search for the People of Shudrak, obscuring his face with bandages to hide his identity.

Undead Busters
With the Lugunicans returning home, Vincent tasked Spica, Cecilus, and Arakiya with exterminating the remaining undead left behind by the Great Disaster. However, due to Priscilla's death leaving Arakiya to ignore Vincent's summons, he had them retrieve her. Afterward, they returned to report to Vincent. After a turbulent conversation caused by Cecilus's rambling and Arakiya's aggression, Vincent finally sent the group off on their mission, and he decided to leave keeping Arakiya in check to Spica, having learned that she could do so.

After Spica's group encountered Volcas, they brought the wolf man to where the emperor and the Nine Divine Generals were. Following the events of the battle that Volcas had with Yorna Mishigure, who he was able to recognize as Iris, Volcas sought to be executed by Vincent with the Yang Sword, whereas Yorna obstinately did not want to accept that outcome. Realizing that there was a possibility Yorna could revolt again, Medium O'Connell, his new empress consort, suggested to Vincent that Volcas should be chosen to fill the vacancy in the Nine Divine Generals. She believed her proposal would not only cater to Yorna and fill the vacancy left by Chisha, but with Volcas being the direct cause behind Eugard Vollachia's decree to execute the wolf people and mole people, forgiving him and having him join their side would show that Vincent was serious about keeping the decree rescinded. Vincent took her proposal seriously, and when she accidentally let slip that it was originally her brother Flop's suggestion, she told Vincent that she just wanted to improve Vincent's view of her as his empress. Regardless, after hearing Medium out, Vincent proceeded to meet with Volcas in person to discuss her proposal with him.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
Originally, Vincent was primarily a non-combatant, and it was his mind and extraordinary strategic sense that made him dangerous. However, this changes upon drawing the Yang Sword. Once drawn, his combat skills increase dramatically, allowing him to fight alongside powerful warriors on the level of his sister, ancestor, and the Nine Divine Generals.

Intelligence
Keen Intellect: Rather than using physical strength as his strong point, Vincent displays an impressive intellect and the capability to come up with complex and interluded plans to outsmart, outplay, and win against his opponents. Coupled with extremely strong individuals such as Cecilus Segmunt, Vincent easily won the Imperial Selection Ceremony by outsmarting and slaughtering his enemies, eventually crowning himself as the seventy-seventh emperor of the Vollachia Empire.

Excellent Memory: Vincent has such a great memory that he could recognize the names and faces of a vast majority of the citizens of his nation, including all of his subordinates and people of interest who could pose a threat to or become a valuable asset of the throne, despite not having met them before. As such, only people who have remained in obscurity, such as the People of Shudrak, are impossible to grasp the names and faces of for him. It was because of this that he was able to provide names to the undead in the Great Disaster, despite the fact that several of the undead died before his time.

Equipment
Yang Sword Vollachia (陽剣ヴォラキア, Youken Vorakia): As a member of the Imperial Family of Vollachia, Vincent is capable of summoning and using the Yang Sword Vollachia, otherwise known as the Yang Sword, an ornate crimson sword with light that shines like the sun. The sword appears out of thin air when the user wishes to use it, and it cuts and burns whatever the user desires, including magic or souls. The flame of the Yang Sword is also stated to protect the emperor from anyone deemed unworthy by the sword. Although typically considered not so capable of combat, once he draws his sword, he is given the strength necessary to wield his sword, allowing him strength and speed incomparable to his normal state.
Cloak of Concealment (姿隠しのマント, Shikakushi no Manto): A meteor that, when worn, allows a user to temporarily conceal their presence by tricking others' sense of sight. However, it cannot mask things like sound, odor, footsteps, or anything else like it.
Two Rings with the Emperor's Crest: Following his escape from the Crystal Palace, Vincent took two rings with the emperor's crest with him. Both rings were meteors, with one of them being able to cast fire spells and the other one's effects remaining unknown. The first ring was blown to pieces during the Rite of Blood Subaru and Vincent had to go through in order to gain the People of Shudrak's trust, and the other ring was destroyed by Vincent during their battle with Arakiya in Guaral, which resulted in the entire room getting flooded by copious amounts of mana which inflicted temporary mana sickness to Arakiya, allowing the group to drive her off.
Recognition Obstruction Mask: This mask, in shape of an oni face, was given to Vincent by the members of the People of Shudrak and allows him to obstruct anyone from perceiving him, making his identity completely unrecognizable to anyone save for the individuals Vincent himself wishes to reveal his identity too, and to people who possess absolutely certainty about Vincent's true identity. Taritta stated the mask was used a long time ago by one of the previous emperors of Vollachia who formed a partnership with the Shudraks, in order to visit the forest without being recognized.

intro: Zarestia (ザーレスティア) is the Slasher, one of the Four Great Spirits. She dwells at Zarestia's Bed. Though she has yet to appear in the main story, she first appears in the Kararagi Reaper Incident side story.
appearance: Zarestia is an inhumanly beautiful woman with white skin. She has milky-white shaggy hair with a lime strand, white eyebrows, and sharp almond-shaped eyes with a bright yellow color. She wears an immaculate pure white kimono with a lime sphere and the right side over the left, giving the impression of burial clothes, but with the skirt shortened to the mid-thigh and freely exposing her long, slender legs.
personality:
At her core, Zarestia is childish and temperamental despite both her apparent and actual age. She has a foul-mouthed and arrogant manner of speech, often referring to people as if they were animals, and she greatly prizes her freedom. Despite this, Zarestia has been known to compromise her desires for the sake of others. She enjoys the company of others, helping them, and making them happy, as well as receiving their gratitude and praise. Even in the event that she loses her Light Sphere, which contains the bulk of her power, and must retrieve it, though she is not above destroying entire towns to retrieve it, she is resistant to killing others during such an attack, to the point that she will raise the residents above a town to avoid hurting them during her rage. Meanwhile, for those she assumes to be such a thief, if they do not return her Light Sphere, then she is willing to become violent and unwilling to listen to them, even if the person she faces is not the thief and is merely the victim of a misunderstanding.

Despite her regular demeanor, when Zarestia wields the power of her Light Sphere, she becomes a compulsive murderer who thinks of nothing but killing and has a constant desire to kill anything and everything. Everything leads back to murderous intent, regardless of target, mood, time, reason, or circumstance. Even when she doesn't want to kill, she wants to kill. However, when stripped of her Light Sphere, her bloodlust and incessant impulse to kill are removed. Despite this, she will still seek to reclaim it if separated.

She also has a deep trauma and hatred towards alcohol, and coming into contact with it is enough to put her into shock.
history:
Early Life
Zarestia predates both the Witch and the Dragon. Stories of those times describe her as a great beast. Her head would raise the wind, her hands would add fire, her tail would hoist up the water, and her feet would dig up the soil, all of which she enjoyed and would do repeatedly.

She rejoiced in her freedom, undisturbed by anyone, and was praised and admired by all. In turn, she began listening to their requests and would usually lend them her aid whenever she was awake, though sometimes she missed her former freedom and would ignore them. Eventually, people began bringing gifts for her when they came to ask for favors, though she had little interest in them. However, she appreciated their feelings and was glad they were happy with her doing what she liked.

Over time, requests became increasingly more specific, and her followers began asking for more and more from Zarestia. Though she enjoyed her freedom, she also enjoyed how they would praise and pamper her. Before long, she had grown accustomed to doing as everyone told her. One day, they came to her with a particularly odd request. They asked for fire and nothing else. She initially found the request disagreeable and asserted her freedom by turning it down, only for everyone to leave her. Finding her freedom to be lonesome, she went to them and agreed to their request for fire. However, she secretly raised the wind as well, as only the wind was indispensable to her as the symbol of her freedom.

After Zarestia returned, the people invited her to a party where she was given alcohol for the first time, and she fell asleep away from her nest for the first time as well. While she slept, the people removed her limbs, stripping her of all elemental powers besides wind. Confused, she asked for an explanation, and they accused her of burning their towns and villages as her wind had caused the flames to spread. They bathed her in alcohol and lit her ablaze, and she saw they were pleased to watch her burn as she screamed in pain. Realizing she still had her head and power over wind, she resolved to kill them all and slew each and every one of them.

Since then, Zarestia has been filled with bloodlust, and to express her freedom she would kill anything and everything. She took for herself the title of the Most Beautiful Reaper (最も美しい死神), after how the people called her "shinigami" when she killed them in the end and how they had once called her "beautiful".

Kararagi Reaper Incident
A short time after the Great Disaster, in Kararagi, angry and looking for a thief who had apparently stolen her Light Sphere, she attacked Banan with a windstorm - an incident that would come to be known as the Shinigami Disaster - destroying half of the town, holding its residents in the air like hostages, and she confronted Ricardo, who she believed was the thief. Bruised, injured, and realizing that he would be unable to defeat, stop, or reason with her, Ricardo decided to sit down and take her attacks. Because of this, she used her wind to try and force him to give up the location of her Light Sphere, but due to his tenacity, she stopped attacking him, released the windstorm that was ravaging the town, and released her hostages. Afterwards, they decided to talk, introducing themselves to each other. Sometime after Ricardo quelled Zarestia's rage, Anastasia's group arrived and were led to the holding cells in Riften Magoji's mansion, where Zarestia was being held. During their conversation, Julius noticed that she was a Great Spirit and introduced himself, while Halibel unintentionally riled her up by noticing her strange constitution, that something was missing. However, when Anastasia mentioned Zarestia being responsible for other such town-destroying wind cataclysms, Zarestia declared otherwise, saying that she only rampaged in Banan. Shortly afterward, this is confirmed when a massive tornado appeared outside of Banan, not made by Zarestia. After giving her orders and securing Zarestia's assistance, the group made their way to stop the tornado. Although they managed to quell the winds, however, they soon realized that Anastasia and Echidna had gone missing.

A full day after being taken, Anastasia and Echidna were brought back to Banan by Black Tia, their captor, and shortly after, likely due to her exhaustion catching up with her, Anastasia passed out with a fever. Though Julius tended to her and attempted to help heal her with his spirits, he was unable and settled for practicing with Halibel to become stronger. At some point, Anastasia woke up from the sound of clashing steel to find Zarestia waiting for her. Zarestia, who wanted to talk with Anastasia about Black Tia, told her that Black Tia was currently in a cell and that her attitude and speech were due to the Light Sphere's influence on her. Afterward, Anastasia asked Zarestia to gather the others.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
As a great spirit, Zarestia holds tremendous power. She can easily and casually destroy towns and defeat the likes of a warrior of Ricardo's strength with complete ease. Likewise, when she has her Light Sphere on her, she becomes more bloodthirsty and lethal, making her much more dangerous. This being said, in the present day, she is significantly weaker than she was in her much earlier days when she could command other affinities. At present, the full extent of both her current and previous strengths remain unknown.

Magic/Spiritual Arts
While Zarestia once exerted great control over the four primary magic affinities, her current self retains only her extremely powerful wind magic. Her control over wind magic is exceptional. When she attacked Banan, she simultaneously used her magic to destroy the town around her, hold all of the town's residents high in the sky with her wind and kept them from harm, and concentrated attacks on Ricardo with ease.

Physical Traits
Enhanced Olfaction: Zarestia has a heightened sense of smell, particularly when it comes to blood. With it, she can determine her enemies or people who she has met before. However, she can be mistaken with at times: she mistook Ricardo and Halibel for the one who stole her Light Sphere due to a similar scent coming off of both him and the thief.

Equipment
Light Sphere (光珠, Mi Tama): The gem that serves as Zarestia's anchor and the source of her power. Without it, Zarestia exists as only a portion of herself, less than half, and loses her desire to kill. Zarestia's anchor may be used to access much of her power and take her form, though one receives her obsession with killing as well.

intro: Tishua Astrea (ティシュア・アストレア) was the mother of Theresia van Astrea and the wife of Veltol Astrea. She played lesser supporting roles in Sword Demon Love Story and Sword Demon Battle Ballad.
appearance: Tishua had flax-colored hair and a slim face. Despite her age, she was a youthful and spirited beauty.
personality: A comely and sharp-minded woman who had something of a mischievous streak, especially when it came to interacting with her husband, in which she was often seen teasing Veltol's habits, such as his over-protective nature and general floppish behavior. Although most of time she sided with her daughter when Veltol and Theresia argued, particularly when Wilhelm was involved, Tishua was still very supportive of her husband.
history:
Sword Demon Love Story: The Bride's Father
After the two decided to get married, Wilhelm and Theresia left for the Astrea Domain so that Wilhelm could ask her parents for her hand in marriage. After arriving there, Wilhelm was nervous to meet them, which made Theresia happy. Soon after, Veltol and Tishua arrived in the meeting room, and Veltol immediately put pressure on Wilhelm. The four sat down and spoke, Theresia talking about some things with her mother while Veltol decided to determine if Wilhelm was worthy of Theresia. Despite the man's apparent disapproval, Wilhelm was about to ask for Theresia's hand, but Veltol was quick to explode, resulting in him and Theresia getting into an argument. Tishua apologized for it and noticed his tea was empty, and though she was about to offer to refill it, Veltol did instead. However, Theresia stopped him, as Veltol had drugged his tea. Cornered, Veltol mentioned that it wasn't poison but a drug that made one lose control of their bladder, leading to Theresia snapping at him. After Tishua told him the way to the bathroom, she asked if Wilhelm would be able to adjust to their family, to which he answered by calling them mother and father and saying that it would probably be hard to get along with Veltol. Receiving a positive response from Tishua, he left to use the bathroom.

Sword Demon Love Song
In the three months that followed, Theresia brought Wilhelm to meet her parents. However, thanks to Veltol, their upcoming wedding faced numerous setbacks and obstacles. Thanks to his interference, three days before their official wedding date, he used his authority to force the Zergev Squadron to patrol a few towns around the capital, knowing full well that it would take three days to accomplish. When Theresia and Carol Remendis went to chide Veltol, even threatening to leave House Astrea, Tishua was quick to join in, claiming his actions were petty. The next day, Theresia waited patiently for the return for the Zergev Squadron with Carol and her parents. Eventually, Bordeaux Zergev arrived and informed her of the squad's return, and soon after, her wedding took place. Despite Wilhelm being unable to clean himself off after the mess he went through, the wedding went off perfectly, and the two were married.

In the month that followed, Veltol made numerous appearances, much to Theresia's frustration, and eventually, he even suggested going along on the honeymoon as well, leading to another argument. However, with help from Tishua, they were able to get him to leave. Despite this, Veltol was still set on joining them, and Tishua was against his meddling. This being said, he had official business in Picoutatte, and he left. Later, Tishua was informed of the incidents that took place there, and she made her way to the city.

intro: Veltol Astrea (ベルトール・アストレア) was the father of Theresia van Astrea. He played supporting roles in Sword Demon Love Story and Sword Demon Battle Ballad.
appearance: Veltol had relatively long hair along with a red beard and a red mustache. He wore bordeaux colored clothes, those representing of nobility.
personality: Veltol was considered to have an overprotective personality towards his daughter, Theresia, his wife, Tishua, and his three sons. Though this facet of his personality sometimes went too far, the love he held for his family was what truly distinguished him as a person. He went to extreme lengths to protect his family despite being unskilled with the sword. He sometimes acted pettily around the people he disliked, but in the end, once they got to know them better, he would warm up and treat them as family. This said, as the head of a noble house, Veltol can play that role perfectly, often exuding a noble aura when faced with others besides his family. Despite his less than average talent with a sword, he is willing to challenge someone to a duel if they insult the people he cares for.
history:
Sword Demon Love Story: The Bride's Father
After the two decided to get married, Wilhelm and Theresia left for the Astrea Domain so that Wilhelm could ask her parents for her hand in marriage. After arriving there, Wilhelm was nervous to meet them, which made Theresia happy. Soon after, Veltol and Tishua arrived in the meeting room, and Veltol immediately put pressure on Wilhelm. The four sat down and spoke, Theresia talking about some things with her mother while Veltol decided to determine if Wilhelm was worthy of Theresia.
