intro: Yorna Mishigure (ヨルナ・ミシグレ) is the Third ranking Divine General of the Sacred Vollachia Empire and the ruler of the Demon City of Chaosflame. She plays a major supporting role in Arc 7 and Arc 8, and she is one of the main characters in the Iris and the King of Thorns EX chapter.
appearance:
Yorna is a beautiful and tall fox woman with a thin and alluring physique. Perhaps her most striking facial feature is her slit blue eyes that give off a languid yet sharp look that can captivate anyone with whom she crosses sight. Her hair is neatly arranged, primarily white in color but slowly shifts to orange towards its tips. Furthermore, Yorna adorns her head in a variety of animal bones, horns, teeth, scales and other ornaments, making her appearance majestic and somewhat mythical. As a fox human, she has a pair of sharp orange fox ears and, uniquely, nine white and orange fox tails.

Adorning herself in a richly colored kimono that vaguely exposes her thin white shoulders, Yorna gives off an incredibly languid and relaxed air. Her attire consists of a primarily blue kimono with a floral pattern, that has its sleeve edges and its collar's colors in bright green. She keeps it all together with a green belt that has a black floral pattern adorning it. In addition, Yorna can usually be seen smoking from her purple and golden kiseru.

As Iris, she was a human who had flax hair tied in a braid and blue eyes. She wore a red dress with orange and black around the ends of the sleeves and the hem, a blue hood, and she wore red shoes. She was described as having a plain face and plain features.
personality:
Yorna can best be described as problematic and hard to deal with, having even been described by Zikr Osman as someone with a desire for destruction, and according to Kafma Irulux, she represents a danger to the emperor. Despite bearing the rank of "Seventh", she frequently starts revolts which have forced Vincent to dispatch the Imperial Army and the Divine Generals more than once, though he considers her too necessary for Chaosflame, to have her be executed for treason, effectively making her some sort of a trouble-child of the Nine Divine Generals. Furthermore, despite her hatred for the Empire and the Imperial Way that governs it, Yorna's goal was connected to the position of the emperor of Vollachia, and though Vincent Vollachia could only speculate that her wishes were to be the emperor's favorite mistress due to the vagueness of her goal, she wanted desperately to repeal the extinction decree put on the wolf and mole humans that was put in place centuries ago by her lover Eugard Vollachia, both for their sake and her own, as repealing the decree would also result in her soul being free from her curse. She was ultimately able to achieve her goal following the Great Disaster, successfully convincing Eugard to have the decree repealed.

When conversing and interacting with others, Yorna tends to act in an extremely relaxed and almost spoiled manner, appearing somewhat arrogant which can be seen with her often taking her time to answer even to the very emperor of the Vollachian Empire. Furthermore, her words are often provoking or teasing, which often tends to anger people with shorter tempers, such as the aforementioned Kafma. She is not above spinning a situation into a conflict for her own amusement, with Subaru initially noting that she was far more vicious and terrible than he had imagined her from hearing everything Vincent and Zikr had to say about her after seeing how she handled both Vincent's and his enemies' envoys during a meeting. In some ways, she's remarkably similar to Priscilla Barielle, but with next to no verbal abuse and a much more languid tone. This being said, she primarily showed this while speaking towards people who were intent on dragging her into their affairs, and when speaking with other people, she has shown to be rather friendly and easy to speak to.

Yorna also has a very soft spot for children and demi-humans, and after becoming a Divine General, despite her overall goal, she prioritized making a safe haven for demi-humans. Because of her love for her people, those very people treasure her, offering her various gifts made from parts of themselves, which Yorna treasures, to the point that she finds it loathsome that those precious gifts act as substitutes for her life during battle. She is willing to go to extreme lengths in order to protect her people, and whenever she started a rebellion against the Empire, it was always for another person's sake. When Tanza's sister, Zoey, was tortured and killed by imperial soldiers, she shared her grief and rage with Tanza before declaring her rebellion until the heads of the soldiers responsible were brought to her. Likewise, during the fake "Great Disaster" in Chaosflame, she went directly against Vincent's orders to flee the city and put her all on the line in order to protect it and ensure a safe haven for those persecuted by the Empire for their blood lineage. Likewise, though she is able to take the life of her enemies, she does not like to do so, and she can only do so after much resignation and significant anguish to her heart. It is for this reason that Yorna manifested the Soul Marriage Technique, which could not be mastered without compassion for others.
history:
Around 300 years before the present era, a village girl named Iris (アイリス, Airisu) met and sheltered Eugard Vollachia, an emperor of Vollachia who was ousted from his throne. The two fell in love and Iris sheltered and supported Eugard's path to return to his position. However, when they were to meet one day, they were betrayed, and Iris was killed by the wolf human and mole human races. After the emperor lost Iris, he descended into madness. He resultingly chose to eradicate all wolf humans and mole humans who remained in the Empire. However, his madness was not quelled, and Eugard chose to cast a curse on Iris, using the slain wolf and mole humans as the core for it. This curse, the Soul Marriage Curse, brought her back to life at the cost of experiencing endless reincarnation.

Post-Reincarnations
Beginning the cycle of reincarnation, Iris sought to dispel the Soul Marriage Curse to free herself from its effects, and it became her dearest wish to reunite with Eugard. The genesis of this fervent wish was related to the existence of the Stargazers, which she believes is one of the Vollachia Empire's evil practices. She also learned how to use the ancient Soul Marriage Technique.

Many years later, Iris was reincarnated as a human with the name Sandra Benedict (サンドラ・ベネディクト, Sandora Benedikuto). As Sandra, she had a child with the seventy-sixth emperor of Vollachia, Drizen Vollachia. Their child was named Prisca Benedict. However, Sandra perished to give birth to Prisca, and she reincarnated into a fox human under a new name: Yorna Mishigure. She became the Demon City of Chaosflame's “Mistress” because of her lineage and lived through the Imperial Selection Ceremony as Yorna, not knowing that her child had been spared and took the name Priscilla. Sometime after Vincent Vollachia was coronated as the seventy-seventh emperor of Vollachia, Yorna was appointed as the Imperial Army's Seventh ranked Divine General once the Nine Divine General system was reestablished.

Sword Identity
Around two to three months before the main story, Yorna launched a rebellion against the Empire upon discovering that Tanza's older sister, Zoey, was murdered for sport by soldiers stationed at a fortress close to Chaosflame. After Tanza's audience with her, Yorna began by attacking the fortress and killing most of the soldiers there; however, a few soldiers escaped. Soon, she was confronted by Madelyn Eschart, but their battle came to a standstill. Ending their battle, Yorna told Madelyn of the soldiers who left the fortress, asking that they be sent to her in return for stopping her rebellion.

Sometime after Madelyn relayed her message, Yorna came face to face with Cecilus Segmunt and Arakiya when the Imperial Army's generals assaulted Chaosflame. Despite the power that the Blue Lightning and the Spirit Eater both had as two of the strongest combatants in the Empire, they were unable to defeat Yorna due to her usage of Soul Marriage. In the end, Yorna's demands were met, and the emperor himself personally ordered the escaped soldiers to be sent to Chaosflame, ending the rebellion.

Undead Busters
With the Great Disaster over, Yorna and the citizens of Chaosflame sought to rebuild the city even greater than it was before. After Medium O'Connell became Vincent's empress consort, she sought marital advice from her, Serena Dracroy, and Madelyn to visit her. Before long, Cecilus's party returned to Garkla, intending to speak with Vincent about how to handle Volcas. Upon reaching the location that the emperor and the Nine Divine Generals were staying at, Yorna met with Volcas, and they engaged in combat. However, he did not make any attempt to fight back during their battle, and he stated that she smelled like Iris, to which she affirmed that she had gotten stronger since they last met. Although her appearance, expressions, voice, and presentation were completely different to Volcas, he recognized her laughter, which was the same as it was 300 years ago. Following the events of the battle, Volcas sought to be executed by the emperor with the Yang Sword, whereas Yorna obstinately did not want to accept that outcome. Realizing that there was a possibility Yorna could revolt again, Medium suggested to Vincent that Volcas should be chosen to fill the vacancy in the Nine Divine Generals. She believed her proposal would not only cater to Yorna and fill the vacancy left by Chisha Gold, but with Volcas being the direct cause behind Eugard's decree to execute the wolf people and mole people, forgiving him and having him join their side would show that Vincent was serious about keeping the decree rescinded. After hearing Medium out, Vincent proceeded to meet with Volcas in person to discuss her proposal with him.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
Despite being among the lower end of the Nine Divine Generals, Yorna has centuries of experience, and she is capable of drawing out enough power that she can prevent any of her people from dying from an attack. Moreover, she can fight against even the top three of the Nine Divine Generals, not be killed while fighting them, and even push them back. Although her strength scales with her emotions, at their peak, they make Yorna an immeasurably powerful force, especially in terms of home defense.

Techniques
Soul Marriage Technique (魂婚術, Konkon-jutsu): Soul Marriage is a long-lost secret technique of the old world that has been forgotten by most people that requires compassion for others to master. By dividing her own Od and bestowing it onto someone of her choosing, Yorna imbues them with power more or less reflective of her own, granting them the physical might to throw house-sized boulders like cannonballs, and she greatly boosts their healing capabilities to the point someone acting under her Soul Marriage can receive multiple fatal wounds and be healed completely in a few short moments. However, in order for Soul Marriage to work, Yorna must not only love the receiver of this ability, but she must also be loved by that person in return. If this condition is not met, Soul Marriage will not work. Furthermore, as long as Yorna feels self-love and has a strong affirmation that what she is doing is right, the technique can give her extraordinary power. However, if her own sense of self-love and of her actions being right begins to wane, her strength will drop dramatically, to the point that someone the caliber of Rowan Segmunt could come close to killing her. Likewise, if someone whom she loves wholly affirms and believes that they are loved, the effects of the technique will also be tremendous for them. The effects of the Soul Marriage Technique may also create a flame in the eye of someone who is under its effects.
Damage Substitution: By imbuing the technique into personal beloved objects given to her, said objects can take damage in her place, preventing Yorna from taking injuries.
Environment Manipulation: By applying this technique to inanimate objects, such as her golden kiseru, the Crimson Lapis Castle, and the Demon City of Chaosflame itself, she is able to manipulate or strengthen everything in her environment; this being said, the same restrictions that apply to the people under the technique's effect apply to inanimate objects as well: she must be able to love the objects that she uses the technique on and spend time and devotion into them, and if that love, time, and devotion is lacking, it can reduce the effectiveness of the technique on said objects or land. She has applied this technique by manipulating a roof's tiles to form steps in thin air, which she can use to freely jump around on, or create pathways from the ground beneath. During the Destruction of Chaosflame, Yorna cast Soul Marriage upon all of the city, allowing her to attack the shadows by manipulating nearby buildings and throwing them at the incoming tendrils. She is even capable of manipulating something as minuscule as dust and use it as a defense, or intangible substances like her kiseru's smoke, which she can use as a shield against strikes as powerful as Olbart's, or to repair damage done to her environment.
Detonation: Anything under the effects of the Soul Marriage Technique is capable of creating an explosion. Of course, this ordinarily comes with the cost of said objects being destroyed in the process. She demonstrated this ability when she not only blew up the Crimson Lapis Castle but also Chaosflame itself to repel the shadow during the Destruction of Chaosflame. This is also capable of being used by any person imbued with the technique. Tanza, who was under its effects, was able to trigger such an explosion from her body, which managed to fully repel the remnants of said shadow. However, while it is unknown if it was solely unique to Tanza or something that would happen with any other person imbued by the technique, Tanza survived the explosion without injury, and instead, she and the one at the center of her target, Subaru, were instead sent flying to the other side of the country.

Curse
Soul Marriage Curse (魂婚呪, Konkon Noroi): The Soul Marriage Curse, also called the Binding of Thorns (茨の縛め, Ibara no Imashime) by Priscilla Barielle, is a curse that drags a lost soul back without handing it over to Od Lagna. It was cast onto Yorna by Eugard Vollachia. Because Yorna's soul cannot go to Od Lagna upon death, it instead fails to receive the proper treatment of a soul after its death, goes into the earth, and repetitively reincarnates her into another vessel. It is unknown if the curse has any relation with the Soul Marriage Technique. Thus far, she has been stated to have lived more than ten lives. Yorna's curse seems to be catalyzed through the deaths of the wolf and mole humans, and with the decree for their deaths being removed, the curse is likely to eventually subside.

Equipment
Golden Kiseru: Yorna can usually be seen walking around with her golden kiseru, taking in rainbow puffs of smoke at her own leisure. When in battle, though, she can be seen frequently using it as a weapon, as it has been strengthened by the Soul Marriage Technique to the point that it can shatter a kunai used by Olbart.
Numerous Beloved Articles: Yorna wears various accessories, jewelries, and even articles of clothing that were made by those who love her. Imbued with her Soul Marriage Technique, the various objects can receive any fatal or severely injuring attacks meant for Yorna, though at the cost of the articles themselves.

intro: Tarco Ulrat (タルコ・ウルラート) is a demi-human that was introduced as a new character in Re:Zero Lost in Memories when Emilia, the members of her camp, and Wilhelm were all sent to the Demi-Human War 50 years ago.
appearance:
Tarco is a middle-aged man with bushy white eyebrows, a scar on his left side of his face, and long black hair that has grey and white strands closer to the tips. He also holds a braid adorned on his right side of his hair. Due to his demi-human blood, he has fangs and wolf-like ears on his head. He wears light armor with fur on the inside, a heavy shoulder guard his right shoulder, and also adorns himself with a long blue cape.

In his Beast form, he has grey and cream white fur on his body. Additionally, he has features similar to Ricardo with black hair on his chest and arms, but also holding tusks on the sides of his mouth. He has a large scar on his right shoulder and tattered clothing when he was in his human form, only for him to become bare-chested and barefoot, leaving only his pants intact.
abilities_text:
Master Swordsman: Tarco is capable of using dual swords during combat.

Beastification: Tarco, like Garfiel, can use his ancestral demi-human blood to transform himself into a tall bipedal grey wolf, almost like a werewolf; with massive and thick limbs as well as razor-sharp fangs and claws which can easily rip a man or even a fully grown earth dragon in two with a single swipe. Tarco's physical strength in his wolf form was increased exponentially. He can also use his swords during this form.
Resonance Wave: In this form, he unlocks an ability that unleashes a violent burst of destructive mana from his mouth.

Inhuman strength and speed: Due to his demi-human blood, Tarco is extremely strong.

name: Weitz Rogen
intro: Weitz Rogen (ヴァイツ・ログン) is a former gladiator at the Gladiator Island Ginunhive and a member of Subaru's Unit during the latter's stay on the island who later joined the Pleiades Battalion. He made his debut in Arc 7.
appearance: Weitz is a well-built bald man with black eyes. Most of his body, including his arms, legs, chest, and head are covered with blue tattoos.
personality: Weitz is an antisocial and cowardly man who talks in a low, hushed voice. His treatment towards others is blunt and often accompanied with threats. Weitz wishes to be treated normally, but since he never had the opportunity to be trusted by those around him, he began to act how he was perceived. However, under the surface, Weitz is a loyal and trusting individual. In return for being kind towards him, Weitz offers genuine help and shows respect to those who extend him a hand. His loyalty is so strong, in fact, that he has a tendency to forget common sense due to his wish to assist the one he is loyal to. When he wanted to follow Subaru to assist him in the Conquest of the Undead Capital, he was willing to latch onto the bottom of the carriage they were using, paying no attention to the fact that he would eventually tire out and be forced to let go, not only subverting his intentions, but also putting himself at risk of great harm.
history:
Weitz was born in Glarasia, a city where the Empire's arms are primarily manufactured. As an orphan, he started working at city's workshops in return for food. Weitz aimed to be normal, but due to his introverted nature, he never talked to anyone. As time passed, people started regarding him as mysterious and creepy. One day, when some stocked materials from a workshop he frequently worked at went missing, Weitz was falsely accused of illegally stealing and selling the materials. Unable to disprove the allegations, a tattoo was inked onto Weitz's body, which branded him as a criminal. After he was no longer accepted into working, Weitz was ironically forced to steal materials from workshops in order to stay alive, fully embracing his status as a criminal. As a result of this, Weitz quit trying to be normal and instead chose to become someone who would be viewed as dangerous. To achieve this goal, he voluntarily covered himself in them from head to toe in more tattoos.

Eventually, Weitz had heard a rumor over a drink, and he discovered the identity of the man who had initially falsely accused him through it. Weitz would later retaliate by beating him and biting his ear off. Intending to leave the man beside him crying, shouting, and bleeding, he suddenly found himself surrounded by guards. After being forced to surrender, he quickly spit the man's ear before being apprehended and sent to jail. Weitz was consequentially sent to the Gladiator Island as his punishment.
abilities_text: Equipment: Weitz has wielded a large two-handed hammer and was somewhat well-trained with it despite having amateur movements while using it.

name: Trellock
intro: Trellock (トレロコ) is a serial killer from Gusteko.
appearance: Trellock appeared as a skinny young man in his early twenties with moderately long ashen-colored hair.
personality: Trellock is a serial killer who targets people whose faces he yearns, destroys their faces, and removes the mask of their “persona”. He uses them to “become” like his victims and employ their personalities. The personality he was last known to have employed was that of a sociable yet wary peddler.
history:
One Wild Night
For a few weeks, Trellock was responsible for a string of six recognized serial murders where each victim had their faces damaged. He eventually crossed paths with a peddler but failed to tear his face off. Trellock got caught in a snowstorm sometime later and visited a church on the mountains overlooking Leanotte. Upon entering, he was greeted by Noelle Tuérico, Admonsah, and Omega and her group. He proceeded to participate in the discussions revolving around Pastor Coatl's murder while continuing to simulate the peddler’s personality, up until Maqueena used Muskrim to make nearly everyone fall asleep. Trellock did not fall completely unconscious, however, but his movement was temporary limited by the effects of the sleeping flower.When Trellock could move his body again, he attempted to remove Colette's face, which activated her Beast Protection Bracelet. His body vanished, leaving nothing but bloodstains behind in the basement and church, making it unknown whether or not he survived the ordeal.

intro: Zank Metley (ザンク・メトレイ) is a former Temple Knight of the Gustekan Church.
appearance: Zank is a tall man in his mid-twenties with short, brown hair and dark skin.
personality: Zank at first comes off as a cold zealot who, as a Temple Knight, is willing to go to any length to eliminate heretics. However, unlike other followers of the Church, he is not as quick to condemn everyone involved with said heretic, and he has shown to be willing to work with others to accomplish his goals. He had always questioned the teachings of the Church, and when those very teachings put his fiancée, who he cares greatly for and is willing to kill to protect, at risk of being killed by the very people she fought with, he decided to go against those teachings, even going as far as to kill other followers. This made him wary of other followers, such as Noelle Tuérico, and after confronting Omega, his faith in the church was gone.
history:
Omega in Wonderland
Having grown up in the same village as Mikli, the two joined the Church together, rising in both strength and rank until eventually, the two became Temple Knights of the Church, and after meeting the Holy King, they suggested for the two to marry, which they accepted. However, before the ceremony could take place, Mikli was sent to hunt a heretic, which led to her going missing. Because of this, Zank decided to take other followers and retrieve Mikli from the heretic. However, after witnessing the town of Sylphoa, where Mikli had gone missing, under a sleep spell, his followers suggested to kill everyone in the town, including Mikli, claiming that it was in accordance with the teachings and Holy Will. In response, Zank killed all five followers who had traveled with him, and he set up a barrier around the town to prevent others from entering the town's vicinity.

At some point after this, Omega's party arrived in Sylphoa, Omega having dispelled his barrier, and Omega and Colette had passed out. Meeting with Noelle and Palmyra, who had been able to ignore the spell thanks to Noelle's seal, he took their group to a large tent that only he was using. However, after explaining what was going on and finding conflict with Palmyra, who did not adhere to the Church's teachings, Colette's unconscious body turned into her beast form, a result of her Beast Protection Bracelet detecting danger, to protect everyone, and with Zank declaring her a heretic, Colette took Palmyra and Omega out of the tent, leaving Noelle to negotiate to take care of the more pressing matter of the town's sleep spell, leading to a temporary alliance between the two.

Shortly after this, Noelle found Shion, who was partially responsible for the town falling asleep. She warned Noelle that Zank killed all of his allies, and shortly after, Zank began fighting with Noelle and the beastified Colette. However, after Palmyra awoke and claimed that Mikli was still alive, Zank spoke with Omega, who had also awoken. After Omega told him to claim that the heretic was dead to the Church, he would need to resign, and because Mikli had lost her blessing permanently, she would also likely lose her position as a Temple Knight. After being told that he couldn't chase both being a follower of the Church and his fiancée, his faith in the Church was completely broken, and he left with Mikli, deciding to resign from the Church.
abilities_text: Blessing of People Repulsion (人除けの祝福, Hito Noke no Shukufuku): As a Temple Knight, Zank has the Blessing of People Repulsion, a red-colored spirit that creates barriers. It can create invisible small, short-range barriers, as well as a large barrier, which each make prevent people from being able to trespass beyond the barriers. It takes considerable skill to create barriers around a larger area and gives those who approach it a strange feeling. In addition, the Blessing's effects can be broken through with magic.

name: Zoey
relatives: Tanza (younger sister)
intro: Zoey (ゾーイ) was a servant of Yorna Mishigure and the older sister of Tanza.
appearance: Zoey was a deer human girl with a pair of antlers. When she took up residence in Chaosflame, she began to wear a kimono. As Zoey was Tanza's sister, it can be presumed that the two resembled each other.
personality: Zoey was viewed as a strong-willed and kind-hearted woman by Tanza. She scolded Tanza when she cursed the world, and was the most serious and hardworking servant that Yorna had.
history:
Zoey and Tanza's birthplace was ravaged and destroyed by bandits who sought to earn profits when the spread of a superstition claiming that boiling the antlers of deer humans could create a panacea. Their parents were murdered by the bandits, and the two of them barely escaped with their lives. From that point onward, the sisters lived a harsh life of suffering while attempting to evade those who sought to kill them for their antlers or to prey on their weakness, as has been customary for the Vollachia Empire. Zoey put herself through harsh circumstances to even obtain a plate of soup for her and Tanza. After they had continued to flee for a long time, the two of them eventually heard rumors of a paradise called Chaosflame, and Zoey led Tanza there. Yorna greeted the sisters when they arrived at Chaosflame and embraced them. Although Zoey had not cried when her parents died, when a spectacle was made of her so she could obtain soup, or when Tanza levied curses towards her, she began to sob as she embraced Yorna. Tanza, too, cried at this scene. 

In Chaosflame, the sisters were provided with suitable meals and a bedroom. Being the most hardworking of Yorna's servants, Zoey carried out her responsibilities dutifully. However, two years after arriving at Chaosflame, while Zoey was guiding demi-human tribes into the city, she passed a fortress of Imperial Soldiers who were conducting a military exercise. They attacked the demi-humans under the guise that they were potential enemies. Zoey would unfortunately be murdered and tortured for sport by the soldiers, who would then disgrace her corpse. As a result of Zoey's death, Yorna attacked the fortress and killed a majority of the soldiers there for revenge, and when a few of them escaped, she carried out a full-scale rebellion against the Empire to retrieve the escaped soldiers.

intro: Vague Adgard (ヴェイグ・アドガルド) is a prince of Gusteko who is known throughout the world as the Mad Prince, one of the three people said to be on par with the Kingdom's Reinhard van Astrea in terms of overall martial skill, alongside the Empire's Cecilus Segmunt and the City-States's Halibel.
appearance: Vague is a large man with a stern yet refined appearance that is described to be so unforgettable that it leaves a lasting impression in one's mind. He has long yellow-green hair that is neatly slicked back on one side and hangs over his shoulder on the other side, a small beard, a Sanskrit-like tattoo on the left side of his face, a well-trained physique, eyes that contain an unyielding resolve, and slightly-tanned dark skin. He wears a magnificent black uniform, in addition to having a white coat with a feathery collar at the top draped on his shoulders.
personality:
The Mad Prince, perhaps befitting of his title, is considered crazed. Although Vague acts as a kind and considerate man to anyone he may encounter normally, whenever he concerns himself with spirits, he feels an intense drive to eradicate them and will not hesitate to murder others so long as it is for the purpose of killing spirits, which he absolutely despises. He is not above murdering even his own blood relatives, although it is unknown why he did so, and indicates that he even believes he should be erased, as he replied to someone else's comment that he should erase himself by saying “not yet” and it was “too soon”.

Vague meticulously manages his anger and believes that, from his own experience, the full extent of one's anger lasts for six seconds. This notion, along with the mana consumption of his Enchanted Sword, led to his establishment of a rule to finish a battle within six seconds so he can maximize the anger he unleashes against his opponents.
history: Vague was born as a true descendent of the royal blood of Gusteko to a human mother and a great spirit, despite how the biology of spirits should not allow them to have the capacity to produce a child. For unknown reasons, he killed 15 or 16 of his siblings, was branded a national traitor, and was subsequently imprisoned and confined to Gusteko's northernmost tower, which seals the powers of spirits.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
Vague's martial skill is the greatest in Gusteko and is said to be on par with Reinhard's. Although it was in non-canon material, it was said that he was responsible for killing seven beings on the level of Great Spirits (Odglass, Zarestia, and the evolved forms of five of Julius Juukulius's contracted spirits). With his Divine Protections, which allow him to progressively become stronger the longer he fights, and his Enchanted Sword, which has absorbed the power of spirits he has killed, he had amassed enough strength by that point in time to handily slay a Muspel-empowered Arakiya mere seconds after confronting her, and to fight off her, Madelyn Eschart with Mezoreia's dragonhusk, Lumera Ia Juukulius, and Clind all at once. In the present day, however, it is unclear just how powerful he is.

Divine Protection
Though presently unknown how many he has in total, Vague is known to possess at least five Divine Protections due to his ability to steal them from others.

Divine Protection of Usurpation (簒奪の加護, Sandatsu no Kago): Vague was born with the Divine Protection of Usurpation, which has the power to plunder the Divine Protections of other people. It is unknown if this power has any conditions for its activation.
Divine Protection of Adaptability (適応の加護, Tekiō no Kago): This power enables Vague to adapt to any situation and environment.
Divine Protection of Isolation (孤独の加護, Kodoku no Kago): A power that can constantly raise Vague's battle capabilities when he is fighting people solo.
Divine Protection of Repetition (反復の加護, Hanpaku no Kago): This power allows for the same, repeated movements made by Vague over the course of a battle to become increasingly refined.
Divine Protection of Indomitability (不屈の加護, Fukutsu no Kago): Although the exact effects of this power are unconfirmed, it normally activates at the moment of its user's death. However, due to Vague's unique constitution as the world's only spirit human, his heart does not beat, causing the Divine Protection to remain perpetually active.

Physical Traits/Flow Method
Unique Constitution: Due to his nature as the world's only existing spirit human, Vague's physical makeup is fundamentally different from others in the world.
Constitution Shifting: Vague is capable of switching his body between his physical human body and his spirit body in a manner similar to Arakiya. It is unclear how many benefits this provides him.
Non-Beating Heart: Because he is a hybrid between humans and spirits, his heart does not beat, putting him in a position that can be considered neither dead nor alive. While it is unclear if this provides him any natural benefits, it is because of this that is he capable of using one of his Divine Protections to its fullest extent, as it only triggers when the user's life has come to an end.
Unaging Body: Due to his spiritual nature, Vague has stopped aging, and he is known to be capable of living for centuries while appearing as a man in his prime.
Great Mana Pool: Due to his spiritual nature, Vague boasts in impressive amount of mana, and he is shown to use his mana in conjunction with the Curse Swords Aeon to impressive effect.
Spiritual Mana Attunement: Vague is capable of detecting where a being is utilizing magic or mana, even from across a large distance. He is able to track down spirits by using this sense.

Equipment
Curse Swords Aeon (呪剣アイオーン, Juken Aiōn): In the non-canon Re:Sacrificing Life In Another World from Zero IF story, Vague wields the Curse Swords Aeon, which make up one of the Enchanted Swords. They are a pair of twin swords that, when activated, transform into blades of light that drain the user's mana and manifest a sharpness that corresponds to it, which can allow them to cleave through strong defenses. However, they are unsuited for longer battles due to their energy consumption, which contributed to Vague establishing a six second rule with its usage. The ability of the Curse Swords allows them to absorb the power of an opponent. As Vague was only known to have used this power on spirits, it is unknown if it can be applied to beings besides them. Although it is unclear whether he used them before being sealed away, in the silhouetted image provided by the anime, he is shown to be wielding a pair of swords that seemingly match the physical descriptions of them, so it is possible that he has used them previously.

intro: Whitaker Goldario (ウィテカー・ゴルダリオ) was the final head of House Goldario and a backer of Eugard Vollachia before his coronation as Vollachia's emperor. A victory contractor for the Imperial Selection Ceremony, he was the guiding figure behind Eugard's rise to the imperial throne.
appearance: Whitaker was a young man in his early twenties with dark red hair and narrow amber eyes. He dressed in a formal jacket.
personality:
Whitaker was a cunning man who utilized every means available to him to fulfill his purpose of backing an imperial family member to ensure they would become emperor, employing numerous subordinates, including shinobi, who acted as his eyes and ears. Despite that, he had a reckless and childish side to him, as his schemes were rooted from a desire to bear witness to that which was “dramatic”. For this reason, he sided with Eugard in the Imperial Selection Ceremony. Furthermore, Whitaker cared deeply for the welfare of his sister, Terriola, and consistently endeavored to guarantee her a prosperous life, even after she opposed his failed rebellion. He also had a habit of using the English loan word “dramatic”, a word passed down in the Goldario family, when the situation called for it, with it being unknown who and where they learned it from.

It is unclear when Whitaker became a Stargazer and what his commandment to fulfill was. Although his sister believed it was his intention from the beginning to betray the King of Thorns and install himself on his throne, he admitted that he had not always intended to betray Eugard shortly before his death.
history:
As the head of the Goldario family, despite outwardly being designated a commoner, Whitaker was entrusted with the responsibility to observe every candidate for the Imperial Selection Ceremony and determine which of contenders to be the advisor of like his predecessors before him. As the King of Thorns, Eugard Elcanti, began to show interest in involving himself in the Imperial Selection Ceremony, a move unexpected from him, Whitaker watched him and the other candidates from the sidelines with his sister, Terriola.

After exerting various efforts to verify the existence of the Goldarios, Eugard Elcanti finally managed to get in contact with Whitaker over a Conversation Mirror, introducing himself to the advisor with Iris at his side. Whitaker exposed his intent to regard Eugard as the successive emperor, choosing to side with him because of the response to his circumstances of his life and his curse not being rooted out of anger or lamentation, but from something else, and since siding with him granted the Goldarios the highest odds of success. With Iris's affirmation of Eugard's candidacy, Whitaker ascertained his plan to conspire with him. After their conversation ended, he spoke with Terriola about the King of Thorns and his relationship with Iris, and expressed his awareness of his sister's interest in Eugard.

From then on, Whitaker began travelling around Vollachia, making preparations to ensure Eugard would acquire the imperial throne, procuring an abundance of Conversation Mirrors necessary to contact him with while doing so. During this period of preparation, he corroborated Volcas's capabilities as being worthy of the Nine Divine Generals, attempted to ask Eugard why Iris was an exception to the binding of his Curse of Thorns only to fail to receive an answer, and subsequently attempted to gauge his interest in Terriola, proposing that she could serve as a candidate for an empress consort to him, to which the King of Thorns said he would consider. Suddenly, Eugard pulled out the Yang Sword, signaling his father had died just then and that it was time to commence the Imperial Selection Ceremony.

When it was discovered that Iris had an illness, Whitaker did research to determine it was Battle Craze Syndrome, that the healer who nursed her back to health when she was contracted it had only subdued it despite being unaware of its nature, and visited her to inform her of his findings and gifted her medicinal herbs he had quickly gathered with his influence to aid in her recovery, entrusting their use to Lynek in order to cure the disease and save her life. Once Eugard killed his final sibling, he was congratulated over a Conversation Mirror by Whitaker, who had prepared a “dramatic” gift for him. Iris, finally cured of her disease, had rushed to see Eugard; however, she was afflicted by his Curse of Thorns, triggering the emperor-to-be to repeatedly yell out Whitaker's name in horror as she was assaulted by his thorns' binding. The ensuing fallout resulted in Volcas aiming his claws over Whitaker's neck in rage, pinning him responsible for Iris having succumbed to Eugard's curse, only being stopped from taking his life by Terriola. Attributing the herbs as having produced this situation, Volcas was countered by Whitaker by mentioning Iris's preexisting illness. Volcas then left to see Iris, leaving the siblings to continue preparing for Eugard's coronation.

Alone, the two spoke about the unexpectedness of Iris losing her resistance to the Curse of Thorns, with Whitaker saying that curing her had “backfired”, rousing suspicion in Terriola. Eugard's Curse of Thorns had expanded in its scope and began to pierce people through Conversation Mirrors, leaving only indirect communication as the only remaining method to viably contact him with. As Terriola left to continue preparing for the coronation, she saw Whitaker muttering to himself, wondering what the most “dramatic” plot twist from there would be. Sometime thereafter, Lynek bore news to Iris, revealing that Whitaker Goldario had launched a rebellion against Eugard, intending to murder him by setting fire to the Imperial Residence in the Imperial Capital. However, Terriola intervened before his assassination could be carried out, allowing Eugard to escape. Regarding his sister a traitor and knowing that she had loved Eugard, Whitaker imprisoned Terriola, and the siblings argued. Whitaker had come to the conclusion that Eugard needed to be dispatched because his Curse of Thorns was going haywire, believing there was no other option, which Terriola vehemently refused to accept, being under the impression he had intended to murder the King of Thorns prior to his coronation and install himself on the throne from the beginning. She expressed her abhorrence for her brother, receiving no answer in return.

The rebellion caught Eugard by surprise due to both his own incompetence and Whitaker's meticulousness and shrewdness. Without the aid of Terriola, who aided him in escaping from the Imperial Residence before it could be set ablaze, he would have died. Pursued by the Nine Divine Generals, whom Whitaker had made his allies, he reasoned that the rebellion had been hastily planned and his past loyalty had not been a lie. Though he briefly considered surrendering, he was encouraged to ascend to the position of emperor by Iris, who confessed her feelings to him. Driven by love, he systematically slew the Nine Divine Generals one by one. Whitaker appeared before Eugard after the final Divine General was killed, admitting defeat. He imparted some final advice to Eugard relating to the Goldario family's dissolution and managing the water supply in the north region of the Imperial Capital, and made sure Terriola would be spared from the consequences of his actions, expressing relief once her safety was assured. He revealed that it was not his intention to rebel from the beginning, and commented on how fateful and “dramatic” it was for House Goldario to be remembered as traitors, before proceeding to kneel and bow his head, offering his neck to Eugard. Receiving final words of commend for his service, Whitaker Goldario was executed by Eugard Elcanti, putting an end to the Thief Emperor's rebellion.

However, Terriola intervened before his assassination could be carried out, aiding Eugard in escaping the Imperial Residence in the Imperial Capital before it was set ablaze. Regarding his sister a traitor and knowing that she had loved Eugard, Whitaker imprisoned Terriola, and the siblings argued. Whitaker had come to the conclusion that Eugard needed to be dispatched because his Curse of Thorns was going haywire, believing there was no other option, which Terriola vehemently refused to accept, being under the impression that this was his intention from the start. She expressed her abhorrence for her brother, receiving no answer in return.

Once her brother's rebellion failed and her house fell into ruin, Terriola cut her hair to signify her severance of the Goldario name. Swearing her fealty to Eugard, she gathered the shinobi that served the Goldario family to cooperate with him. However, they could not stop Volcas from murdering Iris. At Iris's funeral, Terriola revealed the existence of the Soul Marriage Curse to Eugard and implored him to use it in an attempt to ensure that he and his lover could reunite someday. To withstand Eugard's Curse of Thorns, she drank poison, imploring him to produce an heir with her to fulfill his duty as emperor while directing his true love to his one and only Iris, and that she would be the first to bear an heir. Eugard responded that he would consider her proposal, but that she would bear no responsibility in his consideration to cast the Soul Marriage Curse. From Eugard's point of view, if his love toward Iris was to produce a curse, the responsibility would be his alone, and neither Terriola nor Volcas could interfere, as it was between him and his star.

Following her conversation with Eugard, she spoke with Lynek, whom she had kept hidden to brew poison for her and to protect him from the imminent policy that decreed the execution of all wolf people and mole people. Despite the decree, Lynek had no words of apology for his brethren, as he and Volcas had made their decisions, and he chose to prioritize Eugard and Iris over his pack. She prepared a refuge for him at the Gladiator Island surrounded by Lake Violane and considered turning it into a prison for convicts to act as a distraction for him. Affirming to him that she had not spoken of her feelings for Eugard to him so she would not be a thief like her brother, the Thief Emperor, she wished Lynek well, and he set off for Lake Violane.

At some point, Eugard accepted Terriola's proposal, and the two produced a child. As a consequence of the effects of the poison she ingested multiple times to resist the Curse of Thorns, Terriola died at a young age. Before her death, she confessed her true feelings to Eugard. The child she gave birth to went on to achieve victory in the Imperial Selection Ceremony and become Vollachia's sixty-second emperor, making Terriola an ancestor to the modern imperial family.

intro: Volcas (ヴォルカス) is one of the Nine Divine Generals of the Sacred Vollachia Empire.
appearance:
Volcas is a wolf person with a muscular build covered with dark black fur whose body can be said to be a lethal weapon. He has golden-colored eyes, black bangs that droop over one of his eyes, fangs as sharp as blades that protrude from his mouth, and beastly claws at the ends of his trunk-like arms. For a wolf person, Volcas is taller than average.

As a zombie, he possesses a vessel of earth, various cracks that run across his body, pitch-black sclera, and radiant golden irises differing from those he had in life.
personality:
Volcas deeply detested Vollachia's Law of Iron and Blood for allowing for the weak to be abandoned. As a wolf person who lived and was sustained by his pack, for most of his life, his community took precedence over everything else. He valued it more than anything and would not hesitate to permit them to maraud villages in order to gather resources that guaranteed their survival or seek vengeance for members of his pack who were killed. Despite despising Vollachia's mantra, when placed in a situation where he exacted retribution for his fallen brethren and aimed to ward off the ensuing counterattack with violence, he believed he had no other choice but to kill or be killed, and to prove his pack's strength to protect them, which would ironically cause him to adhere to the Law of Iron and Blood. He had a strong sense of determination for matters relating to his pack and to achieve his own desires when he could, and confidence in his own strength and capabilities. He also spoke rudely to those he knew and frequently bantered with or hurled insults to them.

After being saved by Iris, Volcas started to care for her, beginning to treat her similarly to members of his pack, and eventually, he fell in love with her. While not entirely loyal to Eugard, he was willing to serve the King of Thorns as long as it was what Iris wanted. By the time she was gradually whittling down her lifespan to stay at Eugard's side, Volcas's love for her had grown so large that he decided to prioritize his selfish feelings for her over the welfare of his pack. In order to end her suffering at the hands of poison, he chose to murder her, and to ensure that Eugard had the will to continue his reign in accordance with what he thought would be her wish, Volcas deliberately condemned his pack and their kin to persecution by asserting that they would avenge him, surmising that the King of Thorns would likely slaughter them in an act of retribution, which subjected them to the Empire's retaliation for a period of nearly 300 years.
history:
Iris and the King of Thorns
With his immense strength, Volcas became the leader of a “pack” of demi-humans. Several members of their pack would attempt to maraud a village within the Elcanti Domain, and the Elcanti army, which had been directed by Eugard Elcanti to guard villages within the domain, slew the bandits and burned their bodies. Roughly twenty days later, Volcas and his pack participated in a retaliatory attack to avenge their fallen comrades. He tore apart and murdered most of the villagers, with only a number of women and children surviving the onslaught. They were captured and placed in cages within a cave the pack used as a base. Though most of the village women were sobbing and feared for their lives, one of them, Iris, stood up to Volcas, undeterred by his rage even upon learning he had murdered her parents and friends. Believing that his pack's only chance at survival was to eradicate their enemy, he rejected the girl's attempt to reason with him. Suddenly, he detected the scent of anger mixed in with the wind, emanating from a lone man who was approaching their base, and expressed confusion over what the man could accomplish by himself.

With sword in hand, the man, Eugard Elcanti, arrived by himself to prevent unnecessarily sacrificing the soldiers in his army. With his Curse of Thorns unilaterally binding everyone in the vicinity, besides Iris, most members of the pack were quickly defeated without a fight. Volcas used his claws and attempted to tear open his chest to remove the thorns that had imparted themselves onto it, to no avail. Ignoring his self-inflicted injuries, Volcas clashed with Eugard, attempting to kill him in one blow with his sheer physical ability and relentless assaults spanning just over than ten seconds, but was repelled with the sword techniques of the King of Thorns and stopped fighting, having exerted his efforts. Volcas believed Eugard's lack of a counterattack was an insult to him, but the man corrected that belief, saying that the wolf person was strong and that he could not risk something bad happening in order to save the hostages. Eugard then freed Iris and prepared to execute Volcas and his pack. However, rather than wishing for their execution, Iris chose to forgive Volcas and the pack, imploring Eugard to spare their lives, shocking both of the men. Despite the murder of her friends and parents, Iris wished to forgive them anyways to prevent them from perpetuating a cycle of battle and death. Listening to Iris's request, and verifying that she would not regret this result, Eugard decided to spare the pack and asked Volcas for his name. As a consequence of their defeat, the members of the pack were bound by Collars of Subservience and conscripted into a disciplinary unit obligated to serve the Elcanti Domain.

Volcas often left the disciplinary unit's training sessions to disturb Iris while she was being taught by Lynek, chiming in by bantering with the village girl. After Whitaker Goldario joined their faction, the man gauged Volcas as having the power to the ascend to the Nine Divine Generals under Eugard's reign. As he began moving with the disciplinary unit when it came time to act in the Imperial Selection Ceremony, he spoke with Eugard over a Conversation Mirror, being given the instruction to have the soldiers refrain from marauding as they had done before to limit bloodshed. In return, Volcas told Eugard he did not need to be on the front lines and to stay by Iris's side. He said he would not act for their sake, requesting that he receive proper treatment in exchange for fulfilling his duties, to which Eugard replied by evaluating he was more than worthy of receiving the treatment of a General.

When it was discovered that Iris lost her ability to stay in close proximity to Eugard upon being cured of her Battle Craze Syndrome, Volcas aimed his claws over Whitaker's neck in rage, pinning him responsible for her having succumbed to the Curse of Thorns, and he was only stopped from taking the man's life by Terriola. Attributing the herbs used to cure her as having produced this situation, Volcas was countered by Whitaker by mentioning Iris's preexisting illness. Volcas then left to see Iris, leaving the siblings to continue preparing for Eugard's coronation alone. Some time later, he entered the Musik Castle where Iris had been briefly staying at and spoke with her. Believing he was indebted to her due to her decision to spare him and that he could not repay her with his life, Volcas declared to Iris that she could treat and use him however she wished. Shedding tears in response, he licked her tears in accordance with tradition for an adult from his pack to lick the tears of the young to comfort them. Just afterwards, Lynek appeared to inform Iris that Whitaker Goldario had launched a rebellion in tandem with the Nine Divine Generals against Eugard, intending to murder him by setting fire to the Imperial Residence in the Imperial Capital. 

To return to Eugard's side and encourage him to take arms against Whitaker, who planned to install himself on the throne once the King of Thorns was killed, Iris requested Lynek to use the herbs he had been gifted to create a medicine that would simulate the effects of Battle Craze Syndrome, which he reluctantly accepted after Volcas demanded an explanation from her. With Iris's encouragement, Eugard swiftly extinguished the lives of the Nine Divine Generals and Whitaker, putting a stop to the revolt, and his coronation proceeded as planned, being crowned as emperor by his beloved. Having been within the range of the Curse of Thorns for an extended period of time, Iris began to cough up blood when she returned to her quarters. Lynek warned her that she was pushing herself too hard, feeling guilty for creating a poison that was whittling down her life. Volcas, who was with the two, told Iris he was siding with her above all else, rather than with the Vollachia Empire, and that Eugard had no issue with his loyalties, giving her a cup of water after saying this. Though tolerating her selfishness despite the risk to her life, Volcas expressed genuine concern for her mind and body. Lynek rejected her proposal to teach her how to brew it herself, as she would not have been able to make it even if she had learned how to, yet he also had the responsibility of complying with her selfish request in order to remain with Eugard, placing him in a predicament where he would have had to continue bestowing her with poison out of obligation. Volcas delivered her a gentle insult, and Iris proceeded to rest in order to conserve her energy in order to interact with her beloved Eugard.

Iris's poisoning of herself troubled Volcas, who did not wish to see her suffer. In his mind, he was left with only two decisions to end her suffering. The first would be to take away her reason from using the poison, and the second was to physically stop her from using it outright. The first option, kill Eugard, would send Vollachia in disarray, something that neither he nor anyone else wished to see come to fruition. Thus, to prevent Iris from having to suffer the effects of the poison, Volcas made the decision to brandish his claws and tore into her back, removed her heart, and clutched it within his hand, performing this in the garden of the Crystal Palace to allow Eugard to witness it.

With Iris's collapsed body lying by Volcas's feet in a pool of blood, being held in his arms, Eugard discovered the scene. His Curse of Thorns activated and bound themselves to Volcas, producing an immense, agonizing pain within him, as well as Iris's heart, which became entwined with thorns. Eugard only pronounced a single word, why, upon observing Volcas's actions. He then opened his mouth and ate Iris's heart, swallowing it whole, making Eugard repeat his question. Volcas claimed it was a wolf person's nature, and that he had been waiting for this moment from the beginning. The emperor proceeded to shout Volcas's name, unsheathing the Yang Sword Vollachia from the air, incinerating his enemy's arm at the elbow instantly with the flames quickly spreading to his whole body. Although Volcas had always valued and prioritized his pack, in his last moments, he instead chose to prioritize his star, Iris, whom he had fell in love with. With his last breaths, he told Eugard to not think this was the end, and that his brethren would turn their fangs against him, to which he replied, suppressing the urge to yell and unleash his rage, by saying he would repel and eradicate anyone with ill intentions who came his way. Swinging the Yang Sword once more, Volcas pronounced once more that, in the end, Eugard was just a normal man, given his reaction to Iris's death. Though Volcas felt guilty for bringing his pack into his selfish whims, he did not regret it, and told Eugard to take his time, believing that he would have the woman he loved all to himself in death.

As a result of Iris's murder at the hands of Volcas, when Eugard publicly announced her death, he also began the decree that ordered the extermination of wolf people, the race the murderer of his beloved had belonged to, as well as the mole people, the race that Lynek, who had been perceived as a collaborator in her death, belonged to. While Volcas's plan of giving Eugard a reason to live by eradicating the two races had succeeded, his single miscalculation had been that the King of Thorns loved Iris far more than he could have imagined. Rather than performing the policy out of a desire for vengeance, which had been Volcas's goal, after learning of the existence of the Soul Marriage Curse from Terriola, he chose to bind the lives of the slaughtered wolf people and mole people as a means of preventing Iris's soul from being forfeit to Od Lagna, perpetually forcing her to reincarnate anew into vessel after vessel, with this eventually starting sometime after Eugard's reign. In the meantime, the soul of Volcas waited in vain in the Corridor until he could achieve a reunion with the one he sought.

Undead Busters
Resurrected in an undead form during the Great Disaster, Volcas's great strength allowed him to resist the compulsory force Sphinx used to place most zombies under her command. As such, he refrained from taking part in any battles during the disaster. Following Arakiya's assimilation with Muspel, limiting the lingering undead to have only one more life, he persisted afterwards unlike those who were killed or had ceased to desire anything and faded away, desiring to reunite with Iris, whose name he spoke.

He encountered an undead weaponkin by the name of Breznon and quickly disarmed and dispatched the man with his claws and fangs. This sight was witnessed by Cecilus Segmunt, who introduced himself to Volcas and in turn asked for his name. Recognizing Volcas from the tale of Iris and the King of Thorns and as a warrior whose name was spoken throughout Vollachia's history, the two Generals clashed in battle, which ended in the Blue Lightning's victory. However, as they were near Chaosflame and Yorna, rather than seeking to have Spica eat Volcas's name, Cecilus tried reasoning with Arakiya to let the wolf person stick around for the time being. While Cecilus and Arakiya were quarreling, Spica patted Volcas's head, causing him to reminisce back to when Iris had done so to him.

Upon reaching the location that the emperor and the Nine Divine Generals were staying at, Yorna Mishigure engaged in combat with Volcas. However, he did not make any attempt to fight back during their battle, and he stated that she smelled like Iris, to which she affirmed that she had gotten stronger since they last met. Although her appearance, expressions, voice, and presentation were completely different to Volcas, he recognized her laughter, which was the same as it was 300 years ago. Following the events of the battle, Volcas sought to be executed by the emperor, Vincent Vollachia, with the Yang Sword, whereas Yorna obstinately did not want to accept that outcome. Realizing that there was a possibility Yorna could revolt again, the new empress consort, Medium O'Connell, suggested to Vincent that Volcas should be chosen to fill the vacancy in the Nine Divine Generals. She believed her proposal would not only cater to Yorna and fill the vacancy left by Chisha Gold, but with Volcas being the direct cause behind Eugard's decree to execute the wolf people and mole people, forgiving him and having him join their side would show that Vincent was serious about keeping the decree rescinded. After hearing Medium out, Vincent proceeded to meet with Volcas in person to discuss her proposal with him. At some point afterwards, Volcas accepted the proposition, becoming a member of the Nine Divine Generals.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
Volcas possesses strength far beyond that of even an ordinary wolf person. In terms of pure might, Volcas was described as the pinnacle of strength in Vollachia during his time, and he was only outclassed by Eugard Vollachia, whose prowess and technique with the sword was able to counter him even without the Curse of Thorns. Likewise, his strength was enough to allow him to resist the influence of Sphinx's compulsory force so that he could act on his own.

Physical Traits/Flow Method
Among the wolf people, Volcas is particularly powerful, possessing a muscular body and large arms he can move at such swift speeds that his relentless assault of an opponent can be compared to the speed of a tornado, while his movements seem as quick as the blink of an eye.

Powerful Jaw: As a wolf human, Volcas has sharp fangs rather than teeth. That, combined with his jaw strength, allow him to easily crush the iron legs of a powerful weaponkin like Breznon.

Powerful Claws: Volcas has sharp, blade-like claws capable of tearing through iron and piercing into someone's body or reducing them to a clump of blood in a single blow. With them, he is easily able to rip a person's heart out of their body or sever the legs of his enemies with ease.

Heightened Olfaction: As a wolf person, Volcas has a strong, keen sense of smell, allowing him to detect the amount of people in a given area by their scent. From his many experiences in combat, he is also able to distinguish the smell of anger emanating from those who were preparing to do battle.

intro: Tiga Rauleon (ティーガ・ラウレオン) is an emissary of the Divine Dragon Church. He plays an antagonistic role in Arc 10.
appearance: Tiga is a gentle-looking and handsome man with bright-green colored hair and distinctive yellow eyes, whose affective gestures suit him. Tiga's attire consists of a long violet suit with gold highlights and black pants and boots. He adorns himself with a jet-black wide-brimmed, bowl-shape hat, a purple rose on his coat, and a gold pendant that is in the shape of the Divine Dragon.
personality:
Tiga is a friendly young man who is able to get along with others rather easily. He also acts with a sense of responsibility as a member of the Divine Dragon Church, especially concerning matters of Filore and her reckless behavior, and he is quick to chide both her and his other coworkers for their behavior should he believe it necessary. He does seem to have a slightly competitive side as well, as upon seeing Filore's triumphant expression at gaining a new friend in Emilia, he said such an expression was unacceptable before looking toward Natsuki Subaru and asking him to be his friend.

Despite his usual demeanor, Tiga is easily capable of making cruel and harsh decisions when necessary. Though not unwilling to give an ultimatum to his opponents according to the wishes of a friend, he can ruthlessly attack said opponent even if it means burning away said friend and even himself in the process. At the same time, however, he declares that his doing so is due to needing to reclaim his life. His ruthlessness has been described by Beatrice as akin to Roswaal's.
abilities_text:
Overall Power
Tiga is a considerably strong combatant capable of going toe to toe with the likes of someone on the level of Crusch Karsten, and his willingness to bring harm to his own body and fight dirty make him far more dangerous. This being said, both he and Heinkel Astrea believe that his skill do not reach the likes of Wilhelm van Astrea's, as they both believed that if they confronted each other, Tiga would most certainly lose.

Physical Traits/Flow Method
Expert Swordsman: Tiga is an excellent swordsman with enough skill to fight evenly with someone on the level of Crusch. His attacks are brutal and efficient, aiming for limbs with his strikes and weaving spins into his swordsmanship, reminiscent of a spinning top. He is also shown to be able to seamlessly weave in kicks while he attacks without breaking his momentum.

Magic
Tiga is capable of using fire magic. However, as he had previously claimed to be incapable of using magic, Beatrice suspects that either that was a bluff or that there was some other reason he was able to cast magic.

Intelligence
Keen Observation: Tiga is rather perceptive in combat. After only being exposed to it for a mere few moments, he was able to come up with a countermeasure to use magic when under the influence of EMT.

Equipment
Shamshir: Tiga wields a curved sword called a shamshir as his primary weapon.

name: Tornel
intro: Tornel (トルネル) is a member of the Beloved Children. He plays an antagonistic role in Arc 10.
appearance: Tornel is a young boy in his early to mid-teens with chestnut colored hair and light blue eyes, and his bangs cover his right eye. He carries around a large yellow lamp that contains Lagmite ore within it. He wears a light tan robe that is a little longer than his body, and a similarly colored beret. He has on a darker tan button-up shirt with a white collar and light purple tie, a light purple sash that hangs from his shoulder to his waist, brown shorts, brown boots, light purple socks that almost come up to his knees, and bandages on one knee.
personality: Tornel has a tendency to constantly apologize, whether for simply speaking or in response to others' actions. He is afraid of people being mad at him and will apologize when someone is angry, even if he is not the target of their anger. He often appears nervous around others and seems to have a habit of clutching his head when he is overwhelmed.
abilities_text:
Techniques
Detour (遠回り, Tōmawari): Tornel has the capacity to make people unable to reach their intended destination, resulting in them becoming lost in the process of attempting to reach it. When someone subject to Tornel's Detour attempts to travel to another place, such as from one point of a building to another, they will repeatedly go through the same rooms, and the distance between them and their destination will not shrink. However, it is possible for other abilities, like Subaru's Cor Leonis, to surpass the effects of Detour, allowing someone who is subjected to its power to reach a destination. Upon deactivating his power, a blue light will coalesce in the area before returning everything to normal.
